englishExplanation: Infant LP: L4-L5 or L5-S1 (spinal cord ends at L3 in infants). Adults/children: L2-L3 or below. Avoid neck hyperflexion in infants (airway compromise).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـspinal cord بالـinfants بتخلص عند L3، بعكس الكبار اللي بينتهي عند L1-L2. عشان كده في الـinfant بتعمل الـlumbar puncture عند L4-L5 أو L5-S1، بعد ما تحسب خط الـiliac crests وتستخدم الـspace اللي تحس إنه فيه ما بين الـL4 و L5. ولازم تتجنّب الـhyperflexion للرقبة لأنها بتأثر على الـairway. أما الكبار أو الأطفال فالموضع المعتاد L2-L3 أو تحت، يعني القاعدة مختلفة مع الـinfant.
الفخ: الخيار A (L1-L2) هو الفخ لأن الناس بتحسب مكان العمود الفقري عند الكبار، بس عند الـinfant الـcord أقصر وبيخلص عند L3. ولازم تتجنب الـneck hyperflexion عند الرضّع لأنه بيأثر على الـairway.

question: During which of the cardinal movements of labor is it appropriate to check for a nuchal cord?

options.text: External rotation of the fetal head
Internal rotation of the fetal head

correctAnswer: External rotation of the fetal head
englishExplanation: After delivery of fetal head (external rotation): check for nuchal cord. Loose → slip over head. Tight → clamp x2, cut between, unwind. If cut → deliver immediately.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بعد ما يطلع رأس الجنين وبيعمل external rotation، هاد الوقت المناسب تفحصوا منه على nuchal cord، أي هل الحبل ملفوف على رقبة الجنين. الفحص لازم يصير بعد delivery of the head وقبل delivery of the body. إذا الحبل loose بينزلق فوق الرأس بدون مشكلة. وإذا كان tight بتقفله بمشبكين، تقطعه بينهم وتفكّه. وإذا انقطع الحبل بتولّد فوراً.
الفخ: الخيار D (internal rotation of the fetal head) هو الفخ لأن فحص الـnuchal cord بيصير بعد الـexternal rotation مو بعدها. والخيار B (extension) غلط لأن الـextension بتكون قبل ما يطلع الرأس. اللي بينفع بكمّل وبيحكّم الـdelivery فوراً.

question: How should the umbilical cord in a newborn be managed for most US hospital-based births?
englishExplanation: ACOG: dry cord care for US hospital births (keep dry, water only if soiled). Delayed clamping 30-60s (increases iron stores, decreases NEC/IVH in preterm). Double-clamp 3 cm from abdominal wall.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في most US hospital births، الـACOG بينصح بـdry cord care، يعني تخلّي الحبل ناشف وما تحط عليه شي إلا إذا اتسخّ وبيحتاج ماء. بيتأخر القطع 30-60 ثانية، وهاد بيزوّد مخزون الحديد وبيقلّل NEC و IVH في الخدج. والقفل بيتعمل مرتين على بعد 3 cm من جدار البطن. يعني الخيار A (70% alcohol) ما بتنصح فيه ACOG، والـclamping بيعمل بعد 3 cm من جدار البطن.
الفخ: الخيار A (Apply 70% alcohol) هو الفخ لأن الـdry cord care هي الموصى بها في معظم Delivery Rooms داخل أمريكا، والـalcohol مش جزء من الـprotocol. والخيار C (double-clamp at insertion site) غلط لأن الـdouble clamp بيعمل على بعد 3 cm من جدار البطن.

question: What is the next best step in the management of an infant with omphalitis?
englishExplanation: Omphalitis: infection of umbilical stump, polymicrobial (S. aureus, S. pyogenes, gram-negatives). Requires IV antibiotics (antistaphylococcal penicillin + aminoglycoside). Can progress to sepsis/necrotizing fasciitis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـomphalitis يعني التهاب في بقايا الحبل السري بعد ما ينفصل، وهاد بسبب عدوى بكتيرية. والعدوى بكونها polymicrobial، يعني فيها S. aureus و S. pyogenes و gram-negatives مع بعض. عشان كده لازم تعطي IV antibiotics، وده anti-staphylococcal penicillin مع aminoglycoside. والموضوع خطير لأن الـomphalitis ممكن يتطور لـsepsis أو necrotizing fasciitis بسرعة.
الفخ: الخيار C (topical antibiotics) هو الفخ لأن الـomphalitis مش superficial، هي عدوى ممكن توصل للـblood والـfascia. والـsilver nitrate بيتعامل مع granuloma السرة مش مع التهاب، وإعطاء antibiotics عن طريق الفم بطيء وما في داعي له.

question: An infant presents with omphalitis and history of recurrent infections. What is the most likely underlying condition?
englishExplanation: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (autosomal recessive): delayed cord separation + omphalitis + recurrent infections. Inability to form pus, no leukocytosis. Treatment: antibiotics, HSCT for severe.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـtriad اللي بتجمع omphalitis مع عدوى متكررة و فصل متأخر للحبل السري، وهاد strongly مع leukocyte adhesion deficiency، وهي مرض وراثي autosomal recessive. السبب إن الـleukocytes ما بتعرف توصل لمكان العدوى، فالمريض ما بيقدر يعمل pus ولا بيسوي leukocytosis. العلاج antibiotics، وفي الحالات الشديدة بنلجأ لـHSCT. ولازم تفكر فيها بأي baby عندو recurrent infections مع omphalitis.
الفخ: الخيار D (necrotizing fasciitis) هو الفخ لأن هاد complication ممكن يصير بـomphalitis، بس هو مش المرض الأساسي اللي بتفسر الـrecurrent infections. والخيار B (funisitis) يعني التهاب الحبل نفسه وهو سببه bacteria مش نقص مناعي.

question: Which infant clinical presentation warrants urgent surgical consultation?

options.text: Induration of umbilical stump and abdomen
Small, red, moist, velvety umbilical mass

correctAnswer: Induration of umbilical stump and abdomen
englishExplanation: Omphalitis extending to abdominal wall → risk of necrotizing fasciitis → urgent surgical consult. Umbilical hernia reducible = no surgery. Granuloma = silver nitrate.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لما الـomphalitis تنتشر من بقايا الحبل للـabdominal wall، بتولّد صلابة (induration) في السرة والبطن، وهاد بيخلي خطر necrotizing fasciitis كبير، فهاد اللي بيستدعي استشارة جراح عاجلة. أما الـumbilical hernia القابلة للرد (reducible) فما بتحتاج عملية، والـgranuloma بتنحل بالـsilver nitrate. لازم تفرق بينها وبين الـumbilical hernia والـgranuloma لأنهم مش كلهم الحالات بيحتاجوا جراح. ولو شفت صلابة حول السرة والبطن، لا تستنى وتواصل مع الجراح على طول.
الفخ: الخيار B (bulging umbilicus when crying) هو الفخ لأن هاد hernia قابلة للرد وبيروح لحاله. والخيار D (small red moist velvety mass) هو الـgranuloma وبيتعالج بالـsilver nitrate، والخيار A (bleeding) مش هو اللي بيستدعي الجراح.

question: A 36-week pregnant woman in cardiac arrest. Fundal height near xiphoid. What type of abdominal incision for emergency cesarean delivery?
englishExplanation: Perimortem cesarean: vertical midline from 4-5 cm below xiphoid to 2-3 cm above pubic hair. Initiate within 4-5 min of maternal arrest. No need to scrub abdomen, no need to move to OR.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: عند الـcardiac arrest عند الحامل، لازم تبتدي بـperimortem cesarean خلال 4-5 دقيقة من توقف القلب. والشق بيكون vertical في الـmidline abdominal، يبدأ من 4-5 cm تحت الـxiphoid وينتهي 2-3 cm فوق عظام العانة. وما في داعي تعقم البطن ولا تنقل المريضة للـOR، لازم تبدأ بالشق على طول. والـmidline vertical بيضمن وصول سريع للـuterus بدون ما تضل تعقم.
الفخ: الخيار A (low transverse) هو الفخ لأنه شق فيه وقت، وفي وقت الـcardiac arrest ما في وقت. والخيار B (low vertical) مش هاد لأن الشق لازم يبدأ تحت الـxiphoid مش تحت السرة.

question: During the physical examination of a female sexual assault victim, what is the most likely injury?
englishExplanation: Sexual assault: most common genital injury = posterior fourchette (tense band of mucous membrane). Genital exam often normal despite assault. Colposcopy increases detection 6%→53%.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أهم إصابة في المنطقة التناسلية عند ضحية الاعتداء الجنسي بتطلع هي الـposterior fourchette، يعني حزمة مشدودة من الـmucous membrane. لازم تعرف إن الـgenital exam ممكن يطلع طبيعي رغم ما صار اعتداء، و الـcolposcopy بيزوّد اكتشاف الإصابات من 6% إلى 53%. يعني الفحص العادي ما بيكفي، وكمان الـvaginal wall والـhymen مش أكثر إصابات شيوعاً. ولازم تتعامل مع هاي الحالة بحساسية وخصوصية.
الفخ: الخيار D (vaginal wall) هو الفخ لأن أغلب الإصابات بتبقى superficial، لكن الـposterior fourchette هي الأكثر شيوعاً. والخيار A (hymen) أقل شيوعاً، وكمان الفحص الطبيعي ما بيلغي الاعتداء.

question: When obtaining a history from a reported sexual assault victim, on which element of the history should the emergency department avoid focus?

options.text: Details leading up to the assault

correctAnswer: Details leading up to the assault
englishExplanation: Sexual assault history: gather info for focused exam + forensics. Leave details leading up to assault to investigating authorities (avoid conflicting statements). Document alcohol/drugs, condom use, gynecologic history.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لمّا تاخد الـhistory من ضحية اعتداء جنسي، المطلوب منك هو المعلومات اللي بتساعدك تعمل فحص focused وتجهّز الـforensic documentation. أمّا تفاصيل اللي صار قبل الاعتداء، بتخليها للجهات اللي بتحقّق، عشان ما يصير عندك statements متعارضة. بس لازم توثّق alcohol وdrugs، وcondom use، والgynecologic history. وهاد معناه إن الـfocused history هو اللي بيساعدك تقرر إيش تفحص بالتفصيل.
الفخ: الخيار A (alcohol use) هو الفخ لأن الكحول وثّقته بتوثّقه بس ما لازم تسأل عن تفاصيل الاعتداء. الخيار D (gynecologic history) غلط لأنه جزء من التوثيق المطلوب توثيقه، واللي بتتركه للجهات هو تفاصيل اللي قبل الاعتداء.

question: After a sexual assault examination is completed, how should the evidence be handled until it can be transferred to police?

options.text: Leave on the charge nurse desk
Store in the emergency department refrigerator

englishExplanation: Chain of custody: evidence kit must remain in kit collector's direct line of sight or locked securely until collected by law enforcement. Failure = inadmissible in court.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بعد ما تخلص فحص الاعتداء، الـevidence kit لازم يضل إما بالخط المباشر لنظرك أو محفوظ بقفل محكم لين ما تيجي الشرطة تاخده. هاد اسمه chain of custody، ولول ما التزمت فيه بتخسر الـkit قيمتها القانونية وما بتقبل بالمحكمة. ولازم ما تتركه بمكتب الممرض ولا بغرفة المريضة أو بالثلاجة، لأن الـdocumentation نفسه جزء من الدليل.
الفخ: الخيار A (leave in the patient's room) هو الفخ لأن أي حدا بيقدر يلمس الـkit وبتخسر الـchain of custody. والخيار D (refrigerator) غلط لأن التبريد ما بيعوّض الحماية، والـkit لازم يكون بمتناول اللي جبّع أو بمكان مقفل.

question: What is the most common complication of prolonged restraint use?
englishExplanation: Restraint complications: abrasions/bruising most common. Death from improper positioning (hog-tie, face-down). Also hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis. Use soft nylon, de-escalation first, sedatives if needed.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: complications اللي بتصير مع التقييد الطويل أكثرها شي انتفاظ و abrasions وكدمات، وهاد أكثر شي بتلاقيه عند المريض. لازم تستخدم soft nylon restraints وتعمل de-escalation أول شي وتستخدم sedatives عند الحاجة. لأن improper positioning زي الـhog-tie أو وضع الوجه على الأرض سبب deaths، والـhyperthermia والـrhabdomyolysis بعد كمان ممكن تصير، خاصة لما الشد يطول والـpatient ما يتحرّك.
الفخ: الخيار B (death) هو الفخ لأن الـdeath مش الأكثر شيوعاً، وبينتج من improper positioning زي الـhog-tie أو حط الوجه على الأرض. الأكثر شيوعاً هو الـabrasions، والـde-escalation قبل الـsedatives بيوصل لنتيجة أحسن.

question: Which finding most suggests delirium as a cause of agitation?
englishExplanation: Delirium: acute onset, waxing/waning, altered awareness/attention. Visual hallucinations (not auditory). Look for life-threatening causes: WHIMPS (Withdrawal, Hypoxia, Intracranial, Metabolic, Poisoning, Seizures).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الخيار لأنه الـ delirium صفاته الأساسية acute onset مع تبديل بالـ awareness والـ attention. يعني الوعي والتركيز بيتبدلوا بسرعة وبيتغيّروا بين وقت وآخر، وهاد بيخلي نرجّح delirium مش شي تاني. ولما نشوف تغيّر مفاجئ بالوعي لازم نكبّر الصورة وندوّر على أسباب خطيرة، وWHIMPS معناها Withdrawal وHypoxia وIntracranial وMetabolic وPoisoning وSeizures، وهاد كله أسباب لازم نعالجها بسرعة.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على auditory hallucinations لأنهم فاكرين أي hallucination بتدل على mental illness. بس بالـ delirium الـ hallucinations الغالبا visual مش auditory. وإذا الـ symptoms gradual وثابتة مع الوقت، هاد ما بيناسب delirium لأنه ببدا acute.

question: A 6-year-old with autism spectrum disorder is brought in for violent behavior. Visibly upset, attempts to strike staff. What is the best next step?

options.text: Have caregiver attempt to soothe child
Speak loudly to gain child's attention

correctAnswer: Have caregiver attempt to soothe child
englishExplanation: Autism: sensory processing issues. Try non-invasive soothing first (caregiver best resource). Avoid restraints (intolerable). Benzodiazepines risk paradoxical reactions. Lower voice volume.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن هاد الطفل عنده autism spectrum disorder، واللي صار إنه بيتbombarded بمشاعر حسية قوية، فأول خطوة لازم تكون soothing غير invasive عن طريق الـ caregiver. الـ caregiver هو أحسن resource لأنه يعرف الـ triggers والـ routines بتاع الطفل، فخلّيه يهدّيه. وبعدها تجنّب الـ four-point restraints لأنها ما بتتحمّلها هالأطفال وبتزيد الـ agitation، والـ benzodiazepines ممكن تعمل paradoxical reactions، وخفّض صوتك بدل ما تصرخ.
الفخ: أكثر خيار بينفّذه الطلاب هو administer benzodiazepines for sedation لأنهم يفتكرون إنه الطفل عنيف ومخدر يهدّيه. بس هاد مش أول خطوة لأن الـ benzodiazepines ممكن تعمل paradoxical reactions، والـ restraints أسوأ. بدّلها: هدّي البيئة والـ caregiver مع خفض الصوت.

question: Autistic children have an elevated risk of having what other concomitant disease?
englishExplanation: Autism comorbidities: epilepsy (11-30% vs 1.2% general), ADHD, GI dysfunction, dental issues, allergies. Also genetic syndromes: fragile X, Down, Angelman.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الأطفال اللي عندهم autism معروف إنهم أعلى خطر يصيبهم epilepsy مقارنة بالأطفال العاديين. الـ prevalence عند أطفال autism بتوصل 11-30% بينما عند عامة الناس بس 1.2%، وكمان في genetic syndromes مرتبطة بـ autism زي fragile X وDown وAngelman وكلها بتزيد خطر الـ seizures. فلما طفل عنده autism بيبدأ يعمل seizures، لازم تفكر بـ epilepsy من أول لحظة.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على ADHD أو الـ GI dysfunction لأنهم شايفين إنهم comorbidities شائعة بـ autism. بس الشي اللي بيسبب seizures هو epilepsy. والـ genetic syndromes زي fragile X وDown هي اللي بترفع الخطر، فمش أي comorbidity بيعمل نفس الشي.

question: A 9-month-old with epilepsy presents in status epilepticus. Multiple admissions for same. Neuroimaging normal. Undetectable antiepileptic medication. Which form of child abuse?
englishExplanation: Medical neglect: caregiver failure to provide medical care/treatment. Most common in children <1 year. Consider family resources/comprehension before assuming intentional harm.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن المشكلة الحقيقية إن أدوية الـ antiepileptic ما كانت موجودة عند الطفل إطلاقاً، وهاد معناه إن الـ caregiver ما وفّر له الرعاية الطبية المطلوبة. وهاد هو تعريف medical neglect بالضبط، وهو أكثر نوع إساءة بينشوف عند الأطفال أقل من سنة. بس قبل ما نفترض إن في قصد سيء من الأهل، لازم نراجع موارد الأسرة وفهمهم للحالة.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على physical abuse أو emotional abuse لأنهم شايفين تكرار الدخول للمشافي وغياب الأدوية. بس الأثر الناقص هو الـ medication نفسه، فهاد failure to provide medical care مش سوء معاملة. وبعدين لازم تفكر بموارد الأسرة قبل ما تحكم على النية.

question: A 6-month-old with 22q11.2 microdeletion (DiGeorge syndrome) presents with seizures. Afebrile. Which electrolyte abnormality should be evaluated?
englishExplanation: DiGeorge syndrome: parathyroid hypoplasia → hypocalcemia + hyperphosphatemia. Presents with seizures, tetany, jitteriness. Measure ionized calcium.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن هاد الطفل عنده 22q11.2 microdeletion يعني DiGeorge syndrome، وهاد الـ syndrome بيصاحبه hypoplasia of the parathyroid glands، ولما الـ parathyroid ما تشتغل كويس بيطلع عنده hypocalcemia مع hyperphosphatemia. والـ hypocalcemia هاد بيسبب seizures وtetany وjitteriness، خصوصاً عند طفل 6 شهور وبدون حرارة. عشان كاد لازم نقيس ionized calcium، وهاد هو الـ electrolyte abnormality اللي لازم تفحصه عند أي طفل فيه syndrome هاد وبيعمل seizures.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على hypophosphatemia لأنهم سمعوا إن الـ phosphate إله علاقة بالـ calcium. بس في DiGeorge الـ phosphate مرتفع مو منخفض، فالـ hyperphosphatemia هي اللي بتمشي مع الـ hypocalcemia. والـ seizures اللي مع tetany بتوجّهك للـ calcium.

question: What consideration should be made when caring for an autistic child in the emergency department?

options.text: Assign room in center of ED

englishExplanation: Autism: minimize stimuli - dim lights, close door, isolate room (away from center), minimize staff. Engage caregivers, use child life specialists.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الطفل الـ autistic بيتbombarded بسرعة بالـ sensory stimuli، وعندنا بالـ ED بيكون كل شي إضاءة وضوضاء وأشخاص حوله. عشان كاد لازم minimize الـ stimuli: تهدّي الإضاءة، تسد الباب، وتخليه بغرفة بعيدة عن وسط الـ ED. وكمان قلّل عدد الـ staff اللي شغالين معاه وادرِج الـ caregivers مع child life specialists، هيك بتقلّل الـ overload اللي بيسبّب السلوك الصعب عنده.
الفخ: بعض الطلاب بيفتكروا إنه الحل إنه تحط الطفل بغرفة وسط الـ ED وتستخدم كثير staff. بس هاد بيزوّد الـ sensory overload والـ overstimulation. الحل إنك تعزله، تهدّي الإضاءة، وتقلّل الإزعاج حواليه.

question: A 68-year-old with lower abdominal pain and distended abdomen, unable to void for 6 hours. US shows enlarged bladder with 250 mL. 14 Fr Foley fails. What catheter next?
englishExplanation: Urethral obstruction (BPH): coudé catheter (semirigid curved tip) passes obstruction. Smaller catheter insufficient. Suprapubic if all else fails + urology unavailable.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن هاد المريض عنده urinary retention مع distended bladder و250 mL بالـ ultrasound، والـ 14 Fr Foley ما قدرت تعدّي. غالباً السبب obstruction بالـ urethra من BPH، والـ Coudé catheter إلها curved tip شبه صلبة بتبحر بالـ blockage. وcatheter أصغر مثل 12 Fr ما بيعاد كافي لأنها أصغر وما رح تعدّي، والـ suprapubic catheter بخيار أخير لو فشل كل شي وurology مش متاح.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على 12-Fr Foley لأنهم فاكرين إنه catheter أصغر أسهل يمر بالـ urethra. بس هاد بيزوّد المشكلة مع الـ obstruction مو بيحلها. والـ suprapubic catheter مش أول خطوة، هي بس آخر حل.

question: A 75-year-old with BPH unable to urinate. Suprapubic catheter placed, 1.2 L output. What is the next best step?

options.text: Observe patient for at least 4 hours

correctAnswer: Observe patient for at least 4 hours
englishExplanation: Postobstructive diuresis risk with >800 mL output: observe 4 hours. If >200 mL/hr → admit for electrolytes + renal function. Otherwise discharge with urology follow-up.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ drainage طلع 1.2 L وهذا كافي إنه يخلق postobstructive diuresis بعد ما شيلنا الـ obstruction، وهاد خطر حقيقي على الـ kidney. فالمطلوب نراقب المريض أربع ساعات على الأقل ونقيس الـ urine output. إذا الـ output تجاوز 200 mL في الساعة لازم ندخله للـ admission ونعمل electrolytes وrenal function، أما إذا ظل أقل من هيك بيصير discharge مع urology follow-up.
الفخ: خيارات الـ hospital admission والـ emergent urology consultation بتبان أذكى، بس مش دلوقتي. أول thing تراقب الـ urine output بعد الـ drainage. إذا تجاوز 200 mL/hr بتدخل، أما لأ بتخرج مع متابعة urology.

question: When obtaining a cystourethrogram in an adult patient with pelvic trauma, what volume of contrast medium must be instilled into the bladder to prevent a false-negative evaluation?
englishExplanation: Cystography: 400 mL contrast to prevent false-negative. Indications: penetrating trauma, inability to void, blood at meatus, scrotal hematoma, unstable pelvic fracture, high-riding prostate. Retrograde urethrogram FIRST.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ cystography بتحتاج contrast كافي يملا الـ bladder ويعطي visualization واضحة لجدار الـ bladder. حجم 400 mL هو اللي بيمنع false-negative، لأنه إذا ما في كفاية الـ bladder ما بين-distended ولا بيظهر الـ leak. الـ indications للـ cystography: penetrating trauma، inability to void، blood at meatus، scrotal hematoma، unstable pelvic fracture، وhigh-riding prostate، وكمان لازم retrograde urethrogram FIRST قبل أي شي.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على 200 mL لأنه رقم وسط ومنطقي. بس القليل ما بيعمل distension كافي وبيرجعلك false-negative. وكمان لا تنسى retrograde urethrogram FIRST إذا في اشتباه injury بالـ urethra.

question: An 18-year-old with testicular pain after bicycle riding. US shows no blood flow to right testicle. What is the correct initial technique?

options.text: Laterally rotate the patient's left testicle
Laterally rotate the patient's right testicle
Medially rotate the patient's left testicle
Medially rotate the patient's right testicle

correctAnswer: Laterally rotate the patient's right testicle
englishExplanation: Testicular torsion (right): manual detorsion - laterally/externally rotate (counterclockwise facing patient's head). 'Opening a book' technique. Most twist medially. If pain worsens → opposite direction.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ ultrasound ما أظهر blood flow بالـ right testicle وهاد strongly suggests testicular torsion، وهي حالة emergency لازم ترجّع الـ blood flow بسرعة. الـ manual detorsion بتعملها بـ rotating the testicle laterally يعني خارجياً، باتجاه counterclockwise إذا كنت واقف faced patient، وهاي التقنية سميتها opening a book technique. ولاحظ إن أغلب الـ torsions بتكون medially، بس الـ detorsion بتتم بالاتجاه المعاكس للـ twist.
الفخ: الفخ إن الطلاب بيروحوا على medially rotate للـ right testicle لأنهم سمعوا إن أغلب الـ torsions medially. بس الـ detorsion معناها الفك عكس الـ twist، وهاد بسير laterally على اليمين. وإذا الألم زاد أثناء المحاولة، تبدّل الاتجاه فوراً.

question: Terrorist attack with unknown chemical powder. Patients arrive with respiratory symptoms. What should be the first step?

options.text: Restrict ED entrance until the chemical is identified

englishExplanation: Unknown chemical powder: gross decontamination - remove clothing, brush off powder, soap and warm water. Ideally outside ED. Avoid diluted bleach (harmful). Disperse gas may not require decon.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن هاد unknown chemical powder، وأول خطوة لازم تكون gross decontamination: تشيل كل الملابس المتأثرة وتنفض البودرة عن الجسم. وبعدها تستعمل soap وماء دافئ، والأفضل إن هاد كله يصير برّا الـ ED قبل ما تدخل المنطقة. diluted bleach ما بنصح فيها لأنها بكون harmful على المريض، أما إذا تبيّن إن المادة gas فممكن ما تحتاج decontamination أصلاً.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على decontaminate with diluted bleach أو rapid sequence intubation لأنهم شايفين patients عندهم respiratory symptoms. بس الـ bleach بيعمل ضرر، والـ intubation مش أول خطوة. شيل الملابس وانفض البودرة وإلا بـ soap وماء دافئ.

question: Which characteristic would be considered abnormal in a patient undergoing an ultrasound for abdominal pain?
englishExplanation:
Normal gallbladder wall <3 mm (any age). CBD <7 mm until age 70 (+1 mm/decade after). Wall >3 mm = cholecystitis concern.

Review notes: ["html_markup_or_entities"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ normal thickness of the gallbladder wall أقل من 3 mm مهما كان عمر المريض، يعني 4.3 mm عند شخص 50 سنة هاد abnormal وبيعطي concern بـ cholecystitis. أما الـ common bile duct فيبقى أقل من 7 mm لحد عمر 70، وبعدين يزيد 1 mm لكل decade، فـ 7.6 mm عند شخص 80 سنة هاد طبيعي. وسمك الـ wall 2.8 mm عند طفل 6 سنين هاد كمان طبيعي.
الفخ: إنك تحكم على الـ common bile duct 7.6 mm عند شخص 80 سنة إنه abnormal، لأن الـ CBD بيزيد 1 mm لكل decade بعد الـ 70. 2.8 mm عند طفل 6 سنين رقم طبيعي. المعيار المعتمد لكل الأعمار هو 3 mm لسمك الـ wall.

question: A 29-year-old after rollover MVC. FAST shows anechoic fluid above the diaphragm. How should these results be interpreted?
englishExplanation: FAST: anechoic fluid above diaphragm = hemothorax. Below diaphragm (Morison pouch) = hemoperitoneum. Pericardium = around heart.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ FAST كشف سائل anechoic فوق الـ diaphragm، وهاد معناه إن فيه hemothorax أي دم متجمع بالـ pleural space. الـ location هو اللي بيحدد كل شي: تحت الـ diaphragm في Morison pouch يعني hemoperitoneum، وحوالين القلب يعني hemopericardium. فلما تشوف fluid فوق الـ diaphragm لازم تفكر bleed داخلي مش fluid تاني، وبعد الـ MVC هاد لازم ينفعال بسرعة.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على hemoperitoneum أو hemopericardium لأنهم فاكرين إن أي سائل بالـ FAST يعني نزيف داخل البطن. بس hemoperitoneum بيبان تحت الـ diaphragm في Morison pouch. السائل فوق الـ diaphragm يعني hemothorax.

question: According to the principles of ALARA (as low as reasonably achievable), which ultrasound function has the highest risk of potential harm?

options.text: B-mode ocular ultrasound on ocular preset

englishExplanation: ALARA: Doppler on early fetus highest risk (thermal injury to sensitive tissue). Avoid Doppler on fetus/eye. B-mode with ocular preset is negligible. Thermal index (TI) and mechanical index (MI) indicate risk.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن مبدأ ALARA يعني إننا نعمل الـ ultrasound بأقل ضرر ممكن، والسؤال سؤال عن أعلى خطر. الـ Doppler على fetus بيسبب thermal injury لأن نسيج الجنين حساس، وهاد أعلى خطورة بين كل الخيارات. عشان كاد ما بنعمل Doppler على fetus ولا على الـ eye. أما B-mode مع ocular preset فالخطر فيه negligible. والـ risk level بيتبين بـ thermal index وmechanical index.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على ultrasound of the lung أو B-mode ocular ultrasound لأنهم شايفينها اختبارات عادية. بس الـ Doppler على الجنين هو اللي بيعمل thermal injury. أما الـ B-mode مع ocular preset ما بتسبب ضرر يُذكر.

question: A 78-year-old with severe abdominal pain. POCUS of the abdominal aorta shows contained pseudoaneurysm and dissection flap. What is the next best step?

options.text: Admit to ICU for anti-impulse therapy
Obtain CT angiography of the aorta

englishExplanation: Ruptured AAA with pseudoaneurysm + dissection: emergent vascular surgery. POCUS 95-100% sens for AAA. Anti-impulse therapy for type B dissection (BP <120/80, P <60). REBOA contraindicated in dissection.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ POCUS طلع pseudoaneurysm contained مع dissection flap، وهاد يعني ruptured AAA، والحالة emergency لازم تنادي vascular surgery على طول. الـ POCUS حساسته بتوصل 95-100% لـ AAA، فما في داعي تأخر. الـ anti-impulse therapy بتنفع مع type B dissection وبتخلّي الـ BP تحت 120/80 والـ pulse تحت 60، بس هي مو الحل. والـ REBOA ممنوعة مع الـ dissection.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على CT angiography أو ICU مع anti-impulse therapy لأنهم يفتكروا لازم تصوّر أو تستقرّب المريض أولاً. بس الـ dissection وهو موجود أصلاً، فالـ CT مو أول خطوة والـ REBOA contraindicated. الحل تنادي vascular surgery emergently.

question: An 87-year-old with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. POCUS shows dilated bowel loops with retrograde peristalsis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation: SBO on POCUS: dilated loops (>25 mm) + abnormal peristalsis (to-and-fro). 88% sensitive, 54% specific. No radiation or contrast needed.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ POCUS طلع dilated bowel loops مع retrograde peristalsis، وهاد pattern بيعني SBO. الـ SBO على POCUS حساسيته 88% وspecificity 54%، وما بتحتاج radiation ولا contrast عشان توصل لهاد التشخيص. والـ appendicitis وcholecystitis وdiverticulitis بتمرض هما بيألم وبيتقيّأ، بس هما مش بالشكل هاد من dilated loops مع abnormal peristalsis، ولما الـ loops تكون أكبر من 25 mm بهاد الـ peristalsis فالتشخيص بيسهل.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على appendicitis أو cholecystitis لأن المريض عنده nausea وvomiting وabdominal pain وهاد symptoms عامة. بس اللي بيحسم هو dilated loops مع abnormal to-and-fro peristalsis، وهاد مش inflammation.

question: FAST examination shows fluid in Morison's pouch. What is the minimal amount of free fluid present in the abdomen?
englishExplanation: FAST minimal detectable fluid: 200 mL (avg 600 mL for RUQ positive). Trendelenburg for RUQ/LUQ, reverse for pelvic. Repeat FAST if high suspicion with negative initial.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن أقل amount of free fluid الـ FAST بيقدر يكتشفه هو 200 mL، يعني أي fluid تشوفه بـ Morison pouch لازم يكون 200 mL أو أكثر. وبـ right upper quadrant الـ averagePositive output بيوصل 600 mL. ولما تشك بـ bleed والـ FAST طلع negative، اعمل Trendelenburg للـ RUQ وLUQ وعكسها للـ pelvic، وكرر الـ FAST إذا لزم.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على 0 mL أو 50 mL لأنهم فاكرين الـ fluid لازم يكون كتير عشان يبان. بس حساسية الـ FAST معناها إنه بيكشف حتى 200 mL. أما 600 mL فهو averagePositive output للـ RUQ مش الحد الأدنى.

question: A 26-year-old pregnant woman with vaginal spotting. POCUS shows fetal pole with complex free fluid outside uterus. What is the best next step?

options.text: Consult OB emergently; ectopic pregnancy identified
Follow-up in 48 hours for repeat beta quant; gestational sac identified

correctAnswer: Consult OB emergently; ectopic pregnancy identified
englishExplanation: Ectopic pregnancy: fetal pole/heart tones OUTSIDE uterus. Free fluid = ruptured ectopic - surgical emergency. 4-10% of maternal deaths. IUP nearly excludes ectopic (except IVF).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ POCUS طلع fetal pole مع complex free fluid برّا الـ uterus، وهاد معناه إن هاد ectopic pregnancy. ووجود الـ free fluid يعني إن الـ ectopic انفجرت، وهاد surgical emergency لازم تتصل بـ OB فوراً. الـ ectopic pregnancy سبب 4-10% من وفيات الأمهات، عشان كاد التأخير خطر. أما الـ IUP nearly بستبعد الـ ectopic إلا في حالات الـ IVF.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على follow-up في 48 ساعة أو manage expectantly لأنهم شافوا gestational sac. بس لو في IUP بتستبعد الـ ectopic، فوجود fluid معقدة برّا الرحم مع fetal pole يعني ectopic ruptured. لا تأجل عليه.

question: An 80-year-old with urinary retention. POCUS of bladder shows width and height but length not properly measured. What is the best approximation of bladder volume?
englishExplanation: Bladder volume = length × width × height × coefficient (0.52 spherical most accurate; 0.72 most common). Must have all 3 dimensions. Height measured twice here - length missing.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن معادلة حجم الـ bladder بتحتاج الثلاثة dimensions: length وwidth وheight، ومعامل يضرب فيهم. وهاي الـ ultrasound ما قاس الـ length صح، بل قاس الـ height مرتين، يعني المعطيات ناقصة وما بنقدر نحسب الـ volume. الـ coefficient 0.52 هو الأدق لما الـ bladder شكله spherical، و0.72 هو الأكثر استخداماً، بس حتى بدون ما تعرف الـ coefficients لازم يكون عندك الأبعاد الثلاثة كلها.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تاخد رقمين من الـ image وتحسب، أو إنك تفترض إن 0.72 هي الصح لأنها الأكثر شيوعاً. بس الـ length ناقصة، و0.52 هي الأدق. ارجع قيس الأبعاد الثلاثة قبل ما تحسب.

question: An 86-year-old with tachycardia, hypotension, and erythematous swollen leg. POCUS shows gas and fluid in soft tissue. What is the best course for definitive treatment?

options.text: Surgery consultation for emergent operative intervention

correctAnswer: Surgery consultation for emergent operative intervention
englishExplanation: Necrotizing fasciitis on POCUS: subcutaneous gas (hyperechoic specks with posterior shadowing) + fluid. Surgical emergency. Antibiotics alone insufficient. Cellulitis = cobblestoning. Abscess = hypoechoic collection.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ POCUS طلع gas وfluid بالـ soft tissue، ومع tachycardia وhypotension وساق حمراء ومتورمة، هاد necrotizing fasciitis. الـ gas بتبان كنقاط hyperechoic مع posterior shadowing، وهاد surgical emergency. والمضادات الحيوية لوحدها ما بتكفي أبداً، لأن الـ definitive treatment هو عملية فورية من غير تأخير، والـ bedside incision and drainage بكسل هاد الـ necrotizing fasciitis، أما الـ cellulitis بتبان cobblestoning والـ abscess collection hypoechoic.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على broad-spectrum antibiotics وICU admission لأن المريض عنده sepsis. بس الـ antibiotics لوحدها مش علاج definitive بـ necrotizing fasciitis، الحل عملية. والـ cellulitis بتبان cobblestoning والـ abscess collection hypoechoic، مو gas.

question: A patient with erythematous swollen painful knee. POCUS of knee shows effusion. What is the best next course of action?
englishExplanation: Red, hot, swollen knee with effusion → arthrocentesis to rule out septic joint. POCUS: linear probe sagittal anterior/superior to patella. Fluid deep to quadriceps tendon.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن عندك knee حمراء وساخنة ومتورمة ومؤلمة، وفيها effusion، وهاد لازم تستبعد فيه septic joint. أحسن خطوة هي diagnostic arthrocentesis وتطلع السائل للفحص. وبـ POCUS بتستخدم linear probe بالسهم sagittal فوق patella من قدام، والسائل بيطلع deep to the quadriceps tendon، ولما الـ effusion مع inflammation لازم تفحص السائل أول شي مش تصوّر.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على CT أو MRI للـ knee لأنهم فاكرين إن الـ imaging بيساعد يحدد السبب. بس الـ effusion مع الاحمرار والسخونة لازم تفحص السائل أول شي. الـ imaging ما بتغني عن arthrocentesis.

question: POCUS of arm for ultrasound-guided IV. Arrow points to thin-walled, nonpulsatile, collapsible structure. Cannulation will result in which outcome?
englishExplanation: Vein: thin-walled, nonpulsatile, collapsible, larger than artery. Artery: thicker wall, pulsatile, noncompressible. Nerve: hyperechoic honeycomb. Bone: hyperechoic line with posterior shadow.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الصفات اللي وصفتها: thin-walled وnonpulsatile وcollapsible، وهاي كلها صفات الـ vein. الـ artery عندها جدار أسمك وpulsatile وnoncompressible، والـ vein كمان أكبر من الـ artery، بينما الـ nerve بتظهر كـ honeycomb hyperechoic والـ bone كخط hyperechoic مع posterior shadowing. وعليه لازم تتوقع venous blood return، والمهم إنك تفرق بين الـ pulsatility والـ compressibility قبل ما تحط الـ needle.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تخلط بين الـ vein والـ artery. الـ bright red pulsatile blood return يعني إنك داخل الـ artery وهاد خطر. انتبه للـ pulsatility والـ compressibility: الـ collapsible يعني vein.

question: An emergent IJ central line. POCUS shows lung point. What is the best next step?

options.text: No action is necessary; a central line is acceptable to use
Remove and replace the central line
Vascular surgery consultation for carotid injury

englishExplanation: Lung point = pneumothorax (diagnostic). POCUS central line protocol: visualise wire in vein, flush in RA, lung sliding to exclude PTX. Lung point = PTX → chest tube.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ lung point اللي ظهر بالـ POCUS معناه pneumothorax، وهاد diagnostic. ولما تحط central line لازم تتأكد إن الـ wire داخل الـ vein، وإن الـ flush وصل للـ right atrium، وبعدين تتأكد من الـ lung sliding عشان تستبعد الـ pneumothorax. ولما الـ lung point موجود، هاد بيعني إن عندك pneumothorax، فالخطوة الجاية هي chest tube.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على central line تانية أو vascular surgery لأنهم شايفين إن المشكلة بالخط نفسه. بس الـ lung point معناه pneumothorax وهاد لازم chest tube emergently. تغيير الـ central line ما بيعالج السبب.

question: When attempting to place an ultrasound-guided IV, which location is the best target?
englishExplanation: Best vein for US-guided IV: thin wall + collapsible + shallow (0.3-1.4 cm) + >0.4 cm diameter + away from arteries/nerves. 'B' is an artery. 'A' and 'C' smaller or deeper.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن أحسن vein للـ ultrasound-guided IV لازم يكون thin wall وcollapsible، وقريب من السطح بين 0.3 و1.4 cm، وقطره أكثر من 0.4 cm، بعيد عن الـ arteries والـ nerves. و'D' هي اللي بتجمع هاد الشروط، أما 'B' فهي artery و'A' و'C' أصغر أو أعمق فما بنعدّيهم بسهولة. لازم تختار الوعاء اللي بيسهل تدخل فيه وتقدر تعمل cannulation بأقل trauma.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار 'B' لأنه أكبر وواضح على الصورة. بس 'B' artery، واللي بتدخله فيه ممكن يصير extravasation أو ضرر للـ vessel. 'A' و'C' أصغر أو أعمق، فراجع الـ depth والـ diameter قبل ما تختار.

question: During CPR, TEE shows compressions over the LVOT. What is the best next step?
englishExplanation: TEE during CPR: compressions over LVOT → obstruction. Reposition for more effective compressions. TEE advantages: better window, no interruption, detects fine VF masquerading as asystole.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن الـ TEE أثناء الـ CPR بيبيّن إن الـ compressions صارت فوق الـ LVOT، وهاد بيعطّل الـ blood flow بدل ما يوزّعه. الحل إنك تغيّر موقع الـ compressions عشان تضغط بشكل أكثر فعالية. والـ TEE من advantages إنه بيوفر نافذة أحسن بدون ما توقف الـ compressions أو تضيع أي ثانية، وبيقدر يكشف fine VF بيتشبه asystole.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على cease resuscitation أو perform defibrillation لأنهم شافوا إن الـ output ضعيف. بس المشكلة بموقع الضغط فوق الـ LVOT مو بالـ rhythm نفسه. وفيه احتمال الـ asystole هو fine VF، فالتشخيص لازم يكون واضح قبل ما تقرر.

question: A hypotensive patient. RUSH examination shows lung point. What is the best next step?
englishExplanation: Lung point = pneumothorax (likely tension given hypotension). Immediate needle decompression. RUSH mnemonic HI-MAP (heart, IVC, Morison, aorta, pneumothorax).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها hypotension، وفحص الـ RUSH طلع عندها lung point، وهاد بحد ذاته دليل على pneumothorax، ومع وجود hypotension الغالب إنه tension pneumothorax. السبب إن ضغط الـ air بالـ pleural space بيمنع الرجوع الوريدي للقلب فبينزل الـ cardiac output وبيصير shock صادم. ولهذا السبب لازم تعمل needle chest decompression فورًا، لأنها بتفك الضغط وبترجّع الـ venous return، وأي تأخير أو علاج للـ shock بس بدون فك الضغط ما بيعالج السبب.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار initiate fluid bolus أو inotrope لأن المريضة عندها hypotension، بس هاد بيعالج عرض مش السبب. الـ fluid bolus ما بيرفع الضغط لأن الـ pleural pressure واقف، والـ inotrope بيزيد الـ workload بلا فايدة. افحص وبتشوف lung point، وروح للـ decompression.

question: An unstable stab wound patient. eFAST shows fluid around the heart. What is the best next step?
englishExplanation: Traumatic pericardial tamponade in unstable patient: thoracotomy (not pericardiocentesis - only temporizing). Penetrating chest trauma + tamponade = surgical emergency. Fluid anterior to descending aorta = pericardial.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها unstable مع طعنة، والـ eFAST طلع عندها fluid حوالين القلب، وهاد معناه traumatic pericardial tamponade. الـ fluid اللي قدام الـ descending aorta هو اللي بيفرّق وبينه وبين الـ hemothorax، وبيأكد إن السوائل pericardial. لازم تعمل thoracotomy فورًا لأنه هاد طعنة في الصدر مع tamponade، يعني حالة جراحية طارئة وبالنزيف كل دقيقة بتزيد الخطر. الـ pericardiocentesis بيعمل drainage مؤقت بس ما بيعالج المصدر.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار pericardiocentesis لأنها سريعة وبتعمل drain لل fluid، أو chest tube لأنك شايف سوائل. بس الـ pericardiocentesis بس temporizing للمريض غير المستقر، والـ chest tube ما بتحل tamponade القلبي إطلاقًا.

question: Which technique should be attempted first to remove a nasal foreign body without the use of restraints in a young pediatric patient?
englishExplanation: 'Parent's kiss': ~80% effective, no restraints. Parent occludes nonaffected nostril + blows into patient's mouth. Then BVM positive pressure, forceps, catheter balloon. ENT if fails.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد أول شي لازم تجربه لإزالة جسم غريب من الأنف عند طفل صغير، وبدون ما تحتاج restraints. الـ Parent's kiss بينجح بحوالي 80% من الحالات، وبيتم من غير أي تقييد للطفل. الطريقة إن الوالد يسد الـ nostril السليم وي blow في فم الطفل، وبهيك القوة بتطلع الجسم الغريب. بس إذا ما نجح هالشي، بتنتقل للـ BVM positive pressure وبعدها forceps وبعدها catheter balloon، وإذا كل هالشي فشل لازم تدخل ENT.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تبدأ بـ back blows أو BVM على طول، وهاد غلط لأن الـ back blows مش technique لإخراج جسم غريب من الأنف، والـ BVM بيجي بعد ما الـ Parent's kiss يفشل. الـ forceps كمان ما تبدأ فيها مباشرة.

question: A woman with laceration to plantar foot. Swollen erythematous area. Bedside US shows hyperechoic structure in subcutaneous tissue. What is the best interpretation?
englishExplanation: Retained foreign body: hyperechoic structure + posterior shadowing. US more sensitive than x-ray for wood/nonmetallic FB. Attempt removal if superficial; antibiotics if infection.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في laceration بقدم الرجل وكتلة منتفخة وحمرانة، والـ bedside ultrasound طلع فيه structure hyperechoic داخل الأنسجة تحت الجلد. هاد معناه retained foreign body، لأن الـ ultrasound أذكى من الـ x-ray لما يكون الجسم خشبي أو غير معدني، والـ hyperechoic مع posterior shadowing بيلفت عليه. لازم تحاول تشيله لو كان superficial، وتبدأ antibiotics لو في inflammation أو infection.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار cellulitis with abscess أو necrotizing fasciitis، بس الـ ultrasound لو ما طلع فيه أي body، ما في دليل على أي منهم. كمان normal soft tissue ultrasound ما ينفع، لأنه طلع عندك structure hyperechoic.

question: A medical student has developed a new blood test. 100 patients: 80 in pain, 20 pain-free. 60 with pain positive, 20 negative. 10 without pain positive. What is the sensitivity?
englishExplanation:
Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN) = 60/80 = 0.75 (75%). Specificity = TN/(FP+TN) = 10/20 = 0.50. PPV = 60/70 = 0.86. NPV = 10/30 = 0.33.

---

# SOURCE BOOK: PEER-Case-Series-2026 — 2 questions
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ sensitivity هي احتمال إن الفحص يطلع positive عند الناس اللي عندهم المرض فعلًا، وبتحسبها TP مقسوم على TP + FN. هون 80 مريض عندهم ألم، و 60 منهم طلع عندهم الفحص positive، يعني 20 FN. عشان كذا الـ sensitivity = 60/80 = 0.75، يعني 75%. الـ other options هي الأرقام الثانية: 0.5 هي specificity و 0.86 هي PPV و 0.33 هي NPV.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار 0.86 أو 0.5 لأنهم بيوصلوا ترتيب طبيعي، بس 0.86 هي PPV و 0.5 هي specificity. تذكّر: الـ sensitivity بتقيس بين مرضى الفحص positive، والـ specificity بين الأصحاء.

question: An academic ED that primarily cares for adults with pediatric hospital nearby. How should this ED best prepare to care for pediatric patients?

options.text: Hire a pediatric hospitalist to care for all pediatric patients
Limit staff education on pediatric management
Review pediatric treatment protocols every 10 years

englishExplanation: The National Pediatric Readiness Project (PRP) ensures all hospitals that care for children are ready to provide high-quality pediatric emergency care. 70% of pediatric visits take place at EDs with few pediatric patients. Focus on staff education, protocols, and pediatric-dosed medications/equipment.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: 70% من زيارات الأطفال بتصير في EDs ما إلها إلا كم طفل، وهاد الـ ED أصلاً بيتعامل مع بالغين. من هالسبب لازم يكون جاهز إنه يعالج الأطفال بإتقان، وهاد بالضبط هدف الـ National Pediatric Readiness Project اللي بيضمن إن كل مستشفى بيعالج أطفال جاهز يعطي رعاية طوارئ أطفال عالية الجودة. فالتركيز لازم يكون على تعليم الموظفين و وضع protocols و توفير أدوية و أجهزة بجرعات الأطفال. و crash cart مخصص للأطفال بيخليك جاهز بعد لحظات بدون ما تبحث.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار hire a pediatric hospitalist أو limit staff education. توظيف شخص واحد ما بيغطي زيارات الأطفال اللي بتصير بـ EDs بشكل عام، وتقليل التعليم بيزيد الخطر. و مراجعة الـ protocols كل 10 سنين يعني تسيب شي outdated لسنوات.

question: A patient presents with severe sepsis. Based on CMS core measures, which finding meets the definition of septic shock?

options.text: BP 70/50 after 30 mL/kg of lactated Ringer
Lactate >2 mmol/L after 20 mL/kg of normal saline
Lactate >3 mmol/L prior to any fluid administration
P >120 bpm after 1 L of normal saline

correctAnswer: BP 70/50 after 30 mL/kg of lactated Ringer
englishExplanation:
CMS defines septic shock as severe sepsis plus persistent hypotension after 30 mL/kg crystalloid resuscitation OR lactate ≥4 mmol/L. CMS criteria must be met for reimbursement. Lactate >2 but <4 is 'severe sepsis' not 'septic shock'.

---

# SOURCE BOOK: PreTest-5e — 23 questions
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ CMS بتعرّف septic shock على إنها severe sepsis مع persistent hypotension بعد ما تعطي 30 mL/kg من crystalloid، أو lactate 4 mmol/L أو أعلى. هون المريض تعامل مع 30 mL/kg من lactated Ringer وفضل عنده BP 70/50، يعني لسه ما استجاب للسوائل. هاد بالضبط تعريف الـ CMS، والمهم إنه لازم تطبق المعايير لأنها شرط للتعويض. الـ lactate 2-3 بيعتبر severe sepsis بس مش septic shock.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار lactate >2 أو lactate >3 أو P >120. الـ lactate >2 أقل من 4 يعني severe sepsis مش septic shock، والـ lactate قبل أي سوائل ما بيعمل معيار CMS. و الـ tachycardia بعد لتر سالين مش criterion.

question:
You are a passenger aboard an airplane when a 78-year-old woman
starts complaining of chest pain and difficulty breathing. You are the only
medical professional available and volunteer to help. Fortunately, the
aircraft is well-equipped with basic medical equipment, advanced cardiac
life support (ACLS) medications, and a cardiac monitor. On examination,
the passenger’s BP is 75/40 mm Hg, HR is 180 beats/minute, and RR is 24
breaths/min. On examination, the patient is in obvious distress, but able to
answer basic questions. Her heart is tachycardic, regular, and without
murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Physical examination is remarkable for a
bounding carotid pulse. You attach the cardiac monitor and see a regular

rhythm at 180 beats/min with wide QRS complexes and no obvious P
waves. After asking the pilot to make an emergency landing, what is the
most appropriate next step?
englishExplanation:
141.  The answer is b. The patient is in ventricular tachycardia (VT), a
wide complex tachycardia. VT originates from ectopic ventricular
pacemakers and is usually a regular rhythm with a rate greater than 100

beats/min and wide QRS complexes. Treatment of VT is primarily
dependent on whether or not the patient is stable. Evidence of acute altered
mental status, hypotension, continued chest pain, or other signs of shock are
signs of instability. Unstable patients, such as the passenger on this
airplane, should receive immediate synchronized cardioversion. It is
critical that the cardioverter be placed in the synchronized mode, which
permits a search for a large R wave and a corresponding shock around the
incidence of such a wave. A shock administered outside of this constraint
can induce ventricular fibrillation (VF).
Stable patients can be treated with antidysrhythmics. Amiodarone (a)
lidocaine, (d) and procainamide (e) can all be administered. Verapamil (c)
should not be used in VT as it may accelerate the HR and cause
hypotension.

![PreTest-5e-00141 source page 151](images/PreTest-5e-00141-PreTest-5e-p0151.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00141 source page 152](images/PreTest-5e-00141-PreTest-5e-p0152.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00141 source page 189](images/PreTest-5e-00141-PreTest-5e-p0189.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00141 source page 190](images/PreTest-5e-00141-PreTest-5e-p0190.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ monitor طلع منتظم عند 180 beat/min مع QRS complexes عريضة وبلا P waves واضحة، وهاد ventricular tachycardia. المريضة عندها BP 75/40 مع chest pain، وهاد علامات instability واضحة. في الـ VT treatment بيعتمد على stability المريض: الـ unstable بيعملوا synchronized cardioversion فورًا، والـ device لازم يكون بالـ synchronized mode عشان يدوّر على R wave كبيرة ويصدم حواليها. صدمة برا هالشرط ممكن تحوّل الـ rhythm لـ VF. أما المريض المستقر فيعالج بأدوية مثل amiodarone أو lidocaine أو procainamide.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تعطي IV amiodarone أو IV lidocaine أو procainamide، وهاد أدوية الـ stable مرضى. و verapamil خطر لأنه ممكن يرفع الـ HR ويسبّب hypotension عند مرضى VT.

question:
Shared scenario:
You are on duty in the emergency department (ED) when you are notified
that an explosion and mass casualty event has occurred. The first patient, an
approximately 30-year-old man, arrives poorly responsive and confused. He
is sweating profusely and vomiting, with an episode of diarrhea. Vital signs
include a blood pressure of 170/90 mm Hg, respiratory rate (RR) of 22
breaths/minute, heart rate (HR) of 55 beats/minute, temperature 37.0°C, and
pulse oximetry 93% on room air. He requires frequent suctioning of his
airway. His pupils are pinpoint and he has prominent rales on lung exam.

191.   After you clear and control the patient’s airway, what is the most
appropriate initial pharmacologic therapy?
englishExplanation:
191.  The answer is a. The patient was exposed to an organophosphate.
Organophosphates inhibit acetylcholinesterase, the enzyme responsible
for the breakdown of acetylcholine. The patient is having a “cholinergic
crisis.” Overstimulation of muscarinic and nicotinic receptors leads to his
symptoms, commonly remembered by the mnemonics SLUDGE
[salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, gastrointestinal (GI) upset,
emesis] or DUMBBELS (defecation, urination, miosis, bronchospasm,
bronchorrhea, emesis, lacrimation, salivation). The initial pharmacologic
treatment for organophosphate toxicity is to administer atropine until the
patient no longer has significant secretions and the mucous membranes
appear slightly dry. Atropine is an anticholinergic; therefore, it
competitively inhibits the excess acetylcholine, both peripherally and in the
central nervous system (CNS).
Flumazenil (b) is a mixed agonist/antagonist that can be used to reverse
benzodiazepine effects. Due to a risk of seizures and limited benefit, it is
used infrequently. Methylene blue (c) is used to reverse
methemoglobinemia. Naloxone (d) is used to reverse opiate (eg, heroin)
overdoses. Sodium bicarbonate (e) has a number of uses in overdose, but is
primary used to treat the cardiac effects of tricyclic antidepressant (TCA)
overdose and to enhance the elimination of aspirin through urinary
alkalization.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: العرض اللي عند هاد المريض بيضل organophosphate poisoning، يعني cholinergic crisis. من الـ marker الـ SLUDGE و DUMBBELS: salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, GI upset, emesis، ومعه miosis, bronchospasm, bronchorrhea. الـ organophosphate بتثبّط acetylcholinesterase فبيصير overstimulation لمستقبلات muscarinic و nicotinic، ولهذا لحاله طالع sweats و vomiting و diarrhea و bradycardia مع pinpoint pupils. العلاج الأول هو atropine لحد ما توقّف الـ secretions الكثيرة وتبقى الـ mucous membranes شوي ناشفة.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار naloxone أو flumazenil أو methylene blue. الـ naloxone للـ opiate overdose، والـ flumazenil للـ benzodiazepines، والـ methylene blue للـ methemoglobinemia، و sodium bicarbonate أساسية للـ TCA overdose.

question:
Shared scenario:
During an emergency medical services (EMS) ride along, your team
receives a call for multiple injured patients after an explosion at a city
building. When you arrive at the scene, there is an incident commander (IC)
who instructs you that there are dozens of injured casualties and delegates
you to help triage the wounded according to the simple triage and rapid
treatment (START) system. You are directed to a secure area where the fire
department EMS has brought dozens of injured office workers. You
approach a patient who has several abrasions on his torso, face, and
extremities. He has no spontaneous respirations. You perform a chin lift and
note chest wall movement and audible spontaneous respirations.

481.   What color triage tag would you assign this patient?
englishExplanation:
481.  The answer is c. In mass-casualty incidents, one of the most vital
components of triage is to assign the appropriate acuity level of injury in
an easy to implement, standardized, and efficient manner. The most widely
used triage system is the START system that focuses on assessing three
parameters. These are as follows:
1.   Respirations
2.   Perfusion
3.   Mental status
Patients are assessed based on these three parameters and then assigned
a colored triage tag corresponding to one of the following triage categories:
Immediate: immediate care and transfer necessary
Delayed: delayed transfer and care until all “reds” are cleared
Minor: “walking wounded” and lowest priority to transfer
Deceased: dead at the scene from nonsurvivable injuries
Patients who are wounded but are able to walk on scene are given a
green tag (a) signifying a low priority and are attended to or transferred last.
Next, patients are assessed for ability to breathe. If they are not breathing,
the airway is positioned. If breathing resumes, they are labeled “red” (c) as
depicted in the previously mentioned example. If no spontaneous breathing
resumes, they are labeled “black” (e). If they are breathing spontaneously
and have an RR greater than 30 breaths/minute, they are assigned a red tag
(c). In patients with a spontaneous RR below 30 breaths/minute, next their
perfusion is assessed by checking a radial pulse and capillary refill. If there
is no radial pulse or if the capillary refill is greater than 2 seconds, they are
assigned a red tag (c). For those with a radial pulse or capillary refill under

2 seconds, the next step is a brief mental status examination in which they
are asked to follow simple commands (eg, squeeze the examiner’s hand). If
they cannot do this, they are given a red tag (c). However, if they can follow
simple commands, they are given a yellow tag (b). There is no blue tag (d)
in the START system. The following image is an example of a START
Triage tag, sometimes used by EMS services to designate a patient’s triage
category.

![PreTest-5e-00481 source page 621](images/PreTest-5e-00481-PreTest-5e-p0621.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00481 source page 630](images/PreTest-5e-00481-PreTest-5e-p0630.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00481 source page 631](images/PreTest-5e-00481-PreTest-5e-p0631.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد نظام START للـ mass casualty، وبيقيّم ثلاث حاجات: respirations و perfusion و mental status. هالمريض ما عنده spontaneous respirations، فـ أول شي بتعمله airway positioning. لما رجع عنده تنفس و chest wall movement، بيتصنّف على أساس إنه breathing، وهاد بيعطيه tag أحمر يعني immediate care و transfer ضروري. و patients اللي بيمشوا على رجليهم بياخذوا green tag وآخر واحد بيننقل، وإذا ما رجع التنفس بياخد black.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تعطي green tag لأنه wounds بت superficial، بس green يعني walking wounded والمريض هذا ما بيمشي. والـ black بيكون لو ما رجع عنده تنفس بعد positioning الـ airway، وهنا التنفس رجع.

question:
While working in the emergency department (ED), you receive a
medical control radio call from EMS regarding a 38-year-old woman who
developed acute severe respiratory distress while eating a peanut-based dish
at a local restaurant. She has erythematous wheals all over her body and has
diffuse wheezes on auscultation. Her blood pressure is (BP) 92/55 mm Hg,
heart rate (HR) is 115 beats/minute, respiratory rate (RR) is 28
breaths/minute, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. EMS informs
you that they are a basic unit. What are the most appropriate initial orders
for the EMS unit given their level of training?

options.text: Administer supplemental oxygen and proceed to the ED as quickly and
Establish intravenous (IV) access and administer IV epinephrine and a
Establish IV access and administer a normal saline bolus
Perform orotracheal intubation for impending respiratory failure

englishExplanation:
484.  The answer is d. The National Highway Traffic and Safety
Administration Act of 1966 set recommendations for first responder and
emergency medical technician (EMT) training courses. Because prehospital
personnel are covered by state and in some cases local authority, the State
Board of Emergency Medical Services is authorized to modify some aspects
including recommended course lengths and scope of practice, leading to
variances in EMS systems and practices from state to state. There are four
major levels of EMS training and credentialing established within the
National EMS Scope of Practice Model. These are as follows:
1.   First responders include mandatory training given to firefighters,
police officers, and community EMS responders. These are often the
first people to arrive on scene. They are trained in CPR, basic life
support (BLS), and basic trauma care. Current recommendations are
approximately 40 hours of training.

2.   Emergency medical technician basic (EMT-B) is the lowest EMT
level. They can perform BLS, automated external defibrillation (AED),
basic assessments, and assist in medication administration. They
cannot establish IV access; however, in almost all states they can
administer IM medications based on predefined protocols or via a
verbal order from an online medical physician. The recommended
curriculum is a course length of 110 hours.
3.   Emergency medical technician intermediate (EMT-I) personnel
have completed EMT-B requirements and are trained in procedures
such as establishing IV access, ET intubation, and manual
defibrillation. Current recommendations are approximately 300 to 400
hours of training.
4.   Emergency medical technician paramedic (EMT-P) is the most
advanced EMT level. They receive all EMT-I training in addition to
training to perform advanced airway procedures, needle
decompression of the chest, ECG interpretation, external pacing, and
advanced drug therapy within predefined standardized protocols.
Recommendations for their training curriculum range from 1000 to
1200 hours.
In this case, the patient is having an anaphylactic reaction secondary to
a peanut allergy. The best initial treatment is IM epinephrine. EMT-B units
are trained to administer IM medications; in some states, they may require
an order from the online medical physician before administration. Although
the patient requires emergent transport (a), an EMT-B unit should be able to
provide potentially life-saving care on scene. EMT-I units are trained to
establish IV access in order to administer IV fluids (c) and medications (b),
as well as perform ET intubation when indicated (e).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريضة عندها anaphylaxis واضح من 땅، يعني urticaria و wheezing مع hypotension. والـ EMS unit هي basic unit يعني EMT-B، وهالمستوى بيقدروا يعملوا BLS و AED و assist في administering medications، بس ما بيقدروا يفتحوا IV access. و حسب الـ National EMS Scope of Practice Model، الـ EMT-B بيقدر يعطي أدوية IM حسب protocols predefined أو بناءً على order من physician. فأول خيار منطقي هو IM epinephrine.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار IV epinephrine أو normal saline bolus مع IV access، بس الـ EMT-B ما بيقدر يفتح IV access. و IM epinephrine أسرع لأنه بيتعطى فورًا وبيوصل للعضلات مع الدوران.

question:
A married couple is hiking a mountain in a large national park, when
one partner slips and falls down a steep hill. He hits his chest wall on a tree
trunk, and a branch impales his left flank. He also hears a “pop” from his
left knee and cannot move his lower leg. He is conscious and tells his

partner to go for help because he cannot move and is having difficulty
breathing. His partner hikes back to the park ranger’s headquarters for
assistance. The ranger calls report over the radio requesting assistance in
transporting the patient to your ED, which is located approximately 50
miles away. There is a service road adjacent to the hiking trail and it is a
clear, sunny day. What is the most appropriate transfer modality to send to
the scene?

options.text: Send an EMS van via the service road to extricate the patient and
Send the park ranger in his mountain terrain–equipped vehicle to
Send a rotary-wing helicopter and have the park ranger mobilize ground
Send an EMS pickup chassis with an integrated modular patient care
Send a fixed-wing EMS aircraft and mobilize the park ranger’s

correctAnswer: Send a rotary-wing helicopter and have the park ranger mobilize ground
englishExplanation:
485.  The answer is c. There are three modes of transportation available
to most EMS systems: ground transportation, rotary-wing air (helicopter)
transportation, or fixed-wing air (small plane) transportation. Ground
transportation is used for the vast majority of acutely ill or injured patients.
Air transport is indicated when air transport time would be
significantly less than ground transport time. Other indications for air
transport are severe injury in which rapid transport is essential; unstable
vital signs; significant trauma in patients younger than 12 years; patients

older than 55 years or pregnant; multisystem injuries; ejection from a
vehicle; pedestrian struck or motorcyclist struck; death in same passenger
compartment; penetrating trauma to the abdomen, pelvis, chest, neck, or
head; crush injury to the abdomen, chest, or head; and fall from significant
height. This is not an exhaustive list and the specific scenario and clinical
assessment must always be factored into every individual case.
Once the decision to use air transportation has been made, the next
decision is to employ a rotary-wing or a fixed-wing aircraft. A rotary-wing
aircraft has a range of 50 to 150 miles and is indicated in scenarios of
entrapped trauma patients with extrication time expected to exceed 20
minutes or locations in a topographically difficult-to-reach area by ground
transportation. Keep in mind that rotary-wing air transportation is limited
by poor weather and both modes of air transport carry an inherent risk of
crashing that must be considered by the physician. A fixed-wing aircraft is
indicated for distances longer than 100 miles when rapid transport is
essential. This mode of transportation is also limited by weather, lack of
runways, and refueling. One must also consider possible altitude problems
for the patient such as pneumothorax, ET cuff, and balloon catheters.
However, there are no absolute contraindications to fixed-wing air
transport.
In this case, even though there is a service road adjacent to the hiking
trail, ground transportation (a, b, and d) is not appropriate due to several
factors, including prolonged travel time (the nearest hospital is 50 miles
away), a topographically difficult-to-reach surface area, and prolonged
extrication time. In this scenario, a rotary-winged aircraft (helicopter)
would be ideal because it could assist in the extrication process as the hiker
fell down a steep hill and cannot move. A fixed-wing aircraft (e) is not the
best choice because ground transportation would still be needed and the
patient would have to endure a prolonged extrication time. Additionally, the
patient has difficulty breathing secondary to blunt chest trauma suggestive
of a pneumothorax, which could be significantly worsened by the altitude
required by fixed-wing transport.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده penetrating trauma للصدر مع injury للرجل وصعوبة تنفس، يعني حالة حرجة بتحتاج نقل سريع. الـ ED بعيدة 50 ميل، والوصول إليك بالطريق الجبلي بياخد وقت طويل، والـ helicopter بيوصل أسرع بمراحل. الـ air transport بين indication لها مثل severe injury و unstable vital signs و penetrating trauma للـ chest و multitrauma. وبعد ما قررت تستعمل جو، بتختار rotary-wing لأن مداه من 50 لحد 150 ميل وبيعمل hover فوق المكان وبيسند الإخلاء.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار ground transportation أو fixed-wing aircraft. الأرضي بيطول وقت والشمس ماطالعة بس ما بيساعد، والـ fixed-wing يحتاج مطار وبياخد وقت تجهيز وبيهبط بعيد عن الجبل. والـ helicopter هو الأنسب للخلاء من مكان صعب.

question:
Shared scenario:
A railroad freight car is overturned while traveling through a suburban area
and hundreds of gallons of chemical waste are spilled at the scene. Several
railroad crew members were heavily exposed to the chemicals and are
reported to be in critical condition. Some have already died from the
exposure. The IC sets up a hot-zone perimeter and has designated
decontamination zones. You receive a call from a hazardous material
(HAZMAT) paramedic unit with a patient in distress who they believe will
not survive long.

486.   Under which of the following circumstances is it acceptable to
immediately transport the patient directly from the hot zone without going
through decontamination?

options.text: If it is reasonably certain that the patient will not survive long enough
If the toxic chemical is identified and the EMS personnel have adequate
If the IC orders EMS to bypass the decontamination zone due to the
If the resources at the incident site are overwhelmed by the number of
It is never acceptable to bypass the decontamination process after a

correctAnswer: It is never acceptable to bypass the decontamination process after a
englishExplanation:
486.  The answer is e. The most important rule of disaster management for
chemical agents is the contaminated patient should never be allowed to
enter the ED before being decontaminated. Each state has a standard

operating procedure for mass casualty decontamination. The following are
critical steps in the management of chemical mass casualty exposures:
•   Recognition of a toxic chemical exposure
•   Rapid identification of the agents involved
•   Information retrieval on the toxicity and secondary contamination
potential of the agent
•   Proper protection of self, hospital personnel, already hospitalized
patients, and the facility itself from secondary contamination or loss
of serviceability to other patients
•   Decontamination and triage of victims
•   Stabilization and medical treatment of victims
•   Protection of the community-at-large from secondary contamination
This question pertains to the decontamination step of a toxic chemical
exposure, which is clearly of imminent risk to the surrounding community
because some of the crew has already died. Patient decontamination should
occur outside the hospital. Hot, warm, and cold zones should be established
and cordoned off with brightly colored tape. The hot zone is the area of the
toxic substance exposure or may be the hospital area where arriving patients
with no prior decontamination are held. The warm zone is an area where
thorough decontamination and further medical stabilization occur. This area
should be arranged so that there is no risk of primary contamination, but
secondary contamination (transfer of the toxic substance from the victim to
personnel or equipment) may occur. Hence, only trained personnel with the
proper personal protective equipment (PPE) are allowed in the hot and
warm zones. The cold zone is the area to which fully decontaminated
patients are transferred. The warm and cold zones should be established
upwind, uphill, or upstream of the hot zone to minimize extension of the hot
zone into other decontamination areas. There is no personnel flow between
the different zones. The following figure is a schematic representation of a
HAZMAT incident area.

(Reproduced with permission from Shareaf Walid, MD.)
There are no circumstances in which hot and warm zone
decontamination can be bypassed, especially in the event of a potentially
lethal exposure. Bypassing contamination zones (a, b, c, and d) would put
the public-at-large, including the ED, which is never acceptable. One salient
point to remember is that clothing should be removed quickly as this act
is thought to accomplish 80% of the decontamination.

![PreTest-5e-00486 source page 623](images/PreTest-5e-00486-PreTest-5e-p0623.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00486 source page 624](images/PreTest-5e-00486-PreTest-5e-p0624.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00486 source page 634](images/PreTest-5e-00486-PreTest-5e-p0634.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00486 source page 635](images/PreTest-5e-00486-PreTest-5e-p0635.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00486 source page 636](images/PreTest-5e-00486-PreTest-5e-p0636.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أهم قاعدة في إدارة الكوارث الكيميائية إن المريض الملوّث ما يوصل الـ ED قبل ما ينعمله decontamination، لأن هالشي بيحمي المجتمع والمريضين التانيين وطاقم المستشفى من secondary contamination. لازم الـ decontamination يصير خارج المستشفى، وهاد بيتم بعد ما تحدد الـ hot و warm و cold zones وتلفّهم بشريط ملوّن. حتى لو المريض بيموت بسرعة، التعرض السام خطر على الكل، خصوصاً إذا الـ toxin مش معروف.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار أي خيار من الخيارات اللي بتبرر تخطّي الـ decontamination، مثل إن المريض ما راح ينجو أو إن الـ IC أمر. السبب إن الـ IC بيأمر بالسلامة مش بتخطّي خطوة، والـ toxin المجهول هو أخطر الحالات.

question:
Shared scenario:
An Emergency Medical Dispatcher receives a 9-1-1 call from a frantic
family member who found their 67-year-old mother lying on the ground
unresponsive at their home residence. They report that she has a pulse in
both wrists, however does not appear to be breathing. After verifying the

caller’s pertinent demographic information and dispatching the appropriate
EMS unit to the scene, the Emergency Medical Dispatcher stays on the line
with the caller in order to provide additional pre-arrival instructions.

489.   Which of the following is an appropriate pre-arrival instruction that
the Emergency Medical Dispatcher is qualified to give to the caller?

options.text: Administer the patient’s home BP medication
Open and clear the patient’s airway
Reposition the patient in an upright seated position

correctAnswer: Open and clear the patient’s airway
englishExplanation:
489.  The answer is d. In the United States, 9-1-1 was adopted as the
universal emergency telephone access number in 1973, and since then has
been the mainstay of public access to emergency services such as police,
fire, and EMS. 9-1-1 Dispatch centers are staffed by specially trained and
qualified operators called Emergency Medical Dispatchers who are
regulated by the EMS subdivision of the NHTSA, which falls under the
oversight of the Department of Transportation (DOT). Emergency Medical
Dispatchers are trained to use a chief complaint centered, standardized
algorithm to determine the priority and severity of the call, in order to
dispatch the appropriate level of EMS unit. After establishing the priority
level of the call and dispatching the appropriate unit, the operator can then
provide the caller with simple instructions for potentially life-saving
maneuvers based on the situation.

In the previously mentioned case, the most appropriate action would be
to open and clear the patient’s airway (d) of any potential obstruction. The
patient appears to be apneic, and clearing an airway obstruction could be a
rapid and lifesaving maneuver. While initiating CPR (c) is an instruction
that the operator is qualified to give, this patient has a pulse and thus does
not require CPR at this time. Many EMS systems have opted to provide
compressions-only CPR instructions to bystanders, avoiding the mouth-tomouth breaths, to simplify telephone instructions and improve bystander
compliance. Administering the patient’s home medications (a) is not a part
of the BLS algorithm, and bystanders are generally not advised to give
home medications beyond aspirin for cardiac-related complaints.
Bystanders are encouraged to leave the patient in the position in which they
were found, and to avoid repositioning or moving them in any way (e)
provided that the scene is safe. However, if CPR is needed, dispatchers will
instruct callers to position the patient flat on the floor. While the impetus for
encouraging bystanders to leave the patient unmoved is to avoid potential
cervical spinal cord injury, there is no recommendation for bystanders to
establish or maintain formal cervical spine precautions (e). 9-1-1 dispatch
operators are also trained and qualified to give basic instructions regarding
hemorrhage control as well as childbirth assistance in the pre-arrival period
after appropriate EMS units have been dispatched.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد 9-1-1 dispatcher وبيعطي تعليمات قبل وصول EMS، وبيشتغل من خوارزمية موحدة حسب chief complaint. هون المريضة 67 سنة، لقوها من بيتها وما بتتنفس بس عندها pulse بالـ wrists. يعني المشكلة أول شي airway، والـ dispatcher من حقه يقول للمتصل يفتح الـ airway ويزيل أي انسداد. هاد الإجراء ممكن ينقذ حياتها بسرعة. وفي المقابل، CPR ما منوسب لأنها عندها pulse.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تقول للمتصل يبدأ CPR، بس هي عندها pulse فالـ compressions ما لازم. وإنك تجيب دوا الضغط أو الـ cervical spine، وهي أشياء ما جاوب عليها. الخيار الصح هو الـ airway.

question:
A patient is brought in by EMS after sustaining injuries from a motor
vehicle accident. Law enforcement arrives with the patient and informs you
that the patient is under arrest. Your patient’s vital signs are stable. You
send basic blood work, including blood alcohol level, a chest radiograph,
and a urinalysis. The blood alcohol level comes back above the legal limit
for operating a motor vehicle. The rest of the workup is unremarkable. The
police officer requests a copy of the patient’s medical record. What is the
proper response to his request?

options.text: Because the patient is in police custody, he does not have the same right
Refusal to give the officer the records is considered obstruction of
Unless the patient consents, you are obligated to refuse the officer’s
As a licensed physician, you are allowed to use your best judgment in a
You may release all pertinent medical information, but can withhold

correctAnswer: Unless the patient consents, you are obligated to refuse the officer’s
englishExplanation:
492.  The answer is c. The HIPAA (1996) was created to protect patients’
privacy rights by establishing rules for disclosures of confidential health
information. The act was intended to standardize health information
transfers, require identification numbers for providers, health plans, and
employers, and to protect confidential protected health information (PHI).
The inclusion of PHI protection resulted from fears that electronic transfers
and ID numbers could be misused. Hence, the law penalizes disclosures of
confidential health information that are not authorized in writing by the
patient. The secretary of health and human services imposes civil monetary
penalties for violation of any HIPAA requirement, up to $25,000 per
disclosure. Police officers do not have automatic access to a patient’s

medical record, even if the patient is in their custody. Only if the police
serve you with a subpoena for court-ordered medical records are you
obligated to share them without the patient’s written consent.
Incarcerated patients (a) are still protected by HIPAA regulations and
are entitled to confidentiality of PHI. As a physician, there are no legal
ramifications for abiding by HIPAA regulations; in fact, both you and your
institution are liable for monetary and civil penalties if HIPAA rules are
broken (b). HIPAA privacy regulations are not subject to case-by-case
discretionary judgments (d) but rather must be followed with only certain
special exceptions, such as psychotherapy notes and disclosures for billing
issues, which are outside the physician’s scope of practice. Answer choice
(e) is incorrect because unauthorized release of medical records violates the
HIPAA laws.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ HIPAA سنة 1996 وُضعت عشان تحمي خصوصية المريض و تمنع أي إفصاح عن الـ PHI بدون إذن خطي من المريض. و الشرطة ما عندهم حق تلقائي يطّلعوا على الـ record حتى لو المريض موقوف عندهم. بتقدر تعطيهم الـ records بس إذاPolice قدّموا subpoena من المحكمة. وأنا كـ doctor ملزوم ألتزم بالـ HIPAA، ومخالفتي بتعرّضني وبالمستشفى لعقوبات مدنية.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تعطي الـ officer كل السجلات لأنه موقوف، أو إنك تستخدم best judgment كـ physician عشان تعطيه إياه. الـ arrest ما بيشيل الـ HIPAA protection، والشي الوحيد اللي بيجبر المستشفى هو subpoena.

question:
A 67-year-old man is brought to the ED by EMS with a chief
complaint of chest pain. He is found to be short of breath and diaphoretic.
He reports that he vomited 1 hour ago and subsequently feels better. He
describes substernal chest pressure that started while doing yard work. He
has a history of coronary artery disease and hypertension. He has regularly
scheduled appointments with a cardiologist at a neighboring hospital. He
requested to be taken to that hospital, but EMS refused and brought him to
your ED because it was only 5 minutes away. The patient is angry and

requests a transfer to his cardiologist’s hospital, which is 20 minutes away.
What is the best course of action?

options.text: You must politely refuse his request and work the patient up for acute
Contact the neighboring hospital; if the patient’s cardiologist accepts the
Transfer the patient only if he has stable vital signs and his cardiologist
Transfer the patient immediately and inform EMS that they should have
Perform the appropriate medical screening examination (MSE), in this

correctAnswer: Perform the appropriate medical screening examination (MSE), in this
englishExplanation:
493.  The answer is e. The Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor
Act (EMTALA) mandates that unstable patients cannot be discharged or
transferred except for medical necessity. The purpose of EMTALA was
to discourage low-income and high-risk patients from being transferred
from one ED to another for financial advantage. Under EMTALA, any
patient presenting to an ED has the right to an MSE to determine if an
emergency medical condition (EMC) exists without regard to the patient’s
ability or willingness to pay for services rendered. If an EMC exists, the
hospital must stabilize the condition within its capacity. If the hospital
cannot stabilize the condition, the staff is further obligated to transfer the
patient to a facility capable of providing adequate care. It is important to
understand that an MSE is not simply a triage examination, and requires
any further indicated workup including consultations if necessary, to
determine if an EMC exists. If an EMC is not yet stabilized, a transfer
cannot be made unless the transferring physician certifies that the benefits
outweigh the risks and the transfer is medically appropriate. Additionally,
the transferring hospital must do everything in its capacity to minimize the
risk of transfer, and the receiving hospital must have available space and
personnel and agree to accept the patient. Any hospital that negligently
violates an EMTALA policy can be penalized up to $50,000 per violation
and physicians who negligently violate may also have to pay up to $50,000
per violation. Civil money penalties such as EMTALA violations are not
covered by malpractice insurance.

In this vignette, the patient has a history of coronary artery disease and
presents with shortness of breath, diaphoresis, chest pressure, and vomiting.
Given his history, presentation, age, and risk factors, it is clear that the
patient is at high risk for a myocardial infarction (MI). Hence, the proper
MSE is an ECG and troponin in order to rule out an MI before transfer (a,
b, c, and d). If the patient is having an MI and the current facility has the
capability of providing effective management based on standard-of-care
protocols, they are obliged to admit the patient to their facility. If the current
facility does not have the capacity to effectively treat the patient (ie, a
cardiac catheterization suite), they can transfer the patient if a receiving
hospital agrees to accept him and he is deemed stable for transfer.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: تحت الـ EMTALA، أي مريض يوصل الـ ED عنده حق في MSE عشان تحدد إذا في emergency medical condition، بدون ما تتأثر بقدرته أو رغبته بالدفع. وفي هالحالة المريض عنده chest pain وتاريخ coronary artery disease، يعني ممكن في EMC. الـ MSE مو بس triage، لازم يشمل الـ ECG و الفحوصات الأساسية مثل troponin، وبياخد وقت قبل ما تفكر بالنقل. وإذا في EMC والمستشفى ما قادر يثبّت حالته، وقتها بتبعت نقل لـ EMS.
الفخ: الفخ إنك مباشرة تنقله لمستشفى الـ cardiologist لأنه طلب كذا، أو ترفض تفحصه وتعمله workup. EMTALA بتمنع تفريغ أو نقل المريض غير المستقر إلا لضرورة طبية، والنقل لازم يكون مبرر طبيًا بعد MSE.

question:
Shared scenario:
EMS is responding to a call at a local high school football game. One of the
high school football players is unresponsive to verbal stimuli after a helmetto-helmet collision with another player. His BP is 100/65 mm Hg, HR is 60
beats/minute, and RR is 12 breaths/minute. There is a small crack at the top
of the helmet, but it is otherwise intact and strapped tightly to the patient’s
head.

495.   EMS calls medical control to request permission to remove his
helmet in order to assess for head trauma. What is the most appropriate
prehospital management of this patient?

options.text: Do not attempt to remove the helmet, maintain cervical spine
While maintaining cervical spine precautions, carefully remove the
Check the patient’s pupils and if there is asymmetry, remove the helmet
Wait at the scene for a physician to arrive with an electric saw for
Do not remove the helmet but assess the cervical spine for step-off or

correctAnswer: Do not attempt to remove the helmet, maintain cervical spine
englishExplanation:
495.  The answer is a. A properly fitted football helmet with shoulder pads
holds the head in a position of neutral spinal alignment; field removal of

these devices is not recommended. Instead, the helmet and shoulder pads
should remain on as the athlete is immobilized and transported on a rigid
backboard. Simultaneous removal of the helmet and shoulder pads should
be done after clinical assessment and radiographs at the hospital.
Radiographs can be repeated after removal of the helmet as clinically
indicated.
The proper removal of a football helmet requires four people and should
not be attempted out of hospital (b). Even with pupil asymmetry, the EMT’s
best course of action is to expeditiously transport the patient to the ED for
definitive care because EMTs are not trained to perform any techniques to
relieve impending uncal herniation (c). The use of an electric saw is not
indicated and unnecessary prehospital delays should be avoided (d).
Adequate cervical spine assessment is unreliable and potentially dangerous
in the prehospital setting and would also unnecessarily delay transport (e).
arabicExplanation:
