ليش: الـ football helmet مع الـ shoulder pads المظبوطين بيمسكوا الرأس ب neutral spinal alignment، وهاد السبب إن إزالة الجهاز بالميدان مو مقترحة. فبيخلوا الـ helmet والـ shoulder pads على المريض، وبيثبّتوه على backboard صلب وينقلوه للـ ED. إزالة الـ helmet والـ shoulder pads مع بعض لازم تتم بعد الفحص السريري والأشعة بالمستشفى. و الـ removal بيحتاج أربع أشخاص، فما ينفع يعملوه في الميدان.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تشيل الـ helmet عشان تفحص الـ pupils أو عشان تعمل c-spine assessment في الميدان. الـ EMT ما متدرب على تخفيف impending uncal herniation، وتقييم الـ c-spine بالميدان مو موثوق وبيأخر النقل.

question:
A physician colleague of yours arrives to work and smells of alcohol.
Her speech is slurred and she is making repeated errors in ordering
medications and diagnostic studies for patients. You are concerned about
the safety of patients. Who of the following should be notified first about
this physician’s behavior?
englishExplanation:
560.  The answer is d. Health care providers have a duty to protect patients
from impaired physicians when the impaired are unable or unwilling to seek
help for themselves. Impairment is the inability of a provider to safely and
effectively care outpatient care duties. Signs of impairment include failure
to meet job responsibilities (eg, arriving late to work), forgetfulness during
tasks, or evidence of substance use. The American College of Emergency

Physicians (ACEP) Code of Ethics states, “Emergency physicians shall deal
fairly and honestly with colleagues and take appropriate action to protect
patients from health care providers who are impaired or incompetent.”
Handling an impaired colleague should begin in a stepwise fashion. When a
colleague notices impairment of skill or judgment, he or she should
approach the physician about their concerns first.
If the physician fails to respond to this direct approach or patient safety
or wellbeing is at risk, reporting to the other answer options (a), (b), (c),
and (e) may need to be utilized.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: إلنا واجب نحمي المرضى من الطبيب المعطّل لما يكون هو ما بيقدر ولا بيميل يطلب مساعدة لحاله. والتعامل مع هاد الموقف بيبقى على خطوات: أول شي تقرب من زميلك وبتحكي معاه عن اللي شفته. هو فعلاً مسحوب على كحول، كلامه مش واضح، وبيرتكب أخطاء في orders، وهاد مؤشرات impairment واضحة. فلما تتعامل معاه مباشرة أو تبلّغ عنو، بتعمل بالضبط زي ما ACEP Code of Ethics طالب، وبيبقى الخيار ethics committee و administrator و الخيارات التانية للحالات اللي ما بتتجاوب.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تبلّغ مباشرة للـ hospital administrator أو ethics committee أو police. الخطوات بتبدأ منك ومن الطبيب نفسه، وبعدها بتستخدم باقي الخيارات بس إذا ما استجاب أو كانت سلامة المريض بخطر.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding the epidemiology of 
out-of-hospital cardiac arrest is true?

options.text: Most patients have an automated external defibrillator applied
Most surviving to hospital discharge will not have major persistent neurologic deficits.
Only 2% of EMS-treated out-of-hospital cardiac arrests survive

correctAnswer: Most surviving to hospital discharge will not have major persistent neurologic deficits.
englishExplanation:
It is estimated that 180,000 patients are treated for out-of-hospital 
cardiac arrest each year in the United States. The number of patients receiving bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) remains low, averaging 40%. The proportion of emergency medical services (EMS)–treated 
cardiac arrest patients with an initial shockable rhythm has declined over 
time to 18% in recent US studies. Automated external defibrillators are 
applied in a minority of cases prior to EMS arrival. Recent epidemiologic 
data from cardiac arrest registries indicate the survival rate to hospital discharge for EMS-treated, out-of-hospital cardiac arrest is about 10%. Of 
patients surviving to hospital discharge, independent of neurologic status 
on presentation, 79% have good neurologic function.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لازم تنتبه للرقم: من مرضى cardiac arrest اللي عالجتهم EMS، نسبة اللي بيوصلوا discharged من المستشفى حوالي 10% بس. ومن بين هؤلاء اللي عاشوا، 79% عندهم function عصبي كويس، بمعنى إن most منهم مش بيخرجوا مع persistent neurologic deficits كبيرة. و برضو الـ bystander CPR بيضل حوالي 40% بس، والـ AED قبل وصول EMS بيتطبق بأقلية من الحالات، و الـ shockable rhythm proportion نزلت لـ 18%.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار إن most patients بياخدوا AED أو إن most patients بياخدوا bystander CPR. الأرقام هاد قليلة، لأن الـ AED بيتطبق بأقلية من الحالات و الـ bystander CPR حوالي 40% بس، و 2% رقم قديم مش مطابق.

question: Which of the following is the goal of the primary survey?

options.text: Determine which consultations should be obtained.
Do an AMPLE (allergies, medications, past medical history, last
Obtain pertinent historical data from the paramedics.
Rapidly identify critical life-threatening diagnoses and begin

correctAnswer: Rapidly identify critical life-threatening diagnoses and begin
englishExplanation:
The emergency clinician should use a standardized 
approach to the initial evaluation of these patients. Following the 
Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) algorithm of ABCs in the primary survey allows the timely identification of critical diagnoses and 
intervention without delay. The primary survey should be performed 
in a standardized fashion immediately after the patient arrives in the 
emergency department. The goal of the primary survey is to identify 
critical, life-threatening diagnoses rapidly and begin treatment at the 
time of diagnosis. The goals of the secondary survey are to obtain pertinent historical data about the patient and injury as well as evaluate 
and treat injuries not found on the primary survey. An AMPLE history 
should be obtained.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ primary survey بيعمله المتعامل بالطوارئ فور ما المريض يوصل الـ ED، وبيسير على algorithm الـ ATLS اللي هو ABCs. هدفه الأساسي إنك تكتشف بسرعة كل تشخيصات الـ critical والـ life-threatening وتبدأ العلاج وقت التشخيص بدون أي تأخير. أما الـ secondary survey فمهمته غير كذا: بتاخد من تاريخ المريض وبتفحص و treat injuries اللي ما ظهرت في الـ primary survey، وعلى هذا الأساس بتاخد الـ AMPLE history.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار إن الـ primary survey هدفه إنه ياخد history من الـ paramedics أو يعمل radiographic evaluation أو يحدد استشاراته. هاد كله بيصير في الـ secondary survey أو بعد ما تستقر حالة المريض.

question:
Which of the following injuries is appropriate for traction splinting 
by prehospital providers?

options.text: Femoral fracture with bone protrusion through the skin
Severe crush injury of leg with obvious deformity of the knee
Suspected closed mid shaft femoral fracture

correctAnswer: Suspected closed mid shaft femoral fracture
englishExplanation:
Traction splints can provide pain relief, immobilization, 
and limit blood loss when applied correctly to a femoral fracture. 
However, contraindications to the use of traction splints include pelvic fractures, patellar fractures, ligamentous knee injuries, and tibia 
or fibula fractures. Traction in the prehospital setting should not be 
applied to any open fracture that has exposed bone. Such reduction 
pulls grossly contaminated bone fragments back into the wound 
before adequate débridement can be undertaken in the operating 
room.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ traction splint للـ femoral fracture بيشتغل بشكل صحيح بيعطي ألم أقل، ويثبّت الكسر، وبيقلل فقد الدم. المناسبين له cases مثل suspected closed mid-shaft femoral fracture. وبالمقابل في contraindications واضحة: pelvic fractures، patellar fractures، ligamentous knee injuries، و tibia أو fibula fractures. وكمان ما ينفع تحط traction على أي open fracture فيها exposed bone، لأن الـ reduction بيرجّع عظام ملوثة للجرح قبل ما ينعمل débridement بالغرفة.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تحط traction splint على femur fracture وطلع منها عظم، أو على injury بالـ knee. الـ open fracture و ligamentous knee injuries عندها contraindications واضحة، و وضع traction عليها بيعمل ضرر أكبر.

question:
An 85-year-old man presents with acute onset of right-sided weakness that began 1 hour before arrival. His family states that he was 
recently diagnosed with dementia and has refused to take any of his 
medications for more than 1 week but had otherwise been relatively 
healthy. Emergency medical services (EMS) report a prehospital 
blood pressure of 240/110 mm Hg. On examination, the patient 
has clear evidence of an acute stroke with severe deficit (National 
Institutes of Health [NIH] Stroke Scale = 24), but his gag reflex is 
intact. His initial blood pressure is 230/110 mm Hg. A head computed tomography (CT) scan shows diffuse white matter ischemic 
disease but no evidence of acute infarct or hemorrhage. The most 
appropriate next step is which of the following?

options.text: Repeat the blood pressure and, if 185/110 mm Hg or higher, start
Contact neurosurgery for intracranial pressure monitoring.
Give a dose of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) immediately.

correctAnswer: Repeat the blood pressure and, if 185/110 mm Hg or higher, start
englishExplanation:
Despite his advanced age, this is a relatively highfunctioning individual with acute onset of a severe stroke. He is within 
the time window for administration of tPA, but his blood pressure is 
excessively elevated. According to the American Heart Association/
American Stroke Association guidelines, efforts should be made to 
reduce his blood pressure to less than 185/110 mm Hg before tPA 
administration. Other agents, such as labetalol, would also be appropriate to use.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: عندك مريض عنده acute ischemic stroke حاد مع NIHSS = 24، والـ CT ما طلع فيه infarct ولا hemorrhage، فالمريض داخل بوقت الـ window للـ tPA. المشكلة إن ضغط دمه 230/110، وعنده رفض للأدوية من أسبوع، وهاد بيعني إن حالة غير مستقرة وممكن نرفض. الـ AHA/ASA guidelines بتقول لازم نزّل الضغط أقل من 185/110 قبل ما نعطي tPA. يعني نعيد قياس الضغط، وإذا 185/110 أو أعلى نبدأ nicardipine infusion بجرعة 5 mg/hour، وبيتقدر نستخدم labetalol كمان.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تعطي tPA على طول أو تنزل الضغط بـ sublingual nifedipine. الـ tPA ممنوعة قبل ما ينزل الضغط تحت 185/110، والـ sublingual nifedipine مش الخيار المفضل. و الاتصال بـ neurosurgery للـ ICP monitoring مش أول خطوة.

question:
Your Emergency Department receives a report of a “dirty bomb” 
explosion with multiple injuries and deaths on scene. Which injuries would you be most likely to see?
englishExplanation:
“Dirty bomb” is a term for a traditional explosive device to 
which an amount of radioactive material has been added. The greatest 
risk of injury is from traditional blast/explosive effects. The risk of radiation injury and contamination from a “dirty bomb” is extremely low. 
The small amount of radioactive material that survives the explosion 
is concentrated in the area immediately around the explosion, where 
victims are likely killed by the blast itself.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ dirty bomb يعني جهاز متفجر تقليدي plus شوية مادة مشعّة added. أكبر خطر للإصابة هو من تأثيرات الانفجار نفسه، أما خطر الـ radiation injury والـ contamination فبسيط جداً. المادة المشعة اللي بتضل بعد الانفجار مركّزة في المنطقة القريبة من الانفجار، وهيك الناس هناك غالباً بيقتلهم الـ blast قبل ما يوصلهم أي تعرّض إشعاعي. يعني بالـ ED بترى الجروح و الـ soft tissue injuries والـ orthopedic injuries، مش علامات الـ radiation sickness.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تستنى injuries الإشعاعية مثل hematopoietic أو gastrointestinal أو neurologic injuries. هاد الخطأ لأن الـ dirty bomb ضرره الأساسي انفجاري، والمواد القليلة المشعّة ما بتسبب syndrome إشعاعي بهالحجم.

question:
Which of the following is the proper sequence for caring for patients 
from a mass casualty incident involving potential radiologic contamination?

options.text: Decontamination, assess with radiation meter, emergency stabilization, mass casualty triage
Assess with radiation meter, decontamination, mass casualty triage, emergency stabilization
Assess with radiation meter, decontamination, emergency stabilization, mass casualty triage
Mass casualty triage, emergency stabilization, assess with radiation meter, decontamination
Decontamination, emergency stabilization, mass casualty triage,

correctAnswer: Mass casualty triage, emergency stabilization, assess with radiation meter, decontamination
englishExplanation:
In radiation incidents, the immediate risk to patients and 
providers from radiation injury is low. The most immediate risks are 
from traditional ABCD compromises. Thus, mass casualty triage and 
emergency stabilization take precedence, followed by an assessment 
for radiologic contamination, and decontamination if needed. This is 
in contrast to chemical or biologic incidents, where decontamination 
takes precedence.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في حوادث الإشعاع، الخطر الفوري على المرضى والطاقم من الإشعاع ضعيف. أخطر شي هو الـ ABCD compromises التقليدية، يعني التنفس والدورة الدموية والاختلال الوظيفي الحاد. عشان كذا ترتيب الخطوات بيبدأ بـ mass casualty triage، وبعدها emergency stabilization، وبعدين assessment للـ radiologic contamination بالـ radiation meter، وأخيراً decontamination إذا لزم. هاد بخلاف حوادث الـ chemical أو الـ biologic، فيهم الـ decontamination بتاخد الأولوية.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تبدأ بـ decontamination لأنك شفت مثال كيميائي أو بيولوجي. بس هون الخطر الفوري من الـ ABCs، والـ radiation meter والتطهير بيجوا بعد الـ triage والاستقرار، وإلا تأخرت بتتعامل مع اللي ممكن يموت.

question:
A 45-year-old man is inadvertently exposed to a radiation field 
of 850 mSv/hour for 4 hours while working on the clean-up of a 
nuclear power plant. In addition to general supportive care, which 
of the following medications may improve his survival?
englishExplanation:
This patient’s radiation dose is sufficient to produce the 
hematopoietic component of acute radiation syndrome (ARS). Cytokines or colony-stimulating factors have shown modest effects in 
improving survival. Irradiated patients may develop oral herpes, and 
acyclovir can be used for treatment but does not affect survival. Anemia is present in most irradiated patients but is typically not clinically 
significant, and erythropoietin has no role. DTPA is a chelating agent 
that can be used for patients with internal exposure to plutonium 
or transuranics. Potassium iodine is useful if a patient is exposed to 
radioactive iodine, because it will compete with the radioactive iodine 
for uptake into the thyroid gland, resulting in overall less radioactive 
uptake.
   
   	 C H A P T E R 1 3 4 : Q U E S T I O N S AND ANS WERS —cont’d.

1836.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض اتعرض لحقل إشعاعي 850 mSv/hour لمدة 4 ساعات، وهاد dose كافي يطلع منه hematopoietic component من acute radiation syndrome. الـ cytokines أو colony-stimulating factors أظهرت تأثير بسيط بتحسين الـ survival. الـ acyclovir بنستخدمه إذا في herpes شفوي بس ما بيأثر على النجاة، والـ erythropoietin ما إله دور لأن الـ anemia غالباً مش سريرية. الـ DTPA للـ internal exposure لـ plutonium أو transuranics، والـ potassium iodide بس إذا التعرض كان لـ radioactive iodine.
الفخ: الفخ إنك تختار erythropoietin لأن فيه anemia، أو potassium iodide لكل التعرضات الإشعاعية. الـ erythropoietin ما إله دور، والـ potassium iodide بيشتغل بس مع radioactive iodine وبيمنع uptake في الـ thyroid.

question:
Which method of communicating is adequate to utilize with a deaf 
or hard-of-hearing patient?
englishExplanation:
Using a certified interpreter for the hard-of-hearing is the 
only reliable way of communicating with such patients.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه التواصل مع مريض الـ deaf أو الـ hard-of-hearing لازم يتم عن طريق certified interpreter معتمد، وهاد هو الطريق الوحيد الموثوق عشان توصل المعلومة بشكل صحيح وتفهم إيش قاعد تشرح للمريض. أي طريقة ثانية، حتى لو بدت سهلة وأسرع، ممكن تضيع معلومات مهمة وتخلي المريض ما يفهم خطته العلاجية. عشان كده الاعتماد على certified interpreter هو الخيار الآمن والفعّال.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط اللي بيلجأ إليه الطلبة هو family member أو lip reading أو الكتابة على notepad لأنهم بيوفروا وقت ومصاريف. بس هدول مو reliable، لأن certified interpreter متدرّب على لغة الإشارة ويلتزم بالمعنى الصحيح لكلام المريض.

question:
Which of the following organizations have suggested guidelines to 
address cultural competence in educational standards?
englishExplanation:
These are just some of the medical organizations that have 
developed guidelines to assist medical schools and residency programs 
in teaching physicians-in-training to become culturally competent in 
their approach to patients from minority groups.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه كم منظمة طبية كبيرة طوّرت إرشادات بتساعد كليات الطب وبرامج الـ residency يعلّموا الأطباء المتدربين كيف يولّوا cultural competence في تعاملهم مع المرضى من minority groups. من بين هاد المنظمات، AAMC و Liaison Committee on Medical Education و Accreditation Council on Graduate Education. يعني جواب All of the above هو الأصح لأن المنظمات الثلاثة كلهم فعلاً وضعوا guidelines للـ cultural competence.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار منظمة وحدة وحدة بدل ما تجمعهم، وتفتكر إن الإجابة لازم تكون اسم جهة واحدة. الخيار D صح لأن كل المنظمات المذكورة طوّرت guidelines للـ cultural competence في التعليم الطبي.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding human trafficking 
inquiry is true?

options.text: It is imperative that trafficked victims recount their history
The primary goal of inquiry is disclosure.
Inquiry is a series of protocol-based standard questions designed
The goal of inquiry is to provide a safe environment for patients

correctAnswer: The goal of inquiry is to provide a safe environment for patients
englishExplanation:
Rather than disclosure, the goal of inquiry is to provide a 
safe environment in which patients feel empowered to share as much 
or as little as they choose where strengths and resilience are recognized. 
Inquiry-based assessment is an active process that includes openended questions and dialogue.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ inquiry عن human trafficking مش زي الاستجواب، لأن هدفه الأساسي مش إن المريض يعترف أو يفصح، بل إنك توفّر بيئة آمنة يحس فيها المريض إنه قادر يقول قد إيش بده يقول. التقييم المبني على inquiry عملية نشطة فيها أسئلة مفتوحة وحوار، مش سلسلة أسئلة protocol-based جاهزة، وهو بيعرف نقاط القوة والمرونة عند المريض. عشان كده جواب D هو الأصح.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو B أو A، يعني تشوف الـ inquiry على إنه disclosure إجباري أو إن المريض لازم يحكي تاريخه كامل. لازم تفهم إن Inquiry بيحترم اختيار المريض بكشف اللي يحب، مش ضغط عليه.

question: Which of the following factors does not affect equitable care in sexual minority populations?
englishExplanation:
Same-sex couples with adopted children can face difficulty in legal recognition of parenthood, resulting in barriers in medical decision making and obtaining appropriate health care. Although 
marriage equality provided the opportunity for stronger and automatic 
protections previously denied to same-sex couples, only 51% of samesex couples’ households are legally married compared to over 90% of 
heterosexual households. Sexual minority patients have less access to 
health care and are less likely to have health insurance compared to 
majority counterparts. ED provider education about sexual minorities 
is often inadequate, limited or absent, leading to lack of understanding 
and poorly informed decision making or advocacy on behalf of sexual 
minority populations.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه كل الخيارات اللي قدامك بأأثر فعلياً على الـ equitable care لسكان sexual minorities. العائلات same-sex مع أطفال متبنين واجهت صعوبة بالتعرّف القانوني على الوالدية، وهاد بيعمل barriers في القرار الطبي والحصول على الرعاية، وكمان 51% بس من هاد البيوت legally married مقابل فوق 90% من heterosexual households. منيح كمان إن minority patients عندهم وصول أقل للرعاية وأقل احتمال عندهم تأمين، و ED provider education عن sexual minorities ضعيف ومحدود أو غايب.
الفخ: الخطر هو إنك تختار same-sex marriage لأنه يحس إنها ما تأثر بشكل مباشر. بس هي تأثر، لأن مساواة الزواج وفّرت حماية أقوى وأوتوماتيكية كانت محرومة منها هاد الأزواج من قبل.

question: Which of the following factors impact health outcomes?
englishExplanation:
Access to transportation affects an individual’s ability to 
access care, adhere to appointments, and carry out treatment plans, 
having a direct impact on health. These individuals have worse health 
outcomes and mortality compared with those who are housed. Delayed 
care is a common issue that arises in the ED as uninsured and underinsured patients often are unable to access care prior to an ED visit. 
Lack of access to healthy foods leads to increased rates of mental health 
problems, low birth weight, depression, hypertension, diabetes, and 
hyperlipidemia.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه وصول الناس للنقل بيأثر بشكل مباشر على قدرتها توصل للرعاية وتلتزم بمواعيدها وتنفّذ خطط علاجها. كذلك الناس اللي ما عندهم سكن عندهم نتائج صحية أسوأ ووفاة أعلى مقارنة مع الناس اللي عندهم بيت. Delayed care مشكلة شائعة في الـ ED لأن الناس غير المؤمَّنين أو ضعاف التأمين ما بيقدروا يوصلوا للرعاية قبل زيارة الـ ED، وكمان لما ما في وصول لأطعمة صحية بيزيد معدل مشاكل الصحة النفسية و low birth weight و depression و hypertension و diabetes و hyperlipidemia.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو إنك تختار وحدة بس، لأن السؤال ما سألك عن عامل واحد. النصيحة إنك تقرأ الخيارات كلها وتشوف إن كلها factors لها تأثير مباشر على النتائج الصحية.

question: Which of the following ED-based strategies can counteract SDOH?

options.text: Systematic screening in the emergency department can be a significant step in recognizing patients with significant SDOH.
Addressing SDOH must occur only within the health care system for the strategy to be successful.
Addressing concerns of health literacy first will substantively
Violence prevention is not a reasonable strategy in combating

correctAnswer: Systematic screening in the emergency department can be a significant step in recognizing patients with significant SDOH.
englishExplanation:
Most departments do not currently screen for social needs. 
Instead, social needs arise during the course of the patient encounter. 
Options for systematic screening exist but require implementing a 
framework to address social needs.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه أغلب الأقسام حالياً ما تعمل screening منظم للاحتياجات الاجتماعية للمريض، يعني الـ social needs بتظهر بشكل طبيعي أثناء زيارة المريض. بس في خيارات موجودة لعمل systematic screening، وهاد بيعمل خطوة كبيرة عشان نتعرف على المرضى اللي عندهم needs كبيرة. ولتشغّل هالشيء لازم تبني framework واضح للتعامل مع هالاحتياجات، عشان كده جواب A هو الأصح.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار B أو D، يعني تشوف إن الحل لازم يكون داخل نظام الرعاية أو إن violence prevention مو حل منطقي. الـ SDOH ما بتنحل بمكان واحد، وإلّا لازم يشتغل إطار شامل.

question:
Which of following health-related benefits available in the United 
States can impact access to care and health outcomes?

options.text: Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) is a specific program focused on providing access to care for children up to age
The Affordable Care Act requires plans and issuers that offer
The Hill-Burton Act of 1946 mandates charity care obligations
Part A Medicare benefits are essential to supporting prescription

correctAnswer: The Hill-Burton Act of 1946 mandates charity care obligations
englishExplanation:
Facilities built with assistance from the Hill-Burton Act of 
1946 have legally mandated charity care obligations. There are specific 
programs focused on providing access to care for children under the 
age of 18, including the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP). 
The Affordable Care Act requires plans and issuers that offer dependent child coverage to make coverage available until the child reaches 
the age of 26. Medicare is administered and funded by the federal government and contains several parts including inpatient hospital coverage (Part A), outpatient medical coverage (Part B), alternative coverage 
options including Medicare Advantage (Part C), and prescription drug 
coverage (Part D).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه المرافق اللي اتبنت بتمويل Hill-Burton Act of 1946 عليها التزامات charity care مفروضة بالقانون. وكمان في برامج ثانية لتحسين الوصول للرعاية، زي Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) الموجه للأطفال تحت 18 سنة، و Affordable Care Act اللي بيلزم خطط التأمين بتمديد تغطية الأبناء لحد عمر 26 سنة. و Medicare نفسه موزّع على عدة أجزاء، منها Part A للتغطية داخل المستشفى و Part B للعيادات و Part C و Part D للأدوية، يعني جواب C هو الأصح.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار CHIP أو ACA لأنهم فعلاً بيساعدوا الناس في الوصول للرعاية. بس السؤال عن التزام قانوني إجباري، و Hill-Burton Act هو اللي بيلزم المرافق اللي اتبنت بتمويله تقدّم charity care.

question:
Which of the following is required when planning a clinical experience abroad in which the GEM physician will be providing direct 
clinical care without supervision?

options.text: Current medical licensure from the country within which care
Current medical licensure from the GEM physician’s home
Written agreement between the GEM physician and a licensed
No local medical license is required as long as the GEM physician is practicing within the same scope as allowed by home

correctAnswer: Current medical licensure from the country within which care
englishExplanation:
The direct delivery of unsupervised medical care should 
only be provided by a GEM physician with a current and valid license 
issued by the appropriate regulatory body of the country within which 
care will be delivered. Additional requirements, such as hospital credentialing, are also generally required.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ GEM physician اللي رح يقدّم رعاية طبية مباشرة وبدون إشراف لازم يكون عنده رخصة طبية سارية من الجهة التنظيمية في البلد اللي رح تُقدّم فيه الرعاية. وكمان في متطلبات إضافية عادةً، مثل hospital credentialing، لازم تنطبق كمان. عشان كده جواب A هو الأصح، مش الرخصة من بلد الطبيب الأصلي، وهاد الشرط الأساسي لممارسة هالشكل من الرعاية.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو B أو D، يعني إن يكفي رخصة بلد البيت أو إن ما في داعي لرخصة محلية. هاد بس إذا كانت الرعاية بإشراف، أما بدون إشراف فالرخصة المحلية شرط أساسي.

question:
Which of the following scenarios often creates ethical dilemmas for 
those providing humanitarian assistance?

options.text: Triage of patients by local custom

correctAnswer: Triage of patients by local custom
englishExplanation:
Although all these issues are important, humanitarian 
workers often have ethical concerns about triage based on local customs versus severity of illness
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه كل هالمواضيع مهمة، بس اللي بيعمل مشاكل أخلاقية حقيقية عند العاملين في المجال الإنساني هو موضوع triage. فالعاملين بيواجهوا قلق أخلاقي لما يطلبوا منهم يوزّعوا المرضى حسب العادات المحلية بدل ما يعتمدوا على شدة المرض. ولأن المنطقة ممكن يكون فيها عادات مختلفة عن قواعد triage العالمية، فالقرار بيصير صعب. عشان كده جواب D هو الأصح.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار water أو housing أو سياسات الحكومة المحلية لأنهم مشاكل عملية مهمة. بس هي مشاكل لازم تنحل، مو dilemmas أخلاقية مباشرة بتفرضها قرارات triage.

question: Which of the following best describes the Sphere Handbook?

options.text: A global compilation of nongovernmental agencies
A description of legal decisions in international courts
An educational guide to global relief efforts
A guide that sets internal standards for humanitarian aid

correctAnswer: A guide that sets internal standards for humanitarian aid
englishExplanation:
The Sphere Handbook, a collaborative project of humanitarian response experts, sets international standards for the provision 
of humanitarian aid and is widely considered to define the gold standard of global humanitarian response.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه Sphere Handbook هو مشروع تعاوني بين خبراء الاستجابة الإنسانية، ووظيفته إنه بيضع معايير واضحة لتقديم المساعدة الإنسانية. وبيتعتبر على نطاق العالم هو gold standard للاستجابة الإنسانية. يعني هو مرجع عملي بيشتغل عليه كل من يبغى يقدّم مساعدة إنسانية بشكل صحيح، وبيحكم كيف يتقدّم الـ humanitarian aid، وهو مشروع تعاوني بين خبراء فمو مجرد تجميع للوكالات.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار A أو B أو C لأنهم يبانوا منطقيين بحكم إن الـ Handbook وثيقة مهمة. بس هو مش compilation للوكالات ولا وصف لقرارات المحاكم ولا book تعليمي، هو اللي بيحكم كيف Humanitarian aid يتقدّم.

question:
Emergency providers commonly discuss the issue of code status 
with their patients. In terms of prognosis after a cardiac arrest,

options.text: a recent study of nursing home patients experiencing cardiac
there are no good data, so providers should rely on their gestalt
a clinical decision rule called GO-FAR has been validated and
older patients and those with a terminal illness fare surprisingly

correctAnswer: a clinical decision rule called GO-FAR has been validated and
englishExplanation: [Explanation unavailable in supplied source]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه في قاعدة قرار سريرية اسمو GO-FAR تم التحقق منها، وهي بتقدر تعطي providers تنبؤ ببقاء المريض neurologically intact لكل مريض لحاله باستخدام المتغيرات من بيانات سريرته. يعني صار في طريقة منظمة تأخذ من حالة المريض وتطلع له تقدير بدل الكلام العام، وهاد بيعطيك تقدير تقدر تتكلم فيه مع المريض عن code status. عشان كده جواب C هو الأصح.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار B وتقول ما في بيانات، أو A وتتمسك بدراسة على مرضى nursing home. هاد الخيار مبني على قاعدة تم التحقق منها فعلياً، والباقي استنتاجات أو دراسات محدودة.

question:
In a nondeath disclosure setting, deliverance of bad news should 
start with which of the following approaches?

options.text: Allowing the patient to react to the news
Asking the patient if he or she wants to know
Making sure you keep the conversation going to provide comfort
Your knowledge of the complete medical implications and ramifications of the news

correctAnswer: Asking the patient if he or she wants to know
englishExplanation:
Respectful disclosure of difficult news includes assessing 
the readiness and willingness of the patient to receive the news.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه إعلان الخبر الصعب لازم يكون محترم، وأول خطوة فيه إنك تفحص جاهزية المريض وميله لاستقبال الخبر. يعني قبل ما تتكلم بتلاقي نفسك تسأله: هل بدك تعرف هاد الخبر؟ وهيك بتحترم حق المريض يقرر يحكي وقت هو جاهز له. وكمان لازم تاخد بالاعتبار إن الخيار جاي قبل أي تفاعل تاني، لأن الإنسان ممكن يكون مش مستعد عاطفياً لأصعب لحظة.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تبدأ بالسماح للمريض يتفاعل مع الخبر أو تحاول تكمّل الكلام عشان تريّحه، قبل ما تعرف إذا هو بدو يعرف. الأصل إنك تسأل أولاً وبعدين كل شي ثاني.

question:
Which of the following can emergency clinicians always rely on for 
appropriate guidance when faced with ethical dilemmas?

options.text: State laws and medical board policies
The American College of Emergency Physicians’ (ACEP) Code

englishExplanation:
All these examples are great for guidance on ethical dilemmas, but none of them can “always” have guidance for every situation 
that can occur.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه state laws و medical board policies و ACEP Code و Hippocratic Oath كلها مراجع ممتازة بتساعدك لما تواجه ethical dilemma. بس المشكلة إن كلمة always هي اللي بتفرق، يعني ما في مرجع واحد يقدر يغطي كل موقف ممكن يصير. عشان كده ما في إجابة من الخيارات تقدر تعتمد عليها دائماً، والجواب D هو الأصح.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار Hippocratic Oath أو state laws لأنهم يبانوا واضحين وقويين. بس هم بيوجّهوك ضمن إطار عام، وما في واحد فيهم بيعطيك جواب لكل ethical dilemma ممكن تصير.

question:
Which of the following is a common source of liability for failure 
to comply with the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act 
(EMTALA)?

options.text: Failure to comply with written hospital policies and procedures
Failure to diagnose an emergency medical condition (EMC)
Failure to properly treat an admitted patient who is boarded in
Failure to stabilize a patient after admission to an inpatient unit

correctAnswer: Failure to comply with written hospital policies and procedures
englishExplanation:
Hospital policies become the hospital’s standard under 
EMTALA. Thus, failure to comply with written policies, a failure to 
follow your own rules, becomes an EMTALA violation when the policies are related to the medical screening and stabilization of patients 
in the ED.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه سياسات المستشفى المكتوبة بتصير هي معيار المستشفى القانوني تحت EMTALA. يعني إذا ما التزمت بالقواعد المكتوبة عندك، هاد بيترجم لخرق في EMTALA. والخرق بيكون لما هالسياسات تخص الفحص الطبي وتثبيت استقرار المرضى في الـ ED. عشان كده جواب A هو الأصح، لأنه failure to follow your own rules بحد ذاته مصدر مسؤولية قانونية.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار B أو C أو D لأنهم أخطاء واضحة ومباشرة. بس هاد السؤال عن مصدر liability مرتبط بـ EMTALA تحديداً، وهنا الخرق بيكون لما ما تلتزم بالسياسات المكتوبة.

question:
A 73-year-old woman is brought by private ambulance to the emergency department (ED) for shortness of breath. Due to ED overcrowding, there are several ambulance stretchers in line ahead of 
her at triage. At what point does the hospital accept responsibility 
for this patient?

options.text: When she was placed in the ambulance
When the ambulance arrived on hospital property
When the patient is seen by the emergency clinician
When the patient is seen by triage personnel

correctAnswer: When the ambulance arrived on hospital property
englishExplanation:
The Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act 
(EMTALA) defines the time of acceptance of responsibility as when 
the patient comes to the ED. In its EMTALA regulations, the Centers 
for Medicare and Medicaid (CMS) defines the term comes to the ED 
to include anywhere on hospital property, so the hospital’s duty and 
responsibility for the patient are triggered when the ambulance arrives 
on hospital property.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه EMTALA بتحدد لحظة قبول المسؤولية للمريض لما يوصل الـ ED، و CMS بتفسّر عبارة comes to the ED على إنها أي مكان داخل أرض المستشفى. يعني لحظة وصول الإسعاف لأرض المستشفى هي اللي بتبدأ فيها مسؤولية المستشفى، وما بيفرق إذا كان في طابور من الـ stretchers قدام بسبب الازدحام. عشان كده جواب B هو الأصح، حتى لو المريض ما انشاف بعد.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار C أو D لأنهم بيبانوا منطقيين، يعني إنك لازم تشوف المريض بالعيادة. بس حتى لو ما انشاف من emergency clinician أو من triage، وصول الإسعاف لأرض المستشفى بكفّي.

question:
According to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services 
(CMS), which of the following patients may a hospital with specialized capabilities and available capacity refuse to accept in transfer 
solely because the patient is uninsured?

options.text: A patient with an unstable emergency condition admitted to
Any patient the hospital chooses to reject
An emergency department (ED) patient with an unstable emergency condition who is at another hospital that is unable to stabilize the patient
An inpatient with an unstable emergency condition at another

correctAnswer: An inpatient with an unstable emergency condition at another
englishExplanation:
CMS guidelines state that hospitals do not have to accept 
an inpatient, as defined by CMS, in transfer from another hospital 
under any circumstances, even if its decision to decline to accept the 
patient in transfer will result in the patient’s death.

CHAPTER E8  Quality Improvement and Patient Safety
2453.e83
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه Medicare بيميّز بين الـ outpatients والـ inpatients حسب تعريف CMS، وهاد التمييز مهم بكل سؤال نقل. و guidelines الـ CMS بتقول إن المستشفى مش ملزوم يقبل أي inpatient من مستشفى ثاني بالـ transfer تحت أي ظرف. وحتى لو رفضه معناه إنه ممكن يموت، المستشفى مش ملزوم. عشان كده جواب D هو الأصح، أما مريض الـ ED فيحميه EMTALA.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار C وتفتكر إن المريض بحالة غير مستقرة لازم ينقل. صحيح إن EMTALA بتغطي مريض الـ ED، أما الـ inpatient فما إله حق إنو ينقل بالـ transfer، وما في مستشفى ملزم يقبله.

question: Which of the following triage assessments are important contributors to error in emergency medicine?

options.text: Inappropriate triage to a treatment area

correctAnswer: Inappropriate triage to a treatment area
englishExplanation:
An inappropriate triage to a specific treatment area may 
create a bias in the minds of the treating physician and staff, leading 
to delays in care or misdiagnoses. This may be more pronounced with 
undertriage versus overtriage.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه لما تعمل triage للمريض على منطقة علاج مش مناسبة، هاد بيخلق bias في ذهن الطبيب والطاقم اللي عاملين مع المريض. التحيّز هاد بيخليهم يتأخروا بالعلاج أو يعملوا misdiagnosis. وهاد بيكون أوضح إذا كان undertriage مقارنة بـ overtriage. عشان كده جواب C هو الأصح، لأن التوجيه لأرضية العلاج الغلط بيأثر على كل قرار بعده.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار triage by age أو triage by nursing personnel لأنهم طرق triage حقيقية ومعروفة. بس هي طرق مقبولة، المشكلة الحقيقية لما توجّه المريض لمكان علاج غلط وتخلق bias عند الفريق.

question: What is a key driver of patient experience?
englishExplanation:
Key drivers of patient experience are communication, 
empathy, expectation setting, and wait times.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه تجربة المريض مش بس عن النتيجة، بل عن كيف صار التعامل معه من أوله لآخره. والعنصر الأساسي اللي بيحدد هالتجربة هو Communication، ومعها empathy و expectation setting و wait times. يعني لازم تركّز على طريقة الكلام مع المريض لأنها هي المحرك الأول. وجود خبرة الطاقم أو ED boarding أو nursing ratios بيأثر برضو، بس مو المفتاح الأساسي.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار ED boarding أو years of staff experience لأنهم بتبانوا مؤثرين بوضوح. بس السؤال عن key driver لتجربة المريض، و Communication هي العنصر الأول اللي بيربط كل شي.

question:
What specific strategies exist to impact individual wellness for 
emergency clinicians?

options.text: A focus on individual well-being alone is usually sufficient to
Vigorous daily exercise has been shown to improve the ability to
Peer groups that allow for reflection and sharing on the meaning
Health care organizational engagement has little impact in individual physician wellness but can improve efficiency of care in

correctAnswer: Peer groups that allow for reflection and sharing on the meaning
englishExplanation:
The current consensus suggests the importance of physicians focusing on their own well-being, but this alone is not enough 
to prevent burnout. Physical exercise has been shown to improve the 
mood of physicians and to help them cope with difficult situations. A 
strong business case exists for organizations to invest in and promote 
engagement in combatting and reducing physician burnout, including 
strategies of supporting executive leadership dedicated to improving 
and sustaining professional well-being across organizations.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه التركيز على well-being الفرد لحاله مش كافي، لأنه ما بيمنع الـ burnout بنفسه. الـ Physical exercise حسّن mood الأطباء وساعدهم يتعاملوا مع المواقف الصعبة. وكمان الـ peer groups اللي بتسمح بالتأمل وبتقاسم المعنى بتزيد engagement الأطباء وبتقلل depersonalization، والمنظمات لما استثمرت وروّجت للengagement صار عندها سبب قوي يقلل الـ burnout، وهاد كله بيخلي جواب C هو الأصح.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار A أو B لأنهم كلهم يبدو منطقيين ومفيدين. بس التركيز على الفرد لحاله أو على التمارين لحاله ما بكفي للوقاية من الـ burnout، والـ peer groups بتأكد على Reflection والمشاركة.

question:
A systems model of physician burnout includes all of the following 
features, except:

options.text: Governmental agencies and regulatory bodies including licensing boards

englishExplanation:
The process of physician burnout is complex and occurs 
within a multilevel system that includes the individual, the front-line 
care delivery team, the health care organization, and the external environment (governmental agencies, regulatory bodies, societal norms, 
etc.) (see Fig. e10.3). To effectively address burnout, interventions must 
be directed at all levels of this complex system

2456.e111
CHAPTER e11  Forensic Emergency Medicine
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ burnout عملية معقدة بتصير جوّه نظام متعدد المستويات. هاد النظام بيضم الفرد بنفسه، وفريق تقديم الرعاية في الـ front line، ومؤسسة الرعاية الصحية، والبيئة الخارجية اللي فيها governmental agencies و regulatory bodies و societal norms. ولأن المشكلة متشعّبة بهالشكل، أي تدخل لازم يوجّه لكل المستويات مع بعض، والديني ما هو جزء من النموذج، لذلك الجواب D.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار A أو C لأنهم يبانوا مكونات واضحة في النظام. بس الـ burnout بيصير عند الفرد والمؤسسة والبيئة الخارجية، ومفيش عنصر ديني مذكور ضمن مكونات النموذج.

question:
Which of the following best defines direct medical oversight in the 
prehospital setting?

options.text: Concurrent direction of EMTs providing patient care
Use of prehospital patient care protocols
Use of standing field treatment protocols

correctAnswer: Concurrent direction of EMTs providing patient care
englishExplanation:
Direct medical oversight is the concurrent direction of 
EMTs providing patient care, which can be at the scene or online over 
radio or cell phone.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ direct medical oversight معناه إن الطبيب يوجّه الـ EMTs اللي بيدعموا المريض بشكل مباشر ومتزامن وقت ما بيعالجوا المريض. وهاد ممكن يكون على موقع الحدث أو أونلاين عن طريق الراديو أو الهاتف. يعني ما هو policies أو protocols مكتوبة ولا quality improvement program، الجواب A هو الأصح لأنه التعريف المباشر للإشراف الطبي.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار B أو D لأنهم جزء مهم من EMS. بس هدول أدوات وبروتوكولات جاهزة، أما الـ direct medical oversight فهو توجيه مباشر ولحظي من الطبيب للـ EMTs.

question:
Which of the following prehospital interventions has been shown to 
improve patient outcome?

options.text: Endotracheal intubation in severe head trauma

englishExplanation:
Rapid defibrillation has been shown to improve outcomes 
for patients in cardiopulmonary arrest; other interventions have not 
shown proven benefit in the prehospital setting.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ defibrillation السريع اتثبت إنه يحسّن نتائج المرضى اللي عندهم cardiopulmonary arrest. وهاد هو الشي الوحيد اللي لقيت له فائدة مثبتة في بيئة ما قبل المستشفى. أما endotracheal intubation للأطفال أو في severe head trauma أو intraosseous needle placement أو needle cricothyrotomy، فمافيهم فائدة مثبتة في الـ prehospital setting. عشان كده جواب A هو الأصح.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار endotracheal intubation لأنه إجراء بيبان قوي ومألوف للطلبة. بس الفايدة المثبتة في الـ prehospital setting هي الـ rapid defibrillation وبس، أما الباقي فلسه ما أثبتت فايدة.

question: Which of the following statements is true regarding air medical transport (AMT)?

options.text: AMT does little to improve outcomes when used for STEMI transport from rural areas.
AMT scene response for acute stroke is limited by emergency medical service providers' inability to effectively triage and identify patients who would likely benefit from HEMS scene response.
Faster times to a trauma center are not required for outcomes benefit from AMT.
The emphasis for AMT of neonates is often more on the mode of transport than on the transport team.

correctAnswer: Faster times to a trauma center are not required for outcomes benefit from AMT.
englishExplanation: Air medical transport may provide outcome benefit for selected trauma patients beyond simple transport time reduction. Appropriate use depends on patient severity, geography, crew capability, and access to definitive trauma care. For some patients, the advanced team and earlier critical-care interventions may contribute to benefit even when faster arrival alone is not the only driver.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ AMT ممكن يفيد بعض مرضى الـ trauma بنتيجة أحسن، حتى لو ما كانت الفايدة بس تقليل وقت النقل. والفايدة تعتمد على شدة حالة المريض والجغرافيا وقدرة الطاقم وإمكانية الوصول لعناية trauma نهائية. ولبعض المرضى، الفريق المتقدم والتدخلات المبكرة في critical care بيكونوا مصدر الفايدة، فجواب C هو الأصح.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار A أو B لأنهم يبانوا منطقيين. بس الـ AMT مو بس نقل أسرع، الفريق المتقدم والتدخلات المبكرة ممكن يفرقوا حتى بدون وصول أسرع.

question:
Safety is a critical consideration for all air medical operations. 
Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: If the patient’s condition is severe, it is prudent to request service
Spectators should be kept at least 200 feet away from the landing
The use of a hospital helipad for emergency medical service
Vehicles and personnel should be kept at least 50 feet away from

correctAnswer: Spectators should be kept at least 200 feet away from the landing
englishExplanation:
2458.e133
CHAPTER E13  Air Medical Transport
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه السلامة من أهم الاعتبارات في كل عمليات الـ air medical، وهاد بيخلي ترتيب منطقة الهبوط جزء أساسي من الشغل. الجواب الصح بيقول إن المشاهدين لازم يبعدوا 200 feet على الأقل عن منطقة الهبوط. أمّا الـ vehicles والأشخاص فالمسافة عندهم 50 feet، وهاد الفرق اللي لازم تاخده بالاعتبار، فالخيار B هو اللي بيعبّر عن مطلب السلامة.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار D وتخلط بين vehicles والأشخاص وبين المشاهدين، أو تختار C وتركز على helipad المستشفى. الخيار B بيتكلم عن المشاهدين و200 feet عن منطقة الهبوط.

question:
A working knowledge of aviation physiology is vital to understanding the effects of AMT on pilots, medical personnel, and patients. 
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the aviation 
physiology gas laws?

options.text: Boyle’s law explains the physiologic effects of expansion and
Charles’ law can be shown as Pt = P1 + P2 + P3…Pn.
Dalton’s law accounts for the gas changes that result in decompression sickness.
Henry’s law explains why the ambient temperature decreases

correctAnswer: Boyle’s law explains the physiologic effects of expansion and
englishExplanation: [Explanation unavailable in supplied source]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه Boyle's law بتشرح العلاقة بين ضغط الغاز وحجمه، وهاد الأساس اللي بيشرح التغيرات الفسيولوجية لما الغازات بتتمدد أو بتنتكمش في المساحات المغلقة داخل الجسم. التغيير في الارتفاع أثناء الطيران بيأثر على الضغط، وهاد بينعكس على الغازات المحبوسة في الجسم. وبما إن السؤال عن aviation physiology gas laws، فجواب A هو الأصح، أما صيغ الباقي فهي مش صحيحة.
الفخ: الخطر إنك تختار Charles' law أو Dalton's law أو Henry's law لأنها أسماء قوانين gases مشهورة. بس كل واحد منهم بيشرح علاقة مختلفة، والعلاقة بين الضغط والحجم هي Boyle's law.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct with regard to landing 
zone safety?

options.text: During night operations, spotlights should be toward the
If the aircraft is parked on a slope, approach and depart on the
In a rear-loading helicopter, it is safe to approach or depart from
Vehicles and personnel should be kept at least 50 ft from the

correctAnswer: If the aircraft is parked on a slope, approach and depart on the
englishExplanation: [Explanation unavailable in supplied source]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة الصحيحة هي B، وبتقول إنو إذا كانت الطائرة متوقفة على منحدر، بنقرب منها وبننطلق باتجاه الجانب النازل يعني الـdownhill side. يعني المعنى الأساسي: الاقتراب والإقلاع لازم يصيروا على جهة النزول من المنحدر. الخيارات التانية كلها بتتكلم عن شي ثاني عن سلامة منطقة الهبوط وما إلها علاقة بالطائرة المتوقفة على منحدر. ولازم نذكر إنو المصدر ما فيه شرح مفصل لهاد البند، فكل اللي بنقدر نأكده هو جواب الخيار نفسه.
الفخ: الفخ إنو تختار خيار ثاني لأنك تفتكر إنو السؤال عن أمان منطقة الهبوط بشكل عام، مثل مسافة الـ50 ft عن الـrotor أو الـspotlights وقت الليل. لازم تميز إنو السؤال عن طائرة واقفة على منحدر، فالجواب لازم يحكي عن جهة النزول.

question:
How can one characterize application of the Secondary Assessment 
of Victim Endpoint (SAVE) triage guidelines?

options.text: Triage decisions are based on patient outcome expectations.
It is applicable to day-to-day hospital operations.
Patients are sorted immediately after the incident.
The guidelines provide detailed management of psychogenic

correctAnswer: Triage decisions are based on patient outcome expectations.
englishExplanation:
The SAVE system is designed specifically for care in an 
austere environment. It triages patients into (1) those who will die 
regardless of treatment, (2) those who will live regardless of treatment, 
and (3) those who would benefit from austere intervention. The triage 
decisions are based on field outcome expectations from existing survival and morbidity statistics.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة A صح لأن قرارات الفرز في نظام SAVE بتتبني على توقعات نتائج المرضى بالميدان، وهاد بياخد من إحصائيات البقاء والـmorbidity الموجودة. نظام SAVE مصمم خصيصاً للتعامل مع المرضى في بيئة فقيرة شوية، وبيصنّفهم لثلاث فئات: اللي رح يموتوا سواء انعالجوا أو لا، واللي رح يعيشوا سواء انعالجوا أو لا، واللي رح يستفيدوا من تداخل محدود. يعني البنية كلها مرتكزة على احتمالات النتيجة، مش على ترتيب سريع أو على تشغيل يومي.
الفخ: خيار B هو الفخ الأكبر، لأنه يخلّيك تفتكر إنو SAVE تصلح للاستخدام اليومي بالمستشفى، بينما هي مصممة لبيئة الكوارث القاسية. وخيار C فخ تاني لأنو الفرز بيصير حسب النتيجة المتوقعة من العلاج، مش لمجرد وصول المريض بعد الحادث.

question: Which of the following best describes the National Disaster Medical System (NDMS)?

options.text: It does not include private sector institutions.
It does not involve the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).
The medical response element consists of Department of Defense
The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) has

correctAnswer: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) has
englishExplanation:
The NDMS is a federally coordinated initiative that is a 
cooperative program between the DoD, VA, DHHS, and Department 
of Homeland Security (DHS) with oversight provided by DHHS. The 
NDMS provides a system of coordinated mutual aid agreements among 
federal, state, local, and private institutional entities for resource and 
personnel provision in times of disaster. The medical response element 
includes dozens of volunteer civilian medical teams that supplement 
the local medical infrastructure.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة D صح لأن الـNational Disaster Medical System (NDMS) هو مبادرة فيدرالية منسّقة، وبرنامج تعاوني بين الـDoD والـVA وDHHS وDHS، والإشراف عليه بيكون من DHHS. الـNDMS بيوفّر نظام اتفاقيات مساعدة متبادلة بين الجهات الفيدرالية والولاية والمحلية والمؤسسات الخاصة، عشان توصل الموارد والأشخاص وقت الكوارث. وعنصر الاستجابة الطبية فيه بضم فرق طبية مدنية متطوعة بتكمّل البنية الطبية المحلية.
الفخ: الخيارات التانية بتوهمك إنو النظام ما إلو ارتباط بالـVA أو إنو ما بيطلع فيه القطاع الخاص، بينما هو برنامج تعاوني بيشملهم كلهم. وخيار C فخ لأنه بيخلّيك تفتكر إنو عنصر الاستجابة الطبية هو الـDoD، والحقيقة إنو الفرق المدنية المتطوعة هي اللي بتكمّل البنية المحلية.

question:
What is accurate advice that one would give to those planning a 
disaster response?

options.text: Critical incident stress debriefing is best conducted 1 or 2 weeks
Medical resupply systems are the most vulnerable component of
One of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) system’s four
The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has a

correctAnswer: One of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) system’s four
englishExplanation:
One of the VA health system’s four mandated missions is 
emergency management. Although controversy exists, critical incident 
stress debriefing, if used, should be implemented as early as possible. 
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has full-spectrum disaster coordinating responsibility. Communications systems are likely the 
most vulnerable systems.

Emergency Medical Services and Disaster Preparedness
2459.e146
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة C صح لأن مهمة إدارة الطوارئ (emergency management) هي واحدة من المهام الأربعة المفروضة قانونياً لنظام صحة الـVA. هاد بيخلي الـVA طرف أساسي في التخطيط للكوارث والاستجابة إلها، فأي حدا بخطط لوقت الكوارث لازم يحسب حسابه. ولازم تذكر كمان إنو DHS عندها مسؤولية التنسيق الكاملة عبر كل مراحل الكوارث، وإنو أنظمة اتصالات التواصل هي غالباً أضعف الأنظمة.
الفخ: خيار A فخ لأنه بيوحي إنو الـcritical incident stress debriefing لازم ينتظر أسبوع أو أسبوعين، والحقيقة إنه لازم ينعمل بأسرع وقت ممكن إذا انستخدم. وخيار D فخ لأنه بيوحي إنو FEMA هي المسؤولة الكاملة، بينما التنسيق الكامل موزعة على DHS.

question:
Which of the following statements is not a feature of comprehensive 
emergency management?

options.text: An incident management system consistent with NIMS should
Health care facilities should perform a hazard vulnerability analysis to assess community risks.
Most incident management systems are characterized by five
The four phases of comprehensive emergency management

correctAnswer: The four phases of comprehensive emergency management
englishExplanation:
The four phases of CEM are mitigation, preparedness, 
response, and recovery. These phases represent a continuum over time, 
and more than one phase may be in effect at the same time (e.g., even 
during the response phases, recovery actions may take place.)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة D هي اللي موش feature من الـcomprehensive emergency management، لأن المراحل الأربعة الحقيقية هي mitigation وpreparedness وresponse وrecovery. الخيار D بيحكي عن pre-event وevent وpost-event وrecovery، وهاد تقسيم غلط. المراحل هي continuum على مدار الوقت، وممكن أكتر من مرحلة تكون شغالة بنفس الوقت، يعني وقت response ممكن تبلّش إجراءات recovery عملياً. وهاد الفرق لازم يكون واضح وقت ما تبني خطة.
الفخ: الفخ إنو تختار A أو C لأنهم بيكملوا بشكل منطقي عن الـNIMS، بس موش كل جملة عن emergency management بتكون feature منو. لازم تركز على تقسيم المراحل: mitigation وpreparedness وresponse وrecovery، موش pre-event وevent وpost-event.

question:
After an earthquake, what resource would be expected to provide 
the most rapid and effective search and rescue activity finding the 
most victims who would most likely survive?
englishExplanation:
Uninjured survivors perform the most rapid and effective 
search and rescue activity after an earthquake. These private citizens 
will recover most victims who ultimately survive. Although formal 
urban search and rescue teams will eventually arrive, they do not find 
many victims and it is unknown how many survive. National Guard 
Civilian Support Teams and disaster medical assistance teams do not 
perform search and rescue activities.
   

CHAPTER E15  Weapons of Mass Destruction
2460.e159
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة B صح لأن الناجين غير الجرحى بيعملوا أسرع وأكتر فعالية بعملية البحث والإنقاذ بعد الزلزال، وهولك بيسترجعوا أكثر الضحايا اللي رح يبقوا أحياء. فرق البحث والإنقاذ الرسمية بتيجي بعدين، بس ما بتلاقي ضحايا كثيرين، ومن غير ما تعرف كم منهم رح ينجو. وبالآخر، فرق الـNational Guard Civil Support وفرق الـdisaster medical assistance ما بتعمل بحث وإنقاذ أصلاً.
الفخ: الفخ إنو تختار A لأنو الكلام عن فرق البحث والإنقاذ، بس هاد ضعيف لأنو الفرق الرسمية بتوصل متأخر وبتلقى ضحايا قليلين. وخيار C وD زي بعض، يعني الفرق دي ما بيعملوا بحث وإنقاذ أصلاً، فاللي بيعملوه هم الناس العاديين.

question: Which of the following statements best describes issues in management of anthrax infection?

options.text: Antibiotics do not change the mortality of cutaneous disease.
Doxycycline or ciprofloxacin are both options for single-agent
Sputum culture and Gram stain obtained early in the disease

englishExplanation:
Cutaneous anthrax causes a severe, although nontender, 
peripheral vesicle that progresses to an eschar accompanied by 
regional adenopathy. Antibiotics lower the mortality from cutaneous 
anthrax twenty-fold. For inhalational, gastrointestinal, and cutaneous anthrax with toxicity, intravenous (IV) treatment is with ciprofloxacin or doxycycline plus at least two other agents. Regarding 
inhalational anthrax, mechanical ventilation may not improve mortality and sputum cultures and Gram stains are not helpful until late 
in the disease.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة B صح لأن الـcutaneous anthrax بيسبب فقاعة (vesicle) على الأطراف، وهاي الفقاعة شديدة رغم إنها non-tender، يعني المصاب ما بيحس بألم لما تضغط عليها. بعدها بتتحول إلى eschar مع تضخم الغدد اللمفية في نفس المنطقة. ولازم تذكر إنو الـantibiotics بتخفض وفيات الـcutaneous anthrax بعشرين ضعف، يعني العلاج مهم، بس الألم مش من الأعراض اللي بتوصف.
الفخ: خيار A فخ لأنه بيوحي إنو الـantibiotics ما بتنفع، والحقيقة إنها بتخفض الوفيات بعشرين مرة. وخيار D فخ لأنه بيوحي إنو الـsputum culture والـGram stain بيساعدوا من أول المرض، بس هما ما بيفيدوا إلا متأخرين في الـinhalational anthrax.

question:
Several children ages 5 to 8 years old have definitely been exposed 
to anthrax spores. Health department officials have brought these 
children to the emergency department (ED). They are all ambulatory with normal vital signs and without symptoms. Which of the 
following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Outpatient ciprofloxacin for 60 days or until the children have

correctAnswer: Outpatient ciprofloxacin for 60 days or until the children have
englishExplanation:
See Box e15.5. For children without toxicity, ciprofloxacin, doxycycline, or amoxicillin orally is indicated for a minimum of 60 
days or until the child has received three doses of vaccine. The vaccine 
has not been approved for children but may be indicated to reduce the 
long-term exposure to antibiotics. Note that weaponized anthrax may 
be penicillin-resistant.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة C صح لأن الأطفال اللي اتعرضوا لـanthrax spores بدون أعراض وبدون toxicity، لازم ياخدوا ciprofloxacin عن طريق الفم لحد 60 يوم على الأقل أو لحد ما ياخدوا ثلاث جرعات من الـvaccine. هاد لأنه بدون toxicity بيكون العلاج عن طريق الفم كافياً. والـvaccine لسه ما معتمد للأطفال، بس ممكن ينقص التعرض الطويل للمضادات الحيوية. ولازم تذكر إنو الـanthrax المسلّح ممكن يكون مقاوم للpenicillin.
الفخ: الفخ إنو تختار D أو B لأنهم أقصر مدة، بس الـpenicillin VK لسبعة إلى عشرة أيام أو doxycycline لخمس أيام ما بتغطي فترة الحماية اللي بتحتاجها. وكمان الـweaponized anthrax ممكن يكون مقاوم للpenicillin، فالإعتماد عليه خطر.

question: Which of the following statements regarding blast injury is true?

options.text: Classically, there are three different types of blast injury.
Primary blast injury is caused by flying debris and bomb fragments.
Exacerbation of asthma is an example of tertiary blast injury.
Secondary blast injury is the most common cause of morbidity

correctAnswer: Secondary blast injury is the most common cause of morbidity
englishExplanation:
Of the four types of blast injury, secondary blast injury is 
the most common cause of morbidity and mortality. These injuries are 
caused by flying debris generated by the explosion. An asthma exacerbation could be considered a quaternary injury in the correct setting. 
Tympanic membrane rupture is not an accurate predictor of internal 
injuries in blast events.
   

CHAPTER E16  Tactical Emergency Medical Support and Urban Search and Rescue
2462.e167
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة D صح لأنو من الأنواع الأربعة لإصابات الانفجار، الـsecondary blast injury هو السبب الأكثر شيوعاً للـmorbidity والوفاة بعد حدث الانفجار. وسببه القطع والمتفرجات اللي بتطلع من الانفجار وتصيب الجسم مباشرة، يعني أكثر من نصف الإصابات سببها الحطام المتطاير. ولازم تذكر إنو الـexacerbation للـasthma ممكن يتحسب إصابة quaternary في السياق المناسب، وإنو تمزق الـtympanic membrane مش مؤشر دقيق لإصابات داخلية.
الفخ: خيار B فخ لأنه بيخلط بين الـprimary والـsecondary، فالـprimary بسببها الضغط بتأثير الموجة، أما الـsecondary فالطيران والمتفرجات. وخيار C فخ لأنه بيوحي إنو الـasthma tertiary، بينما حسب الشرح ممكن تكون quaternary.

question:
The principles of TEMS have largely developed from which type of 
incidents?
englishExplanation:
The principles of TEMS have largely developed from lessons learned during military conflicts and most closely emulate the 
medical support structure of military special operations units.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة B صح لأن مبادئ الـTEMS (Tactical Emergency Medical Support) في معظمها تطورت من الدروس المستفادة أثناء الصراعات العسكرية. والنتيجة إنو أكثر نظام بتقلّده هو بنية الدعم الطبي عند وحدات العمليات العسكرية الخاصة. يعني هاد المجال نشأ من بيئة عسكرية مش من الكوارث المدنية، مع إنه بيشتغل جوّه ساحة المعركة. ولما تسمع عن TEMS لازم تفكر بالميدان military مش بالـcivilian disasters.
الفخ: الفخ إنو تختار A أو C لأنهم بيبانوا منطقيين، بس مبادئ TEMS ما انبنت على أحداث الـmulticasualty ولا على الكوارث الطبيعية. التمييز بسيط: الأساس تاريخياً هو الصراعات العسكرية وبنية العمليات الخاصة.

question:
Which of the following is the primary responsibility of the USAR 
team emergency clinician?

options.text: Ensuring a public health framework exists for the region
Ensuring that entering a collapsed building is safe
Supporting the health and welfare of team members

correctAnswer: Supporting the health and welfare of team members
englishExplanation:
The USAR team emergency clinician must be familiar 
with the types of medical conditions that may be encountered by the 
team. The USAR team emergency clinician has a primary responsibility to the team members should they require medical attention. Secondarily, treatment of entrapped patients can be done but is not their 
primary mission. Ensuring broader elements of a public framework in 
a disaster-affected area is typically beyond the conventional role of the 
USAR clinician, though this individual may liaison with other health 
and medical personnel in the same geographic area of operations.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة D صح لأن مسؤوليته الأساسية كطبيب طوارئ بفريق الـUSAR هي أعضاء الفريق أنفسهم إذا احتاجوا عناية طبية. ولازم يكون عارف أنواع الحالات الطبية اللي ممكن تصير للفريق. وعلاج المرضى المحتجزين ممكن ينعمل، بس مش مهمته الأساسية. وأما بناء إطار عام للصحة العامة بالمنطقة فبيتجاوز الدور الاعتيادي، مع إنه ممكن ينسق مع كوادر صحية ثانية بنفس منطقة العمليات.
الفخ: خيار C هو الفخ لأنه بيوحي إنو مهمته الأساسية علاج المحتجزين، والحقيقة هاد عمل ثانوي. وخيار A فخ لأنه بيخلّيك تفتكر إنو دوره بناء framework للصحة العامة بالمنطقة، وده برّا الدور التقليدي للطبيب.

CHAPTER E1: QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
1. Research projects based in settings outside of the GEM physician’s
home country require which of the following special considerations
with regard to research ethics?

options.text: Ethical approval must be obtained only at the GEM physician’s
United States-based IRBs do not cover international settings, and
Ethical approval is required from both the GEM physician’s
If the research is planned in a country that does not have an IRB,

correctAnswer: Ethical approval is required from both the GEM physician’s
englishExplanation:
Ethical approval for any research project must be obtained
from the GEM physician’s home institution, any partner institutions,
and any research sites. In the event that a formal IRB does not exist for
a certain research site, efforts must be made to obtain and document
ethical approval from an appropriate site representative.

CHAPTER E14: QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
1. How can one characterize application of the Secondary Assessment
of Victim Endpoint (SAVE) triage guidelines?

options.text: Triage decisions are based on patient outcome expectations.
It is applicable to day- to- day hospital operations.
Patients are sorted immediately after the incident.
The guidelines provide detailed management of psychogenic

correctAnswer: Triage decisions are based on patient outcome expectations.
englishExplanation:
The SAVE system is designed specifically for care in an
austere environment. It triages patients into (1) those who will die
regardless of treatment, (2) those who will live regardless of treatment,
and (3) those who would benefit from austere intervention. The triage
decisions are based on field outcome expectations from existing sur -
vival and morbidity statistics.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة A صح لأن نظام SAVE مبني على توقعات النتائج بالميدان، يعني بيستخدم إحصائيات البقاء والـmorbidity الموجودة لتقدير نتيجة كل مريض. وSAVE مصمم خصيصاً للتعامل مع المرضى في بيئة austere، وبيصنّفهم لثلاث فئات: اللي رح يموتوا سواء انعالجوا أو لا، واللي رح يعيشوا سواء انعالجوا أو لا، واللي رح يستفيدوا من تداخل محدود. يعني قرارات الفرز عنده مرتبطة بالنتيجة المتوقعة من المريض.
الفخ: B فخ لأنه بيوحي إنو SAVE للتشغيل اليومي بالمستشفى، وC فench لأنه بيحكي عن فرز فوري بعد الحادث. التمييز إنو SAVE شغل بيئة الكوارث القاسية، والقرار فيها بينصم على احتمالية النتيجة من العلاج مش على التوقيت.

CHAPTER E11: QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
1. When documenting a gunshot wound, it is important to do which
of the following?

options.text: Describe the appearance, physical characteristics, and location
Determine the type of bullet used.
Estimate the caliber of the bullet.

correctAnswer: Describe the appearance, physical characteristics, and location
englishExplanation:
Emergency clinicians should not identify wounds as
“entrance” or “exit. ” Instead, their charting should include a detailed
description, using appropriate forensic terminology, of the wound’s
characteristics and location without speculating about its function or
the caliber or type of bullet (projectile) used to create it.

question: A newly graduated emergency physician is comparing contracts for multiple job offers. Some jobs will have her working as an employee while others would compensate her as an independent contractor. Which of the following should she be aware of as an independent contractor?

options.text: Independent contractors are legally required to waive their due process rights
Independent contractors are more likely to be audited by the IRS
Independent contractors are paid only on a relative value unit basis
Independent contractors report their income on a W-2 form

correctAnswer: Independent contractors are more likely to be audited by the IRS
englishExplanation:
Emergency medicine contracts, like any employment contract, require a basic understanding of legal and financial concepts that every physician should possess. Without careful scrutiny and attention, physicians may enter into a contract that may be unfair, difficult to get out of, or contain items that may portend a difficult work environment. In general, there are three employment models under which most contracts are written: employee, independent contractor, or partner. Employees are hired by the hospital and are generally paid a yearly salary for an agreed-upon number of hours worked. For the most part, they are offered a benefits package including health, disability, and life insurance, as well as retirement benefits. The employer or hospital withholds taxes from each employee’s paycheck as well. Employed physicians generally enjoy more job security and may also be sheltered from having personal assets targeted in the event of a lawsuit.

The independent contractor employment model classifies an individual as their own company or business offering their services in a way they see fit. This model affords greater flexibility, more control, and certain tax advantages, and physicians can customize their benefits and retirement since they are normally not provided as a benefit. Disadvantages include more money dedicated to overhead costs, including accounting and legal fees, and less job security. Furthermore, because the government dictates whether someone qualifies as an independent contractor, they are more likely to be audited by the IRS.

Partnership opportunities allow physicians to buy into usually a small independent group and offer a track to eventually become an equal partner and owner of the group and share in the profits. Physicians must also be aware of other key issues included in every contract other than scheduling parameters, compensation, and nonclinical duties. Most contracts provide information for termination due to a material breach of the contract. This should be specific, outline what constitutes a material breach, and allow for the amelioration of the breach if desired by the physician. Due process is a legal term that dictates physicians should be afforded a hearing prior to involuntary termination. However, many contracts include terms that allow for termination without cause. With the rise of contract management groups employing physicians at many hospitals across the country, it is common that contracts include a waiver of due process. Contracts should contain language delineating whose responsibility it is to purchase a tail coverage. Tail coverage refers to insurance purchased to protect against possible future claims against a physician that occurred prior to his or her termination date. Lastly, restrictive covenants or noncompete clauses may be included in contracts to dissuade or prevent physicians from leaving to work for a competitor. Some states have banned restrictive covenants altogether, while others allow them to exist based on a geographical area or for a reasonable period after employment.



Independent contractors are not legally required to waive their due process rights (A) as hospitals are required by law to afford physicians due process rights. However, many contracts require that physicians waive this right and it cannot be negotiated.

Independent contractors are not only paid on a relative value unit basis (C). They can be paid purely hourly, on a relative unit value basis, or a combination of both. Relative value units are used by Medicare to provide economic values for services provided and, in some contracts, are used to pay physicians based on productivity.

Independent contractors report their income on a 1099-MISC form (D) and calculate their taxes in this way. Employees receive W-2 forms from their employers yearly, outlining their compensation and the taxes withheld.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the definition of an integration clause?

Reveal Answer:
A clause in a contract that states that everything written in the contract supersedes any verbal or written agreements made prior to the contract signing and is unenforceable.

question: In a rural emergency department, there is only one surgeon who works on call. The surgeon is becoming overwhelmed with the volume of consults that occur and, as a result, is considering quitting and moving to an academic hospital. This would result in significant issues in caring for patients in this region. The emergency department director meets with the surgeon, and they come up with a plan that during the night hours, there will be no consults unless they involve an immediately life-threatening process. This should reduce night consults by ≥ 90%. The surgeon agrees to arrive at the hospital at 7 AM every day to begin seeing all the consults in person the following morning. Which of the following types of conflict resolution is this?
englishExplanation:
There are many methods of conflict resolution. It is important to approach conflicts with the mindset that the issue at hand needs to be resolved while considering future rapport that can be built or tarnished in the process. It is best to pick methods that involve working together and coming to a resolution acceptable to both parties. Sometimes, accommodation is the most appropriate method of resolving conflict when it comes with minimal cost to the accommodating party and does not set a bad precedent. Negotiation is another method in which both parties have an exchange. There is a give-and-take approach to the issue, and finally, both parties come to an agreement that is acceptable. Negotiation involves slightly more conflict than collaboration. Collaboration involves taking an approach in which both parties actively work together to fix an issue (less of a give-and-take and more of a “how can we both fix this” mindset). Finally, sometimes it may be challenging to resolve a conflict. Arbitration is a process whereby a third party bridges the gap and observes and interacts with individuals in conflict. They may more empathetically understand the challenges from each party’s viewpoint and attempt to smooth over any conflicts that may arise.



Avoidance (A) involves avoiding the issue entirely and not discussing it. There are many circumstances in which avoidance is appropriate. An example is if a physician found their colleague annoying when working next to them on shift. If a simple solution exists, such as moving to a different workstation, that is a better and simpler method of dealing with the issue when compared to other methods. Confrontation (C) would involve directly calling out the person involved and arguing about their action or decision. An example of confrontation would be calling out the surgeon in a staff meeting and directly bringing up the harm his leaving would potentially bring to the hospital and patients. While confrontation may be a part of conflict resolution, when very direct and aggressive, it is often unlikely to be effective. Litigation (D) involves using the law to resolve an issue. An example of litigation may be filing a lawsuit against a hospital that violates an employment agreement. This is the most costly and often the most unpleasant method of dealing with conflict.

One Step Further
Question:
What type of conflict resolution technique involves finding a middle ground in which both parties give and take to reach an agreement?

Reveal Answer:
Compromise.

question: Which anatomic site of central venous access is associated with the lowest rates of bloodstream infection and thrombosis?
englishExplanation:
Central venous access is common in critically ill patients, and the catheters are often placed in the emergency department prior to admission. Complications of central venous catheterization include both immediate complications and delayed complications. Immediate complications include bleeding, arterial puncture or cannulation, pneumothorax, dysrhythmia, catheter malposition, and air embolism. Delayed complications include infection, venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, and venous stenosis. Ultrasound-guided insertion of central venous catheters, especially using the internal jugular vein, has been shown to greatly reduce the number of immediate complications. The site of cannulation also influences the rate of complications. Complications like pneumothorax are most common with attempted subclavian vein access and less common with internal jugular and femoral vein access. However, the subclavian vein approach is associated with fewer bloodstream infections and thrombosis.



The external jugular vein (A) is not used for central venous access.

The femoral vein (B) is associated with the lowest rate of mechanical complications but has higher rates of catheter-related infection.

Internal jugular vein (C) cannulation has a higher rate of bloodstream infection than subclavian access but a lower rate of mechanical complications.

One Step Further
Question:
What five steps, when used together, have been shown to reduce catheter-related bloodstream infections?

Reveal Answer:
Hand hygiene prior to donning sterile gloves, chlorhexidine skin prep, maximal barrier precautions (e.g., mask, cap, sterile gown and gloves), avoidance of femoral vein insertion, and use of ultrasound-guided cannulation.

question: Rigid chest syndrome is a noted adverse effect of which of the following medications?
englishExplanation:
Administration of appropriate analgesia and sedation is a vital component of the practice of emergency medicine. Knowledge of the physiology, duration of action, potency, and side-effect profile of the options for pain management is key to ensuring appropriate treatment of patients and upholding the principle of nonmaleficence. Each option employed for pain control has the potential for adverse effects, and tailoring a regimen is dependent upon the indication for pain management, patient age, weight, current medications, and comorbidities.

Fentanyl, a synthetic opioid with multiple routes of administration including intravenous, intramuscular, transdermal, and intranasal, is a highly lipophilic compound, which accounts for its quick onset and brief duration of action. These traits make fentanyl an ideal option for patients who require delicate titration of analgesia, or who may necessitate serial examinations over a period of observation.

Though exceedingly rare, high or repeated dosing of fentanyl can lead to diffuse muscle rigidity, particularly of the thoracic and abdominal musculature, leading to rigid chest syndrome, which can lead to hypoxia and ventilatory compromise. Treatment includes administration of naloxone, respiratory support such as supplemental oxygenation and bag-valve-mask ventilation, and if conservative measures fail, neuromuscular blockade.



Hydromorphone (B) is an opioid analgesic approximately seven times as potent as morphine, and it has a similar side-effect profile with nausea, vomiting, and pruritus as the most common adverse reactions.

Ketamine (C), a dissociative medication primarily utilized for procedural sedation, has been increasingly investigated as an analgesic at doses of one-tenth to one-third of those used for anesthesia. Hypersalivation and vomiting are noted side effects, with anesthetic doses having the potential for emergence reactions with psychomotor agitation.

Though not an option for pain management, midazolam (D) is a benzodiazepine that has been used historically with fentanyl for conscious sedation. Its side-effect profile includes hypotension, respiratory depression, and paradoxical CNS stimulation.

One Step Further

Reveal Answer:

question: For which etiology of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest does induced hypothermia carry the best improvement in survival with good neurologic outcomes?
englishExplanation:
Approximately two-thirds of mortality during the postcardiac arrest period is explained by anoxic brain injury. Many of the pathophysiologic features of anoxic brain injury are thought to be minimized by the early initiation of therapeutic hypothermia because it decreases cerebral oxygen demands and reduces reactive oxygen species formation. Therapeutic hypothermia (32–36°C) (the terminology recently changed to targeted temperature management) has become a standard of care in the care of post-arrest patients who achieve a return of spontaneous circulation but remain comatose. The original trials showed a significant survival benefit in patients whose initial rhythm was either ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia. Additional observational data has suggested a modest benefit in the other rhythms and the American Heart Association now recommends therapeutic hypothermia in all unresponsive post-cardiac arrest patients.

In the first hours after cardiac arrest, the core temperature of the body is lowered and maintained there for at least 12–24 hours. Recent data suggests that the most important element in post-cardiac arrest care is the avoidance of fever. Furthermore, newer evidence suggests similar improved outcomes with targeted normothermia (36–37.5°C). Hypothermia can be induced by a variety of different methods including surface cooling, ice-cold infusions, evaporative transnasal cooling, and endovascular cooling catheters. Although studies have examined cooling efficacy and time to target temperature, no available studies have compared different cooling devices with respect to the key clinical endpoints of mortality and morbidity. Other key interventions include focusing on ensuring adequate oxygenation and ventilation, support of circulation, consideration of coronary angiography, and general critical care measures, such as blood glucose control. Regarding oxygenation and ventilation, it is important to avoid hypoxia and hyperoxia, which may lead to oxygen toxicity and increased mortality. Additionally, hypocarbia which causes cerebral vasoconstriction and hyperventilation may lead to decreased cardiac output. Hemodynamic instability is common after cardiac arrest. Stabilization includes fluid therapy, vasoactive drugs, and consideration of mechanical support such as an intra-aortic balloon pump or left ventricular assist device, to maintain a mean arterial pressure of 65–100 mm Hg taking into consideration the patient’s normal blood pressure and severity of myocardial dysfunction.



Targeted temperature management has shown less benefit in patients with an initial rhythm of asystole (A) or pulseless electric activity (B). Sinus bradycardia (C) should not lead to cardiac arrest.

One Step Further
Question:
What explains approximately two-thirds of the deaths during the postcardiac arrest period?

Reveal Answer:
Anoxic brain injury.
