question: Which anatomic space is most likely to contain free fluid on an eFAST examination of a trauma patient?
englishExplanation:
The eFAST exam is an important part of the trauma evaluation for suspected blunt and penetrating abdominal injuries. An anechoic stripe found on eFAST suggests the presence of free fluid. In the supine position, free fluid will travel toward the more dependent portions of the abdomen and chest. As a result, the eFAST exam focuses on evaluating the following areas for free fluid: Morison pouch (hepatorenal space), splenorenal recess, pouch of Douglas (retrouterine or rectovesicular space), pericardium, and pleura. Gravity causes free intraperitoneal fluid to collect in the dependent portions of the peritoneal cavity.

The main cavity in the peritoneum is divided into two compartments that are connected by the paracolic gutters. The right paracolic gutter connects the hepatorenal space (Morison pouch) to the pelvis. Free fluid in the right upper quadrant will collect in this space and overflow into the pelvis. The left paracolic gutter is more anterior than the right, and due to ligamental attachments, free fluid will overflow from the left paracolic gutter or splenorenal space into the right paracolic gutter before flowing into the pelvis. Free fluid in the epiploic foramen will also flow toward Morison pouch. Therefore, in a supine patient, Morison pouch is the first site of fluid accumulation, regardless of the site of injury.



Pericardium (B) refers to the space around the heart. It is not part of Morison pouch and is not the most common site of fluid accumulation.

Retrouterine or rectovesicular space (C) describes the pouch of Douglas in the pelvis, not Morison pouch, and is not the most common site of fluid accumulation. As described above, fluid will accumulate in the right paracolic gutter before flowing into the pelvis.

The splenorenal recess (D) would be visualized on an ultrasound of the left upper quadrant. Its location is more anterior, and due to ligamentous attachments, free fluid will overflow into the right paracolic gutter.

One Step Further
Question:
What variables does the PECARN abdominal injury rule use to assess the severity of intra-abdominal injuries in children?

Reveal Answer:
Physical evidence of abdominal wall trauma, Glasgow Coma Scale score, abdominal tenderness, and vomiting.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Ultrasound: Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST)

Views: hepatorenal, splenorenal, pelvis, pericardium
Stable patient + positive FAST → CT
Unstable patient + negative FAST → repeat FAST or DPL
Unstable patient + positive FAST → laparotomy
eFAST adds pulmonary evaluation
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ eFAST من أهم أجزاء تقييم الـ trauma، والسطر anechoic بيشير لوجود free fluid. عند المريض المستلقي، السوائل الحرة بتتحرك للـ dependent parts، والـ Morison pouch aka hepatorenal space هو أول مكان بتتجمع فيه السوائل بصرف النظر عن مكان الإصابة. الـ right paracolic gutter بوصل الـ hepatorenal space للـ pelvis، فالـ fluid في الـ RUQ بيتجمع هناك ويفض للـ pelvis. ولهذا بنبدأ فحصنا من الـ RUQ.
الفخ: اختيار pericardium أو pouch of Douglas أو splenorenal recess. هاي أماكن بنفحصها بـ eFAST برضو، بس الـ fluid بالـ supine patient أول شي بتتجمع في الـ Morison pouch. و fluid حول القلب يعني إصابة قلبية مش بطن.

question: Which of the following measurements can be used as a marker to assess for the presence of increased intracranial pressure?
englishExplanation:
Ocular ultrasound can be used in the emergency setting to aid in the evaluation of globe trauma, vitreous hemorrhage, intraocular foreign bodies, and retinal detachment. It has also been found to be an easy method of assessing intracranial pressure. A normal optic nerve sheath diameter is up to 5 mm in adults, 4.5 mm in children, and 4.0 mm in infants. Using a high resolution linear array transducer, the diameter of the optic nerve sheath is measured 3 mm behind the globe. The average of three measurements is taken for each eye. An optic nerve sheath diameter > 5 mm in adults predicts an intracranial pressure of > 20 mm Hg with a sensitivity and specificity of 88–94% and 76–93%, respectively.



Elevated intraocular pressure (A) can be seen in acute glaucoma but does not correlate with intracranial pressure.

Posterior chamber depth (C) can be decreased in the setting of a ruptured globe.

An increase in retinal thickness (D), indicating macular edema, can be due to numerous causes such as diabetes, uveitis, and retinal vein occlusion, but does not correlate with increased intracranial pressure.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the sensitivity of detecting retinal detachment by ocular ultrasound?

Reveal Answer:
97–100% when performed by an emergency physician.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Ultrasound: Ocular Pathology

Retinal detachment: hyperechoic membrane (retina) tethered to the optic nerve as the patient moves their eye
Posterior vitreous detachment: thin, hyperechoic membrane off the posterior surface of the globe that is NOT tethered to the optic nerve, very mobile
Vitreous hemorrhage: swirling echogenic material in the posterior chamber with eye movement (washing machine sign)
Central retinal artery occlusion: diminished or absent flow of the CRA with color Doppler mode
Lens dislocation: hyperechoic convex shape in vitreous chamber detached from normal anterior position
Retrobulbar hematoma: anechoic lucency just posterior to the globe
Optic nerve pathology (papilledema): measure the optic nerve 3 mm posterior to the retina
Width > 5 mm is considered abnormal
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ ocular ultrasound طريقة سهلة وسريعة لتقييم الـ intracranial pressure. الـ optic nerve sheath diameter الطبيعي لحد 5 mm عند الكبار و4.5 mm عند الأطفال و4.0 mm عند الرضّع. بتقيسه بـ high resolution linear array transducer على بعد 3 mm خلف الـ globe، وبتاخد متوسط 3 قراءات لكل عين. و القطر فوق 5 mm عند الكبار بيتنبأ بـ intracranial pressure فوق 20 mm Hg.
الفخ: اختيار intraocular pressure أو posterior chamber depth أو retinal thickness. الـ intraocular pressure بيزيد بـ acute glaucoma وما بيرتبط مع الـ intracranial pressure. أما الـ posterior chamber depth فينقص مع ruptured globe، والـ retinal thickness بيزيد بأسباب تانية زي diabetes.

question: An 8-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with right eye pain after hitting a low-hanging leafy tree branch while riding her bicycle. Which of the following may be interfered with by a fluorescein stain in this patient?

options.text: Eversion of the upper lid for evaluation of the palpebral conjunctiva

englishExplanation:
Fluorescein is a fluorescent, green-orange dye that has a low affinity for intact corneal epithelium but high affinity for the basement membrane of the cornea. When applied to the eye, it highlights any epithelial defects, especially when visualized with a cobalt blue filter on an ophthalmoscope or with a black light (i.e., Wood lamp).

Fluorescein is typically supplied as a fluorescein-impregnated paper strip due to its low solubility in water. Fortunately, the affinity for the basement membrane is so high that very little is needed to highlight any corneal epithelial defects.

Fluorescein is commonly used to diagnose a corneal defect, contact lens abrasion, corneal ulcer, and an ophthalmologic herpes simplex infection. It can also detect the defect made by a corneal foreign body, but a slit lamp will better visualize the foreign body. Fluorescein can interfere with visual acuity, inspecting the anterior chamber, and a funduscopic examination, especially in the case where there is a large corneal abrasion. These should be performed prior to fluorescein staining whenever needed.



Assessing extraocular movements (A) can be performed and seen even if a corneal abrasion is stained.

Fluorescein does not interfere with Inspection of the palpebral conjunctiva (B) by eversion of the eyelid as it does not have affinity for eyelid mucosa.

Fluorescein does not affect the intraocular pressure, so measurement of the intraocular pressure (D).

One Step Further
Question:
What device is used for temporary eye protection in patients with a ruptured globe during interhospital transfer?

Reveal Answer:
An eye shield, not an eye patch.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Corneal Abrasion

Sx: pain, photophobia, tearing, or foreign body sensation
Uncontrollable crying in infants
Dx: fluorescein stain
Tx
Most are self-limiting
Topical antibiotics to prevent superinfection is common practice
Add antipseudomonal coverage for those who wear contact lenses
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ fluorescein صبغة بتبيّن أي عيب في الـ corneal epithelium، وبتستخدم مع cobalt blue filter أو Wood lamp، وبتستخدم لتشخيص corneal defect و contact lens abrasion والـ ulcers. المشكلة إن الـ fluorescein بيأثر على الـ visual acuity، وعلى فحص الـ anterior chamber، وعلى الـ funduscopic exam، خصوصاً إذا في abrasion كبير. ولهذا لازم هاد الفحوصات تنعمل قبل الصبغة. أما الـ eyelid mucosa فماعندها affinity للصبغة.
الفخ: اختيار assessing extraocular movements أو eversion الجفن العلوي أو قياس الـ intraocular pressure. هاي كلها ممكن تتعمل حتى بعد الصبغة، لأن الـ fluorescein ما إلها affinity مع الـ eyelid mucosa وما بتأثر على الـ IOP. الـ anterior chamber هو الفحص الوحيد اللي بتخرّبها الصبغة.

question: A 26-year-old man with no significant medical history presents with a painful erection that has been present for 4 hours. You decide to perform an aspiration. If the dorsal midline is considered to be 12 o’clock, which of the following is the best way to approach this procedure?
englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with ischemic priapism. Priapism can be divided into two general categories: ischemic (low flow) and non-ischemic (high flow). High-flow priapism is typically painless and usually is associated with trauma, congenital anomaly, or fistula leading to excessive inflow. Priapism can also be associated with spinal cord injury, which can occur anywhere along the cord, leading to a high-flow state. This vignette describes a case of painful priapism, which is most commonly ischemic, or low flow. In ischemic priapism, the prolonged low-flow state can be caused by blood dyscrasias (such as sickle cell disease), medications, and cancers. The mechanism of recurrent priapism is thought to be secondary to dysregulation of nitric oxide and cGMP, leading to difficulty with smooth muscle relaxation. A prolonged erection leads to tissue hypoxia and acidosis, which can progress to tissue damage as early as 4–6 hours after onset of the erection, with irreversible damage in 24–48 hours. Of the men with ischemic priapism lasting for more than 24 hours, 90% do not regain the ability to have sexual intercourse. During aspiration, injection of phenylephrine is often used to encourage vasoconstriction, further facilitating detumescence. In the treatment of priapism, it is critical that the anatomy of the penis is understood. Importantly, the dorsal veins run along the midline of the penis at 12 o’clock, so the dorsal midline should be avoided. The dorsal arteries and nerves lie on either side of the dorsal veins. The urethra lies on the ventral side of the penis. The blood that needs to be aspirated lies in the corpora cavernosa, which are found bilaterally in the center of the penis. Aspiration at 2 or 10 o’clock is the best approach to avoid the other structures in the dorsal and ventral areas of the penis. This is followed by injection of phenylephrine into the corpus cavernosum using the same landmarks.



Aspirating at 12 o’clock (B) risks injuring the dorsal vein and should be avoided.

Aspirating at 6 o’clock (C) is incorrect, as this is the location of the urethra.

Aspirating at 9 and 3 o’clock (D) is unnecessary because there is communication of blood flow between the corpora cavernosa, so only one side needs to be accessed.

One Step Further
Question:
What lab study can be obtained to differentiate between ischemic and nonischemic priapism?

Reveal Answer:
Cavernous blood gas analysis.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Priapism

Low-flow: venous, painful, emergency
Highest risk in individuals with sickle cell disease
Tx: corpora cavernosa aspiration, intracavernous phenylephrine
Use dorsal penile nerve block
Injection and aspiration performed at 2 o’clock or 10 o’clock position
High-flow: arterial, semierect, painless
Often related to trauma
Tx: observation, arterial embolization
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض عنده ischemic priapism، يعني انتصاب مؤلم استمر 4 ساعات، وهو غالباً low flow، بعكس الـ high-flow اللي بيكون غير مؤلم وبيصير بعد trauma أو fistula. الانتصاب الطويل بيسبّب hypoxia و acidosis في النسيج، وبيصير ضرر غير قابل للعكس خلال 24-48 ساعة. و وقت الـ aspiration لازم نفهم تشريح القضيب، والـ dorsal veins ماشية على الـ midline، فبن aspirate من 10 أو 2 o'clock بعيد عن الـ vessels الوسطى، وغالباً مع phenylephrine.
الفخ: اختيار 12 o'clock، لأن الـ dorsal veins ماشية على الـ midline وهاد بيزيد خطر النزيف لما تدخل الإبرة. الـ aspiration بده site آمن بعيد عن الـ vessels، وبعده بتحقن phenylephrine عشان نساعد على الـ vasoconstriction.

question: Which of the following is an indication for a resuscitative hysterotomy in a pregnant patient who loses a pulse?

options.text: CPR ongoing for 30 minutes following cardiac arrest
Fundus at the level of the xiphoid

correctAnswer: Fundus at the level of the xiphoid
englishExplanation:
A resuscitative hysterotomy (perimortem cesarean section) is performed in pregnant patients in cardiac arrest with uterine size above the umbilicus (gestational age > 20–24 weeks). A uterine fundus at the level of the xiphoid in a pregnant patient in cardiac arrest meets the criteria for resuscitative hysterotomy. It should be performed within 4 minutes of cardiac arrest and should be completed by 5 minutes after arrest for the best outcome. This procedure increases the venous return and cardiac output and can improve maternal hemodynamics for a better outcome for the fetus. A scalpel, large scissors, and hemostats are needed. Immediate and emergent consultation of general surgery and obstetrics for assistance is optimal but should not delay the procedure.

This procedure requires first prepping the entire abdomen with chlorhexidine. Then, use a scalpel to make a long midline incision from the uterine fundus to just above the pubic symphysis. Next, enter the peritoneal cavity using the scissors and make an incision into the uterine cavity with the scalpel. Using the scissors, enlarge the incised opening. Deliver the fetus, clamp the umbilical cord, cut the cord, and hand the fetus off to the neonatal team. Follow with the delivery of the placenta, and then pack the uterus with sterile gauze before resuming cardiopulmonary resuscitation.



30 minutes after cardiac arrest (A) is not an indication for resuscitative hysterotomy and may be a reason to not perform the procedure, which should be started within 4 minutes of cardiac arrest for positive outcomes.

A gestational age of 19 weeks (C) would not be an indication for a resuscitative hysterotomy. An estimated age > 20–24 weeks is an indication.

The presence of a shockable rhythm (D) may be a contraindication to performing a resuscitative hysterotomy, as this alternative cause can be addressed and may obviate the need for this invasive procedure.

One Step Further
Question:
At what gestational age does the fundus approach the xiphoid?

Reveal Answer:
Approximately 36–38 weeks gestation.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Resuscitative Hysterotomy (Perimortem Cesarean Section)

Indication: reported gestational age anywhere near viability (20–26 weeks) or fundus at or above the umbilicus + loss of maternal vital signs
Performed if no return of spontaneous circulation in first 4 minutes of CPR
Completed within 5 minutes of cardiac arrest for best outcome
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ resuscitative hysterotomy يعني cesarean section أثناء الحمل، وبتعمل للمريضة الحامل اللي فقدت النبض إذا كان حجم الرحم فوق السرة، يعني gestational age أكثر من 20-24 أسبوع. الـ uterine fundus اللي على مستوى الـ xiphoid بيحقق هاد الشرط. ولازم تتم خلال 4 دقايق من الـ cardiac arrest وتخلص بـ 5 دقايق لأحسن نتيجة، لأن هاد بيزود الـ venous return والـ cardiac output وبيحسّن الـ maternal hemodynamics.
الفخ: اختيار CPR لمدة 30 دقيقة أو gestational age 19 أسبوع أو وجود rhythm شاردي. الـ 19 أسبوع أقل من الحد المطلوب، والـ shockable rhythm ما بيغيّر المعيار اللي بنحكم عليه. والوقت اللي بنحسبه هو 4-5 دقايق مش 30.

question: Which of the following is the most appropriate location to perform a thoracentesis?

options.text: Anterior in the lateral one-third of the clavicular line second intercostal space
Anterior midclavicular line second intercostal space
Midaxillary line in the tenth intercostal space
Posterior midscapular line in the eighth intercostal space

correctAnswer: Posterior midscapular line in the eighth intercostal space
englishExplanation:
A thoracentesis is both a diagnostic and therapeutic procedure that can be used to remove fluid from the pleural space. The most common locations chosen for the procedure include the posterior midscapular line or the midaxillary line. The location of the thoracentesis should be guided by ultrasound to determine if there is a deep fluid pocket and no other structures that could be damaged. It is crucial to ensure that the site of insertion is above the ninth rib (eighth intercostal space), as penetrating below this rib heightens the danger of injuring the diaphragm, liver, or spleen.

This procedure is done under sterile conditions with local anesthesia. The needle and catheter are advanced until there is pleural fluid pulled back. A sample can then be pulled off and sent for analysis, and the apparatus can be connected to a vacuum container. If a large volume of pleural fluid is removed, patients may experience irritation and coughing toward the end of the procedure. Moreover, the removal of a large volume of fluid can also lead to reexpansion pulmonary edema. Other complications that can occur are trauma to local structures, infection, injury to the lung parenchyma, and pneumothorax (most common).



Anterior in the lateral one-third of the clavicular line (A) or anterior midclavicular line (B) would not be appropriate or common locations for a thoracentesis.

Midaxillary line in the tenth intercostal space (C) risks entering the abdominal cavity. If a bedside ultrasound clearly shows a deep fluid pocket with no abdominal structures, perhaps a lower rib level could be used, though this would not be typical.

One Step Further
Question:
What criteria can be used to determine if an effusion is transudative or exudative?

Reveal Answer:
Light criteria.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Thoracentesis

Indications: diagnostic (~ 50 mL) and therapeutic (~ 1.5 L)
Fluid evacuation site: one or more ICS below top of effusion in the midscapular or posterior axillary line
No needle insertion below ninth rib
Contraindications: needle insertion through infected area
Complications: pneumothorax, organ injury
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ thoracentesis إجراء diagnostic وtherapeutic مع بعض، يعني بيسحب السوائل من الـ pleural space. أكثر الأماكن شيوعًا لازم تتم فيه هي الـ posterior midscapular line والـ midaxillary line، وبيتم تحديد المكان بالـ ultrasound عشان نتأكد إذا في جيب سوائل عميق وما في بنى ممكن تتأذى. لازم نقطة الدخول تكون فوق الضلع التاسع، يعني بالـ eighth intercostal space، لأن الدخول تحت هالارتفاع بيزيد خطر إصابة الـ diaphragm أو الـ liver أو الـ spleen. والإجراء بينعمل بشروط تعقيم مع تخدير موضعي.
الفخ: الفخ هو إن الطالب يروح على الـ anterior midclavicular line أو الـ clavicular line في الـ second intercostal space، وهاد أماكن أمامية مو معتادة للـ thoracentesis. وكمان الخيار بالـ midaxillary line بالـ tenth intercostal space خطر لأنه تحت الضلع التاسع.

question: A 19-year-old man presents with a stab wound to the left chest. While he is being transferred to your stretcher, he loses his pulse. Which of the following is most likely to result in return of spontaneous circulation?
englishExplanation:
Patients with penetrating trauma who lose a pulse in transport or the emergency department should be considered for resuscitative thoracotomy. The vast majority of ED thoracotomies are performed on penetrating trauma patients. The survival rate for patients undergoing resuscitative thoracotomy after cardiac arrest from penetrating trauma is roughly 15%. Unfortunately, the survival rate with blunt trauma is much less. In general, ED thoracotomy should only be considered in patients who have signs of life at some point after their trauma. Thoracotomy allows for exposure of the major organs of the chest. The main goals of resuscitative thoracotomy are the identification and treatment of pericardial tamponade or cardiac defect, cross-clamping of the aorta, and internal cardiac massage.



External chest compressions (A) have never been shown to be beneficial in patients with traumatic arrest.

A left chest thoracostomy tube (B) can be placed simultaneously while a thoracotomy is performed, but it is unlikely to be helpful alone in restoring spontaneous circulation.

Pericardiocentesis (C) is suboptimal in comparison to thoracotomy for relief of pericardial tamponade in an arrest situation.

One Step Further
Question:
Where should the incision be made into the pericardium during resuscitative thoracotomy?

Reveal Answer:
The incision should be made at the apex near the diaphragm anterior and parallel to the left phrenic nerve.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Thoracotomy

Most likely to benefit: patient with penetrating chest trauma who arrests in field or ED
NG tube can distinguish esophagus from aorta
Anterolateral incision over fifth intercostal space
Phrenic nerve runs along superolateral aspect of the pericardium of the left ventricle
Aorta lies anterior to vertebrae and posterolateral to esophagus
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريض عنده penetrating trauma وفقد نبضه أثناء النقل، وهاد بالضبط من الحالات اللي لازم تعمل فيها resuscitative thoracotomy. أغلب الـ thoracotomies بالـ ED بتكون لمرضى penetrating trauma، ومعدل النجاة تقريبًا ١٥٪. أهداف الـ thoracotomy هي كشف وعلاج الـ pericardial tamponade أو عيب بالقلب، والـ cross-clamping للـ aorta، والـ internal cardiac massage. والأثر أقل بكثير مع blunt trauma، والمفروض ما تنفّذ إلا إذا في علامات حياة بعد الإصابة.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تختار external chest compressions، لأنها ما ثبتت أبدًا إنها بتفيد في الـ arrest بسبب trauma. وكمان left chest thoracostomy ممكن تحطه بالتوازي، بس لحاله مش رح يرجّع الـ circulation. أما pericardiocentesis فهو أقل من thoracotomy بعلاج الـ pericardial tamponade وقت الـ arrest.

question: A 35-year-old man is diagnosed with a right-sided peritonsillar abscess. Which of the following is a contraindication to performing drainage in the ED?
englishExplanation:
For proper visualization during incision and drainage of a peritonsillar abscess, the patient must be able to open his or her mouth widely. Therefore, severe trismus is a contraindication to performing needle aspiration or incision and drainage. Trismus occurs due to irritation of the pterygoid muscle by local infection or inflammation. Maneuvers to optimize visualization include having the patient sit up with his or her head in the sniffing position, using a tongue depressor, and using a headlamp, which allows for better illumination and use of both hands. Other contraindications to ED drainage of a peritonsillar abscess include recurrent peritonsillar abscess (indication for tonsillectomy), evidence of deep neck tissue extension, significant coagulopathy, and airway obstruction.



Drooling (A), otalgia (B), and voice changes (D) occur as the abscess expands in size but are not contraindications to performing a drainage of a peritonsillar abscess.

One Step Further
Question:
Which pole of the tonsil is most commonly affected in a peritonsillar abscess?

Reveal Answer:
The superior pole, followed by the middle pole, followed by the inferior pole.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Peritonsillar Abscess Aspiration

Premedicate with opioid + intramucosal anesthetic
Use ultrasound guidance to determine area of fluctuance
Insert needle into area of fluctuance (or superior pole followed by middle and inferior pole)
Avoid internal carotid artery (2.5 cm posterolateral to tonsil)
Contraindications: severe trismus, noncooperative patient
Complication: carotid artery laceration
arabicExplanation:
ليش: عشان نعمل incision and drainage لـ peritonsillar abscess، لازم المريض يفتح فمه واسعة عشان نشوف الموضع. والـ severe trismus بيمنع هالشي لأنه بيحصل لما الـ infection والـ inflammation ي irritوا الـ pterygoid muscle، فبيصير مافيش رؤية كافية. يعني هاد contraindication واضح للـ needle aspiration والـ incision and drainage. ولتحسين الرؤية بنخلّي المريض قاعد ورأسه بـ sniffing position، وبنستخدم tongue depressor و headlamp حتى نضوي بإيدين.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تختار drooling أو otalgia أو voice changes، وهاد كلهم بيطلعوا مع كبر حجم الـ abscess وما بيعنيوا إنك ما تقدر تنزف. وcontraindications تانية هي recurrent peritonsillar abscess، أو علامات انتشار للـ deep neck tissues، أو coagulopathy، أو block بالـ airway.

question: Which of the following is associated with an increased risk of postlumbar puncture headache?

options.text: Sitting the patient upright after the procedure

englishExplanation:
A lumbar puncture is the access into and removal of CSF from the spinal canal. It is a common procedure in emergency medicine, as it is the gold standard for diagnosing meningitis. Less common indications include evaluation of encephalitis, intracranial hypertension, and demyelinating conditions. Contraindications include skin infection overlying or near the puncture site, significant lumbar spine trauma, platelets < 20 x 109/L, and cranial mass with elevated intracranial pressure.

The procedure can be performed with the patient sitting upright or in lateral decubitus. The latter is preferred, as it allows for measurement of the opening pressure. The patient’s L4–L5 intervertebral space is then identified. After appropriate sterilization and anesthesia, the needle, with the bevel up if in the lateral position, should be inserted perpendicular to the patient and directed toward the umbilicus. Once past the “popping” sensations, which should be the ligamentum flavum and dura, the stylet should be removed and CSF should be drained. After collection of 1 mL of CSF into each of all four tubes, the stylet should be replaced before removal of the needle. An adhesive bandage can be placed over the insertion site. Common pitfalls include nonoptimal patient positioning, not truly directing the needle toward the patient’s umbilicus, and withdrawing the needle without the stylet in place. The most common complication is a postlumbar puncture headache. Use of a cutting needle (Quincke), use of a larger bore needle (e.g., 18-gauge), and multiple attempts have been associated with postlumbar headaches. Laying patients flat after the procedure and removing less CSF have not been shown to prevent postlumbar puncture headaches.



Low opening pressure (A) and sitting the patient upright after the procedure (B) have not been found to be associated with postlumbar puncture headaches.

The use of a noncutting needle (D) has been shown to decrease the likelihood of postlumbar puncture headaches.

One Step Further
Question:
What infection requires serial lumbar punctures to ensure CSF sterility after treatment?

Reveal Answer:
Cryptococcal meningitis.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Lumbar Puncture

Absolute contraindication: infection near puncture site
Adult needle placement: L3–L4 (L2–L3 could be an option)
Child needle placement: L3–L4
Infant/neonate needle placement: L4–L5
​Opening pressure measurement accurate only in recumbent patients
Xanthochromia (yellow): SAH, hyperbilirubinemia
↑ WBCs: bacterial or fungal infection, leukemia, vasculitis
↑ PMN: bacterial infection
↑ RBCs: SAH, traumatic tap
↓ glucose: bacterial or TB meningitis, CNS tumors
↑ protein: bacterial or TB meningitis, SAH, traumatic tap, MS, Guillain-Barré
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ lumbar puncture هو الـ gold standard لتشخيص الـ meningitis، وكمان له استعمالات بتقييم الـ encephalitis والـ intracranial hypertension والحالات الـ demyelinating. والـ post-lumbar puncture headache بتحصل لما السوائل تتسرب من الـ dura، وكلما كان ثقب الـ dura أكبر صار التسرّب أكثر. للذلك الـ 18-gauge needle الغليظة هي اللي بتزيد الخطر، لأنها بتعمل فتحة أكبر بالـ dura. ولما تطلع الإبرة بدون الـ stylet أو الـ positioning مو مثالي، بيزيد التسرّب كمان.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تختار low opening pressure أو إنك تخلّي المريض قاعد بعد الإجراء، وهاد ما إله علاقة بزيادة خطر الـ headache. أما الـ noncutting needle فموضوعه سلامة الإبرة أثناء الدخول، مو بحد ذاته.

question: What is the likely diagnosis based on the above echocardiographic findings?
englishExplanation:
Point of care echocardiography in the emergency department has benefits in terms of aiding in diagnosis and guiding treatment plans. The clinician is able to identify pericardial effusions, estimate ejection fraction, and assess for right heart strain. The video in the question stem shows a four-chamber view of the heart in which the right and left ventricles, as well as the right and left atria, are viewed from the apex of the heart. The mitral and tricuspid valves are in view as well. The right ventricle appears to be equal or even larger in size compared to the left ventricle. Additionally, the septum appears to be flattened, and the right ventricular systolic function is diminished. All of these findings are consistent with right heart strain. Right heart strain can occur in the setting of pulmonary embolism.



Point of care ultrasound is capable of identifying an aortic dissection (A). However, a CT angiography is a more optimal study. With an ultrasound, a suprasternal view of the aortic arch or a parasternal long-axis view of the thoracic aorta may visualize a dissection flap.

Cardiac tamponade (B) can be clinically diagnosed by the triad of hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and jugular venous distension. On bedside echocardiogram, patients with tamponade will have a pericardial effusion with right ventricular collapse during diastole.

Patients who develop acute mitral regurgitation (C) can be critically ill, especially in the setting of acute ischemia leading to papillary muscle rupture. Echocardiography is vital in making a quick diagnosis and will show a prolapse of the mitral leaflet into the left atrium.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the McConnell sign finding on echocardiography?

Reveal Answer:
Akinesia at midfree wall with normal motion at apex of right ventricle, which is specific for pulmonary embolism.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Ultrasound: Right Heart Strain (Pulmonary Embolism, Pulmonary Hypertension)

Right ventricle dilation
Right ventricle hypokinesis
Interventricular septal flattening (D sign)
Tricuspid regurgitation
Paradoxical septal wall motion
Right-to-left ventricular ratio > 1.0
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ point of care echocardiography بيساعدنا نشخّص ونوجّه خطة العلاج، وبنقدر منّو نشوف الـ pericardial effusions ونقدّر الـ ejection fraction ونفحص علامات الـ right heart strain. بهاد الفحص، الـ right ventricle طلع بحجم الـ left ventricle أو أكبر، والـ septum طلع مسطح، والـ right ventricular systolic function ضعيفة. هاد كله بيوحي بـ right heart strain، وهاد بيصير مع الـ pulmonary embolism.
الفخ: الفخ هو cardiac tamponade، بس هاد بتبان على الـ echo كـ pericardial effusion مع collapse للـ right ventricle أثناء الـ diastole، مش كـ right heart strain. أما الـ aortic dissection فالـ CT angiography أ better، والـ ultrasound ممكن بس يحتاج views معينة.

question: An emergency physician is asked to provide telehealth medical assistance to a nonphysician advanced practitioner in a stand-alone rural ED. They are resuscitating an adult patient in cardiac arrest and request help for the patient’s airway due to low end tidal carbon dioxide readings despite ongoing high-quality chest compressions. They have minimal training for endotracheal tube placement and have a low intubation success rate. Which of the following instructions regarding advanced airway intervention should the physician give at this time?

options.text: Continue bag-mask ventilation and resuscitation efforts
Perform an open cricothyrotomy and transfer the patient
Place a supraglottic airway device and continue resuscitation efforts
Place an endotracheal tube and transfer the patient

correctAnswer: Place a supraglottic airway device and continue resuscitation efforts
englishExplanation:
American Heart Association (AHA) guideline regarding airway interventions in cardiac arrest recommends that, if an advanced airway is used, a supraglottic airway device can be used for adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in settings with low tracheal intubation success rates or minimal training opportunities for endotracheal tube placement.

Therefore, in this scenario, it is reasonable for the physician providing telehealth support to instruct the advanced practitioner to place a supraglottic airway device and continue resuscitation efforts. Clinicians who employ advanced airway techniques (e.g., orotracheal intubation, supraglottic airway device placement) must maintain their skills and knowledge through ongoing training and real-life practice.

In addition to proper bag-mask ventilation, clinicians should be comfortable with advanced airway strategies and have a backup (secondary) strategy in place as a rescue method. Administering bag-mask ventilation without an advanced airway device may not allow adequate ventilation in all patients during cardiac arrest resuscitation and does not provide sufficient protection against aspiration.

Once an advanced airway is in place, continuous waveform capnography should be set up to assess for proper ventilation. Capnography should be monitored from the field to the time the patient arrives at the hospital to help monitor for endotracheal tube displacement or complications.



Bag-mask ventilation (A) is appropriate in initial resuscitation but can be technically difficult to perform effectively over time, especially during prolonged CPR or with limited personnel. In the context of cardiac arrest with low end-tidal carbon dioxide, which may suggest poor ventilation or perfusion, an advanced airway can improve ventilation and facilitate capnography monitoring. A secure advanced airway like an supraglottic airway device reduces the likelihood of ventilation failure or gastric insufflation.

Cricothyrotomy (B) is a last-resort surgical airway used in “can’t intubate, can’t ventilate” situations. It is highly invasive, requires technical skill, and is not appropriate as a first-line intervention in a setting where simpler airway tools are available.

Placing an endotracheal tube (D) increases the risk of prolonged airway attempts and interruptions in compressions. Given the practitioner’s low intubation success rate, supraglottic airway devices are safer and faster in this context.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the ventilation rate that should be provided to a patient in cardiac arrest once an advanced airway is placed?

Reveal Answer:
One breath every 6 seconds (10 breaths per minute).

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Airway Devices and Techniques

Video-assisted laryngoscopy: may have a better chance of first-pass success, especially in those predicted to have a difficult airway
Direct laryngoscopy: a historically valid technique that is becoming the first backup to video laryngoscopy
Flexible endoscope: an endoscopy is passed through the vocal cords under continuous visualization and serves as an introducer for an endotracheal tube
Extraglottic devices
Laryngeal mask airway: seals above the glottis to provide ventilation
King laryngeal tube: disposable, rapidly placed, easy-to-use tube with distal and proximal balloons that is inserted blindly and fills the esophagus and hypopharynx
Cricothyrotomy: surgical airway through the cricothyroid membrane and is used as a last resort
Needle cricothyrotomy: surgical airway of choice in children < 10–12 years old as a last resort
arabicExplanation:
ليش: حسب إرشادات الـ AHA، لو رح تستعمل advanced airway وقت الـ cardiac arrest، فالـ supraglottic airway device خيار مناسب للبالغين بوقت الـ out-of-hospital cardiac arrest، خاصة لما نسبة نجاح الـ tracheal intubation قليلة أو ما في فرص تدريب على وضع الـ endotracheal tube. وهاد بالضبط وضع هالمريض، فيلازم تحط الجهاز وتكمّل باقي الـ resuscitation efforts. ولازم بعد ما تحط الجهاز تعمل waveform capnography للتأكد من التهوية.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تكتفي بـ bag-mask ventilation، وهاد ما بيضمن تهوية كافية ولا حماية ضد aspiration. وكمان الـ endotracheal tube مو منطقي لأن صاحبك غير مدرّب عليه، والـ cricothyrotomy إجراء invasive ومخاطره أعلى.

question: What nerve runs along the lateral aspect of the left ventricular pericardium?
englishExplanation:
An ED thoracotomy is a potentially lifesaving procedure that is within the ED clinicians’ scope to perform. Indications include penetrating chest trauma with cardiac arrest in the ED, systolic blood pressure < 50 mm Hg after fluid resuscitation, and severe shock with signs of cardiac tamponade. Blunt chest trauma with cardiac arrest in the ED is a controversial indication. Patients with isolated cardiac wounds have the highest survival rate after an ED thoracotomy, and approximately 17% of these individuals will survive the procedure.

A left lateral approach is preferred. To prepare for the procedure, if time allows, place towels or sheets under the left posterior chest and place the patient’s arm above the head. An anterolateral incision is made at the fourth or fifth intercostal space, which is just beneath the nipple in male individuals and at the inframammary fold in female individuals. The incision should be made from the sternum to the posterior axillary line. Scissors can be used to divide the intercostal muscles and avoid lung laceration. A rib spreader is placed between the ribs. Clots should be evacuated, and care should be taken to avoid the clinician being injured by broken ribs.

The pericardium should be opened next if cardiac tamponade is present or suspected. The left phrenic nerve runs along the superolateral aspect of the pericardium of the left ventricle, which makes it vulnerable to injury during an ED thoracotomy. Therefore, the phrenic nerve should be identified, and an incision should be made anterior to the nerve. Small cardiac wounds can often be compressed by digital pressure while en route to the operating room. Large injuries may require placement of a Foley catheter into the wound to temporarily stop the hemorrhage and allow for suture repair.



The cardiac plexus (A) is at the base of the heart and provides autonomic innervation to the heart itself. The cardiac plexus is divided into a superficial part, which lies in the concavity of the aortic arch, and a deep part, between the aortic arch and the trachea.

The recurrent laryngeal nerve (C) is a branch of the vagus nerve that supplies motor function and sensation to the larynx. It is recurrent because its branches innervate the laryngeal muscles in a circuitous route. It initially descends into the thorax before rising between the trachea and esophagus to reach the neck.

The vagus nerve (D) is the longest cranial nerve. It contains motor and sensory fibers and, because it passes through the neck and thorax to the abdomen, has the widest distribution in the body. However, it does not course through the pericardium.

One Step Further
Question:
What major function will be lost if the phrenic nerve is lacerated?

Reveal Answer:
Diaphragmatic breathing. The phrenic nerve innervates the diaphragm.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Thoracotomy

Most likely to benefit: patient with penetrating chest trauma who arrests in field or ED
NG tube can distinguish esophagus from aorta
Anterolateral incision over fifth intercostal space
Phrenic nerve runs along superolateral aspect of the pericardium of the left ventricle
Aorta lies anterior to vertebrae and posterolateral to esophagus
arabicExplanation:
ليش: وقت الـ ED thoracotomy، الـ left phrenic nerve بيمشي على الجانب الـ superolateral من الـ pericardium للـ left ventricle، وهاد بالضبط السبب اللي خلّاه ييجي بالسؤال. عشان كذا لازم ننتبه لمكانه أثناء فتح الـ pericardium وكمان أثناء وضع rib spreader. والـ ED thoracotomy نفسه إجراء ممكن ينقذ حياة، ودواعيه penetrating chest trauma مع cardiac arrest في الـ ED، أو systolic blood pressure أقل من ٥٠ mm Hg بعد fluid resuscitation، أو shock شديد مع علامات cardiac tamponade.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تختار الـ vagus أو الـ recurrent laryngeal، وهادوا ما بيمشوا على الجانب الـ superolateral من الـ pericardium للـ left ventricle. والـ cardiac plexus ما هو العصب اللي بندور عليه بهاد الوصف.

question: An electrocardiogram is obtained in triage in a hypotensive older patient. No further information is available. Which of the following medications is likely present at a toxic level?
englishExplanation:
Digoxin is used therapeutically as an inotropic agent to increase myocardial contractility and also as a rate control agent to decrease conduction through the atrioventricular (AV) node. The drug inhibits the surface sodium-potassium ATPase, which alters the sodium gradient of the sodium-calcium exchanger leading to increased levels of intracellular calcium. Additionally, digoxin increases the vagal activity at the sinoatrial and AV nodes. At toxic levels, digoxin can cause almost any dysrhythmia or conduction block. However, certain dysrhythmias are more specific for digoxin toxicity including slow and regular atrial fibrillation, junctional tachycardia, atrial tachycardia with a block, and bidirectional ventricular tachycardia. In acute toxicity, patients experience a variety of noncardiac symptoms although nausea and vomiting are almost always present. Hyperkalemia is the most severe electrolyte abnormality associated with digoxin toxicity and prognosis is correlated with serum potassium levels. Patients do not typically survive when the serum potassium level exceeds 5.5 mEq/L.



Amiodarone (A) may lead to torsades de pointes as a result of QT prolongation in terms of ventricular dysrhythmias. It is relatively uncommon and typically occurs in conjunction with other QT prolonging agents.

Flecainide (C) is a class IC antidysrhythmic that has prodysrhythmic effects in some trials and is associated with increased mortality. Thus, its use has decreased. It does slow conduction through the AV node and His-Purkinje system and causes prolongation of the PR and QRS intervals. As a result of impaired conduction through the AV node, it may also cause first and second degree heart block. It does not affect repolarization and thus has no effect on the QT interval. It is not the most likely cause of biventricular tachycardia.

Propranolol (D) is a beta-blocker. In cases of beta-blocker toxicity, the cardiac manifestations include severe bradycardia and hypotension. Other findings may include altered mental status and hypoglycemia. It does not predispose patients to ventricular dysrhythmias.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the classic visual change of digoxin toxicity?

Reveal Answer:
Yellow-green chromatopsia.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Digoxin Toxicity

Hypokalemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity
Sx: nausea, vomiting, vision changes (yellow halos)
ECG: PVCs, atrial tachycardia with AV block, slow Afib, bidirectional ventricular tachycardia
Dx: digoxin level, kidney function, hyperkalemia is associated with a poor prognosis
Tx: digoxin-specific antibody fragment
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ digoxin بينستخدم كـ inotropic agent ليزيد تقلّص الـ myocardium، وكمان كـ rate control agent يبطّئ التوصيل عبر الـ AV node. وبتركيز سام بيسبب تقريبًا أي dysrhythmia أو block، بس في dysrhythmias معينة مخصوصة أكثر للـ digoxin toxicity زي الـ slow regular atrial fibrillation والـ junctional tachycardia والـ atrial tachycardia with a block والـ bidirectional ventricular tachycardia. وكمان الغثيان والقيء موجودين دايمًا بالـ acute toxicity، والـ hyperkalemia أخطر خلل إلكتروليتي.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تختار Amiodarone، وهو بيسبب torsades de pointes من تطويل الـ QT، وهاد بيصير غالبًا مع أدوية تانية تطوّل الـ QT. أما الـ Flecainide فهو class IC antidysrhythmic وعنده تأثيرات prodysrhythmic في بعض التجارب.

question: A 4-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with purulent discharge from the nose for 1 week. On anterior rhinoscopy, you see the above image. What is the most appropriate next step in treatment?

options.text: Forceps removal of the object visualized on anterior rhinoscopy
Irrigation with saline to remove the object
Nasal plain radiograph to determine what the object is and to see if there are other objects in the nasal passage

correctAnswer: Forceps removal of the object visualized on anterior rhinoscopy
englishExplanation:
Nasal foreign bodies are common in the pediatric population. Sometimes parents witness the foreign body insertion, but many times, the presenting chief concern will be chronic, purulent nasal discharge in a child who is otherwise well (afebrile, no dyspnea, no upper respiratory symptoms). If nasal discharge is limited to a single nostril, suspect a foreign body.

Typically, the foreign body is visible on direct anterior rhinoscopy. Once identified, removal with forceps, small hooks, or suction is appropriate. If the foreign body has remained for many weeks, it may be surrounded by granulation tissue, and removal may cause local bleeding. Adjuncts such as vasoconstriction with a nasal decongestant or topical anesthesia using viscous lidocaine may be used. If the emergency clinician is unable to remove the foreign body easily, then the patient can follow up with an otolaryngologist as an outpatient for removal. Special consideration should be given to food particles, as they can swell while retained in the nasal vestibule, making them very difficult to remove. Disk batteries are also a concern because they can cause a caustic burn, leading to septal perforation or scarring. If the emergency clinician cannot remove the battery, then consult otolaryngology emergently.



Emergent otolaryngologist consultation (A) is only appropriate if the nasal foreign body is suspected to be a disk battery and is not warranted for all nasal foreign bodies or foreign bodies that can be easily removed in the ED. Urgent outpatient follow-up with the otolaryngologist in the following week is appropriate for foreign bodies that cannot be removed in the ED.

Irrigation with saline (C) is never used as a technique to remove a nasal foreign body since this can push the foreign body deeper into the nasal vestibule and lead to aspiration or choking.

Nasal plain radiographs (D) are not useful in most cases, as most nasal foreign bodies are radiolucent.

Oral antibiotics (E) would not address the underlying cause of this patient’s purulent drainage. Foreign bodies that have been present for a prolonged period of time can lead to sinusitis, which would be an indication for antibiotics. In these situations, the foreign body would still need to be removed.

One Step Further
Question:
What are the common pathogens that should be targeted with antibiotic therapy in cases of secondary infection from a nasal foreign body?

Reveal Answer:
Streptococcal and staphylococcal species.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Nasal Foreign Body

Most often in children
Unilateral mucopurulent and foul-smelling nasal discharge
Tx: big kiss (positive pressure in mouth by parent while occluding unaffected nares)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ nasal foreign bodies شائعة عند الأطفال، وكثير من المرات الأهل ما يشوفوا وقت إدخال الجسم، والـ symptom اللي بتيجي هي discharge قيحي من الأنف لمدة أسبوع لطفل حاله كويس بدون fever أو dyspnea. إذا الـ discharge كان من فتحة وحدة، لازم تشك بوجود foreign body. وغالبًا بتنشافه مباشرة على الـ anterior rhinoscopy، ولما تشوفه بتنزعه بـ forceps أو hooks صغيرة أو suction، وكمان ممكن تستعمل vasoconstriction أو topical lidocaine.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تعمل nasal plain radiograph عشان تعرف شو الجسم، وهاد بيلغي وقت وبي和提高 فايدة لأن الـ foreign body بيشوف مباشرة بالـ anterior rhinoscopy. والـ emergent ENT consultation ما بتتحتاج إلا إذا كان الـ disk battery أو إذا الـ removal صعب.

question: Which of the following is the most appropriate management of a physician who intubated a patient later diagnosed with N. meningitidis meningitis?

options.text: Rifampin 600 mg twice a day X 4 doses

correctAnswer: Rifampin 600 mg twice a day X 4 doses
englishExplanation:
Healthcare workers who have direct mucosal contact with patients diagnosed with N. meningitidis meningitis secretions (mouth-to-mouth resuscitation, endotracheal intubation, or nasotracheal suctioning) should have chemoprophylaxis with rifampin 600 mg twice a day for 4 doses. Health care workers are not at increased risk for the disease if they were not directly in contact with the patient’s secretions. Household contacts have a higher rate of transmission (about 5%) and should also be offered chemoprophylaxis with rifampin. It is also vital to warn close contacts to vigilantly watch out for symptoms consistent with meningitis including fever, rash, headache, or neck pain.



Ceftriaxone 250 mg intramuscularly (A) and ciprofloxacin 500 mg by mouth (B) once are other effective treatment recommendations. Some type of chemoprophylaxis (C) must be offered to health care workers who are exposed to secretions.

One Step Further
Question:
What drugs are typically used in the treatment of fungal meningitis?

Reveal Answer:
Amphotericin B, flucytosine, miconazole, and fluconazole.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Neisseria meningitidis Meningitis

May present as an outbreak that involves individuals living in close quarters
Sx and findings: headache, fever, nausea, vomiting, myalgias
May be associated with petechiae, ecchymosis, DIC, sepsis
Tx: third-generation cephalosporin (e.g., ceftriaxone)
Chemoprophylaxis options: rifampin, ciprofloxacin, ceftriaxone
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أي healthcare worker إلو تلامس مباشر مع إفرازات مريض عنده N. meningitidis meningitis، زي ما صار مع الـ endotracheal intubation، لازم ياخذ chemoprophylaxis بـ rifampin 600 mg مرتين باليوم لمدة ٤ جرعات. واللي ما إلو تلامس مباشر مع الإفرازات ما عندو زيادة خطر بالمرض. أما الـ household contacts فعندهم نسبة نقل أعلى حوالي ٥٪، وبنفس السبب بنعرض عليهم chemoprophylaxis بـ rifampin. ولازم ننبّه الـ close contacts ينتبهوا لأعراض الـ meningitis زي الحمى والطفح والصداع وتيبّس الرقبة.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تكتفى بـ no treatment، وهاد غلط لأن لازم يتقدّم chemoprophylaxis لكل healthcare worker إلو تعرض للإفرازات. وكمان الـ Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM والـ Ciprofloxacin 500 mg فمّوي مرة وحدة خيارات فعّالة، بس مش بالجرعة والطريقة اللي بالمفتاح.

question: The following patients present to the ED for disruptive behavior. Which of them should be treated by immediate application of physical limb restraints?

options.text: A 12-year-old boy who needs punishment for refusing to stay on the hospital gurney
A 15-year-old boy who found a scalpel in the room and is trying to cut his wrists
A 16-year-old girl with disorganized behavior and incorrect emotional responses
A 17-year-old girl shouting expletives and using offensive hand gestures at the staff

correctAnswer: A 15-year-old boy who found a scalpel in the room and is trying to cut his wrists
englishExplanation:
Physical limb restraints are devices used to limit limb movement. The use of physical limb restraints is considered humane when the patient is an imminent threat to themself or others (including staff), such as being found actively harming themself, assaulting a team member, or preventing necessary care (e.g., intoxication, head injury). Restraints should also be used when the patient is causing damage to the environment. While it is essential to attempt to use de-escalation techniques and consider chemical restraints before physical restraints, a patient who found a scalpel in the room and is trying to cut his wrists needs imminent physical restraint.

Restraints can cause psychological trauma to patients, and their use has been shown to increase the risk of staff injury in some studies. Rarely, patients instead are grateful and feel safer while restrained. Agitated and violent patients need physical limb restraints to allow the team to safely care for them when verbal de-escalation techniques are inadequate. Restraints should never be threatened or used as punishment. When needed, they should be applied by at least five trained staff, one to control each limb and one to control the head. Patients in restraints are at significant risk of asphyxiation, especially when prone or in a Trendelenburg position, and should have their vital signs checked continuously. Restraints should be removed from patients at the earliest possible opportunity.



Restraints should never be used as a punishment (A).

Patients with disorganized behavior (C), such as those with schizophrenia, are frequently verbally redirectable and not usually violent. Furthermore, chemical restraint may be indicated before physical restraint in this situation.

While shouting expletives and using offensive hand gestures (D) is ill mannered, if patients are not interfering in their or others’ care and are not an imminent threat, restraints should not be used.

One Step Further
Question:
Which medication is recommended for an escalating pediatric patient with a known psychiatric disorder not yet meeting criteria for physical restraints?

Reveal Answer:
Olanzapine or another nonsedating atypical oral antipsychotic.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Emergency Management of Agitation and Violence

Ensure staff safety
Use verbal techniques and remove the patient from an agitating environment
Physical restraints only when necessary
Chemical restraints may be needed
Options and combinations include droperidol, midazolam, haloperidol, lorazepam, olanzapine, and ziprasidone
Assess for medical causes of agitation (hypoglycemia, hypoxia, poisoning, overdose, infection, CNS lesions)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ physical limb restraints بتعتبر إنسانية لما يكون المريض تهديد وشيك لحد ذاته أو لغيره أو عشان يمنع تقديم رعاية ضرورية له. هالمريض لقى scalpel بالغرفة وعم يحاول يقطع معاصعه، يعني هاد تهديد وشيك على حاله ومحتاج restraint فوري قبل ما يأذي حاله. ولازم نحاول أول شي الـ de-escalation والـ chemical restraints قبل الـ physical restraints، بس هون الخطر واضح وما في وقت.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تختار الطفل اللي بدو punishment، لأن الـ restraints ما بتستخدم أبدًا كعقاب ولا كمتهديد. واللي بيسبّب إزعاج بس مثل الصراخ والشتم ما عنده خطر وشيك على النفس، والـ restraint بيحتاجه لما يكون فيه تهديد فعلي.

question: A 16-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with aggressive behavior. He is in four-point restraints, and the EMS team suspects drug use based on the environment of the call. The patient seems confused and disoriented, intermittently fighting his restraints. His heart rate is 170 bpm, blood pressure is 182/112 mm Hg, and temperature is 38.2°C. His pupils are dilated, and he has diffuse muscle rigidity, worse in the lower extremities. He has sweat on his forehead. Which of the following should be the primary medication used to chemically sedate this patient?
englishExplanation:
Chemical sedation of agitated patients is a vital skill in the emergency department to protect both staff and patients. The amount and type of sedative used depends on the suspected cause of the agitation. For example, agitation from opiate withdrawal is best treated with a partial opiate agonist (e.g., buprenorphine), and psychosis from schizophrenia is best treated with a second-generation atypical antipsychotic (e.g., olanzapine). This patient has signs of sympathomimetic toxicity from 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) intoxication. Sympathomimetic toxicity presents with agitation, diaphoresis, tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, and mydriasis. The reason this is most likely MDMA intoxication is the additional findings like that of serotonin syndrome, which can present similarly and includes muscle rigidity, particularly in the lower extremities. Both of these syndromes can also result in seizures. Treatment for sympathomimetic toxicity and serotonin syndrome, especially when hyperthermia is included, is with high doses of intravenous benzodiazepines (e.g., lorazepam). Benzodiazepines are the best choice in this case due to their good antiepileptic properties and predictability. Most patients will tolerate high doses of benzodiazepines without developing apnea. The dose can be titrated upward until the patient calms and has reduced muscle contraction, reducing the risk of rhabdomyolysis. The cumulative amount needed may be extremely high, up to 10 times higher than the recommended maximum of 4 mg/dose.



Clonidine (A) is an imidazoline alpha-adrenergic agonist most commonly used for agitation due to undifferentiated delirium, disorganization, or developmental delay. It is also sometimes used for agitation due to anxiety. It is associated with hypotension, bradycardia, and sometimes disinhibition. The improvements from clonidine are inconsistent and, in some studies, have not been shown to be better than placebo, making clonidine less helpful in treating sympathomimetic toxicity. Droperidol (B) is a butyrophenone in the class of typical antipsychotics that is commonly used for mania, psychosis, delirium, and alcohol or benzodiazepine intoxications. It is also sometimes used for undifferentiated agitation. Unfortunately, it reduces the seizure threshold, interferes with heat dissipation, and causes a prolonged QTc, making it less likely to result in improvement in sympathomimetic toxicity and serotonin syndrome. Ketamine (C) is an N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor antagonist and is structurally similar to phencyclidine. It has a predictable effect, causing amnesia, and is commonly used for painful procedures in the emergency department. It is associated with hypertension, tachycardia, and increased muscle tone, making it less useful in the setting of a sympathomimetic intoxication.

One Step Further
Question:
How should restraints be used in a patient with severe undifferentiated agitation?

Reveal Answer:
With an entire team of at least five people.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Emergency Management of Agitation and Violence

Ensure staff safety
Use verbal techniques and remove the patient from an agitating environment
Physical restraints only when necessary
Chemical restraints may be needed
Options and combinations include droperidol, midazolam, haloperidol, lorazepam, olanzapine, and ziprasidone
Assess for medical causes of agitation (hypoglycemia, hypoxia, poisoning, overdose, infection, CNS lesions)

ليش: هالمريض عنده علامات sympathomimetic toxicity من MDMA intoxication، وهي agitation و diaphoresis و tachycardia و hypertension و hyperthermia و mydriasis. وكمان في muscle rigidity خصوصًا بالأرجل، وهاد بيحيّينا على إن الموضوع فيه serotonin syndrome. وعلاج الحالتين، خاصة مع وجود الـ hyperthermia، هو جرعات عالية من الـ IV benzodiazepines مثل lorazepam، لأنه أفضل خيار من ناحية الـ antiepileptic properties ومن حيث التنبؤ بالأثر.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تختار Ketamine أو Droperidol، بينما الخيار الأفضل هو الجرعات العالية من الـ benzodiazepines لأنها بتغطي الـ agitation والـ muscle rigidity مع بعض. ولازم titrate الجرعة لفوق لحد ما المريض يهدأ، وأغلب المرضى بي toleratelو جرعات عالية بدون apnea.

question: Which of the following is an indication for defibrillation?

options.text: Torsades des pointes in an alert patient
Ventricular tachycardia in a hypotensive patient

englishExplanation:
Defibrillation involves delivering an unsynchronized shock to the heart to convert pulseless rhythms into rhythms with a pulse. Pads should be placed in either the anterior and posterior position or the left lower chest and right upper chest position. Defibrillation should only be performed in patients without a pulse. If a patient with a pulse is defibrillated, it is possible that the electrical shock can be delivered during ventricular repolarization, resulting in cardiac arrest. Defibrillation is generally only appropriate for ventricular fibrillation, pulseless ventricular tachycardia, and pulseless torsades des pointes. Early defibrillation in pulseless shockable rhythms improves outcomes by restoring perfusion.



Asystole (A) and pulseless electrical activity are both nonshockable rhythms. Management is centered on high-quality CPR and addressing any possible underlying cause, such as hyperkalemia or tension pneumothorax.

Torsades des pointes in an alert patient (B) would suggest that the patient has a pulse and a perfusing rhythm. In such a case, magnesium sulfate and cessation of all QTc-prolonging medications are optimal care.

Ventricular tachycardia in a hypotensive patient (D) is best managed with cardioversion. If the patient’s blood pressure is not low, medications such as amiodarone could be used first.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the preferred treatment for atrial fibrillation in a hemodynamically stable patient with normal blood pressure?

Reveal Answer:
Rate control agents, including beta-blockers or calcium channel blockers.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Defibrillation

Indications: ventricular fibrillation, pulseless ventricular tachycardia
Biphasic device: initial dose of 120–200 J (if unknown, use maximum available); second and subsequent doses should be equivalent or higher
Monophasic: 360 J
Pediatrics: first shock 2 J/kg, second shock 4 J/kg, subsequent shocks ≥ 4 J/kg to maximum 10 J/kg or adult dose
Complications: soft tissue injury, myocardial injury, cardiac dysrhythmias
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ defibrillation يعني صدمة غير متزامنة للقلب، هدفها تحوّل rhythms بدون نبض إلى rhythms فيها نبض. ولازم تنعمل لمريض بدون نبض بس، لأنها إذا انطبقت على مريض عنده نبض ممكن تصيبه وقت الـ ventricular repolarization وتسبب arrest. وكمان الصدمة المتأخرة بتقلل النتيجة، فالـ defibrillation البكر بالـ pulseless shockable rhythms بيساعد يرجّع الـ perfusion. والـ ventricular fibrillation من أهم الـ shockable rhythms.
الفخ: الفخ هو asystole، لأنه rhythm غير قابل للصدمة، والعلاج فيه CPR عالية الجودة ومعالجة السبب مثل hyperkalemia أو tension pneumothorax. أما torsades عند مريض واعي يعني عنده نبض فبتعمل magnesium sulfate، والـ VT مع hypotension بتتم بالـ cardioversion.

question: You received a radio call from EMS that there was an industrial incident downtown, and multiple patients are imminently expected as a mass casualty. The team does not yet know what agent is involved, but patients are already presenting at the emergency department on their own. What is the best way to prevent contamination from critical patients before treating them in a regularly equipped emergency department?

options.text: Remove clothing and wash the faces
Wear level A personal protective equipment

correctAnswer: Remove clothing and wash the faces
englishExplanation:
In mass casualty situations, despite best practices and planning, a large number of patients will self-extricate and present in random order. This will mean that triage and universal decontamination will be a challenge. Nonetheless, the most effective initial technique for decontamination is to remove all patient clothing and visible contaminants from the body and to wash the face with water. This should be done in an area other than the clinical areas of the emergency department to prevent contamination of medical staff and equipment prior to intervention. In critical patients, this must happen rapidly before they are assessed for the need for airway, oxygen, bronchodilators, or systemic antidotes. For patients who can afford the time delay, and if appropriate resources are available, a full decontamination shower may proceed before intervention.



Decontamination showers (A), if available, may not be feasible for a patient in distress or who is too weak or disabled to assist in the process.

Few triage scenes have the equipment available to test for radioactive isotopes (C), and waiting for such equipment would cause an inordinate delay. If properly superficially decontaminated, the risk from radioactive materials can be minimized to allow for the safe care of critical patients without testing for radioactive hazards.

Level A personal protective equipment (D) is a completely encapsulated chemical-protection suit with self-contained oxygen. This level of protective equipment is rarely available outside of military and biomedical research settings or hazmat response teams. Clinicians should instead aim to initially decontaminate their patients, dress as protectively as possible, and work in well-ventilated spaces.

One Step Further
Question:
True or false: early onset of nausea and vomiting are indicative of severe radiation exposure.

Reveal Answer:
True.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Decontamination Procedures

Perform outside of clinical care areas
Remove clothing, brush off dust and powders, and wash faces quickly for critically ill patients
Use full decontamination showers if available and patients have the ability to use them
Level C personal protective equipment should be used by clinicians
Use warm water and scrub adherent material
Contain runoff water to limit environmental contamination

ليش: في حالات الـ mass casualty، رح يوصل ناس كثيرون بأنفسهم وبدون ترتيب مهما عملنا triage. وهاد مهم لأن أكتر طريقة فعّالة للـ decontamination الأولي هي إنك تشيل كل ملابس المريض وكل ما هو ظاهر عليه من ملوثات، وتغسل وجهه بالماء. لازم هاد يصير بعيد عن مناطق العلاج بالـ ED عشان ما تتلوث المعدات ولا الطاقم. وبالنسبة للمصابين الذين حالتهم حرجة، لازم هاد يصير بسرعة قبل ما نفحصوا الـ airway والأكسجين والـ bronchodilators والـ antidotes.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تفترض إنك تحتاج decontamination showers لكل واصل، بس هاد مش عملي مع مريض بحالة حرجة أو ضعيف ما بيقدر يساعد. وكمان معظم الـ scenes ما فيها جهاز فحص radioactive isotopes، وكمان level A PPE مش هاد الحل.

question: Which of the following is the most appropriate setting to defibrillate a pregnant patient in ventricular fibrillation?
englishExplanation:
Management of ventricular dysrhythmias may require defibrillation during maternal resuscitation. Defibrillation should not be delayed in the coding pregnant patient. The physiological changes of pregnancy, including increases in blood volume and decreases in functional residual capacity, do not appear to alter transthoracic impedance or transmyocardial current. Therefore, current energy requirements for adult defibrillation are appropriate for use in pregnant patients (biphasic shock 120–200 Joules with subsequent increase in energy output if the first shock is ineffective). The same advanced cardiac life support guidelines apply for defibrillating a pregnant patient as you would a nonpregnant patient. However, if fetal monitoring is in place when cardiac arrest occurs, it is reasonable to disconnect the monitor to eliminate the theoretical risk of electric arcing.



50 J (C) and 100 J monophasic (A) are too low of a dose for ventricular fibrillation.

Defibrillation (D) is not contraindicated in pregnant patients and should occur in the same manner as if the patient were not pregnant.

One Step Further
Question:
Should epinephrine be administered during cardiac arrest in a pregnant patient?

Reveal Answer:
Yes.

ليش: لو المريضة الحامل وقفت بـ ventricular fibrillation، ما لازم تأخر الـ defibrillation. والتغيرات الفيزيولوجية بالحمل، زي زيادة حجم الدم ونقص الـ functional residual capacity، ما بغيّروا الـ transthoracic impedance ولا الـ transmyocardial current. يعني نفس متطلبات الطاقة للبالغين بتنطبق على الحامل، وهي biphasic shock من ١٢٠ لـ ٢٠٠ J، وإذا الصدمة الأولى ما نفعت بنرفع الطاقة. ونفس إرشادات الـ ACLS بتنطبق على الحامل متل ما بتنطبق على أي حدا.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تروح على ٥٠ J أو ١٠٠ J monophasic، وهاد قليل مرة على ventricular fibrillation. وكمان الـ defibrillation مو contraindicated بالحمل، ولو في fetal monitor ممكن تفصله وقت الـ arrest.

question: On ultrasonographic examination, which of the following findings would most suggest a favorable site for needle insertion in paracentesis?
englishExplanation:
Ultrasonography can be a useful aid in many emergency department procedures. It has been shown to improve clinician comfort and patient safety in central line insertion, pericardiocentesis, and paracentesis. Understanding the behavioral properties of sound can aid in interpreting these bedside images. On ultrasound, fluid, such as ascitic fluid, appears as an anechoic pocket, as the ultrasound wave is not reflected back to the transducer. A large anechoic pocket, most commonly in the right or left lower quadrant of the abdomen, is a favorable location for paracentesis. Identification of the largest pocket should be obtained and a paracentesis catheter may be introduced using sterile technique. The use of ultrasound allows a reduced risk of bleeding and bowel perforation. Ultrasound may also be used to verify the location and help avoid vascular structures such as the inferior epigastric artery or dilated epigastric veins caused by cirrhosis. A distended bladder will also appear as an anechoic pocket, as it is similarly fluid-filled and should thus be emptied or its location verified prior to needle insertion.



Anisotropy (B) is a principle of spectral reflectors, such as tendons, referring to the differing reflective properties of the material based on the angle of incidence of the light. This means that when the ultrasound beam is perpendicular to the tendon, it will appear hyperechoic. However, a small change in this angle will result in a loss of echotexture as the sound is reflected away from the transducer.

Anterior shadowing with reverberation artifact (C) would be consistent with free air, such as hollow viscus perforation. The ultrasound beams cannot transverse air, causing a shadowing artifact similar to that seen on lung ultrasonography.

A hyperechoic pocket (D), or brighter area, would not be consistent with fluid or ascites. Hyperechoic structures include the bony cortex and connective tissues.

One Step Further
Question:

Reveal Answer:

The removal of intraperitoneal fluid
Indications: new-onset ascites, suspected spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, to relieve cardiorespiratory and GI symptoms related to tense ascites
Contraindications: uncorrected coagulopathy with associated DIC, bowel dilation or obstruction, abdominal hematoma, infection or engorged veins over puncture site
U/S can help detect as little as 100 mL of fluid
Spinal needle in those with obesity
Preferred entry sites
RLQ or LLQ entry 4–5 cm superior and medial to anterior superior iliac spine
Infraumbilical midline entry 2 cm below the umbilicus
Insert needle perpendicular to the skin or use the Z-track method

question: What physiologic benefit does high-flow nasal cannula oxygen provide?

options.text: Improves carbon dioxide washout of physiologic dead space
Provides fewer peak inspiratory flows than required

correctAnswer: Improves carbon dioxide washout of physiologic dead space
englishExplanation:
Respiratory distress from acute respiratory failure has many underlying etiologies, which can be categorized as hypoxemic, hypercapnic, or a combination of both. Arterial blood gas sampling aids in defining the type of respiratory failure. Further evaluation regarding the underlying etiology typically includes a laboratory and imaging workup tailored to the patient. In patients with hypoxemic respiratory failure without hypercapnia, high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen has been shown to decrease the work of breathing and improve oxygenation.

A 2014 randomized crossover study by Rittayamai et al. found a reduction in the work of breathing in patients receiving supplemental oxygen by high-flow delivery systems, as evidenced by improved respiratory rate, downtrending tachycardia, and greater patient comfort. Patients also experienced improvements in oxygenation. Their proposed mechanism is secondary to the minimal positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) provided by the high-flow delivery mechanism and the potential for washout of carbon dioxide.



Decreasing functional residual capacity (FRC) (A) is the opposite effect of HFNC. It actually increases FRC slightly by providing low-level PEEP, helping alveolar recruitment.

Dilution of oxygen (C) is not happening with HFNC. It delivers a stable FiO₂ by preventing dilution with room air.

Fewer peak inspiratory flows than required (D) is seen in the standard nasal cannula and face masks. They may fail to meet inspiratory demand, but HFNC provides higher flows than the patient’s peak inspiratory flow, ensuring effective oxygen delivery.

One Step Further
Question:
What echocardiography marker of volume status is less reliable for patients on positive pressure ventilation?

Reveal Answer:
Inferior vena cava diameter and collapsibility.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Noninvasive Ventilation

Reduces work of breathing
Interface types
Nasal cannula
Nasal plugs or pillows
Nasal mask
Full-face mask
CPAP: continuous level of positive airway pressure to prevent airway collapse
BPAP: positive airway pressure during expiration and inspiration, with a higher level of airway pressure during inspiration
High-flow nasal cannula: delivers positive airway pressure comfortably by matching inspiratory effort
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ high-flow nasal cannula بتقلل الـ work of breathing وبتحسّن الـ oxygenation عند مرضى الـ hypoxemic respiratory failure بدون hypercapnia. ودراسة عشوائية سنة ٢٠١٤ لقت إن معدل التنفس قل، والـ tachycardia قل، والمريض صار أكثر ارتياحًا. والسبب المقترح إن الآلية بتوفّر PEEP خفيف وبتساعد على شطف الـ carbon dioxide من الـ physiologic dead space، وهاد بيفسّر ليش الـ CO₂ ينزل أسرع. وكمان هي بتوصل FiO₂ ثابتة لأنها بتمنع التخفيف بهواء الغرفة.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تختار إن الـ HFNC بتقلل الـ functional residual capacity، بالعكس هي بتزيده شوي بالـ low-level PEEP وبتساعد الـ alveolar recruitment. أما الخيار الأخير فغلط، لأن الـ HFNC بتوفّر peak inspiratory flows عالية مش أقل.

question: Which of the following represents the preferred management of a severely painful thrombosed external hemorrhoid in the acute 48-hour setting?
englishExplanation:
Thrombosed external hemorrhoids presenting within 48–72 hours of symptom onset should be excised. Hemorrhoids occur when small vascular beds become engorged. Both external and internal hemorrhoids can present with bright red blood per rectum. Nonthrombosed external hemorrhoids can be managed with warm water baths, analgesics, stool softeners, and a high-fiber diet.

However, acutely thrombosed external hemorrhoids will not improve with conservative therapy and require excision. Failure to fully remove the clot results in rebleeding, swelling, and skin tag formation. If the thrombosed external hemorrhoid is not excised, it will go on to ulcerate over the next several days.



Reduction (B) should be performed on nonthrombosed external hemorrhoids if possible.

Simple incision and evacuation (C) of the clot is associated with a risk of reaccumulation and thrombosis, whereas excision has been shown to prevent recurrent thrombosis. Incision to remove the clot can be done to help alleviate pain in situations in which excision is not feasible.

Sitz baths (D) are helpful for nonthrombosed external hemorrhoids.

Surgical referral (E) should not replace excision in an acutely thrombosed hemorrhoid.

One Step Further
Question:
What anatomic structure delineates internal hemorrhoids?

Reveal Answer:
Internal hemorrhoids originate above the dentate line.

PE

External: distal to the dentate line

ليش: الـ thrombosed external hemorrhoids اللي بتظهر خلال ٤٨ لـ ٧٢ ساعة من بداية الأعراض لازم ين excision. والـ hemorrhoids بتحصل لما الـ vascular beds الصغيرة تصير متنفخة. والـ external hemorrhoids غير thrombosed ممكن تندار بالـ warm water baths والـ analgesics والـ stool softeners والـ high-fiber diet، بس الـ thrombosed الحاد ما بيتحسن بالـ conservative therapy. ولما ما نشيل الـ clot كامل بيعود النزيف والتورم ويعمل skin tag.
الفخ: الفخ هو إنك تعمل simple incision and evacuation للـ clot، وهي مرتبطة بخطر reaccumulation و thrombosis جديد، بينما الـ excision بتمنع تكرار الـ thrombosis. أما الـ reduction بتنعمل للـ غير thrombosed، والـ sitz baths منيحوت للـ غير thrombosed كمان.

question: What is the initial tidal volume setting for an intubated patient?
englishExplanation:
Initial ventilator settings for most intubated patients should deliver a tidal volume of 6–8 mL/kg of ideal body weight. This recommendation is based on the treatment of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), which has been studied extensively. The basic findings of the ARDS Network are that the injured lung is best managed with low pressures and low volumes. The initial rate should be set at 12–14 breaths per minute. The principle is the same regardless of whether the patient is receiving pressure-controlled ventilation or volume-controlled ventilation.



The other options are not ideal for initial ventilator settings. Tidal volumes are based on ideal body weight, not actual body weight (A, B), as lung volumes do not change with actual weight. A tidal volume of 4 mL/kg of ideal body weight (C) may be reasonable to keep plateau pressures < 30 mm Hg, but initial settings at 6–8 mL/kg are recommended. In patients with asthma requiring intubation, the same initial tidal volume applies but setting lower ventilation rates (10 breaths/min or lower) and higher flow rates (above 60 L/min) provides prolonged time for expiration.

One Step Further
Question:
What is PEEP, and what should the initial settings be in the patient without asthma?

Reveal Answer:
Positive end-expiratory pressure is a way to maintain positive pressure in the lungs at the end of expiration. It is generally set at 5 cm H₂O.
