question:
A 34-year-old man with a history of severe asthma presents to the ED
with sudden onset difficulty in breathing. Vital signs include RR 36
breaths/minute, temperature 37°F, and oxygen saturation of 85% on room
air. Despite aggressive treatment, he requires emergent endotracheal
intubation. He is given etomidate and succinylcholine for rapid sequence
induction. Shortly after intubation, he develops muscle rigidity and a
temperature of 40.0°F. Which of the following is the most appropriate next
step in treatment?

options.text: Administer IV antibiotics and order a chest X-ray

englishExplanation:
220.  The answer is b. This patient has malignant hyperthermia (MH), a
rare reaction associated with some inhaled anesthetics and succinylcholine.
It is caused by an abnormality in the ryanodine receptor on the sarcoplasmic
reticulum on skeletal muscle. Abnormal triggering results in increased
muscle metabolic activity. The diagnosis can be challenging, but the clinical
findings include muscle rigidity, hyperthermia, and hypercarbia.
Treatment is with dantrolene, which sequesters calcium back into the

sarcoplasmic reticulum. Succinylcholine and other triggers must be
scrupulously avoided in potentially susceptible individuals.
Bromocriptine (a) is a dopamine agonist and can be used to treat
neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS). While there are some similarities
between MH and NMS, MH is caused by succinylcholine and some inhaled
anesthetics, while NMS is caused by dopamine antagonist medications such
as antipsychotics. IV antibiotics and a chest X-ray (c) should be considered
in the treatment of bacterial pneumonia. While the fever in the setting of
respiratory failure could be related to pneumonia, the muscle rigidity and
the association with succinylcholine suggest MH. IV fluids (d) may be of
benefit to help prevent circulatory collapse, however will not treat the
underlying pathology. Physostigmine (e) is used to treat central and
peripheral antimuscarinic syndrome.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض طلع عنده malignant hyperthermia بعد ما انبوب بـ succinylcholine مع etomidate. السبب إنو في خلل في الـ ryanodine receptor على الـ sarcoplasmic reticulum، فبيصير تنشيط زايد للعضلات وارتفاع كبير في الـ metabolism. أكتر العلامات اللي بتميّزه هي muscle rigidity مع hyperthermia و hypercarbia بعد التخدير. العلاج هو dantrolene لأنه بيرجّع الـ calcium جوّال الـ sarcoplasmic reticulum، ولازم نتجنّب succinylcholine وأي inhaled anesthetic بالمريض اللي ممكن يكون معرّض.
الفخ: بعض الناس بيختاروا bromocriptine لأنو سمعوا فيها مع neuroleptic malignant syndrome. الفرق إنو NMS بييجي من dopamine antagonists زي antipsychotics، بينما malignant hyperthermia بييجي من succinylcholine مع بعض الـ inhaled anesthetics. وكمان IV antibiotics أو chest X-ray مش هاد البحث.

question:
A 58-year-old man presents to the ED complaining of generalized
weakness for the last 2 days. He states that a few days ago he had
abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea when his whole family got sick
after a picnic. These symptoms resolved a day and a half ago, but he has not
been eating well and now feels weak all over. He has a history of
hypertension for which he takes hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ). His primary
physician recently increased his dose. His BP is 144/87 mm Hg, HR is 89
beats/minute, RR is 12 breaths/minute, and temperature is 98.7°F. The
physical examination reveals hyporeflexia. His electrocardiogram (ECG) is
shown in the figure. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
335.  The answer is d. This patient presents with hypokalemia, secondary
to increased potassium losses through vomiting and diarrhea as well as
reduced oral intake. HCTZ is a potassium-wasting diuretic medication that
can also cause hypokalemia. Potassium deficiency results in
hyperpolarization of the cell membrane and leads to muscle weakness,
hyporeflexia, intestinal ileus, and respiratory paralysis. Characteristic
ECG findings include flattened T waves, U waves, and prolonged QT and
PR intervals.
Hypernatremia (a) and hyponatremia (b) mainly affect the CNS,
resulting in headache, anorexia, lethargy, and confusion. In more severe
cases, hyponatremia causes seizures, coma, and respiratory arrest, whereas
patients with profound hypernatremia develop ataxia, tremulousness, and
spasms. Hyperkalemia (c) can lead to cardiac dysrhythmias and typically
exhibits distinctive ECG findings, including peaked T waves, prolonged QT
and PR intervals, and widened QRS complex that can progress to a sine
wave pattern. Signs of hypercalcemia (e) include bony and abdominal pain,
renal stones, and altered mental status (remembered by: “bones, stones,
groans, and psychiatric overtones”). In addition, cardiac effects include
bradycardia, heart blocks, and shortened QT interval on ECG.

![PreTest-5e-00335 source page 400](images/PreTest-5e-00335-PreTest-5e-p0400.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00335 source page 401](images/PreTest-5e-00335-PreTest-5e-p0401.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00335 source page 420](images/PreTest-5e-00335-PreTest-5e-p0420.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض عنده hypokalemia لثلاثة أسباب: vomiting و diarrhea خلاوه يفقد potassium، وبعدين ما أكل كويس فقل الـ intake، وزادوا جرعة HCTZ وهو diuretic بيسحب potassium مع الفلور. نقص الـ potassium بيعمل hyperpolarization للـ cell membrane، فبتظهر symptoms زي muscle weakness و hyporeflexia و intestinal ileus و respiratory paralysis. وعلى الـ ECG بتشوف flattened T waves و U waves مع prolongation في الـ QT والـ PR intervals.
الفخ: طالب بيختار hyperkalemia لأنه شاف تغييرات على الـ ECG، بس هاي علامات hypokalemia مو hyperkalemia. اعرف إنو hyperkalemia بتيجي peaked T waves و widened QRS وممكن توصل لس sine wave، بينما hypernatremia و hyponatremia و hypercalcemia بتعطي symptoms مختلفة كل واحد لحاله.

question:
A 6-month-old boy is brought to the ED after being found apneic and
cyanotic at home. The patient’s mother called 911 and began
cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). The patient responded within
seconds to minutes. On arrival at the ED, he was noted to be awake and
responsive, but slightly mottled with mild respiratory distress. Within
minutes of arrival, the patient becomes apneic suddenly, cyanotic, and
bradycardic. Which of the following is the most important initial response?

options.text: Jaw thrust, chin lift, and bag-valve-mask ventilation

correctAnswer: Jaw thrust, chin lift, and bag-valve-mask ventilation
englishExplanation:
363.  The answer is c. This patient has become apneic and requires assisted
ventilation. The correct approach is to do a jaw thrust and chin lift in
order to provide optimal airway positioning and begin bag-valve-mask
ventilation. This is the most important skill to learn in pediatric
resuscitation. In many cases, providing oxygenation and ventilation
appropriately is all that is needed to resolve the bradycardia and circulatory
issues. The most common cause of arrest in children is respiratory
arrest. This is a classic case of respiratory arrest causing cyanosis and
subsequent bradycardia.
Epinephrine (a) is certainly in the algorithm for bradycardia, but the
first step in resuscitation is always addressing the airway. Oxygen should be
administered to this patient and a nonrebreather face mask (b) can provide
high oxygen delivery. However, the patient is not actively breathing, so this
method is ineffective. Endotracheal intubation (d) may be necessary to
establish a definitive airway in this patient. However, it will take time to set
up and perform. The simplest and quickest intervention is jaw-thrust or
chin-lift with bag-valve-mask ventilation. Chest compressions (e) are soon

to follow in this patient’s resuscitation if ventilation is not effective alone,
but the initial intervention is attention to airway and breathing.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الطفل صار apneic و cyanotic و bradycardic، يعني وقف التنفس وما عاد في أكسجين. أول شي لازم تعمله هو تفتح الـ airway بـ jaw thrust و chin lift، وبعدها تبدأ بـ bag-valve-mask ventilation. لأنه في الأطفال أكثر شي بيسبّب arrest هو توقف التنفس، والـ hypoxia هي السبب اللي بيخلّي القلب يبطّئ. ولما التهوية تتعمل صح، غالباً الـ bradycardia والمشكلات في الـ circulation بتتحل لحالها.
الفخ: بعض الناس بيختاروا endotracheal intubation أو oxygen عن طريق nonrebreather facemask، بس الـ intubation بياخد وقت والـ mask ما بتعمل شي لمريض ما بيتنفس. الـ epinephrine والـ chest compressions بيجوا بعدين إذا التهوية ما كفت لحالها.

question:
A 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension and diabetes
presents with shortness of breath and a rash that began while he was at
dinner. He has a known allergy to peanuts. His vital signs on arrival are
temperature 98.7°F, BP 89/45 mm Hg, HR 124 beats/minute, RR 28
breaths/minute, and oxygen saturation 88% on room air. He is given
epinephrine 1 mg intramuscularly for anaphylaxis instead of the
recommended 0.3 to 0.5 mg. His symptoms resolve and he is monitored for
4 hours without return of symptoms. Which of the following should be
disclosed to the patient?

options.text: He was given an inappropriate dose of medication
He was given the wrong medication for his condition
Because his symptoms improved, nothing needs to be disclosed
Because he was given the correct medication, nothing needs to be
Because he improved after epinephrine, he should receive a higher dose

correctAnswer: He was given an inappropriate dose of medication
englishExplanation:
564.  The answer is a. The patient was given an inappropriate dose of
medication. The recommended dose of intramuscular epinephrine for
anaphylaxis in an adult patient is 0.3 to 0.5 mg. This patient received 1 mg
IM, which is at least twice the recommended dose. The patient’s clinical
condition improved, and he was monitored without any recurrent
anaphylaxis. One might be tempted to assume that because the patient did
not suffer any harm that nothing needs to be disclosed to the patient.
However, an error was made, and although it did not lead to harm or a
bad clinical outcome (a nonharmful event), it still should be disclosed to
the patient. Other types of clinical errors include near misses, harmful
events, and death. The Code of Ethics of the American Medical Association
states that physicians should always deal honestly and openly with patients.
Recommendations for disclosing medical errors include timely disclosure
(ie, not waiting for the patient to find out later than an error occurred),
communicate clearly without ambiguity or misleading, explain potential
outcomes as a result of the error, elicit questions from the patient or family,
and offer a sincere apology to the patient.
Answer choice (b) is incorrect; he was given the correct medication for
his condition, but an incorrect dose. Answer choices (c) and (d) are
incorrect because the error should be disclosed to the patient. Answer
choice (e) is incorrect because this deviates from medical guidelines
suggesting recommended dosage of therapy.

question:
Which of the following provides the highest ETo2 after 3 minutes of 
ambient pressure tidal volume breathing?

options.text: Nonrebreather mask with oxygen flow at 15 L/min
Nonrebreather facemask at flush rate oxygen (40 to 90 L/min)

correctAnswer: Nonrebreather facemask at flush rate oxygen (40 to 90 L/min)
englishExplanation:
Flush flow rate oxygen using a nonrebreather mask provides an ETo2 of 85%. This is in comparison with an ETo2 level in the 
mid-50s with a nonrebreather mask at 15 L/min flow. The increased 
inflow rate outcompetes room air entrainment around the margin of 
the mask and increases the fraction of inspired oxygen (Fio2) resulting 
in better nitrogen washout.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ nonrebreather facemask مع oxygen ب flush rate (40 إلى 90 L/min) بيطلع أعلى ETo2، يعني حوالي 85% بعد ثلاث دقايق من التنفس بـ ambient pressure tidal volume. السبب إنو الـ flow السريع هاد بيكبّر سحب هواء الغرفة من حواف الماسك، فبيزيد الـ Fio2، وبتتحسن الـ nitrogen washout. مع mask على 15 L/min بس، الـ ETo2 بيوصل لنص الخمسينات بس.
الفخ: الخيار A بيبان منطقي لأنه نفس الـ nonrebreather، بس 15 L/min أقل بكثير من الـ flush rate. والـ high-flow nasal cannula أو الـ Venturi mask ما بيقدموا نفس النتيجة بعد ثلاث دقايق.

question:
Until how long after an acute burn is succinylcholine considered 
safe to use for RSI?
englishExplanation:
Succinylcholine can produce severe (and fatal) elevations 
in serum potassium levels after administration in patients with burns. 
However, this vulnerability to succinylcholine-induced hyperkalemia 
is not clinically significant until at least 5 days after the acute burn. As a 
result, succinylcholine remains the paralytic of choice if rapid sequence 
intubation occurs less than 5 days after the burn.
   

33.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ succinylcholine بيسبّب ارتفاع خطير وممكن مميت في الـ serum potassium، بس هاد الـ vulnerability للـ hyperkalemia ما بيبان بشكل سريري قبل 5 أيام على الأقل من الـ acute burn. يعني لو صار RSI قبل 5 أيام من الحرق، يضل الـ succinylcholine هو الـ paralytic of choice لأنه سريع وبيوفر أحسن ظروف للـ intubation. بعد ما يعدّي الخمسة أيام لازم تتجنّبه بسبب خطر الـ hyperkalemia.
الفخ: الخيارين 24 ساعة و 48 ساعة بيبانوا منطقيين لأنهم أقصر، بس هوك الخطر اللي بيسببه الـ succinylcholine ببدا يظهر بعد 5 أيام مو قبلها. فاختار المدة الأطول مو الأقصر.

question:
Which of the following is a potential adverse effect of intubation 
and positive-pressure ventilation?
englishExplanation:
Positive-pressure ventilation (PPV) is associated with several complications. Some of these can quickly become life-threatening. 
This reality underscores the importance of familiarization with the 
common problems that arise as a result of PPV. Most complications 
result from changes in thoracic physiology when positive pressure is 
present for part or all of the respiratory cycle. Potential adverse effects 
of PPV include an increased work of breathing because of asynchrony 
or improperly set triggers, an increase in intrathoracic pressure, 
ALGRAWANY

References
33.e2
decreased venous return to the heart and decreased cardiac output, an 
increased ventilation/perfusion ratio, air trapping and intrinsic positive end-expiratory pressure, barotrauma, decreased renal blood flow 
and glomerular filtration rate with fluid retention, nosocomial infections of the lungs and sinuses, respiratory alkalosis, and agitation and 
increased respiratory distress.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ positive-pressure ventilation ممكن يسبّب مضاعفات كثيرة، وأغلبها بييجي من تغيّر في فسيولوجيا الصدر وقت ما يصير ضغط موجب جزء من دورة التنفس. واحدة من هاد المضاعفات زيادة الـ work of breathing، وبيصير لما يكون في asynchrony بين المريض والـ ventilator أو الـ triggers مو مضبوطة صح. كمان بيرتفع الـ intrathoracic pressure وبيقل الـ venous return والـ cardiac output، وبتزداد الـ V/Q ratio مع air trapping و iPEEP، وبتجي barotrauma و نقص في الـ renal blood flow.
الفخ: الخيارات التانية فيها decreased intrathoracic pressure و decreased V/Q ratio و increased cardiac output، بس الـ PPV بيعمل العكس: بيزود الـ pressure جوّال الصدر، وبيزود الـ V/Q ratio، وبيقل الـ cardiac output. فلازم تفكر بالاتجاه مو بالاسم.

question: Regarding a patient who develops acute distress on mechanical ventilation, which of the following is the most accurate?

options.text: Accidental extubation is a common cause of increased airway
Anaphylaxis would cause immediate increases in both peak
All patients in distress should be immediately removed from the
Compared to patients with restrictive lung disease, patients with

correctAnswer: Compared to patients with restrictive lung disease, patients with
englishExplanation:
One of the most life-threatening complications of mechanical ventilation is loss of adequate cardiac output because of elevated 
intrathoracic pressure from intrinsic PEEP (iPEEP). Intrinsic PEEP 
can be precipitated by a respiratory rate that is too high, which does 
not allow patients to fully exhale before the delivery of another breath. 
Patients with obstructive lung disease such as COPD or acute asthma 
are particularly sensitive to this phenomenon, also known as “breath 
stacking.” Although patients with restrictive lung disease may develop 
iPEEP with an inappropriate respiratory rate, this is much more likely 
to occur in patients with obstructive conditions. If patients are not 
hemodynamically unstable, they do not need to be removed from the 
ventilator, and in hemodynamically unstable patients, pneumothorax 
should only be presumptively treated if removing the patient from 
the ventilator does not improve the situation. Accidental extubation 
is a common cause of decreased airway pressures, and although anaphylaxis would cause increases in PIP, it would not typically cause 
increases in Pplat.

41.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض اللي فجأة تعب على الـ mechanical ventilation ممكن يكون عنده iPEEP، وسببه respiratory rate عالية ما بتسمحله يطلع الزفير كله قبل ما تجي النفخة الجاية. مرضى الـ COPD والـ asthma، يعني الـ obstructive lung disease، أكثر تأثراً بهالشي لأنو الـ expiratory time عندهم محدود. والـ iPEEP بيرفع الـ intrathoracic pressure وبيقل الـ cardiac output، وهاد من أخطر مضاعفات الـ ventilation. مرضى الـ restrictive disease ممكن يصير عندهم الشي نفسه، بس أقل احتمالاً.
الفخ: لو المريض صار غير مستقر hemodynamically، مش دايماً لازم تشيله من الـ ventilator، والـ pneumothorax لازم تنعالجه بشكل استباقي بس إذا شيلته من الـ ventilator وما تحسّن الوضع. وكمان الـ anaphylaxis بيزود الـ PIP مو الـ Pplat، والـ accidental extubation بتقل الـ airway pressures.

question:
Which of the following is a class 1 recommendation from the 2015 
American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary 
Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care?

options.text: Forty-eight hours from arrest is the earliest time the clinical
All comatose patients with return of spontaneous circulation
EEG monitoring is not necessary or indicated for comatose
Infusion of cold saline should be used to induce cooling in the

correctAnswer: All comatose patients with return of spontaneous circulation
englishExplanation:
The 2015 guidelines update confirms that all comatose 
(lack of meaningful response to verbal commands) patients with ROSC 
following cardiac arrest should receive targeted temperature management (TTM), regardless of location of arrest or rhythm type. Because 
the neurological examination is unreliable in the first few days following arrest, 72 hours is the earliest possible time that one may consider using it to provide prognostic information to surrogate decision 
makers. Non-convulsive seizures are common following cardiac arrest 
therefore EEG monitoring, if available, should be performed frequently 
or continuously in comatose survivors of cardiac arrest. Finally, multiple randomized controlled trials showed that cold intravenous fluids 
in the pre-hospital setting increased the rate of pulmonary edema and 
rearrest. We do not recommend this practice.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في guidelines بتاعة AHA سنة 2015، الـ class 1 recommendation إنه كل مريض comatose بعد رجوع الـ spontaneous circulation (ROSC) من cardiac arrest لازم ياخد targeted temperature management (TTM). هاد سواء الـ arrest كان داخل المستشفى أو برّا، وسواء الـ rhythm كان shockable أو non-shockable. السبب إنو الـ neurological examination مو reliable في أول كم يوم بعد الـ arrest. والـ EEG monitoring مهم لأنو الـ non-convulsive seizures شائعة، والـ cold saline بالـ pre-hospital زاد pulmonary edema و re-arrest.
الفخ: الخيار A بيحكي إنو الـ exam بيعطي معلومات prognostic بعد 48 ساعة، بس الـ guidelines بتقول إنو ممكن ما نعملها قبل 72 ساعة. وكمان الـ cold saline infusion مو recommended لأنها زادت الـ pulmonary edema.

question:
Which chest compression/ventilation ratio is recommended during 
adult resuscitation efforts performed by health care professionals 
before placement of an advanced airway?
englishExplanation:
A 30:2 compression/ventilation ratio is currently recommended for health care professionals in all adult resuscitation scenarios. 
Although recent evidence has suggested that chest compression-only 
CPR is effective when performed by bystanders in the out-of-hospital 
setting, there is inadequate evidence to recommend this as an alternative strategy for health care professionals, except when inadequate 
personnel are present to provide compressions, ventilation, and other 
resuscitative activities.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: نسبة الضغط للتهوية 30:2 هي الموصى بها حالياً لكل الـ health care professionals في كل سيناريوهات الـ adult resuscitation. السبب إنو الأدلة على CPR بالضغط بس (compression-only) قوية، بس هاي بالأصل خارج المستشفى وبيعملها bystanders مو الـ healthcare professionals. مع الـ healthcare team كامل، ما في داعي نلجأ لها إلا إذا نقص الـ personnel يخلّينا ما نقدر نغطي الضغط والتهوية مع بعض. يعني تضغط 30 مرة وبعدين تعطي نفس الكمية بالتهوية مرتين.
الفخ: ناس بيختاروا 10:1 لأنو شافوا هاد الرقم بالأطفال، بس السؤال عن adults. وكمان compression-only CPR مو بديل موصى فيه للـ healthcare professionals إلا إذا نقص personnel.

question:
In the cyanotic patient, clinical improvement with supplemental 
oxygen is most suggestive of which of the following underlying processes?

options.text: Congenital heart disease with right-to-left shunting

englishExplanation:
Clinical improvement with oxygen suggests diffusion 
impairment, hypoventilation, or an increased V/Q ratio due to mismatch. Patients who do not respond to oxygen are more likely to have 
decreased V/Q ratio abnormalities, such as shunting from pulmonary 
consolidation or congenital heart disease with right-to-left shunting, or 
abnormal hemoglobin. Arterial emboli will generally not be affected by 
supplemental oxygen.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: تحسّن المريض المزرق لما تعطيه supplemental oxygen بيحكي إنو السبب diffusion impairment أو hypoventilation أو increased V/Q ratio بسبب mismatch. الـ COPD بييجي بهالشكل لأنو فيه impaired exchange بين الـ alveoli والـ blood. أما الـ shunting من right-to-left congenital heart disease والـ methemoglobinemia، فالمريض ما بيستجيب للأكسجين لأنو الدم بيوصل بدون أكسجين أصلاً. وكمان الـ arterial emboli عادةً ما بتتأثر بالـ supplemental oxygen.
الفخ: الـ hyperventilation بيعطي نفس التحسن لأنه بيزود الـ alveolar ventilation، بس مو السبب المتعلق بالأكسجين. القاعدة: تحسّن بالأكسجين يعني COPD، وما تحسّن يعني shunt أو abnormal hemoglobin أو arterial emboli.

question:
The primary goal in the emergency care of a head trauma patient 
is prevention or reduction of secondary insults that are known to 
worsen outcome after traumatic brain injury (TBI). This includes 
acutely preventing:
englishExplanation:
Avoiding or reversing hypotension and hypoxia is essential 
in the acute management of TBI patients in the emergency department. 
Hypotension and hypoxia each double the risk of mortality following 
TBI.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الهدف الأساسي في طوارئ الـ head trauma هو منع أو تقليل الـ secondary insults اللي بنعرف إنها بت worsen الـ outcome بعد الـ traumatic brain injury. من أهم هاد الـ insults هو hypotension و hypoxia، ولازم تتجنّبهم أو تعكسهم في الـ ED. السبب إنو كل واحد منهما بيضاعف خطر الـ mortality بعد الـ TBI. يعني لازم نرفع الـ pressure ونتأكد إنو الأكسجين كافي، من غير ما نعمل ضرر ثاني للدماغ.
الفخ: الخيار D فيه all of the above ومعه malnutrition، بس malnutrition مش من الـ secondary insults اللي بنعالجها acutely في الـ ED. وكمان الخيارين A و B لحالهم مش كافيين، لازم نمنع الاتنين مع بعض.

question:
Which of the following statements is true regarding cerebral blood 
flow (CBF), cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP), and intracranial 
pressure (ICP)?

options.text: CBF autoregulation is lost below a CPP of 60 mm Hg.
CPP closely parallels diastolic blood pressure.
Normal ICP is 65 to 195 mm Hg.
The only resistance to CBF is ICP.

englishExplanation:
CBF depends on CPP, which is the blood flow pressure gradient. CBF resistance is provided by mean systemic venous pressures 
and ICP, predominantly by the latter. CPP closely parallels MAP offset 
by ICP; thus, the formula CPP = MAP − ICP. ICP is estimated clinically 
by the central venous pressure unless a ventricular catheter is in place 
and ICP can be directly determined. CBF autoregulation is lost below 
a CPP of 40 mm Hg. Normal ICP is 5 to 15 mm Hg or 65 to 195 mm 
H2O.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ cerebral blood flow بيعتمد على الـ CPP، وهو الـ pressure gradient اللي بيسمّي الدم. الـ resistance بيجي من الضغط الوريدي العام ومن الـ ICP، والأخير هو الأهم. ولأنو الـ CPP بيوازي الـ MAP ناقص الـ ICP، فالصيغة هي CPP = MAP - ICP. الـ ICP بيتقدر بالـ central venous pressure إلا إذا في ventricular catheter، والـ CBF autoregulation بتضيع تحت CPP الـ 40 mm Hg، والـ ICP الطبيعي 5 لـ 15 mm Hg.
الفخ: الخيار A بيحكي إنو الـ autoregulation بتضيع تحت 60، بس الرقم الصح هو 40. وكمان الخيار C غلط، لأنو الـ ICP الطبيعي 5 لـ 15 mm Hg مو 65 لـ 195، والأرقام التانية هي mm H2O.

question:
Central pontine myelinolysis is a potential adverse event associated 
with the administration of which of the following medications?
englishExplanation:
Central pontine myelinolysis is a potentially adverse event 
associated with hypertonic saline administration.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ central pontine myelinolysis مضاعفة ممكن تحصل لما نعطي hypertonic saline، وهاد هو الربط بين الدواء والـ adverse event. هي بتعمل damage للـ myelin في الـ pons، وبيصير هذا مع التغير السريع في الـ serum sodium والـ osmolality وقت ما خلايا المخ بتشد الماء جوّالها. الباقي من الخيارات، يعني etomidate و mannitol و methylprednisolone و pentobarbital، ما منّهم مرتبط بالـ central pontine myelinolysis بهالشكل.
الفخ: طالب ممكن يفكر إنو mannitol هي الغلط لأنها كمان osmotic agent، بس mannitol بيتّعمل لخفض الـ ICP وهاد الـ association بيخص الـ hypertonic saline. فلازم تحفظ: CPM = hypertonic saline.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding airway management 
after penetrating neck trauma is true?

options.text: Awake fiberoptic intubation is the first-line technique.
Bag-valve-mask ventilation should be high tidal volume, low
Cervical spine immobilization is typically unnecessary.
Nasotracheal intubation is relatively contraindicated in neck
Preintubation nasogastric tube (NGT) placement may be lifesaving.

correctAnswer: Cervical spine immobilization is typically unnecessary.
englishExplanation:
Unless there is concomitant blunt injury or evidence of 
spinal cord injury, cervical immobilization is not needed. Oral intubation after rapid sequence intubation (RSI) is the technique of choice 
and is successful in almost all cases. Although rarely a first line choice, 
nasotracheal intubation has been used successfully in these trauma 
patients. Gentle bag-valve-mask technique with low pressure is indicated to avoid venous air embolism (VAE) and subcutaneous emphysema. NGT placement, if done at all, should be gentle and placed after 
intubation.
CHAPTER 36  Neck Trauma

397.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بعد penetrating neck trauma، الـ cervical immobilization مش لازم إلا إذا في concomitant blunt injury أو فيه دليل على spinal cord injury. والـ oral intubation بعد RSI هي التقنية المفضلة وبتنجح في أغلب الحالات. ولازم تعمل bag-valve-mask ventilation بـ gentle technique وبـ low pressure عشان تتجنّب venous air embolism والـ subcutaneous emphysema. وإذا رح تحط NGT لازم يكون gently وبعد الـ intubation، مش قبلها.
الفخ: الخيار E بيحكي إنو الـ NGT قبل الـ intubation ممكن ينقذ حياة، بس إذا حطيته قبل ما تضمن الـ airway ممكن تزود المشكلة. والخيار D مش دقيق، لأنو الـ nasotracheal intubation قلّ نجاحها بس استُعملت بنجاح مع مرضى neck trauma.

question:
A 14-month-old girl presents in respiratory distress after eating a 
hot dog for lunch. Her mother states that she had stepped out of the 
kitchen, and when she came back, her daughter was sitting forward 
with noisy breathing and obvious distress. Which of the following 
management interventions is contraindicated?

options.text: Blind finger sweep as the first step

correctAnswer: Blind finger sweep as the first step
englishExplanation:
Blind finger sweeping has resulted in the conversion of 
partial to complete airway obstruction when objects are displaced into 
the subglottic space. For this reason, the technique has lost favor as 
an initial maneuver in pediatric and adult patients. It is recommended 
that up to five back blows be delivered (with the patient in a head-down 
position), followed by chest thrusts. Intubation or needle cricothyroidotomy may be performed if other maneuvers fail and circumstances 
dictate their need.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد البنت عندها partial airway obstruction من جسم غريب، وهاد هوت دوج. الـ blind finger sweep صار contraindicated لأنه في مرات الجسم بينزلق تحت، فبيحوّل الـ partial obstruction لـ complete obstruction في الـ subglottic space. عشان هيك هاي التقنية فقدت favor كأول maneuver بالـ pediatric والـ adult patients. التوصية إنك تعمل لحد 5 back blows والـ patient برأسه لتحت، وبعدها chest thrusts، وإذا كل هاد فشل ممكن intubation أو needle cricothyroidotomy.
الفخ: طالب بيختار chest thrusts أو back blows كإجابة ممنوعة، بس هاد هما التوصية نفسها. السؤال بيسأل عن الشي contraindicated، وهو الـ blind finger sweep، لأنه بيزوّد خطر انسداد الـ airway الكامل.

question:
A 67-year-old male with a history of an ischemic cardiomyopathy 
and an implantable cardiac defibrillator (ICD) presents with complaints of multiple shocks from his ICD in the past day. Interrogation of his ICD shows no evidence of any shocks in the past 2 
months. What is the most appropriate management plan?

options.text: Cardiology consultation for reprogramming of ICD
Reassurance and follow-up with his cardiologist
Temporary ICD deactivation with magnet application

correctAnswer: Reassurance and follow-up with his cardiologist
englishExplanation:
This patient has experienced 2 “phantom shocks.” The 
perception of a shock in the absence of the actual ICD firing occurs 
in approximately 10% of patients with an ICD and is associated with 
significant anxiety and stress. Appropriate management includes 
reassurance and discharge with a patient’s cardiologist. There is 
no role for IV amiodarone, reprogramming of the ICD or magnet 
application.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض حكى إنو الـ ICD ضربه عدة مرات، بس الـ interrogation ما لقي أي shock فعلي بآخر شهرين. يعني هاد ما عنده إلا phantom shocks، يعني إحساس بصدمة بدون ما الجهاز ين firing. بيحصل هالشي عند حوالي 10% من مرضى الـ ICD، وبيصير معاه قلق وتوتر كبير. أحسن إدارة هي تطمّنه وتخرجه مع متابعة عند الـ cardiologist بتاعه. ما في أي داعي لـ IV amiodarone ولا لإعادة برمجة الـ ICD ولا لتطبيق magnet.
الفخ: طالب بيحاول يبرمج الـ ICD أو يحط magnet لأنو سمع عن treatment للحالات اللي الجهاز بيفصل فيها، بس هون ما في شواطش حقيقية. الفرق: phantom shock يعني إحساس بصدمة بدون firing، وبيحتاج طمأنة مش تدخل.

question:
A 55-year-old woman presents with progressive dyspnea, chest 
pain, and cough over 5 days. She has a past history of renal failure and is on dialysis, last 2 days ago. She does not smoke. Vital 
signs are: temperature, 100.2°F (37.9°C) oral; heart rate, 120 beats 
per minute; respiratory rate, 26 breaths per minute; blood pressure, 
100/60 mm Hg; and oxygen saturation, 96% on room air. Physical 
examination is remarkable for 3-cm jugular venous distention at 
45 degrees, clear lung fields on auscultation, tachycardia without a 
friction rub, trace pretibial edema, and weak peripheral pulses that 
disappear during expiration. Chest radiograph shows an enlarged 
cardiac silhouette and clear lung fields. What would be the most 
appropriate initial intervention?

options.text: Endotracheal intubation with rapid sequence induction
Computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest
Isotonic fluid bolus and point of care cardiac ultrasound

correctAnswer: Isotonic fluid bolus and point of care cardiac ultrasound
englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with cardiac tamponade, presumably secondary to an uremic pericardial effusion. Pulmonary embolus 
is a consideration but less likely, given the picture of normal oxygen 
saturation and an enlarged heart. The initial intervention should be 
fluid loading to maintain preload and cardiac output, followed by 
ultrasound confirmation and likely pericardiocentesis. Fluid loading 
in renal failure may easily result in pulmonary edema, so expeditious 
relief of tamponade is indicated. It is too early for intubation because 
the patient is oxygenating adequately.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض عنده cardiac tamponade، غالباً من uremic pericardial effusion لأنه عنده renal failure وعمعه dialysis. علامات هاد واضحة: distension بالـ jugular veins مع pulmonary fields clear، وضعف الـ peripheral pulses اللي بيختفي مع الزفير، و cardiac silhouette كبير على الـ chest radiograph. أول تدخل هو loading بسوائل isotonic عشان نحافظ على الـ preload والـ cardiac output، وبعدها ultrasound للتأكيد و大概率 pericardiocentesis. لازم ننهي الموضوع بسرعة لأنو الـ fluids ممكن تعمل pulmonary edema عند مريض renal failure.
الفخ: الـ pulmonary embolus بيجي على بالBAL لأنو في dyspnea و tachycardia، بس هون الـ oxygen saturation طبيعية والـ cardiac silhouette كبير، فالـ tamponade أرجح. وكمان الـ intubation مو الوقت الصح لأنو المريض أكسجينة adequate.

question:
A 16-year-old female with a known history of hereditary 
angioedema (HAE) presents with facial swelling. Which HAE medication is not approved for patients in this age group?
englishExplanation:
Icatibant is approved for treatment in adults aged 18 
years or older. Berinert is approved for the treatment of HAE in adult 
and pediatric patients (no lower age limits). Ruconest approved for 
use in adults and pediatric patients ages 11 and older. Ecallantide is 
approved for adult patients and pediatric patients 12 years and older. 
Cinryze is a prophylactic HAE medication not approved for use in 
acute attacks.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ icatibant معتمد لـ treatment الـ hereditary angioedema عند الـ adults اللي عمرهم 18 years or older، ومريضتنا عمرها 16 سنة، فممنوع نعطيه لها. الباقي من الأدوية معتمدين بالعمر: Berinert للـ adult والـ pediatric بدون حد أدنى للعمر، وRuconest للـ adults والـ kids aged 11 and older، وEcallantide للـ adults والـ kids aged 12 and older. أما الـ Cinryze فهو دواء وقائي للـ HAE، ومعتمد للـ prophylaxis مش للـ acute attacks.
الفخ: لو ركزت بس على اسم الدواء ممكن تخلط بين Ecallantide و Ruconest. خلّينا نعرف إنو icatibant هو الوحيد اللي معتمد 18 plus، وإنو Cinryze دواء prophylaxis مش treatment للـ acute attack.

question:
A 76-year-old female is receiving a unit of packed red blood cells, 
when she suddenly develops shortness of breath. On examination, 
she has crackles on auscultation of her lungs bilaterally. Which 
of the following is true regarding transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO) and transfusion-related acute lung injury 
(TRALI)?

options.text: Chest x-ray can often distinguish between TACO and TRALI.
Only TACO should be treated with noninvasive positivepressure ventilation.
TACO typically requires the presence of a significant comorbidity.
TRALI can be treated with aggressive diuresis.

correctAnswer: TACO typically requires the presence of a significant comorbidity.
englishExplanation:
While it is possible to receive enough blood products for 
a healthy person to become volume overloaded, TACO is much more 
commonly seen in patients with underlying heart or renal failure. 
Both TACO and TRALI result in pulmonary edema, meaning they 
can present with similar chest x-ray findings and physical exam findings. Both entities can be treated with noninvasive positive-pressure 
ventilation or intubation and mechanical ventilation, as both treatments are effective in treating pulmonary edema. TRALI, however, 
will not respond to diuretics, because the cause of the pulmonary 
edema is an inflammatory response within the lungs rather than systemic volume overload.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد السؤال بيفرّق بين TACO و TRALI بعد نقل الدم. الـ TACO يعني إنو المريض تبعّل بضغط volume زيادة، وهاد بيحصل غالباً عند مرضى عندهم heart أو renal failure. الاتنين بيسبّبوا pulmonary edema، فالـ chest x-ray والـ exam findings ممكن يكونوا متشابهين، والاتنين ممكن ينعالجوا بـ noninvasive positive-pressure ventilation أو intubation. الفرق الأساسي إنو الـ TRALI سببه inflammatory response داخل الرئة مو volume overload.

question:
A 23-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by 
her boyfriend with a change in mental status. He reports that the 
patient had her psychiatric medications adjusted 3 days ago and has 
been confused since then. The patient’s vital signs are: blood pressure: 162/100 mm Hg; heart rate: 140 beats/min; respiratory rate: 
22 breaths per minute; and temperature: 40.2°C. On physical examination, the patient is noted to have muscle rigidity. Laboratory 
tests are pending. Intravenous (IV) access is obtained, and balanced 
crystalloid fluids are started. Cool mist and fans are applied to the 
patient. What therapy is indicated next?
englishExplanation:
The patient has neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) 
and the best first line treatment option is a benzodiazepine, such as 
lorazepam. Acetaminophen is ineffective in treating the hyperthermia, 
which should be treated with active cooling measures. Cyproheptadine can be used in serotonin syndrome but does not improve NMS. 
Dantrolene can be used in malignant hyperthermia and for refractory, 
severe muscle rigidity but has no mechanistic indication in NMS, and 
evidence for its use is of low quality. Diphenhydramine is used for acute 
dystonia and does not affect the course of NMS.

1961.e2
PART IV  Environment and Toxicology
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض عنده neuroleptic malignant syndrome، يعني عدّلوا أدويته النفسية قبل 3 أيام ومعه confusion و hyperthermia عند 40.2 و muscle rigidity مع tachycardia و hypertension. أحسن أول-line treatment هو benzodiazepine مثل lorazepam. والـ hyperthermia بتنعالج بـ active cooling مثل cool mist والـ fans، مش بـ acetaminophen. والـ dantrolene ماله mechanistic indication في NMS، ومو مستعمل لهنا إلا في rigidity شديدة refractory.
الفخ: cyproheptadine بتخلّي الطالب يفكر فيها لأنها treatment معروف، بس هي للـ serotonin syndrome مو NMS. والفرق بالـ cause: NMS من dopamine antagonists زي antipsychotics، وmalignant hyperthermia من succinylcholine والـ inhaled anesthetics.

question:
Relative to rapid sequence intubation (RSI) in adults, children 
undergoing RSI:

options.text: Are less affected by stomach pressures.
Are more likely to develop bradycardia in response to hypoxia.
Maintain their oxygen saturations longer after paralytics are

correctAnswer: Are more likely to develop bradycardia in response to hypoxia.
englishExplanation:
Children have a higher metabolic rate and thus a higher 
oxygen demand. In the absence of respiratory support, children will 
drop their oxygen saturations more quickly than adults due to their relatively greater consumption of oxygen. Hypoxia is the most common 
reason for bradycardia during intubation in children. The more pliable 
pediatric thorax combined with children's lower ventilatory reserve 
make stominflation a significant impediment to effective respiratory 
support. Pediatric intubations are infrequent and multiple pediatric 
intubation attempts are more common in children than in adults.
arabicExplanation:

الفخ: الخيارين D و E اتجاههم معكوس، لأنو الـ pediatric thorax أكثر مرونة والـ saturations بتنزل أسرع مو أبطأ. وكمان الخيار A غلط لأنو ضغط الـ stomach في الأطفال بيعمل مشاكل أكبر، لا أقل.

question:
Which of the following medications have shown a mortality benefit 
for children in arrest without a clear etiology?
englishExplanation:
There are no randomized control trials of medications in 
pediatric arrest. However, observational studies suggest that epinephrine is beneficial. Other medications are only beneficial for specific 
indications, such as glucose for hypoglycemia.

2051.e3
CHAPTER 159  Neonatal Resuscitation
arabicExplanation:
ليش: ما في randomized control trials لأدوية الـ pediatric arrest، بس الـ observational studies بتبيّن إنو الـ epinephrine مفيد، والجرعة المستخدمة هي 0.01 mg/kg. باقي الأدوية مو مفيدة بشكل عام، كل واحد منها له indication محددة، زي الـ glucose في حالات hypoglycemia. يعني لسه ما في غير الـ epinephrine اللي عنده دليل benefit في الـ arrest بدون etiology واضحة. والـ fluids والـ electrolytes بيعالجون حسب الحاجة، مش كـ medication ثابت لكل طفل.
الفخ: طالب بيحط normal saline أو sodium bicarbonate أو calcium chloride كإجابة لأنها familiar، بس الأدلة بتبيّن إنو غير الـ epinephrine مفيدة بس لـ specific indications. فالجرعة 0.01 mg/kg هي اللي عندها benefit.

question:
An 80-year-old female with history of COPD and arthritis comes to 
the ED following an episode of loss of consciousness while seated at 
the table after eating lunch. The patient and her husband, who witnessed the event, deny any symptoms prior to the event and deny 
any recent illness or symptoms. Her vitals are normal, and her physical exam is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most likely 
etiology of the syncopal episode?
englishExplanation:
Syncope is more likely to have a serious etiology in older 
adults, with 40% ultimately found to have a cardiac etiology. Hypoglycemia is highly unlikely because she does not have diabetes and just ate 
lunch. Cerebrovascular accident and infection are potential causes of 
syncope but are much less likely given that she has been well, asymptomatic, and her examination is normal.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بالمريض المسن اللي عنده loss of consciousness بدون شكاوى قبلها و بدون غياب، السبب cardiac هو الأرجح. السبب إنو الـ syncope عند الـ older adults بكون عندو serious etiology بنسبة 40% بنهاية المطالعة، وبيكون قلبي. الفحص والـ vital signs عندها طبيعيين، وهاد بيرجّح إنو الرجوع المؤقت للدم للقلب أو مشكلة كهربائية. والـ hypoglycemia مستبعدة لأنها مو عندها diabetes واكلت للتو.
الفخ: cerebrovascular accident أو infectious process بيبانوا منطقيين، بس هم أقل احتمالاً لأنو المريضة كانت بخير وبلا symptoms والـ exam طبيعي. الـ key هو السن: فوق 65 يعني الـ cardiac etiology لازم تفكر فيها أول.

question: A 36-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with decreased hearing and a sensation of fullness in her right ear. She reports using cotton-tipped applicators over the past week to remove earwax. Vital signs include a temperature of 98.4°F, a heart rate of 82/min, a respiratory rate of 16/min, a blood pressure of 118/72 mm Hg, and an oxygen saturation of 99% on room air. On physical examination, the right external auditory canal is occluded with cerumen. Warm saline irrigation is performed with an 18-gauge catheter and a plastic curette, but during the procedure, the patient suddenly experiences decreased hearing in the right ear. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Admit the patient to the hospital and arrange for an otolaryngology consultation
Discharge home with a course of oral antibiotics
Have the patient keep the ear dry and arrange otolaryngology follow-up
Place a cotton ball in the ear and discharge home
Prescribe topical otic fluoroquinolone drops and arrange otolaryngology follow-up

correctAnswer: Have the patient keep the ear dry and arrange otolaryngology follow-up
englishExplanation:
This patient experienced an iatrogenic tympanic membrane perforation during cerumen disimpaction and irrigation. Tympanic membrane perforations most often occur in the pars tensa, the thinnest and most anterior portion of the membrane. Causes include infectious complications such as acute otitis media, barotrauma from pressure changes (flying, scuba diving), blast injuries, and instrumentation or attempts at wax removal.

Clinical presentation may include sudden otalgia, hearing loss, tinnitus, and sometimes bloody otorrhea. On physical examination, findings may include visible perforation, dried blood, or inability to visualize the intact tympanic membrane. Most perforations are small and heal spontaneously within weeks to months.

Diagnosis of tympanic membrane perforation is clinical, with management focusing on supportive care. In the absence of contamination or infection, antibiotics are unnecessary. The ear should be kept dry to prevent secondary infection, and referral to otolaryngology is recommended to ensure appropriate follow-up and hearing assessment.



Admitting the patient to the hospital and arranging for otolaryngology consultation (A) is unnecessary for a stable, uncomplicated tympanic membrane perforation after irrigation. Hospitalization and urgent consultation are reserved for penetrating or blast injuries, temporal bone fracture, severe vertigo or facial nerve weakness, or suspected ossicular disruption.

Discharging home with a course of oral antibiotics (B) is not appropriate, as systemic antibiotics are not indicated for a clean, uncomplicated perforation without signs of infection. Oral therapy is recommended when acute otitis media is present or when the perforation is contaminated, such as after exposure to dirty water, and infection is suspected.

Placing a cotton ball in the ear and discharging home (D) does not address care for a tympanic membrane perforation and may trap moisture. The ear should be kept dry, with cotton used only to prevent water exposure during bathing, and otolaryngology follow-up is needed to ensure healing and assess hearing.

Prescribing topical otic fluoroquinolone drops (E), such as ofloxacin, is not needed when there is no contamination or otorrhea. Treatment with otic drops is appropriate only if infection develops or the perforation is contaminated, and aminoglycoside-containing drops should be avoided due to ototoxicity.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common cause of tympanic membrane perforation?

Reveal Answer:
Infection.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Tympanic Membrane Perforation

Foreign body, infection, blast, ↑ barometric pressure
Pars tensa most commonly perforated
Sx: pain, ↓ hearing, bleeding
​Tx: keep ear dry, analgesics, antibiotics for contaminated injuries
90% heal in a few months
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة كانت بتلمس ودنها بـ cotton-tipped applicators، وبعد ما عملنا irrigation للـ cerumen فجأة صار عندها ضعف سمع. هاد يعني إنها اتسببت بـ iatrogenic tympanic membrane perforation أثناء شيل الشمع. أكثر مكان بيتمزق فيه الغشاء هو pars tensa لأنه أرق جزء وأقرب قدام، وأغلب الثقب صغير وبيتعالج لحاله خلال أسابيع لشهور. وبما إن التشخيص إكلينيكي وما في تلوث ولا عدوى ما بنحتاج antibiotics؛ الحل إن الوذ تفضل ناشفة مع تحويل لـ otolaryngology للمتابعة وفحص السمع.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو antibiotics أو حجز بالمستشفى. هاد ثقب بسيط بدون علامات خطر، فما في داعي تحجز ولا تعطي antibiotics، والـ cotton ball ما بتنفع. الحجز والاستشارة العاجلة بتكون لحالات penetrating أو blast injury أو كسر temporal bone أو دوار شديد أو شلل facial nerve.

question: A 42-year-old woman reports 2 days of pain and swelling in the right submandibular area. She has dry mouth and worsening swelling and pain during mealtime. Vital signs include a T of 98.8°F, HR of 82 bpm, BP of 122/80 mm Hg, RR of 16/minute, and SpO2 of 100% on room air. Which of the following is the first-line treatment for this condition?
englishExplanation:
This patient has symptomatic sialolithiasis, which results in outflow obstruction by a stone or calculus in the salivary gland or duct. The submandibular location is most commonly involved because it has more viscous secretions and runs an uphill course. Patients with sialolithiasis note xerostomia (dry mouth), along with increasing swelling and pain during mealtime.

Most salivary stones pass spontaneously. To aid in passage, patients should be started on sialagogues (e.g., sour lozenges), which stimulate salivary secretions and help expel the stone. If they are distal enough, palpable stones may also be milked from the duct by gentle stroking in a posterior to anterior direction.



Antihistamines (A) can worsen this condition by decreasing saliva production and are contraindicated. If possible, patients taking prescribed antihistamines or any medication with anticholinergic effects should discontinue them until symptoms resolve.

Dilation and incision (B) involves manually enlarging and opening the salivary duct to remove the stone surgically. If the obstruction does not resolve with conservative therapy, it may be required to remove the stone.

Oral antibiotics (C) are not required in simple sialolithiasis. However, when suppurative sialadenitis is present, oral antibiotics with staphylococcal coverage are recommended. Sialadenitis typically presents with more severe pain, overlying erythema, fever, malaise, and purulent discharge from the salivary duct.

Sialoendoscopy (E) is a minimally invasive procedure to remove salivary stones that do not resolve with conservative treatment. Because most cases of sialolithiasis improve with conservative treatment (e.g., gland massage, warm compresses, sialagogues, oral analgesics), this is not considered first-line treatment.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common cause of viral sialoadenitis?

Reveal Answer:
Mumps parotitis, which, in contrast to bacterial parotitis, is usually bilateral.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Sialolithiasis

Salivary gland stone causing duct obstruction
Sx: recurrent mouth swelling and pain, worse with meals
Common sites: submandibular gland (most common), parotid gland
Tx: gland massage, warm compresses, sialagogues (e.g., lemon drops)
Severe cases: stone removal (manual or surgical)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها symptomatic sialolithiasis، يعني فيه حجر ساد يمنع خروج الـ saliva من الـ submandibular gland أو الـ duct. وآخر هاد الغدة أكتر وحدة بتتأثر لأن إفرازاتها أكثف وبيجري صاعد. المريضة عندها xerostomia يعني فم ناشف، والتورم والألم بيزيدوا وقت الأكل. أغلب الـ stones بتطلع لحالها، فـ sialagogues مثل الـ sour lozenges بتحفّز إفراز الـ saliva وبتساعد بطرد الحجر. ولما الحجر قريب ممكن نضغط عليه برفق من ورا لقدام.
الفخ: الـ antihistamines بتزيد المشكلة لأنهم بيقللوا إنتاج الـ saliva، والـ antibiotics ما إلها لازمة في سialolithiasis بسيطة. الـ dilation and incision عملية جراحية بتعملها إذا فشل العلاج المحافظ، والـ sialoendoscopy مش أول خطوة.

question: A 65-year-old woman with a history of atrial fibrillation presents with melenic stools. She is found to have a hemoglobin of 5.6 g/dL and consents to a transfusion of packed red blood cells. About 5 minutes after the transfusion begins, the patient reports back pain. On re-evaluation, she is pale, diaphoretic, and gasping for air. Her vital signs are rechecked and found to be T 38.9°C, HR 130 bpm, BP 85/40 mm Hg, and RR 24/min. Which of the following laboratory values is consistent with the patient’s most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Hemolytic transfusion reactions occur as a result of a robust host immune response against donor cells, resulting in cell lysis, the release of cytotoxic and vasoactive agents, activation of the coagulation cascade, and disseminated intravascular coagulation. These reactions are responsible for the majority of transfusion-related mortality and are usually the result of an error in pretransfusion testing, patient identification, or blood labeling. ABO incompatibility is the most common cause. Hemolytic transfusion reactions are typically immediate, an important factor in their diagnosis. Signs and symptoms include transfusion site pain, back pain, fever, chills, hypotension, shortness of breath, and tachycardia. The transfusion should be stopped immediately, and the remainder of the blood sent along with a sample of the recipient’s blood post-transfusion for testing. Evaluation should include a complete blood count, prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), haptoglobin, and a direct Coombs test. Labs should be consistent with hemolysis: haptoglobin levels drop as they are consumed in the hemolytic process, LDH and indirect bilirubin levels rise as they are released from the lysed cells, and the direct Coombs test, which evaluates for antibodies attached to red blood cells, should be positive. Treatment of the reaction is largely supportive with fluids, and vasopressors should be given to support blood pressure and kidney perfusion. These patients must often be admitted to a critical care bed for treatment and monitoring.



Indirect bilirubin (B) is the product of the degradation of heme released from red blood cells as they lyse. Indirect bilirubin is expected to rise in hemolysis, whether transfusion-related or not. The same is true for LDH (C), which is also released by the lysis of red blood cells. The direct Coombs test evaluates for the presence of antibodies attached to red blood cells—it is a test of immune hemolysis. The mechanism of hemolytic transfusion reactions is host antibody attack of donor cells, and as such, the direct Coombs test (D) should be positive.

One Step Further
Question:
How often are transfusions associated with an adverse reaction?

Reveal Answer:
Approximately 20% of the time.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction

Etiology: destruction of donor RBCs by recipient antibodies due to ABO or other antigens or RBC alloantibodies
Sx and findings (immediate or within 24 hours of transfusion): fever, chills, flank pain, red or dark urine, hypotension, manifestations of DIC (e.g., oozing)
Dx: laboratory evidence of hemolysis, direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test may be positive
Tx: stop transfusion, notify transfusion service, IV hydration, pressors (if needed)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها هبوط شديد بالـ hemoglobin، وبعد ما بدأت تنزف packed red blood cells بـ 5 دقايق حسّت بألم بالضهر، وطلع شحوب وتعرّق وضيق نفس، مع حرارة 38.9 و tachycardia و hypotension. هاد كله hemolytic transfusion reaction، وهي بتبدأ فوراً وأشيع سببها عدم توافق ABO. في التحلل الـ haptoglobin بينقص لأنه بينستهلك، والـ LDH والـ bilirubin غير المباشر بيزيدوا لأنهم بيطلعوا من الخلايا المدمرة، والـ direct Coombs بطلع positive. لازم توقفوا الـ transfusion فوراً وتبعثوا بقية الدم مع عينة من المريضة.
الفخ: الخيارات التانية كلها معكوسة، فالـ indirect bilirubin والـ LDH لازم يزيدوا مو يقلوا، والـ direct Coombs ما بتكون negative لأن هدفها تبين أجسام مضادة ملتصقة بالكريات الحمراء. احفظ الترتيب: haptoglobin نازل، و LDH و bilirubin طالعين.

question: A 27-year-old woman with no known medical history presents to the ED after a motor vehicle collision. On arrival, she is confused, has a BP of 80/45 mm Hg, and has an HR of 128 bpm. Her FAST is positive for perihepatic fluid. A packed red blood cell transfusion is started, and suddenly, she becomes dyspneic with audible stridor, diffuse inspiratory and expiratory wheezing, and a generalized urticarial maculopapular rash. What is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Allergic reactions related to transfusions are similar to medication-induced or environmentally-mediated type I IgE hypersensitivity reactions. Mild allergic reactions after transfusions manifest dermatologic changes (e.g., urticaria) and pruritus and constitute most transfusion-related allergic reactions. Anaphylaxis is a clinical diagnosis and manifests with multisystem involvement, including acute pulmonary findings (e.g., dyspnea, hypoxia, wheezing, stridor), hemodynamic alterations (e.g., tachycardia, hypotension), dermatologic changes (e.g., maculopapular rash, urticaria, mucosal edema), gastrointestinal distress (e.g., nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain), and central nervous system abnormalities (e.g., anxiety, altered mentation, syncope).

Treatment includes withdrawal of the precipitating factor, such as stopping any ongoing transfusions. Patients with anaphylaxis should receive 1:1,000 concentration epinephrine 0.3–0.5 mg intramuscular every 5–15 minutes, with consideration of an epinephrine infusion if the initial response to intramuscular therapy is inadequate. Other supportive adjuncts include supplemental oxygen, intravenous rehydration, short-acting inhaled beta-agonists, antihistamines (e.g., diphenhydramine, ranitidine), glucocorticoids (e.g., methylprednisolone, dexamethasone), glucagon, and additional vasopressors if patients experience refractory distributive shock.



A febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reaction (B) presents with fever and generalized symptoms (e.g., headache, myalgias, dyspnea, pain) secondary to recipient antibody to leukocytes in donor products and cytokine accumulation during product storage. This risk has been reduced substantially since the standardization of leukoreduction of blood products.

A hemolytic transfusion reaction (C) occurs when there is incompatibility between the patient and donor ABO blood types or recipient antibodies to donor antigens. Clinical features include a high-grade fever that begins almost immediately after the transfusion is begun, as well as headache, hypotension, and signs of related end-organ dysfunction (e.g., hematuria or dark urine due to kidney failure and dyspnea due to pulmonary edema). Laboratory results will be consistent with hemolysis (e.g., elevated bilirubin, positive Coombs test).

Transfusion-associated circulatory overload (D) presents with gradual onset shortness of breath, often with hypertension and signs of volume overload (e.g., jugular venous distention, lower extremity edema, elevated central venous pressure, elevated brain natriuretic peptide).

Transfusion-related acute lung injury (E) presents with the sudden onset of dyspnea, hypoxemia, fever, bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and absent signs of volume overload. It should not be confused with transfusion-associated circulatory overload.

One Step Further
Question:
What patient populations require cytomegalovirus screening of transfusion products?

Reveal Answer:
Patients who are pregnant, immunocompromised, transplant recipients, transplant candidates, or premature infants.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Transfusion Complications

Massive transfusion: coagulopathy, hypothermia, hypocalcemia
Febrile reaction: common complication, fever or chills

question: A 44-year-old woman develops acute shortness of breath during a transfusion for anemia. Her transfusion is immediately stopped. Vital signs include T 99.0°F (37.2°C), BP 104/64 mm Hg, HR 104 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 85% on room air. Her chest X-ray shows diffuse bilateral infiltrates and normal heart size. Which of the following best describes the pathophysiology and required management for this patient's condition?

options.text: Excessive cardiac preload requiring intravenous diuresis
Inadequate cardiac preload requiring volume resuscitation
Permeability pulmonary edema requiring supportive care

correctAnswer: Permeability pulmonary edema requiring supportive care
englishExplanation:
This patient has transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI), a specific form of acute respiratory distress syndrome. TRALI occurs in about 1 of 12,000 transfusions and is the leading cause of transfusion-related mortality in the United States. It presents as sudden onset hypoxemia within 6 hours of transfusion of any blood product, including packed red blood cells. It is thought that either leukocyte antibodies or other substances in donor plasma interact with the recipient’s white blood cells and pulmonary vascular endothelium, causing permeability and pulmonary edema. Like other forms of acute respiratory distress syndrome, it is defined by a ratio of arterial oxygen concentration to the fraction of inspired oxygen (PaO2 / FiO2) < 300. It must be distinguished from cardiogenic pulmonary edema, specifically transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO), as the management approach is completely different. While TACO is treated with diuretics, TRALI may deteriorate with aggressive diuresis. TACO is more likely to present with elevated blood pressure, while TRALI may have low blood pressure. A small cardiac silhouette on a chest X-ray is more suggestive of TRALI than circulatory overload. Treatment is with respiratory supportive care, which may include oxygen, intubation, and lung protective ventilation strategies. All cases of suspected TRALI should be reported to the blood bank.



Many of the known transfusion reactions involve an antibody-mediated reaction (A), including TRALI, along with hemolytic transfusion reaction, febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reaction, mild allergic reactions, and anaphylaxis. However, systemic corticosteroids are not part of the management in TRALI. Steroids are used as part of the management of anaphylaxis, along with epinephrine and antihistamines. Anaphylaxis after transfusion is thought to involve a reaction to donor IgA and occurs more commonly in patients with a genetic IgA deficiency.

Excessive cardiac preload requiring intravenous diuresis (B) is a description of TACO, not TRALI.

Inadequate cardiac preload requiring volume resuscitation (C) may be true of many patients with hypovolemia receiving transfusions. However, it does not describe TRALI, which is the specific adverse transfusion reaction occurring in this case.

Reveal Answer:
Extravascular hemolytic transfusion reaction.

question: Which organ system do the clinical manifestations of anaphylaxis most often involve?
englishExplanation:
Anaphylaxis is an IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction. Antigens bind to IgE on the surface of mast cells and basophils, resulting in degranulation of mediators. Histamine is the most important mediator and is responsible for most symptoms related to anaphylaxis.

Symptoms typically occur within minutes of exposure. The most frequently seen symptoms (in nearly 90% of patients with anaphylaxis) involve the skin. Patients often describe a generalized feeling of warmth and tingling followed by pruritus, which can be accompanied by flushing, urticaria, and angioedema.

Anaphylaxis is highly likely if one of the following criteria are met: (1) acute onset of symptoms involving the skin, mucosal tissue or both in addition to either respiratory compromise or signs and symptoms of end organ dysfunction (e.g., hypotension, syncope), (2) symptoms involving two organ systems (e.g., skin/mucosal tissue, respiratory compromise, hypotension or gastrointestinal symptoms) that rapidly occur after exposure to a likely allergen, or (3) hypotension after exposure to a known allergen for that patient.



Cardiovascular (A) signs and symptoms of anaphylaxis include hypotension, chest tightness, and dysrhythmias, including sinus tachycardia, premature atrial and ventricular contractions, and atrial fibrillation. Approximately 30–50% of patients with anaphylaxis will have cardiovascular symptoms.

GI (B) signs and symptoms include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. They occur in 25–30% of affected patients.

Respiratory (C) signs and symptoms, including dyspnea, wheezing, hoarseness secondary to laryngeal edema, and respiratory failure, occur in 70–80% of patients with anaphylaxis.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the drug of choice for the treatment of anaphylaxis?

Reveal Answer:
Epinephrine 0.3–0.5 mL (1:1,000 concentration) IM.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Anaphylaxis

Preexisting IgE antibodies → mast cell degranulation → shock, airway compromise
Leading cause of fatal anaphylaxis: penicillin (adults), peanut (children)
PE
Skin: urticaria, flushing
Mucosal tissue: lip, tongue, uvula swelling
Respiratory: bronchospasm, dyspnea, stridor
GI: vomiting, diarrhea, crampy abdominal pain
Cardiovascular: hypotension or end-organ dysfunction
Epinephrine
Adults: 0.3–0.5 mL 1:1,000 (1 mg/mL) solution IM every 5–15 min
Children: 0.01 mg/kg 1:1,000 (1 mg/mL) solution IM every 5–15 min
​Refractory hypotension in a patient on beta-blockers: glucagon
Adjunctive medicines include histamine H1 and H2 antagonists, corticosteroids, beta-2 agonists, and glucagon
arabicExplanation:
ليش: anaphylaxis هي reaction حساسية من نوع IgE. البادخل binds على الـ IgE عالـ surface الـ mast cells والـ basophils، فبيحصل degranulation وتطلع الـ mediators، وأهمها histamine اللي مسؤول عن أغلب الأعراض. الأعراض بتصير خلال دقايق من التعرض. والأعراض الجلدية بتشوفوها بـ 90% تقريباً من مرضى anaphylaxis، يعني إحساس بدفء عام و tingling مع pruritus، ومعه flushing و urticaria و angioedema، وهاد كمان معيار من معايير تشخيص الـ anaphylaxis.
الفخ: الخيار الي بيلفت الانتباه هو cardiovascular لأن الـ hypotension بيخيف، بس الأعراض القلبية موجودة بـ 30–50% من الحالات بس، والـ GI أقل كمان. احفظ إن الـ skin هي الأكثر شيوعاً بـ 90% تقريباً.

question: A 29-year-old man presents to the emergency department for facial swelling. He states that symptoms started 1 hour prior to arrival after being slapped on the right side of his face. He reports that symptoms started with mild right-sided facial swelling but has progressed to involve his entire face as well as his mouth. He has no history of allergies. He does not use any medications. When asked, he notes that his father and paternal grandfather have had similar episodes in the past but were never formally diagnosed. On exam, he has bilateral facial swelling with edema noted in the lips, tongue, and uvula. There are no rashes on the skin exam. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
englishExplanation:
The patient is presenting with hereditary angioedema and should be given fresh frozen plasma. Hereditary angioedema is an autosomal dominant disorder that is characterized by a deficiency of C1 esterase inhibitor. Patients will present with recurrent acute bouts of angioedema without urticaria or pruritus. Minor trauma can trigger episodes, but oftentimes a clear trigger is not identifiable. Hereditary angioedema can be diagnosed by obtaining serum C4 levels.

Normal treatments for anaphylaxis and allergic reactions, such as epinephrine, corticosteroids, and antihistamines, are ineffective at treating hereditary angioedema. Assessment and protection of the airway is the most important aspect of management, as asphyxiation from laryngeal edema is the most common cause of death. First-line medical treatment involves the administration of either plasma-derived or recombinant C1 esterase inhibitor. Bradykinin B2-receptor antagonists and kallikrein inhibitors are also effective treatments. However, these therapies are often unavailable, so fresh frozen plasma is the therapy of choice.



Cryoprecipitate (A) is prepared from plasma and has a role in treating many bleeding disorders but is not efficacious in treating hereditary angioedema.

Epinephrine (C) is a first-line treatment for anaphylaxis, which can also present with angioedema, but is ineffective in hereditary angioedema.

Diphenhydramine (B) is effective at treating histamine-mediated allergic reactions but has no role in hereditary angioedema.

One Step Further
Question:
What level of serum C4 suggests hereditary angioedema?

Reveal Answer:
< 30% of normal.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Angioedema

Sx: swelling of the tongue, face, larynx, bowels
Mast cell mediated: associated with urticaria, bronchospasm, hypotension
Allergic reactions (type I hypersensitivity), ASA, NSAIDs, idiopathic
Dx: tryptase level may confirm episode was mast cell mediated
Bradykinin mediated: not associated with urticaria
ACE inhibitors, hereditary or acquired C1 inhibitor deficiency
Dx: ↓ C4 in C1 inhibitor deficiency, C1 inhibitor protein level and function
Tx
Laryngeal angioedema: airway management, intubation
Anaphylaxis: epinephrine, IVF
Nonanaphylaxis mast cell mediated: antihistamines, steroids
ACE inhibitors: discontinue culprit medication, supportive care
Hereditary: C1 esterase inhibitor concentrate, kallikrein inhibitor, bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist, fresh frozen plasma
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده hereditary angioedema، يعني disorder وراثي dominant فيه نقص بـ C1 esterase inhibitor. الدلائل المهمة إن التورم جاء فجأة بعد slap خفيف على الوجه، ومفيش urticaria ولا pruritus، وإنه في تاريخ عائلي عند أبوه وجدّه. التشخيص بقياس serum C4. وأهم نقطة في الإدارة هي الـ airway، لأن الخنق من الـ laryngeal edema هو سبب الوفاة. العلاج الأساسي هو C1 esterase inhibitor من البلازما أو recombinant، وكمان مضادات Bradykinin B2 و kallikrein inhibitors، بس لأن هاد therapies غالباً ما بتكون متوفرة، fresh frozen plasma هو الخيار المتاح.
الفخ: الفخ الأساسي إنك تعطي epinephrine أو antihistamines أو corticosteroids لأنك فاكرها anaphylaxis عادي، وهاي ما بتشتغل بالـ hereditary angioedema لأن المشكلة مش histamine. وكمان cryoprecipitate مش للـ hereditary angioedema.

question: A patient presents to the ED with an anaphylactic reaction to peanuts and receives epinephrine. The beta-2 agonist effect from epinephrine has which one of the following primary actions?
englishExplanation:
Anaphylaxis is a severe, dramatic type-1 hypersensitivity reaction (i.e., immunoglobulin E-mediated) that can progress rapidly and may cause death if not recognized and treated early and appropriately. Definitions vary from source to source as to the criteria for anaphylaxis. It should be suspected when a patient exposed to a known allergen develops hypotension. Anaphylaxis is associated with urticaria; generalized flushing or itching; or swelling of the tongue, lips, uvula, or skin within minutes to hours after allergen exposure, along with either respiratory distress or hypoxia, hypotension, or other organ dysfunction (e.g., syncope, incontinence). Finally, the presence of two or more of the following within minutes to hours after allergen exposure is diagnostic of anaphylaxis: skin or mucosal changes, respiratory symptoms, symptomatic hypotension, vomiting or persistent GI cramps.

Anaphylaxis occurs when IgE interacts with mast cells and basophils, causing them to degranulate and release their contents (inflammatory mediators), beginning a cascade of inflammatory responses. These contents include histamine, tryptase, and cytokines (e.g., tumor necrosis factor-alpha). Prostaglandins and leukotrienes are downstream products of this cascade. Physiologic changes that occur in response to these inflammatory mediators include vasodilation, bronchial secretion, tachycardia, bronchoconstriction, and increased vascular permeability.

Epinephrine is the mainstay of therapy and acts on alpha- and beta-adrenergic receptors. Activation of alpha-1 receptors decreases mucosal edema and induces peripheral vasoconstriction, improving hypotension. Beta-1 receptor activation leads to increased heart rate (chronotropy) and contractility (inotropy). Beta-2 receptor activation leads to bronchodilation and stabilizes mast cells and basophils to limit the further release of inflammatory mediators. The dose of epinephrine for anaphylaxis is 0.3–0.5 mg to be given intramuscularly in the anterolateral thigh.



The alpha-1 (not beta-2) activation from epinephrine leads to decreased mucosal edema (A).

Increased chronotropy (B) and inotropy (C) are the result of beta-1 (not beta-2) receptor activation.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the IM dose of epinephrine for anaphylaxis in children < 30 kg?

Reveal Answer:
0.01 mg/kg of 1:1,000 concentration IM or 0.15 mg autoinjector.
