Pseudocholinesterase deficiency is the correct diagnosis, as it leads to prolonged paralysis after suxamethonium administration due to the body's inability to break down the drug effectively. This genetic condition affects about 1 in
3000 people and is known as sux apnoea.
https://www.rcoa.ac.uk/sites/default/files/documents/2019-11/Factsheet-Suxapnoeaweb.pdf
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بعد ما عملنا rapid sequence induction بـ suxamethonium، المريضضل مشلول أكتر من ساعتين، وهاد بيحكي إن جسمه ما قدر يفكك الـ drug بشكل كافي. السبب هو pseudocholinesterase deficiency، يعني نقص في الإنزيم اللي بيكسّر الـ suxamethonium. هاد نقص وراثي بيصير لواحد من كل 3000 شخص تقريباً، وبيعرفوا اسم تاني له sux apnoea. لأن الـ enzyme ناقص، الشلل بيفضل شويان طويل بعد ما ياخد الجرعة.
الفخ: الناس بيسووا malignant hyperthermia لأنهم بيسمعوا إن العضلات بتنقبض بعد دوا التخدير، بس هاد بيبدأ بحرارة عالية وتصلّب صلب، مش شلل مستمر بس. وneuromuscular junction disorder بيكون مزمن ويظهر قبل الدوا. لازم تفرّق إن المشكلة كلها بقاء الشلل بعد الـ suxamethonium.

question:
A 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes presents to the Emergency Department with reduced consciousness and agitation. She
was found by her carer.
Vital signs:
• HR 92
• BP 138/84
• RR 18
• SpO2 97% on room air
• Temp 36.8°C
Examination:
• GCS 11 (E2 V3 M6)
• Confused and agitated
• Capillary glucose 2.8 mmol/L

The triage nurse has cannulated her.
What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Encourage the patient to drink a can of coke

englishExplanation:
200ml 10% dextrose
Explanation
Patient has severe symptomatic hypoglycemia (GCS 11, glucose 2.8)
with IV access. Using 10% dextrose results in lower post-treatment hyperglycaemia. Given the risk of extravasation and phlebitis from 50%
dextrose, 10% dextrose is the preferred option. 150- 200 mls of 10%
dextrose is usually sufficient to correct hypoglycaemia for most patients.
Incorrect Answers Explained:
A) IM Glucagon: Inappropriate when IV access is available. Used in unconscious diabetics without IV access. Takes longer to work.
C) 400mL 10% dextrose: Unnecessarily large fluid volume.
D) Continuous infusion: Too slow for acute symptomatic hypoglycemia.
It is used for maintenance after initial correction. The patient needs immediate glucose elevation.
E) Oral Coke: Dangerous in reduced consciousness (GCS 11). Aspiration
risk. Oral glucose is only appropriate in alert patients who can protect
their airway.
https://www.rcemlearning.co.uk/modules/management-of-hypoglycaemia/lessons/management-9/topic/treatment-of-diabetic-emergency/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاي المريضة عندها hypoglycaemia symptomatica severe، يعني GCS 11 وجلوكوز 2.8 mmol/L، وعندها IV access جاهز من الـ triage nurse. عشان كذا لازم تعطيها على طول 200 ml من 10% dextrose IV. الـ 10% بيعطي hyperglycaemia أقل بعد العلاج، وبتخفف خطر الـ extravasation والـ phlebitis اللي بتراوح مع الـ 50% dextrose. عادةً 150 لـ 200 ml من 10% بيكفوا most من المرضى، فمفي داعي تعطي volumes كبيرة.
الفخ: الـ IM glucagon بيتأخر شوي وبيستعمل للمريض اللي ما عنده IV access، وهنا في. والـ coke عن طريق الفم خطر لأن GCS 11 وخطر aspiration، والـ oral glucose بس للمريض الـ alert اللي بيحمي airway بتاعه. والـ continuous infusion بطيئة وبيستعمل بعد التصحيح الأولي.

question:
During direct laryngoscopy, which of the following Cormack-Lehane grades is characterised by visualisation of only
the epiglottis, with no view of the glottis?
englishExplanation:
Grade III
Explanation
Cormack-Lehane Grade III is characterised by visualisation of only the epiglottis, with no view of the glottis. This
grading system is used to assess the difficulty of endotracheal intubation during direct laryngoscopy.

Grade I shows a full view of the glottis
Grade II shows a partial view of the glottis or arytenoids
Grade III is characterised by visualisation of only the epiglottis, with no view of the glottis
Grade IV shows no glottic structures visible (not even the epiglottis)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00526 source page 487](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00526-study-p487.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00526 source page 488](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00526-study-p488.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00526 source page 1115](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00526-frcem-p1115.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00526 source page 1116](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00526-frcem-p1116.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: نظام Cormack-Lehane بيقيّم صعوبة الـ endotracheal intubation وقت الـ direct laryngoscopy. بـ Grade I بتشوف الـ glottis كاملة، وGrade II بتشوف جزء منها أو الـ arytenoids. أما Grade III فاللي ظاهر هو الـ epiglottis بس، وما في أي view للـ glottis. هاد بالزبط هو التوصيف اللي بالسؤال. وGrade IV معناها ما في أي glottic structures ظاهرة، ولا الـ epiglottis. النظام بيقسّم الصعوبة لأربع درجات عشان تعرف مستوى Tubing difficulty.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو Grade I وGrade II، لأن هدول بيبنوا جزء من الـ glottis أو الـ arytenoids. وGrade IV معناها حتى الـ epiglottis ما بتشوفها. ذاكر إن Grade III يعني epiglottis بس.

question:
A 25-year-old female presents to the Emergency Department with severe asthma exacerbation. Her vital signs
show SpO2 88% on 15L non-rebreather mask, respiratory rate 40, heart rate 135, BP 145/90. Despite appropriate
initial management, including nebulised bronchodilators. IV steroids and magnesium, she continues to deteriorate
and requires intubation.
Which of the following is the most appropriate induction agent?
englishExplanation:
Ketamine 1-2mg/kg
Explanation
Ketamine is the preferred induction agent for severe asthma requiring intubation because:
It has bronchodilating properties through indirect β2-agonist effects
It maintains respiratory drive and preserves airway reflexes longer than other agents
It provides cardiovascular stability through sympathomimetic effects
arabicExplanation:
ليش: Ketamine هو agent الاختيار لما يكون عندك severe asthma وتحتاج intubation. السبب إنه إلو خصائص bronchodilating عن طريق تأثير indirect β2-agonist على الـ bronchi. كمان بيحافظ على الـ respiratory drive وبيخلي الـ airway reflexes أطول من باقي الـ induction agents. وكمان بيوفر ثبات للـ cardiovascular system عن طريق تأثيراته sympathomimetic. يعني بتحمي القلب والرئة بنفس الوقت، وهاد اللي بيفرق في الربو.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو propofol أو thiopentone، لأنهم induction agents عاديين بلا bronchodilating effect. وetomidate حتى لو cardioselective ما بتوصف كـ bronchodilator. وmidazolam لحاله ما بيعطي sedation كافية، وممكن يزيد bronchospasm.

question:
You are delivering a teaching session on resuscitation in special circumstances. The foundation doctor asks which
manoeuvre is recommended for a deteriorating pregnant patient to relieve aortocaval compression.

options.text: Manually displace the uterus to the right
Manually displace the uterus to the left

correctAnswer: Manually displace the uterus to the left
englishExplanation:
Manually displace the uterus to the left
Explanation
In pregnant patients beyond 20 weeks gestation, the gravid uterus can compress the inferior vena cava and aorta in
the supine position, reducing venous return and cardiac output. Manual left uterine displacement helps relieve this
aortocaval compression by moving the weight of the uterus off these major vessels.
This manoeuvre is preferred over left lateral tilt as it:
Allows effective chest compressions to be performed if needed
Can be performed while maintaining spinal immobilization if trauma is present
Provides immediate relief of compression
https://www.resus.org.uk/print/pdf/node/11323

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00535 source page 1130](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00535-frcem-p1130.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00535 source page 1131](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00535-frcem-p1131.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00535 source page 1132](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00535-frcem-p1132.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00535 source page 1133](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00535-frcem-p1133.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بعد 20 أسبوع حمل، الـ gravid uterus بيميل يضغط على الـ inferior vena cava والـ aorta وهاي بوضعية supine. هاد الضغط بنقص الـ venous return والـ cardiac output. الـ manual left uterine displacement بيرفع ثقل الرحم عن هالأوعية الكبيرة وبيخفف الضغط بشكل مباشر وفوري. هاد أحسن من الـ left lateral tilt لثلاث أسباب: بتقدر تعمل compressions فعالة، وبتقدر تستمر بالـ spinal immobilization إذا في trauma، وبتعطي راحة فورية للـ compression. فبيترجع الـ venous return وبيتحسن الـ cardiac output.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو supine position أو head-down tilt، لأن هدول بيزيدوا الضغط على الـ vena cava والـ aorta. وكمان الـ left lateral tilt بيعطي راحة أقل وبتصير compressions الصدر أصعب.

question:
A 72-year-old female with polytrauma following a fall down stairs has completed the primary survey and had a normal CT Trauma Scan. Rapid sequence intubation (RSI) was performed to secure the airway for transfer to ITU.
The patient was connected to a portable ventilator and monitors, and the transfer checklist was completed before
being transferred.
During transfer to ITU, an alarm is triggered, indicating "APNOEA."
Which of these is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.text: Stop the transfer and return to ED

englishExplanation:
Check the EtCO2 connection
Explanation
During transfer, the “APNOEA” alarm likely indicates a monitoring issue OR an ETT/ventilator disconnection.
Connection/dislodgement issues are common in transfer scenarios. If there is no connection issue and the patient is

truly apneic, the next step would be to disconnect the ventilator and manually bag the patient.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: إنذار APNOEA أثناء الـ transfer غالباً بيحكي إن في مشكلة بالـ monitoring أو إن الـ ETT فك من الـ ventilator. مشاكل الـ connection والـ dislodgement شائعة جداً في سيناريوهات النقل، فهاد أول لازم تتحقق منه. لازم تفحص الـ EtCO2 connection فوراً عشان تتأكد إن الـ ETT لسا بالبلعوم وإن الـ patient عم يتنفس. إذا ما في مشكلة بالـ connection والمريض فعلاً apneic، الخطوة الجاية هي تفصل الـ ventilator وتسوي manual bagging. بس الفحص لازم يكون قبل أي شي ثاني.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو ترفع الـ FiO2 لـ 1.0، لأن زيادة الأكسجين ما بتحل الـ disconnection. وكمان ترجع للم Emergency بيضيّع وقت، وendotracheal suction مش أول خطوة إذا الـ ETT مفصول.

question:
A 35-year-old patient presents to the Emergency Department with sudden onset of shortness of breath, widespread
urticaria, and hypotension following a bee sting.
Which of the following statements about the pathophysiology of this patient's condition is most accurate?

options.text: IgM is the primary antibody responsible for the allergic reaction
Complement activation is the main trigger for mast cell degranulation
IgE bound to mast cells initiates the release of histamine and other mediators
T-cells directly cause the symptoms of anaphylaxis
IgG is the key immunoglobulin in immediate hypersensitivity reactions

correctAnswer: IgE bound to mast cells initiates the release of histamine and other mediators
englishExplanation:
IgE bound to mast cells initiates the release of histamine and other mediators
Explanation
IgE is the primary mediator of anaphylaxis. When an allergen (in this case, bee venom) cross-links IgE antibodies
bound to mast cells, it triggers degranulation and the release of various inflammatory mediators, including histamine,
which cause the symptoms of anaphylaxis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها anaphylaxis بعد لدغة نحلة، يعني ضيق نفس مفاجئ وurticaria منتشرة مع hypotension. الـ IgE هو الوسيلة الأساسية بالـ immediate hypersensitivity، وهو مربوط على سطح الـ mast cells. لما الـ allergen، وهو سم النحل، يعمل cross-link للـ IgE، هاد بيفعّل degranulation ويطلق الـ mediators مثل histamine. هاد الـ mediators هي اللي بيسبّبوا الـ urticaria والـ hypotension والـ bronchospasm. يعني بدون IgE مافي allergic reaction من هاد النوع.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو IgM أو IgG، لأنهم مش الـ immunoglobulin اللي بيشتغل بالـ immediate hypersensitivity. وكمان T-cells ما بيسبّبوا الأعراض مباشرة، والـ complement activation مش الـ trigger الأساسي للـ degranulation.

question:
A 45-year-old Japanese man presents to the emergency department after he had a witnessed syncopal 
event. The patient denies any prodromal symptoms 
prior to the event nor injuries secondary to the event. 
He denies recent illness, chest pain before or after the 
event, bloody or back bowel movements, shortness of 
breath, recent surgeries, or lower extremity swelling. 
He has no significant past medical history or social history and he takes no medications. He is adopted and 
does not know his family history. Physical examination including vital signs are unremarkable. Laboratory evaluation shows no abnormalities. Chest x-ray 
shows no acute abnormalities. ECG was performed 
and is shown in Figure 2.1. What is the appropriate 
NEXT step in care for this patient?

options.text: Discharge patient home with outpatient followup with his primary care physician
Order a CT angiogram to rule out pulmonary

englishExplanation:
1.  The answer is A. (Chapter 11) The ECG shown is consistent with Brugada’s syndrome. In leads V1 and V2, it displays the typical downsloping ST-segment elevation and 
additionally the QRS morphology mimics a right bundle 
branch block pattern. This syndrome commonly affects 
men of Southeast Asia and Japanese descent, is autosomal 
dominant genetically, and results in sodium channel dysfunction. It is crucial to identify due to the risk of sudden 
cardiac death. This can be prevented by placement of an 
internal automatic implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. 
The ECG pattern is not consistent with an ST-elevated 
myocardial infarction so emergent cardiac catheterization is not warranted. The risk of sudden death that is 
preventable by insertion of an automatic implantable 
cardioverter-defibrillator (AICD) mandating cardiology 
involvement and not simply follow-up with a primary care 
physician. Nothing in the history of present illness, physical examination, laboratory evaluation, or ECG suggests a 
pulmonary embolus as the cause of the patient’s syncope.

![Tintinalli-2023-00021 source page 22](images/Tintinalli-2023-00021-Tintinalli-2023-p0022.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00021 source page 27](images/Tintinalli-2023-00021-Tintinalli-2023-p0027.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ ECG عند هاد المريض بيبيّن Brugada's syndrome، يعني في leads V1 وV2 شف ST-segment elevation هابط بشكل مائل وشكل الـ QRS بيعاكس right bundle branch block. هاد الـ syndrome بيصيب خاصة رجال من Southeast Asia واليابان، وبيورث autosomally dominant، وبيخلي في dysfunction بالـ sodium channels. أهم شي بيه خطر sudden cardiac death، وهاد الخطر ممكن تمنعه لما تحط AICD. يعني لازم تستشير cardiology لتركيب الجهاز، مو بس متابعة مع طبيب العائلة.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو CT angiogram لاستبعاد pulmonary embolism، لأن ما في شي بالتاريخ ولا الفحص ولا الـ ECG بيوجه لسبب الـ embolism. وكمان ما في داعي cardiac catheterization طارئ لأن الـ ECG مش ST-elevation MI.

question:
What does the section marked with the letter X on the 
end-tidal capnogram represent (Figure 2.2)?
englishExplanation:
6.  The answer is B. (Chapter 16) W portion represents 
inspiratory baseline. The V portion represents expiratory upstroke. The X portion represents expiratory plateau. The Y portion represents end-tidal concentration. 
The Z portion of the capnogram represents inspiratory 
downstroke.

![Tintinalli-2023-00026 source page 23](images/Tintinalli-2023-00026-Tintinalli-2023-p0023.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00026 source page 24](images/Tintinalli-2023-00026-Tintinalli-2023-p0024.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00026 source page 27](images/Tintinalli-2023-00026-Tintinalli-2023-p0027.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ capnogram بيقسّمه لأجزاء، وكل جزء إله معنى. الجزء W هو الـ inspiratory baseline، وجزء V هو الـ expiratory upstroke. الجزء X اللي عليه علامة بالسؤال هو الـ expiratory plateau، يعني الجزء المستوي اللي بتشهده أثناء الزفير. أما الجزء Z فهو الـ inspiratory downstroke. والـ end-tidal concentration هو الجزء Y، مو X. فالموجة كلها بترتيب W-V-X-Y-Z، وحددي X هو اللي بين الـ upstroke والـ downstroke.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو end-tidal concentration، لأن هاد هو الجزء Y مو X. وinspiratory baseline هو الجزء W. لازم تحفظ الترتيب W-V-X-Y-Z عشان ما تضيّع.

question:
A 70-year-old woman with dementia presents with 
signs and symptoms consistent with acute gastroenteritis for the past 4 days. Her caregivers report 
that she has been unable to eat or drink due to her 
severe vomiting and has also had profuse diarrhea. 
On examination, she is notably dehydrated, tachycardic, and lethargic. Her labs reveal a sodium level 
of 165 mEq/L. Her prior sodium level 3 months 
prior was 150 mEq/L. Her caregivers state that her by 
mouth intake is poor at baseline due to her dementia 
and she usually has chronic mild hypernatremia. She 
is admitted for IV fluid resuscitation and correction 
of her sodium level. She is started on high-volume 
D5 water IV fluids. Twelve hours later, she becomes 
acutely unresponsive and has to be intubated. Repeat 
labs reveal a sodium level of 135. Based on this information, what is your diagnosis as the cause of her 
change in mental status?
englishExplanation:
7.  The answer is C. (Chapter 17) In patients who have 
acute hypernatremia, and the adaptation of brain cells is 
thus incomplete, correction of sodium levels can be performed at the rate of 1 mEq/L/h. However, in patients of 
whom hypernatremia is chronic, onset >48 hours, the rate 
of correction should be lower, no more than 0.5 mEq/L/h 
with a total maximum correction in 24 hours no more 
than 10 to 12 mEq. The patient in this question stem had 
her sodium dropped 30 points within 12 hours, which is 

CHAPTER 2  •  Resuscitation
15
much too fast. As a result, this patient has developed diffuse cerebral edema with resulting neurologic changes. 
Osmotic demyelination syndrome occurs after the rapid 
correction of low sodium levels. Central pontine myelinolysis is the old former term used for what is now called 
osmotic demyelination syndrome, which again occurs in 
the setting of rapid correction of hyponatremia. Acute 
intracerebral hemorrhage is not the correct diagnosis as 
this is not the known complication from rapid correction 
of sodium levels.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها hypernatremia مزمنة، يعني أكثر من 48 ساعة، والـ sodium كان 150 قبل 3 شهور ووصل 165. بهاد الشكل من chronic hypernatremia لازم تصحّح الـ sodium ببطء، ماكسيموم 0.5 mEq/L/h، وما في أكتر من 10 لـ 12 mEq خلال 24 ساعة. هون الـ sodium نزل 30 نقطة خلال 12 ساعة، وهاد كتير سريع. التصحيح السريع بهاد الشكل بيسبّب diffuse cerebral edema، وهاد اللي فسّر تغيّر الوعي عندها. أما acute hypernatremia فالتصحيح المسموح فيها 1 mEq/L/h.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو osmotic demyelination syndrome، لأن هاد بيصير بعد التصحيح السريع للـ low sodium مو للـ high sodium. وcentral pontine myelinolysis هو الاسم القديم للـ osmotic demyelination نفسه. أما acute intracerebral hemorrhage فمش من الـ complications المعروفة للـ sodium correction.

question:
A 65-year-old man presents to the emergency department complaining of coughing, increased sputum 
production, and dyspnea with exertion. He has a past 
medical history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. On examination, he is mildly tachypneic, 
speaks short sentences, and has wheezing in bilateral 
lung fields. He has a new oxygen requirement and is 
placed on 2L nasal cannula. He is tachycardiac, afebrile, 
with normal blood pressure. A rhythm strip is obtained 
which reveals the following (Figure 2.3). What is the 
APPROPRIATE management of this patient?

options.text: Bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics, and hospital admission

correctAnswer: Bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics, and hospital admission
englishExplanation:
8.  The answer is B. (Chapter 18) This is a patient whose 
rhythm strip displays multifocal atrial tachycardia (MAT). 
MAT has three or more distinct p-wave morphologies. 
This irregular rhythm is most often found in elderly 
patients with decompensated chronic lung disease, but it 
may also be present in patients with heart failure and/or 
sepsis. Treatment for MAT is directed toward the underlying disorder, which is why answer B that focuses on 
treatment for the patient’s chronic obstructive pulmonary 
disease (COPD) exacerbation is the correct answer. Antidysrhythmic treatment is not indicated for MAT, which is 
why the other answers are all incorrect.

![Tintinalli-2023-00028 source page 24](images/Tintinalli-2023-00028-Tintinalli-2023-p0024.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00028 source page 28](images/Tintinalli-2023-00028-Tintinalli-2023-p0028.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ rhythm strip بيبيّن multifocal atrial tachycardia، يعني 3 أو أكثر من أشكال مختلفة للـ p-wave. هاد الـ irregular rhythm بييجي غالباً عند كبار السن مع chronic lung disease decompensated، وممكن كمان مع heart failure أو sepsis. هاد pacient عنده COPD exacerbation وعنده require جديد للأكسجين، يعني المشكلة الأساسية هي راحته. العلاج الأساسي للـ MAT هو معالجة السبب اللي وراه. ولهذا bronchodilators وsteroids وantibiotics ودخول المستشفى هي الخطوة الصح.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو أي antiarrhythmic مثل amiodarone أو diltiazem أو metoprolol، لأن antidysrhythmic treatment مش indicated للـ MAT. اللي بيسوّا كذا بيفكّر إنه rhythm تسرّع قلب، بس هاي مش ventricular tachycardia.

question:
For which of the following conditions is digoxin 
contraindicated?
englishExplanation:
9.  The answer is D. (Chapter 19) Digoxin use is contraindicated for ventricular arrhythmias. Ventricular tachycardia is an adverse side effect of digoxin use and thus using 
it as treatment for this condition would likely worsen the 
ventricular tachycardia. Digoxin is indicated for rate control for atrial fibrillation or atrial tachycardia, but it is not 
considered first-line therapy. Digoxin is also used for symptom control in congestive heart failure when symptoms are 
unrelieved by diuretics and angiotensin-converting enzyme 
inhibitors.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ digoxin ما بينفع مع ventricular arrhythmias. أصلاً الـ ventricular tachycardia هو نفسه adverse effect ممكن يصير مع الـ digoxin، فإعطاؤه عشان يعالجه معناه إنك بتخلي الـ VT أسوأ. الـ digoxin بينفع في rate control عند الـ atrial fibrillation والـ atrial tachycardia، بس مو first-line therapy. كمان بينفع لتخفيف الأعراض في congestive heart failure لما الـ symptoms ما تتحسن مع الـ diuretics والـ ACE inhibitors. فالـ contraindication الجواب هو ventricular tachycardia.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو atrial fibrillation وatrial flutter، لأن الـ digoxin مسموح فيهم للـ rate control. وcongestive heart failure ما فيها contraindication. لازم تفرّق ventricular arrhythmias عن supraventricular ones.

question:
What is the MOST common adverse reaction in 
patients treated with hyperbaric therapy?
englishExplanation:
11.  The answer is A.  (Chapter 21) Middle ear barotrauma is the most common adverse effect of hyperbaric 
oxygen treatment (HBO). As the ambient pressure within 
the hyperbaric chamber increases, the patient must equalize the pressure within the middle ear. If the patient is 
unable to achieve this, tympanostomy tubes must then 
be placed in order for HBO therapy to continue. Nuclear 
cataract can occur when treatment hours exceeds 150 to 
200 hours. Progressive myopia may occur in patients who 
undergo prolonged daily HBO therapy, but typically it 
reverses within 6 weeks after termination of treatments. 
Finally, acute oxygen toxicity is also a known complication of HBO, occurring in one to four times per 10,000 
patient treatments and usually manifests as grand mal 
seizures.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أكثر adverse effect شيوعاً مع hyperbaric oxygen therapy هو middle ear barotrauma. السبب إن الـ ambient pressure جوّا الـ chamber لما بيزيد، لازم المريض يعمل equalization للضغط بالأذن الوسطى. إذا ما قدر، بيتبارا وبيحصل ضرر. عشان يكمّل العلاج بالـ HBO لازم ينحطوا tympanostomy tubes. وكمان كل ما زاد الوقت الكلي بالـ chamber، زادت المضاعفات. فهاد أكتر شي بيصير بصراحة.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو oxygen toxicity، لأنها أقل شيوعاً،大约 1 لـ 4 مرات لكل 10,000 علاج، وبتظهر كـ grand mal seizures. وnuclear cataract بتحتاج 150 لـ 200 ساعة، وprogressive myopia بتتحسن ضمن 6 أسابيع بعد التوقف.

question:
A 22-year-old woman who is 38 weeks pregnant is 
visiting her grandfather who is a current patient in 
the emergency room. While talking to her grandfather and eating her lunch, she suddenly begins to 
choke on a chicken nugget. She grabs her neck with 
both hands and staff quickly recognizes the universal 
sign for an airway obstruction. Initially, she is able to 
cough and speak, and the staff encourages her to continue her spontaneous efforts to clear the obstruction. 
However, she soon develops an ineffective cough, is 
no longer able to speak, becomes dyspneic and cyanotic, but she is still awake and alert. The physician is 
then called to bedside. What is the NEXT appropriate 
course of action?

options.text: Continue to encourage the patient’s spontaneous
Start performing the Heimlich maneuver, using
Start performing the Heimlich maneuver, using

correctAnswer: Start performing the Heimlich maneuver, using
englishExplanation:
12.  The answer is C. (Chapter 22) In the patient who is 
choking, if they are able to speak, cough, and exchange 
air, then he or she should be encouraged to continue their 
spontaneous efforts to clear the obstruction. However, 
once air exchange becomes inadequate, such as when the 
individual is cyanotic or unable to speak, then immediate intervention is required. In the awake patient, a blind 
finger sweep should never be attempted. While for the 
majority of patients, the Heimlich maneuver consists of 
subdiaphragmatic abdominal thrusts; for some patients, 
it is impossible for the rescuer to reach around to the 
patient’s abdomen. Pregnancy and morbid obesity are two 
common examples. In these circumstances, a chest thrust 
maneuver should be used instead. Because the patient in 
this scenario is 38 weeks pregnant, chest thrusts should be 
used instead of subdiaphragmatic abdominal thrusts.

![Tintinalli-2023-00032 source page 24](images/Tintinalli-2023-00032-Tintinalli-2023-p0024.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00032 source page 25](images/Tintinalli-2023-00032-Tintinalli-2023-p0025.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00032 source page 28](images/Tintinalli-2023-00032-Tintinalli-2023-p0028.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة كانت able to speak وكحبت، فبدينا نشجعها تكمل محاولاتها لحالها. بس لمّا الـ air exchange صار غير كافي، يعني صارت زرقانة، مش able to speak، وكحتها ضعيفة، هون لازم نتدخل فوراً. هي 38 أسبوع pregnant، يعني الـ subdiaphragmatic abdominal thrusts مش مناسبين لها. لما المنقذ ما يقدر يلف حوالي البطن، بيستخدموا chest thrusts بدالها. والحمل هو السبب الشائع، مع morbid obesity كمان.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو blind finger sweep، لأنه ما ينعمل أبداً بالمريض الواعي وبيخلي الجسم يدفع foreign object أكتر لمجرى الهواء. وكمان abdominal thrusts هي الغلط لأن الرحم بالحمل بيمرر الدفع للعلوي.

question:
Both during cardiac arrest and afterward with return 
of spontaneous circulation, hyperventilation is not 
recommended. The pathophysiology that occurs 
from hyperventilation (and thus why it is not recommended) is which of the following?

options.text: Hyperventilation causes decreased intrathoracic pressure and decreased venous return with

englishExplanation:
13.  The answer is C. (Chapter 24) Hyperventilation is not 
routinely recommended because it can increase intrathoracic pressure and decrease venous return with resulting 
decreased cardiac output. Additionally, the hypocarbia 
resulting from hyperventilation results in decreased blood 
flow to the brain, thus worsening anoxic brain injury. In 
the postarrest patient, physicians should target normocapnia (pCO2 35–45), which is usually achieved with 10 to 
12 ventilations per minute. In the patient who is in cardiac 
arrest and has an advanced airway, the provided breaths 
should be no more than 10 per minute. If the patient does 
not have an advance airway, the compression to breath 
ratio is 30:2.

![Tintinalli-2023-00033 source page 25](images/Tintinalli-2023-00033-Tintinalli-2023-p0025.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00033 source page 28](images/Tintinalli-2023-00033-Tintinalli-2023-p0028.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ hyperventilation موصى فيه وقت cardiac arrest ولا بعد رجوع الـ spontaneous circulation، والسبب إنه بيزود الـ intrathoracic pressure وبينقص الـ venous return. والنتيجة decreased cardiac output. وكمان الـ hypocarbia اللي بتيجي معاه بتقلل الدم اللي رايح للدماغ، وهاد بيزيد ضرر Anoxic brain. بعد الـ arrest لازم تستهدف normocapnia، يعني pCO2 بين 35 و45. وبيوصل 10 لـ 12 نفس في الدقيقة، أو 10 بالحد الأقصى إذا في advanced airway، ونسبة 30:2 إذا ما في.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو إن الـ hyperventilation بتخلي الـ intrathoracic pressure ينقص، لأن بالعكس بتزوده وبتنقص الـ venous return. والخيار التاني إنه الـ cardiac output بيزيد، وهو فعلياً بينقص.

question:
Which of the following represents the physiologic 
changes that occur during pregnancy?
englishExplanation:
14.  The answer is C. (Chapter 25) Pregnant patients have 
larger tidal volume ventilation, which results in increased 
minute ventilation. This is necessary due to increased 
carbon dioxide increase, especially by the third trimester 
and during labor, and also due to progesterone directly 

16
TINTINALLI’S EMERGENCY MEDICINE EXAMINATION AND BOARD REVIEW, 9TH EDITION
stimulating the central respiratory center. It is thus not 
uncommon to see in a healthy pregnant patient, an arterial blood gas with mild respiratory alkalosis. Both cardiac output and plasma volume increase by 30% to 50%. 
Peripheral vascular resistance decreases by 20%.

![Tintinalli-2023-00034 source page 25](images/Tintinalli-2023-00034-Tintinalli-2023-p0025.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00034 source page 28](images/Tintinalli-2023-00034-Tintinalli-2023-p0028.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00034 source page 29](images/Tintinalli-2023-00034-Tintinalli-2023-p0029.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الحوامل عندهم tidal volume ventilation أكبر، وهاد معناه إن الـ minute ventilation بيزيد. هاد لازم يصير لأن الـ carbon dioxide بيزيد، خاصة بالثلث التالت من الحمل وأثناء الـ labor. وكمان لأن الـ progesterone بيزيد stimulation للمركز التنفسي. عشان كده الـ arterial blood gas عند الحامل السليم ممكن يبيّن respiratory alkalosis خفيف. وكمان الـ cardiac output والـ plasma volume بيزيدوا 30% لـ 50%، والـ peripheral vascular resistance بينقص 20%.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو decreased cardiac output أو decreased plasma volume، لأن الاتنين بيزيدوا بالحمل مو ينقصوا. وكمان الـ peripheral vascular resistance بتنقص 20% مش بتزيد.

question:
Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding 
post arrest targeted temperature management (TTM)?

options.text: Aim for a core temperature of less than 32°C
Bradycardia is common when starting TTM.
Clinical neurologic reflexes post arrest are predictive of cardiac arrest outcome.
Pregnant women should be excluded from TTM.

correctAnswer: Bradycardia is common when starting TTM.
englishExplanation:
15.  The answer is B. (Chapter 26) Bradycardia is common 
with targeted temperature management (TTM) and can 
be pronounced with induction but is usually of little clinical consequence and requires no treatment. It is important 
to note that the clinical neurologic reflexes are not predictive of cardiac arrest outcomes. There is still considerable debate about the exact targeted core temperature for 
postarrest cooling. Recommendations range from 32 to 
36°C but not lower than 32°C. TTM for pregnant patient 
varies among institutions. Several case reports have demonstrated good outcomes for postarrest pregnant patients.

![Tintinalli-2023-00035 source page 25](images/Tintinalli-2023-00035-Tintinalli-2023-p0025.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00035 source page 29](images/Tintinalli-2023-00035-Tintinalli-2023-p0029.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ bradycardia شي شائع مع targeted temperature management، وبتكون واضحة خاصة وقت starting الـ cooling. بس عادةً ما إلها أي clinical consequence، وما بتحتاج treatment. الـ TTM بيعتمد على تبريد الـ core temperature، والتوصيات بتتراوح بين 32 و36 درجة بدون ما ننزل تحت 32. وكمان الـ neurologic reflexes بعد الـ arrest ما بتتنبأ بنتيجة القلب. هاد كله بيخلي جملة الـ bradycardia هي الصحيحة.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو استبعاد الحوامل من TTM، لأن في عدة case reports بتبيّن نتائج كويسة لمريضى الحمل بعد الـ arrest. وكمان ما في داعي ننزّل الـ core temperature تحت 32 درجة، والـ neurologic reflexes ما بتتنبأ بالنتيجة.

question:
A 7-year-old female patient of normal body mass 
index (BMI) presents to the emergency department 
after she was hit by a car while riding her bike. She has 
significant facial fractures and noted blood and swelling of her airway. Attempts at oral intubation fail and 
she additionally cannot be oxygenated or ventilated 
using bag valve mask ventilation. A 16-gauge catheter 
is inserted percutaneously through her cricothyroid 
membrane and jet ventilation is initiated. Which of 
the following represents the CORRECT psi of oxygen 
to deliver?

options.text: Until adequate chest rise and fall is noted, which
Until adequate chest rise and fall is noted, which
Until adequate chest rise and fall is noted, which
Until adequate chest rise and fall is noted, which

correctAnswer: Until adequate chest rise and fall is noted, which
englishExplanation:
18.  The answer is A. (Chapter 30) In children younger 
than 12 years, especially younger than 8 years, in whom 
the physician cannot oxygenate or ventilate and cannot 
achieve oral intubation and a surgical airway is needed, 
a cricothyrotomy is not recommended. Young children 
are more likely to have late complications, especially stenosis, as their larynx is more easily damaged with this 
procedure. A tracheotomy is preferred but this is out of

arabicExplanation:
ليش: البنت عمرها 7 سنين، صدمتها سيارة وهي راكبة عجلة، وعندها كسور بالوجه مع دم وتورّم بالـ airway. الـ intubation بالفم فشل، وكمان ما قدر يتنفس أو ينVentilate بالـ bag valve mask. فحطوا catheter مقاس 16-gauge عبر الـ cricothyroid membrane وبدأوا jet ventilation. هاد الاستخدام هو bridge مؤقت لحد ما يعملوا definite surgical airway. لما تستخدم jet ventilation عند طفل، بتبدأ بـ 0.5 psi/kg وبتزيد لحد ما تشوف adequate chest rise and fall. والـ psi عند الأطفال عادةً أقل من 30 mm Hg.

question: All of the following when present can signal a potential airway management difficulty EXCEPT:
englishExplanation:

a patient because of difficulty getting a seal on the mask. 
The same holds true for a small or large chins. There are 
multiple factors associated with airway management difficulties as noted in Table 2.1. Mallampati scores help to 
identify patients that may be challenging to intubate. The 
lower the score, the better view of the posterior pharynx 
(Figure 2.6).

![Tintinalli-2023-00039 source page 25](images/Tintinalli-2023-00039-Tintinalli-2023-p0025.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00039 source page 26](images/Tintinalli-2023-00039-Tintinalli-2023-p0026.jpg)

arabicExplanation:

question:
Which of the following drugs used to treat dementia is available in a 
transdermal preparation?
englishExplanation:
4. D.  Rivastigmine
Donepezil, galantamine, and rivastigmine are acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and can be used for the 
treatment of mild to moderate Alzheimer’s disease. Rivastigmine is available in a transdermal patch. 
Memantine is a glutamate receptor antagonist and can be used for moderate Alzheimer’s disease 
in patients who are unable to take acetylcholinersterase inhibitors, and for patients with severe disease. Rotigotine is a dopamine receptor agonist available as a patch and used for the treatment of 
Parkinson’s disease; it’s not a treatment for dementia.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Technology Appraisal 217. Donepezil, galantamine, 
rivastigmine, and memantine for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease. March 2011.

question:
A 76-year-old woman with Parkinson’s disease was admitted with 
confusion and shortness of breath. Her Parkinson’s disease was normally 
controlled with co-beneldopa 125 mg at 8.00 a.m., 11.00 a.m., 2.00 p.m., 
and 5.00 p.m., and 125 mg controlled release at 8.00 p.m. She lived with 
her husband and had twice-daily carers to help with personal care. She 
was usually mobile with a zimmer frame.
On examination, she was pyrexial with signs of right lower lobe 
pneumonia, which was confirmed on X-ray. Her bedside swallow 
assessment revealed an unsafe swallow.
How should you manage her Parkinson’s disease medication?

options.text: Continue Parkinson’s disease medication orally with close supervision
Convert her L-dopa dose to a rotigotine transdermal patch
Place a naso-gastric tube and continue the same Parkinson’s disease medication
Place a naso-gastric tube and convert the Parkinson’s disease medications to soluble forms
Stop all Parkinson’s disease medication until formal swallow assessment

englishExplanation:
24. D.  Place a naso-gastric tube and convert the medications to soluble forms
Patients with Parkinson’s disease admitted to hospital for other medical or surgical problems are 
often treated by staff unfamiliar with managing Parkinson’s disease.
Missing dopaminergic medications will result in an exacerbation of symptoms causing immobility, 
rigidity, or rarely neuroleptic malignant syndrome with mental status change, rigidity, raised creatinine kinase, fever, and dysautonomia.
Co-beneldopa (Madopar) comes in capsules and, therefore, cannot be crushed and given via a 
naso-gastric tube as it will significantly alter drug release and metabolism. However, dispersible 
forms exist which can be replaced like for like in terms of dose to achieve the same therapeutic 
effect; however, no controlled release dispersible preparation is available. If the patient had been 
taking co-careldopa (Sinemet), which comes in tablets, this can be crushed and given via a nasogastric tube; however, the night-time controlled-release preparation cannot be crushed and should 
be replaced by a crushed standard-release co-careldopa. If the patient was nil-by-mouth and a

nasogastric tube could not be tolerated then the dopamine agonist rotigotine can be used, as it is a 
transdermal patch. This can also be used as an alternative to other dopamine agonists if no oral or 
nasogastric route is available.

question:
A ventilated patient with severe traumatic brain injury has received propofol at 5
mg/kg/hour for 72 hours. He develops otherwise unexplained lactic acidosis,
rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalaemia, acute kidney injury and progressive bradyarrhythmia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Propofol infusion syndrome is a rare but potentially fatal complication associated
particularly with prolonged high-dose propofol exposure. Characteristic features include metabolic or lactic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalaemia, lipaemia, hepatomegaly, acute kidney injury, electrocardiographic abnormalities, bradyarrhythmia and cardiac failure. Recognised risk factors include severe neurological injury,
sepsis, impaired tissue oxygen delivery, catecholamines, corticosteroids and propofol doses usually exceeding 4 mg/kg/hour for more than 48 hours. Propofol must be
stopped immediately and an alternative sedative used while organ support is
instituted.
Clinical Pearl
Classic Setting:
Propofol infusion syndrome is most strongly associated with prolonged high-dose
infusions, commonly more than 4 mg/kg/hour for longer than 48 hours.
Core Features:
Unexplained metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalaemia, acute kidney injury and cardiovascular collapse should trigger suspicion.
ECG Warning:
Brugada-like or other new electrocardiographic changes and progressive bradyarrhythmia can precede cardiovascular failure.
Risk Amplifiers:
Severe neurological injury, sepsis, reduced oxygen delivery, catecholamines, inotropes and corticosteroids increase risk.
Immediate Action:
Stop propofol promptly rather than merely reducing the infusion rate.
Supportive Care:
Correct electrolyte and acid-base abnormalities and provide renal, circulatory and
respiratory support; extracorporeal support may be required in refractory collapse.
No Specific Antidote:
Management is withdrawal and intensive organ support because no proven antidote
exists.
Prevention:

Use the lowest effective dose, reassess ongoing need frequently and investigate otherwise unexplained acidosis or rising creatine kinase early.

question: Regarding the management of a severe amitriptyline overdose, all of the following statements are true EXCEPT:

options.text: The primary goals are supportive care, including airway protection and management of hypotension.
IV sodium bicarbonate is indicated for a QRS duration > 100 ms or ventricular arrhythmias.
Seizures should be treated with benzodiazepines.
Hemodialysis is an effective method for enhancing drug elimination.
Physostigmine is generally contraindicated due to the risk of precipitating

correctAnswer: Hemodialysis is an effective method for enhancing drug elimination.
englishExplanation:
Rationale for Correct Answer:
Hemodialysis is ineffective for TCA clearance due to the drug's large volume of distribution (often >10 L/kg) and high protein binding (>90%). The fraction of drug in
the plasma available for removal is negligible compared to the tissue load.
Sodium Bicarbonate Therapy:
Sodium bicarbonate is the mainstay of treatment for TCA-induced cardiotoxicity. It
works via two mechanisms: increasing serum sodium concentration to overcome
sodium channel blockade, and inducing alkalinisation (target pH 7.45-7.55) which
decreases drug binding to the sodium channels. Indications include QRS prolongation >100 ms, ventricular arrhythmias, and refractory hypotension.
Contraindications:
Physostigmine is contraindicated in TCA overdose as it can precipitate seizures and
asystole. Class Ia (e.g., quinidine), Ic (e.g., flecainide), and III (e.g., amiodarone) antiarrhythmics are also contraindicated as they may exacerbate conduction delays
and QT prolongation.
Mechanism of Toxicity:
Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) exert toxicity via blockade of rapid cardiac sodium
channels (leading to QRS prolongation and myocardial depression), antagonism of
alpha-1 adrenergic receptors (causing vasodilation and hypotension), and inhibition
of muscarinic receptors (resulting in anticholinergic signs such as tachycardia and
delirium). Additionally, GABA-A receptor antagonism contributes to the high
seizure risk.
Clinical Pearl
TCAs are Not Dialyzable:
This is due to their large volume of distribution and high protein binding.
Sodium Bicarbonate Indications:
For QRS >100 ms, administer IV sodium bicarbonate (e.g., 50-100 mmol or 1-2
mmol/kg) to narrow the QRS complex. Maintain a target serum pH of 7.45-7.55.
Hypotension Management:
The initial treatment for hypotension is IV fluids, followed by direct-acting vasopressors like norepinephrine if needed.
Avoid Physostigmine:
The risks of using this agent in TCA overdose (worsening cardiac conduction block,
causing seizures) far outweigh any potential benefits.
Prolonged Observation:

Patients should be observed for at least 6 hours post-ingestion. If asymptomatic
with a normal ECG at 6 hours, they may be medically cleared. Symptomatic patients
require ICU admission.
Intralipid Rescue:
Intravenous Lipid Emulsion (ILE) therapy (20% Intralipid) is indicated for refractory hypotension or cardiac arrest unresponsive to standard resuscitation and
sodium bicarbonate.
ECG Hallmark in aVR:
A terminal R wave >3 mm in lead aVR (R/S ratio > 0.7) is a highly sensitive and
specific marker for significant TCA toxicity and predicts the risk of seizures and
arrhythmias.
Mechanism of Bicarbonate Efficacy:
Sodium bicarbonate works via two synergistic mechanisms: the sodium load overcomes competitive blockade at the Na+ channel, while serum alkalinisation reduces
the fraction of ionised drug available to bind the channel.
Hyperventilation Strategy:
In intubated patients with severe toxicity where bicarbonate is not immediately effective or available, mechanical hyperventilation to induce respiratory alkalosis (target pH 7.50-7.55) can serve as a temporising measure to reduce cardiotoxicity.
Phenytoin Contraindication:
Phenytoin is a Class 1b antiarrhythmic with sodium channel blocking properties. It
is contraindicated in TCA-induced seizures as it may exacerbate cardiac conduction
delays.
Anticholinergic Toxidrome:
Recognise the classic anticholinergic features accompanying TCA overdose: hyperthermia, dry skin/mucous membranes, mydriasis (dilated pupils), urinary retention, and delirium.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاي الجواب لأنها هي الجملة الوحيدة الغلط بين الخيارات. الـ hemodialysis مش فعّال لتنقية الـ TCA، لأن الـ drug عنده volume of distribution كبير غالباً فوق 10 L/kg، وprotein binding فوق 90%، يعني نسبة الدواء بالـ plasma واللي ممكن تتشال ضئيلة جداً مقارنة بالـ tissue load. والباقي كلها صح: الـ sodium bicarbonate هو mainstay بالـ TCA-induced cardiotoxicity وبيزود الـ serum sodium ويعمل alkalinisation بهدف pH 7.45-7.55، والـ benzodiazepines للـ seizures، وphysostigmine contraindicated.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو IV sodium bicarbonate أو benzodiazepines، لأن هدول صح. الفخ الحقيقي هو إنك تفكّر إن dialysis بيشيل الـ TCA، وهو مش فعّال لأن معظم الدواء متشبّع بالـ tissues. وكمان physostigmine خطير لأنه بيسبّب seizures وasystole.

question:
At the end of a long surgery, a patient has received a deep neuromuscular blockade with rocuronium. The anaesthetist administers a large dose of sugammadex

for reversal. What is the mechanism of action of this drug?

options.text: It is an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that increases acetylcholine in the synapse.
It is a selective relaxant-binding agent that encapsulates the rocuronium
It is a central nervous system stimulant that overrides the blockade.
It directly stimulates the post-synaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptor.
It is a calcium-channel agonist that facilitates acetylcholine release.

correctAnswer: It is a selective relaxant-binding agent that encapsulates the rocuronium
englishExplanation:
Mechanism of Action:
Sugammadex is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin (composed of 8 glucose
monomers) designed with a lipophilic inner cavity and a hydrophilic outer surface.
This structure allows it to function as a Selective Relaxant Binding Agent (SRBA) by
encapsulating the lipophilic steroid nucleus of aminosteroid neuromuscular blocking agents. It forms a very tight 1:1 complex with high affinity (rocuronium > vecuronium >> pancuronium). By sequestering free drug in the plasma, it creates a
steep concentration gradient that promotes the rapid dissociation of the neuromuscular blocker from nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction.
The water-soluble complex is then excreted unchanged by the kidneys.
Clinical Application:
Unlike neostigmine, which has a ceiling effect and cannot reverse deep blockade,
sugammadex can reverse any depth of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium or vecuronium, provided the appropriate dose is administered. It avoids the
muscarinic side effects associated with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (e.g., bradycardia, bronchospasm, hypersalivation), although monitoring for hypersensitivity
and bradycardia is still required.
Clinical Pearl
Encapsulation Reversal:
Sugammadex is a selective relaxant-binding agent (SRBA), not a cholinesterase
inhibitor.
Aminosteroid Specific:
It only works for rocuronium and vecuronium. It has no effect on benzylisoquinolinium drugs (like cisatracurium) or succinylcholine.
Reverses Deep Block:
The major advantage of sugammadex is its ability to rapidly and reliably reverse a
profound neuromuscular block, which neostigmine cannot do.
Dosing is Key:
Dosing is determined by the depth of block: 2 mg/kg for moderate block (appearance of T2 on TOF), 4 mg/kg for deep block (1-2 post-tetanic counts), and 16 mg/kg
for immediate reversal of rocuronium (e.g., 3 minutes after 1.2 mg/kg induction
dose).
Contraceptive Interaction:

Sugammadex encapsulates steroid hormones, reducing the efficacy of hormonal
contraceptives. The interaction is equivalent to one missed daily pill; patients
should be advised to follow the 'missed pill' advice in the package leaflet for oral
contraceptives or use non-hormonal backup for 7 days.
Renal Considerations:
The sugammadex-rocuronium complex is excreted renally. It is not recommended
for use in patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) as the complex is retained, though high-flux dialysis can remove it.
Re-paralysis Wait Times:
If neuromuscular blockade is required shortly after sugammadex reversal, benzylisoquinoliniums (e.g., cisatracurium) are preferred. Re-administration of rocuronium requires a waiting period (e.g., 24 hours for normal doses) or massive dose escalation depending on the time elapsed and renal function.
Bradycardia Risk:
While avoiding neostigmine-induced muscarinic effects, sugammadex itself is associated with marked bradycardia and, rarely, cardiac arrest. Cardiovascular monitoring should continue after administration.
Coagulation Assay Interference:
Sugammadex can cause transient prolongation of prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) for up to 60 minutes due to interference
with assay phospholipids. This is a laboratory artifact and does not correlate with
increased clinical bleeding risk.
Hypersensitivity Reactions:
Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, can occur even without prior exposure. Incidence is higher than initially reported; symptoms may include flushing,
urticaria, erythematous rash, hypotension, and bronchospasm.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ sugammadex هو gamma-cyclodextrin معدّل، مكوّن من 8 glucose monomers، إلو cavity داخلي lipophilic وسطح خارجي hydrophilic. هاد البناء بيمكّنه يشتغل كـ Selective Relaxant Binding Agent، يعني بيعبّي جزيئة الـ rocuronium steroid nucleus داخل الكAVI. بيعمل complex بنسبة 1:1 وبقوة ارتباط عالية، وبيسحب الـ drug الحر بالـ plasma فبتعمل concentration gradient قوية. النتيجة إن الـ rocuronium بينفصل بسرعة عن الـ nicotinic acetylcholine receptors بالـ neuromuscular junction، وبعدها الـ complex المائي بينطرح بالـ kidneys.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو acetylcholinesterase inhibitor زي neostigmine، لأنها بتزود الـ acetylcholine بالـ synapse. وneostigmine إلها ceiling effect وما بتقدر تقلب deep blockade، بينما sugammadex بتقدر. وكمان sugammadex بتشتغل بس مع rocuronium وvecuronium.

question:
Regarding the metabolism and pharmacokinetics of Fentanyl, which statement is
false?

options.text: Fentanyl is more lipophilic than Morphine, allowing for a more rapid onset of
Fentanyl's short duration of action is due to its rapid redistribution to inactive
Fentanyl has a context-sensitive half-time that increases with prolonged
Fentanyl is primarily excreted unchanged in the urine.
Fentanyl's metabolism can be affected by drugs that interact with the CYP3A4

correctAnswer: Fentanyl is primarily excreted unchanged in the urine.
englishExplanation:
Analysis of Option D (False Statement):
This statement is false. Fentanyl is extensively metabolised by the liver via Ndealkylation (primarily CYP3A4) to norfentanyl and other inactive metabolites.
Less than 10% (typically 6-7%) of the drug is excreted unchanged in the urine. This
contrasts with morphine, where renal excretion of active metabolites plays a larger
role.
Pharmacokinetics:
•Lipophilicity (A): Fentanyl has an octanol:water partition coefficient of ~813 (vs
1.4 for morphine). This high lipophilicity allows rapid blood-brain barrier

penetration and fast onset. •Redistribution (B): Termination of effect after a
bolus is due to rapid redistribution from the central compartment to peripheral
lipid-rich tissues, not metabolism. •Context-Sensitive Half-Time (C): Fentanyl
accumulates in lipid stores during infusion. As duration increases, the contextsensitive half-time (CSHT) rises significantly. After ~2-3 hours of infusion, its CSHT
exceeds that of sufentanil. •Metabolism Interactions (E): As a CYP3A4
substrate, fentanyl clearance is reduced by inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin,
ketoconazole, ritonavir) and increased by inducers (e.g., rifampicin,
carbamazepine).
Clinical Pearl
Redistribution Ends the Effect (Initially):
For a single bolus of a lipophilic drug like fentanyl or propofol, the termination of
effect is due to redistribution, not metabolism.
Metabolism for Clearance:
Fentanyl is metabolised to norfentanyl, which is pharmacologically inactive. This
makes fentanyl a safer choice than morphine in renal failure, as it lacks active metabolites that can accumulate (unlike morphine-6-glucuronide).
Context-Sensitive Half-Time:
This describes the time for plasma concentration to fall by 50% after stopping an infusion. Fentanyl's CSHT increases markedly with infusion duration due to saturation of peripheral lipid compartments, unlike remifentanil.
Remifentanil Comparison:
Unlike fentanyl, remifentanil is metabolised by non-specific plasma and tissue esterases, giving it an extremely short and predictable context-sensitive half-time (~34 minutes) regardless of infusion duration.
CYP3A4 Interactions:
Fentanyl's metabolism can be affected by CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole)
which increase its levels, or inducers which decrease them.
Neuraxial Spread & Lipophilicity:
Due to high lipophilicity, intrathecal fentanyl has limited rostral spread (segmental
analgesia) and a risk of early respiratory depression. Conversely, hydrophilic morphine spreads rostrally in CSF, carrying a risk of delayed respiratory depression.
First-Pass Metabolism:
Fentanyl undergoes significant hepatic first-pass metabolism, resulting in low oral
bioavailability (~30%). This necessitates alternative routes of administration (IV,
transdermal, transmucosal/sublingual) for clinical efficacy.
Effect-Site Equilibration (t1/2ke0):

Fentanyl has a t1/2ke0 of approximately 5-6 minutes. Peak clinical effect occurs
several minutes after a bolus, necessitating administration prior to noxious stimuli
(e.g., laryngoscopy) to blunt the response effectively.
Chest Wall Rigidity:
Rapid high-dose administration can cause "wooden chest syndrome", making ventilation difficult. This is mediated via basal ganglia dopaminergic and GABAergic
pathways, not direct muscle action.
Transdermal Depot:
Fentanyl patches create a subcutaneous depot. After patch removal, serum levels
decline slowly (terminal half-life 17-24 hours) due to continued absorption from this
depot.
Serotonin Syndrome Risk:
Fentanyl has weak serotonin reuptake inhibitor properties and can contribute to
serotonin syndrome when combined with MAOIs or SSRIs, unlike morphine.
Fentanyl-Induced Cough:
A paradoxical cough may occur after IV bolus (incidence up to 65%), potentially due
to pulmonary C-fibre stimulation or citrate additives in the formulation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاي الجواب لأنها هي الجملة الغلط. الـ fentanyl بيتmetabolized بالكبد عن طريق N-dealkylation، وأهم إنزيم هو CYP3A4، فبيطلع mainly نorfentanyl وmetabolites غير فعّالة. أقل من 10% من الدواء، يعني حوالي 6-7%، بينطرح بالـ urine بدون تغيير. هاد بيخالف morphine، اللي الطرح renal للـ active metabolites فيه أكبر. والباقي كلها صح، مثل كون الـ fentanyl أ lipophilic من morphine بـ partition coefficient حوالي 813 مقابل 1.4.
الفخ: لو اخترت A أو C فأنت فاكر إنهم غلط، بس هم صح. A صح لأن الـ fentanyl أ lipophilic من morphine وبيوصل للدماغ بسرعة. C صح لأن الـ CSHT بيزيد كل ما طال وقت الـ infusion.

question: A 70-year-old man with an eGFR of 25 mL/min/1.73m2 receives regular morphine for cancer pain and develops increasing sedation and respiratory depression. Accumulation of which metabolite best explains this?

options.text: Morphine-6-glucuronide, an active opioid agonist renally cleared
Morphine-6-glucuronide, which is inactive but neurotoxic
Morphine-3-glucuronide, which is a potent mu-opioid agonist

correctAnswer: Morphine-6-glucuronide, an active opioid agonist renally cleared
englishExplanation:
Morphine undergoes hepatic glucuronidation to morphine-3-glucuronide (M3G,
~60%, not a mu-agonist but neuro-excitatory) and morphine-6-glucuronide (M6G,
~10%, a potent mu-opioid agonist). Both are renally excreted and accumulate in renal impairment. M6G accumulation is the best explanation for prolonged sedation
and respiratory depression in this patient, whereas M3G is more associated with
myoclonus, hyperalgesia and allodynia.
Clinical Pearl
M6G - the Active One:
Morphine-6-glucuronide is a potent mu-opioid agonist and can drive prolonged sedation and respiratory depression when it accumulates.
M3G - Neuro-excitatory:
Morphine-3-glucuronide has no clinically useful mu-opioid agonism and is associated with myoclonus, allodynia and opioid-induced hyperalgesia.
Renal Clearance:
Both glucuronides are renally eliminated; accumulation in acute kidney injury or
chronic kidney disease can produce delayed and prolonged toxicity.
Preferred Alternatives:
Fentanyl and alfentanil have no clinically important active renally cleared metabolites and are often preferred when renal function is severely impaired.
Oxycodone Caution:

Oxycodone clearance is reduced in renal impairment and both parent drug and metabolites may accumulate, so dose reduction and close monitoring are required.
Delayed Presentation:
Toxicity can worsen after repeated dosing as active metabolites accumulate.
Naloxone Duration:
Recurrent respiratory depression may occur after a naloxone bolus because naloxone is shorter acting than accumulated M6G; repeated doses or an infusion may be
necessary.
Metabolic Fractions:
M3G is the predominant glucuronide, while a smaller fraction is converted to pharmacologically active M6G.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده eGFR 25 ومأخ morphine بانتظام، ومع ذلك sedation وrespiratory depression بيزيدوا. السبب هو تراكم الـ morphine-6-glucuronide، وهو active opioid agonist قوي على الـ mu receptor. الـ morphine بيتعمله glucuronidation بالكبد فيطلع M3G حوالي 60% وM6G حوالي 10%. الاتنين بينطرحوا بالـ urine، فلما الـ renal function تختل تراكموا. وM6G تحديداً هو اللي بيسبّب sedation طويل وrespiratory depression، على خلاف M3G اللي بيطلع معاه myoclonus وhyperalgesia وallodynia.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو morphine-3-glucuronide، لأن هو مش mu-agonist فعّال، وهو neuro-excitatory. وكمان codeine ونormorphine مش الأيضinitions المستعملة. وبما إن الاتنين بينطرحوا بالـ urine، فالـ renal impairment بيخليهم يتراكموا. تذكّر: M6G هي الفعّالة وM3G هي neuro-excitatory.

question:
Which class of antifungal agents exerts its effect by binding directly to ergosterol
in the fungal cell membrane, creating pores and causing cell death?
englishExplanation:
Polyenes (Amphotericin B, Nystatin):
Polyenes bind with high affinity to ergosterol, the principal sterol in fungal cell
membranes. This binding disrupts membrane integrity by forming transmembrane
pores, leading to leakage of intracellular ions (specifically potassium) and subsequent cell death. Their selectivity arises because they bind more avidly to ergosterol
than to cholesterol (the mammalian sterol), though some cross-binding to cholesterol occurs, causing toxicity.
Azoles (Fluconazole, Voriconazole):
These inhibit the fungal cytochrome P450 enzyme 14-alpha-demethylase. This prevents the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol, leading to the accumulation of toxic
methylsterols and impaired membrane structure.
Echinocandins (Anidulafungin, Micafungin, Caspofungin):

These inhibit the synthesis of beta-(1,3)-D-glucan, an essential component of the
fungal cell wall. This leads to osmotic instability and cell lysis. They are fungicidal
against Candida species.
Flucytosine:
This is an antimetabolite converted inside the fungal cell to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU),
which interferes with DNA and RNA synthesis.
Allylamines (Terbinafine):
These inhibit squalene epoxidase, an early step in ergosterol biosynthesis, leading to
squalene accumulation and ergosterol depletion.
Clinical Pearl
Polyene Mechanism of Action:
Amphotericin B forms pores in the fungal cell membrane by binding directly to ergosterol, causing leakage of intracellular cations.
Amphotericin B Formulations:
Amphotericin B binds weakly to mammalian cholesterol, contributing to toxicity.
Liposomal formulations encapsulate the drug, reducing delivery to the renal tubule
and significantly lowering nephrotoxicity rates compared to conventional amphotericin deoxycholate.
Azole Drug Interactions:
Azoles inhibit 14-alpha-demethylase to stop ergosterol synthesis. Crucially, they are
potent inhibitors of human CYP450 enzymes, necessitating careful review of drug
interactions (e.g., with tacrolimus, warfarin, or statins) in the ICU.
Echinocandin Clinical Role:
Echinocandins inhibit beta-(1,3)-D-glucan synthase (cell wall). They are currently
the first-line empirical treatment for invasive candidiasis in critically ill patients (especially those who are haemodynamically unstable or have recent azole exposure)
per UK and international guidelines.
Flucytosine Resistance:
Flucytosine must never be used as monotherapy due to the rapid development of resistance. It is classically combined with Amphotericin B for the treatment of
Cryptococcal meningitis.
Candida Species Resistance:
Candida krusei possesses intrinsic resistance to fluconazole. Candida glabrata exhibits dose-dependent susceptibility or resistance. Identification of species is critical
for de-escalation from echinocandins.
Azole Therapeutic Drug Monitoring:

Voriconazole and Posaconazole require TDM due to non-linear pharmacokinetics
(Voriconazole) and variable absorption. Sub-therapeutic levels lead to failure;
supra-therapeutic levels cause neurotoxicity and hepatotoxicity.
Amphotericin B Nephrotoxicity Mechanism:
Nephrotoxicity arises from afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction and direct tubular
epithelial toxicity. Sodium loading (e.g., 500-1000ml 0.9% saline) prior to administration can attenuate the vasoconstrictive component.
Amphotericin-Induced Electrolyte Disturbances:
Amphotericin B causes a distal renal tubular acidosis (Type 1 RTA) and increases
membrane permeability in the distal tubule, leading to profound hypokalaemia and
hypomagnesaemia which require aggressive replacement.
Voriconazole Adverse Effects:
Unique side effects include transient visual disturbances (altered colour perception,
photophobia), phototoxicity (skin rash), and periostitis due to fluoride accumulation with long-term use.
QT Interval Effects:
Most azoles (fluconazole, voriconazole, posaconazole) prolong the QT interval.
Isavuconazole is a notable exception, which causes QT shortening.
Echinocandin Spectrum Limitations:
Echinocandins have poor penetration into the CNS and urinary tract due to high
protein binding and large molecular weight. They are inactive against Cryptococcus
neoformans and most dimorphic fungi.
Beta-D-Glucan Diagnostic:
1,3-beta-D-glucan is a cell wall component released by many fungi (Candida,
Aspergillus, Pneumocystis) but not Mucorales or Cryptococcus. It serves as a useful
serum biomarker for invasive fungal disease but can have false positives from IVIG,
albumin, or certain antibiotics.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ polyenes، وهما amphotericin B وnystatin، بترتبط بـ affinity عالية مع الـ ergosterol، وهو الـ sterol الأساسي بـ membranes الفطر. هاد الربط بيعمل transmembrane pores وبيخرب سلامة الـ membrane، فبتسرّب ions من داخل الخلية، خاصة الـ potassium، وبيتموت الفطر. الـ selectivity بتيجي لأنهم بيرتبطوا أكتر من الـ cholesterol اللي بستhuman cells، بس في cross-binding للـ cholesterol وهاد مصدر الـ toxicity.
الفخ: الخيار الغلط هو azoles، لأنهم ما بيربطوا بالـ ergosterol مباشرة، هم بيثبّطوا fungal cytochrome P450 named 14-alpha-demethylase فبتتراكم methylsterols. وechinocandins بتمنع تصنيع beta-(1,3)-D-glucan بالـ cell wall.

question:
A patient with a metastatic neuroendocrine (carcinoid) tumor of the midgut
presents with flushing, diarrhea, and signs of right-sided heart failure.
Echocardiography is performed to assess for carcinoid heart disease. Which valve
is most characteristically and severely affected by this condition?
englishExplanation:
Pathophysiology:
Carcinoid heart disease (CHD) results from the secretion of vasoactive substances
(primarily serotonin, also bradykinin and tachykinins) by neuroendocrine tumours.
When liver metastases are present, these substances bypass hepatic first-pass metabolism and reach the right heart. Serotonin acts specifically on 5-HT2B receptors
on the valvular subendocardium, triggering TGF-beta signalling which stimulates fibroblast proliferation and plaque deposition.
Valve Involvement Pattern:
The tricuspid valve is the most frequently and severely affected structure. Fibrous
plaques deposit on the ventricular aspect of the leaflets, causing retraction and fixation in a semi-open position. This results in severe, torrential tricuspid regurgitation
(TR). The pulmonary valve is involved in ~50% of cases, typically causing stenosis
(PS) combined with regurgitation. Left-sided valves are spared because pulmonary
vascular endothelium inactivates serotonin (via monoamine oxidase) before blood
returns to the left atrium.
Diagnosis and Management:
Echocardiography is the gold standard for diagnosis. NT-proBNP is a sensitive
screening biomarker (UKINETS guidelines). Management involves somatostatin
analogues (e.g., octreotide, lanreotide) to control hormonal secretion and surgical
valve replacement for severe heart failure. Bioprosthetic valves are generally preferred over mechanical valves due to the high bleeding risk associated with hepatic
dysfunction and potential need for future procedures.
Clinical Pearl
Right Heart Rules:
Carcinoid heart disease is a disease of the right heart. Think Tricuspid Regurgitation
and Pulmonary Stenosis (TRPS).
Liver Metastases are Key:
Significant carcinoid syndrome and heart disease usually only occur once the tumour has metastasised to the liver, allowing the secreted hormones to bypass firstpass metabolism and enter the systemic circulation.
Fixed and Frozen Valves:

Echocardiography typically reveals 'frozen' valves with thickened, retracted leaflets
that fail to coapt. Plaques characteristically deposit on the ventricular aspect of the
tricuspid valve and the arterial aspect of the pulmonary valve.
Treatment:
Medical therapy (somatostatin analogues) controls symptoms but does not reverse
cardiac damage. Valve replacement is the only definitive treatment for carcinoid
heart failure and should be considered before irreversible right ventricular dysfunction occurs.
Carcinoid Crisis:
Anaesthesia or surgery can provoke a massive release of vasoactive substances,
leading to a life-threatening 'carcinoid crisis' characterised by profound haemodynamic instability.
Left-Sided Exceptions:
Left-sided valve involvement is rare (<10%) and suggests either a right-to-left intracardiac shunt (e.g., Patent Foramen Ovale) allowing bypass of the lungs, or a primary bronchial carcinoid tumour releasing substances directly into the pulmonary
veins.
Screening Biomarker:
N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is the recommended screening tool for carcinoid heart disease in patients with midgut NETs. Levels >260
pg/mL should trigger echocardiographic assessment (UKINETS guidelines).
Mechanism of Fibrosis:
The pathognomonic valvular fibrosis is mediated by serotonin stimulation of 5HT2B receptors on cardiac valvular subendocardial cells, which upregulates TGFbeta signalling and promotes fibroblast proliferation.
Pellagra Risk:
In carcinoid syndrome, up to 60% of dietary tryptophan is diverted to serotonin
synthesis (normally <1%), leading to niacin deficiency. This can present as pellagra
(dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia).
Perioperative Octreotide:
Patients require high-dose octreotide infusion (e.g., 50-100 mcg/hr) prior to and
during surgery to prevent carcinoid crisis; bolus dosing alone is often insufficient to
suppress hormone release during tumour manipulation.
Imaging Modalities:
While echocardiography assesses cardiac involvement, Gallium-68 DOTATATE
PET/CT is the gold standard for localising the primary tumour and metastases, having largely replaced the older Octreoscan.
