question:
Musculoskeletal
A 6-year-old boy presents after being bitten by a neighbor's dog 1 hour ago. He
suffered deep puncture bites on the hand, foot, upper arm, and face. His vital
signs include BP 120/70, P 110, R 20, and T 37.1°C (98.8°F). He has no known
medical history. He is allergic to penicillin but has tolerated cephalexin before.
What are the best intravenous antibiotics to administer?
englishExplanation: A third-generation cephalosporin and anaerobic agent (in this case, metronidazole) are the preferred antibiotic regimen in the clinical set- ting of a dog bite. Approximately 90% of all bites are dog bites, and the majority of bites occur in boys 5 to 9 years old. The most common oral bacterium is Pasteurella (50% of all dog bites), although additional bacteria including Capnocytophagia, Bartonella, and multiple anaerobes are also commonly isolated. 9/20/26, 1:18 AM PEER for Physicians - Case Series 2026-1 — Answered  Page 792 of 974
arabicExplanation:
ليش: عضّة dog بتنحل بـ third-generation cephalosporin مع agent يغطي anaerobes، وهاد هو Ceftriaxone مع metronidazole. حوالي 90% من اللدغات من الكلاب، وأكثر بكتيريا شيوعاً Pasteurella بنسبة 50% من لدغات الكلاب، مع وجود Capnocytophaga و Bartonella و anaerobes متعددة. المريضة حساسة من penicillin بس تحمّلت cephalexin قبل، فالـ cephalosporin بخير، ولأن الجرح deep punctures في أربع مناطق فالـ IV antibiotic هي الأنسب.
الفخ: الخيار B فيه cefepime مع azithromycin وما في فيه metronidazole اللي بيغطي anaerobes، والخيار A فيه ampicillin-sulbactam والمريضة حساسة من penicillin. الـ metronidazole جزء أساسي من الإجابة.

question:
A 35-year-old man presents to the ED with right hand swelling, pain,
and erythema that began 3 days ago. He denies any trauma, sick contacts,
insect bites, or recent travel. The patient’s vitals are significant for an oral
temperature of 101°F. Upon physical examination, you note an area of
erythema surrounding multiple small lacerations over the right third and
fourth metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints with localized tenderness. The
patient is neurovascularly intact with limited flexion caused by the swelling

and pain. Given this presentation, what is the most appropriate disposition
for this patient?

options.text: Suture and close follow-up with a hand surgeon
Suture and prescription for oral antibiotics
Wound irrigation and prescription for oral antibiotics

englishExplanation:
286.  The answer is e. This patient most likely sustained a closed-fist
injury, which has high infection rates and evidence of poor wound healing.
Wounds sustained by punches to the jaw and human bites, also known as
“fight bites,” are classically over the metacarpal joints. Penetration deep
into the joint space and infection are common given the positioning of the
hand during the injury, human oral flora, and delay in seeking treatment.
Infected wounds are polymicrobial and specifically include Eikenella
corrodens, a facultative anaerobic gram-negative rod harbored in human
dental plaque. It acts synergistically with aerobic organisms to increase the
morbidity of these injuries. The joint spaces must be examined under full
range of motion to detect any tendon lacerations or presence of foreign
bodies. Hand radiographs should also be obtained to examine for any bony
involvement. IV antibiotics and admission are the appropriate disposition.
The antibiotics of choice are directed at Staph sp, Strep sp, and gramnegative organisms (typically ampicillin/sulbactam IV or

amoxicillin/clavulanic acid (PO)) with broader coverage in the
immunocompromised patient. The wounds should be left open with a sterile
dressing, splinted in the position of function (hand-holding-glass position)
and elevated. Human bites have resulted in the transmission of hepatitis B,
hepatitis C, syphilis, and herpes. Although human immunodeficiency virus
(HIV) is present in human saliva, it is in relatively small amounts and
considered a low risk for transmission. Appropriate antivirals and testing
should be considered in these patients.
You should never suture these lacerations (a and b). Wound irrigation
and tetanus prophylaxis (c and d) are warranted in conjunction with IV
antibiotics.

![PreTest-5e-00286 source page 344](images/PreTest-5e-00286-PreTest-5e-p0344.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00286 source page 345](images/PreTest-5e-00286-PreTest-5e-p0345.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00286 source page 370](images/PreTest-5e-00286-PreTest-5e-p0370.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00286 source page 371](images/PreTest-5e-00286-PreTest-5e-p0371.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد classic fight bite، يعني جرح على الـ MCP joints ناتج عن لكم، ومعو infection واضحة: احمرار وتورم من 3 أيام مع حرارة 101 درجة. جروح اللكم نسبة الـ infection فيها عالية لأنه بيتنفاذ عميق وممكن يوصل الـ joint space، وبسبب flora الفم وبسبب تأخر طلب العلاج. البكتيريا المميزة هي Eikenella corrodens، والعالج IV antibiotics مع admission، والجرح يضل مفتوح مع splint على position of function.
الفخ: الخيارين A و B بيقترحوا الخياطة، بس في fight bite الجرح ما ينخيط. و antibiotic فموي لحاله مع الـ C مش كافي مع علامات infection وحرارة.

question:
A 31-year-old homebuilder is cutting a piece of wood when the table
saw backfires and amputates his left thumb at the base. You stabilize the
patient and call the plastic surgeon. What is the best method of preserving
the amputated digit?

options.text: Cleanse it with 10% povidone-iodine solution to remove gross
Cleanse it with normal saline to remove gross contamination, wrap it in
Cleanse it with normal saline to remove gross contamination, wrap it in
Place it in a container of 10% povidone-iodine solution and store this
Attempt reimplantation of the amputated part with 3-0 nylon sutures

correctAnswer: Cleanse it with normal saline to remove gross contamination, wrap it in
englishExplanation:
290.  The answer is c. The best way to preserve an amputated part is to
rinse it with normal saline to remove gross contamination, wrap it in sterile
gauze moistened with saline or lactated ringers, and place it in a sterile,
watertight container. Then store this container in ice water.
Povidone-iodine (a and d) is a strong antiseptic solution that is used
commonly in the hospital setting, particularly in the operating room to
create a sterile field. However, it is thought to be injurious to fibroblasts and
may limit wound healing. The amputated part should not be placed directly
on ice or in ice water (b) because this may also damage the tissue.
Reimplantation (e) of the thumb should be performed by a plastic surgeon
in the operating room. The risk of tissue death increases the longer the
severed part is not properly stored.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أحسن طريقة لحفظ الجزء المبتور إنه يتغسل بـ normal saline للتخلص من التلوث، ينلف بـ sterile gauze مرطبة بـ saline أو lactated ringers، يوضع في حاوية sterile watertight، والحاوية تنحط فوق ice water. المهم إنو القطعة نفسها ما تنحط مباشرة على الثلج ولا بماء الثلج، لأنو هاد بيضر الأنسجة وبيزيد موت النسيج، وكل ما الوقت يطول خسارة النسيج بتكون أكبر.
الفخ: povidone-iodine في الخيارين A و D مضاد بكتيريا قوي بيضر الـ fibroblasts وبيبطئ التئام الجرح. والخيار E reimplantation شغل plastic surgeon في غرفة العمليات مش في الـ ED.

question:
Shared scenario:
A 24-year-old woman presents to the ED after accidentally slamming her
finger in the car door 2 hours prior to arrival. There is no obvious deformity
and she appears to have full range of motion of her ungual fingers. You
notice blood collecting under her fingernail. The nail edges are intact.

300.   What is the appropriate management of her subungual hematoma?

options.text: Remove the nail from the nail bed
Scalpel insertion under the nail edge

englishExplanation:
300.  The answer is e. An uncomplicated, painful subungual hematoma
that does not involve disruption of nail edge should be drained via
trephination. Trephination is performed using electrocautery or by twisting
an 18 G needle through the nail. Once the trephination is performed, the
blood that had collected under the nail will drain, alleviating pain and
pressure. Multiple trephinations are sometimes needed.

Some experts suggest that painless hematomas may be left alone and do
not require drainage Trephination and drainage is normally performed to
alleviate pain and discomfort for the patient. If the nail edges are disrupted
or the hematoma involves greater than 50% of the nail bed, the entire nail
should be removed (c) to evaluate for nail bed laceration. Nail bed
lacerations require repair with suturing since optimal initial management of
the damaged nail bed decreases the likelihood of chronic painful nail plate
deformity. Scalpel insertion under the nail edge (d) is the appropriate
method to drain a paronychia. A pressure dressing (a) would cause
increased pain and is not indicated. Buddy taping the finger (b) is not
indicated.

![PreTest-5e-00300 source page 354](images/PreTest-5e-00300-PreTest-5e-p0354.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00300 source page 355](images/PreTest-5e-00300-PreTest-5e-p0355.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00300 source page 377](images/PreTest-5e-00300-PreTest-5e-p0377.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00300 source page 378](images/PreTest-5e-00300-PreTest-5e-p0378.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد subungual hematoma غير معقد، يعني حواف المسمار سليمة والدم متجمع تحت المسمار وسليم من ناحية الـ fracture. trephination بتصريف الـ blood المتجمع تحت المسمار وبيخفف الألم والضغط، و بتعمل بـ electrocautery أو بإبرة 18 G ملوية. أحياناً بتحتاج أكثر من ثقب واحد، والـ hematoma اللي بدون ألم ممكن تتركه بمزاجه لأنو ما في فايدة من تدخل بدون داعي.
الفخ: نزع المسمار بالكامل (C) بس إذا حواف المسمار متضررة أو الـ hematoma أكبر من 50% من الـ nail bed. و D scalpel تحت حافة المسمار هاد لإدارة paronychia، و pressure dressing و buddy taping مش لازم.

question:
A 26-year-old man presents to the ED in severe pain with a Gila
monster attached to his arm after he was bitten. He is the animal’s main
handler. He reports localized 10/10 pain. He denies weakness, nausea, or
light-headedness. The animal attached itself 45 minutes ago. The animal is
carefully removed from his arm by staff. What is the most appropriate next
step?

options.text: Check for any remaining embedded teeth and begin wound care

correctAnswer: Check for any remaining embedded teeth and begin wound care
englishExplanation:
452.  The answer is a. There are only two venomous lizards; the Gila
Monster, which is native to the southwestern United States, and the
bearded lizard in Mexico. These animals are usually not aggressive,
despite the Gila monster’s name, and bites are usually a result of direct
handling as in this case. Both the Gila monster and the Mexican-bearded
lizard are easily identified by their thick bodies and beaded scales (with
either a white and black or pink and black configuration), but are rare in the
wild. Envenomation occurs via the glands along the lower jaw. The venom
is introduced into the victim through grooved teeth that the animal uses to
continuously chew after it has bitten down. These teeth may become
embedded in the victim, distributing more venom, and should be removed
on arrival. Initially, symptoms involve pain, erythema, and swelling at the
bite site. There is not typically associated skin necrosis. Systemic symptoms
can develop later, including nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis, tachycardia, and
hypotension. Angioedema has been documented with both species in some
cases.
Antivenin (b) is not available as these bites are rarely fatal. Broadspectrum antibiotics (d) and tetanus prophylaxis (c) should be administered
at a later interval. Applying a suction device (e) is never warranted in
envenomation injury. The patient should be observed for at least 6 hours for
systemic effects.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بعد إزالة الحيوان، أول خطوة هي تدقيق البحث عن أسنان متبقية عالقة بالجلد والبدء بـ wound care، لأنو أسنان الـ Gila monster مسنّنة grooves وممكن تضل عالقة وتواصل تنشر السم. التسميم بيبدأ من غدد على طول الفك السفلي، والأعراض الأولى ألم واحمرار وتورم بدون skin necrosis، والـ systemic symptoms ممكن تظهر بعدين مثل nausea و vomiting، والمريض لازم يراقب لسّه 6 ساعات على الأقل.
الفخ: الخيار E suction device ما بينفع أبداً مع أي envenomation، والخيار D broad-spectrum antibiotics و tetanus بييجوا بعدين مش أول خطوة. والخيار B antivenin مش متوفر لأنو لسّعان صعب.

question:
A 25-year-old man presents to the emergency department (ED) with a
right forearm laceration that he sustained from a piece of glass during a bar
fight. He complains of pain at the laceration site, but denies foreign body
sensation. On examination, the laceration is superficial and 4 cm in length.
The patient demonstrates intact strength and sensation distally. Which of the
following statements regarding radiographic imaging of this patient is true?

options.text: Imaging can be omitted because he does not have foreign body
Imaging is not indicated because retained glass does not cause an
Plain films are the next best step in the management of this patient
Computed tomographic (CT) scan is the most commonly used modality
Plain films cannot rule out bone, teeth, or glass fragments larger than 2

correctAnswer: Plain films are the next best step in the management of this patient
englishExplanation:
500.  The answer is c. On plain films, 80% to 90% of foreign bodies can
be seen. Glass larger than 2 mm is visible on plain film.
Foreign body sensation (a) has a sensitivity of 43% and specificity of
83%. Therefore, lack of a foreign body sensation cannot be used to rule out
a foreign body. Retained foreign bodies may lead to a local granulomatous
inflammatory response or to local and systemic infection (b). CT is capable
of detecting more types of foreign bodies than plain film, but it is not
commonly used given the time needed and expense (d). Plain film can
usually locate metal, bone, teeth, pencil graphite, gravel, sand, and
aluminum (e). Plain film cannot detect wood, thorns, some plastics, and
other organic matter.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: plain films هي الخطوة الجاية، لأنو 80-90% من الـ foreign bodies بتظهر عليها، و glass أكبر من 2 mm باين على الأشعة العادية. و إحساس الـ foreign body عندو sensitivity 43% و specificity 83%، يعني إنو نفي الإحساس ما بينفي وجود جسم غريب. الـ CT بيكشف أنواع أكثر بس مش مستخدم كتير بسبب الوقت والتكلفة، والـ plain film بيحدد metal و bone و teeth و gravel.
الفخ: الخيار A بيقول الـ imaging ممكن يُتجاهل مافي foreign body sensation، وهذا غلط لأن الإحساس مو حساس. و D بيقول CT هي modality الأكثر استخداماً، بينما plain film هو المعتمد.

question:
A 30-year-old woman presents to the ED with a left hand laceration.
She reports cutting herself while attempting to slice a bagel. She has a
superficial 2-cm laceration over the left thenar eminence. No deeper
structures are involved. What is the best way to clean the wound?

options.text: Punch holes in a normal saline bag or bottle and irrigate the wound
Use a high-pressure syringe and irrigate with water
Wound cleaning is unnecessary because the wound was sustained from a
Soak her hand in normal saline for 30 minutes

correctAnswer: Use a high-pressure syringe and irrigate with water
englishExplanation:
501.  The answer is b. To achieve low bacterial counts through irrigation, a
pressure of 5 to 8 psi is recommended. This pressure can be generated
with an irrigation syringe or a 35-mL syringe and a 19-gauge needle.
Water (both sterile or tap) is as equally efficacious as sterile normal saline.
The common recommendation for the amount of irrigant to use is 60 to 100
cc per 1-cm wound length.
Using normal saline bottles or bags with holes (a) may not generate
adequate pressure. Soaking (d) is ineffective in cleansing wounds.
Disinfectants (e) such as povidone-iodine should not be used on an open
wound because they can impair host defenses and promote bacterial growth.
Last, irrigation is necessary (c) regardless of the method of the sustained
injury.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الغسل بضغط 5 إلى 8 psi هو اللي بيحقق أقل عدد بكتيريا، وهاد الضغط بيتولد من irrigation syringe أو من syringe 35 mL مع 19-gauge needle. و water، سواء sterile أو tap، فعّال بنفس القدر تماماً كـ normal saline، والكمية الموصى بها 60 إلى 100 cc لكل 1 cm من طول الجرح. ولمّا الجرح نظيف ومسطحي ما في فيه بنية أعمق، والـ irrigation ضروري مهما كانت طريقة الإصابة.
الفخ: ثقوب في كيس أو قنينة saline (A) مش بتولّد ضغط كافي، و D soak 30 دقيقة ما بتنظف الجرح. و E povidone-iodine على جرح مفتوح بيضعف دفاعات المضيف وبيشجّع نمو البكتيريا.

question:
A 40-year-old man presents to the ED with a left foot puncture
wound from stepping on a rusty nail. His last tetanus vaccine was during
childhood and resulted in a severe allergic reaction and a prolonged hospital
stay. Which of the following is true regarding tetanus immunization in this
patient?

options.text: Give neither tetanus toxoid nor immunoglobulin
Give tetanus toxoid and immunoglobulin with diphenhydramine

englishExplanation:
502.  The answer is b. Tetanus toxoid is contraindicated in patients who
have had a severe allergic reaction, including respiratory distress or
cardiovascular collapse. Tetanus immunoglobulin can be used in these
patients. Local reaction at injection site resulting in redness, pain, and
swelling is not considered a contraindication.
The use of tetanus toxoid is contraindicated (a and c) even if the patient
is given diphenhydramine (e). The patient should be given immunoglobulin
(d), if the injury is high-risk (eg, puncture wound from a rusty nail).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: tetanus toxoid ممنوع عند أي حد عدو severe allergic reaction تشمل respiratory distress أو cardiovascular collapse، وهذا اللي صار معاه من طفولته. tetanus immunoglobulin ممكن تُعطى لهالحالات، والـ local reaction على موضع الحقن بحمرة وألم وتورم مش بتعتبر contraindication. و الإصابة هاي high-risk يعني puncture wound من مسمار صدئ، فالـ immunoglobulin ضرورية وهاد هو الخيار الصحيح.
الفخ: الخيار C بيقول immunoglobulin مع toxoid، و E بيقول toxoid مع immunoglobulin و diphenhydramine، والاثنين غلط لأنو الـ toxoid نفسه ممنوع. و diphenhydramine مش بتحوّل الحالة لآمنة.

question:
A 27-year-old man presents to the ED after an altercation with the
laceration shown in the following figure. There are no dental fractures and
his tetanus immunization is up-to-date. What are the most appropriate next
steps in management?
(Reproduced, with permission, from Knoop KJ, Stack LB, Storrow AB. Atlas
of Emergency Medicine. New York, NY: McGraw Hill; 2002:162.)

options.text: Infraorbital nerve block and approximation of the vermilion border
Infiltration of local anesthesia into the lip and approximation of the
Infraorbital nerve block, closure of mucosal defects before the
Infiltration of the lip with local anesthesia, closure of dermis and
Closure with a commercially available tissue adhesive and Steri-Strips

correctAnswer: Infraorbital nerve block and approximation of the vermilion border
englishExplanation:
505.  The answer is a. This is a laceration of the face crossing the
vermilion border (demarcation of the lip mucosa and facial skin). The goal
of repair in this case is approximation of the vermilion border with less
than 2 mm of displacement because significant displacement is cosmetically
unappealing. An infraorbital nerve block is required because local
anesthesia would distort tissue anatomy, thereby limiting appropriate
approximation. The first stitch should focus on approximating the border
before closing the other aspects of the wound.
Infiltration with local anesthesia (b and d) will distort the tissue
anatomy and may make proper alignment unreliable. It should only be used
if the patient fails nerve block. Initial alignment of the dermis or mucosal
aspects of the laceration (c and d) may make approximation of the

vermilion border difficult. Tissue adhesive and Steri-Strips (e) should not be
used to close the lip as it is subject to pulling forces of facial movement.
Wound separation in this case could result in a cosmetically unappealing
outcome.

![PreTest-5e-00505 source page 649](images/PreTest-5e-00505-PreTest-5e-p0649.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00505 source page 650](images/PreTest-5e-00505-PreTest-5e-p0650.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00505 source page 659](images/PreTest-5e-00505-PreTest-5e-p0659.jpg)

![PreTest-5e-00505 source page 660](images/PreTest-5e-00505-PreTest-5e-p0660.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد laceration بيعدّي على vermilion border، يعني الحد الفاصل بين جلد الوجه و mucosa الشفة. الهدف تقريب الـ border بإزاحة أقل من 2 mm لأنو الإزاحة الكبيرة بتعطي نتيجة تجميلية سيئة. و لازم infraorbital nerve block لأنو infiltration of local anesthesia بتشوّه anatomy النسيج وبتعطي approximation غير دقيق، وأول غرزة بتكون على الـ border قبل الباقي.
الفخ: الخيارين B و D بيستخدموا infiltration مع local anesthesia، وهاد بيسبّب misalignment. و E tissue adhesive مع Steri-Strips مش بتنفع للشفة لأنها تحت قوى شد من حركة الوجه.

question:
Shared scenario:
A 44-year-old woman presents to the ED with a deep puncture wound to
her left forearm after she was bitten by her neighbor’s dog. The animal is
appropriately vaccinated.

506.   Which of the following is best initial approach to wound management
in this patient?

options.text: Irrigate the wound thoroughly, reassure the patient that infections
Irrigate the wound thoroughly, suture it to prevent infection, and
Irrigate the wound thoroughly, begin prophylactic antibiotics, and
Irrigate the wound thoroughly and consult the on-call infectious
Place a dry pressure dressing over the wound, apply topical antibiotics,

correctAnswer: Irrigate the wound thoroughly, begin prophylactic antibiotics, and
englishExplanation:
506.  The answer is c. Puncture wounds, owing to their depth, cannot be
cleaned adequately. Often, closure is not necessary in small puncture
wounds that, following initial management in the ED, demonstrate adequate
healing. However, for large puncture wounds, delayed primary closure
can improve the cosmetic outcome and decreases the risk of abscess
formation and wound infection.
Approximately 5% of dog bites and 40% of cat bites become infected
and the risk of infection depends on many host factors (ie, immunity, blood
flow in small skin capillaries, etc.) as well as more physician-centered
factors such as the ability to cleanse the wound appropriately. Given that
this patient suffered a puncture wound that will not be able to be cleaned
adequately, discharging the patient without prophylactic antibiotics (a) is
incorrect. Copious irrigation is crucial in preventing wound infections. Most
bite wounds can be repaired with primary closure, however puncture
wounds, small lacerations, and hand and foot wounds carry higher risks of
infection and therefore are best managed with delayed primary closure and
when closed should not be closed “tightly,” so that whatever bacterial load
has settled into the wound has an portal to exit (b). Pasteurella is the most
common organism in cat bites (d) and concern over a possible Pasteurella
infection would not be a reason to initiate an emergent consult to an
Infectious Disease specialist in the ED. The most commonly used antibiotic
for dog and cat bites is amoxicillin/clavulanate (e). Clindamycin with a
fluoroquinolone can be used for dog bites in penicillin-allergic patients.
Doxycycline can be used for cat bites in penicillin-allergic patients. Topical
antibiotics are not an appropriate prophylactic antibiotic choice in a patient
with a puncture wound suffered from an animal bite.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: puncture wounds بسبب عمقها ما بتتقدر تنظف بشكل كافي، وعادة مالها داعي closure في الـ puncture الصغيرة إذا كان التئام الجرح adequate. تقريب 5% من لدغات الكلاب و 40% من لدغات القطط بتصير infected، والخطر بيعتمد على عوامل المضيف وكمان على جودة التنظيف. و copious irrigation هي المفتاح لمنع العدوى، ومع prophylactic antibiotics والمتابعة لازم تنزل للمريضة.
الفخ: الخيار B بيقترح الخياطة لمنع العدوى وهي غلط، لأنو الخياطة بتمسك البكتيريا جوّا الجرح. و A بيقترح الخروج بدون antibiotic وده غلط، و D استشارة infectious disease مش أول خطوة.

question:
A 23-year-old man presents to the ED complaining of a wound to his
left lower extremity. He was pulling branches out of a flooded creek in his
backyard, when he punctured his left calf. His legs were in the water when
the wound occurred. The puncture wound is 1 cm in diameter, several
centimeters deep, and demonstrates surrounding erythema. After irrigating
the wound, you discover a splinter within the wound. Which of the
following is the most appropriate next step(s)?

options.text: Obtain radiographs to evaluate for additional foreign bodies
Suture the wound using 4-0 nylon suture in a simple interrupted fashion
Dress the wound with a sterile bandage and treat with an oral
Remove the splinter and treat with an oral fluoroquinolone
Remove the splinter, suture the wound, and treat with an oral

correctAnswer: Remove the splinter and treat with an oral fluoroquinolone
englishExplanation:
508.  The answer is d. Foreign bodies with potential to cause an infection
and inflammatory response require immediate removal (eg, thorns,
splinters, spines, teeth, and soil-covered objects). These materials may
cause intense and excessive inflammatory responses. If the ED physician
cannot remove the foreign body, the appropriate specialist should be
consulted. After the splinter is removed, the patient should be treated with
an outpatient fluoroquinolone. Wounds with stagnant freshwater exposure
are at high risk of infection with gram-positive bacteria, Pseudomonas, and
Aeromonas species, and require empiric antibiotic coverage.
Because organic materials are radiolucent, radiographs will not assist in
locating organic foreign bodies (a). Thorough direct visual inspection is
necessary to locate and remove all organic foreign bodies. Treatment with
antibiotics (c) is necessary, but less important than the removal of the
foreign body. Closing a puncture wound, especially with a retained foreign
body, will lead to an inflammatory response and likely infection. Closing
this patient’s wound would not be appropriate management (b and e).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أي foreign body قادر يعمل inflammation أو عدوى لازم يتشال فوراً، وهاد الـ splinter لازم تشيله الأول، وإذا ما قدرت تشيله لازم تستشير specialist. بعد الشيل بتعالج بـ oral fluoroquinolone، لأنو التعرض لماء راكد بيزيد خطر gram-positive bacteria و Pseudomonas و Aeromonas، فالـ empiric coverage ضروري. و الأجسام العضوية radiolucent فالـ radiographs مش بتفيد في تحديد موقعها.
الفخ: الخيار B و E بيقترحوا الخياطة بعد إزالة الـ splinter، وهي غلط لأنو قفل جرح فيه جسم غريب بيخلي inflammation واحتمال عدوى. و A radiographs مش منطقية مع مادة عضوية.

question:
Shared scenario:
A 21-year-old woman presents to the ED with a superficial 2-cm midforehead laceration sustained from a fall. You irrigate and close the wound.
She is concerned about her long-term cosmetic outcome and requests
detailed wound care instructions.

509.   Which of the following statements would be an appropriate wound
care instruction to give?

options.text: Avoid direct sun exposure while the wound is healing
The wound should not be washed until sutures are removed
Sutures should be removed in 7 to 10 days
Appearance of the scar at suture removal will be the final cosmetic
Good suturing technique and meticulous wound care guarantee no scar

correctAnswer: Avoid direct sun exposure while the wound is healing
englishExplanation:
509.  The answer is a. Direct sun exposure during healing can lead to
permanent hyperpigmentation. Therefore, patients should be advised to
avoid direct sun exposure and use sunblock for up to 12 months after the
injury.
Patients should be instructed to wash the wound with gentle soap and
water (b), as early as 8 hours after sutures are placed. Although the wound
should be kept dry, instructing against washing is inappropriate. Healing
wounds should be patted dry to avoid dehiscence from forceful wiping. The
patient should be informed that all lacerations scar (e). Good repair and

wound care will improve the appearance of the scar but will not inhibit scar
formation. Wounds that heal by delayed closure have the poorest cosmetic
outcome. Good wound edge approximation, use of appropriate suture
material, and early suture removal all lead to better cosmetic outcomes. The
early appearance of the scar is not reflective of the long-term outcome (d).
Facial sutures should be removed in 3 to 5 days. Leaving sutures in for 7 to
10 days leads to a poorer cosmetic outcome (c).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: التعرض المباشر للشمس وقت الشفاء بيسبّب hyperpigmentation دائم، فالمريض لازم يتجنّب الشمس ويستخدم sunblock لمدة 12 شهر بعد الإصابة، وهاد بيحمي من الصبغة الدائمة. و ده مناسب كتعليمات wound care. و إضافةً إلى ذلك، كل الجروح بتعمل scar مهما كان care ممتاز، والغسل بـ gentle soap و water مسموح من بعد 8 ساعات من وضع الخياطة مع تنفيف بلطف.
الفخ: الخيار B منع الغسل لحد ما تشيل الخياطة غلط، لأنو الغسل المسموح بيحسّن الشكل. و C إن الخيوط تنشال بعد 7-10 أيام مش صح للوجه، بتنشال بعد 3-5 أيام، و D و E مش دقيقين.

question:
A 30-year-old chef presents to the ED with a complete fingertip
amputation. Her knife slipped while chopping vegetables. She brought the
amputated pulp in a plastic bag. On examination, the patient has a clean, 5
mm in diameter dermal slice on the distal volar tip of the second digit.
There is profuse nonpulsatile bleeding. There is no trauma to the DIP joint,

proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint, or the nail. Her most recent tetanus
booster was 1 year ago. Which of the following is the most appropriate next
step in management?

options.text: Consult hand surgery for replantation of the pulp in the operating room
Irrigate the hand and replant distal tip in the ED as soon as possible
Perform a digital block with lidocaine and epinephrine to control
Immediately place the amputated tip on ice to prevent cell death
Discharge the patient with a pressure dressing and splint after the wound

correctAnswer: Discharge the patient with a pressure dressing and splint after the wound
englishExplanation:
512.  The answer is e. This patient has a less than 10-mm dermal slice that
is generally managed with bleeding control, nonadherent dressings, and
a finger splint to prevent reinjury and decrease pain. Dressing changes
have to be performed every 24 to 48 hours. Fingertip amputation greater
than 10 mm, exposure of the bone, or involvement of the nail may require a
hand surgeon consultation. However, this patient’s dermal slice is 5 mm and
does not involve the phalanx or nail; therefore, it can be managed
conservatively. Pressure dressing is typically sufficient to control bleeding
in dermal tip amputations. If hemostasis is not achieved with direct
pressure, commercial hemostatic agents can be used.
The management of fingertip amputations is controversial. For
amputations involving a significant amount of the distal digit, various
techniques, such as partial-thickness skin grafts and full-thickness skin
grafts, exist. Most of these are performed in the operating room by a hand
surgeon. However, replantation of a less than 10-mm dermal tip is not
indicated (a, b, and d). Despite replantation, the amputated tip is most
likely to necrose and slough off. Using the amputated piece as a natural
dressing is unnecessary given the small size of the wound. Digital blocks
(c) are helpful for pain relief while the patient irrigates the distal tip.
Epinephrine is not recommended for use on the digits. The most appropriate
way to achieve hemostasis is with direct pressure.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاي fingertip amputation بس 5 mm، يعني dermal slice أصغر من 10 mm بدون involvement للمفاصل أو nail أو العظم. كده بتتم بالـ bleeding control و pressure dressing و nonadherent dressing مع finger splint بعد ما تتـ irrigate وتتحكم بالنزيف، وتغيير الـ dressing كل 24 إلى 48 ساعة. و قطع أكبر من 10 mm أو involvement في nail هاد بيحتاج hand surgeon.
الفخ: الخيارات A و B و D بتتكلم عن replantation، وهي مش indicated لقطع أقل من 10 mm لأنو الجزء غالباً بيموت ويسقط. و D تحديداً وضع القطعة مباشرة على الثلج بيضر الأنسجة.

question:
A 25-year-old graduate student presents to the ED stating that
approximately 4 hours ago she burned her left hand after spilling a very
small amount of a 5% hydrofluoric (HF) on herself. The patient says the
symptoms were initially quite mild, but now the pain is severe. Examination
of the affected area reveals a 3-cm area on the dorsal surface of the left
hand that is white with surrounding erythema, exquisite tenderness, and
edema with multiple small bullae. No other injuries are evident. What is the
most initial step in the management of this patient?

options.text: Perform a wrist block, irrigate the hand with tap water for 10 minutes,
Apply 2.5% calcium gluconate gel to the affected skin
Inject 5% calcium gluconate directly into the affected skin
Nebulize 2.5% calcium gluconate and have the patient breathe the
Update the patient’s tetanus and inject 8.4% sodium bicarbonate

correctAnswer: Apply 2.5% calcium gluconate gel to the affected skin
englishExplanation:
513.  The answer is b. The most appropriate initial step is to apply 2.5%
calcium gluconate gel to the wound. HF acid burns can superficially
appear very benign, and often the more dilute the solution is, the greater the
risk for toxicity because the recognition of symptoms is often delayed.
Tissue damage from HF acid burns is caused by both corrosive burns from
the hydrogen ions themselves, and also chemical burns from tissue
penetration of the fluoride ions. After penetrating, the fluoride ions form
insoluble salts with calcium and magnesium and also form soluble salts
with other cations that then dissociate rapidly leading to further release of
fluoride ions and more tissue destruction. Systemic toxicity occurs when the
body’s stores of calcium and magnesium become depleted leading to
enzymatic dysfunction and subsequently cellular death. The majority of
deaths result from fatal cardiac arrhythmias.
While injecting 5% calcium gluconate (c) into the wound may
ultimately prove to be the definitive treatment for this patient, this is not the

next step. Calcium gluconate acts to bind the fluoride ions at the side of
injury. Nebulized calcium gluconate (d) would not allow for the drug to
have any impact on the injury. While analgesia and local wound care are
important (a), this does not actually treat the HF acid exposure. Although
HF acid is classified as a weak acid, injecting sodium bicarbonate (e) is not
an appropriate or effective treatment for this injury.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أول خطوة هي وضع 2.5% calcium gluconate gel على الجلد المتضرر، لأنو الـ fluoride ions بتخترق الأنسجة وتعمل salts مع calcium و magnesium، فالـ gel بيربط fluoride بمكان الإصابة. و الـ HF burns ممكن تبان بسيطة، وكل ما المحلول أرق كانت الخطورة أعلى لأنو الأعراض بتتأخر. و على مستوى الجسم، نقص calcium و magnesium بيسبّب enzymatic dysfunction و arrhythmias قاتلة.
الفخ: حقن 5% calcium gluconate داخل الجلد (C) ممكن يكون definitive بس مش الخطوة الجاية. و D nebulized calcium gluconate مالها تأثير على الإصابة، و E sodium bicarbonate ما بتعالج التعرض لـ HF.

question:
Shared scenario:
A 12-year-old girl is out playing in her backyard when she finds a kitten.
She is able to trap the kitten and plans to bring it home as a pet. While
carrying the kitten back to her house, the kitten bites her left forearm. The

girl drops the kitten and runs home to tell her father who then promptly
brings the patient in for evaluation.

517.   Evaluation in the ED reveals two small puncture wounds on the left
hand over the dorsal surface with no active bleeding, no erythema, and
normal neurovascular exam. Which of the following should be avoided in
the management of this girl’s wound?

options.text: Thoroughly examine the wound as well as perform a neurovascular
Obtain radiographs to identify any foreign bodies including possible
Thoroughly clean the wound with high-pressure syringe and sterile
Close the wound with tissue adhesive

correctAnswer: Close the wound with tissue adhesive
englishExplanation:
517.  The correct answer is d. The patient has sustained two small
puncture wounds secondary to a cat/kitten. Careful examination of the
wound should be done through flexion/extension to determine presence of
foreign body and/or damage to underlying structures including
neurovascular bundles (a). Radiographs are recommended for any
mammalian bite to identify any potential foreign body or bony involvement

(b). Mammalian bites are at high risk for infection and these wounds should
be cleansed thoroughly and left open with healing by secondary intention
(c). Tissue adhesive should never be used to close puncture wounds,
especially those caused by a bite (d). Sutures may be utilized if the
laceration is larger/gaping or involves the face but should be placed loosely
and with nonabsorbable sutures. Prophylactic antibiotics are
recommended for all mammalian bites including dogs and cats (e).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: السؤال بيسأل شو لازم يتجنّب، والجواب D يعني tissue adhesive. لأنو puncture wounds، وخصوصاً عضّات الحيوانات، ما تنقفل أبداً بـ tissue adhesive. و C بيحكي cleanse thoroughly و left open بالـ secondary intention، و A examination مع neurovascular و flexion و extension ضروري، و B radiographs مطلوبة لأي mammalian bite، و E prophylactic antibiotics مطلوبة لكل عضّات الثدييات.
الفخ: الناس بتختار E لأنها حاسة إنها مو ضرورية، بس antibiotic مطلوب لكل mammalian bites. الخيار اللي لازم يتجنّب هو adhesive، وهاد ما بيتناقض مع موضوع antibiotics.

question:
A patient presents after a fist fight with a puncture wound to his 
hand. Which description of the presentation has the best prognosis?
englishExplanation:
Fingertip penetration. The three factors that have been 
found to worsen the prognosis for a “fight bite” injury are delay in identification and treatment of the wound, an increase depth of the wound 
as it is more likely to include the tendon, and intrusion into the joint 
of the tooth. A puncture wound of the fingertip is much less likely to 
create a significant infection due to the close septae that decrease the 
likelihood of spreading bacteria in an open wound.
   

522.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الخيار A هو fingertip penetration، وهاد أفضل prognosis بين الخيارات. الـ factors اللي بت worsen prognosis في fight bite هي تأخر اكتشاف الجرح و treatment، وزيادة عمق الجرح لأنو ممكن يوصل tendon، و intrusion السنو داخل الـ joint. أما ثقب الـ fingertip فالـ close septae بتقلل احتمال انتشار البكتيريا في جرح مفتوح، فالعدوى أقل بكتير.
الفخ: الخيارات B و C و D هي بحد ذاتها العوامل اللي بت worsen prognosis، فلو اخترتها غلط. افصل: تأخر العلاج و involvement المفصل كلهم بيزيدوا الخطورة، أما fingertip penetration هو الخيار الوحيد المريح.

question: Which of the following is associated with an increased risk of infection?

options.text: Avoidance of epinephrine use in wound anesthesia
Use of clippers instead of razors for hair management near
Use of tape over sutures for wound closure

englishExplanation:
Silk yields the highest infection rates, whereas monofilament synthetic substances have the lowest risk of infection. Other risk 
factors are listed in eBox 50.1
arabicExplanation:
ليش: silk threads بتدي أعلى infection rates بين مواد الخياطة، بينما monofilament synthetic substances عندها أقل خطر على الـ infection. فـ silk هي المادة اللي مرتبطة بزيادة احتمال الـ infection في الجرح، وهاد سبب اختيارها كإجابة. والخيارات التانية زي تجنّب epinephrine و استخدام clippers بدل razors و high-pressure irrigation هي إجراءات بتقلل الخطر مو تزيده.
الفخ: الخيار B high-pressure irrigation اللي الناس بتحسبها خطر، بينما هي بتقلّل العدوى. و A تجنّب epinephrine إجراء وقائي، و E tape over sutures هاد بيزيد المشكلة مش بيحلها.

question:
Which of the following factors is most likely to require no antibiotic 
prophylaxis?
englishExplanation:
Antibiotic prophylaxis is often provided for patients 
with wounds with gross contamination, patients with severe crush 
injuries, and immunocompromised patients. Prophylaxis is also 
required for patients with cat bites. Seven of eight randomized trials 
of dog bite wounds showed no benefit with antibiotics. Human bites 
or lacerations to the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint are termed 
“fight bites,” and these wounds have a high incidence of infection. 
Thus, of the choices given, dog bites have the lowest incidence of 
infection and therefore are the least likely to require prophylactic 
antibiotics.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: السؤال بيسألك أي نوع جرح هو الأقل احتمالاً إنه يحتاج antibiotic prophylaxis، وسبع من ثماني دراسات randomized على dog bite wounds ما показаوا أي فايدة من المضادات الحيوية. Dog bite عنده أقل نسبة عدوى بين كل الخيارات، بينما cat bites دايماً بتاخد prophylaxis. و human bites المعروفة باسم fight bite عندها نسبة عدوى عالية، فحتى هي بتغطي بالمضادات الحيوية، وكمان الجروح المتسخة والـ immunocompromised patients بتحتاج prophylaxis.
الفخ: كثير طلبة بيختاروا human bite أو cat bite لأنهم بيسمعوا إن أي جرح عضخ لازم ياخد antibiotics. فرّق بين cat bite و dog bite، وكمان لاحظ إن human bite نوعها fight bite لها نسبة عدوى عالية فعندها لازم antibiotic prophylaxis.

question:
A 75-year-old woman presents with a puncture mark on her hand. 
She reports being bitten by her cat the previous night. Which of the 
following statements regarding this patient’s injury is true?

options.text: Capnocytophaga canimorsus is the organism of concern.
Cats are very clean animals and do not carry any virulent strains.
Cats produce superficial infections because their teeth are not
Concern exists for a virulent gram-negative bacterium, which
Irrigation and topical antibiotics are indicated.

correctAnswer: Concern exists for a virulent gram-negative bacterium, which
englishExplanation:
Cats have long, slender, pointed teeth that can penetrate 
tendons, joints, and bone, inoculating bacteria deep into these tissues. 
Cat bites have a substantially higher risk of infection than dog bites do. 
Another important factor in the development of wound infection after 
cat bites involves the presence of Pasteurella multocida, a highly virulent, gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic rod found in the oral cavity 
or nasopharynx of 70% to 90% of healthy cats.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الجواب بيحكي عن بكتيريا خطيرة اسمها Pasteurella multocida، وهي gram-negative rod عالية الخطورة موجودة في الفم أو nasopharynx عند 70% لـ 90% من القطط السليمة. أسنان القطة طويلة ورفيعة ومدببة، فبتقدر تخترق tendons و joints و bone وتحقن البكتيريا عميق جوّا الأنسجة. كمان cat bite عنده أعلى خطر عدوى من dog bite، والجرح هنا كان puncture mark فالعدوى ممكن تصير بسرعة وتسبب cellulitis سريع.
الفخ: الخيار اللي بيحكي إن القطط نظيفة وما فيها سلالات virulent هو غلط، لأن 70% لـ 90% من القطط السليمة عندها Pasteurella multocida. وكمان ما تكتفي بـ irrigation و topical antibiotics لأن الخطر هو عدوى بكتيريا عميقة.

question:
A 19-year-old man presents 10 hours after sustaining a dog attack. 
He has multiple lacerations on his head and right hand. What is the 
appropriate management of this patient?

options.text: Repair the hand and the head lacerations
Repair the hand laceration but not the head laceration
Repair the head laceration but not the hand laceration
Use Steri-Strips on all and give him a prescription for amoxicillinclavulanate (Augmentin)

correctAnswer: Repair the head laceration but not the hand laceration
englishExplanation:
For dog bites, the infection rate of hand wounds is as high as 
30%, regardless of suturing, whereas the infection rate of dog bites elsewhere averages 9%. Similarly, dog bites of the face and neck (including 
punctures) have lower infection rates of 0% to 5% even when they are 
sutured. Bite wounds of the face and scalp from any species that are 
less than 12 hours old may be cleansed well and sutured. Most other 
bite wounds that are going to be closed should have this done within 
6 hours.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: عند dog bite، نسبة العدوى في جروح الإيد بتوصل لـ 30% حتى لو خرّطت الجرح، بينما الجروح في أماكن ثانية متوسطها 9%، وجروح الوجه والرقبة عندها نسبة عدوى 0% لـ 5% حتى لو خُرّطت. هاد الخيار هو إصلاح جروح الرأس لأنها عمرها 10 ساعات يعني أقل من 12 ساعة، والجرح بعمر 10 ساعات ممكن يتغسل كويس ويتخاط، أما جرح الإيد فهو تجاوز 6 ساعات ولازم يبقى مفتوح.
الفخ: الخيار اللي بيقول إصلاح الإيد بس مو الرأس هو اللي الناس بتوقعه، لأنهم بيفكروا كل bite لازم يتخاط. فرّق: الوجه والرقبة لحظة الخطر أقل، أما جروح الإيد فعندها نسبة عدوى أعلى حتى مع الخياطة.

question:
A patient presents to the emergency department (ED) complaining of severe burning of both hands since leaving her building this 
morning. In her history, you find out that the metal doors of her 
housing complex had just been cleaned of all rust. She has small 
blisters on her palms and a white appearance to the skin. What is 
the next step?

options.text: Consult plastics for an alkali burn.
Leave blisters, cover with bacitracin and gauze.
Mix calcium gluconate with KY jelly, apply to hands, and cover
Obtain pain control and prescribe oral clindamycin.

correctAnswer: Mix calcium gluconate with KY jelly, apply to hands, and cover
englishExplanation:
The rust cleaning and physical findings are descriptive of 
a hydrofluoric acid burn. It is also commonly used in the production 
of microelectronics, etching glass, for removing rust, and for cleaning 
cement and bricks. Calcium gluconate (2.5%) gel is the preferred topical agent. However, this gel is often not available in hospital pharmacies, but it can be made by mixing 3.5 g calcium gluconate powder in 
150 mL of a water-soluble lubricant. The gel should be secured by an 
occlusive cover, such as a latex glove.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه البنت تعرّضت لـ hydrofluoric acid burn، لأن أبواب المبنى نُظّفت من الصدأ وهي تستعمل هاد الحمض لإزالة rust. الحرارة الشديدة مع البثور والجلد الأبيض بهاد الشكل بتدل على هاد النوع من الحروق. العلاج المفضّل هو gel من calcium gluconate بنسبة 2.5%، ولما ما يتوفر بالpharmacy بتعمله بنفسك بخلط 3.5 g من بودرة calcium gluconate مع 150 mL من lubricant ذابل بالماء، ولازم تغطي المنطقة بغطاء occlusive مثل glove لاتكس عشان الـ gel يثبّت على الجلد.
الفخ: الخيار D اللي بياخد pain control مع clindamycin دا بيحكي عن infection وحالتها مو infection. والحل الصح هو الـ calcium gluconate gel مع occlusive cover، لأن جرح hydrofluoric acid burn بيلزمه علاج موضعي مخصوص مش antibiotics.

question: What is the etiology of most tendinopathies?

options.text: Recent or previous complete tendon rupture

englishExplanation:
Tendinopathies are thought to be precipitated by repetitive 
microtrauma and mechanical overload rather than true inflammation 
of the tendon
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي بتسبب أغلب الـ tendinopathies هي mechanical overload و repetitive microtrauma، مش inflammation حقيقية بالـ tendon. يعني الـ tendon بيتعب ويتراكم عليه إجهاد فوق طاقته بشكل متكرر، وهاد بيؤدي لتغيرات في الوتر نفسه بدل ما يصير فيه inflammation. الـ inflammation الحقيقي بالـ tendon نادر، ولازم تفهم إن احمرار وتورم بالـ tendon مش بالضرورة يعني inflammation للوتر نفسه.
الفخ: الخيار C اللي بيقول high-grade inflammation هو الفخ الأساسي، لأن الناس بتتمسك بكلمة inflammation وبتعدي عليها. بس الآلية الحقيقية هي الإجهاد الميكانيكي المتكرر، والتهاب حقيقي بالـ tendon نادر.

question:
A 62-year-old male farmer with no medical problems presents with 
leg pain and muscle spasms. He reports moderate to severe pain 
and muscle spasms in the calf that have occurred and worsened 
during 3 days. Two weeks prior, he suffered a puncture wound to 
his ankle just above his boot top with a piece of metal. Examination 
is remarkable for a heart rate of 115 beats/minute, blood pressure 
of 170/110 mm Hg, and a healing clean wound above the medial 
malleolus with no evidence of active infection. The calf is in active 
spasm with some increased tone in the peroneal musculature also. 
Which of the following statements regarding this patient’s disease is 
true?

options.text: A radiograph should be obtained to assess for subcutaneous air.
Admission for intravenous (IV) antibiotics is indicated.

englishExplanation:
Localized tetanus reflects a local neuromuscular process 
with pain and spasm. It is likely due to a partial immunity. Immune 
globulin is indicated. Although mortality is lower, it can progress to 
generalized tetanus, and admission is warranted.
   

CHAPTER 119  Viruses
1634.e3
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض عنده localized tetanus، يعني عملية neuromuscular محلية بتسبب ألم وتشنّج في العضلات. السبب غالباً immunity جزئية لأن جرح الكاحل كان puncture wound ممكن يلوثه Clostridium tetani spores. في هاد الحالة لازم تعطي tetanus immune globulin، ومش بس tetanus toxoid، ولازم تعمل admission كمان لأن الـ mortality أقل بصح ممكن يتحول لحالة generalized tetanus.
الفخ: الخيار C اللي بيقول outpatient management هي الغلطة، لأن الـ localized tetanus ممكن يتطور إلى generalized tetanus. وكمان ما تكتفي بـ tetanus toxoid لحالها، لازم tetanus immune globulin معاها.

question:
An abrasion collar can be associated with which of the following 
types of wounds?
englishExplanation:
An abrasion collar (also referred to as an abrasion margin, 
rim, or ring) results from skin indentation as the bullet penetrates the 
surface. This collar is an abraded area of tissue that surrounds an entry 
wound as the result of friction between the bullet and epithelium. These 
usually result from distant or long-range wounds, which are inflicted 
from far enough away that only the bullet makes contact with the skin. 
When an abrasion collar is the only visible superficial clinical finding 
present, the term indeterminate range describes the range of fire. Most 
entrance wounds will have an abrasion collar aside from those on the 
palms and soles, which usually appear slit-like.
arabicExplanation:

question:
When managing a gunshot wound victim, which of the following is 
not important for forensic evidence collection?

options.text: Do not clean the patient’s the hands with alcohol or Betadine.
If soot is noted on the hands of the victim, cover with paper bags.
Place each article of clothing in a separate paper bag.
Use metal forceps to handle a bullet to prevent contamination.

correctAnswer: Use metal forceps to handle a bullet to prevent contamination.
englishExplanation:
Never remove a bullet with metal hemostats or pickups 
because metal tools can obliterate the microscopic markings (the telltale fingerprint) of the gun from which it was shot. A victim’s clothing 
may hold the answer to critical questions, such as “How far away was 
the assailant who fired the weapon?” and “Which hole is the entrance 
and which the exit?” Articles of clothing removed from a wounded 
patient should be placed in separate paper bags to preserve the trace 
evidence on them and to avoid accidentally transferring evidence from 
one article to another (cross-contamination). Always cover a patient’s 
hands with paper bags when the presence of soot is suspected. A 
gunshot residue test may determine whether a victim or suspect has 
been in close proximity to a weapon that has been fired. Factors that 
decrease the sensitivity of gunshot residue tests include washing the 
skin with alcohol or Betadine.
   

e122
Emergency Medical Services and Disaster Preparedness

الفخ: الخيار D اللي بيقول كل قطعة ملابس بـ paper bag لحالها هو ضروري فعلاً، فلازم تميزه عن الخيار E. وكمان الخيار B صح لأنه لازم تغطي اليدين بـ paper bags لما تشوف soot.

question:
A 74- year- old patient presents with a gaping wound from a dog
bite, complaining of pain at the site. The dog belongs to a friend, has
reportedly had “all his shots, ” and is in custody. The patient is from
Central America but has lived in the US for more than 50 years; he
does not recall his immunization history. Besides copious irrigation
and wound dressing, which of the following should be included in
the treatment of this patient?

options.text: Diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus toxoids (Tdap) and tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG)

correctAnswer: Diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus toxoids (Tdap) and tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG)
englishExplanation:
Studies show that many people are inadequately immu -
nized, especially patients older than 70 years old, immigrants, and
people with no education beyond grade school. Patient immuni -
zation histories are often unreliable. Given the inability to predict
which wounds are high risk, all wounds should be approached with
suspicion. Inadequately immunized patients need a dose of Tdap and
TIG. Because studies suggest that 10% to 40% of the population in the
United States is inadequately immunized against diphtheria, diphthe -
ria vaccination should be given along with tetanus toxoid. Many adults
are not immunized against pertussis, and the incidence of disease has
been rising since the 1980s. In 2005, a new acellular form of the pertussis vaccine became available and is recommended for all adults.

question: A 30-year-old man with no previous eye history presents to the emergency department with pain and photophobia in his right eye after working on a wood carving project. He thinks wood got into his eye when he was carving. On examination, the patient is having difficulty opening his right eye due to pain and he has excessive tearing. He reports blurry vision. After the installation of tetracaine, the pain begins to subside, and he is able to open his eye for examination. A small foreign body is visualized over the lateral cornea and is removed with a cotton swab. Fluorescein staining shows a small epithelial defect at the site of the previously noted foreign body. The remainder of the ophthalmic exam is unremarkable. What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient?

options.text: Polymyxin plus neomycin plus hydrocortisone drops

englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with symptoms of a corneal abrasion and he was found to have a small corneal foreign body. Any patient who has severe eye pain with photophobia or foreign body sensation preventing the opening of the eye generally can be presumed to have a corneal epithelial defect. Corneal abrasions can be classified as traumatic, contact lens-related, or spontaneous. Spontaneous defects in the corneal epithelium may occur without any obvious injury. Eyes that have had a previous injury are prone to spontaneous abrasions. On examination of a patient with symptoms of corneal abrasion or foreign body, the clinician should first ensure there is no penetrating trauma or ruptured globe. The diagnosis of corneal abrasion should be confirmed with fluorescein staining. All foreign bodies should be removed with irrigation, a cotton swab, or with a foreign body spud within 24 hours of injury. Patients should be treated with topical antibiotics to prevent superinfection. An ointment is theoretically better because it provides lubrication, but many patients prefer drops instead. Since there is not any mention of contact lens use in this patient, appropriate treatment for this patient’s corneal abrasion and foreign body would include polymyxin plus trimethoprim drops. The pain can be treated with topical or oral nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medications.



Cyclopentolate drops (A) are parasympathetic medications that inhibit the miotic, or pupil-constricting, response to light. These drops can help with any photophobia symptoms, but they will not relieve the foreign body sensation. The effect of the drops can last for 24–36 hours and, generally, small abrasions heal within that period of time. Therefore, these drops are not recommended unless patients have very large corneal abrasions with significant photophobia. Additionally, this option did not include antibiotic treatment, which is the only recommended therapy for corneal abrasion and foreign bodies.

Gentamicin drops (B) would be indicated for patients who wear contact lenses. Such patients are at risk for infection from Pseudomonas species, so fluoroquinolones or aminoglycosides are indicated. This patient does not wear contact lenses and aminoglycosides should be avoided because they can be toxic to the epithelium.

Polymyxin plus neomycin plus hydrocortisone drops (C) should be avoided because the use of steroids slows epithelial healing and reduces host resistance to superinfection.

One Step Further
Question:
What physical examination finding would suggest an open globe injury?

Reveal Answer:
A teardrop or misshapen pupil.

Apply topical anesthesia
Use cotton-tipped applicator, needle with the slit lamp, or Alger brush to dislodge
If metallic object, remove rust rings in 24–48 hours
Consult ophthalmology for large or deep foreign bodies
Postprocedure topical antibiotics

الفخ: الخيار C اللي بي polymyxin مع neomycin مع hydrocortisone، أو الخيار A cyclopentolate drops. الـ cyclopentolate بتعمل تخدير للعين (cycloplegic) وتسكين، مو antibiotic، والـ antibiotic هنا هو اللي بيمنع الـ superinfection.

question: A young man presents to the emergency department with eye pain. Fluorescein staining and Wood lamp examination show the finding above. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
englishExplanation:
The patient is presenting with a corneal abrasion, as seen on Wood lamp examination. Corneal abrasions are a common cause of red or painful eyes. They are usually caused by direct trauma but can also be caused by contact lens irritation, ultraviolet light exposure, or wind exposure. Patients usually report a foreign body sensation, pain, and photophobia. Corneal abrasions can be diagnosed by a careful eye examination with fluorescein staining, as it can help identify a corneal epithelial defect. When visualized under a cobalt blue filter on a slit lamp or under a Wood lamp, there will be uptake of the fluorescein dye in the corneal defect, causing it to appear green.

The majority of corneal abrasions heal spontaneously. Thus, treatment involves providing symptomatic control and preventing superinfection. Small abrasions may not require further treatment, but either erythromycin ointment or polymyxin solution can be used if antibiotics are given. If the patient wears contact lenses, ciprofloxacin or another agent that can cover Pseudomonas infections should be used. If an abrasion is > 2 mm or very painful, an additional cycloplegic agent can be prescribed to provide more symptomatic relief. Small abrasions can be reexamined within 48–72 hours. Large abrasions or abrasions involving the central visual axis should be reexamined by an ophthalmologist within 24 hours. Of note, topical anesthetics should not be prescribed, as they can inhibit corneal healing and suppress the blinking reflex, which is protective of the eye.



Neomycin ointments (B) should be avoided in corneal abrasions to prevent hypersensitivity reactions.

Prednisolone eye drops (C) can be effective in treating traumatic iritis, which is another common cause of eye pain but would be inappropriate in the setting of an isolated corneal abrasion.

Timolol eye drops (D) can be used to treat acute angle-closure glaucoma to lower intraocular pressure by decreasing aqueous humor production but would have little utility in treating corneal abrasions.

One Step Further
Question:
What type of injury does a positive Seidel test imply?

Reveal Answer:
Full-thickness corneal injury.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Corneal Abrasion

Sx: pain, photophobia, tearing, or foreign body sensation
Uncontrollable crying in infants
Dx: fluorescein stain
Tx
Most are self-limiting
Topical antibiotics to prevent superinfection is common practice
Add antipseudomonal coverage for those who wear contact lenses

الفخ: الخيار D timolol drops هو للـ glaucoma، والخيار C prednisolone eye drops مش علاج لل abrasion. وانتبه: إذا كان المريض بيستعمل contact lenses فالـ antibiotic لازم يغطي Pseudomonas زي ciprofloxacin.

question: Which of the following pediatric intranasal foreign bodies needs to be removed expeditiously in the emergency department?

options.text: A posterior foreign body that is barely visible

englishExplanation:
Intranasal foreign body insertion is found, almost exclusively, in pediatric patients. Most children are asymptomatic, but they may present with pain, nasal discharge, bleeding, or simply visualization of the foreign body in the nose. The majority of intranasal foreign bodies are in the right nare, can be visualized in the anterior nasal passage, and are appropriate for removal by an emergency clinician. Otolaryngology referral is warranted for patients with posterior foreign bodies that cannot be visualized, impacted foreign bodies with significant swelling and inflammation, penetrating foreign bodies, and any foreign body that cannot be removed due to poor cooperation or bleeding. However, a few types of foreign bodies that need to be removed expeditiously in the emergency department are button batteries, paired disc magnets inserted into each nostril, and superabsorbent polymer beads. Button batteries can cause alkaline tissue necrosis and result in septal perforation within several hours. Paired magnets inserted into each nostril attach at the nasal septum and can cause perforation from chronic compression. Superabsorbent beads can become lodged over a few days, leading to tissue necrosis. Positive pressure techniques are recommended first-line treatments to remove an intranasal foreign body. If this does not work, several instruments can be used to remove the foreign body, including a suction catheter, a small Foley catheter, or alligator forceps. Pediatric patients will generally need sedation since this procedure is often only successful if the patient remains still.



A posterior foreign body that is barely visible (B) should not be removed by the emergency clinician since it is prone to complications. Patients with a posterior foreign body can be given an urgent otolaryngology referral.

Similarly, a single magnet (C) does not necessarily need to be removed in the emergency department. If it is easily visualized, it may be simple for the emergency clinician to remove, but a single magnet does not pose a risk for septal perforation.

A sponge (D) can also be removed by the emergency clinician, but it does not need to be done expeditiously. A patient with a sponge in the nose should try to avoid getting the area wet or moist since the sponge will expand and then be more difficult to remove.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common complication of a chronic intranasal foreign body?

Reveal Answer:
Bacterial sinusitis.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Nasal Foreign Body

Most often in children
Unilateral mucopurulent and foul-smelling nasal discharge
Tx: big kiss (positive pressure in mouth by parent while occluding unaffected nares)

question: A 20-year-old man presents with a superficial laceration to the volar aspect of his forearm sustained after a piece of glass broke in his hand. There is no evidence of tendinous injury and his neurovascular exam is normal. Which of the following is the best suture type and size to use for repair of this patient’s laceration?
englishExplanation:
Sutures are either absorbable or nonabsorbable. Within each category, there are monofilament and braided sutures. Typically, the smallest suture size used for procedures in the emergency department is 6-0 and the largest is 0-0. Careful consideration of a patient’s laceration including depth, width, tissue involved, location, and mechanism of injury dictates which suture and technique to use for closure. For superficial, linear lacerations to the volar forearm, a 4-0 or 5-0 nonabsorbable monofilament suture, such as polypropylene or nylon, should be used. For gaping or deep lacerations to this area, 4-0 absorbable sutures may be required for deeper closure. Nonabsorbable monofilament sutures should be removed in 7–10 days.



Poliglecaprone (A) is an absorbable monofilament suture that may be used for gaping wounds or lacerations to the volar forearm that require deeper closure.

Nylon (C) is a nonabsorbable monofilament suture and polyglactin (D) is a braided absorbable suture. A 6-0 suture would be too small for an extremity laceration. These would be more appropriate for certain facial lacerations.

Reveal Answer:
5 mg/kg (7 mg/kg with epinephrine).

question: A 25-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a laceration to his right leg sustained yesterday while working on a construction site. He did not want to leave work at the time, so went home overnight and presents for evaluation this afternoon. He reports no other injuries. On his right lateral lower leg, he has a 5 cm laceration with surrounding dried blood. After evaluating for foreign bodies, you ask the nurse to gather cleaning supplies. Which of the following solutions provides adequate wound cleansing to help prevent infection without damaging tissues?

options.text: Sterile normal saline plus povidone iodine

englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with an acute disruption of the skin, a very common concern in the emergency department. Wounds need to be well vascularized, free of devitalized tissue, clear of infection, and moist to allow for adequate healing. It is imperative for the emergency clinician to understand these requirements. First, wounds with devitalized tissue or contamination require debridement prior to further wound care. Wounds should also be evaluated for foreign material that needs to be removed. Irrigation of the wound should occur to remove loose material and decrease the bacterial load. All wounds are colonized with microbes, but not all wounds are infected. There is no high-level evidence to recommend one particular irrigant over another. The act of irrigation, the volume of irrigant, and the pressure used probably provide the biggest benefits. Normal saline is often used as an irrigant, but there are no significant differences in rates of infection when using clean tap water versus normal saline. Additionally, clean tap water does not damage healthy tissue. Therefore, this patient can be adequately managed with clean tap water.



Hydrogen peroxide (B) can actually damage the tissues and delay healing. It is not recommended as an irrigant in the emergency department.

Sterile normal saline plus chlorhexidine (C) is unnecessary and can also irritate the tissues. Although chlorhexidine has been considered less cytotoxic than other irrigant additives, some studies have shown delayed healing.

Sterile normal saline plus povidone iodine (D) has been considered bactericidal, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus. However, studies have shown delayed healing without decreased rates of infection.

One Step Further
Question:
What topical remedy has been used since ancient times for wound healing and has been shown to improve healing of superficial burns?

Reveal Answer:
Honey.

Sterile gloves unnecessary

No clear evidence that prophylactic antibiotics ↓ infection risk
Risk factors for infection
Peripheral vascular disease

Lidocaine with epinephrine
Contamination
Injury > 8 hours

الفخ: الخيار B hydrogen peroxide هو الفخ لأنه بيأذي الأنسجة وبيأخر الشفاء. والخيار C اللي فيه chlorhexidine زيادة مالها داعي وبيهيّج الأنسجة. وما تنسى إن أهم شي هو الري نفسه وحجمه والضغط اللي بتعمله.

question: An 8-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with a facial laceration after a fall. He has a 2-cm linear laceration extending vertically through his left lower lip, crossing the vermilion border. Which of the following is the most appropriate method of analgesia for his repair?
englishExplanation:
Facial lacerations are among the most common traumatic injuries treated in the emergency department, and adequate anesthesia is essential for proper wound preparation and repair. Three primary modalities exist: local infiltration, topical anesthetics, and regional nerve blocks. Local infiltration with lidocaine (with or without epinephrine) is the most commonly used method and is appropriate for most simple facial lacerations. Topical anesthetics such as LET gel (lidocaine 4%, epinephrine 0.1%, tetracaine 0.5%) are particularly valuable in pediatrics, as they eliminate the pain and anxiety associated with needle injections and are recommended as a first-line option for simple facial and scalp lacerations in children. Regional nerve blocks, including the supraorbital, infraorbital, and mental nerve blocks, are indicated when local infiltration would cause unacceptable tissue distortion (e.g., at the vermilion border or eyelid margin), when large wounds would require potentially toxic doses of local anesthetic, or when infiltration would be particularly painful. The mental nerve block is performed by everting the lower lip, identifying the mental foramen below the second premolar, and injecting 1–2 mL of local anesthetic (e.g., 0.25% bupivacaine or 1–2% lidocaine) after aspiration. [3-4] Contraindications to regional nerve blocks include local infection at the injection site, known allergy to the anesthetic agent, and distorted anatomy (e.g., from prior fractures). Contraindications to topical LET include application to mucous membranes and areas of end-arterial supply (nose, ears, digits, penis) due to the risk of epinephrine-induced vasoconstriction.

Complications of facial anesthesia are generally uncommon but include local anesthetic systemic toxicity from inadvertent intravascular injection or excessive dosing, allergic reactions, hematoma formation at the injection site, and temporary nerve injury. Aspiration before injection during nerve blocks is essential to prevent intravascular delivery. Topical LET has been associated with rare adverse effects, including mydriasis, when applied near the eye. Regional nerve blocks may fail to achieve complete anesthesia, while tissue distortion from local infiltration represents a significant practical limitation when repairing lacerations at cosmetically important areas, such as the vermilion border, hairline, or eyebrow. Each of these limitations should be considered when choosing a route of anesthesia for wound management.



While nitrous oxide (A) can reduce pain and anxiety during laceration repair in children, it provides anxiolysis and mild analgesia rather than true local anesthesia. It would be insufficient as the sole anesthetic for suturing a through-and-through lip laceration and does not address the need to avoid tissue distortion at the vermilion border.

Although local lidocaine with epinephrine (B) is the most commonly used method for facial lacerations in general, local infiltration at the vermilion border causes tissue edema and distortion that obscures the precise skin-vermilion junction, making accurate alignment and cosmetically optimal repair significantly more difficult.

Topical lidocaine-epinephrine-tetracaine gel (D) is an excellent first-line topical anesthetic for simple pediatric facial and scalp lacerations. However, it is contraindicated for mucous membranes, and a laceration that crosses the vermilion border involves the mucosal surface of the lip.

One Step Further
Question:
Why should benzocaine be avoided as a mucosal topical anesthetic in children?

Reveal Answer:
Due to its high risk of causing methemoglobinemia in children.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Facial and Dental Nerve Blocks

Supraorbital nerve: ipsilateral forehead and scalp
Infraorbital nerve: area between lower eyelid and upper lip
Posterior superior alveolar nerve: ipsilateral maxillary molars
Inferior alveolar nerve: ipsilateral mandibular teeth, lower lip, chin
Mental nerve: ipsilateral lower lip and chin

ليش: الجرح 2 cm عمودي بيمر على الـ vermilion border، وهاد المكان local infiltration بيسبب تشوّه واضح بالأنسجة. وكمان الحقن بالـ needle بيزعج الطفل، وفي هاد الحالة الـ regional nerve blocks هي الأنسب. الـ mental nerve block بتنعمل بإخراج الشفة السفلى وبتحديد الـ mental foramen تحت الـ second premolar، وبعدين بنحقن 1 لـ 2 mL من anesthetic بعد الـ aspiration.
الفخ: الخيار A local lidocaine مع epinephrine هو الأكثر شيوعاً، بس بيسبب تشوّه عند الـ vermilion border وبيزعج الطفل. أما الخيار D topical LET فهو أول خط للخدوش البسيطة بالوجه والـ scalp.

question: A 23-year-old man presents to the ED after getting into a fistfight with his friend. Examination shows a 4 cm laceration on the right side of his forehead. When asked to raise his eyebrows, he is only able to lift his left eyebrow. What is the most appropriate way to repair this wound?

options.text: Close with one layer of sutures
Close with two layers of sutures

correctAnswer: Close with two layers of sutures
englishExplanation:
The patient is presenting with a likely galeal laceration, which will need to be repaired separately from the superficial aspect of the wound. The layers of the scalp include subcutaneous tissue, galea aponeurosis, connective tissue, and periosteum overlying the bone.

The galea is a key anchoring structure of the frontalis muscle and, if disrupted, can lead to asymmetric contraction of that muscle. Identification can also be made with direct exploration of the wound. Galeal lacerations > 5 mm should be repaired with absorbable sutures. Repair of the galea will also prevent subgaleal infections, subgaleal hematomas, and improve cosmetic outcomes.



Closure with cyanoacrylate (A), also known as skin glue, should be reserved for minor superficial lacerations that are well approximated.

Closing with one layer of sutures (B) or applying staples (C) could be considered for closing the superficial skin of the laceration, but would not address the galeal injury underneath.

question: A 53-year-old man works as a metal fabricator in a local tool-and-die shop. While he was grinding a piece of iron, he felt something hit his eye. He flushed his eyes three times but still feels like there is something “in there.” Examination reveals severe left eye conjunctival injection, excessive tearing, and eyelid erythema. Which of the following stains is used in combination with slit lamp examination with blue filter?
englishExplanation:
Corneal abrasions occur when the corneal epithelium becomes disrupted. There are several causes, including dry eyes, foreign bodies (fingernails, animal paws, chips of wood or metal, and branches or leaves), and contact lens use. They usually heal on their own with no complications. The major symptoms are pain, foreign body sensation, photophobia, blurred vision, tearing, eyelid edema, conjunctival injection, difficulty opening the eye, and multiple patient attempts to wash out the eye. If suspected, initial evaluation requires the use of fluorescein and a slit lamp. If ocular penetration or retained foreign body is suspected, then order an ocular CT or MRI, depending on the metal content of the object. Fluorescein sodium-impregnated filter paper is commonly used in staining the eye to identify defects in the cornea. Fluorescein uptake occurs in areas of defects. This is performed using a blue light that will show the fluorescein as yellow-green in the area of defect.



Ammoniacal silver (A) is used in the study of fungal bone infections.

Rhodanine (C) is used to study copper deposits in tissue, such as liver tissue in a patient with Wilson disease.

Trichrome (D) staining is a basic procedure used in the histological study of tissues under a microscope.

One Step Further
Question:
What is a complication of corneal abrasion?

Reveal Answer:
Corneal ulcer with scarring.

Most are self-limiting

question: Which of the following best describes high frequency ultrasound transducers used for detecting soft tissue foreign bodies?

options.text: They are best at detecting deep foreign bodies and have the highest image resolution
They are best at detecting deep foreign bodies but have poor resolution
They are best at detecting shallow foreign bodies and have the highest image resolution
They are best at detecting shallow foreign bodies but have poor resolution

correctAnswer: They are best at detecting shallow foreign bodies and have the highest image resolution
englishExplanation:
Bedside ultrasonography is a useful tool in detecting soft tissue foreign bodies that may be missed by conventional radiography. They are also useful in guiding removal of those foreign bodies once diagnosed. The frequency of the ultrasound transducer affects the likelihood of being able to detect a foreign body. Higher frequency transducers have a reduced depth of penetration and are best for detecting shallow foreign bodies. While a 12.5 MHz transducer can detect a foreign body at up to 2 cm in depth, a 3.5 MHz transducer can locate foreign bodies that are up to 10 cm deep. The resolution of the image is also affected by the transducer frequency. Higher frequencies allow for greater resolution of the image and are better at detecting small foreign bodies.



Low frequency transducers are best at detecting deep foreign bodies (A, B) but do not have the highest image resolution.

High frequency transducers are best at detecting shallow foreign bodies (D) but have good resolution.

One Step Further
Question:
What are the advantages of a phased array transducer?

Reveal Answer:
It provides a smaller footprint than a curved linear array probe and offers excellent image quality for evaluation of moving structures (e.g., heart).

question: A fully vaccinated 4-month-old infant presents to the ED after a dog bite. The infant’s parents state that the dog became agitated after the infant picked up its toy and bit the infant’s arm. On examination, you see several puncture wounds on the left upper arm and a complex laceration on the infant’s face. A CT of the facial bones and a plain film of the arm are obtained and are negative for acute fractures. Which of the following represents the best next step in care, in addition to wound irrigation and antibiotic prophylaxis?
englishExplanation:
This infant has sustained a puncture wound that is potentially contaminated with a neurotoxin called Clostridium tetani. Clostridium spores are ubiquitous in the environment and can contaminate wounds, placing those who are unimmunized or underimmunized at risk for tetanus. Tetanus is a clinical diagnosis that can present as localized muscle spasms in the area near the injury, trismus, facial muscle spasms, or even generalized muscle spasms. DTaP vaccination is typically administered at ages 2, 4, and 6 months, between 15 and 18 months, and between 4 and 6 years.

This infant, while fully vaccinated for their age, would have only received a total of two DTaP vaccines. Having received fewer than three doses of DTaP means this infant is underimmunized, so treatment with DTaP plus tetanus immune globulin would be required. Furthermore, this wound should be considered contaminated, given that it is a puncture wound. Crush, burn, frostbite, and projectile wounds should also be considered contaminated and at higher risk.



DTaP vaccination alone (B) would not be appropriate for a puncture wound in a patient who has received fewer than three tetanus vaccinations.

Td vaccination (C), which only protects against tetanus and diphtheria, is a booster administered to children > 7 years old and who have previously received Tdap vaccination.

Tdap (D) vaccination is administered to children > 7 years old. This formulation has a full dose of the tetanus vaccine but smaller doses of diphtheria and pertussis. It is only appropriate to use for vaccination in those who have already received the full DTaP series.

One Step Further

Reveal Answer:
Metronidazole or penicillin for 10–14 days.
