question: A 3-year-old boy presents to the emergency department after a dog bite. He tried to “ride” a new family dog while it was eating and it bit him on the head. He has a 1 cm gaping laceration to his scalp that is just through the dermis. You decide to treat with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid and prepare for wound closure. Which of the following is the best choice for initial pain control in this patient?
englishExplanation:
Controlling pain during a minor procedure improves patient compliance and reduces the need for further sedation, allowing for a more optimal cosmetic repair. It also improves parental satisfaction and reduces anxiety in children for future visits. There are a number of needle-free options to reduce pain during a procedure. Additional methods, including behavioral (e.g., distraction, positioning, positive reinforcement) or pharmacologic sedation (e.g., nitrous oxide, intranasal midazolam), can be used to augment topical anesthesia when needed. The needle-free method that should be used depends on whether the skin is intact or broken. For lacerations < 5 cm in length, initial pain control should be with a topical lidocaine-epinephrine-tetracaine cream. This topical cream does not always provide complete analgesia but helps to reduce the pain of local infiltration when needed. When augmented, 1% buffered lidocaine is recommended. Lidocaine-epinephrine-tetracaine cream works best on children and on the face and should not be used near mucous membranes.



Injected 1% lidocaine with epinephrine (A) will provide adequate analgesia. However, it will result in significant pain and anxiety in the patient, which frequently produces a suboptimal situation for proper wound closure.

A needle-free lidocaine delivery system (B) uses compressed gas to deliver subdermal lidocaine over intact skin, not a laceration.

Vapocoolant spray (D) may desensitize intact skin just prior to venipuncture, IV placement, or an intramuscular injection but should not be used on a laceration.

One Step Further

What is the treatment for lidocaine toxicity besides supportive care and dysrhythmia management?

Reveal Answer:
20% lipid emulsion therapy.

الفخ: الخيار A injected 1% lidocaine مع epinephrine بيعطي تسكين كافي، بس بيألم الطفل وبيخليه anxious وهاد بيخرب الخياطة. والخيار B needle-free system بتستعمل فوق جلد سليم، وهنا الجلد مفتوح.

question: A 4-year-old girl presents to the emergency department after being bitten in the face by a family dog. She has two linear but irregular and gaping lacerations on her left cheek. There is no evidence of eye or nerve injury. Which of the following is the most appropriate choice of suture material for wound closure in this patient?
englishExplanation:
Well-chosen suture material can result in superior wound closure, decreased risk of infection, and decreased trauma to children when absorbable material is appropriate. Each suture material has a set of properties, including structure (e.g., braided or monofilament), tissue reactivity, tensile strength, elasticity, memory, and absorbability. Absorbable materials also vary in the time expected to maintain tensile strength. This depends, in part, on the size of the suture, with smaller numbers indicating thicker suture material. Braided material increases the risk of infection because it can harbor bacteria between strands and should only be used in wounds that are at low risk for infection. In general, animal bites should not be closed due to the high risk of infection, except for cosmetic areas such as the face.

Primary skin closure of the face is best performed using nylon, as this is a monofilament that has extremely low tissue reactivity. It has good tensile strength but is not absorbable and has inferior knot security, needing four or five ties to secure one knot. Good alternatives on the face are polypropylene, fast-absorbing gut, or polyglactin 910 irradiated. Sizes recommended on the face include 5-0 and 6-0 material, with thicker material for absorbable sutures, as thinner absorbable sutures have poor tensile strength and are more likely to cause wound dehiscence. Polypropylene has similar properties to nylon. Fast-absorbing gut is an older material that is absorbable within 7–10 days, but causes more tissue reaction and has poor tensile strength. Polyglactin 910 irradiated is also absorbable within 5–7 days and has good tensile strength, but it is braided. Absorbable sutures still in place after 7 days should be removed, as any suture material left in place for > 10 days will cause additional scarring.



Chromic gut (A) is similar to fast-absorbing gut but has a longer half-life and would likely need to be removed, making it a suboptimal choice for an absorbable suture in this case.

Polyglactin 910 (C) is appropriate to use for deep sutures on the face, but should not be used superficially on the face with a wound at high risk of infection, as it is braided and has a half-life of 28 days.

Polyglactin 910 irradiated (D) is absorbable and has a shorter half-life than polyglactin 910, so it is appropriate for use on the face, but it is braided and should not be used in wounds at high risk for infection, such as a dog bite.

Reveal Answer:

question: A 5-year-old child presents to the emergency department with his parents after hitting his head on a table 30 minutes prior to arrival. His parents are holding a towel on the child's head to stop the bleeding. There was no loss of consciousness, and the child is acting himself. Vital signs include a BP of 100/58 mm Hg, HR of 106 bpm, RR of 19/minute, and a T of 98.7°F. Physical examination reveals a gaping 4 cm linear laceration on the posterior scalp that is actively bleeding. The child needs to be sedated in order to repair the laceration, and the parents would prefer to not have to return for suture removal. Which of the following suture materials is most appropriate for wound closure?
englishExplanation:
Absorbable sutures, such as Vicryl, are degradable and lose strength in < 60 days. Absorbable sutures are generally used for subcutaneous (i.e., skin) and mucosal closures. Their highly reactive nature allows them to be broken down and absorbed over days to weeks. these do not need to be removed

Vicryl is an absorbable braided polymer of lactide and glycolide with low reactivity, good knot security, and fair tensile strength, making it suitable for mucosa and skin, especially of the scalp, trunk, extremities, and face. Absorbable sutures do not need to be removed, so are ideal when removal would be difficult, such as lacerations under casts, for children, and for those who require sedation for initial wound closure. Vicryl typically holds for 7–10 days.





Dacron (A), nylon (B), prolene (C), and silk (D) sutures are nonabsorbable and would require the child in this scenario to attend a follow-up for removal of the sutures. This is not ideal for the patient in this scenario as he required sedation for initial laceration repair.

question: What type of suture is most appropriate to reduce wound edge punctures, tension, and risk of necrosis on a volar hand laceration that has poor circulation at the wound edges?
englishExplanation:
Sutures are a strong way to close wounds and allow for the best approximation of the wound edges. The ideal suture type for wound closure depends on the type of wound; each has its advantages and disadvantages. Horizontal mattress sutures are a good choice for wounds in which poor circulation to the wound edge and risk of skin necrosis are concerns, like on the volar surface of the hand. With horizontal mattress sutures, the needle is inserted 5–10 mm from the wound edge, passes through the base of the wound, and exits 5–10 mm from the edge of the wound on the other side. The needle is then inserted again on the same side of the exit, at about 5 mm parallel to the first throw, and comes out 5 mm from the initial entry point. The wound is pulled closed, and the suture is tied on one side of the wound.



While continuous subcuticular (A) sutures reduce tension on the surface of the wound, these sutures pass through the dermal-epidermal junction, which is technically difficult in the thin skin of the volar hand. Horizontal mattress sutures are more appropriate in this location.

Simple interrupted (C) sutures and vertical mattress (D) sutures might strangulate the tissues in this low perfusion area.

question: An 18-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a large laceration to his left knee extending across the joint. The laceration is repaired primarily in the ED. Discharge instructions should include suture removal within which of the following time periods?
englishExplanation:
Proper wound closure not only restores skin integrity, but also helps fight against infection, scarring, and functional impairment. Lacerations may be closed primarily with sutures, staples, adhesive tapes, tissue adhesives, or hair apposition. When sutures are placed, the location of the laceration helps determine the time period during which sutures should remain in place. It is important to discuss follow-up care with patients prior to discharge so they understand when to return for suture removal and wound examination. Sutures placed to repair lacerations that cross major joints (e.g., knee, elbow) should be removed after 10–14 days. These lacerations are under high tension both at rest and during motion and require a longer duration for appropriate tissue healing.



Facial sutures should be removed within 3–5 days (C) to preserve cosmesis.

A period of 7–10 days (D) is recommended for sutures to remain in place in most other locations.

Only retention sutures (i.e., those placed to provide tension reduction to the primary suture line) may remain for up to 21–30 days (B).

ليش: هاد الجرح كبير وبيعدّي على الـ knee يعني مفصل رئيسي. الخيوط بمكانها بتحدد وقت النزع، والخيوط اللي بتعبر مفاصل كبيرة بتكون تحت شد عالي وقت الراحة وأثناء الحركة فبتحتاج وقت أطول عشان الأنسجة تشفى. علشان كده لازم تنزّع الخيوط بعد 10 لـ 14 يوم، أما الوجه فـ 3 لـ 5 أيام، وأغلب الأماكن التانية 7 لـ 10 أيام.
الفخ: الخيار D 7 لـ 10 أيام هو للمكان التانية، والخيار C 3 لـ 5 أيام للوجه بس. والخيار B 21 لـ 30 يوم بيخص الخيوط اللي بتعمل tension reduction على خط الخياطة الأساسي.

question:
Which of the following is TRUE with respect to 
sutures?

options.text: Tensile strength increases with the gauge size of

englishExplanation:
1.  The answer is A. (Chapter 41) The use of absorbable 
verses nonabsorbable suture material for percutaneous 
repairs in the emergency department for most cases is clinically irrelevant. The use of absorbable suture material can 
be especially helpful in children who might be traumatized 
by manipulating the wound again to remove the sutures. 
Nonabsorbable sutures retain their tensile strength for 
60 days, whereas absorbable sutures lose most of their tensile strength in less than 60 days. Thinner suture material 
is generally preferred over larger-diameter suture material 
as it produces less damage to tissues and leaves a smaller 
hole in the skin. The higher the gauge size, the lower the 
tensile strength of the suture material.

![Tintinalli-2023-00063 source page 40](images/Tintinalli-2023-00063-Tintinalli-2023-p0040.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00063 source page 43](images/Tintinalli-2023-00063-Tintinalli-2023-p0043.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: السؤال بيسألك إيش الصح عن الخيوط، والجواب A. لأغلب الحالات، الفرق بين absorbable و nonabsorbable بالـ ED عملياً ما بيفرق كتير. لسه الـ absorbable مفيدة بشكل واضح عند الأطفال لأنهم ما بيحتاجوا يشيلوا الخيوط والخياطة ما بتتمزق مرة ثانية، والخيوط nonabsorbable بتحتفظ بقوة tensile 60 يوم بينما الـ absorbable بتخسر معظم قوتها بأقل من 60 يوم. وبالنسبة للحجم، الخيط الرفيع أفضل لأنه بيعمل ضرر أقل بالأنسجة وبيسوي ثقب أصغر.
الفخ: الخيار B اللي بيقول larger-diameter أفضل، بالعكس تماماً؛ الخيط الرفيع بيعمل ضرر أقل وبيسوي ثقب أصغر بالجلد. وكلما زاد الـ gauge size قلّت tensile strength، فالـ 6-0 أرقّ وأضعف من الـ 4-0.

question:
Which of the following is TRUE with respect to 
wound location and infection risk?

options.text: Highly vascular areas have low risk of infection
There is conclusive evidence to support the use
Highest baseline skin bacterial counts are found
Facial and scalp wounds with heavy contamination have a low rate of infection regardless of

correctAnswer: Facial and scalp wounds with heavy contamination have a low rate of infection regardless of
englishExplanation:
2.  The answer is D.  (Chapters 39 and 42) Due to their 
vascularity, scalp and facial wounds have a very low infection rate, degree of cleaning has not been shown to have 
an impact on this rate. In fact, in resource poor situations, 
facial and scalp wounds have been repaired with adhesive 
strips without prior cleaning and irrigation. Fecal contamination is always associated with a high risk of infection. 
Lowest baseline skin bacterial counts are on the upper arms, 
legs, and torso; highest are in moist areas such as axilla, 
perineum, intertriginous areas, and toe web spaces. Oral 
antibiotics while traditionally recommended for intraoral 
lacerations have inconclusive evidence to support their use.

![Tintinalli-2023-00064 source page 40](images/Tintinalli-2023-00064-Tintinalli-2023-p0040.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00064 source page 43](images/Tintinalli-2023-00064-Tintinalli-2023-p0043.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإجابة D صحيحة لأن جروح الـ scalp والوجه عندها نسبة عدوى قليلة جداً بسبب الـ vascularity الكثيرة. يعني حتى لو الجرح ملوث كتير، معدل العدوى بيبقى منخفض. ودرجة التنظيف ما أثبتت إنها بتأثر على هاد المعدد أبداً. حتى بمشاهد قليلة موارد، الناس كانوا بيرمموا جروح الوجه والـ scalp بـ adhesive strips بدون تنظيف ولا irrigation. وبالمقابل، التلوث بالبراز (fecal contamination) دايماً بييجي مع خطر عدوى عالي.
الفخ: الناس بتختار B لأنهم بيحسوا إنه في أدلة قاطعة على benefit الـ antibiotics، بس هاي الأدلة inconclusive مو conclusive. وC غلط لأن أعلى baseline counts للجلد بتكون بالمناطق الرطبة مثل الـ axilla والـ perineum، مو بالوجه اللي نسبته منخفضة أصلاً.

question:
Which of the following is the MOST IMPORTANT 
part of hand examination prior to administration of 
anesthesia?

options.text: Two-point sensation of hands and fingers
Quality of pulses distal to injury

correctAnswer: Two-point sensation of hands and fingers
englishExplanation:
3.  The answer is C. (Chapters 40 and 43) All represent 
important parts of the examination that should be completed prior to anesthesia. Complete evaluation of sensation including two-point discrimination should always 
be accomplished prior to initiation of anesthesia. Normal 
two-point discrimination is less than 6 mm. Motor function may be impaired by pain from the injury and better assessed afterwards. Distal pulses and capillary refill 
should not be affected by anesthetic application proximal 
to the wound. Be sure to assess tendons after anesthetizing the wound. The patient may have tendon function but 
have a tendon injury that you would not be able to detect 
without visualizing the tendon through the wound opening throughout the range of motion.

![Tintinalli-2023-00065 source page 40](images/Tintinalli-2023-00065-Tintinalli-2023-p0040.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00065 source page 43](images/Tintinalli-2023-00065-Tintinalli-2023-p0043.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لازم تعمل تقييم كامل للـ sensation، ومن ضمنه two-point discrimination، قبل ما تبدأ تعطي anesthesia. لأنه إذا وضعت anesthesia قبل الفحص، مش بتقدر تعرف إذا فيه nerve injury ولا لأ. الـ normal two-point discrimination أقل من 6 mm. ولازم تخلّي الفحص كله مكتمل قبل ما تبدأ، وكمان الـ motor function ممكن تتأثر من الألم نفسه فالأفضل تقيّمها بعد التخدير.
الفخ: الخيار B هو اللي الناس بتختاره لأنه بيشتكي عن الوتر والحركة، بس الـ motor function قد تتأثر بالألم نفسه فالأفضل تقيّمها بعد التخدير. والـ distal pulses والـ capillary refill ما بتتأثر من anesthetic واقف proximal للجرح.

question:
A 40-year-old right-hand dominant man presents 
with curvilinear puncture wounds over his fourth and 
fifth metacarpal phalangeal joints on his right hand. 
Which of the following organisms are you concerned 
about and want to make sure antibiotics you prescribe 
will cover?
englishExplanation:
4.  The answer is A. (Chapter 43) The scenario describes 
the classic “fight bite” or puncture wounds/lacerations 
caused by striking another person’s teeth with a clenched 
fist, Eikenella is the organism of concern and amoxicillin/clavulanate would be antibiotic of choice. Pasturella 
would be primary concern for animal bites and again 
amoxicillin/clavulanate would be agent of choice. Pseudomonas would be of concern for puncture through a shoe 
or fresh water contamination and ciprofloxacin or other 
antipseudomonal coverage would be needed. Staph aureus 
remains the concern for skin source infection, and firstgeneration cephalosporin or other beta-lactam is first-line 
agent despite methicillin resistance increasing prevalence.

![Tintinalli-2023-00066 source page 40](images/Tintinalli-2023-00066-Tintinalli-2023-p0040.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00066 source page 43](images/Tintinalli-2023-00066-Tintinalli-2023-p0043.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد بالضبط fight bite الكلاسيكي، يعني شخص ضرب سنون واحد تاني بإيده مقفولة، والخنجر طلع فوق مفاصل الـ metacarpophalangeal. البكتيريا اللي لازم تخاف منها هي Eikenella. والـ antibiotic of choice هو amoxicillin/clavulanate لأنه بغطي Eikenella مع Pasteurella بنفس الوقت. وبالمقابل، Pasteurella هي concern الأساسي مع لدغات وعضّات الحيوانات، و Pseudomonas بت concern مع puncture من خلال حذاء أو تلوث بماء عذب، و Staph aureus بتخص إصابات مصدرها الجلد والـ first-generation cephalosporin هو first-line فيها.
الفخ: الناس بتختار B (Pasteurella) لأنها أشهر بكتيرا، بس هاي بتخص لدغات وعضّات الحيوانات مو سنون الإنسان. وD (Staph aureus) بتخص إصابات مصدرها الجلد، وC (Pseudomonas) بتخص وخز الإبر من خلال حذاء.

question: In which of the following situations would cyanoacrylate be LEAST EFFECTIVE for closing a wound?

options.text: Superficial wound oriented parallel to line of

englishExplanation:
7.  The answer is D. (Chapter 41) Cyanoacrylate is similar 
to 4-0 absorbable subcuticular sutures in strength but not 
as strong as staples. It is well suited for superficial lacerations under low tension. Works well for children’s facial 
lacerations that are easily approximated, as it does not 
require removal, generally sloughing off in 5 to 10 days. 
It forms its own bio-occlusive dressing. It can be used in 
conjunction with paper tape closures for added strength 
to thin layer skin closures. It is not well served for closing 
areas of high skin tension, widely gaping wounds, or areas 
of varying tension such as over joints.

![Tintinalli-2023-00069 source page 41](images/Tintinalli-2023-00069-Tintinalli-2023-p0041.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00069 source page 43](images/Tintinalli-2023-00069-Tintinalli-2023-p0043.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ cyanoacrylate قوته قريبة من 4-0 absorbable subcuticular sutures، بس مش قوية مثل الـ staples. هي ممتازة للجرح السطحي اللي التوتر فيه قليل. وبالذات لجروح وجه الأطفال اللي سهلة التقريب، لأنها ما بتحتاج شيل وبيتساقط لوحدها خلال 5 لـ 10 أيام. بتشتغل كـ bio-occlusive dressing لوحدها، وبتقدر تجمعها مع paper tape closures لزيادة القوة. بس ما بتنفع areas فيها شد عالي، ولا الجرح اللي فراغه واسع، وكمان ما بتنفع بالمناطق اللي التوتر فيها متغير زي فوق المفاصل.
الفخ: A و B بيخلّوك تفتكر إنها مناسبة للأطفال والجرح البسيط، وهي فعلاً كذلك. السؤال asks LEAST effective، فاللي بيبقى ضعيف هو الجرح اللي التوتر فيه متغير، مو الجرح السهل.

question:
What is the BEST WAY to repair laceration shown in 
Figure 4.1?

options.text: Close skin layer only with 6-0 nonabsorbable

correctAnswer: Close skin layer only with 6-0 nonabsorbable
englishExplanation:
9.  The answer is A. (Chapter 42) Auricular lacerations 
involving the cartilage often can be closed in the emergency department by simply closing the overlying skin 
with interrupted 6-0 nonabsorbable sutures. Care should 
be taken to include the thin layer of perichondrium when 
placing skin sutures, as well as ensuring any loose cartilage 
fragments are kept in place for possible later reconstruction 
if needed. This will provide adequate support for cartilage 
healing. Skin should not be cut nor should loose pieces of 
cartilage removed. An auricular pressure dressing should 
be applied for 24 hours and rechecked to ensure there is no 
hematoma development that may cause ear deformation 
from cartilage damage in the healing process. If hematoma develops, sutures are removed hematoma drained, 
resutured, and pressure reapplied with another recheck in 
24 hours. Very complex lacerations, those extending 
into the canal, significant tissue loss, or involvement of 
the tympanic membrane are best referred to a specialist 
(Figure 4.3).

![Tintinalli-2023-00071 source page 41](images/Tintinalli-2023-00071-Tintinalli-2023-p0041.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00071 source page 44](images/Tintinalli-2023-00071-Tintinalli-2023-p0044.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ auricular lacerations اللي فيها cartilage غالباً بتتقفل في الـ ED، بس يكفي إنك تقفل الـ skin فوقها بـ interrupted 6-0 nonabsorbable sutures. لازم تنتبه إنك تضم الـ thin layer of perichondrium مع الخياطة، وأي pieces of cartilage loose لازم تخلّيها بالبلاصة. الـ skin ما بتقطعه، والـ cartilage ما بتشيله. وبتحط auricular pressure dressing لمدة 24 ساعة وبعدها تعيد الفحص، لأنه الـ hematoma ممكن يصير deformation للأذن.
الفخ: B (debride the skin edges) و C (remove loose pieces of cartilage) الناس بتختارهم لأنهم بيحسوا إنه تنظيف أفضل، بس هاد بيفضح الـ cartilage ويخلي الأذن تتشوّه. و D (two-layer closure) مش لازم من غير ما يكون فيه داعي.

question:
A 28-year-old man has sustained a laceration from 
a knife to his left cheek 3 cm anterior to the earlobe 
attachment and just inferior to the zygoma. Which of 
the following should raise suspicion of parotid duct 
injury?

options.text: Sensory loss in the V2 branch of the trigeminal

englishExplanation:
10.  The answer is A. (Chapter 42) A branch of the facial 
artery along with the buccal branch of the facial nerve 
travel with the parotid duct. The presence of arterial 
bleeding or paralysis of the cheek should raise significant 
concern with any injury occurring in a zone posterior to 
a line drawn vertically through the lateral canthus and 
inferiorly to a line drawn from frenulum to tragus. See 
Figure 4.4. Ptosis of the upper lid would be from injury to 
oculomotor nerve, and the lower lid is innervated from 
zygomatic branch of the facial nerve. Mandibular branch 
(V2) of the trigeminal nerve travels above the zygoma.
FIGURE 4.3  Reproduced with permission from J.E. Tintinalli, J.S. Stapczynski, O.J. Ma, 
D. Yealy, G.D. Meckler, D.M. Cline: Tintinalli’s Emergency Medicine: A Comprehensive Study 
Guide, 9th Edition. McGraw-Hill Education; 2020.

![Tintinalli-2023-00072 source page 41](images/Tintinalli-2023-00072-Tintinalli-2023-p0041.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00072 source page 44](images/Tintinalli-2023-00072-Tintinalli-2023-p0044.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ parotid duct بيسير معاه branch من الـ facial artery ومعاه الـ buccal branch من الـ facial nerve. يعني إذا شفت نزيف شرياني أو شلل بالخد، لازم تشك بإ injury في الـ parotid duct. المنطقة الخطرة هي أي منطقة posterior، يعني خلف خط عمودي من الـ lateral canthus، وتحت خط من الـ frenulum للـ tragus. والمريض عنده جرح 3 cm قدام-earlobe وتحت الـ zygoma، يعني جوّات هالمنطقة.
الفخ: C (ptosis) بتوهمك إنه الـ facial nerve، بس الجفن العلوي بيتعصب من الـ oculomotor nerve. أما الـ lower eyelid في عصبه الـ zygomatic branch من الـ facial nerve، والـ V2 branch من الـ trigeminal nerve بيسير فوق الـ zygoma.

question:
You are staffing a small critical access hospital. A distal 
fingertip amputation less than 1 cm2 in an 11-year-old 
child is noted on examination. There is no involvement of the nail bed and no exposed bone. Which of 
the following is the recommended treatment?

options.text: Immediate transfer to tertiary care center 3 hours
Healing by secondary intent with nonadherent
Replacement of the amputated tip as a fullthickness skin graft after defatting and cleaning

correctAnswer: Healing by secondary intent with nonadherent
englishExplanation:
11.  The answer is B.  (Chapter 43) Healing by secondary intent is the preferred method of treatment with 
better cosmetic appearance, sensation, and functional 
outcomes. Daily cleaning, soaks, and dressing change is 
all that is needed when no bone is exposed and nail bed is 
intact especially for wounds 1 cm2 or less in size. The use 
of defatted amputated tissue as a full-thickness graft may 
be helpful for larger tissue defects. The flap may develop 
necrosis and fall of as the underling tissues heal. V-Y flap, 
generally done by the hand surgeon, may be used in closing an amputation through the nail bed with exposed tuft. 
This will require shorting of the bone with the use of a 
rongeur to adequately cover the defect.

![Tintinalli-2023-00073 source page 41](images/Tintinalli-2023-00073-Tintinalli-2023-p0041.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00073 source page 44](images/Tintinalli-2023-00073-Tintinalli-2023-p0044.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ healing by secondary intent هي الطريقة المفضلة، لأنها بتطلع بنتيجة تجميلية أحسن و sensation و function أحسن من الـ graft. كل اللي تحتاجه هو تنظيف يومي و soaks وتغيير للضمادات. هاد بكفي بشكل خاص لما ما في exposed bone والـ nail bed سالم، وكمان للجرح اللي مساحته 1 cm² أو أقل. فالـ patient 11 سنة، ما في bone ولا nail bed، يعني هاد هو الخيار.
الفخ: C (استخدام النص المقطوع كـ full-thickness graft) ممكن بس نافع مع defects أكبر، و D (V-Y flap) بيعمله الـ hand surgeon لما الـ amputation يمر بالـ nail bed مع exposed tuft وهنا ما في. و A (تحويل فوري) مش لازم.

question:
A partial flexor tendon injury is identified on a 
volar hand laceration affecting the palm of the hand. 
The patient is able to flex all digits at the metacarpophalangeal, proximal interphalangeal, and distal 
interphalangeal joints. Which of the following is the 
MOST APPROPRIATE management?

options.text: Hand surgeon consultation for follow-up in 2 to
Primary wound closure after tendon repair by
Superficial laceration repair with 4 weeks of position of function splinting

correctAnswer: Hand surgeon consultation for follow-up in 2 to
englishExplanation:
12.  The answer is A. (Chapter 43) Most hand surgeons 
prefer to repair full-thickness flexor tendon injuries 
within 24 hours. If delayed, they should be seen within 
2 to 3 days for repair within 7 days, beyond 10 to 14 days 
post injury scaring and tendon retraction complicate 
repair. Splinting should be done with flexion at the wrist 
and metacarpophalangeal joint and extension at distal and 
proximal interphalangeal joints. Partial flexor tendon injuries should be seen by a hand surgeon for timely follow-up 
and may require repair, especially flexor digitorum superficialis that may cause trigger finger if unrepaired. And 
experienced emergency physician may undertake repair 
of partial or complete extensor tendon lacerations on the 
dorsum of the hand located between the distal wrist and 
metacarpophalangeal joint.
FIGURE 4.4  Reproduced with permission from J.E. Tintinalli, J.S. Stapczynski, O.J. Ma, 
D. Yealy, G.D. Meckler, D.M. Cline: Tintinalli’s Emergency Medicine: A Comprehensive Study 
Guide, 9th Edition. McGraw-Hill Education; 2020.

32
TINTINALLI’S EMERGENCY MEDICINE EXAMINATION AND BOARD REVIEW, 9TH EDITION

![Tintinalli-2023-00074 source page 41](images/Tintinalli-2023-00074-Tintinalli-2023-p0041.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00074 source page 44](images/Tintinalli-2023-00074-Tintinalli-2023-p0044.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00074 source page 45](images/Tintinalli-2023-00074-Tintinalli-2023-p0045.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أغلب جراحي اليد بيفضلوا يصلحوا الـ full-thickness flexor tendon injuries خلال 24 ساعة، وإذا تأخر لازم يشوفوا المريض خلال 2 لـ 3 أيام للإصلاح خلال 7 أيام. لأنه بعد 10 لـ 14 يوم بتظهر الـ scarring والـ tendon retraction وبتعقّد الإصلاح. والـ partial flexor tendon injuries لازم يتابعها جراح يد بسرعة، وممكن تحتاج إصلاح خاصة لو أصاب flexor digitorum superficialis لأن هاد ممكن يصير trigger finger. ولازم تعمل splinting بـ flexion للـ wrist والمفاصل مع extension للـ interphalangeal.
الفخ: C (إغلاق الجرح بعد إصلاح الـ tendon) مش لازم لأن الـ injury جزئي وممكن يلتئم من غير تدخل. و D (أربع أسابيع من الـ position of function splinting) تخص الـ superficial lacerations مو إصابات الـ flexor tendon.

question:
Which of the following could aid in the detection of a 
joint capsule laceration of the knee?

options.text: Fluorescein saline injection into the wound to
Methylene blue injection into joint capsule
Saline load test of joint capsule

correctAnswer: Saline load test of joint capsule
englishExplanation:
13.  The answer is D.  (Chapter 44) Articular capsule 
lacerations are extremely difficult to detect on examination. Gas in a joint space on a plain radiograph is diagnostic. When gas is not present, saline load test is the 
best method of determining joint integrity. Injection of 
enough saline into the joint space to demonstrate leakage 
into the wound is a positive test, and false negative may 
occur if too little saline is injected. Installation of 60 to 
100 mL of saline into the knee joint may be required 
to avoid a false-negative test. Fluorescein may be added 
to saline injected to aid in detection, and methylene blue 
should not be added as it does not add accuracy and will 
cause staining of joint structures complicating intraoperative repair of intra-articular injuries.

![Tintinalli-2023-00075 source page 41](images/Tintinalli-2023-00075-Tintinalli-2023-p0041.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00075 source page 42](images/Tintinalli-2023-00075-Tintinalli-2023-p0042.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00075 source page 45](images/Tintinalli-2023-00075-Tintinalli-2023-p0045.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: كشف الـ articular capsule lacerations صعب جداً بالفحص العادي. إذا لقيت gas بالـ joint space على plain radiograph، هاد بيكفي للتشخيص. وإذا ما في gas، أحسن طريقة تبيّن سلامة الـ joint هي saline load test. بتحقن saline كفاية داخل الـ joint space لحد ما تشوف تسريب داخل الجرح، وهاد بيجي test positive. ولازم تحقن 60 لـ 100 mL من الـ saline عشان تتجنب الـ false negative.
الفخ: B (methylene blue) الناس بتختاره لأنهم بيحسوا بيساعد بالكشف، بس ما بيزود الدقة وبيصبّغ الـ joint structures، وهاد بيعقّد الإصلاح الجراحي للـ intra-articular injuries. و A (fluorescein) ممكن ينضاف للـ saline بس هو بيساعد بس.

question:
Which of the following will LIKELY yield a false 
negative for detection of an Achilles tendon 
laceration?
englishExplanation:
14.  The answer is A.  (Chapter 44) Direct examination 
and exploration as the foot is put through range of motion 
is good method for detecting lacerations, a “catch” may 
be felt for partial tendon injury. Ultrasound allows direct 
examination of the entire tendon. Thompson test, squeezing the calf as the patient lies prone with the knee bent and 
lower leg up should produce plantar flexion, comparing 
to the opposite side may help detect subtle injuries. Active 
plantar flexion may yield a false negative as the tibialis 
posterior muscle also plantar flexes the foot at the ankle.

![Tintinalli-2023-00076 source page 42](images/Tintinalli-2023-00076-Tintinalli-2023-p0042.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00076 source page 45](images/Tintinalli-2023-00076-Tintinalli-2023-p0045.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ direct examination مع exploration للمشاية خلال الـ range of motion طريقة كويسة لكشف الـ lacerations، وممكن تحس بـ catch إذا كانت الـ injury جزئية. والـ ultrasound بيكشف الـ tendon كله بشكل مباشر. والـ Thompson test، يعني تعصر الـ calf والمريض مستني على كرشه ورجله مرفوعة، لازم يعطي plantar flexion، وتقارن مع الجهة الثانية عشان تكتشف الـ subtle injuries. بس الـ active plantar flexion ممكن تعطي false negative، لأن الـ tibialis posterior muscle بيعمل plantar flexion كمان للقدم عند الـ ankle.
الفخ: C (Thompson test) هي أكثر اختبار الناس بتثق فيه، بس السؤال asks أي اختبار LIKELY يعطي false negative. الـ tibialis posterior بيعمل الحركة نفسها، فبتحس إن القدم تتحرك بالشكل الطبيعي وإنت فاكر إن الـ tendon سليم.

question:
Prophylactic use of which of the following classes 
of antibiotics may be used in immunosuppressed 
patients who are bitten by a dog?
englishExplanation:
17.  The answer is D.  (Chapter 46) Capnocytophaga 
infection is rare but rapidly progressive systemic illness 
in immunocompromised patients with dog bites. Patients 
with prior splenectomy, diabetes, immunosuppression, 
and alcoholics are at highest risk of this disease. Systemic 
illness may occur in the absence of local wound infection. Penicillin class antibiotics should be routinely considered for this group of patients. While lincomycin class 
(clindamycin) does cover Capnocytophaga, it does not 
provide adequate coverage of Pasturella and should not be 
used alone for dog and cat bites.

![Tintinalli-2023-00079 source page 42](images/Tintinalli-2023-00079-Tintinalli-2023-p0042.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00079 source page 45](images/Tintinalli-2023-00079-Tintinalli-2023-p0045.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: عدوى Capnocytophaga نادرة، بس بتكون systemic illness سريعة التقدم عند الـ immunocompromised مرضى لدغات الـ dog. أعلى خطورة عند اللي عندهم prior splenectomy أو diabetes أو immunosuppression أو alcoholics. وممكن يبان الـ systemic illness بدون أي wound infection موضعي. لازم دايماً تفكر بـ penicillin class antibiotic لهالمجموعة من المرضى، لأنه هي اللي بتغطي الـ Capnocytophaga بشكل كافي.
الفخ: A (clindamycin) هي الاختيار الشائع لأنها بتغطي Capnocytophaga، بس هي ما بتغطي Pasteurella كفاية، فما بتنفع لوحدها في لدغات الـ dog والـ cat. والـ penicillin class هي اللي لازم تتحسب لهالمجموعة.

question:
A 32-year-old female farmer sustained a laceration on 
a rusty nail protruding from a barn stall door while 
cleaning animal stalls. Last tetanus immunization was 
7 years ago. The patient reports a severe local reaction at 
that time with significant swelling and pain at the sight 
of injection. What is the APPROPRIATE management 
with respect to the concern for exposure to tetanus?

options.text: Administer tetanus toxoid and tetanus immune
Watch for signs of tetanus and treat if they

englishExplanation:
19.  The answer is A. (Chapter 47) Tetanus toxoid prophylaxis should be given if the patient has had primary (more 
than three doses) immunization more than 10 years previous for a clean wound or more than 5 years for a contaminated or high-risk wound. Tetanus immunoglobulin should 
be given for patient with high risk wound and incomplete 
(less than three doses) or no previous immunization with 
tetanus toxoid. Tetanus toxoid is only contraindicated for 
history of previous neurologic reaction or systemic reaction. Local reaction is common and not a contraindication 
to vaccination. Patients with history of severe local reaction 
often have a history of frequent previous vaccinations and 
have a high serum tetanus antitoxin level; they should not 
be vaccinated more frequently than every 10 years. Tetanus 
immunoglobulin should be given to patients with highrisk injuries that are contraindicated for tetanus toxoid.

![Tintinalli-2023-00081 source page 42](images/Tintinalli-2023-00081-Tintinalli-2023-p0042.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00081 source page 45](images/Tintinalli-2023-00081-Tintinalli-2023-p0045.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ tetanus toxoid prophylaxis بتتحسب إذا المريض كان خلص التطعيم الأساسي يعني أكثر من 3 جرعات، وكان من زمان: أكثر من 10 سنوات لجرح نظيف، أو أكثر من 5 سنوات لجرح ملوث أو high-risk. هون الجرح من nail صدئة وهو جرح ملوث، وآخر تطعيم 7 سنين، فالمفروض تعطي tetanus toxoid دلوقتي. والـ tetanus immunoglobulin بتتحسب للمريض اللي جرحه high risk وما خلص التطعيم الأساسي أو ما تلقى تطعيم خالص.
الفخ: الناس بتنسى إنه الحد 10 سنوات pertains للجرح النظيف، والجرح الملوث الحد 5 سنوات بس. وكمان الـ severe local reaction مو contraindication للتطعيم، واللي عنده تاريخ reactions شديدة غالباً عنده مستوى anti-tetanus عالي.

question:
A 57-year-old female with a history of hypertension presents with headache, mild confusion, 
and vomiting. She describes an acutely worsening global headache over the last several hours 
with nausea and vomiting. A family member states she is confused. She admits to 
noncompliance with her blood pressure medications for the last week. Vital signs are: T 98.4, HR 
92, BP 220/130, RR 20, SpO2 97%. Examination reveals a patient in moderate discomfort, 
papilledema, hypertensive retinopathy, and a non-focal neurologic examination. Laboratory 
studies, EKG, and noncontract CT brain are all normal. Which of the following is the most 
appropriate next step in management?
englishExplanation:
The patient has hypertensive encephalopathy. The history of acute headache with 
vomiting and confusion in the setting of severely elevated blood pressure is characteristic. 
Neuroimaging with CT scan is often normal. The treatment is immediate reduction of blood 
pressure by as much as 30%. By definition, hypertensive encephalopathy is reversible when 
blood pressure is reduced. Neurosurgical consultation may be indicated later in the course, but 
blood pressure management should be instituted early. Lumbar puncture would be 
contraindicated in this circumstance due to the papilledema indicating increased intracranial 
pressure. Corticosteroids are indicated in cases of temporal arteritis, which is on the differential 
diagnosis but is far less common than hypertensive encephalopathy and requires the presence 
of an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate. MRI of the brain can add important structural 
information but is not indicated emergently.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريضة عندها hypertensive encephalopathy. تاريخ صداع حاد مع vomiting و confusion مع ضغط 220/130، كل هاد بيوصف الحالة. الـ CT brain غالباً بيطلع طبيعي، وهاد بيشدّ على التشخيص. العلاج هو lowering فوري للضغط بنسبة توصل لـ 30%. وبالdefinition، الـ hypertensive encephalopathy بتنعكس لما ينزل الضغط، فبدّك تبدأ ضبط الضغط من أول. والـ neurosurgical consultation ممكن تتأجل لبعدين، بس إدارة الضغط لازم تبدأ بدري.
الفخ: D (corticosteroids) الناس بتختارها لأن الـ temporal arteritis جزء من الـ differential، بس هو أندر جداً ويحتاج elevated ESR. و C (lumbar puncture) contraindicated بسبب الـ papilledema، و E (MRI) مش طارئة.

question:
A 61-year-old male presents to the ED with a chief complaint of chest pain. His EKG is shown 
below. Which of the following is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Ectopic atrial rhythm in the low atria

englishExplanation:
The patient’s EKG appears to demonstrate an ectopic atrial rhythm with inverted P 
waves in lead II. However, the QRS axis is also flipped 180 degrees from normal. These findings 
indicate limb lead reversal. Specifically, the left leg and the right arm have been reversed. As a 
result, lead II becomes inverted, leads I and III become inverted and switch places, while leads 
aVR and aVF simply switch places. The only limb lead that is unaffected is aVL, which remains 
unchanged.

![subjects1200-c809b7af8302aa64 source page 5](images/subjects1200-c809b7af8302aa64-p0005.jpg)

![subjects1200-c809b7af8302aa64 source page 6](images/subjects1200-c809b7af8302aa64-p0006.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ EKG بيبيّن ectopic atrial rhythm مع inverted P waves في lead II، بس الـ QRS axis كمان مقلوب 180 درجة عن الطبيعي. هاد المزيج بينطابق على limb lead reversal، وتحديداً تبديل الـ left leg مع الـ right arm. وبسبب هاد الـ lead II بينقلب، والـ leads I و III بينقلبوا وبتبادلوا الأماكن، بينما aVR و aVF بس بتبادلوا مع بعض. والـ lead الوحيد اللي ما بيتأثر هو aVL.
الفخ: A (ectopic atrial rhythm في الـ low atria) هي اللي بتخليك تقرأ الـ EKG غلط، لأن الـ inverted P wave لحالها بيحكي على الـ rhythm. بس لما الـ axis بعده مقلوب 180 درجة، هاد مش physiology، هاد أخطاء في توصيل الـ leads.

question:
A 29-year-old male is sent by his primary care doctor’s office for evaluation of an abnormal 
EKG. He is asymptomatic and his physical examination is normal. The EKG is shown in below. 
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
englishExplanation:
The patient has asymptomatic first-degree atrioventricular (AV) block with a 
prolonged PR interval but no dropped beats. This is commonly seen in healthy individuals, has 
no prognostic significance, and requires no further evaluation or management.

![subjects1200-ecb5203b75286554 source page 8](images/subjects1200-ecb5203b75286554-p0008.jpg)

![subjects1200-ecb5203b75286554 source page 9](images/subjects1200-ecb5203b75286554-p0009.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ EKG بيبيّن first-degree atrioventricular block، يعني الـ PR interval مطوّل بس بدون أي dropped beats. وهاد شائع عند الناس الأصحاء، وما عنده أي prognostic significance. والمريض asymptomatic والـ exam بتاعه طبيعي، فما في داعي تستعمل drugs ولا تعمل evaluation إضافي ولا حتى متابعة خاصة. يعني أحسن خطوة management هي إنك ما تعمل أي therapy acute.
الفخ: الناس بتخاف من كلمة block بالـ EKG وبتبدأ تتدخل. بس block أول درجة مع مريض asymptomatic و hemodynamically stable ما بيستدعي atropine ولا amiodarone ولا transcutaneous pacing ولا synchronized cardioversion.

question:
When compared with patients with deep venous thrombosis (DVT) of the lower extremities, 
patients with an upper extremity DVT

options.text: Are more likely to have an underlying diagnosis of cancer
More often have an inherited or acquired hypercoagulable state
More commonly experience complications as a result of the DVT

correctAnswer: Are more likely to have an underlying diagnosis of cancer
englishExplanation:
Patients with an upper extremity DVT tend to be younger and leaner than their lower 
extremity DVT counterparts. They less commonly have an inherited or acquired hypercoagulable 
state but more commonly have an underlying diagnosis of cancer. In fact, most upper extremity 
DVTs are associated with an indwelling catheter (often used for chemotherapy or long-term 
antibiotics). Though patients with an upper extremity DVT experience complications less often 
than patients with lower extremity DVTs, approximately 6% of patients still develop a PE (versus 
as many as one-third of patients with a lower extremity DVT), so patients require long-term 
anticoagulation, typically for 3 to 6 months after diagnosis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: مرضى الـ upper extremity DVT بيكونوا أصغر سناً وأسم من مرضى الـ lower extremity DVT. عندهم inherited أو acquired hypercoagulable state أقل شيوعاً، بس بيكثروا يكون مرتبطين مع تشخيص سرطان. وكمان أغلب الـ upper extremity DVTs مرتبطة بـ indwelling catheter، يعني catheters مستخدمة للـ chemotherapy أو للـ antibiotics طويلة الأمد. رغم إن المضاعفات عندهم أقل، حوالي 6% بيطوروا PE مقابل واحد من كل ثلاثة بمرضى الـ lower extremity DVT.
الفخ: C (hypercoagulable state) و E (مضاعفات أكثر) و A (إنهم أكبر سناً) كلهم عكس الواقع. أما D (ما في داعي anticoagulation) غلط كمان، لأن مرضى الـ upper extremity DVT محتاجين long-term anticoagulation عادةً 3 لـ 6 أشهر.

question: Which of the following is true regarding troponin I in acute myocardial infarction (MI)?

options.text: Sensitivity at 6 hours after MI is 95%
Specificity at 6 hours after MI is 95%

correctAnswer: Specificity at 6 hours after MI is 95%
englishExplanation:
Troponin I is highly specific for cardiac muscle. It starts rising between 3 and 6 hours 
after infarction, peaks at 12 to 24 hours, and returns to normal within 7 days. The specificity of 
troponin I is excellent at 6 hours post infarction, but the sensitivity does not approach 100% 
until 12 hours.

![subjects1200-555fbf35da90f624 source page 9](images/subjects1200-555fbf35da90f624-p0009.jpg)

![subjects1200-555fbf35da90f624 source page 10](images/subjects1200-555fbf35da90f624-p0010.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ troponin I عالية جداً بالخصوصية لعضلة القلب. بتبدأ ترتفع بين 3 و 6 ساعات بعد الـ infarction، وبتوصل ذروتها بين 12 و 24 ساعة، وبترجع طبيعية خلال 7 أيام. والـ specificity ممتازة بعد 6 ساعات من الـ infarction. بس الـ sensitivity ما بتقرب من 100% إلا بعد 12 ساعة. يعني بعد 6 ساعات لو طلعت النتيجة إيجابية فبثق فيها، بس لو طلعت سلبية ما بنستبعد الـ MI.
الفخ: D (sensitivity 95% بعد 6 ساعات) هي الغلطة الشائعة، لأن الـ sensitivity ما بتقرب من 100% إلا بعد 12 ساعة. و A و B غلط لأن الـ troponin I بتبدأ ترتفع بعد 3 لـ 6 ساعات وبتبلغ ذروتها 12 لـ 24 ساعة.

question:
Which of the following is a possible complication of left ventricular assist device (LVAD) 
placement and use?
englishExplanation:
Left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) are associated with a host of complications. All 
patients require anticoagulation to reduce the risk of pump thrombosis. While the use of 
anticoagulants increases bleeding risk, the risk is further increased because patients with LVADs 
develop an acquired von Willebrand syndrome because the pump machinery breaks the 
normally long vWF chains into shorter, less effective segments. The driveline connects the 
extracorporeal electronic controller to the motor which is attached to the heart. As with any 
foreign body, drivelines are susceptible to infection and are covered with a sterile dressing. 
Right heart failure is a frequent complication either secondary to the increased right heart 
workload or to a malignant rhythm such as ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation (which has less 
effect on the left heart because it is device dependent).

![subjects1200-dcf384d9c8f605f5 source page 10](images/subjects1200-dcf384d9c8f605f5-p0010.jpg)

![subjects1200-dcf384d9c8f605f5 source page 11](images/subjects1200-dcf384d9c8f605f5-p0011.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ LVAD بيسبب كذا نوع من المضاعفات. كل المرضى لازم ياخدوا anticoagulation عشان يقلّلوا خطر pump thrombosis. وبنفس الوقت الـ anticoagulants بتزود خطر النزف، وبيزداد أكتر لأن مرضى الـ LVAD بيكسبوا acquired von Willebrand syndrome، لأن مكنة الـ pump بتكسّر سلاسل الـ vWF الطويلة لقطع أقصر وأقل فعالية. والـ driveline بتربط الـ controller الخارجي بالموتور، وبما إنها foreign body فهي عرضة للعدوى ولازم sterile dressing. وكمان right heart failure مضاعفة متكررة بسبب increased right heart workload أو malignant rhythm.
الفخ: A (gastrointestinal bleeding) صحيحة لحالها، بس الناس بتوقف عندها وتنسى الباقي. الخيارات الأربعة كلها صحيحة، فالـ All of the above هو الجواب الصح.

question:
A 7-year-old female presents with syncope without a prodrome. EKG shows QT 
prolongation. Family history is most likely to reveal which of the following?
englishExplanation:
Prolongation of the QT interval may be due to congenital or acquired causes. 
Congenital long QT syndromes may be associated with deafness (Jervell–Lange–Nielsen 
syndrome) or without deafness (Romano–Ward syndrome). Acquired causes can be from 
electrolyte abnormalities, environmental conditions, or medication effects. Excessive 
prolongation can result in potentially fatal ventricular dysrhythmias, such as ventricular 
fibrillation and torsades de pointes. Treatment is usually with magnesium and standard 
advanced cardiac life support (ACLS) protocols. Prevention of ventricular dysrhythmias is with 
chronic β-blocker therapy and sometimes pacemakers/defibrillators.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: prolongation الـ QT ممكن يكون congenital أو acquired. الـ congenital long QT syndromes ممكن ترتبط بـ deafness، وهاد اسمه Jervell-Lange-Nielsen syndrome، أو من غير deafness واسمه Romano-Ward syndrome. الـ acquired causes بتيجي من اضطراب الأيونات أو ظروف بيئية أو تأثير الأدوية. والـ prolongation الشديد ممكن يسبب ventricular dysrhythmias خطيرة مثل ventricular fibrillation و torsades de pointes. والعلاج عادةً magnesium وبروتوكولات ACLS.
الفخ: E (short stature) و A (cystic fibrosis) و B (Hirschsprung disease) مو من الـ syndromes المرتبطة بـ long QT. واللي لازم تفرّق بينه وبين الـ Jervell-Lange-Nielsen syndrome هو الـ Romano-Ward syndrome اللي من غير deafness.

question: Which of the following is true regarding EKGs in posterior wall MI?

options.text: Abnormalities are most commonly seen in V3.
ST elevations in precordial leads are diagnostic.
Tall R waves are the earliest findings.
T-wave inversions are common in V1–V3.
Posteriorly placed leads are more accurate than anterior leads.

correctAnswer: Posteriorly placed leads are more accurate than anterior leads.
englishExplanation:
Posterior wall MIs occur with infarction of the right coronary artery or left circumflex 
artery, depending on the anatomic dominance of the patient. Standard EKG electrodes are 
anteriorly placed and may not exhibit infarction patterns of ST elevation—posterior electrodes 
are more accurate at diagnosing posterior wall MIs. Infarction patterns in posterior wall MIs are 
opposite of those in anterior wall MIs—posterior MIs will show ST depression instead of ST 
elevation, R waves instead of Q waves, and upright T waves instead of T-wave inversions. Leads 
V1 and V2 are the most specific anterior leads for posterior wall infarction. Tall R waves, like Q 
waves, are the latest findings in posterior MIs.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ posterior wall MIs بتحصل مع infarction بالـ right coronary artery أو الـ left circumflex artery، حسب الـ anatomic dominance. الـ electrodes بالـ EKG العادي بتتحط قدام، وممكن ما تبيّن نمط الـ ST elevation للـ infarction. الـ posterior electrodes أدق بتشخيص الـ posterior wall MIs. ونمط الـ infarction بالوراء عكس اللي قدام: ST depression بدل ST elevation، و R waves بدل Q waves، و T waves موجبة بدل inversion.
الفخ: C (Tall R waves هي أول شي) غلط، لأنها زي Q waves آخر ظهور. و D (T-wave inversions في V1–V3) غلط لأن الـ posterior MIs بتطلع T waves موجبة. و A غلط لأن الأدق هم V1 و V2 مو V3.

question:
In patients receiving a normal 12-lead EKG, which of the following is true regarding 
reciprocal ST depressions seen in acute MI?

options.text: They are more commonly seen in inferior MIs than anterior MIs.
They have poor specificity for acute MI.
They are more commonly seen in acute pericarditis than acute MI.
They are usually upsloping when seen in the setting of acute MI.

correctAnswer: They are more commonly seen in inferior MIs than anterior MIs.
englishExplanation:
Reciprocal ST depressions associated with ST elevations have high specificity for acute 
MI (reported to be >90%) and are not usually present in nonischemic conditions. Their presence 
confers a higher risk of poor outcomes. Reciprocal ST depressions are usually downsloping. Most 
inferior wall MIs exhibit reciprocal ST depressions, whereas most anterior wall MIs do not.

![subjects1200-c299bae6276a8f15 source page 12](images/subjects1200-c299bae6276a8f15-p0012.jpg)

![subjects1200-c299bae6276a8f15 source page 13](images/subjects1200-c299bae6276a8f15-p0013.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ reciprocal ST depressions المصاحبة للـ ST elevations عندها specificity عالية جداً لـ acute MI، ومذكور فوق 90%، وهي ما بتظهر عادةً بالحالات اللي مش ischemic. ووجودها بيعطي risk أعلى لنتائج سيئة. والـ reciprocal ST depressions عادةً بتبقى downsloping. وأغلب الـ inferior wall MIs بتظهر عندها، بينما أغلب الـ anterior wall MIs ما بتظهر. يعني منتشرة على الـ leads المقابلة للـ infarction.
الفخ: E (upsloping) غلط لأن الـ pattern هاد downsloping. و C (poor specificity) غلط لأن الـ specificity فوق 90%. و A (little prognostic significance) غلط لأن وجودها بيعني outcome أسوأ.

question:
A 55-year-old female presents with a progressively worsening, painful, swollen, and 
discolored left leg shown below. Which of the following is the most likely pathophysiologic 
mechanism?
englishExplanation:
The patient has phlegmasia cerulea dolens, which is diagnosed by the clinical triad of 
cyanosis, pain, and edema due to massive lower extremity venous thrombosis. The cyanosis is 
due to a combination of increased venous backflow and compromised arterial flow. Phlegmasia 
alba dolens is similar but lacks cyanosis and instead appears as a blanched extremity. Treatment 

involves admission, intravenous anticoagulation, and possibly surgical thrombectomy and 
fasciotomy.

![subjects1200-f6ddec3548ad5d38 source page 13](images/subjects1200-f6ddec3548ad5d38-p0013.jpg)

![subjects1200-f6ddec3548ad5d38 source page 14](images/subjects1200-f6ddec3548ad5d38-p0014.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريضة عندها phlegmasia cerulea dolens، وهي triad من cyanosis و pain و edema بسبب massive lower extremity venous thrombosis. الـ cyanosis بييجي من combination بين increased venous backflow و compromised arterial flow. والـ treatment بيشمل دخول المستشفى، intravenous anticoagulation، وممكن thrombectomy جراحية و fasciotomy. لاحظي إنه في نسخة اسمها phlegmasia alba dolens بتظهر بس بدون cyanosis.
الفخ: C (infection) هي اللي الناس بتختارها لأنها سهلة، بس الوصف اللي عندنا بيطابق massive venous thrombosis. و D و E (autoimmune و allergy) ما بيقدروا يشرحوا الـ cyanosis والـ pain والـ edema مع بعض.

question:
In patients older than 85 years, which of the following is the most common symptom during 
MI?
englishExplanation:
Elderly, diabetic, and female patients frequently have atypical anginal symptoms. The 
extreme elderly (>85 years) experience shortness of breath as the most common symptom 
during an MI. Nausea, typical chest pain, syncope, and fatigue may also be present. The 
emergency physician (EP) can never clinically rule out the diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome 
in elderly patients just because they lack frank chest pain. Choices D and E occur more 
frequently in dehydration and infection than in MI.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المرضى الكبار والـ diabetic والـ نساء بيكثروا من عندهم أعراض angina غير نمطية. واللي بعد الـ 85 سنة بالضبط، الـ shortness of breath بيكون أكثر عرض عندهم وقت الـ MI. وممكن كمان تلاقي nausea و typical chest pain و syncope و fatigue. يعني الـ emergency physician ما بيقدر يستبعد acute coronary syndrome عند كبير السن بس لأنه ما عنده chest pain صريح.
الفخ: A (chest pain) هي الإجابة اللي الناس بتختارها تلقائياً لأن الـ MI مرتبط فيها، بس بعد الـ 85 الـ dyspnea هو أكثر شيوعاً. و D و E (altered mental status و fever) أكثر شيوعاً بالـ dehydration والـ infection من الـ MI.

question:
Which of the following is usually the earliest symptom to occur in patients with aortic 
stenosis (AS)?
englishExplanation:
AS usually occurs due to congenital bicuspid structure, calcific degeneration, or 
rheumatic heart disease. The classic murmur is a systolic crescendo–decrescendo murmur at the 
right upper sternal border or cardiac base. The natural history of AS usually follows a sequence 
of findings, starting with angina, followed by syncope, and then heart failure. As each 
subsequent finding occurs, the mortality increases significantly. Valve replacement is the only 
definitive treatment once symptoms appear.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ AS غالباً بيحصل من congenital bicuspid structure، أو calcific degeneration، أو rheumatic heart disease. الـ murmur الكلاسيكي هو systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur عند الـ right upper sternal border أو cardiac base. والتاريخ الطبيعي للـ AS بيسير بترتيب: أول شي angina، بعدين syncope، وآخر شي heart failure. وكل ما ظهر العرض التالي، الـ mortality بيزيد بشكل كبير. والـ valve replacement هو العلاج الحاسم الوحيد بعد ما الأعراض تظهر.
الفخ: E (paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea) و D (orthopnea) بتيجي بعدين، لما المريض يبدأ يعمل heart failure. و C (syncope) هو العرض الثاني مش الأول، فاللي بتسمعه أول شي لازم يكون angina.

question:
Among patients presenting with an NSTEMI, which of the following describes the 
appropriate use of antiplatelet therapy?

options.text: Aspirin alone, given in doses of 162 to 325 mg, is the standard of care.
Aspirin plus a GPIIbIIIa inhibitor should be given in all cases.
Either clopidogrel or a GPIIbIIIa inhibitor should be used in addition to aspirin.
Patients should only receive clopidogrel in addition to aspirin if no percutaneous intervention
Clopidogrel is only indicated for patients who are intolerant of aspirin.

correctAnswer: Either clopidogrel or a GPIIbIIIa inhibitor should be used in addition to aspirin.
englishExplanation:
Dual antiplatelet therapy is the recommended approach in patients with NSTEMI. 
Upon arrival to the ED, all patients should be given between 162 and 325 mg of uncoated aspirin 
to be chewed immediately. Uncoated aspirin is preferred over enteric coated aspirin because of 
its more rapid absorption. At these doses, aspirin nearly immediately, completely, and 
permanently (until a new platelet is made) inhibits thromboxane A2 production which is critical 

for platelet aggregation. In addition to aspirin, patients should receive either clopidogrel (a 
thienopyridine, along with ticlopidine and prasugrel) or a GPIIbIIIa inhibitor, such as abciximab, 
eptifibatide, or tirofiban. Most guidelines recommend clopidogrel as the first-line agent in 
patients being managed without PCI while clopidogrel or a GPIIbIIIa inhibitor can be used in 
patients subjected to an invasive strategy. While some studies have suggested that higher 
loading doses should be used, the recommended loading dose of clopidogrel in the setting of 
NSTEMI remains 300 mg unless immediate catheterization is going to be performed (in which 
case the recommended dose is 600 mg).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ dual antiplatelet therapy هو الأسلوب الموصى فيه لمرضى NSTEMI. أول ما يوصل المريض للـ ED، لازم كلهم ياخدوا من 162 لـ 325 mg من uncoated aspirin مضغة وتبلعها على طول. والـ uncoated aspirin أفضل من enteric coated لأنه يمتص أسرع. وبهالجرعات الـ aspirin يوقف إنتاج thromboxane A2 بشكل شبه فوري وكامل، و thromboxane A2 هو اللي حاسم في platelet aggregation. و غير الـ aspirin، لازم المريض ياخد clopidogrel أو GPIIbIIIa inhibitor مثل abciximab أو eptifibatide أو tirofiban.
الفخ: A (aspirin لحاله) ناقص لأنه لازم antiplatelet تاني مع aspirin. و B (GPIIbIIIa في كل الحالات) مش دقيق، لأن clopidogrel هو first-line لمن يديروا بدون PCI. و D و E غلط، لأن clopidogrel مش بس لل-aspirin-intolerant.

question:
A 56-year-old male with a history of a prosthetic aortic valve presents for evaluation of fever 
and chills for 1 week. Echocardiogram reveals vegetations on the prosthetic valve. Which of the 
following is the most likely etiologic organism?
englishExplanation:
The patient has endocarditis of a prosthetic valve, which is most commonly due to 
coagulase-negative staphylococci. S. viridans is the most common cause of native valve 
endocarditis. Choices C, D, and E are uncommon causes of native valve endocarditis.

question:
A 66-year-old female who recently completed chemotherapy for colon cancer through a 
right chest Port-a-Cath presents with a chief complaint of right arm pain, swelling, and 
weakness. The right hand is warm, and well perfused. The radial pulse is equal to the 
contralateral side. There is no evidence of cellulitis. An upper extremity deep venous thrombosis 
(DVT) is suspected. Which of the following is the next best test?
englishExplanation:
Doppler ultrasonography is the standard test for evaluating the presence of both 
lower and upper extremity DVT. While MRA has excellent specificity, it is only 80% sensitive for 
the diagnosis of upper extremity DVT. CT angiography has not been evaluated extensively, and 
its test characteristics are not yet known. Direct venography is a highly accurate method of 
diagnosing upper extremity DVT, but it is invasive and time consuming, so it should only be used 
in cases in which ultrasound is nondiagnostic though suspicion remains high. Finally, while 
negative D-dimers can be used in low-risk patients to exclude the presence of a lower extremity 
DVT, no validated criteria exist for proper risk stratification among patients with a possible 
upper extremity DVT. Therefore, the D-dimer cannot be used to exclude upper extremity DVT.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريضة عندها اشتباه بـ DVT في الطرف العلوي بعد chemotherapy وحطت Port-a-Cath. الفحص القياسي لتقييم الـ DVT هو Doppler ultrasound، لأنه noninvasive وسريع وبيأكد وجود الـ thrombosis. MRA حساس بس 80% بس، و CT angiography لسا ما تقيّم كويس، و Direct venography دقيق بس invasive وبياخد وقت، و D-dimer ما في له criteria معتمدة ينفي بها DVT في الطرف العلوي.
الفخ: بعض الناس بيختاروا D-dimer لأنه سريع، بس الـ D-dimer الناقص بيقدر ينفي DVT بس في الطرف السفلي، وما في معايير risk stratification معتمدة للطرف العلوي، و Direct venography بتستخدم بس إذا الـ ultrasound ما وضّح والاشتباه ظل عالي.

question:
A 15-year-old previously healthy female is brought to the ED by her parents with a chief 
complaint of shortness of breath (SOB), palpitations, lightheadedness, and severe fatigue. The 
patient had been diagnosed with “a viral infection” by her pediatrician 5 days before presenting 
to the ED. While she initially seemed to improve, she complains of feeling SOB with a sense that 
her heart is “beating out of her chest” for the past day. Her parents noted she was breathing 
fast, and she appeared to be “winded” even when sitting down. Upon arrival, she is pale and 
ill-appearing, with vitals of T 98.6, P 143, RR 28, BP 105/70, and SaO2 of 92% on RA. A chest 
x-ray demonstrates fluffy bilateral infiltrates. Her lung examination reveals tachypnea with 
increased work of breathing, and rales without wheezes. Which of the following is true of the 
patient’s likely underlying problem?

options.text: The patient’s EKG will most likely reveal supraventricular tachycardia.
An elevated MB isoenzyme of creatine kinase (CK-MB) helps to confirm the patient’s
Loop diuretics and inotropes may be helpful in her management.
Two sets of blood cultures should be drawn and IV antibiotics, and aggressive IV fluids should
Echocardiography will likely reveal previously undiagnosed congenital heart disease.

correctAnswer: Loop diuretics and inotropes may be helpful in her management.
englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with acute CHF, likely due to virally mediated myocarditis. 
While patients with acute myocarditis often present in a more subtle manner than this patient, 
patients may present with a broad range of symptoms, from vague generalized malaise to 
fulminant heart failure. Therefore, the ED physician must maintain a high degree of suspicion in 
patients presenting to the ED with new symptoms in the convalescent phase of a viral illness. 
The most common arrhythmia in patients with myocarditis is sinus tachycardia. Patients rarely 
present with supraventricular tachycardia, but when present, the rate is typically 180 to 260 
beats per minute. Though the CK-MB and troponin are frequently measured in adults with chest 
pain, CK-MB has not been shown to be either sensitive or specific for pediatric patients with 
myocarditis. Elevated troponin levels also demonstrate poor sensitivity (34%) but relatively high 
specificity (82%) for myocarditis. Therapy is not based on the levels of any biomarker. Since this 
patient is presenting with fulminant heart failure, loop diuretics (e.g., furosemide) and inotropes 
(e.g., dobutamine, milrinone) may be essential in her management. Vasodilators (e.g., 
nitroglycerin) are also a mainstay of therapy, but this patient’s relative hypotension may limit 
their use. Early consultation with a pediatric cardiologist is also essential as the patient should 
be transferred to a center with the capability of providing extracorporeal membrane 
oxygenation, should that become necessary. The patient’s lack of fever or cough points against 
pneumonia as a likely diagnosis. Echocardiography is an essential diagnostic tool, but patients 
only rarely have pre-existing, undiagnosed congenital heart disease. Most often, 
echocardiography reveals global left ventricular dysfunction, with variable degrees of left 
ventricular cavity enlargement.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد البنت عندها acute CHF fulminant، والسبب الأرجح myocarditis بعد عدوى فيروسية. اللي صار إنه القلب ما بيضخ كافي، فبتحتاج loop diuretics مثل furosemide ينزلوا السوائل، و inotropes مثل dobutamine أو milrinone يزيدوا الـ contractility. الـ vasodilators مثل nitroglycerin مهمة بس ضغطها منخفض نسبياً، و CK-MB و troponin مو حساسين كفاية عند الأطفال، ولازم استشارة pediatric cardiologist بدري.
الفخ: كثير من الطلاب بيختاروا CK-MB لأنهم فاكرين إنو بيأكد MI، وبيختاروا supraventricular tachycardia أو endocarditis. بس الـ CK-MB و troponin مش حساسين كفاية، و supraventricular tachycardia نادرة، والعلاج مو مبني على أرقام الـ biomarkers.

question: Which of the following is true regarding prosthetic heart valves?

options.text: Bioprosthetic (porcine) valves require anticoagulation therapy with Coumadin.
Prophylactic anticoagulation should be maintained at international normalized ratios (INRs)
Chronic hemolysis occurs in most patients.
In patients with mechanical valves, auscultation of a metallic closure sound indicates serious

correctAnswer: Chronic hemolysis occurs in most patients.
englishExplanation:
A small degree of chronic hemolysis occurs in all patients, which in most cases is 
clinically insignificant if appropriate iron supplementation is instituted. Mechanical, not porcine, 
valves require anticoagulation with Coumadin, and the INR is generally kept between 2.5 and 
3.5. Mechanical valves always have a metallic closure sound—absence of this sound indicates 
valve dysfunction. The risk of endocarditis depends on the length of time the valve is functioning 
but occurs in less than half the number of patients.

![subjects1200-2fb24b584f65ef59 source page 21](images/subjects1200-2fb24b584f65ef59-p0021.jpg)

![subjects1200-2fb24b584f65ef59 source page 22](images/subjects1200-2fb24b584f65ef59-p0022.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في كل مريض عنده صمام صناعي بيصير قدر بسيط من hemolysis المزمن، بس في أغلب الحالات هاد بدون أعراض لما نعطي iron مناسب. اللي صار إنه الدم بيتكسر شوي على الصمام المعدني وهاد متوقع، مو دليل على شي خطير لحاله. بس لازم تفرق بين هاد وبين endocarditis لأنها بتصير بأقل من نص المرضى، والصمامات الميكانيكية دايماً إلها صوت معدني وإذا ما سمعته هاد بيعني dysfunction.
الفخ: كثير من الطلاب بيختاروا endocarditis أو إن الصمام الـ porcine يحتاج Coumadin. الـ Coumadin و INR بين 2.5 و 3.5 مطلوبين للصمامات الميكانيكية بس، و endocarditis بتصير بأقل من نص المرضى.

question:
The amount of time after which a limb exposed to ischemia at room temperature (“warm 
ischemia”) begins to develop irreversible damage is:
englishExplanation:
After 6 hours of warm ischemia, 10% of patients will begin to develop irreversible 
damage to muscles and nerves. After 12 hours, 90% of patients will have irreversible damage.

question:
Which of the following is the most appropriate medication to induce rapid, measured 
reduction of blood pressure in hypertensive crises?
englishExplanation:
Only intravenous medications are appropriate for rapid, measured control of blood 
pressure. Nitroprusside is very easily titrated and extremely effective, making it the drug of 
choice for hypertensive crises. Nifedipine has been associated with severe side effects due to its 
unpredictable response. Isoproterenol is a β-agonist and will not decrease blood pressure. 
Phenoxybenzamine is an α-blocking agent used mostly in the prevention of catecholamine surge 
during therapy for pheochromocytoma. Hydrochlorothiazide is an oral medication appropriate 
for outpatient therapy for chronic hypertension.

![subjects1200-384d12cf33780b25 source page 23](images/subjects1200-384d12cf33780b25-p0023.jpg)

![subjects1200-384d12cf33780b25 source page 24](images/subjects1200-384d12cf33780b25-p0024.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في hypertensive crisis لازم ينزل الضغط بسرعة وبشكل متحكّم فيه، وهاد بيتم بس بالأدوية اللي بتدي عن طريق IV. اللي صار إنه Nitroprusside سهل تعديله بالـ drip وفعّال جداً، فصار drug of choice في هاد hypertensive crises. أما Nifedipine فردّ فعله غير متوقع وقد يسبب آثار جانبية خطيرة، و Isoproterenol ما بينزّل الضغط، و Phenoxybenzamine بيُستخدم أساساً في pheochromocytoma، و Hydrochlorothiazide دوا للمريض الطارج.
الفخ: أكثر الطلاب بيختاروا Nifedipine لأنه دوا معروف للضغط، بس هو بيؤخذ عن طريق الفم مش IV، وممكن يسبب آثار جانبية خطيرة لأن ردّ فعله غير متوقع. تذكّر: hypertensive crisis يعني أدوية IV.

question:
A 43-year-old otherwise healthy male presents with signs and symptoms of pneumonia. 
Antibiotics are ordered and the patient is admitted. An admission electrocardiogram (EKG) is 
ordered and is shown in Figure below. Which of the following is most likely?

options.text: The limb leads have been reversed.
The patient is experiencing demand-ischemia and needs an emergent heart catheterization.
An echocardiogram would likely reveal significant underlying structural heart disease.
The patient has an increased risk for sudden cardiac death.
The patient’s calcium level is profoundly decreased.

correctAnswer: The patient has an increased risk for sudden cardiac death.
englishExplanation:
This patient’s EKG reveals classic or “type 1” Brugada syndrome. Brugada syndrome is 
characterized by a pseudo-RBBB and persistent ST elevation in V1–V3. There are three unique 
patterns of ST elevation consistent with Brugada syndrome. In type 1, the elevated ST segment 
is convex facing upward, and gradually descends to an inverted T wave. This is referred to as a 
“coved type” Brugada pattern, and is most common. Types 2 and 3 have identical patterns, in 
which the elevated ST segment (≥1 mm in type 2, <1 mm in type 3) first descends and then rises 
again after nearing the baseline, creating a “saddle back” appearance. It is associated with an 
upright or biphasic T wave. Brugada syndrome is not normally associated with any structural 
abnormalities. Most “standard” cardiac tests, including echocardiography, stress testing, and 
cardiac MRI are unrevealing. However, patients are at a much increased risk for sudden cardiac 
arrest due to ventricular arrhythmias. Unlike patients with hypertrophic obstructive 
cardiomyopathy, sudden cardiac arrest is not typically due to exercise and more commonly 
occurs in sleep. Most patients with Brugada syndrome undergo electrophysiology testing to 
determine their risk for cardiac arrest as well as the need for an automated implantable 
cardioverter-defibrillator

![subjects1200-141b80c6a9a0eeb6 source page 24](images/subjects1200-141b80c6a9a0eeb6-p0024.jpg)

![subjects1200-141b80c6a9a0eeb6 source page 25](images/subjects1200-141b80c6a9a0eeb6-p0025.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ EKG هاد بيبّن Brugada syndrome type 1، يعني pseudo-RBBB مع ST elevation ثابت في V1–V3 بشكل coved. اللي صار إنه هاد syndrom ما حدا بيسبب متلازمة بنية حقيقية، فـ echocardiography و stress testing و cardiac MRI بيطلعوا طبيعي. بس الخطر الأكبر عند هاد المرضى هو sudden cardiac arrest بسبب ventricular arrhythmias، وغالباً بيحصل أثناء النوم مو أثناء التمرين، وأغلب المرضى بيعملوا electrophysiology testing عشان يحدّدوا إذا محتاجين ICD.
الفخ: بيختاروا إن الـ echocardiogram بتبيّن disease بنيوية، أو إن الـ limb leads متبدّلين، أو إنهم محتاجين emergent catheterization. البنية التشريحية بتكون طبيعية، والـ limb leads مو متبدّلين، والـ Brugada syndrome بيخلي الخطر على الـ arrest كبير.

question: Which of the following is the most common risk factor associated with aortic dissection?
englishExplanation:
Although all the choices are risk factors for aortic dissection, the most common is 
hypertension. Though approximately half the number of patients with Marfan syndrome 
develop aortic dissections, <10% of all dissections are in Marfan patients.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الخيارات كلها risk factors حقيقية لـ aortic dissection، بس hypertension هي الأكثر شيوعاً بينهم. ورغم إنه نص مرضى Marfan syndrome بيصير عندهم dissection، أقل من 10% من كل الحالات بتم عند مرضى Marfan. أما Smoking و atherosclerosis و bicuspid aortic valve فموجودين بس أقل شيوعاً، والسبب إن ضغط الدم العالي بيحط حمل على جدار الـ aorta.
الفخ: Marfan syndrome هي الخيار اللي بيستقطب الناس لأنها مرتبطة بعامل وراثي معروف. بس النسبة الحقيقية أقل من 10% من الحالات، فـ hypertension هي الإجابة.

question:
Which of the following has the greatest immediate effect on preload in the management of 
acute congestive heart failure (CHF)?
englishExplanation:
Nitroglycerin directly dilates the great veins and reduces left ventricular preload. 
Afterload reduction by nitrates is much less prominent. Morphine and loop diuretics such as 
furosemide are also used for preload reduction but have a smaller effect than nitrates. While 
morphine has been used for years as part of the standard treatment of CHF for preload 
reduction, there have been few rigorously conducted randomized trials confirming its benefit. 
Morphine most likely exerts its preload reducing effect by reducing anxiety and subsequent 
catecholamine production and release. Loop diuretics cause preload reduction by inhibiting 
renal sodium reabsorption thereby increasing urine volume and decreasing plasma volume. 
However, the elevated afterload in patients with CHF reduces renal perfusion and thereby limits 
the effectiveness of loop diuretics. Afterload reduction is most commonly achieved through the 
use of angiotensin converteing enzyme (ACE) inhibitors such as enalaprilat, although 
nitroprusside and hydralazine may also be used to achieve this effect. Digoxin causes an 
increase in cardiac contractility without major changes on preload or afterload, and has no role 
in the management of acute CHF. In fact, prior digoxin use has been shown to correlate to 
increased in-hospital mortality among patients admitted with CHF.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: Nitroglycerin بيبوسّع الـ great veins مباشرة، وهاد بيقلّل preload الـ left ventricular بشكل واضح وسريع. اللي صار إنه تأثيره على الـ afterload أقل بكثير، بينما Morphine و loop diuretics مثل furosemide بينقصوا الـ preload بس بأثر أصغر. و Digoxin ما إلها دور في acute CHF لأنها بتزيد الـ contractility بدون ما تغيّر الـ preload ولا الـ afterload، والـ ACE inhibitors مثل enalaprilat هي اللي بتعمل reduction للـ afterload.
الفخ: أكثر الطلاب بيختاروا Morphine أو furosemide لأنهم سمعوا إنهم بيقلّلوا الـ preload، أو Enalaprilat لأنو دوا CHF معروف. بس الـ Enalaprilat بيشتغل على الـ afterload، والـ Nitroglycerin أقوى تأثير مباشر على الـ preload.

question: Which of the following is true regarding the diagnosis of aortic dissection?

options.text: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is more specific than CT or transesophageal
Chest x-ray is normal in most cases.
Transthoracic echocardiogram is useful to confirm the diagnosis.
Aortography is the best screening test.

correctAnswer: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is more specific than CT or transesophageal
englishExplanation:
MRI is the most specific test for the diagnosis of aortic dissection. Logistic difficulties 
prevent routine use of MRI in this setting—for this reason, CT aortogram is the most commonly 
used test and has excellent sensitivity and specificity. Chest x-ray is abnormal in most cases, but 
the sensitivity is not high enough to rule out the diagnosis in high-risk patients. 
Transesophageal, not transthoracic, echocardiography may provide useful structural 
information about the descending aorta, heart, and pericardium, but CT aortogram and MRI are 
far more specific. Aortography is used only in confirmatory settings. Electrocardiography is 
useful only in ruling out other causes of the patient’s symptoms and has no utility in confirming 
the diagnosis of aortic dissection.

![subjects1200-85b61e9eda688597 source page 26](images/subjects1200-85b61e9eda688597-p0026.jpg)

![subjects1200-85b61e9eda688597 source page 27](images/subjects1200-85b61e9eda688597-p0027.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ MRI هي أكثر فحص عنده specificity لتشخيص aortic dissection، والـ CT aortogram بيستخدم أكثر لأنه أسهل وأسرع بالواقع. اللي صار إنه الـ chest x-ray abnormal في أغلب الحالات بس الـ sensitivity مو عالية كفاية تستبعد التشخيص عند المريض الخطر. و Transthoracic echo مفيدة بس CT aortogram و MRI أدق بفرق كبير، و Aortography للتأكيد بس، و EKG ما بتقدر تأكد التشخيص.
الفخ: أكثر الطلاب بيختاروا chest x-ray لأنه متوفر وسهل، أو transthoracic echo لأنه فحص القلب، أو Aortography كـ screening. الـ MRI الأدق، و Aortography للتأكيد بس، و chest x-ray ما بتستبعد التشخيص.

question:
A 4-week-old infant is brought in by his parents breathing fast and appearing sweaty. His 
respiratory rate is 54, BP 88/60, P 200. His skin is pink and capillary refill is about 2 seconds. His 
EKG is shown. Which the following is true (Fig. below)?

options.text: A bag of ice should be held over the infant’s nose and mouth for 30 seconds
The baby has Wolff Parkinson White (WPW) syndrome
Electrical cardioversion should be performed immediately
Verapamil is the intravenous agent of choice

correctAnswer: A bag of ice should be held over the infant’s nose and mouth for 30 seconds
englishExplanation:
This patient has supraventricular tachycardia (SVT). Since the diving reflex is very 
effective in neonates, the first step is to hold a bag of ice or a frozen towel over the patient’s 
nose and mouth for 30 seconds. If the infant fails to convert, the next step is to use adenosine. 
Verapamil is avoided in infants because it may cause significant hypotension. Digoxin, on the 
other hand, may be effective, but has a slow onset. Electrical cardioversion is effective, but is 
reserved for patients with refractory symptoms or who are in shock. Given that this patient has 
good perfusion and is maintaining his blood pressure, electrical cardioversion is not needed. 
Finally, while WPW can lead to SVT, it is not possible to determine if WPW underlies the 
patient’s SVT until after cardioversion.

![subjects1200-1915b4366f31cc12 source page 28](images/subjects1200-1915b4366f31cc12-p0028.jpg)

![subjects1200-1915b4366f31cc12 source page 29](images/subjects1200-1915b4366f31cc12-p0029.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الرضيع عنده supraventricular tachycardia واضحة من الـ EKG، وأول خطوة هي نعمل diving reflex. اللي صار إنه نحط كيس ثلج أو منشفة مجمدة فوق الأنف والفم لمدة 30 ثانية، وهاد بيعمل vagal maneuver قوي عند الرضيع وبيوقف الـ SVT بأغلب الحالات بدون أي دوا. و ما بنعرف إذا ورا الـ SVT في WPW إلا بعد ما يعمل cardioversion.
