ليش: لأن المريضة عندها dyspnea تدريجي مع fatigue وparoxysmal nocturnal dyspnea، ومعها S3 وإزاحة PMI، وهاي علامات كلاسيكية لـ left-sided heart failure. الـ O2 sat 92% على room air مع hypertension. وright-sided failure بتطلع مع JVD وdistension abdomen وتورّم رجلين، وهذي مش موجودة. ومفي علامات shock ولا high-output failure، وhigh-output failure بيحصل مع thyrotoxicosis وchronic anemia وAV malformations، ومفي حدا منها بالتاريخ.
الفخ: بيختاروا right-sided heart failure لأنهم سمعوا كلمة heart failure بس ما لاحظوا الـ S3 وPMI المزاح. والفرق الحقيقي إن left-sided بتطلع مع orthopnea وPND وS3، وright-sided بتطلع مع JVD وedema. والـ cardiogenic shock بيحتاج hypotension مع poor perfusion.

question: A 26-year-old patient presents because of shortness of breath and palpitations that have progressively worsened over the past week. The shortness of breath is most noticeable with light jogging. The patient is otherwise healthy, and their medical history includes no chronic disease conditions. They did have the "viral crud" a few weeks ago. Vital signs are normal except for a heart rate of 130/min. Physical examination shows mild peripheral edema. Laboratory studies reveal an elevated troponin. Electrocardiography is shown. Chest x-ray study shows cardiomegaly. Which of the following organisms is the most common cause of the likely condition?
englishExplanation:

A. Human metapneumovirus
Parvovirus is the most common viral cause of myocarditis of the organisms listed.
Other common causes are enteroviruses, including coxsackievirus as well as Human
Herpes Virus 6. Human metapneumovirus is generally considered to be an uncommon cause of myocarditis.
B. Parainfluenza virus
Parainfluenza virus is not associated with myocarditis.
C. Parvovirus
This patient is presenting with viral myocarditis. The most common ECG change
seen in myocarditis is sinus tachycardia. Other ECG changes that may be observed

and QT interval

question: A 55-year-old female with no past medical history presents after losing consciousness while exercising. She regularly runs 20 miles per week and experienced no symptoms before the episode. She has no history of a prior syncopal episode, and there is no family history of sudden cardiac death. Vital signs are: BP 88/52 mmHg, HR 82/min, RR 14/min, Sp0₂ 99% on room air, T 98.8ºF (37.2ºC). What is the most appropriate disposition for this patient?

options.text: Discharge home with primary care follow-up

englishExplanation:
Admission to a monitored bed
Expl anation
A. Admission to a monitored bed
Admission for syncope should be based on history, physical exam, and ECG findings. High-risk features include exercise-induced syncope and a family history of
sudden cardiac death. The Canadian Syncope Risk Score can be used to identify
low-risk patients who can be discharged home. According to this score, patients
with any SBP reading mmHg and in whom a cardiac etiology is suspected (as in
this case, With exertional syncope) are at high risk. They should be admitted to a
monitored bed.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK442006/
B. Admission to a ward bed
Given her hypotension and syncope, telemetry monitoring is critical for this patient.
A regular ward bed is not appropriate.
C. Discharge home with cardiology follow-up
This patient's hypotension makes her syncope particularly concerning. Discharge is
not appropriate in this instance.
D. Discharge home with primary care follow-up
This patient's hypotension makes her syncope particularly concerning. Discharge is
not appropriate in this instance.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لأن المريضة عملت syncope أثناء التمرين، وهاد feature عالية الخطورة لأنه بيفكر بسبب قلبي. الـ BP عندها 88/52 يعني hypotension، والـ exertional syncope لحاله كافي. قرار الـ admission بيتبنى على الـ history والـ exam والـ ECG، والـ Canadian Syncope Risk Score بيقول إن أي مريض عندو SBP منخفض مع سبب قلبي مشتبه فيه هو high risk، فلازم ين admit على monitored bed.
الفخ: بيختاروا discharge home مع cardiology follow-up لأنهم شافوا إنها شابة وقلبها حلو. بس الـ exertional syncope مع SBP 88/52 بتحطها high risk بنظر الـ Canadian Syncope Risk Score، وبيحتاجوا monitoring. والـ outpatient ما بتمشي مع هاي الحالة.

question: An 18-year-old male is brought by ambulance to the emergency department after a sudden cardiac arrest during football practice. His line coach witnessed this event and immediately placed an automatic external defibrillator on him, shocking him with an immediate return of spontaneous circulation. In the ED, the patient regains consciousness and endorses feeling palpitations immediately before his syncopal episode. Physical examination reveals normal vital signs and is otherwise unremarkable. An emergent formal transthoracic echocardiogram shows normal ejection fraction, normal anatomy, and no wall motion abnormalities. Which of the following EKG findings is consistent with this patient's likely underlying pathology?

options.text: Needle-like Q waves in all leads
Shortened PR-interval and slurred upstroke in the QRS complex

correctAnswer: Shortened PR-interval and slurred upstroke in the QRS complex
englishExplanation:
Shortened PR-interval and slurred upstroke in the QRS complex
Expl anation
A. Electrical alternans
The most frequent cause of electrical alternans is pericardial effusion, although it
can be associated with supraventricular tachycardia, severe left cardiomegaly, or
aortic regurgitation. However, none of these conditions is likely in this post-shock
patient with normal vital signs and an unremarkable transthoracic echo.
B. Needle-like Q waves in all leads
Needle-like Q waves in the inferior and lateral leads, and left ventricular hypertrophy with strain pattern are classic EKG findings of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM). However, with a normal formal transthoracic echocardiogram, HOCM is a less likely diagnosis.
C. SIQ3T3
SIQ3T3, right ventricular strain, incomplete right bundle branch block are classic
EKG findings associated with acute pulmonary embolism. Generally, acute pulmonary embollsm leading to syncope involves a massive clot burden, such as a saddle embolus. In this clinical scenario, with a now asymptomatic patient with normal
vital signs and an unremarkable transthoracic echo, massive pulmonary embolism
is an unlikely diagnosis
D. Shortened PR-interval and slurred upstroke in the QRS complex
Causes of syncope can be divided into cardiac and non-cardiac causes. Cardiac
causes are the most lethal and require prompt identification and admission for further workup. Admission should be based on EKG findings, including ischemia,
Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome, Brugada syndrome, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and QT prolongation. WPW can be identified by a short PR-interval
with a delta wave (slurred upstroke to the QRS complex), which is the most likely
cause of this patient's syncopal episode. Brugada syndrome is identified by an RSR
pattern and ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads. QT prolongation is defined
as a QT interval greater than 500 msec or if the T wave is halfway or more than halfway between the R to R interval. An EKG indicative of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy displays needle-like Q waves and large voltage.

Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK554437/

Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.

question: A 58-year-old man comes to the emergency department because he has increased blood pressure that he noted on a home device this morning. He has no other symptoms. Medical history includes diabetes mellitus, which is monitored by his primary care physician. Temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse rate is 68/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 170/105 mmHg. Neurologic, cardiac, and pulmonary examinations show no abnormalities. Visual acuity is at baseline. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

Expl anation
A. Administer a calcium channel blocker

Elevated Blood Pressure Guidelines state that for asymptomatic elevated blood
pressure, routine medical intervention at an emergency department (ED) is not required. There is a caveat that for patients with poor follow-up, hypertension may be
treated in the ED or therapy initiated for long-term control. First-line treatment options include thiazide diuretics, calcium channel blockers, and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors. This patient has a primary care physician, and outpatient
treatment of his blood pressure is appropriate.
B. Administer insulin
This patient has no signs or symptoms of diabetic ketoacidosis or a hyperosmolar
hyperglycemic state and can resume his normal diabetic treatment regimen and follow-up with his primary care physician as an outpatient.
C. Discharge to home with outpatient follow-up
This patient has asymptomatic hypertension without signs of end-organ dysfunction. Uncontrolled blood pressure is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease,

Elevated Blood Pressure Guidelines state that for asymptomatic markedly elevated
blood pressure, routine screening for acute target organ injury (e.g., serum creatinine, urinalysis, electrocardiography) is not required, though for patients with poor
follow-up, screening for an elevated creatinine level may identify renal disease that
affects disposition. Furthermore, routine medical intervention in the emergency department (ED) is not required. There is a caveat that for patients with poor followup, hypertension may be treated in the ED or therapy initiated for long-term
control. First-line treatment options include thiazide diuretics, calcium channel

question: A 55-year-old male with a history of recently diagnosed and untreated small cell lung cancer presents with acute on chronic shortness of breath for 1-2 hours. He is speaking 4-5 word sentences and is diaphoretic. Vital signs are: BP 78/45 mmHg, P 121/min, RR 29/min, T99.0ºF (37.2ºC), O₂Sat 99% room air. Lung auscultation demonstrates minimal bibasilar crackles, and cardiac auscultation reveals muffled heart sounds. The patient demonstrates 6cm jugular venous distention. ECG is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step in the management of this patient?
englishExplanation:
Expl anation
Normal saline IV bolus
A. Dobutamine
Inotropic agents may be useful as an adjunct, but in this patient with acute cardiac
tamponade and its preload dependent state, the best next step is to administer a
large isotonic fluid bolus.
B. Needle thoracostomy
This patient is presenting in acute pericardial tamponade, not with tension pneumothorax. Tension pneumothorax can also present with jugular venous distention
but has decreased or absent breath sounds and tracheal deviation.
C. Normal saline IV bolus
This patient has acute cardiac tamponade and is in a preload-dependent state.
Initial management is a fluid bolus in order to maintain RV pressure until definitive
surgical management or pericardiocentesis can be performed. The ECG demonstrates electrical alternans which may be seen in cardiac tamponade.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK534806/
Jouriles NJ. Chapter 68. Pericardial and Myocardial Disease. In: Walls RM,
Hockberger RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and
Clinical Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
D. Rapid Sequence Intubation
While this is a tempting answer, a trial of isotonic fluid bolus to increase preload
should be attempted first. Positive pressure mechanical ventilation generally increases intrathoracic pressures (which increases right atrial pressure and decreases
venous return), and in patients with acute cardiac tamponade should be avoided
(unless absolutely necessary) given its preload-dependent state.

question: Which of the following intravenous regimens is recommended for the treatment of intracranial hemorrhage resulting from hypertensive emergency?

options.text: Hydralazine 10 mg every four hours to reduce systolic blood pressure to 120 mmHg
Nicardipine 5 mg/hr titrated to decrease systolic blood pressure to between 140 and 160 mmHg
Nitroprusside 1.0 µg/kg/min until systolic blood pressure is less than 140 mmHg
Phentolamine 5 mg every one to two hours until systolic blood pressure is less than 140 mmHg

correctAnswer: Nicardipine 5 mg/hr titrated to decrease systolic blood pressure to between 140 and 160 mmHg
englishExplanation:
Nicardipine 5 mg/hr titrated to decrease systolic blood pressure to between 140
and 160 mmHg
Expl anation
A. Hydralazine 10 mg every four hours to reduce systolic blood pressure
to 120 mmHg
Hydralazine has been used off-label for hypertensive emergencies but is not recommended as a first-line agent due to variability in the onset and duration of action
and due to the side effect profile. It can cause hypotension, headache, palpitations,
and dizziness.
B. Nicardipine 5 mg/hr titrated to decrease systolic blood pressure to
between 140 and 160 mmHg
Intracranial hemorrhage is associated with hypertension; antihypertensive therapy
is recommended to reduce further bleeding as well as surrounding edema. Careful
titration to a systolic blood pressure to between 140 and 160 mmHg IS necessary to
avoid cerebral hypoperfusion. Nicardipine or labetalol are first-line agents.
Further reading: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK470371/
C. Nitroprusside 1.0 pg/kg/min until systolic blood pressure is less than
140 mmHg
Nitroprusside is not recommended in the setting of intracranial hemorrhage due to
its adverse effects on cerebral autoregulation and ability to raise intracranial
pressure.
D. Phentolamine 5 mg every one to two hours until systolic blood
pressure is less than 140 mmHg
Phentolamine is an alpha-I inhibitor causing vasodilation. This is used for hypertensive emergencies related to pheochromocytoma or sympathetic crisis. It is not
used in the setting of intracranial hemorrhage.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: نزيف داخل الجمجمة (intracranial hemorrhage) مرتبط دائماً بارتفاع الضغط، ولازم ننزل الضغط بلطف عشان نوقف النزيف ونتقص الـ edema حول النسيج. المهم إن الـ systolic blood pressure يقعد بين 140 و 160 mmHg، لأن النزول تحت كذا بيسبب cerebral hypoperfusion. و Nicardipine أو labetalol هم agents الخط الأول، و nicardipine بيبدأ بجرعة صغيرة وبيتعدّل حسب رد الفعل.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تنزل الـ systolic تحت 140 أو تستخدم nitroprusside، لأنه بيعبّط cerebral autoregulation وممكن يرفع intracranial pressure. و hydralazine و phentolamine مو خط أول لأن تأثيرهما متغيّر أو مخصصين لحالات ثانية.

question: Which of the following medications is indicated as the first-line therapeutic for symptomatic hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy?
englishExplanation:
Metoprolol
Expl anation
A. Benazepril
Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors are avoided since they decrease afterload
and can lead to worsening left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in patients with
hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy.
B. Furosemide
Diuretics are only used if patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy
develop secondary heart failure, fluid retention, and/or pulmonary edema.
C. Metoprolol
The first-line treatment for symptomatic hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy
(HOCM) is a beta-blocker.
HOCM is associated with obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract either at
rest or on physiologic exertion. Depending on the severity, left ventricular outflow
tract obstruction can lead to symptoms of dyspnea, chest pain, syncope, fatigue, and
sudden cardiac death. Beta-blockers increase diastolic filling and mediate catecholamine effects on left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. Verapamil and
disopyramide can be used as well but are not first-line. Severe symptoms refractory
to medication therapy also have the option of septal myectomy.
Management of HOCM starts with lifestyle modification such as appropriate hydration, avoidance of caffeine and alcohol, appropriate exercise, and diet. Patients with
HOCM are not to participate in competitive athletics since an abrupt elevation in
catecholamines may trigger sudden cardiac arrest.
Further information:
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34915981/

Hockberger RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and
Clinical Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
D. Nitroglycerin
Nitrates are avoided, since they decrease afterload and can lead to worsening left
ventricular outflow tract obstruction in patients with hypertrophic obstructive

question: A 65-year-old female with a history of hypertension is brought in by ambulance for loss of consciousness just prior to arrival. Fingerstick glucose in the field did not reveal hypoglycemia. She was standing in line at the supermarket when she suddenly felt lightheaded and then lost consciousness which, per witnesses, lasted 2 minutes. She denies head injury, preceding palpitations, headache, chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, numbness, or tingling. Vital signs are normal. ECG does not show abnormalities. Laboratory workup included normal hemoglobin. What is the most likely cause of this patient's syncope?
englishExplanation:
Expl anation
A. Cardiac
Vasovagal
While cardiac syncope must be ruled out, this patient is not experiencing bradycardia, tachycardia, hypotension, ECG changes, or abnormal findings indicating a cardiac etiology.
B. Medication-induced
Medication induced syncope IS certainly a consideration, especially in patients on
beta blockers or diuretics, however it is not the most common cause.
C. Orthostatic
Orthostatic hypotension occurs when the blood pressure decreases at least 20 mm
Hg systolic or IO mm Hg diastolic within three minutes of standing. Orthostatic
syncope results from a postural decrease in blood pressure causing a transient loss
of consciousness due to reduced blood flow to the cerebrum. Symptoms are typically
dizziness, diaphoresis, nausea, and/or vision changes. Neurally mediated (neurogenic) and non-neurally mediated causes can lead to syncope.
D. Vasovagal
Syncope is defined as a temporary loss of consciousness due to a reduction of blood
flow to the brain with a subsequent spontaneous return to baseline. There are many
causes of syncope that range from simple non-cardiac causes, such as vasovagal
syncope, to life-threatening cardiac causes, like hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. It is
imperative that cardiac causes of syncope are identified, and those patients are admitted for further workup. Vasovagal syncope is the most common cause of syncope, but other causes include neurologic (10%), medication-induced, bleeding (hypotension), and idiopathic (30%).
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK470277/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها vasovagal syncope، لأنها كانت واقفة بالطابور وفجأة حسيت بدوار ثم فقدت الوعي ورجعت لحالها، وكل العلامات القلبية سليمة. الـ syncope بيعرف إنه فقد مؤقت للوعي بسبب نقص الدم للمخ مع رجوع تلقائي للوضع الطبيعي، و vasovagal syncope هو السبب الأكثر شيوعاً. ما في عندها bradycardia ولا tachycardia ولا hypotension ولا تغييرات بالـ ECG، فالأسباب القلبية أقل احتمال.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تروح على cardiac syncope أو medication-induced من أول ما تشوف المريضة. افرق إن الـ cardiac syncope بيصير مع bradycardia أو tachycardia أو hypotension أو تخطيط غير طبيعي، و الـ orthostatic hypotension بيحتاج انخفاض 20 systolic أو 10 diastolic خلال 3 دقائق من الوقوف.

question: A 3-year-old male with a history of tetralogy of Fallot is brought in by his parents for shortness of breath. Vital signs are: HR 130/min, RR 35/min, O₂ sat 88% on RA, T 98.6ºF (37ºC). Physical exam reveals a cyanotic male in moderate distress with crescendo-decrescendo harsh systolic ejection murmur. Which of the following is most likely to improve this patient’s condition?
englishExplanation:
Knees to chest position
Expl anation
A. Furosemide
This patient is suffering from a "Tet spell." Furosemide will reduce afterload and
will not work acutely for th1S condition.
B. Hydralazine
Hydralazine will decrease afterload. This patient is suffering from a Tet spell in
which afterload must be increased.
C. Knees to chest position
This patient with tetrology of Fallot is suffering from a "Tet spell." "Tet spells" are
hypercyanotic episodes that present during infancy or toddler age and decrease after five years of age. Dehydration or agitation can precipitate these spells, and if
children do not receive prompt treatment, they can develop cyanosis and hypoxia.
Tetralogy of Fallot is a congenital cyanotic heart condition with four anomalies:
overriding aorta, ventricular septal defect, pulmonary stenosis, and right ventricular
hypertrophy. Tet spells occur due to episodes of cyanosis that result from right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) obstruction. This transient RVOT obstruction occurs
typically during exercise or agitation. As a result, blood is shunted through the VSD
away from the lungs. Treatment is forcing blood back into the lungs to facilitate oxygenation. This can be done by increasing afterload (knee to chest position, phenylephrine if needed) or by increasing pulmonary flow (morphine, beta blockers).
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK513288/
D. Nitroprusside
Nitroprusside will decrease afterload. This patient is suffering from a Tet spell and
the afterload must be increased.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالطفل عنده tetralogy of Fallot وعمره 3 سنين، وهو واقع في نوبة اسمها Tet spell يعني نوبة زرقه حادة سببها انسداد الـ right ventricular outflow tract، فالدم بيتحاشى عن الرئة عن طريق الـ VSD. العلاج الأول هو وضعية الركبتين على الصدر (knees to chest position) لأنها بتزود الـ afterload وبترجّع الدم على الرئة. وممكن نضيف morphine أو beta blockers لزيادة الـ pulmonary flow، و phenylephrine لو احتجنا. ولاحظ إن الـ Tet spells بتقل بعد سن الخمس.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تنزل الـ afterload بـ furosemide أو hydralazine، لأنهم بيعملوا العكس المطلوب تمامًا. افرق إن الهدف هنا مو إنك تنزّل الضغط، بل إنك ترفع الـ afterload عشان الدم يرجع يوكسجيني.

question: A 14-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department because he had sudden onset of light-headedness and near syncope during football practice. The patient is currently asymptomatic, and vital signs are within normal limits. Which of the following findings during evaluation is most likely to indicate that this patient needs to be referred to a cardiologist prior to clearing him to return to sports activity?

options.text: Electrocardiography with decreased voltage in the QRS complexes
Electrocardiography with deep narrow Q waves in the lateral leads
Harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur that increases with hand grip
Soft ejection murmur heard in the second left intercostal space that increases in intensity after exercise

correctAnswer: Electrocardiography with deep narrow Q waves in the lateral leads
englishExplanation:
Electrocardiography with deep narrow Q waves in the lateral leads
Expl anation
A. Electrocardiography with decreased voltage in the QRS complexes
Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is a pathologic cardiac condition in which
the interventricular septum is abnormally thickened. The most common ECG finding is evidence of LVH. This is indicated by increased voltage in the QRS complexes,
particularly in the precordial leads (VI-V6) and lateral leads (I, aVL).
B. Electrocardiography with deep narrow Q waves in the lateral leads
Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is a pathologic cardiac condition in which
the interventricular septum is abnormally thickened. The classic ECG finding in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is large dagger-like "septal Q waves" in the
lateral, and sometimes Inferior, leads due to the abnormally hypertrophied interventricular septum. Criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy are usually present.
These patients should be referred to a cardiologist for further evaluation prior to
participating in sports due to the risk of sudden cardiac death.
Further information:
Jouriles NJ. Chapter 68. Pericardial and Myocardial Disease. In: Walls RM,
Hockberger RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and
Clinical Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
C. Harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur that increases with
hand grip
The murmur of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur that is best heard at the left upper sternal border. The
murmur, however, decreases with hand grip. In addition, almost all cardiac murmurs decrease in intensity during Valsalva (with the exception of HCM), so this maneuver is a crucial part of the cardiac examination if HCM is suspected.
D. Soft ejection murmur heard in the second left intercostal space that
increases in intensity after exercise
This a describing a pulmonary flow murmur, which is a benign murmur. It is a flow
murmur of a normal pulmonary valve. The increased flow of blood caused by conditions such as anenua, fever, and exercise makes this murmur louder.
Page 456 of 4185
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالولد عندو near-syncope أثناء التمرين مع exertion، وهاد من علامات hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy اللي ممكن تسبب sudden cardiac death عند الرياضيين. السمة المميزة بتظهر بالـ ECG على شكل deep narrow septal Q waves بشكل dagger في الـ lateral leads وأحيانًا الـ inferior leads، وغالبًا كمان تلاقي معايير LVH موجودة. ولما تشوف هيك ECG لازم تحوّله على cardiologist قبل ما يرجع يمارس الرياضة.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تاخذ decreased voltage في QRS على أنه HOCM، بس العكس صحيح: التصلب بيزوّد الجهد مش بيقلله. و الـ murmur في HOCM crescendo-decrescendo هارد، بس ما بيزيد مع hand grip.

question: A 3-month-old male infant is brought to the emergency department because he has had sudden crying spells during the past three weeks, and he is getting progressively harder to console. His parents noticed that today while crying, the patient's lips and fingernails turned visibly blue. On physical examination, a crescendo-decrescendo harsh systolic ejection murmur is heard on auscultation. A ventricular septal defect is noted on echocardiography. Which of the following additional findings is most likely to be noted on echocardiography?

options.text: A single great vessel arising from the heart
Transposition of the aorta and pulmonary artery

englishExplanation:
Pulmonary stenosis
Expl anation
A. A single great vessel arising from the heart
During normal fetal development, a single blood vessel divides to form the lower
portion of the aorta and the lower portion of the pulmonary artery. When this divi-
Sion does not occur during fetal development and a single vessel persists, this is
known as truncus arteriosus. A VSD is also present. Severe cyanotic symptoms usually develop within the first few days of life.
B. Pulmonary stenosis
This infant has Tetralogy of Fallot, which is a congenital cyanotic heart disease consisting of four core anatomic features: a ventricular septal defect, overriding aorta
(an enlarged aortic valve that appears to arise from both ventricles instead of the
left ventricle only), pulmonary stenosis, and right ventricular hypertrophy. The
crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur is caused by the right ventricular outflow
obstruction. If this obstruction becomes severe, right-to-left shunting may occur,
causing cyanosis. The infant's episodes of cyanotic crying are known as "tet spells."
Further information: https://w•ww.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK513288/
C. Transposition of the aorta and pulmonary artery
Transposition of the aorta and pulmonary artery is known as "transposition of the
great arteries." A ventricular septal defect is present in about 50% of infants with
this condition. Transposition of the great arteries causes cyanosis at birth and is
typically diagnosed and surgically repaired within the first week of life. It would
therefore be unlikely as a cause of new-onset cyanosis in a 3-month-old
infant. There IS not typically a murmur present, though murmurs may be found, depending on whether a VSD or left ventricular outflow obstruction is also present.
D. Tricuspid valve atresia
Tricuspid valve atresia is always associated with an atrial septal defect and also is
usually accompanied by a ventricular septal defect. A hypoplastic right ventricle is
also present. This is most often diagnosed during the first day of life and almost always by 1 month of age.
Page 472 of 4185
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالرضيع عنده tetralogy of Fallot، وهي congenital cyanotic heart disease بأربع عيوب أساسية: ventricular septal defect، و overriding aorta، و pulmonary stenosis، و right ventricular hypertrophy. الـ murmur الحاد crescendo-decrescendo اللي سمعناه سببه انسداد الـ right ventricular outflow tract، وإذا اشتد الانسداد صار shunt من اليمين لليسار، وهاد سبب نوبات البكاء الزرقاء اللي اسمها tet spells. الـ echo كشف الـ VSD، و pulmonary stenosis هي العنصر الرابع بتلاقيه.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تفكر بـ truncus arteriosus لأنه فيها VSD بعد. افرق إن هاد الـ lesion فيه vessel واحد بس وبيسبب زرق شديد أول أيام الحياة، بينما tet spells عند هالرضيع بتنتهي غالبًا بعد سن الخمس.

question: Which of the following patients should receive amoxicillin as prophylaxis prior to undergoing a procedure?

options.text: A patient with Marfan's undergoing rapid sequence intubation
A patient with mitral valve prolapse undergoing foley catheterization
A patient with prosthetic aortic valve with periapical abscess pending tooth extraction
A patient with rheumatic valvular disease undergoing chest tube placement

correctAnswer: A patient with Marfan's undergoing rapid sequence intubation
englishExplanation:
A patient with prosthetic aortic valve with periapical abscess pending tooth
extraction
Expl anation
A. A patient with Marfan's undergoing rapid sequence intubation
Marfan's is not considered a high-risk indication for prophylaxis. Endotracheal intubation is not concerned a high-risk procedure that would lead to bacteremia.
B. A patient with mitral valve prolapse undergoing foley catheterization
Current guidelines no longer recommend giving prophylactic antibiotics to patients
with mitral valve prolapse.
C. A patient with prosthetic aortic valve with periapical abscess pending
tooth extraction
According to the 2017 AHA guidelines:
Prophylaxis against endocarditis is reasonable before dental procedures that involve
manipulation of gingival tissue, manipulation of the periapical region of teeth, or
perforation of the oral mucosa in patients who have prosthetic cardiac valves or
prosthetic material used for cardiac valve repair. Prophylaxis should have adequate
gram-positive coverage, with the preferred antibiotic being amoxicillin 2gm PO,
given 30-60 minutes prior to the procedure.
Further information: https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/JAHA.117.007596
D. A patient with rheumatic valvular disease undergoing chest tube
placement
Rheumatic valvular disease is not considered a high-risk predisposing factor. Chest
tube placement is not considered a high-risk procedure resulting in bacteremia.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض اللي عنده prosthetic aortic valve ومعه periapical abscess وبيستنى tooth extraction هو اللي لازم ياخذ prophylaxis بـ amoxicillin قبل الإجراء. حسب إرشادات AHA لعام 2017، الـ prophylaxis معقول قبل أي dental procedure فيها manipulation للـ gingival tissue أو للـ periapical region أو perforation للـ oral mucosa، والمرضى اللي عندهم prosthetic cardiac valves أو prosthetic material مستعمل في إصلاح الصمام بيعتبروا من الفئة هاي. الجرعة المفضلة amoxicillin 2 gm عن طريق الفم قبل الإجراء بـ 30-60 دقيقة، والهدف تغطية gram-positive.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تعطي prophylaxis لمريض Marfan's وقت Rapid Sequence Intubation، لأنه مو indication عالية الخطورة و الـ intubation ما بيسبب bacteremia. و mitral valve prolapse مع Foley catheterization كمان مو لحاله يستاهل prophylaxis حسب الإرشادات الحديثة.

question: A 68-year-old man comes into the emergency department via EMS. His ECG currently shows PEA. Which of the following is the most common cause of this rhythm?
englishExplanation:
Hypovolemia
Expl anation
A. Coronary vasospasm
Spasm of the smooth muscle of the coronary arteries can cause transient coronary
occlusion, ischemia, and infarction. It is a rare cause of PEA.
B. Digitalis toxicity
Digitalis toxicity can lead to multiple arrhythmias, including premature ventricular
contractions, AV block, ventricular tachycardia, and ventricular fibrillation. It can
also result in PLA, though this is less common.
C. Hypokalemia
Hypokalemia may be a contributing factor in PEA, but it is rarely the primary cause.
D. Hypovolemia
Pulseless electrical activity (PEA) is the presence of organized electrical activity
without sufficient mechanical contraction of the heart needed to produce a pulse.
Severe hypovolemia is the most common cause of PLA. Hypovolemia results in reduced preload, which prevents the lengthening of cardiac sarcomeres that is needed
to produce meaningful contractions.
The possible causes are remembered as the 6 Hs (Hypovolemia, Hypoxia, Hydrogen
ions (Acidosis), Hyperkalemia or Hypokalemia, Hypoglycemia, Hypothermia) and
the 6 Ts (Tablets or Toxins, Cardiac Tamponade, Tension pneumothorax,
Thrombosis (e.g., MI, PE), Tachycardia, Trauma (e.g., hypovolemia from blood
loss).
Further information: https://w•ww.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK513349/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ PEA معناها إنك شايف نشاط كهربائي منتظم على المونيتور بدون نبض محسوس، و السبب الأكثر شيوعًا لها هو severe hypovolemia. السبب إن نقص الـ preload ما بيخلي الـ sarcomeres تطول، فما بيطلع انقباض فعّال للقلب. لازم تتذكر الـ 6 Hs: hypovolemia, hypoxia, hydrogen ions, hyperkalemia أو hypokalemia, hypoglycemia, hypothermia، ومعها الـ 6 Ts: tablets أو toxins, cardiac tamponade, tension pneumothorax, thrombosis, tachycardia, trauma.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تختار coronary vasospasm أو digitalis toxicity أو hypokalemia. افرق إن الـ vasospasm سبب نادر للـ PEA، و الـ digitalis toxicity ممكن يسوي عدة arrhythmias بس أقل شيوعًا، و الـ hypokalemia نادرًا ما تكون السبب الأساسي.

question: A 70-year-old male presents to a Level 1 emergency department with one hour of crushing left-sided chest pain. Past medical history is significant for a history of ischemic stroke nine months previously. Vital signs are: BP 180/110 mmHg, HR 90/min, RR 12/min, and O₂sat 100%. He is ill-appearing and diaphoretic. EKG is shown. Which of the following is the best intervention for this patient's likely condition?

options.text: Emergently lower the blood pressure using IV agents, then administer thrombolytics

englishExplanation:
Aspirin and percutaneous coronary intervention
Expl anation
A. Aspirin alone
Aspirin alone is not the appropriate management for a STEMI.
B. Aspirin and percutaneous coronary intervention
This EKG demonstrates ST depressions in VI-V5, with prominent R waves in VI and
V2, concerning for an acute posterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Although the patient does not have any absolute contraindications to thrombolytics,
as the patient is at a center where percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) can be
performed within 90 minutes and has a STEMI, PCI is preferred to thrombolytic
therapy.
Further information: O'Gara VI', Kushner FG, Ascheim DD, et al. 2013 ACC/AHA
Guideline for the Management of ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction. Circulation.
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/23247304
C. Aspirin and tenecteplase
If percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) can be initiated within 90 minutes, it is
the better answer choice.
D. Emergently lower the blood pressure using IV agents, then
administer thrombolytics
Elevated blood pressure is only a relative contraindication to thrombolytics, and
PCI would still be preferred.

![HIPPO-00458 source page 483](images/HIPPO-00458-Hipoo-p0483.jpg)

![HIPPO-00458 source page 484](images/HIPPO-00458-Hipoo-p0484.jpg)

ليش: الـ ECG عنده ST depressions في V1-V5 مع R waves بارزة في V1 و V2، وهاد pattern بيوحي بـ posterior STEMI مو بس unstable angina. فالأنسب تعطيه aspirin مع percutaneous coronary intervention. المريض ما عنده contraindications مطلقة للـ thrombolytics، بس مركزه بيقدر يعمل PCI خلال 90 دقيقة، و guidelines بتفضّل الـ PCI على الـ thrombolytic therapy في هالحالة.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تكتفي بـ aspirin لحاله أو تعطي thrombolytics بدل الـ PCI. افرق إن aspirin لحاله ما بتكفي في STEMI، وإن عنده مركز يقدر يعمل PCI خلال 90 دقيقة فالـ PCI أفضل من الـ thrombolysis.

question: A 68-year-old female, with a history of lung cancer, presents to the emergency department with pleuritic chest pain and fatigue for three days. She also notes shortness of breath which worsens at night when she lays in bed. On physical examination, jugular venous distention is noticed along with a pericardial friction rub. The ECG shown reveals which of the following most likely diagnoses?
englishExplanation:
Pericardial effusion
Expl anation
A. Endocarditis
Endocarditis is inflammation of the endocardial surface of the heart (usually involving the heart valves), commonly due to infection. Risk factors include previous
valvular disease or surgery, IV drug use, recent dental procedure, and immunosuppression. Most cases are due to staphylococcus, streptococcus, and enterococcus
species. Patients may have fever, a new murmur, petechiae, splinter hemorrhages,
Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, and Roth spots. There are no specific characteristic
ECG findings, though heart block and signs of ischemia may be present.
B. Pericardial effusion
The ECG finding pictured here is electrical alternans, though seen uncommonly, is
considered pathognomonic for pericardial effusion. Electrical alternans is characterized by alteration of QRS complex height in every other beat due to the heart
swinging back and forth in the fluid-filled pericardium. The other two most common ECG findings associated with pericardial effusion are low voltage of QRS complexes and sinus tachycardia.
A pericardial effusion is the accumulation of fluid within the pericardial space. It
has multiple causes, including infection, trauma, autoimmune disorders, and malignancy. This patient's history of lung cancer is a common risk factor for developing
pericardial effusion. Echocardiography is needed to confirm the diagnosis.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK431089/
C. Pericarditis
Pericarditis is inflammation of the pericardial sac. Though pericardial friction rub is
considered characteristic in cases of pericarditis, it is also seen in pericardial effusions, even with larger volumes. Diffuse ST segment elevation is indicative of
pericarditis.
D. Pulmonary embolism
A pulmonary embolism is the obstruction of a pulmonary artery by an embolus.
Patients typically present with dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. The most common
ECG abnormality is tachycardia. Classically, the ECG associated with a PE is de-
Page 486 of 4185
scribed by a SIQ3T3 pattern: large S in lead I, the presence of a Q wave in lead III,
and an inverted T wave in lead III.

![HIPPO-00459 source page 484](images/HIPPO-00459-Hipoo-p0484.jpg)

![HIPPO-00459 source page 485](images/HIPPO-00459-Hipoo-p0485.jpg)

![HIPPO-00459 source page 486](images/HIPPO-00459-Hipoo-p0486.jpg)

![HIPPO-00459 source page 487](images/HIPPO-00459-Hipoo-p0487.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ ECG عندها بيبيّن electrical alternans، يعني ارتفاع الـ QRS بيتبدّل مع كل نبضة، وهاد بيحصل لأن القلب بيتأرجح جوه pericardium مليانة سائل. هاي العلامة نادرة بس بيعتبرها pathognomonic لـ pericardial effusion. المريضة عندها تاريخ سرطان رئة و JVD و pericardial friction rub، و سرطان الرئة سبب شائع لتجمع السوائل حول القلب. والـ echocardiography مطلوبة لتأكيد التشخيص، ومن أكتر علامات الـ ECG شيوعًا معها low voltage للـ QRS و sinus tachycardia.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تشخّصها endocarditis لأن عندها murmur أو علامات التهاب. افرق إن الـ endocarditis غالبًا بييجي مع حرارة و new murmur و petechiae و splinter hemorrhages، وما إله أي findings مميزة بالـ ECG بعكس الـ electrical alternans.

question: A 66-year-old male with a known 6 cm aortic aneurysm presents with sudden onset abdominal pain, hypotension, and a palpable abdominal mass. What is the most common site that an aneurysm will rupture into?
englishExplanation:
Retroperitoneum
Expl anation
A. Gastrointestinal tract
While this is a possible site of rupture and can be a cause of massive GI bleed, it is
not the most common location.
B. Inferior vena cava
While an aorto-caval fistula can form as a complication of an abdominal aortic aneurysm, this is rare.
C. Intraperitoneum
Intraperitoneal ruptures can occur but are not common
D. Retroperitoneum
All of the answer choices are sites that aortic aneurysms may rupture into, but aortic
aneurysms most commonly rupture into the retroperitoneum. The most rapidly fatal location is the intraperitoneum. Less common sites of rupture include the gastrointestinal tract and the inferior vena cava.
Further information:
Cowell CB. Chapter 72. Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
Prince LA, Johnson GA. Chapter 60. Aneurysmal Disease. In: Tintinalli JE, Ma OJ,
Yealy DM, Meckler GD, Stapuynski JS, Cline DM, Thomas SH, eds. Tintinalli's
Emergency Medicine: A Comprehensive Study Guide, 9e. New York, NY: McGraw-
Hill; 2020.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: كل الخيارات هاي ممكن aneurysm ينفجر فيها، بس الأكثر شيوعًا هو retroperitoneum. المرجع عنده aneurysm 6 cm وبده sudden abdominal pain مع hypotension و abdominal mass palpable، وهاد pattern الكلاسيكي للrupture. الـ retroperitoneum بيخلي النزيف يبقى محصور، بينما الـ intraperitoneum هو الأشد fatality يعني أسرع ما بrmse. الـ gastrointestinal tract و الـ inferior vena cava أقل شيوعًا، و الـ aorto-caval fistula نادرة.

question: A 63-year-old male presents to the emergency department complaining of fatigue for the last several weeks. Past medical history is significant for diabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol. He had a dental root canal procedure performed 6 weeks prior to his ED presentation. Vitals signs are: BP 148/90 mmHg, P 94/min, RR 14/min, O₂sat 97%RA. He complains of subjective fevers at home but is afebrile on presentation. Laboratory testing is significant for hemoglobin 9.7 g/dl, MCV 84. Exam is notable for a faint diastolic murmur heard best at the apex. Which of the following is the most likely organism causing his disease process?
englishExplanation:
Streptococcus viridans
Expl anation
A. Clostridium botulinum
Unless the dentist used rusted and unclean, or recently unearthed and unsanitized
equipment, Clostridium botulinum is unlikely to be an infectious agent, let alone
the cause for this patient's infective endocarditis.
B. Staphylococcus aureus
While Staph aureus is a very common cause of infective endocarditis, this patient
recently underwent an invasive dental procedure, which specifically increases his
risk of Strep viridans as the causal agent.
C. Staphylococcus epidermidis
While it is a common skin flora, Staph epidermidis is not the likely causative organism in this patient who recently received an invasive dental procedure, leading to
bacteremic seeding of his eventual endocarditis.
D. Streptococcus viridans
The patient in the question has subacute endocarditis, characterized by insidious
onset of fatigue, anemia, and a new diastolic murmur. He likely contracted the infection from his recent dental procedure. Streptococcus viridans is the most common etiologic bacterial agent responsible for causing infective endocarditis secondary to odontogenic procedures. The time range from a dental procedure to the
onset of endocarditis may range from 1 to 6 months.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499844/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريض عنده subacute infective endocarditis: تعب من أسابيع، و أنيميا بـ hemoglobin 9.7، و murmur دياستول جديد خفيف عند الـ apex، و حرارة subjective بدون fever عند وصوله. وبما إنه عمل root canal قبل 6 أسابيع، فالجرثومة الأرجح هي Streptococcus viridans، وهي أكثر بكتيريا مسبب الـ endocarditis بعد procedures الأسنان. الوقت بين الـ dental procedure وبداية الأعراض ممكن يوصل من 1 إلى 6 أشهر، وهاد بيفسّر التأخير.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تختار Staphylococcus aureus لأنه شائع بـ endocarditis. افرق إن الـ recent invasive dental procedure هو اللي بيميل للـ Streptococcus viridans، و Staph epidermidis flora عادية بالجلد وما بتعمل bacteremia بعد الأسنان، و Clostridium botulinum مو منطقي.

question: A 37-year-old man with a history of rheumatic fever as a child is seen in the emergency department for a sore throat. Which of the following heart murmurs is most commonly noted as a late sequela of this disease?

options.text: Diastolic rumble heard best over the left 4th intercostal space
Early diastolic murmur heard best over the right 2nd intercostal space
Low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble, possibly with an opening snap

correctAnswer: Low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble, possibly with an opening snap
englishExplanation:
Low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble, possibly with an opening snap
Expl anation
A. Diastolic rumble heard best over the left 4th intercostal space
This describes tricuspid stenosis.
B. Early diastolic murmur heard best over the right 2nd intercostal
space
This describes aortic regurgitation.
C. Low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble, possibly with an opening snap
The mitral valve is most commonly affected in rheumatic heart disease, the late sequelae of acute rheumatic fever. Mitral stenosis is the most common single valve le-
Sion in patients with RHD after the age of 30. Mitral regurgitation is most common
with RHD in patients younger than age 20.
Reference: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430742/
D. Machine-like, rough continuous murmur
This describes patent ductus arteriosus.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمرجع عنده تاريخ rheumatic fever من صغره، والـ rheumatic heart disease من أشهر مضاعفاته المتأخرة إنه يصيب الـ mitral valve. بعد عمر 30 سنة، أكثر valve lesion شائعة عند مرضى الـ RHD هي mitral stenosis. و الـ mitral stenosis بينتج عنه murmur منخفض النبرة في وسط الـ diastole، وأحيانًا بيطلع opening snap لما الـ valve تنفتح بقوة. أما الـ mitral regurgitation فهو الأكثر شيوعًا عند اللي تحت 20 سنة.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تختار الـ tricuspid stenosis أو aortic regurgitation. افرق إن الـ tricuspid stenosis بتسمع على اليسار space 4، و الـ aortic regurgitation بيبدأ مع الـ diastole وبيتسمع على اليمين space 2، و الـ continuous machinery-like murmur هو PDA.

question: A 35-year-old female presents to the emergency department with a cough productive of blood-tinged sputum for one week. She denies fevers, chills, chest pain, shortness of breath, or other related symptoms. Physical exam is significant for a diastolic murmur, and an opening snap heard best at the apex of the heart without radiation. Vital signs are normal, and the chest x-ray demonstrates no pathology. What is the most likely cause of this patient’s hemoptysis?
englishExplanation:
Mitral stenosis
Expl anation
A. Infective endocarditis
This patient has no infective symptoms to suggest infective endocarditis. Further,
the opening snap is suggestive of another pathology.
B. Libman—Sacks endocarditis
Libman-sacks endocarditis is a non-infectious endocarditis due to lupus erythematosis. This patient has no history of autoimmune disease. Further, the opening
snap is suggestive of another pathology.
C. Mitral stenosis
This patient's cardiac exam and hemoptysis are concerning for mitral stenosis.
Mitral stenosis is due to the narrowing of the mitral valve orifice. The most common
cause is rheumatic fever, but the stenosis may not appear clinically relevant for several decades. Mitral stenosis is associated with a diastolic murmur and an opening
snap can be heard due to the forceful opening of the mitral valve. Mitral stenosis
classically can cause varying degrees of hemoptysis.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430742/
D. Wegener's Syndrome
Wegener's syndrome is a granulomatous autoimmune vasculitis which causes damage to blood vessels and organs. This patient has no history to suggest this disease.
Further, the opening snap is suggestive of another pathology.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها mitral stenosis، والـ hemoptysis عندها نتيجة مباشرة لتضييق الصمام. الـ mitral stenosis بيحصل من تضيق فتحة الـ mitral valve، وأكثر سبب له rheumatic fever، ومعروف إنه ممكن يضل بلا أعراض سريرية لعشرات السنين. بتلاقي عندها diastolic murmur و opening snap واضح عند الـ apex من غير radiation، والـ opening snap بيحصل لما الـ valve تنفتح بقوة. و الـ hemoptysis بشكله الكلاسيكي بيصير مع mitral stenosis.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تشخّصها infective endocarditis أو Libman-Sacks endocarditis. افرق إن الـ infective endocarditis بييجي مع حرارة وأعراض التهاب، والـ Libman-Sacks سببه lupus فلا في تاريخ autoimmune disease عندها، والـ opening snap بيرجّع لمشكلة صمامي.

question: An otherwise healthy 48-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by her partner after she had an episode of syncope two hours ago. She is currently asymptomatic. The patient says she was having her blood drawn when she suddenly felt nauseous, noted tunnel vision, and lost consciousness. She was seated in a chair, and the phlebotomist said that she lost consciousness for approximately 20 seconds. Vital signs are within normal limits, and physical examination shows no abnormalities. Electrocardiography also shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
englishExplanation:
Discharge to home
Expl anation
A. Discharge to home
Using the Canadian Syncope Risk tool, this patient's score is -3, which equates to a
0.7 to 1.9% risk of a 30-day serious adverse event. This places her at the lowest risk;
therefore, it is considered appropriate to discharge her to home from the emergency
department (ED) without further observation, workup, or interventions. She can
follow-up with a primary care doctor one week after the initial encounter.
The Canadian Syncope Risk tool takes into account the following: predisposition to
vasovagal syncope, heart disease, systolic pressure in the ED or >180 mmHg,
troponin level >99th percentile for the normal population, abnormal QRS axis (<
—300 or > 1000), QRS duration >130 ms, QTc interval > 480 ms, ED diagnosis of
cardiac syncope or vasovagal syncope. This tool has been externally validated and is
used to predict 30-day serious adverse events in patients presenting with syncope.
It should only be used in patients 216 years of age who present within 24 hours of a
syncopal episode. It should not be used for any patients who have experienced prolonged loss of consciousness min), a baseline mental status change, obvious witnessed seizure, major trauma requiring hospital admission, alcohol or illicit drug intoxication, language barrier, or head trauma causing loss of consciousness.
Further information: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30661373/
B. Observe in the emergency department
This patient has vasovagal syncope that resulted from the sudden drop in blood
pressure and subsequent decrease in cerebral perfusion pressure, which results in a
transient loss of consciousness. Common triggers of vasovagal syncope include
straining, stress, prolonged standing, heat exposure, or the sight of blood. Her
Canadian Syncope Risk score is -3, putting her at very low risk; therefore, discharge
to home with close follow-up is appropriate.
C. Obtain a troponin level
A troponin level is indicated if the clinician suspects a critical arrhythmia or ischemic event. A troponin level is not necessary in order to use the Canadian
Syncope Risk tool. The clinician may use clinical discretion and score the value as
"no," not pathologically elevated if ischemia is not suspected. This is reasonable in
Page 522 of 4185
this case given the patient's age, lack of comorbidities, and presentation. Coronary
ischemia rarely precipitates syncope with the patient appearing benign afterward.
D. Repeat electrocardiography
Arrhythmia is the most common pathologic cause of syncope, which usually occurs
in a biphasic manner (in the first 60 minutes and then five to 10 days after discharge). Therefore, even on the off-chance this is more than vasovagal syncope, the
likelihood that a change will occur in the electrocardiography while monitoring in
the emergency department is low. It is also not indicated given the patient's
Canadian Syncope Risk score of -3.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ syncope عندها كلاسيكي vasovagal: كانت قاعدة وهي تتسحب دم، حسيت بغثيان و tunnel vision، وفقدت الوعي 20 ثانية بس ورجعت لحالها. حسب Canadian Syncope Risk tool، نتيجتها -3، يعني خطر serious adverse event خلال 30 يوم بين 0.7% و1.9% بس، وهي أقل فئة خطورة. عشان كده الأنسب تطلعها من الـ ED بدون observation أو تحاليل أو تدخلات إضافية، وتتابع مع primary care doctor بعد أسبوع.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تحجزها observation أو تطلب troponin أو تعيد الـ ECG. افرق إن الـ vitals والـ ECG عندها طبيعيين ونوبة الإغماء قصيرة، وهي بأقل فئة خطورة بالـ Canadian Syncope Risk tool، فمافي داعي لهالخطوات الإضافية.

question: Which of the following conditions is most likely to be associated with a physical examination finding of a machinery-like murmur?
englishExplanation:
Expl anation
Patent ductus arteriosus
A. Atrial septal defect
Communication between the atria. Murmur characterized by a systolic ejection
murmur that will vary based on the size of the defect. The smaller the defect the
louder the murmur.
B. Coarctation of the aorta
Narrowing of the descending aorta that often results in a late harsh systolic murmur. Patients with coarctation of the aorta may have blood pressure differences in
the two arms depending on where the aorta narrows.
C. Patent ductus arteriosus
Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) represents 5-10% of all congenital heart lesions.
Structurally, it is a persistent communication between the descending thoracic
aorta, and the pulmonary artery that results from failure of normal physiologic closure of the fetal ductus. The hallmark physical examination finding is a continuous
murmur, located at the upper left sternal border, often referred to as a "machinery"
murmur. The murmur often radiates down the left side of the sternum into the
back, and a thrill may also be present.
References:
https : / ,/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430758/
Horeczko T. Chapter 165. Pediatric Cardiac Disorders. In: Walls RM, Hockberger
RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical
Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
D. Ventricular septal defect
Results in a holosystolic murmur heard best in the tricuspid area of auscultation. A
smaller VSD will result in a louder murmur.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الـ murmur اللي اسمه machinery-like هو continuous murmur، وبيطلع بالـ upper left sternal border وبيزول على طول الـ left side of the sternum وللظهر، وأحيانًا بيكون معاه thrill. هاد الوصف الكلاسيكي لـ patent ductus arteriosus، وهي persistent communication بين الـ descending thoracic aorta و pulmonary artery بسبب ما انغلق الـ fetal ductus بشكل طبيعي. والـ PDA بشكل 5-10% من الـ congenital heart lesions كلها.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تختار ventricular septal defect أو atrial septal defect. افرق إن الـ VSD بيعمل holosystolic murmur في منطقة الـ tricuspid، والـ ASD بيعمل systolic ejection murmur بيشدّ حسب حجم الفتحة، والـ PDA هو الوحيد اللي بيعمل continuous murmur.

question: A 13-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department by her coach 15 minutes after she had an episode of syncope during field hockey practice. She has no history of similar episodes, and she is otherwise healthy. Immunizations are up-to-date. The patient's parents are on their way to the hospital. The patient believes she may have had a distant aunt who passed away suddenly at a young age. Cardiac auscultation shows an S1 and S2 without murmurs. Electrocardiography is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
Expl anation
A. Brugada arrhythmia
Patients with Brugada syndrome may present with exertional syncope or may suffer
from sudden death, but it is demonstrated by specific EKG findings (ST-segment elevation in leads VI and V2) that do not match the one in this scenario.
B. Congenital short QT syndrome
This is a very rare inherited channelopathy that can cause syncope and sudden cardiac death in patients with structurally normal hearts.
C. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
An important cause of exertional ischemia in young athletes, HOCM is less likely in
this patient because she does not have the characteristic EKG findings of prominent
voltage or repolarization, and she does not have the physical examination findings
of systolic murmur or extra heart sounds.
D. Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
Classic ECG findings for Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome include a short PR interval and the presence of a delta wave, which can be seen in this ECG. A delta wave
is the fusion of the early depolarization by the accessory pathway and the normal activation via the AV node system.
Further information:
Yealy D, Kosowsky J. Chapter 65. Dysrhythmias. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.

![HIPPO-00484 source page 539](images/HIPPO-00484-Hipoo-p0539.jpg)

![HIPPO-00484 source page 540](images/HIPPO-00484-Hipoo-p0540.jpg)

![HIPPO-00484 source page 541](images/HIPPO-00484-Hipoo-p0541.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ ECG عندها فيه PR interval قصير مع delta wave، وهاد بالضبط تعريف Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. الـ delta wave هي ناتج إن الـ accessory pathway بت depolarize البطين بدري قبل ما يوصل depolarization الطبيعي عن طريق الـ AV node، فبتخلط مع بعض. البنت عندها syncope أثناء رياضة، وعندها تاريخ عائلي بوفاة مفاجئة بعمر صغير، وهاد كله بيوافق WPW اللي بيسبّب arrhythmias عند الرياضيين الصغار.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تفكر بـ Brugada arrhythmia أو hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. افرق إن الـ Brugada بيبيّن ST elevation في V1 و V2، والـ HOCM بيطلع مع زيادة الجهد و systolic murmur، ومافي ولا وحدة منهم بتطلع PR قصير مع delta wave.

question: A 70-year-old male is brought in by ambulance after fainting while walking up a flight of stairs. The patient states, "I feel lightheaded, I do not know what happened." The patient does report months of progressive shortness of breath with exertion, acutely worse today. Vital signs are: BP 210/160 mmHg, HR 92/min, RR 24/min, O₂sat 95% on RA. On exam, the patient is diaphoretic and has a harsh ejection murmur that radiates to his carotids. You note jugular venous distention and 2+ pitting edema to bilateral shins. EKG shows left ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following is the best next step in management for this patient?
englishExplanation:
Consult cardiothoracic surgery
Expl anation
A. Activate cardiac catheterization lab
Although the patient is presenting with exertional syncope concerning for acute
coronary syndrome, the EKG does not indicate emergent cardiac catheterization lab
activation. Given the presence of a new systolic murmur in the setting of exertional
syncope, critical aortic stenosis is of primary concern.
B. Administer nitroglycerin sublingually
This patient is presenting with critical aortic stenosis, which is one of the preloaddependent states one must consider before administering nitroglycerin in cardiac
patients (alongside phosphodiesterase inhibitor use, such as sildenafil).
Nitroglycerin is contramdicated in this patient.
C. Consult cardiothoracic surgery
The patient in the question stem likely has aortic stenosis, a common valvular disorder causing left ventricular outflow obstruction. Symptoms include exertional dyspnea, fatigue, chest pain, heart failure, and syncope. The patient's narrow pulse pressure, harsh systolic murmur, and findings of left ventricular hypertrophy on EKG
are also typical of aortic stenosis. Syncope is a poor prognostic indicator for patients
with aortic stenosis, and urgent surgical management is recommended.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK557628/
D. Order serial troponins and ECGs
This patient is presenting with critical aortic stenosls in the setting of exertional
syncope and clinical heart failure. Patients with severe aortic stenosis causing syncope have a mortality rate approached 50% within 3 years if left untreated; while
workup for acute coronary syndrome may happen concurrently, surgical consultation is required for this patient.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريض عنده critical aortic stenosis. الدلائل: murmur ejection حاد بينزل مع الـ carotids، و JVD و edema مع ضيق الـ pulse pressure، و LVH بالـ ECG. والـ dyspnea التدريجي مع المجهود والـ syncope عند صعود الدرج هي الـ symptoms الكلاسيكية، و الـ syncope إشارة prognostic سيئة عند مرضى الـ aortic stenosis. ولأن المشكلة ميكانيكية في الصمام ومش التهاب، فالأنسب استشارة cardiothoracic surgery بشكل عاجل.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تنادي cardiac catheterization lab أو تعطي nitroglycerin تحت اللسان. افرق إن الـ ECG ما بيبيّن MI اللي بيبيّن cath، والـ nitroglycerin ممنوع هون لأنه بينقص الـ preload وهالمريض preload dependent زي حالات الـ aortic stenosis، وكمان خطره مع sildenafil.

question: A 67-year-old female with a past medical history of insulin-dependent diabetes, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease requiring dialysis three times per week is brought in by the family for chest pain and fatigue. Per the family, the patient missed her dialysis appointment two days ago. Today the patient developed sharp substernal chest pain. Vitals are as follows: T 37ºC (98.6ºF), HR 110/min, BP 95/55 mmHg, RR 20/min, SPO₂ 99% on RA. Physical examination is significant for a moderately uncomfortable patient, alert and oriented only to person, leaning forward, with JVD to the angle of the mandible. No abnormalities are appreciated on cardiac and lung examination. ECG is shown. What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Aspirin, nitroglycerin, and initiation of heparin prior to cardiac catheterization
CT angiogram of the pulmonary vessels

englishExplanation:
Expl anation
Cardiac ultrasound
A. Administration of NSAIDs
The above patient is likely having uremic pericarditis given that she missed dialysis
two days ago. NSAIDs are the initial treatment for acute viral pericarditis and may
be indicated in uremic pericarditis, however initial treatment is dialysis.
B. Aspirin, nitroglycerin, and initiation of heparin prior to cardiac
catheterization
While coronary artery disease should be a serious consideration in this patient given
ST elevation and chest pain, the more likely diagnosis is uremic pericarditis given
diffuse ST elevations in the setting of missed dialysis.
C. CT angiogram of the pulmonary vessels
CT angiogram of the pulmonary vessels would be the diagnostic test of choice in diagnosing pulmonary embolism. Positional chest pain with diffuse ST elevations in
the setting of missing dialysis is more indicative of uremic pericarditis than pulmonary embolism
D. Cardiac ultrasound
The above patient is showing signs concerning for uremic pericarditis, including
sharp positional chest pain with JVD. In addition, the above EKG demonstrates diffuse ST elevations, a finding in pericarditis that is usually preceded by PR depressions. Classic EKG progression of pericarditis is usually as follows: 1) PR depression
and ST-segment elevation 2) normalization of EKG, 3) diffuse t-wave inversions, 4)
EKG normalization. Physical exam may reveal a cardiac rub, but this symptom
comes and goes, so may not always be present. An ultrasound should be performed
when suspicious of pericarditis to evaluate for pericardial effusion and tamponade
physiology as this may require emergent pericardiocentesis. In the absence of tamponade, the initial treatment of uremic pericarditis is dialysis.
Further information:
Jouriles NJ. Chapter 68. Pericardial and Myocardial Disease. In: Walls RM,
Hockberger RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and
Clinical Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.

![HIPPO-00487 source page 546](images/HIPPO-00487-Hipoo-p0546.jpg)

![HIPPO-00487 source page 547](images/HIPPO-00487-Hipoo-p0547.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريضة عندها uremic pericarditis لأنها فوّتت جلستين dialysis، والـ ECG بيبيّن diffuse ST elevations مع PR depressions، والألم sharp و positional بيتحسن لما تميل للأمام ومعها JVD. الخطوة الأساسية بالـ management هي dialysis، و NSAIDs ممكن تنفع في uremic pericarditis بس مو بديل عنها. والـ cardiac ultrasound مطلوبة لتشخيص pericardial effusion وتقييم هل في tamponade.
الفخ: الخطأ إنك تعمل CT angiogram للـ pulmonary vessels أو تفتح الـ cath lab أو تبدأ NSAID بس. افرق إن الـ positional chest pain مع diffuse ST elevations بعد فوات الـ dialysis بيوحي بـ uremic pericarditis أكتر من الـ PE أو الـ ACS، والـ initial treatment هو dialysis.

question: A 45-year-old male with a history of hypertension presents for three weeks of worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea. Vital signs are BP 165/98 mmHg, P 119/min, RR 22/min, O₂Sat 94% room air, and T99.1ºF (37.2ºC). Physical examination reveals 2+ pitting edema in the bilateral lower extremities and jugular venous distention. Chest x-ray demonstrates mild pulmonary vascular congestion, with a normal-sized cardiac silhouette, and EKG is shown. An informal bedside transthoracic echocardiogram image is shown, and the left ventricular ejection fraction appears grossly normal. Blood tests are pending. Which of the following is the next best step in the management of this patient?
englishExplanation:
Expl anation
Furosemide
A. Furosemide
There are many classifications of heart failure, including diastolic and systolic failure and left-sided versus right-sided failure. Diastolic dysfunction usually results
from chronic hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), aortic stenosis and
diabetes. These disease processess lead to a thickened ventricle that has impaired
relaxation, which impaires ventricular filling. These patients are preload dependent
and have a normal ejection fraction. Systolic dysfunction usually results from myocardial ischemia and hypertension and results in impaired contractility and a decreased ejection fraction. These patients are afterload dependent, which means output is dependent on resistance to emptying the ventricle. This patient has multiple
factors consistent with diastolic dysfunction, including a history of hypertension,
ECG findings consistent with LVH, and a normal ejection fraction (EF > 40%).
Diuresis is the mainstay therapy for patients with diastolic heart failure. In acute exacerbations,
nitroglycerin
and
noninvasive
positive
pressure
oxygenation/ventilation often help control respiratory distress. However, unlike in
systolic dysfunction, it is important to know that LV diastolic dysfunction (especially with a small, stiff LV chamber) does poorly in excessive preload reduction
states, underfilling the LV and leading to severe hypotension. Thus, any preload-reducing therapies (diuresis, nitroglycerin, dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers)
should be administered with caution.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK554557/
B. Implantation of cardioverter defibrillator
Oftentimes a bedside informal echocardiogram is useful to distinguish between systolic and diastolic heart failure, in that systolic heart failure will generally manifest
with significantly decreased ejection fraction, while diastolic heart function often
has normal or slightly abnormal ejection fraction. The echo is also useful in distinguishing hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) from restrictive CM, as
restrictive CM have normal appearing wall thickness unlike HOCM's thickened ventricular wall and septum. There is no indication at this time for AICD implantation.
C. Needle aspiration
Page 574 of 4185
The ultrasound demonstrates a normal heart size, with no evidence of overt hypertrophy or pericardial effusion. Given the clinical presentation of congestive heart
failure, it is more likely diastolic rather than systolic.
D. Tenecteplase
There is no indication for administering fibrinolytics/thrombolytics at this time.

question: A 48-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with chest pain beginning earlier in the day. The pain does not radiate, it is worse when she takes a deep breath and improves when she leans forward. The patient states she just recovered from a viral illness and still has a lingering cough with increased shortness of breath today. She has no medication allergies and is not taking any prescribed medications. Physical examination reveals a pericardial friction rub, clear lung fields bilaterally, and no murmurs are appreciated. Laboratory workup shows an ESR of 25 mm/h, CRP 10.0 mg/dL, and troponin 0.02 ng/ml. Chest x-ray and d-dimer are within normal limits. An ECG shows diffuse ST segment elevations. Echocardiogram is pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment for her suspected condition?
englishExplanation:
Expl anation
A. Aspirin
Indomethacin
Aspirin 500 - loomg every 6 - 8 hours should be substituted for NSAIDs in acute
pericarditis in the setting of post-myocardial infarction or for patients already on
antiplatelet therapy. It is also first-line in the first term of pregnancy but contraindicated past 20 weeks of gestation, where acetaminophen may be used. None of these
circumstances apply to the patient vignette in this question.
B. High dose prednisone
Corticosteroids are sometimes used in cases that are refractory to NSAID or
colchicine treatment. Interestingly, several studies have shown the use of corticosteroids early in the disease is associated with an increased incidence of recurrent
episodes. For this reason, NSAIDs are the initial treatment of choice.
C. Indomethacin
This patient is presenting with pericarditis. Pericarditis is inflammation of the pericardial sac which is most commonly preceded by an infection but can also be caused
by radiation, metabolic abnormalities, and autoimmune conditions. Acute pericarditis is suggested when a patient presents with characteristic chest pain and a
pericardial friction rub on exam. Laboratory studies, EKG, and echocardiography
are still utilized to confirm the diagnosis. Typically a diagnosis of acute pericarditis
can be made when a patient meets 2 of the 4 following criteria: pericardial chest
pain, pericardial rubs, new widespread ST-elevation or PR depression on EKG, and
pericardial effusion. Additional supporting evidence includes elevated ESR, CRP,
leukocytosis as well as pericardial inflammation on advanced imaging.
Empiric treatment with high-dose anti-inflammatory agents is the initial treatment
of pericarditis and should continue until symptomatic relief (which typically takes 3
days to 2 weeks). Colchicine can be used in addition to NSAIDs to improve symptoms and reduce the risk of future episodes of pericarditis. Antiinflammatory regimens options include: ibuprofen 600mg every 8 hours, indomethacin 25-50mg every 8 hours, or naproxen 500-1000mg every 12 hours. Aspirin 500 - loomg every 6
- 8 hours should be used instead of NSAIDs in post-myocardial infarction patients
or for those already on antiplatelet therapy.
Page 576 of 4185
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK431080/
Jouriles NJ. Chapter 68. Pericardial and Myocardial Disease. In: Walls RM,
Hockberger RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and
Clinical Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
D. Morphine
Morphine can be used to treat severe pain, but will not treat the inflammation associated with acute pericarditis.

question: A 65-year-old woman with a history of metastatic breast cancer comes to the emergency department because she has had exertional dyspnea for the past two days. Temperature is 37.0°C (98.6ºF), pulse rate is 110/min, respirations are 18/min, and blood pressure is 108/90 mmHg. On physical examination, jugular venous distention is noted, and heart sounds are muffled. Chest x-ray study shows no abnormalities. Cardiac ultrasonography is shown. If this patient suddenly becomes pulseless, which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
englishExplanation:
Pericardiocentesis
Expl anation
A. Epinephrine
While epinephrine is included in Advanced Cardiac Life Support algorithms for sudden cardiac arrest, it is unlikely to resolve the underlying cause of this patient's cardiac arrest. The cardiac ultrasound reveals a large pericardial effusion. Loss of
pulses in this patient would be concerning for cardiac tamponade, which should be
treated with emergent pericardiocentesis.
B. Pericardiocentesis
Cardiac ultrasonography shows a large, anechoic collection of fluid around the heart
consistent with a pericardial effusion. The causes of pericardial effusion are numerous and include infectious, inflammatory/rheumatologic (eg, lupus), malignant,
cardiac (eg, pericarditis, post-myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure), and
renal (eg, end-stage renal disease) and idiopathic causes. There is a spectrum of presentation for pericardial effusion based on the amount of fluid present and rate of
accumulation. Signs and symptoms may include chest pain, dyspnea, jugular venous distention, and muffled heart sounds. Management of pericardial effusion is
dependent on the size and clinical stability of the patient. pericardial or cardiac
tamponade is a complication of a large or rapidly accumulating pericardial effusion,
which compresses the heart, leading to decreased cardiac output, cardiovascular
collapse, and cardiac arrest. Cardiac tamponade requires emergent intervention
with pericardiocentesis.
Further information:
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK431089/
Jouriles NJ. Chapter 68. Pericardial and Myocardial Disease. In: Walls RM,
Hockberger RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and
Clinical Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
C. Thoracotomy
Resuscitative thoracotomy is not commonly performed for nontraumatic pericardial
tamponade, especially without initially attempting a pericardiocentesis.
D. Thrombolytics
Page 590 of 4185
Pulmonary embolism is an important differential diagnosis for a patient presenting
with chest pain, shortness of breath, and a history of cancer. However, the cardiac
ultrasound shows a large pericardial effusion. Loss of pulses in this patient would be
concerning for cardiac tamponade, which should be treated with emergent
pericardiocentesis.

question: An otherwise healthy 30-year-old man is brought to the emergency department via ambulance 30 minutes after he had a brief episode of syncope. He is currently asymptomatic. He says he was standing on the sidelines of a high school football game when he suddenly felt nauseous, noted tunnel vision, and then lost consciousness during the fourth quarter. Immediately prior to the event, he felt diaphoretic and warm. The patient has no history of head injury or chest pain. Witnesses did not notice any seizure activity and say that the patient was unconscious for approximately 15 seconds. Vital signs are within normal limits, and physical examination shows no abnormalities. Electrocardiography also shows no abnormalities. Which of the following findings most likely decreases this patient's risk of a syncope-related adverse event after discharge?

options.text: A likely diagnosis of vasovagal syncope
Loss of consciousness for less than one minute
Vital signs that are within normal limits

correctAnswer: A likely diagnosis of vasovagal syncope
englishExplanation:
A likely diagnosis of vasovagal syncope
Expl anation
A. A likely diagnosis of vasovagal syncope
Vasovagal syncope results from the sudden drop in blood pressure and subsequent
decrease in cerebral perfusion pressure, which results in a transient loss of consciousness. It is thought to be a primitive reflex and evolutionarily protective. It is a
relatively benign and self-limiting presentation unless accompanied by significant
trauma, orthostatic symptoms affecting activities of daily living, or occurring during
high-risk activities like driving.
If using the Canadian Syncope Risk tool, this patient gets -2 points for his presentation of vasovagal syncope (versus cardiac syncope or neither) based on evaluation in
the emergency department (ED). This is a clinical judgment. He would gain an additional (protective) -1 point for his "predisposition to vasovagal symptoms" which the
tool further describes as "triggered by being in a warm crowded place, prolonged
standing, fear, emotion, or pain." Therefore, this patient's total score would be -3,
placing him at a very low risk (0.4%) of adverse events if discharged from the ED
without further observation, workup, or interventions.
The Canadian Syncope Risk tool takes into account the following: predisposition to
vasovagal syncope, heart disease, systolic pressure in the ED or >180 mmHg,
troponin level >99th percentile for the normal population, abnormal QRS axis
or >1000), QRS duration >130 ms, QTc interval >480 ms, ED diagnosis of
cardiac syncope or vasovagal syncope. Of note, for patients without troponin measurements, you can still use the tool. You may use clinical discretion and score the
value as "no," not pathologically elevated if ischemia is not suspected. This is reasonable in this case given the patient's age, lack of comorbidities, and presentation.
Coronary ischemia rarely precipitates syncope with the patient appearing benign
afterward.
This tool has been externally validated and is used to predict 30-day serious adverse
events in patients presenting with syncope. It should only be used in patients 216
years of age who present within 24 hours of a syncopal episode. It should not be
used for any patients who have experienced prolonged LOC min), a baseline
mental status change, obvious witnessed seizure, major trauma requiring hospital
Page 601 of 4185
admission, alcohol or illicit drug intoxication, language barrier, or head trauma
causing LOC.
Further information: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30661373/
B. Lack of head trauma
A lack of head trauma is not necessarily protective in decreasing the rate of serious
adverse events in patients presenting with syncope. Young patients experiencing
syncope without head trauma can still have life-threatening cardiogenic etiologies of
syncope including fatal arrhythmias, Brugada syndrome, or cardiomyopathy.
Of note, one of the exclusionary criteria for using the Canadian Syncope Risk tool is
"head trauma causing loss of consciousness."
C. Loss of consciousness for less than one minute
No specific cut-off has been established for the duration of brief syncopal episodes
proving to be protective from serious adverse events.
It should be noted that one of the exclusionary criteria for the Canadian Syncope
Risk tool is prolonged loss of consciousness (LOC) which is defined as greater than
five minutes.
D. Vital signs that are within normal limits
Patients with systolic pressures in the emergency department of or >180
mmHg are at increased risk for serious adverse events from syncope. However, normal vital signs have not been shown to reduce the risk of serious adverse events
post-syncope.
