الفخ: بعد الناس بتروح على electrical cardioversion أو amiodarone، بس هي مستقرة hemodynamically، وثلاث جرعات adenosine هي جرعة كافية كـ chemical cardioversion. لازم تكمل بالـ rate control قبل ما تفكر بالـ electricity.

question: What is the most likely underlying etiology of cardiac arrest from polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with a normal QT?
englishExplanation: The most common cause of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) with a normal QT interval is myocardial ischemia; monomorphic VT can also be seen in the setting of myocardial ischemia but is most often sec- ondary to a re-entrant mechanism through scarred myocardium (chronic forms of ischemic heart disease). In the acute phase of a myocardial infarction (MI), polymorphic VT and ventricular fibrillation are more common than monomorphic VT. Although re-entry might still be a factor in the etiology of polymorphic VT dur- ing acute ischemia, abnormal automaticity is a more likely mechanism. Patients who present with polymorphic VT should be considered candidates for urgent revascularization therapy due to the high incidence of ischemia. Both monomor- phic and polymorphic VT involve an ectopic pacemaker originating within or be- low the His bundle. In monomorphic VT, the QRS complexes in one lead have the same morphology. In polymorphic VT, the QRS complexes have different mor- phologies in one lead. Incorrect Answer Explanations An inherited reduction in cardiac sodium activity is seen in Brugada syndrome. This syndrome can lead to a polymorphic VT, but myocardial ischemia is the most common underlying cause of polymorphic VT. Electrolyte abnormalities can exacerbate the tendency toward ventricular ectopy, thus leading to polymorphic VT. However, the most common underlying cause of polymorphic VT is acute myocardial ischemia. It is still prudent to correct any electrolyte abnormalities that might be present. A re-entrant mechanism through scarred myocardium is the most fre- quent etiology underlying monomorphic VT and is commonly seen in the chronic phase after an MI. The likelihood of ventricular arrhythmia in a patient with coronary artery disease is directly related to the extent of myocardial damage and scarring. Key Points Consider any patient presenting with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia as a pos- sible ACS patient and a potential urgent revascularization candidate. Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia often develops secondary to a re-entrant mechanism related to scarred myocardium — in other words, in a patient who had an myocardial infarction in the past. Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in a patient with acute ischemia is likely sec- ondary to abnormal automaticity.

الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار electrolyte abnormality أو Brugada syndrome. الـ electrolyte abnormalities ممكن تزيد ventricular ectopy، بس مش السبب الـ most common. و Brugada syndrome وراثي بسبب خلل في الـ sodium channels، والـ re-entrant scar هو للـ monomorphic VT مو للـ polymorphic.

question: A 39-year-old man presents after "passing out" several times over the past 30 minutes. He is alert but distressed. His vital signs are BP 105/70, P 65, R 24, and T 37.1°C (98.8°F); SpO is 97% on room air. During the examination, he loses consciousness, and his pulse is weakly palpable. The monitor demonstrates the rhythm shown below. Within 30 seconds, the rhythm returns to normal sinus, and the patient regains consciousness. The only abnormality noted is a QTc in- terval of 610 msec. In addition to ordering laboratory tests, which therapeutic plan is most appropriate? 2 Credit: Mary Jo Wagner, MD, FACEP.

options.text: Correct metabolic abnormalities; discharge if arrhythmia does not recur
Correct metabolic abnormalities; perform defibrillation if arrhythmia recurs; ad- mit to CCU
Give procainamide 17 mg/kg IV over 15 minutes if arrhythmia recurs; admit to CCU
Start anti-ischemic therapy if ACS is detected; perform synchronized cardiover- sion if arrhythmia persists

correctAnswer: Correct metabolic abnormalities; perform defibrillation if arrhythmia recurs; ad- mit to CCU
englishExplanation:
This patient is experiencing recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) in a configuration that suggests torsade de pointes (TdP). Management in a patient with sustained perfusion (as indicated by a pulse) includes treatment or correction of any inciting event, close monitoring, and defib- rillation or cardioversion of any sustained compromising episode of TdP. Synchronized cardioversion is generally attempted on patients with a pulse. However, because of the polymorphic, undulating nature of TdP, the defibrillator may not be able to lock onto the QRS complexes. This may make it impossible to perform synchronized cardioversion, so it is recommended to simply defibrillate in the setting of unstable TdP. Patients with TdP should also be given 2 g of intra- venous magnesium and consideration of overdrive pacing. Use caution: TdP has a tendency to recur frequently. Patients with this arrhythmia should be admitted to a CCU for further monitoring and treatment. Morphologically, ventricular tachycardia (VT) is separated into two basic subtypes: monomorphic and polymorphic. TdP is a form of polymorphic VT that occurs in the setting of abnormal ventricular repolarization (manifested by prolongation of the QTc interval beyond 450 msec while in a supraventricular rhythm) and the charac- teristic pattern of the TdP (progressively increasing/decreasing QRS complex am- plitude, as noted on the ECG). Of course, a determination of the QTc interval while in this arrhythmia is not possible. In this case, the arrhythmia, with its characteris- tic TdP features and prolonged QTc interval, can be seen in normal sinus rhythm, thus revealing the diagnosis. TdP occurs in the settings of elec- trolyte abnormality (particularly hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia), adverse effects of medications (agents that prolong the QT interval), congenital issues, ACS, and other less common issues. Management in cardiac arrest is similar to that of VT in general but with attention to electrolyte issues, if possible. Incorrect Answer Explanations This patient should be closely monitored, so discharging him is inappro- priate even if he is asymptomatic during his emergency department stay. Admission to the hospital is almost always required in this presentation. Electrical cardioversion should be considered if the arrhythmia recurs and is sus- tained and compromising. Laboratory testing is important, particularly with consid- eration for electrolytes and troponin. Close monitoring and admission to the hospital for further observation and treatment are needed. Procainamide is an excellent antiarrhythmic agent, but it should not be used in this case because it can prolong the QT interval (which is already abnormally long in this patient). Although the stated dose is appropriate, the time of infusion is far too rapid; procainamide can precipitate hypotension if given too quickly. This medication is more appropriately adminis- tered over 45 to 60 minutes. Determination of electrolytes and correction of any significant abnor- mality is a treatment goal. If ACS abnormalities are noted, treatment is appro- priate. However, if electrical therapy is needed for a patient with TdP, synchronized cardioversion is unlikely to be successful. This is because the polymorphic nature of TdP makes it difficult, if not impossible, for the defibrillator to synchronize with the QRS complexes. Instead, defibrillation is recommended in cases of TdP. Key Points Torsade de pointes is a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with an abnormally prolonged QTc interval on baseline ECG. Manage torsade de pointes in cardiac arrest pretty much the same way you manage any VT arrest presentation — if it occurs with a pulse, pay attention to inciting events and optimize oxygenation, ventilation, and perfusion. Don't use procainamide in patients with torsade de pointes.

question: What is first-line therapy for a patient presenting with a wide-complex tachycar- dia and otherwise stable vital signs?
englishExplanation: In stable patients, pharmacologic agents (including procainamide, amiodarone, lidocaine, and magnesium) can be used to terminate a wide-complex tachycardia. However, procainamide is the antiarrhythmic of choice for stable patients; amiodarone and lidocaine are less effective. If Wolff- Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome–related atrial fibrillation or wide-complex atri- oventricular reciprocating tachycardia (AVRT) are suspected, remember to avoid the use of amiodarone. Electrical cardioversion is the preferred treatment for wide-complex tachycardia for patients who are suffering from hemodynamic instability, myocardial ischemia, or failure of other phar- macologic treatment. Incorrect Answer Explanations Adenosine is used to treat supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and is not the first-line treatment for a wide-complex tachycardia. Adenosine inter- acts with receptors on the surface of cardiac cells — activating potassium channels to increase potassium conductance — and indirectly reduces calcium influx into cells. Rarely, a patient in SVT may require a beta-blocker or calcium channel blocker. This patient is presenting with stable ventricular tachycardia and should be treated with an antiarrhythmic, such as procainamide. Atropine is used to treat bradycardia. Although it is a reasonable addition, magnesium is not the initial treatment of choice for ventricular tachycardia. Magnesium is used for tachydysrhythmias as- sociated with QT-interval prolongation, such as torsades de pointes. Key Points Procainamide is the antiarrhythmic of choice for stable patients with a wide-com- plex tachycardia. Amiodarone and lidocaine are less effective. Electrical cardioversion is the preferred treatment for wide-complex tachycardia for the patient who is also suffering from hemodynamic instability, myocardial is- chemia, or failure of other pharmacologic treatment. Magnesium is used for tachydysrhythmias associated with QT-interval prolonga- tion, such as torsades de pointes.

question: Which condition would be best treated by adenosine?
englishExplanation: Adenosine is used for the treatment of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT). Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT) is a regular SVT due to a reentry circuit confined to the atrioventricular (AV) node and perinodal atrial tissue. AVNRT is the most common form of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycar- dia (PSVT), and it accounts for nearly two-thirds of all PSVTs. AVNRT is more com- mon in women. The onset and termination of the symptoms are usually sudden. Adenosine interacts with receptors on the surface of cardiac cells — activating potassium channels to increase potassium conductance — and indirectly reduces calcium influx into cells. As a result, there is a slowing of the sinus rate and an in- crease in the AV nodal conduction delay. Incorrect Answer Explanations Atrial flutter with a 2:1 response is very rapid, so this would need treatment, likely with a calcium channel blocker or beta blocker. Adenosine is used to treat SVT and is not the primary treatment for atrial flutter with a rapid rate. Adenosine is used for the treatment of SVT. Patients presenting with sinus tachycardia should be managed by addressing the underlying cause of their tachy- cardia. Patients with a normal sinus rhythm do not require treatment with adenosine. Adenosine is used for treating SVT. A slow resting rate can be common for athletically fit patients, and it can also be seen in patients on beta blockers. If the bradycardia is new and the patient is symptomatic (eg, syncope, dizziness, or feeling faint) or unstable, then treatment may need to be initiated, which could include at- ropine, dopamine, or external pacing until a permanent or transvenous pacer can be placed.
arabicExplanation:

الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار atrial flutter with 2:1 response لأنهم شايفين rapid rhythm، بس هاد بيتعامل مع calcium channel blocker أو beta blocker، و adenosine مو للـ flutter السريع. والـ sinus tachycardia بتنعالج بمعالجة السبب.

question: A patient with a history of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome presents with palpi- tations. The ECG is shown below. What is the preferred medication in this circumstance? Credit: Ross CH, Schwab TM. In: Mattu A, Tabas J, Brady w, eds. Electrocardiography in Emergency, Acute, and Critical Care. 2nd ed. American College of Emergency Physicians; 2019.
englishExplanation:
This ECG shows a narrow-complex regular tachyarrhythmia without P waves preceding the QRS complex. In the setting of known Wolff- Parkinson-White syndrome (WPW) syndrome, this is consistent with or- thodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT), which accounts for 90% to 95% of all AVRT. According to the 2015 guidelines from the American College of Cardiology, American Heart Association, and Heart Rhythm Society, adenosine is the first-line treatment for hemodynamically stable ortho- dromic AVRT. An important distinction to make in cases of WPW syndrome is whether the ar- rhythmia is orthodromic AVRT (narrow) or antidromic AVRT (wide) or atrial fibrillation. In cases of orthodromic AVRT, adenosine is a first-line agent with calcium-channel blockers and beta-blockers as second-line agents. For an- tidromic AVRT (wide) it is important to avoid typical AV nodal–blocking agents for supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), such as adenosine, calcium-channel block- ers, and beta-blockers. Additionally, in WPW syndrome that presents with atrial fibrillation, AV nodal blockers such as adenosine, digoxin, calcium-channel blockers, and beta-blockers should be avoided. Adenosine is an effective treatment for orthodromic AVRT because it interrupts the causative reentrant loop. This is the same mechanism by which adeno- sine treats atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT) — commonly known as SVT. The major difference is that SVT is caused by a reen- trant loop within the AV node, whereas orthodromic AVRT is due to a reentrant loop involving anterograde conduction through the AV node and retrograde con- duction via the accessory pathway (bundle of Kent). Otherwise, these processes pro- duce very similar clinical presentations and are treated the same. Other AV nodal– blocking agents, such as calcium-channel blockers and beta-adrenergic an- tagonists, can also be used. However, they are recommended as second- line agents (after adenosine) in the aforementioned guidelines. Incorrect Answer Explanations Digoxin is a cardiac glycoside with AV nodal–blocking properties. It was previ- ously used for the treatment of orthodromic AVRT. However, it is not currently a recommended agent because more effective, rapidly-acting agents with fewer side effects are available. Specifically, digoxin can decrease the refractory period of the accessory pathway, increasing accessory pathway conduction and the risk of de- generation to ventricular arrhythmias. Consequently, rapid-acting adenosine is the first choice for medical management of orthodromic AVRT. Diltiazem is a calcium-channel blocker with AV nodal–blocking proper- ties that is effective for terminating orthodromic AVRT. However, dilti- azem is considered a second-line agent to adenosine in this setting, pri- marily due to concern for longer duration of AV nodal blockade relative to adenosine. AV nodal blockade can preferentially shunt conduction through the accessory pathway, which can result in extreme ventricular conduction and degen- eration to ventricular arrhythmias. Consequently, adenosine is the first choice for medical management of orthodromic AVRT; it acts rapidly, has a short duration of action, and can break the reentrant circuit while minimizing vulnerability to exces- sive accessory pathway conduction. Metoprolol is a beta-1–selective beta-blocker with prominent AV node– blocking properties. Like diltiazem, metoprolol can cause longer than desired AV nodal blockade in the setting of WPW syndrome, leaving the patient at risk of ventricular arrhythmia. The evidence supporting the use of beta- blockers generally to treat orthodromic AVRT is less robust than that for nondihy- dropyridine calcium-channel blockers (eg, diltiazem, verapamil), but the available evidence suggests similar effectiveness. However, adenosine has the preferred mix of effectiveness and duration of action, making it the first choice for medical man- agement of orthodromic AVRT.

question: A 7-month-old boy is brought in by his father, who says that the baby woke up from a nap "really agitated and won't stop crying." On examination, the child is awake, responsive, and irritable. His vital signs include BP 58/47, P 236, R 58, and T 37.4°C (99.3°F). An ECG is obtained and shown below. What therapy is in- dicated for this patient? Credit: Michael Gottlieb, MD, FACEP.
englishExplanation:
This ECG shows supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), and the patient has signs of uncompensated shock, with both altered mentation and hypotension. Synchronized cardioversion at 0.5 to 1 J/kg is indicated in this case as the child is unstable. A child presenting with SVT for the first time should undergo cardiol- ogy consultation while in the emergency department as well, but the prognosis is excellent. Disposition is determined based on the patient's age and whether they were treated conservatively (vagal maneuvers or a single dose of adenosine) or war- ranted further medical interventions (antiarrhythmic medications or synchronized cardioversion). Causes of SVT include fever and infections, drug exposure (24%), and congenital heart disease (23%), but the most common cause is idiopathic (50%). Incorrect Answer Explanations Adenosine is dosed at 100 mcg/kg and must be delivered intravenously as quickly as possible in a line located as close to the heart as possible (followed with a saline flush for immediate delivery). Because this patient is unstable, cardioversion should be the first treatment, not an antiarrhythmic medication like adenosine. Defibrillation (ie, using electricity to convert without coordinating or synchroniz- ing with the current rhythm) is inappropriate because the rhythm depicted is SVT. Defibrillation is used for ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia. Vagal maneuvers and adenosine are indicated in patients with stable SVT, but in patients with decompensation, the clinician should prepare for cardioversion im- mediately. There are many different types of vagal maneuvers, including ice to the face (stimulation of the dive reflex), knee-to-chest position with pushing of the legs, forced exhalation, and even rectal stimulation (used predominantly in neonates and infants).

question: The below rhythm is from a patient currently in cardiac arrest. Which condition is most likely associated with this cardiac arrest patient's rhythm? Credit: Mary Jo Wagner, MD, FACEP.
englishExplanation: This rhythm shows a patient with narrow-complex pulseless electrical activ- ity (PEA). Given the scenarios presented, this is most likely COPD re- lated to a pneumothorax from a ruptured bleb. Narrow-complex PEA gener- ally results from mechanical obstruction, coronary ischemia, or hypov- olemia, including hemorrhage. Mechanical obstruction can be caused by a tension pneumothorax, which is associated with COPD and trauma. Other causes of me- chanical obstruction include pulmonary embolism (associated with findings of right-heart strain) and cardiac tamponade (associated with low voltage and electri- cal alternans). Incorrect Answer Explanations Diabetic ketoacidosis is most likely to cause cardiac arrest due to acidosis or electrolyte derangements such as hyper- or hypokalemia, which are not evident on this patient's rhythm strip. Instead, hyperkalemia is associated with peaked T waves, prolonged PR and QRS complex intervals, and in severe cases, a wide-complex bradycardia with a sinusoidal pattern. By contrast, hypokalemia is associated with a U wave and flattening of the T wave in its mild form and dysrhythmias when severe. Cardiac arrest due to acidosis is likely to present with a bradyarrhythmia, particularly if concomitant hyperkalemia is present. Physicians should consider the use of bicarbonate to treat bradycardic PEA if severe acidosis is considered a possible etiology. Cardiac arrest in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) is most com- monly associated with cardiovascular disease (eg, coronary ischemia or ventricular dysrhythmias) or hyperkalemia (ie, peaked T waves, prolonged PR and QRS complex intervals, and in severe cases, a wide-complex bradycardia with a sinusoidal pattern) — neither of which are apparent on this patient's rhythm strip. Hyperkalemia can also cause cardiac arrest in this population, but again, find- ings of hyperkalemia are absent. Finally, although cardiac tamponade can occur in patients with ESRD, causing PEA with a narrow complex, the classic findings for cardiac tamponade include low voltage and electrical alternans. PEA from a tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) overdose is most likely to have a wide QRS complex, which is not evident on this patient's rhythm strip. A wide QRS complex is associated with the inhibitory effect of TCAs on the recovery of car- diac sodium channels. Although the anticholinergic effects of TCAs can cause nar- row-complex tachycardia in lower doses, this effect would not be associated with cardiac arrest.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الـ rhythm بيبيّن narrow-complex pulseless electrical activity، والـ PEA بيسببه غالباً obstruction ميكانيكي أو ischemia تاجية أو hypovolemia. الـ COPD مرتبط بتوترن pneumothorax من rupture لـ bleb، والـ tension pneumothorax بيعطيك PEA. الـ mechanical obstruction من الـ pulmonary embolism و cardiac tamponade بس مش السبب المتوقع بهاد السياق، والـ ECG للـ tamponade بيبين low voltage و electrical alternans.
الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار diabetic ketoacidosis أو end-stage renal disease، بس الـ acidosis والـ hyperkalemia بيسببوا bradyarrhythmia، وهذا الـ rhythm strip ما فيه bradycardia ولا علامات hyperkalemia. والـ cardiac tamponade بتبان مع low voltage و electrical alternans.

question: What is the best description of the following ECG performed on a patient with chest pain? Credit: Harrigan RA. In: Mattu A, Tabas J, Brady W, eds. Electrocardiography in Emergency, Acute, and Critical Care. 2nd ed. American College of Emergency Physicians; 2019.

options.text: Atrial fibrillation with left bundle-branch block
Normal sinus rhythm, first-degree AV block, left anterior fascicular block
Normal sinus rhythm, first-degree AV block, left posterior fascicular block
Third-degree AV block, left anterior fascicular block

correctAnswer: Normal sinus rhythm, first-degree AV block, left posterior fascicular block
englishExplanation: This ECG demonstrates a normal sinus rhythm (P wave is present before each QRS complex). The PR interval is prolonged >200 ms, indicating a first-degree atrioventricular (AV) block. There is a right axis deviation (QRS in lead I is net negative while the QRS in lead aVF is oriented positively) with a normal duration QRS complex. There are small R waves with deep S waves in leads I and aVL. These findings are consistent with a left poste- rior fascicular block. The left bundle of the cardiac electrical conduction system separates into the left an- terior fascicle and the left posterior fascicle (with a small septal fascicle branch). Blocks in these fascicles will present with characteristic ECG changes. Notably, it is important to ensure there is not another reason for a right axis deviation in this case, such as right ventricular strain. In contrast, a left anterior fascicular block will present with a left axis deviation and a normal duration QRS complex. Typically, there will be small R waves with deep S waves in leads II, III, and aVF. There also are no ST-seg- ment or T-wave changes associated with either left anterior or posterior fascicular blocks. Incorrect Answer Explanations The QRS complexes occur at a regular rhythm on this ECG. This is not consistent with atrial fibrillation, as the rhythm will be irregular. The QRS is normal duration and is not consistent with a right or left bundle-branch block, which will present with a QRS complex >120 ms. This ECG is consistent with a left posterior fascicular block. A left anterior fascic- ular block will present with a left axis deviation (positive QRS in lead I and negative QRS in lead aVF) with small R waves and deep S waves in leads II, III, and aVF. The P wave and QRS rates are the same on this ECG, with each QRS being preceded by a P wave. A third-degree AV block would present with a P wave rate dissociated from the QRS rate, with the P wave rate being faster than the QRS rate. The PR interval is >200 ms, making this a first-degree AV block. Furthermore, this ECG is consistent with a left posterior fascicular block, not a left anterior fascic- ular block.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الـ ECG فيه موجة P قبل كل QRS، يعني normal sinus rhythm. بس الـ PR interval مطوّل أكثر من 200 ms، وهاد معناه first-degree AV block. كمان في right axis deviation، يعني الـ QRS في lead I سالب الصافي وفي aVF موجب، ومدة الـ QRS طبيعية، مع موجات R صغيرة و S عميقة في lead I و aVL. هاد كله بيطابق left posterior fascicular block، لأن الـ left bundle بينقسم لـ left anterior fascicle و left posterior fascicle، والـ block في الـ posterior fascicle بيعطي انحراف المحور لليمين.
الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار left anterior fascicular block، بس هي بتدي انحراف لليسار مو لليمين، وموجات R صغيرة مع S عميقة بتظهر في II و III و aVF. وكمان لازم تتأكد إنو ما في سبب تاني للـ right axis deviation مثل right ventricular strain.

question: What is the best interpretation of this ECG? Credit: Harrigan RA. In: Mattu A, Tabas J, Brady W, eds. Electrocardiography in Emergency, Acute, and Critical Care. 2nd ed. American College of Emergency Physicians; 2019.

options.text: Atrial fibrillation with nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay
Atrial flutter with left bundle-branch block
Normal sinus rhythm with left bundle-branch block
Normal sinus rhythm with right bundle-branch block

correctAnswer: Normal sinus rhythm with right bundle-branch block
englishExplanation: This ECG is consistent with a normal sinus rhythm with a right bundle- branch block (RBBB). There is a P wave clearly before each QRS, and each QRS is associated with a P wave. There are no extra P waves, and the P wave and QRS rate is the same, indicating a normal sinus rhythm and not a third-degree atrioven- tricular (AV) block. The QRS complex is widened (>120 ms), which is con- sistent with an intraventricular conduction block; RBBBs and left bun- dle-branch blocks (LBBBs) are the most common cause of a widened QRS. Based on the pattern seen here, there is an RSR' configuration of the QRS complex in leads V1 to V2 with associated ST depression and T-wave inversions. This is coupled with reciprocal changes (deep S waves with upright T waves) in leads I and aVL. This pattern is consistent with a RBBB. A RBBB occurs when there is a block in the conduction down the right bundle-branch. Recall that normal cardiac conduction begins with an impulse in the sinoatrial node to the AV node. This signal extends down the bundle of His where the conduction breaks off into the right and left bundle-branches. These then have Purkinje fibers extending from them that leads to cardiac muscle depolarization. When the right bundle-branch is blocked, the depolarization travels down the left bun- dle-branch and then to the right bundle-branch, causing a delay in ven- tricular polarization denoted by a prolonged QRS interval. The R prime (R') part of the QRS complex seen in a RBBB represents the current moving to the right side of the heart after the left side has depolarized and is paired with deep late S waves in the reciprocal leads (I, aVL, V5, and V6). Bundle-branch blocks (both left and right) can occur for many reasons, including ischemia, scar tissue formation, ventricular hypertrophy, cardiomyopathies, valvular abnormalities, and pulmonary disease, among others. Incorrect Answer Explanations This ECG shows a normal rate of both P waves and QRS complexes, and each QRS complex has a preceding P wave. The rhythm is regular. In atrial fibrillation, the rhythm would be irregular, and P waves would not be seen. Additionally, this block pattern is consistent with a RBBB. “Nonspecific intraventricular conduc- tion delay” is a term used to refer to a prolonged or wide QRS that is not consistent with either a RBBB or a LBBB. Atrial flutter will present with either a regular rate of QRS complexes in a fixed block pattern or an irregular rate with a variable block pattern. Atrial flutter will also present with flutter type repeating P waves in between QRS com- plexes, which is not seen here. Additionally, this pattern is consistent with a RBBB. A LBBB will present with wide notched R waves in leads I, aVL, V5, and V6 with as- sociated T-wave inversions and deep S waves in leads V1 and V2. This ECG is consistent with a normal sinus rhythm, given that each QRS complex is preceded by a P wave at a fixed interval with both the P waves and QRS complexes having the same rate. Additionally, the ECG here shows a RBBB pattern, not a LBBB pattern.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الـ ECG فيه P wave واضحة قبل كل QRS، ومعدل الـ P waves والـ QRS واحد، يعني normal sinus rhythm ومش third-degree AV block. الـ QRS واسع أكثر من 120 ms، وهاد بيتوافق مع intraventricular conduction block. في lead V1 و V2 في نمط RSR مع ST depression و T wave inversion، والتغييرات المتبادلة وهي S عميق مع T موجب في lead I و aVL، وهاد كله signature للـ RBBB. لما يصير block في الـ right bundle، الـ depolarization بينزل بالـ left bundle أولاً وبيأخر بالـ right bundle.
الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار left bundle-branch block أو atrial fibrillation. الـ LBBB بيبان بـ broad notched R في I و aVL و V5-V6 و S عميق متأخر في V1، والـ atrial fibrillation بتكون irregular. هاد الـ ECG منتظم.

question: Which ECG characteristics are associated with a left bundle-branch block?

options.text: QRS duration of 105 ms, right axis deviation, and normal T waves
QRS duration of 110 ms, left axis deviation, and normal ST segments
QRS duration of 130 ms; broad notched R waves in leads I, aVL, and V5 to V6; and late deep S wave in lead V1
QRS duration of 135 ms, RSR' configuration in leads V1 to V2, and late deep S waves in leads I and aVL

correctAnswer: QRS duration of 130 ms; broad notched R waves in leads I, aVL, and V5 to V6; and late deep S wave in lead V1
englishExplanation: A left bundle-branch block (LBBB) occurs when the left bundle-branch in the ven- tricular cardiac conduction pathway is delayed or blocked. This causes the conduc- tion to proceed down the right bundle-branch first and then swing to the left side of the heart. The result is a wide QRS complex (>120 ms) due to delayed ven- tricular depolarization. The R waves in the leads over the left ventricle (I, aVL, and V5 to V6) will be broad due to slowed depolarization of the left ventricle. These leads will discordant ST and T-wave changes relative to the QRS complex. Reciprocal changes will be seen in V1 and often V2, being late deep S waves, as these leads lie over the right ventricle. Bundle-branch blocks, both left and right, can occur for many reasons, including ischemia, scar tissue formation, ventricular hypertrophy, cardiomyopathies, valvular abnormalities, and pulmonary disease, among others. Incorrect Answer Explanations A QRS duration of 105 ms is normal and is not consistent with a LBBB. These ECG findings, with a right axis deviation, may represent a left posterior fascicu- lar block. A QRS duration of 110 ms is normal and is not consistent with a LBBB. These ECG findings, with a left axis deviation, may represent a left anterior fascicular block. RSR' configuration of V1 to V2 with a wide QRS complex is consistent with a right bundle-branch block. This will present with reciprocal changes in leads I and aVL, being deep S waves.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ left bundle-branch block بيصير لما الـ left bundle-branch يتأخر أو يتوقف، فالـ conduction بينزل بالـ right bundle-branch الأول وبيعدي بعدها لليسار، والنتيجة QRS عريض فوق 120 ms. ولأن الـ R waves في الـ leads اللي فوق البطين الأيسر، يعني I و aVL و V5-V6، بتصير broad بسبب بطء الـ depolarization، بتطلع معها تغيرات ST و T معاكسة للـ QRS. والتغييرات المتبادلة بتظهر في V1 وأحياناً V2 كـ S waves عميقة متأخرة، لأن هالـ leads فوق البطين الأيمن.
الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار الـ RSR في V1-V2، بس هاد تعريف RBBB. و QRS مدته 105 أو 110 ms مدته طبيعية وما بيصلح LBBB. والـ right axis deviation مع QRS طبيعي ممكن يكون left posterior fascicular block.

question: A 32-year-old man presents after passing out in his living room. His vital signs are stable, and he is asymptomatic. The physical examination is unremarkable. An ECG is obtained and shown below. What is the underlying diagnosis? Credit: Christopher Amato, MD, FACEP.
englishExplanation:
Brugada syndrome is a genetic disorder that causes abnormal sodium channel function and is associated with a high risk of death. The classic ECG findings with Brugada syndrome, which appear on this patient's ECG, include an incomplete RBBB pattern and ST-segment elevations in leads V1 and V2. Death resulting from Brugada syndrome is related to subsequent polymorphic ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation. Patients commonly have a family history of sudden death or cardiac syncope without structural heart dis- ease. Management in the emergency department includes cardiac monitoring with admission for further monitoring and cardiology consultation. The ultimate treat- ment includes placement of an automatic implanted cardiac cardioverter- defibrillator. The ECG findings can often be normal at the time of evaluation in the emergency department, so any patient with a family history of sudden death should be referred for further evaluation and provocative testing. Incorrect Answer Explanations The ECG findings in prolonged QT syndrome are notable for significant prolon- gation of the QT interval. The syndrome causes increased susceptibility to polymor- phic ventricular tachycardia. However, the QT interval in this patient's ECG is normal. Third-degree AV block (complete heart block) is noted with dissociation of P waves from QRS complexes. A ventricular rate of less than 60 is noted; the specific rate and QRS complex morphologies are dependent on the level of the block (nodal versus infranodal). The PR intervals are normal and regular on this ECG and show no evidence of heart block. Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome can also lead to syncope and, extremely rarely, sudden cardiac death. The associated ECG changes (while the patient is in normal sinus rhythm) are shortened PR interval, delta wave, and minimally widened QRS complex — which are absent in this patient.

Review notes: ["visual_reference_no_image_attached_in_jsonl"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ ECG هاد بيبيّن الـ classic findings للـ Brugada syndrome، وهي incomplete RBBB pattern مع ST-segment elevations في lead V1 و V2. هاد اضطراب وراثي بيسبب abnormal sodium channel function، وخطر الموت فيه عالي بسبب احتمال polymorphic VT أو ventricular fibrillation. من الـ ED بتعمل cardiac monitoring وبدخول بسرعة للمتابعة مع cardiology consultation، والعلاج النهائي زرع ICD. وكثير مرضى عندهم family history من sudden death أو cardiac syncope بدون structural heart disease.
الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار prolonged QT syndrome لأن الـ syncope بيفتح الأبواب، بس الـ QT interval بهالمريض طبيعي. و third-degree AV block بتبان بانفصال P waves عن QRS، والـ Brugada بتبان بالـ ST elevation في V1 و V2 مع RBBB pattern.

question: A 75-year-old woman presents with a decreased level of consciousness. Her vital signs are BP 70/40, P 40, R 12, and T 36.5°C (97.7°F); her bedside blood glucose level is 114 mg/dL. Her rhythm strip is shown. What is the most likely diagnosis? Credit: alfa md/iStock/Getty Images Plus.

options.text: Mobitz second-degree heart block, type I (Wenckebach)
Mobitz second-degree heart block, type II
Sinus bradycardia with premature ventricular contractions

correctAnswer: Mobitz second-degree heart block, type II
englishExplanation:
In Mobitz second-degree heart block, type II, the PR interval is constant (although sometimes prolonged) until there is a dropped beat. This patient is con- ducting only some beats, with the P waves after the premature ventricular com- plexes (PVCs) blocked, which is consistent with Mobitz second-degree heart block, type II. This rhythm strip also demonstrates a bradycardic rhythm. Further analy- sis involves identifying all the P waves and the relationship of each to the following QRS complex. A P wave precedes each normal QRS complex with a relatively nor- mal and nonvarying PR interval. There are some P waves (seen best im- mediately following the QRS complex of the PVC) that are not conducted and have no QRS complex following them. Mobitz type II heart blocks are often seen in an anterior wall myocardial in- farction (MI), whereas type I blocks are more often associated with an increased vagal tone accompanying an inferior wall MI. Distinguishing type II blocks is important because they are more likely to progress to complete heart blocks and have a higher mortality rate. Incorrect Answer Explanations In a complete heart block, there is no association between the P waves and the QRS complexes (complete atrioventricular dissociation). In this case, there is an association between some of the P waves and the QRS complexes. A Mobitz second-degree heart block, type I, referred to as Wenckebach, is associated with progressive PR interval prolongation from beat to beat until there is a dropped beat (or nonconducted P wave). The cycle is then reset. In this case, the PR interval is constant. In sinus bradycardia, although the heart rate is slow, each P wave is followed by a QRS complex. In this patient, some of the P waves are not being conducted, which indicates some type of heart block.

Review notes: ["visual_reference_no_image_attached_in_jsonl"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريضة عندها bradycardia مع drop beats، والـ PR interval يضل constant لحد ما يجي QRS ضايع، وهاد هو تعريف Mobitz second-degree heart block type II. بتلاقي موجات P قبل كل QRS طبيعي بـ PR منتظم، بس في موجات P بعد الـ PVC ما بتوصّل ولا في QRS بعدها. و type II مهم تميّزه لأنه ممكن بيتطور لـ complete heart block و mortality أعلى. و type II غالباً مع anterior wall MI، و type I مع increased vagal tone و inferior wall MI.
الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار complete heart block أو Wenckebach. في الـ complete heart block في قطع كامل بين P waves و QRS، بس هون في علاقة بين بعض الـ P waves والـ QRS. والـ Wenckebach بيبدأ بـ PR تطول تدريجياً قبل الـ dropped beat، مو بهالشكل.

question: Which finding is an indication for placement of a pacemaker?

options.text: New right bundle branch and left anterior fascicular block
Sinus bradycardia with a heart rate of 50 bpm

correctAnswer: New right bundle branch and left anterior fascicular block
englishExplanation: In the presence of a new right bundle-branch block with a left anterior fascicular block, placement of a temporary pacemaker can prevent com- plete heart block and reduce bradycardia. Because both the left anterior fas- cicle and the right bundle branch of the conducting system receive their blood sup- ply from the proximal LAD artery, findings of new bundle-branch blocks suggest oc- clusion of that vessel. PR prolongation and the finding of a new or alternating bun- dle-branch block further increase the likelihood that a complete heart block will de- velop, indicating the need for temporary pacing. In an anterior wall myocardial infarction (MI), necrosis of the septum from occlusion of the left ante- rior descending (LAD) artery, which supplies blood to the left anterior fascicle and the right bundle branch, has a poor prognosis and can progress to complete heart block. Incorrect Answer Explanations First-degree AV block does not need treatment. Higher grade AV blocks in anterior and lateral MIs should have transcutaneous pacing applied, but in infe- rior and posterior MIs, this is typically transient and conservative management is indicated. Bradycardia alone is not an indication for pacing, unless it does not cor- rect with pharmacologic intervention and the patient is unstable. Bradycardia may also result from therapy with beta-blockers and is reversible with discontinuation of these medications. Second-degree heart block, type I (also known as the Wenckebach type) is a much more stable block that rarely needs treatment. Higher grade blocks than Wenckebach are more ominous in anterior/lateral STEMIs, and pro- phylactic placement of a transcutaneous pacemaker is recommended. In inferior/posterior STEMIs, they are usually temporary and can be managed conservatively. Key Points Anterior myocardial infarctions indicate a left anterior descending artery occlusion and can cause necrosis of the septum, leading to arrhythmias. A new right bundle-branch block with a left anterior fascicular block may develop into a complete heart block and thus require pacing.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لما يكون في new right bundle-branch block مع left anterior fascicular block، لازم تحط temporary pacemaker عشان تمنع complete heart block وتقلل الـ bradycardia. السبب إن الـ left anterior fascicle والـ right bundle branch كلهم بياخدوا الدم من الـ proximal LAD artery، فوجود block جديد معناه إنو في occlusion بهالـ artery. وفي الـ anterior wall MI اللي بيعمل necrosis للـ septum، هاد إنذار سيئ وممكن يوصل لـ complete heart block.
الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار first-degree AV block لأنه بسيط، بس هاد ما بحتاج treatment ولا pacing. و bradycardia لحالها مو indication للـ pacing إلا إذا ما استجابت للأدوية والمريض غير مستقر.

question: In children, which condition is most strongly associated with congenital pro- longed QT interval on ECG?
englishExplanation: A family history of exercise-induced syncope is associated with pro- longed QT syndrome. Prolonged QT syndrome is a serious cause of cardiac syn- cope and sudden death in children that can be congenital or acquired. The congeni- tal forms include Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome, which is characterized by re- current exercise- or stress-induced syncope, sudden death, and deafness, and Romano-Ward syndrome, which is similar to Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome but is not associated with deafness. A corrected QT interval longer than 0.44 seconds is considered abnormal, but a corrected QT interval longer than 0.55 seconds is strongly associated with sudden cardiac death. Incorrect Answer Explanations Congenital bicuspid aortic valve is a relatively common cardiac defect, seen in approximately 1% of the population. It can also be seen in patients with Marfan syn- drome, polycystic kidney disease, and other connective tissue disorders. Congenital bicuspid aortic valve can be associated with aortic dissection and aortic aneurysms. By itself, a bicuspid aortic valve does not lead to prolonged QT interval, but there are case reports of the syndromes, such as Marfan syndrome, leading to longer QT interval. Profound bradycardia on prenatal ultrasonography is a nonspecific find- ing. It does not have a known association with prolonged QT syndrome; however, it is associated with fetal loss. Multiple medications are associated with prolonged QT syndrome, but these cases are acquired and not congenital. Thus, syncope after initiating antifungal therapy with drugs such as fluconazole or ketoconazole may be due to ac- quired QT prolongation, but it is not a congenital disorder. Key Points Congenital prolonged QT syndrome is associated with a family history of exercise- induced syncope. A corrected QT interval longer than 0.44 seconds is abnormal but is associated with sudden death if it is longer than 0.55 seconds.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ family history من exercise-induced syncope مرتبط مع prolonged QT syndrome، وهاد سبب خطير للـ cardiac syncope والوفاة المفاجئة عند الأطفال. الـ congenital forms فيها Jervell and Lange-Nielsen syndrome اللي بيتميز بـ recurrent exercise- or stress-induced syncope وموت مفاجئ مع deafness، و Romano-Ward syndrome اللي نفس الشي بس بدون deafness. الـ corrected QT فوق 0.44 ثانية بيعتبر abnormal، وفوق 0.55 ثانية strongly associated مع sudden cardiac death.
الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار congenital bicuspid aortic valve لأنه شائع وبيعمل syncopes، بس هو بيسبب dissection و aneurysms مو QT prolongation. و bradycardia على prenatal ultrasonography مو مرتبطة بالـ prolonged QT، فركز على الـ corrected QT مو على الـ valve.

question: In which condition is a decreased BNP concentration most likely to be found?
englishExplanation: BNP is a counterregulatory neurohormone produced by cardiac my- ocytes in response to the stretching of ventricles and to high end-dias- tolic pressures. For unclear reasons, obese patients produce less BNP than nor- mal, even in those with high left-ventricular end-diastolic pressures. BNP is re- leased into circulation, where it is cleaved into an active BNP and an inactive NT- proBNP. The half-life of BNP is 20 minutes. BNP promotes vasodilation, diuresis, and sodium elimination; suppresses the renin-angiotensin system; and correlates with the presence and severity of heart failure. Incorrect Answer Explanations Cor pulmonale, or sustained right-sided heart failure from pulmonary arteries, will cause BNP elevation from right-sided ventricular dysfunction. Thus, a BNP level may be diagnostically helpful in such patients. A pulmonary embolism causing ventricular dysfunction can elevate BNP con- centrations, typically from right-sided heart failure. For this reason, BNP is often used in risk stratification for patients with pulmonary embolisms. In patients with renal insufficiency, there is a small increase in BNP (due to vol- ume overload and decreased ability to clear metabolites). This is one reason that an elevated BNP is just one piece of information that should be taken in the overall clinical context of the patient when making a diagnosis of heart failure.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ BNP هو neurohormone counterregulatory بينتجه خلايا القلب لما الـ ventricles تتمدد أو الـ end-diastolic pressures ترتفع. لأسباب مو واضحة، مرضى الـ obesity بينتجوا BNP أقل من العادي حتى لو عندهم end-diastolic pressures عالية، فبيطلع عندهم concentration منخفضة. الـ BNP عمره 20 دقيقة، وهو بيسبب vasodilation و diuresis وطرد الصوديوم، وبيكبت renin-angiotensin system، وعلاقته بـ heart failure مهمة.
الفخ: بعد الناس بتختار cor pulmonale أو pulmonary embolism أو renal insufficiency، وهالكلهم بيزوّدوا الـ BNP. الـ cor pulmonale من failure على اليمين، والـ PE بيرفع الـ BNP برضو، والـ renal insufficiency بيزوّد شوي. الـ BNP لازم تقراه مع كل الحالة.

question: Which intervention is most appropriate for hemodynamic support of a patient in medication-refractory cardiogenic shock?

options.text: Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA)

englishExplanation: Patients who present with cardiogenic shock refractory to medical management should be considered for circulatory support with ECMO. Specifically, venoarterial (VA) ECMO is intended to be a temporary hemodynamic support system to allow for recovery and/or deployment of more definitive therapies. Note that local institutional policies will vary as to which patients are candidates for VA ECMO. Not all patients with refractory cardiogenic shock are appropriate candidates. VA ECMO functions by augmenting or replacing (in the event of cardiac ar- rest) cardiac output. The venous circuit is the afferent limb, which feeds into a system that pumps blood into the arterial system directly via an efferent limb. Oxygenation and removal of carbon dioxide also occur during system transit. VA ECMO in the emergency department generally requires placement of two cannulas. These include a venous cannula that drains from either the IVC (femoral approach) or the right atrium (internal jugular approach) and an arterial catheter, most com- monly placed in the right femoral artery. A small catheter is often used to provide arterial perfusion to the right leg. Incorrect Answer Explanations Hemoperfusion is a form of extracorporeal blood purification in which anticoag- ulated blood is filtered through an adsorbent material, usually activated charcoal. It can be paired with hemodialysis and is run similarly. Hemoperfusion was classically used for removal of toxic substances from the blood, but for this role, it has been supplanted by high-flux hemodialysis in most places. It has no direct role in hemodynamic support for medication-refractory cardiogenic shock. Instead, ECMO is the most appropriate choice for hemodynamic support in this setting. The molecular adsorbent recirculating system (MARS) is a form of hemodialysis intended to act as an extracorporeal liver support. It uses a charcoal filter and dialysate augmented with albumin to remove albumin-bound toxins. MARS is primarily for patients with severe hepatic failure. It has no direct role in hemody- namic support for medication-refractory cardiogenic shock. Instead, ECMO is the most appropriate choice for hemodynamic support in this setting. Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) is a temporary endovascular aortic occlusion procedure used to stop life-threatening bleeding distal to the carotid arteries. Depending on the location of balloon placement, it can be used to halt aortic flow from the left subclavian artery and dis- tal (zone I) and more selectively from the pelvis and lower extremities (zone III). It has no direct role in hemodynamic support for medication-refractory cardiogenic shock. Instead, ECMO is the most appropriate choice for hemodynamic support in this setting.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن المريض اللي عنده cardiogenic shock refractory للعلاج الدوائي، لازم تفكر تسوي دعم للدورة الدموية عن طريق ECMO. الـ VA ECMO بيعمل مؤقتاً، بيزوّد cardiac output أو بيبدله بالكامل إذا صار cardiac arrest، وكمان بيعمل oxygenation وبيشيل CO2 من الدم وهو بيمر بالجهاز. في الـ ED غالباً بتحتاج cannula للـ IVC أو الـ right atrium، ومعها arterial catheter بالـ femoral artery.
الفخ: Hemoperfusion وMARS هادِم اشياء بتنقية الدم من السموم، مش جهاز support للدورة الدموية. والـ REBOA بيعمل occlusion للشريان الأورطي، فبتخلي output القلب أقل مش أكثر.

question: Which condition is most likely to result in cor pulmonale?
englishExplanation: Cor pulmonale, a term that means “pulmonary heart,” is characterized by hypertrophy of the right ventricle or alteration of right ventricular function as a result of pulmonary hypertension or chronic lung disease. The most common underlying condition that causes cor pulmonale is COPD because it frequently results in pulmonary hypertension, which is defined as a mean pulmonary arterial pressure greater than 20 mm Hg. Pulmonary hyperten- sion is divided into classifications based on the cause. Other causes of pul- monary hypertension include left heart disease, pulmonary arterial hy- pertension or obstructions, and mixed mechanisms. The pathophysiology of cor pulmonale results from the increased filling pressure in the right ventricle, which often occurs in patients with lung disease. Cor pulmonale, by definition, alters the function of the right ventricle due to a pul- monary process, and even though left heart failure can lead to right heart failure, left heart failure is not considered cor pulmonale. The most common symptom at presentation is dyspnea on exertion, but cor pulmonale patients may also present with jugular venous distention, peripheral leg edema, loud or split second heart sound, and even hepatomegaly or ascites. In addition to COPD, other primary lung disorders that can ultimately result in cor pulmonale include massive pul- monary embolism, interstitial lung disease, pulmonary fibrosis, connec- tive tissue disease, and pneumoconiosis; several different pathophysiologic mechanisms can lead to pulmonary hypertension and, subsequently, to cor pul- monale. Diagnostic modalities, such as laboratory and radiographic studies, should aim to determine and treat the underlying disease causing cor pulmonale. Incorrect Answer Explanations Dilated cardiomyopathy is primarily an enlargement of the left ventricle that causes left ventricular heart failure, which can lead to right heart failure. However, by itself, dilated cardiomyopathy due to left ventricular heart failure is not considered the cause of the right ventricular structural changes that characterize cor pulmonale. Essential hypertension can cause dysfunction of the myocardium (eg, cardiomyopathy, myocardial hypertrophy), which is a disease process of the left ventricle. Any primary abnormality of the left side of the heart or congen- ital heart disease that causes right-sided ventricular disease is not considered cor pulmonale. Remember, cor pulmonale is a term that means “pulmonary heart.” Left-sided heart failure is not a primary disorder of the lung, which is why it is not considered to be cor pulmonale. Cor pulmonale stems from pri- mary lung disorders that result in pulmonary hypertension and impaired function of the right ventricle, either due to dilation or hypertrophy.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ cor pulmonale يعني قلب رئوي، يعني تضخم أو خلل بوظيفة الـ right ventricle بسبب pulmonary hypertension أو مرض رئوي مزمن. أكثر سبب شائع هو COPD لأنه بيسبّب pulmonary hypertension، وهي إن متوسط ضغط الشريان Lung أكثر من 20 mm Hg. هاد الـ pressure العالي بيزوّد filling pressure في الـ right ventricle، وممكن تسمع S2 عالي أو منقسم مع distension في الـ jugular veins.
الفخ: بنخلّي الطالب يختار Left-sided heart failure، بس هي مش cor pulmonale حتى لو أدّت إلى right heart failure، لأن الـ cor pulmonale لازم يكون سببها رئوي. والـ Dilated cardiomyopathy وEssential hypertension مش أمراض رئية أصلاً.

question: Which laboratory finding is an independent predictor of an adverse event in acute heart failure?
englishExplanation: Patients with acute heart failure (AHF) can have a variety of abnormal laboratory test results. Renal function can worsen in up to 25% of patients with heart failure, and an elevation of serum creatinine or BUN is a strong predic- tor of adverse outcomes, including death and extended hospital stay, with a 7% increase in mortality rate for every 10 mL/min decrease in glomerular fil- tration rate. Other abnormalities can include elevation in troponin or lactate, which is associated with worse outcomes. In patients with troponin elevation alone and no ischemic ECG findings, troponin elevation is not necessarily diagnostic for myocardial infarction. Abnormalities in liver function can occur in up to 75% of patients due to systemic congestion and increased portal pressures. Incorrect Answer Explanations Thrombocytopenia can be caused by another hematologic abnormality and is not directly related to adverse events in heart failure. Chronic ane- mia, however, can lead to heart failure due to decreased oxygen delivery to the tissues. A serum sodium level of 136 mEq/L does not meet the definition of hyponatremia. The trials note that a chronic hyponatremia (serum sodium level of ≤134 mEq/L) is associated with worse outcomes in AHF. Elevated WBC counts can be related to many etiologies, such as an infection that can lead to worsening heart failure. The elevated WBC count is not an independent variable.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ renal function بتتدهور في 25% من مرضى heart failure، وارتفاع الـ serum creatinine أو الـ BUN مؤشر قوي على نتائج سيئة زي الموت وإطالة مدة الإقامة في المستشفى. الـ BUN المرتفع بيرفع نسبة الوفيات 7% مع كل نقص 10 mL/min في الـ GFR. وفي abnormalities تانية مثل troponin وlactate، بس الـ BUN هو الفحص اللي بيدّي أقوى prognostic clue هنا.
الفخ: Platelet count 140 وWBC 14,000 وSodium 136 موجودين، بس ما إلهم نفس القوة. الـ Sodium 136 مش hyponatremia لأن التعريف ≤134 mEq/L، والـ thrombocytopenia والـ WBC المرتفع Causes تانية مو مرتبطة مباشرة بالنتائج.

question: A 70-year-old woman with severe pulmonary hypertension presents with dysp- nea and lightheadedness. Her vital signs include BP 95/58 (MAP 70), P 112, and R 26; SpO is 82% on 4-L nasal cannula. On examination, she is cool to the touch with noticeable jugular vein distention. POCUS shows a dilated right ventricle. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
englishExplanation: This patient is experiencing decompensated right ventricular (RV) failure. In chronic pulmonary hypertension, the RV becomes thin-walled, dilated, and highly afterload-sensitive. HFNC is the ideal intervention because it pro- vides a high FiO without the significant increase in intrathoracic pressure associ- ated with positive-pressure ventilation. The primary management priorities are to maintain RV coronary perfu- sion pressure, ensure adequate oxygenation, and minimize further in- creases in pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR). Preventing the RV death spiral is critical. In this spiral, hypoxia triggers pulmonary vasoconstriction, which increases RV afterload and leads to further RV dilation. This dila- tion causes the RV to compress the left ventricle, while systemic hypotension simul- taneously reduces right coronary artery perfusion, causing worsening myocardial is- chemia. Maintaining a systemic MAP that exceeds pulmonary pressures is vital. Furthermore, any intervention that increases intrathoracic pressure, such as NIPPV or intubation, will further increase RV afterload and decrease venous return, often precipitating immediate hemodynamic collapse. Incorrect Answer Explanations Although the RV is traditionally considered "preload dependent," it is extremely easy to overload a failing, chronically dilated RV. Administering 2 L of lactated Ringer solution to a patient who already has evidence of right-sided overload (eg, jugular vein distention) increases RV end-diastolic pres- sure, which pushes the interventricular septum into the left ventricle and worsening RV dynamics. Although NIPPV is a mainstay for left-sided heart failure (to reduce preload and af- terload), it is often harmful in severe RV failure since it increases right- sided afterload and reduces right-sided preload. Similar to intubation, NIPPV can cause hemodynamic collapse. Intubation is one of the most dangerous procedures in a patient with RV failure because the transition to positive-pressure ventilation and the sympatholytic effects of induction agents often lead to immediate car- diovascular collapse and cardiac arrest. The sudden increase in intrathoracic 2 pressure decreases venous return (preload) and increases PVR (afterload), which a failing RV cannot overcome.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن هالمريضة عندها decompensated right ventricular failure بسبب chronic pulmonary hypertension، والـ RV صار thin-walled وdilated وحسّاس جداً للـ afterload. الـ HFNC أحسن خيار لأنه بيوفّر FiO عالية بدون ما يزيد الـ intrathoracic pressure اللي بيضر الـ RV. لازم تحافظ على oxygenation كويس وتتجنّب أي شي بيزوّد PVR عشان ما تدخل في الـ death spiral.
الفخ: NIPPV وintubation بيعملوا العكس، لأن الـ positive pressure بيزوّد afterload على الـ RV وبيقلّل venous return، وهاد ممكن يسبّب collapse فوري. و2 L من lactated Ringer بيزيد الـ preload على RV فاتح وم dilatado، فبتخليه ينهار.

question: Which type of cardiomyopathy is best described as a long-term condition charac- terized by impaired ventricular filling, nondilated ventricles, and normal systolic function early in the disease?
englishExplanation: Restrictive cardiomyopathy is characterized by ventricles that are not dilated but have impaired ventricular filling. Biatrial enlargement is seen on echocardiogram. Usually, there is no ventricular hypertrophy unless an infiltrative disease (eg, amyloidosis) causes an increase in left ventricular thickness. Early in the disease, the systolic function is normal. Plain two-dimensional echocar- diography may not catch the impaired ventricular filling — Doppler echocardiogra- phy is an effective tool for diagnosis. Incorrect Answer Explanations This patient has ventricles that are not dilated. Dilation of the ventricles is pathognomonic for dilated cardiomyopathy, as is suggested by the name. The dilation becomes severe over time, and patients have impaired systolic function and clinical symptoms of heart failure. On echocardiogram, the left ventricle may appear more spherical due to dilation. Left atrial enlargement can also often be seen in conjunction with the other findings described. In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), the left ventricular volume is normal or reduced, and diastolic dysfunction is generally present. Technically, HCM includes a variety of conditions characterized by increased ven- tricular wall thickness or mass that are not caused by cardiovascular pathologies, such as hypertension or valve disease. Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is also known as apical ballooning syndrome or broken heart syndrome. It is considered a stress-induced cardiomyopathy, character- ized by transient systolic dysfunction of the apical and/or middle segments of the left ventricle.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ restrictive cardiomyopathy بتوصف بـ ventricles مش dilated بس فيها impaired ventricular filling. الـ echocardiogram بتبيّن biatrial enlargement، وما في ventricular hypertrophy إلا إذا سببها مرض infiltrative مثل amyloidosis. في بداية المرض الـ systolic function بتكون طبيعية. الـ 2D echo ممكن ما تلتقط مشكلة الـ filling، فالـ Doppler echocardiography هو الأداة الفعّالة للتشخيص.
الفخ: بنخلّي الطالب يختار Dilated cardiomyopathy، بس الـ restrictive فيها ventricles مش dilated وهذا عكس الاسم. وHypertrophic بتتميّز بزيادة سماكة الجدار وdiastolic dysfunction، وTakotsubo اسمها apical ballooning وبيجي بعد stress.

question: What is a causative agent for myocarditis (inflammatory cardiomyopathy)?
englishExplanation: Commonly known as myocarditis, inflammatory cardiomyopathy is acquired. Myocarditis is inflammation of the heart muscle and is pathologically characterized by focal infiltration of the myocardium by inflammatory cells (lymphocytes, plasma cells, and histiocytes). Episodes are often mild, so they do not always come to medical attention. Coxsackie B is one example of a viral agent that can cause myocarditis. Others are listed below. Bacterial: Beta-hemolytic streptococci (rheumatic fever) Corynebacterium diphtheriae Lyme disease Mycoplasma pneumoniae Neisseria meningitidis Viral: Coxsackie B virus Echovirus EBV Hepatitis B virus HIV Influenza virus Parainfluenza virus Incorrect Answer Explanations Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy is a heart muscle disorder, not a func- tion of an inflammatory condition. It is caused by structural abnormalities of the myocardium and causes arrhythmia that is not explained by ischemia, hyper- tension, or valve disease. In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), the left ventricular volume is normal or reduced, and diastolic dysfunction is generally present. Technically, HCM includes a variety of conditions characterized by increased ven- tricular wall thickness or mass that are not caused by cardiovascular pathologies, such as hypertension or valve disease. It should not cause a sudden inflammation of the heart. Left ventricular noncompaction is very rare and is a childhood/developmental disorder. Left ventricular noncompaction is an un- classified cardiomyopathy due to an altered myocardial wall. The left ventricle does not develop correctly, and the cardiac muscle in this area is thick and appears spongy. Consequently, there is continuity between the left ventricular cavity and in- tertrabecular recesses. When severe, left ventricular noncompaction can be associ- ated with heart failure and arrhythmias. Left ventricular noncompaction is a slow progression of symptoms and disease that can later require heart transplant, but it should not cause myocarditis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ myocarditis aka inflammatory cardiomyopathy هي inflammation في عضلة القلب، وبيتكشف فيها focal infiltration للـ myocardium بخلايا inflammatory مثل lymphocytes وplasma cells وhistiocytes. الـ Coxsackie B virus من أشهر الـ viral agents اللي بيسبّبو myocarditis. الـ episodes كتير خفيفة وممكن ما توصل للمستشفى، والأعراض بتبدأ أيام لأسابيع بعد العدوى. والـ manifestations ممكن تكون من أعراض constitutional خفيفة لغاية decompensation cardiopulmonary سريع ممكن يوصل لموت.
الفخ: بنخلّي الطالب يختار HCM أو Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy، وهادِم disorders بنيوية بالعضلة مش inflammation مفاجئ. أما Left ventricular noncompaction نادرة جداً وما إلها علاقة بالتهاب القلب إطلاقاً.

question: In patients with heart failure and dilated cardiomyopathy, which pharmacologic treatment has been proven to improve survival rates?
englishExplanation: Beta-blockers, specifically carvedilol and metoprolol, have been shown to improve survival in patients with dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure. Notably, ACE inhibitors have also been shown to decrease mortality in these patients. Patients should be started on 12.5 mg to 25 mg of metoprolol succi- nate CR/XL daily, with a later goal of 200 mg daily. Incorrect Answer Explanations Chronic therapy for patients with heart failure and dilated cardiomy- opathy may include digoxin, but it does not seem to improve survival rates. Digoxin may be added as part of the treatment regimen for adult patients with mild to moderate heart failure. Its secondary benefit is that it may control ven- tricular rate in patients with atrial fibrillation. Chronic therapy for patients with heart failure and dilated cardiomy- opathy often involves diuretics, such as furosemide, bumetanide, or torsemide. Diuretics allow for patient comfort and treatment of fluid overload sec- ondary to heart failure. However, they do not improve survival rates. Morphine has historically been used in the treatment of congestive heart failure. However, there is no evidence of a mortality benefit, and in fact, some evi- dence of harm. It may be used in a palliative capacity for patients with end-stage heart failure.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ beta-blockers، وبالذات carvedilol وmetoprolol، أثبتوا إنها بتحسّن البقاء عند مرضى heart failure مع dilated cardiomyopathy. بتبدأ الـ metoprolol succinate CR/XL بجرعة 12.5 لـ 25 mg يومياً، والهدف لاحقاً 200 mg يومياً. وACE inhibitors كمان أثبتت إنها بتقلّل الـ mortality عند مرضى الـ dilated cardiomyopathy، بينما الـ diuretics بتخفف الأعراض بس وما بتحسّن البقاء.
الفخ: Digoxin وFurosemide وMorphine كلهم بيوصفوا في heart failure، بس ما بيحسنوا البقاء. الـ Furosemide بيعالج الـ fluid overload وبيعطي راحة، والـ Morphine ما في دليل على فايدة بل في ضرر وبيستخدم بشكل palliative بس.

question: What is the gold standard for diagnosing myocarditis (inflammatory cardiomyopathy)?
englishExplanation: Technically, an endocardial biopsy is the gold standard for diagnosing my- ocarditis, but it is rarely used because of its invasiveness. Instead, a review of clinical symptoms and supportive testing can be used. An ECG, echocardiogram, and chest x-ray may be beneficial as supporting tests to reach this diagnosis. Other helpful studies may include a troponin or BNP level (which may be elevated), PET scan, or cardiac MRI. Fever, myalgias, headache, and tachycardia are common signs and symp- toms of myocarditis. Heart failure can develop in severe cases. Chest pain may occur when pericardial inflammation is also present (myopericarditis). Incorrect Answer Explanations A chest x-ray is usually normal or nondiagnostic in myocarditis. In severe cases in which heart failure is present, cardiomegaly and pulmonary venous congestion/pulmonary edema may also be present. Despite this, a chest x-ray is an adjunct that should be added to the overall workup when considering myocarditis as a potential diagnosis. ECG changes will generally be nonspecific in myocarditis. Examples of what may be seen include nonspecific ST-T–wave changes, ST-segment elevation or PR depression from associated pericarditis, atrioventricular block, and QRS interval prolongation. Echocardiography can help to support the diagnosis of myocarditis, but it can be nonspecific and is not the gold standard. In severe cases, symp- toms of heart failure such as myocardial depression and wall motion abnormalities may be seen. If there is concomitant pericarditis, an effusion may be seen. Newer imaging modalities like nuclear imaging with PET and cardiac MRI may be useful to add.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ endocardial biopsy هي gold standard لتشخيص myocarditis، بس نادراً ما بنستخدمها لأنها invasive. بدلها بنعمل review للأعراض السريرية مع الفحوصات المساندة. الـ ECG والـ echocardiogram والـ chest x-ray بيساعدوا للوصول للتشخيص، وكمان troponin أو BNP ممكن يكونوا مرتفعين، مع cardiac MRI أو PET scan كدراسات مساعدة. الـ fever وmyalgias وtachycardia أعراض شائعة.
الفخ: الـ chest x-ray غالباً طبيعي أو غير مُحدِّد، والـ ECG تغييراته غير نوعية مثل ST-T changes أو PR depression أو AV block. الـ echocardiography بيساند بس مو gold standard، لأن الـ biopsy وحدها اللي بتأكد التشخيص.

question: A 31-year-old man presents after he fainted while mowing his lawn. He remem- bers feeling short of breath before he fainted but is now asymptomatic. A physi- cal examination reveals a healthy-appearing man with a harsh crescendo-de- crescendo midsystolic murmur that increases with a Valsalva maneuver. An ECG is obtained and shown below. Assuming basic laboratory test results are normal, which diagnostic study should be ordered? Credit: William J. Brady, MD, FACEP.
englishExplanation:
The ECG demonstrates left ventricular hypertrophy, and Q waves in leads I and aVL are all characteristic and highly suggestive of hypertrophic car- diomyopathy. Such findings should prompt ordering of transthoracic echocardiography to confirm the diagnosis; furthermore, exercise restriction and cardiology referral should also be considered. Hypertrophic cardiomyopa- thy is an autosomal-dominant disease characterized by disorganized cardiac cell ar- rangement, asymmetric hypertrophy of the ventricular septum, and malformations of the mitral valve leaflets. These structural abnormalities can lead to fatal tach- yarrhythmias and ventricular outflow obstruction. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the single most common cardiac cause of death in young athletes. Patients might present with activity-induced shortness of breath, near-syncope, syncope, chest pain, palpitations, and even sudden death. In addition to strenuous activity or exer- tion, other “hyperadrenergic” states can precipitate arrhythmia, including extreme emotions (anger, fright). Thus, the consideration of adrenergically related syncope is a more appropriate screening process than simply exertional syncope. The most specific ECG findings in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are deep, narrow Q waves in the lateral leads (I, aVL, V5, V6). The most common, however, are large-amplitude QRS complexes consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy and associated ST-seg- ment and T-segment changes in the precordial leads. Other ECG findings might in- clude high-voltage R waves in V1 and V2 and deep narrow Q waves in the inferior leads (II, III, aVF). In the 12-lead ECG from this case, note the presence of promi- nent R waves and ST-segment elevation in the right to mid precordial leads and Q waves in the lateral leads. The lateral Q waves are very specific in the correct clinical setting for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Beta-blockers, which are the mainstay of therapy, decrease the effect of catecholamines on the outflow gradient. Incorrect Answer Explanations Chest x-ray has limited value for stable patients who had a syncopal episode without any respiratory abnormalities. A transthoracic echocardiogram would be a more helpful test in this situation. Coronary CT angiography is useful in some chest pain patients suspected of coronary abnormalities, but it has no value in the initial evaluation of the syncope patient. A transthoracic echocardiogram would be a more helpful test in this situation. Head CT scans have limited utility in the syncope patient who has no neurologic concerns. A transthoracic echocardiogram would be a more helpful test in this situation.

Review notes: ["visual_reference_no_image_attached_in_jsonl"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ ECG بتبيّن left ventricular hypertrophy وQ waves في الـ leads I وaVL، وهاد مميّز بشكل كبير لـ hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. لمّا تشوف هيك ECG لازم تطلب transthoracic echocardiography للتأكيد، مع اعتبار exercise restriction وإحالة الـ cardiology. الـ HCM مرض autosomal dominant فيه ترتيب خلايا قلبي غير منظم وتضخم غير متجانس للـ septum مع تشوهات بـ mitral valve.
الفخ: الـ chest x-ray والـ coronary CT angiography والـ head CT ما إلها دور هون لتشخيص سبب الـ murmur مع الـ syncope. الـ ECG بيعمل screening والتأكيد النهائي دايماً بالـ echocardiography.

question: A 19-year-old man presents after a syncopal event that occurred while he was ex- ercising. What is the diagnostic test of choice to evaluate for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy?
englishExplanation: Transthoracic echocardiography is the diagnostic test of choice to as- sess for suspected hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). It can demon- strate the hypertrophic segment, cardiac function, left ventricular outflow gradient, and any associated valvular abnormalities. Cardiac MRI is generally used as a second-line imaging alternative if the echocardiogram provides inadequate views. Although physical examination and ECG can demonstrate characteristic find- ings, these are considered more appropriate for screening than diagnosis. Physical examination may reveal a crescendo-decrescendo midsystolic murmur that decreases in intensity when the patient is squatting. ECG may reveal classic inferior and lateral “dagger” Q waves. This case is a classic presentation of symptomatic HCM: a young adult patient who develops syncope associated with exertion. Symptoms can range from vague fatigue, dyspnea, chest pain, and palpitations to exertional presyncope and syncope. In some patients, the initial presenting event is sudden death, whereas others may remain asymptomatic. Beta-blockers are first-line treat- ments for HCM. They decrease myocardial contractility and heart rate, thereby increasing the diastolic filling period. The pathophysiology of symptomatic HCM is complex. Classically, symptoms are thought to be due to left ventricular outflow obstruction caused by abnormal left ventricular hypertrophy. Increases in heart rate, such as from exertion in this case, decrease the diastolic filling period, thereby compromising left ventricular fill- ing and worsening function. However, the hypertrophy can occur in different loca- tions and have different levels of severity, leading to heterogeneous presentations. Incorrect Answer Explanations Although a CT scan of the chest can theoretically visualize an abnormally enlarged section of the heart, it has no established role in the evaluation of HCM specifically. In this setting, it would be more valuable for ruling out other dan- gerous causes of syncope, such as a large pulmonary embolism. CT coronary angiog- raphy is also sometimes used to evaluate the coronary arteries in the setting of HCM, but this is generally done only after diagnosis. An echocardiogram is the test of choice to diagnose HCM in this patient. The classic ECG findings associated with HCM include left axis devia- tion, left atrial enlargement, and deep and narrow inferior (II,III, aVF) and lateral (I, aVL, V4 to V6) Q waves, known as dagger Q waves. However, these features are neither universally present nor diagnostic of HCM alone; ECG findings are normal in a small percentage of patients with HCM. Although ECG is an essential part of the diagnostic evaluation for this patient, it is not the best diagnostic test for HCM. This patient should receive a echocardiogram to definitively diagnose HCM. Exercise stress testing may be used following diagnosis of HCM for additional risk- stratification purposes, but it is generally not used as an initial diagnostic test. Instead, this patient should receive a echocardiogram to definitively diagnose HCM.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ transthoracic echocardiography هو diagnostic test of choice لتقييم suspected hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. بيبيّن الـ hypertrophic segment والـ cardiac function والـ left ventricular outflow gradient وأي abnormalities مرتبطة بالـ valves. الـ cardiac MRI بيستخدم كـ second-line imaging إذا الـ echo ما أعطى views كافية. الـ الفحص السريري والـ ECG بيعملوا screening مش diagnosis.
الفخ: بنخلّي الطالب يختار Exercise stress test أو Chest CT، وهادِم ما بيقيسوا الـ septum ولا الـ gradient. الـ echo هو اللي بيكشف تضخم الـ septum، والـ murmur بيخفّ لما يسكّر الـ patient اللي عنده HCM.

question: A pregnant patient presents with shortness of breath. Which finding is most con- sistent with a diagnosis of peripartum cardiomyopathy?
englishExplanation: The most widely accepted definition of peripartum cardiomyopathy man- dates left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of less than 45%. A variety of terms and definitions have been used to characterize peripartum cardiomyopathy, including toxic postpartum heart failure, Meadows syndrome, Zaria syndrome, and postpartum myocardiosis. However, the definition developed by the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) in 2010 (which was included in the 2018 ESC guidelines) is the most widely used and has been incorporated in position statements and management guidelines. The ESC defines peripartum cardiomyopathy as an idiopathic process with the fol- lowing characteristics: Heart failure at the end of pregnancy or in the 5 months following delivery; Absence of another identifiable cause; and Left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of less than 45%. Incorrect Answer Explanations The working definition of peripartum cardiomyopathy precludes an identifiable cause of heart failure, such as cocaine abuse. Several factors are associated with an increased risk of peripartum cardiomyopathy, including preeclampsia or eclampsia, pregnancy-induced hypertension, cocaine cardiomyopathy, and hypertension disorder. Because the etiology of peripartum cardiomyopathy is idiopathic, identifiable causes (eg, cocaine abuse) are excluded. Peripartum cardiomyopathy typically results in systolic dysfunction rather than diastolic dysfunction. Left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of less than 45% is included in the working definition. Although re- strictive cardiomyopathies (eg, amyloidosis or endomyocardial fibrosis) can result in diastolic dysfunction, peripartum cardiomyopathy is associated with systolic dysfunction. Peripartum cardiomyopathy is rarely seen prior to 36 weeks of gesta- tion; most cases present in the 1st month postpartum. Pregnant patients with un- derlying cardiac disease may present with heart failure earlier in the second trimester; however, first-trimester presentations are extremely unlikely.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ peripartum cardiomyopathy حسب تعريف الـ ESC من 2010، اللي اندمج بالـ 2018 ESC guidelines، هي idiopathic process بتحصل آخر الحمل أو بخمسة أشهر بعد الولادة، بدون أي سبب تاني معروف، ومعها left ventricular systolic dysfunction بـ ejection fraction أقل من 45%. هاد التعريف الأوسع قبولاً وبيستخدم في الـ position statements والـ management guidelines.
