question: Which test has the greatest diagnostic value when evaluating a 1-week postpar- tum patient with symptoms of heart failure?
englishExplanation: Echocardiogram should be performed in pregnant and postpartum pa- tients who are clinically suspected of having peripartum cardiomyopa- thy. It usually reveals a dilated left ventricle with reduced left ventricular systolic function and an ejection fraction less than 45%. Other findings may include a dilated left atrium, a left atrial or ventricular thrombus, dilated right ventricle with hypokinesis, mitral and tricuspid regurgitation, or a pericardial effusion. Besides an echocardiogram, the other test that is highly recommended in heart fail- ure and peripartum cardiomyopathy is an ECG. ECG is helpful in identifying car- diac ischemia. Cardiac MRI, cardiac catheterization, and endomyocardial biopsy have limited utility, except in special cases. Incorrect Answer Explanations A measurement of plasma BNP or NT-proBNP may be useful if the diagnosis of heart failure is uncertain. However, it will not provide as much diagnostic in- formation as an echocardiogram and is not as helpful and a good history and physical examination. It is worth noting that elevated BNP levels should be inter- preted with caution because an acute large pulmonary embolism may cause similar elevations of the peptide. Although it is not as useful as an echocardiogram and good history and physical ex- amination in making a diagnosis of heart failure, a chest x-ray may be a useful an- cillary test in select cases. A chest x-ray will typically show an enlarged heart with evidence of congestion and interstitial edema, but an echocardiogram will provide more useful diagnostic information. Elevated D-dimers are generally used to rule-out pulmonary embolism in non- pregnant patients, but they are of less diagnostic utility in pregnant or postpartum patients for whom D-dimers tend to be elevated. An echocardiogram is generally more useful to diagnose heart failure in peripartum cardiomyopathy.

ليش: اللي صار إنه لازم يتعمل echocardiogram لكل مريضة حامل أو بعد الولادة عندها اشتباه بـ peripartum cardiomyopathy. غالباً بيظهر left ventricle dilated مع reduced left ventricular systolic function وejection fraction أقل من 45%. وممكن كمان نشوف left atrium dilated أو thrombus بِـ left atrium أو ventricle، أو right ventricle dilated مع hypokinesis، أو mitral وtricuspid regurgitation، أو pericardial effusion.
الفخ: BNP أو NT-proBNP بتكون مفيدة بس مش informative زي الـ echocardiogram، وكمان ارتفاعها ممكن يكون بسبب pulmonary embolism كبير. والـ D-dimer test وchest x-ray بيضلوا فحوصات مساندة، مش الفحص الأهم لهاد الوضع.

question: Which ultrasound finding is expected in a patient with decompensated peripar- tum cardiomyopathy?

options.text: B-lines in more than two rib spaces limited to the right thorax
E-point septal separation of more than 10 mm
IVC collapsibility index of more than 50%
Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion of more than 17 mm

correctAnswer: E-point septal separation of more than 10 mm
englishExplanation: The E-point septal separation (EPSS) is a surrogate measurement of left ventricular function. Performed in M-mode, the EPSS measures the minimum distance between the interventricular septum and the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve at its maximum excursion in the ventricular diastole. A value of less than 7 mm is considered normal, and a value of more than 10 mm is suggestive of heart failure. The utilization of POCUS in pregnancy has become increasingly popular because it can be done at the bedside, has minimal radiation exposure to the fetus, and is highly sensitive and specific when performed by a trained operator. In heart failure, performance of the “triple scan” (POCUS of the heart, lungs, and IVC) reveals a specific pattern of abnormalities: reduced left ven- tricular function (<45%), diffuse bilateral B-lines, and a plethoric IVC. Overall, POCUS provides a reasonable, quick bedside screening of a suspected peripartum cardiomyopathy, with the potential of minimizing radiation exposure typical of other imaging modalities. Incorrect Answer Explanations B-lines are hyperechoic lines perpendicular to the pleural margin. They move with respiration and erase the normal A-lines. In acute decompensated heart failure, POCUS of the lungs will depict three or more B-lines per rib space in two or more rib spaces bilaterally across the thorax, a pattern indicative of an acute inter- stitial syndrome due to increased fluid in the lungs. Focal B-lines in a single area or in one lung suggest some other lung pathology (eg, pneumonia or pulmonary embolism). In fluid-overload states (eg, acute decompensated heart failure), the POCUS of the IVC typically reveals a plethoric vessel with a very low collapsibility index. An IVC collapsibility index of more than 50% is typically seen in volume-contracted states (eg, dehydration or sepsis). The tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) is a validated parameter of global right ventricular function. A normally functioning right ventricle would demonstrate a TAPSE of more than 17 mm. This test is typically per- formed to assess right ventricular strain (eg, pulmonary embolism) rather than acute decompensated heart failure. In peripartum cardiomyopathy, the primary deficit is reduced systolic function of the left ventricle.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ E-point septal separation بنقيسها بـ M-mode، وهي المسافة الصغرى بين الـ interventricular septum والـ anterior leaflet للـ mitral valve وقت أقصى فتح. أقل من 7 mm بتعتبر طبيعية، وأكثر من 10 mm بتكون suggestive لحد ما يكون فيه heart failure. الـ POCUS بالـ triple scan بتبيّن reduced LV function وB-lines bilateral وIVC plethoric، وهو فحص سريع وبيقلّل التعرض للإشعاع.
الفخ: الـ B-lines مو على اليمين بس؛ في acute decompensated failure بتظهر ثلاث أو أكثر بكل rib space في مساحتين أو أكثر bilaterally. والـ IVC collapsibility index أكثر من 50% معناها للسوائل مو plethoric.

question: Which medication when used in the out-of-hospital setting has been shown to cause harm in acute heart failure?
englishExplanation: Out-of-hospital use of morphine sulfate for presumed pulmonary edema has been associated with a higher rate of endotracheal intubation, particularly in patients whose conditions turn out to have been misdiagnosed in the field. It is also associ- ated with a longer stay in the hospital, a higher rate of ICU admission, and a greater risk of death. Clinical evaluation and empiric therapy often occur simultaneously in acute heart failure (AHF). Initial management consists of supplemental oxygen, car- diac monitoring, pulse oximetry, and intravenous access. Patients with clinical signs of exhaustion or hypoxia despite supplemental oxygen require respiratory support via either invasive or noninvasive means. Pooled data from several randomized, controlled clinical trials suggest that the use of CPAP (at 5-10 mm Hg) improves hemodynamics by reducing preload and afterload, thereby enhancing left ventricu- lar performance in patients with respiratory distress caused by AHF. Ultimately, CPAP has been shown to reduce the need for endotracheal intubation and is associ- ated with a lower mortality rate. Nitroglycerin is another measure to improve pul- monary edema and the work of breathing. Early administration of furosemide in acute pulmonary edema appears to have very little benefit and might result in short- term complications because many patients with AHF are intravascularly volume de- pleted (the volume has been redistributed to the wrong area, such as the lungs). Incorrect Answer Explanations Aspirin has not been found to be harmful in heart failure and should be provided if ischemia is suspected. Other NSAIDs should be avoided due to the risk of renal in- jury and further salt and water retention through their effects on prostaglandin synthesis. A small number of trials have demonstrated rapid improvement in dyspnea after a single dose of sublingual captopril. Significant reduction in blood pressure after in- travenous administration of enalaprilat has also been seen. Nitroglycerin has been proved to be the safest and most effective therapy for pre- sumed pulmonary edema. Compared with placebo therapy in the Vasodilation in the Management of Acute Congestive Heart Failure (VMAC) trial, intravenous ni- troglycerin resulted in marked improvement in dyspnea. The ability of nitroglycerin to decrease preload and produce cardiac vessel vasodilation ultimately reduces my- ocardial effort.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن استخدام morphine sulfate خارج المستشفى لحالة pulmonary edema مفترضة ارتبط مع نسبة أعلى من endotracheal intubation، خاصة عند مرضى اتشخّصوا غلط بالميدان. كمان ارتبط مع مدة إقامة أطول بالمستشفى ونسبة أعلى للدخول للـ ICU وخطر وفاة أكبر. والمبادئ التوجيهية بتقول إن الـ evaluation السريري والـ empiric therapy بصيروا بنفس الوقت مع الأكسجين والمونيتور والـ IV access، والـ Morphine مش جزء منها.
الفخ: الـ Morphine هو اللي بيأذي، مش الـ Aspirin أو الـ Nitroglycerin. الـ Nitroglycerin بيحسّن pulmonary edema وwork of breathing، والـ CPAP بيقلّل الـ preload والـ afterload وبينقّص الـ intubation والـ mortality، بينما الـ Morphine بيخلي الموضوع worse.

question: A patient with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction presents with dyspnea, respiratory distress, and hypoxia. Bedside lung ultrasound is shown below. Which respiratory intervention decreases the risk of intubation? Credit: Frances Russell, MD, FACEP.
englishExplanation:
Symptomatic acute decompensated systolic heart failure with pul- monary edema (as evidenced by B lines on bedside ultrasound) and hy- poxia is best treated with NIPPV in addition to standard medical therapy, such as nitrates and diuretics. A 2019 Cochrane Review noted this combination signifi- cantly decreases endotracheal intubation rates and in-hospital mortality com- pared with standard medical therapy alone. BiPAP or CPAP can be used; as of this writing, there is no evidence to suggest one method is superior to the other — both provide ventilatory and oxygenation sup- port. CPAP works by providing constant pressure throughout the respi- ratory cycle, decreasing the work of the inspiratory musculature and in- 0:00/ 0:05 creasing tidal volume by reducing dead space and increasing alveolar ventilation. Additionally, the increased intrathoracic pressure reduces preload and afterload. Unlike CPAP, BiPAP pressures are different between expiration and in- halation. BiPAP has two elements, the inspiratory positive airway pressure (IPAP) and the expiratory positive airway pressure (EPAP), which is conceptually similar to CPAP. The IPAP is always higher than the EPAP. The difference between IPAP and EPAP is known as the delta pressure and is the measure of the ventilatory support the BiPAP is providing. This allows for active augmentation of ventilation with further decreased respiratory muscle workload while also maintaining the ben- efits attributed to CPAP. Patients with coincidental acute hypercarbia may benefit from this additional ventilatory support. Endotracheal intubation is indicated in settings where NIPPV would be contraindicated, such as depressed or altered men- tal status, apnea, and cardiac arrest. Incorrect Answer Explanations Although this patient should be provided oxygen support, high-flow oxygen, such as with nonrebreather mask or HFNC, has no additional value in this circumstance over other forms of oxygen delivery. When given the choice between high-flow oxygen by nonrebreather mask and NIPPV, NIPPV is the superior choice because it provides oxygen and ventilatory support and can improve outcomes in this setting. Inhaled nitric oxide is a potent, selective pulmonary vasodilator used to treat a variety of right heart and pulmonary vascular conditions, such as pulmonary hypertension. Its mechanism of action is local vasodilation of venti- lated lung, which reduces pulmonary vascular resistance. This improves both V/Q matching and pulmonary arterial forward flow. Although the effect of inhaled nitric oxide on the pulmonary vasculature is similar to that of systemic nitrates, it does not affect systemic preload or afterload. As the left heart is distant from these local pulmonary vascular effects, inhaled nitric oxide is unlikely to provide mean- ingful benefit for acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema. Instead, NIPPV has several beneficial effects in this setting and should be used early and aggressively. Nebulized bronchodilators are valuable in the setting of bronchospasm, such as with asthma or COPD. However, bronchodilators have no estab- lished role in the treatment of acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema. Additionally, use of beta agonists such as albuterol would increase cardiac work by beta-1 receptor stimulation, potentially worsening the patient's clinical condition. Instead, NIPPV has several beneficial effects in this setting and should be used early and aggressively.

BiPAP أو CPAP بيستخدموا، وما في دليل إن واحد أحسن من التاني.
الفخ: الـ High-flow nonrebreather mask ما بيوفّر ضغط إيجابي فبفضل الـ work of breathing. والـ Inhaled nitric oxide والـ nebulized bronchodilators مو للـ pulmonary edema، بينما الـ NIPPV بيقدّم ضغط إيجابي وبيحسّن الـ oxygenation.

question: Which finding has the highest positive-likelihood ratio for a diagnosis of ACS?

options.text: Radiation of pain to both arms

correctAnswer: Radiation of pain to both arms
englishExplanation: Although it is not diagnostic of ACS, the presence of radiation of chest pain to both arms is strongly suggestive of ACS and presents a high like- lihood for it. A JAMA Rational Clinical Examination Systematic Review found this feature to increase the risk of ACS 2.6x (positive LR 1.8-3.7). In the approach to a patient with suspected acute coronary ischemia, the emergency physician has to consider many factors of the history and examination, such as how the patient de- scribes their symptoms, the patient's medical history, whether there is a family his- tory of cardiovascular disease, what clues the ECG provides, and what abnormalities are noted in cardiac markers. In addition to pain radiation to both arms, other high-likelihood features of ACS include chest pain that is similar to the patient's prior anginal chest pain, change in pattern of pain over 24 hours, diaphoresis, known coronary artery disease (CAD), history of pe- ripheral arterial disease, abnormal prior stress test result, a history of myocardial infarction (MI), hypotension, pulmonary edema, ischemic ECG changes, ST depressions, and elevated HEART score. Incorrect Answer Explanations If a patient presents with classic risk factors for CAD (eg, a medical history of hyper- tension, diabetes mellitus, or hyperlipidemia; a family history of MI before age 50; and smoking), the emergency physician should consider ACS. However, these features are not the most suggestive of acute coronary ischemia, and are not even high-likelihood features for ACS. At most, these features represent inter- mediate-likelihood features. Recent cocaine use is a low-likelihood finding for acute MI. More important acute factors are an abnormal prior stress test result, known CAD, peripheral arterial dis- ease, pain radiating to both arms, and pain similar to prior ischemia. Although T-wave flattening is an abnormal ECG finding, it has a low likelihood for ACS. More important markers are pain radiating to both arms, previous abnormal stress test result, and known CAD, among others. ECG findings with the highest likelihood ratios for ACS include ST depression or ischemic-looking ECG. Key Points Radiation of pain to both arms is strongly suggestive of ACS. Clinical features associated with a high likelihood for ACS include pain radiating to both arms, pain similar to prior ischemia, change in pattern of symptoms over 24 hours, diaphoresis, hypotension, and elevated HEART score. The ECG features on the ACS high likelihood list include new ischemic ECG findings or ST depressions. High likelihood features of ACS from a patient's history include known coronary artery disease, peripheral arterial disease, an abnormal previous stress test, or pre- vious myocardial infarction.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن انتشار ألم الصدر على الذراعين مع بعضه مش diagnostic للـ ACS، بس strongly suggestive وبيدّي احتمال كبير. مراجعة من JAMA Rational Clinical Examination لقتها إن هاد العلامة بتزوّد خطر الـ ACS 2.6 مرة (positive LR 1.8-3.7). وطبعاً الـ emergency physician بينظر لتاريخ المرض والفحص والـ ECG والـ cardiac markers مع بعضهم، مو علامة لحالها.
الفخ: Coronary artery disease risk factors بتخليك تفكر بالـ ACS بس إلها likelihood أقل من انتشار الألم على الذراعين. والـ T-wave flattening لحالها مش من علامات ischemia المعتمدة، والـ recent cocaine use ما بيعطي نفس القوة.

question: What is the most appropriate disposition for patients who are being evaluated for ACS based on their HEART score in the emergency department?

options.text: Admit a patient with a HEART score ≤3 for observation and noninvasive cardiac testing
Admit every patient with chest pain for cardiac testing regardless of the HEART score
Discharge a patient with a HEART score of ≤3 with two negative troponins
Discharge a patient with a HEART score of 4 to 6 and a negative initial troponin

correctAnswer: Discharge a patient with a HEART score of ≤3 with two negative troponins
englishExplanation:
Patients with a HEART (History, ECG findings, Age, Risk factors, and Troponin) score of 0 to 3 and two negative high-sensitivity troponins (taken 3 hours apart within 6 hours of onset symptoms) have a <0.4% chance of cardiac-related mortal- ity or myocardial infarction (ie, a Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event [MACE]) and can be safely discharged. The HEART score tool has been validated to predict 30- day adverse events in patients with suspected ACS in the emergency department. However, validation studies of the HEART score revealed the need to add a 3-hr repeat troponin for patients with risk score of 0 to 3 who presented within 6 hours of symptoms onset. This is what is considered a HEART pathway. Multiple studies have shown more than 99% sensitivity of the HEART pathway; a randomized clinical trial has validated the HEART pathway, and no patients had ad- verse cardiac events at 30 days. As in any clinical presentation, it is important to consider all potential diagnoses of chest pain. The HEART score specifically applies to ACS. However, there are multi- ple other causes of chest pain that must be considered and that can be life-threaten- ing if undiagnosed, such as pulmonary embolism or pneumothorax. Incorrect Answer Explanations Most patients with a HEART score of ≤3 do not need to be admitted for further test- ing (eg, noninvasive cardiac testing) to rule out ACS. Patients with a HEART score of ≤3 after two sets of negative troponins can be safely discharged and do not require admission for further evaluation. Not all patients presenting with a history of chest pain need to be admitted, and it is no longer required to admit all patients with a history of chest pain for cardiac test- ing. The addition of the HEART score has helped decrease some of these admis- sions. Multiple studies have shown that low-risk HEART score patients can be safely discharged. Also, there are many causes of chest pain that are not cardiac in nature, some of which do not require hospital admission. Patients with a moderate-risk HEART score (4-6) are at higher risk for adverse car- diac events, and many of these patients should be admitted. If there is clinical con- cern for ACS, a moderate-risk HEART score confers a risk of MACE of >12%. Thus, these patients should be admitted for further cardiac testing. If the patient's troponin is significantly elevated, cardiology should be consulted.

Review notes: ["html_markup_or_entities"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن مريض الـ HEART score بين 0 و3 مع troponins سالبين مرتين (بينفصلوا 3 ساعات، وبال6 ساعات من بداية الأعراض) عنده احتمال أقل من 0.4% للـ MACE، يعني يقدر يطلع بأمان. الـ HEART pathway ضمّن الـ score مع إعادة الـ troponin بعد 3 ساعات، وبيبيّن أكثر من 99% sensitivity، وفي RCT ما صار عند حدا adverse cardiac event خلال 30 يوم. لازم نراجع أسباب ثانية للألم مثل pulmonary embolism.
الفخ: بنخلّي الطالب يدخّل كل مريض بـ HEART ≤3 عشان غير invasive cardiac testing، وهاد غلط لأن أغلبهم مش محتاجين دخول. وكمان الـ HEART 4 إلى 6 مع troponin أول سالب ما بنصرفه على طول.

question: What is an absolute contraindication to beta blocker administration within 24 hours of an acute STEMI?
englishExplanation: Absolute contraindications to beta-blockers include hemodynamic in- stability, cardiogenic shock, acute bronchospasm, severe bradycardia, heart block greater than first degree, and overt heart failure. This patient is hemodynamically unstable; in this setting, beta-blockers should be avoided be- cause they may further reduce blood pressure. In hemodynamically stable patients, beta-blockers decrease myocardial oxy- gen demand by reducing heart rate, blood pressure, ventricular fibrilla- tion, and myocardial contractility. They also improve coronary diastolic perfu- sion by decreasing automaticity and slowing conduction, which causes modest bradycardia and prolongs diastole. The American Heart Association has placed a class A recommendation for oral beta-blockers within a 24-hr window of acute myocardial infarction (MI) if no contraindications are present. In patients with additional signs of heart failure, oral beta-blockers should be initiated after stabilization; intravenous beta-blockers have shown no benefit in ACS management. Incorrect Answer Explanations A patient with COPD without wheezing should be given oral beta-blockers within 24 hours. Acute bronchospasm is considered a contraindication for beta- blocker therapy, but this patient has clear lungs and should be given treatment. Patients with first-degree heart block should be given oral beta-blockers within 24 hours if their ejection fraction is preserved and vital signs are stable. Second- and third-degree heart blocks are considered contraindications to therapy, but treatment with oral beta-blockers is considered safe in first-degree blocks. Patients with stable vital signs should be given oral beta-blockers within 24 hours of an acute STEMI. Absolute contraindications to beta-blockers include hemodynamic instability, cardiogenic shock, acute bronchospasm, se- vere bradycardia, heart block greater than first degree, and overt heart failure.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن contraindications مطلقة للـ beta-blockers تشمل hemodynamic instability وcardiogenic shock وacute bronchospasm وsevere bradycardia وheart block أكبر من first degree وovert heart failure. هاد المريض hemodynamically unstable، فالمشكلة إنه الـ beta-blocker ممكن يخفّض الـ blood pressure أكثر. بينما في الـ stable patients فالـ beta-blockers بتقلّل الـ myocardial oxygen demand وبتحسّن الـ coronary diastolic perfusion.
الفخ: بنخلّي الطالب يستثني COPD بدون wheezing، بس الـ acute bronchospasm هو اللي مانع مش COPD نفسه. والـ first-degree heart block ما يمنع الـ oral beta-blocker خلال 24 ساعة، والـ stable vital signs معناها تقدر تعطي العلاج.

question: A 50-year-old man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes presents with chest pain. An ECG is obtained and is shown below. Which coro- nary artery is the cause of this patient's symptoms? Credit: David Yamane, MD.
englishExplanation:
This patient is having an inferior STEMI, as seen in the ECG with ST eleva- tions in leads II, III, and aVF; this is characteristic of a right coronary artery (RCA) occlusion. Another indicator is that this patient is in a junctional rhythm, indicating atrioventricular (AV) nodal dysfunction. The AV node is sup- plied by the RCA. Other possible complications of inferior wall STEMI include right ventricular infarction and hypotension. Incorrect Answer Explanations This ECG demonstrates inferior wall ischemia, which is inconsistent with circumflex artery occlusion. Occlusions of the circumflex artery will typically cause a lateral STEMI with elevations of leads V5 through V6, I, and aVL. These can also present with reciprocal changes of the inferior leads (II, III, and aVF). This ECG demonstrates inferior wall ischemia, which is inconsistent with left ante- rior descending (LAD) coronary artery occlusion. Occlusion of the LAD causes an anterior wall STEMI. ST elevation is seen in the precordial leads (V1 through V4) with reciprocal changes in the inferior leads (II, III, and aVF). This ECG demonstrates inferior wall ischemia, which is inconsistent with a left main coronary artery occlusion. The left main coronary artery gives rise to both the LAD artery and the circumflex artery. A left main coronary artery occlusion can present with both anterior and lateral STEMI, which cause eleva- tions in the anterior leads (V1 through V4) and the lateral leads (V5 through V6, I, and aVL).

Review notes: ["visual_reference_no_image_attached_in_jsonl"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن هالمريض عنده inferior STEMI، واضح من الـ ST elevations في الـ leads II وIII وaVF، وهاد characteristic ومتعارف عليه لـ right coronary artery occlusion. وكمان هو على junctional rhythm، وده بيدل على خلل بوظيفة الـ AV node، والـ AV node بتغذيه الـ RCA. من complications الـ inferior STEMI كمان right ventricular infarction وhypotension.
الفخ: Circumflex occlusion بتدي lateral STEMI مع ارتفاعات في V5-V6 وI وaVL، والـ LAD بتدي anterior STEMI مع ارتفاعات في V1-V4. أما Left main coronary artery فبتدي anterior وlateral مع بعض، وكلها بتخالف ECG هاد اللي عنده inferior.

question: Which biomarker is the most specific for an acute myocardial infarction?
englishExplanation: Cardiac troponin is both sensitive and specific for myocardial injury, commonly caused by ischemia. An acute myocardial infarction (MI) is the clinical consequence of myocardial injury from cardiac ischemia. Ischemic injury to cardiac myocytes causes the breakdown of myocyte membranes and the subsequent release of intracellular contents, including troponin, into the bloodstream. Because serum troponin does not begin to rise until 2 to 3 hours postinfarction, multiple measurements may be necessary to determine the presence of an acute MI. The di- agnosis of an acute MI requires both biochemical evidence of myocardial injury and clinical symptoms (ie, chest pain). Biochemically, an acute MI is defined as a tro- ponin level above the 99th percentile of the upper reference limit. Incorrect Answer Explanations CK and CK-MB were the most commonly used diagnostic biomarker tests prior to the use of troponin. However, CK and CK-MB are less specific and sensitive than troponin for the detection of myocardial injury. CK is an isoenzyme present in many muscle tissues, including skeletal muscle. Muscle breakdown can lead to increases in serum CK, making it less specific than other biochemical mark- ers of ischemia. The diagnosis of an acute MI requires a two-fold increase in the concentration of CK. However, older individuals with lower muscle mass may not reach the required rise in total CK, making it less sensitive as well. Although CK-MB is more specific than CK for myocardial injury, it is less specific than troponin. The CK-MB fraction is a combination of the dimers of M and B chains of the CK isoenzyme. CK-MB has a high concentration in heart muscle, making it more specific than overall CK. However, CK-MB can be ele- vated in chronic skeletal muscle injury, such as in dermatomyositis or polymyositis, lowering its specificity for the detection of an acute MI. Highly sensitive troponin, as its name suggests, has higher sensitivity but lower specificity than standard troponin testing. The highly sensitive troponin tests were first approved in the United States in 2017. They have improved early detection of cardiac ischemia and increased the negative predictive value for acute MI. However, the 99% percentile criteria of the upper reference limit for highly sensitive troponins may vary with age, renal function, and sex of the patient, making the optimal cutoff for this test unclear.
arabicExplanation:

question: A 40-year-old man with a history of hypertension and tobacco use presents with substernal nonexertional sharp chest pain without radiation. He has no family history of cardiac disease. His troponin is negative at 0 hours and 3 hours. An ECG is obtained and shown below. According to the HEART pathway, what is the next best course of action? Credit: Mattu A, Tabas JA, Brady WJ, eds. Electrocardiography in Emergency, Acute, and Critical Care. 2nd ed. American College of Emergency Physicians; 2019.
englishExplanation:
This patient qualifies for an early discharge with outpatient follow-up. The original HEART (History, ECG, Age, Risk factors, and Troponin) score is a five-ques- tion scoring system, with each question scoring 0,1, or 2 points. This patient scores 0 points for history, 0 points for ECG, 0 points for age, 1 point for risk factors, and 0 points for troponin. With negative troponins at 0 hours and 3 hours, his risk of an adverse cardiac event is low, and he qualifies under the HEART pathway for early discharge. The risk factors included in the HEART score are hypertension, hyperc- holesterolemia, diabetes, obesity, smoking, family history, and atherosclerotic disease. In the original derivation study, a score of 0 to 3 (low risk) was associated with a 2.5% chance of acute myocardial infarction, percuta- neous coronary intervention, coronary artery bypass graft, or death; based on this, discharge of low-risk patients was supported. A score of 4 to 6 points had a 20.3% risk of adverse cardiac events, and a score of 7 or greater had a risk of 72.7%. The HEART score was subsequently validated in several other studies. The HEART pathway combined the HEART score of 0 to 3 (low risk) and a negative troponin at 0 hours and 3 hours to identify low risk patients who were suitable for early discharge. This study found a decrease in length of stay by 12 hours, decreased cardiac testing by 12%, and increased early discharges by 21%. There were no major adverse cardiac events seen within 30 days in those patients identified for early discharge. HEART score calculation. Credit: Infographic: Yanina Purim-Shem-Tov, MD, FACEP; illustration: peterschreiber.media/iStock/Getty Images Plus. Incorrect Answer Explanations Based on the HEART score of 1 and negative troponin tests, this patient has a low probability of an adverse cardiac event within the next 30 days, so hospitalization for coronary angiography is unwarranted. Given this patient's history, ECG, and troponin, his risk for an adverse cardiac event is no more than 2.5%. Since this patient is low risk per the HEART pathway, he does not require admis- sion for stress testing. A select group of low-risk patients with chest pain can be safely discharged early with a reduction in objective cardiac test- ing. This patient's HEART score of 1 and negative troponin testing places him in this low-risk group. The HEART pathway in low-risk patients recommends discharge without further objective testing. Coronary CT evaluates the presence and extent of coronary artery disease using contrast as a means of angiography. This technique has a high accu- racy for detecting obstructive coronary artery disease (>50% luminal narrowing) with high sensitivity and a low rate of false negatives.

الفخ: بنخلّي الطالب يدخّل للمريض للـ coronary angiography أو stress testing أو coronary CT مع إن الـ HEART score منخفض والـ troponins سالبين. الـ score 0-3 بيتم في خطر 2.5%، و4-6 خطر 20.3%، و7+ خطر 72.7%.

question: A patient presents with severe chest pain. An ECG shows a left bundle-branch block. Which ECG criteria would be concerning for an acute myocardial infarc- tion when applying the modified Sgarbossa criteria?

options.text: Concordant ST depression of ≥1 mm in lead III
Discordant ST depression in leads V2 and V3
Discordant ST elevation of ≥1 mm that is 10% the amplitude of the preceding S wave
Discordant ST elevation of ≥1 mm that is 30% the amplitude of the preceding S wave

correctAnswer: Discordant ST elevation of ≥1 mm that is 30% the amplitude of the preceding S wave
englishExplanation: The Sgarbossa criteria were initially designed to assist in identifying pa- tients having an acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in the setting of a left bundle-branch block (LBBB). The original criteria were specific for AMI but were not sensitive. Those original criteria were concordant ST elevation >1 mm in leads with a positive QRS, concordant ST depression in leads V1 to V3, and exces- sively discordant ST elevation of >5 mm in leads with a negative QRS. The criteria were further adjusted into the Smith-Modified Sgarbossa criteria to improve sensi- tivity of the criteria. The modified Sgarbossa criteria are: Concordant ST elevation of ≥1 mm in any lead with a positive QRS complex Concordant ST depression ≥1 mm in leads V1 to V3 Discordant ST elevation of ≥1 mm in any lead with the ST elevation being at least 25% of the amplitude of the preceding S wave (ST:S ratio of ≥0.25) Meeting any of the modified criteria is considered positive and should be considered concerning for an AMI in the appropriate setting. The third modified criterion has a sensitivity reported of 91% compared to the previous defi- nition in the original Sgarbossa criteria that had a sensitivity of 50% to 60%. Incorrect Answer Explanations Concordant ST depression is a criterion in the modified Sgarbossa criteria. However, this is only applicable to leads V1 to V3, not to lead III. Discordant ST depression does not factor into the modified Sgarbossa criteria. The only ST depression criterion in the modified set of criteria is ST depression ≥1 mm in leads V1 to V3. Discordant ST elevation of ≥1 mm that is 10% the amplitude of the preceding S wave does not meet the threshold of at least 25%. The third criteria of the modi- fied Sgarbossa criteria requires the ST elevation be at least 25% of the amplitude of the preceding S wave.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إن الـ Sgarbossa criteria صُمّمت عشان نكتشف الـ acute MI عند مريض عنده left bundle-branch block، والنسخة الأصلية كانت specific بس مو sensitive. عدّلوها وطلعوا Smith-Modified Sgarbossa criteria: concordant ST elevation ≥1 mm في أي lead بـ positive QRS، أو concordant ST depression ≥1 mm في الـ leads V1 إلى V3، أو discordant ST elevation ≥1 mm مع ST:S ratio ≥0.25. الـ criterion الثالث حساسيته 91%.
الفخ: الـ concordant ST depression بتعدي بس لازم تكون في V1 إلى V3 مو في lead III. والـ discordant ST elevation لازم يكون 25% من amplitude الـ S wave، فالـ 10% مش بيكفي، والـ discordant ST depression أصلاً مو criterion.

question: A 56-year-old man presents with severe chest pain of 6 hours' duration. His vital signs include BP 68/38 and SpO 92%. An ECG is obtained and shown below. Transfer to another hospital where cardiac catheterization is available has a door-to-balloon time of 90 minutes. Concurrent with blood pressure stabiliza- tion, which intervention is the best next step? Credit: Heather Rozzi, MD, FACEP.

options.text: Coronary artery bypass grafting as soon as possible
Fibrinolytic therapy now with admission to the ICU
Fibrinolytic therapy with immediate transfer for percutaneous coronary intervention
Immediate transfer for primary percutaneous coronary intervention

correctAnswer: Immediate transfer for primary percutaneous coronary intervention
englishExplanation:
Patients with STEMI and cardiogenic shock or severe heart failure initially seen at hospitals without percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) capabilities should be transferred for cardiac catheterization and revascularization as soon as possible, regardless of time delay from STEMI onset. This patient is hy- potensive, thus in cardiogenic shock. His ECG shows significant anterolateral ST- segment elevation and inferior reciprocal change. Transfer for PCI can be achieved in less than 120 minutes, so he should be transferred immedi- ately without fibrinolytics. Immediate transfer to a PCI center is also recommended for patients without shock if the symptoms have been present for less than 12 hours and the first physician contact-to-balloon time is expected to be less than 120 minutes. Generally, transfer for primary PCI (the preferred strategy in STEMI) is indicated in STEMI patients but is related to the total STEMI duration. Early in STEMI, the recommended time to reperfusion therapy is quite short — if the dura- tion of the STEMI is less than 2 hours, PCI should be initiated in 60 min- utes or less, and if the duration of the STEMI is 2 to 3 hours, PCI should be initi- ated within 120 minutes. Later in the STEMI time course, longer time periods are allowed: after 3 hours of STEMI, PCI should be initiated within 120 minutes. Incorrect Answer Explanations Emergency coronary artery bypass grafting within 6 hours of symptom onset may be considered in patients with STEMI who do not have car- diogenic shock and are not candidates for PCI or fibrinolytic therapy. This pa- tient is demonstrating signs of cardiogenic shock and can be transferred for PCI within 120 minutes, so he should be transferred for primary PCI. Because this patient in cardiogenic shock can undergo PCI within 120 minutes, fibrinolytic therapy is not indicated. In the absence of contraindi- cations, fibrinolytic therapy should be started for patients with STEMI and onset of ischemic symptoms within the previous 12 hours when it is anticipated that primary PCI cannot be performed within 120 minutes. In the absence of contraindica- tions (eg, prior intracranial hemorrhage, known malignant intracranial neoplasm, or suspected aortic dissection) and when PCI is unavailable, fib- rinolytic therapy is reasonable for patients with STEMI if there is clinical or ECG evidence of ongoing ischemia within 12 to 24 hours of symptom onset and a large area of myocardium at risk or hemodynamic instability. Multiple studies have investigated the role of facilitated PCI (full-dose or par- tial-dose fibrinolysis followed by immediate transfer to a PCI-capable facility for PCI) in the management of STEMI. Generally, this reperfusion strategy has failed to show a benefit when giving full-dose or partial-dose fib- rinolytic agents with planned PCI within 90 to 120 minutes as compared to PCI alone, so it is not recommended.

question: An otherwise healthy 37-year-old woman presents 4 days after a vaginal birth with chest pain that has been present for 3 hours. She describes sudden-onset, pressure-like chest pain radiating to the left arm, which has been associated with dyspnea, nausea, and vomiting since it began. She is diaphoretic and is clutching her chest. Her cardiopulmonary and vascular examination findings are unre- markable. Her ECG is shown below. What is the most likely diagnosis? Credit: copyright ACEP.
englishExplanation:
This patient presents with signs and symptoms concerning for spontaneous coro- nary artery dissection (SCAD). SCAD is a form of ACS caused by an acute, atraumatic local dissection resulting in the obstruction of a coronary artery by formation of a false lumen and intramural hematoma. Consequently, SCAD generally presents like other forms of ACS, with anginal chest pain, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, and diaphoresis, among other find- ings. As with other forms of ACS, more severe manifestations can occur, such as ventricular arrhythmias and cardiogenic shock. SCAD is the most common cause of myocardial infarction in pregnant patients and especially in recently postpartum patients (>70%). SCAD is also a major cause of myocardial infarction in women with limited risk factors for atherosclerotic heart disease; SCAD is thought to be responsible for up to 35% of all ACS in women aged 50 years or younger. The left anterior descending artery is most commonly involved. However, SCAD can involve any coronary artery. Major risk factors for SCAD include fibromuscular dysplasia, advanced pregnancy and the recently postpartum period, connective tissue dis- eases, and systemic inflammatory diseases. There is concern for exogenous hormone use as a risk factor as well. Potentially triggering events have been re- ported in a large percentage of cases, such as significant physical exertion (eg, exer- cise or labor, as in this case), cocaine use, or emotional stress. Initial evaluation and management of SCAD is the same as for any patient who presents with symptoms consistent with an ACS. The ECG and troponin level are likely to be abnormal. ECG commonly demonstrates an STEMI, as in this case. Coronary angiography is the diagnostic test of choice, so the diagnosis in most cases is uncertain in the emergency department. Thus, initiation of standard treatments for ACS in the emergency department — such as anticoagulation, an- tiplatelet agents, and antianginals — is reasonable. If the SCAD diagnosis is known (eg, because of positive CT coronary angiography results), anticoagulation may be held because of the theoretical risk of enlarging the intramural hematoma. Early cardiology consultation is strongly recommended. Incorrect Answer Explanations Esophageal rupture is classically associated with heavy retching or vom- iting (Boerhaave syndrome). It presents with acute-onset midsternal chest pain and dysphagia. A chest x-ray will show free mediastinal air, and the diagno- sis is generally made with a contrast esophagogram using water-soluble contrast. Although this patient is vomiting, her symptoms are more consistent with angina than other forms of chest pain. Thus, she is less likely to be experiencing an esophageal rupture than an ACS. Given her risk factors, SCAD is the most likely diagnosis. Perimyocarditis is a potentially life-threatening inflammatory condition involving the pericardium and myocardium. It has a wide variety of in- fectious and noninfectious causes and can result in severely reduced cardiac function. Classically, patients with perimyocarditis present with chest pain, dysp- nea, and fatigue after a preceding viral illness. The ECG can show concave ST el- evations that may mimic the ST elevations from an STEMI but do not involve the coronary arteries. Troponin measurements may be elevated as well. This patient presents with acute-onset, anginal chest pain with no viral symptoms or preceding medical history other than recent delivery, making SCAD a more likely diagnosis than perimyocarditis. Patients in the later stages of pregnancy are at higher risk of pulmonary em- bolism, which should be considered in this setting. However, this patient presents with classic, acute-onset anginal symptoms: pressure-like chest pain radiating to the left arm, diaphoresis, nausea, vomiting, and ST elevations on ECG. Pulmonary embolism is expected to cause pleuritic chest pain and tachycardia rather than these symptoms. Thus, she is less likely to be experiencing a pulmonary em- bolism than an ACS such as SCAD. Given her risk factors, SCAD is the most likely diagnosis.

question: Which finding is most suggestive of myocarditis?
englishExplanation: Myocarditis is an inflammatory condition that causes myocardial dam- age, usually as a result of infectious, immunologic, or toxin-mediated conditions. It can manifest as mild constitutional symptoms, moderate cardiopul- monary symptoms, or fulminant cardiopulmonary decompensation leading to death. The notable physical examination findings are low-grade fever, tachypnea, and tachycardia. Classically, the tachycardia is out of pro- portion to the fever. In most adult cases, the myocardial damage is thought to be autoimmune and triggered by a virus (most commonly Coxsackievirus) or other in- fections. In neonates and infants, injury to myocytes is believed to occur more often because of direct injury by the pathogen itself. The clinical manifestations of myocarditis usually begin days to weeks after the acute infection, especially when viruses are implicated as the cause. Only 50% of pa- tients report a recent upper respiratory or GI viral type of infection. The initial symptoms are nonspecific and constitutional, such as low fever, fatigue, malaise, myalgia, and arthralgia. These mild symptoms are often the reason for initial misdiagnosis or delays in proper diagnosis of this condition. Cardiopulmonary symptoms such as chest pain and dyspnea are also commonly seen. The most common abnormalities on ECG are sinus tachycardia and nonspecific ST-segment or T-wave changes. Chest x-rays may reveal signs of congestive heart failure (cardiomegaly, pulmonary vascular re- distribution, interstitial edema, frank pulmonary edema). Close attention should be paid to the ABCs of resuscitation because patients with fulminant myocarditis can decompensate rapidly. The mainstay of treatment of myocarditis is primarily supportive with a focus on hemodynamic sup- port and management of complications. Incorrect Answer Explanations A low-grade fever can be seen in patients who develop myocarditis, but it is not the most suggestive or classic finding of the disease. Fever with night sweats is characteristic of tuberculosis. In fact, only 50% of patients report a recent vi- ral-type upper respiratory or GI infection. Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea is a symptom seen in patients with de- compensating heart failure; they wake from sleep to sit upright due to sudden increasing shortness of breath. Although patients with myocarditis can have parox- ysmal nocturnal dyspnea with heart failure, it is not the most suggestive symptom of myocarditis. Pleuritic chest pain is a common symptom of acute pericarditis but is less commonly associated with myocarditis. The progression of myocarditis involves necrosis of the myocardial cells with inflammatory cells leading to fibrosis. This does not lead to the irritation or pleuritic pain associated with pericarditis.

question: A patient with a history of lung cancer presents with dyspnea and lightheaded- ness. Their vital signs are notable for BP 88/52 and P 127. A large pericardial ef- fusion and right ventricular end-diastolic collapse are noted on bedside ultra- sound. While arranging for definitive management, what is the most appropriate intervention?
englishExplanation: This patient is presenting with an atraumatic pericardial tamponade, likely due to malignancy. While awaiting definitive management (ie, decompression of the peri- cardial effusion with pericardiocentesis [bedside or otherwise]), intravenous flu- ids should be administered. Cardiac preload is reduced in the setting of in- creased pericardial pressure; intravenous fluids increase cardiac preload and re- verse this process temporarily, but definitive treatment is still required. Most re- sources advocate a small bolus (generally 500 mL) in euvolemic patients to achieve adequate preload augmentation without triggering additional complica- tions, such as pulmonary edema and worsening hemodynamic instability. Characteristic findings of pericardial tamponade include hypotension, tachycar- dia, jugular venous distention, pulsus paradoxus (ie, systolic BP de- crease >10 mm Hg with inspiration), and electrical alternans on ECG. Along with the culprit pericardial effusion, echocardiogram may reveal systolic right atrial or diastolic right ventricular collapse as well as plethoric IVC. Incorrect Answer Explanations Bedside thoracotomy in the setting of pericardial tamponade is indi- cated only following cardiac arrest from penetrating chest trauma. Even if this patient were in cardiac arrest, bedside thoracotomy is not indicated; rather, an emergent bedside pericardiocentesis should be performed. In this scenario, in- travenous fluids are the most appropriate pending definitive decompression with pericardiocentesis. Diuretics can be used in certain circumstances to reduce the size of a small pericar- dial effusion without tamponade physiology. However, in the setting of pericardial tamponade, diuretics would be counterproductive since they reduce preload and can precipitate or worsen hemodynamic instability. Thus, intravenous fluids are more appropriate pending definitive decompression with pericardiocentesis. Although vasopressors may improve blood pressure and stimulate inotropy, they do not directly address the physiology underlying pericardial tamponade–induced ob- structive shock. The impact of reduced preload on cardiac output can only be addressed with increasing preload via volume resuscitation; no amount of vasopressor use will address the fall in stroke volume. Thus, intravenous fluids are the most appropriate intervention pending definitive decompression with pericardiocentesis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده cardiac tamponade من غير رض، وغالباً بسبب سرطان، وهاد مع hypotension و tachycardia و ضيق نفس. لأن الضغط داخل الـ pericardium زايد، الـ cardiac preload قلّ، فالدم ما بيلحق يملأ القلب. Intravenous fluids بتزود الـ preload وبتعكس هالشي مؤقتاً لحد ما ينعمل decompression بـ pericardiocentesis. أكتر المراجع بتنصح بـ bolus صغير حوالي 500 mL لمريض متوازن السوائل عشان ما نسبب pulmonary edema ولا instability زيادة.
الفخ: Bedside thoracotomy بتنعمل بس بعد cardiac arrest من رض chest penetrating، وهالمريض مش هيك. حتى لو وصل arrest، الحل الصحيح هو pericardiocentesis طارئة مو thoracotomy.

question: A 47-year-old man presents with chest pain and dyspnea that started while he was lying on the couch. An ECG is obtained and shown below. What is the appro- priate management? Credit: Bon MC, Alblaihed L. In: Mattu A, Tabas J, Brady W, eds. Electrocardiography in Emergency, Acute, and Critical Care. 2nd ed. American College of Emergency Physicians; 2019. Reproduced with permission from Amal Mattu, MD, FACEP.
englishExplanation:
Pericarditis is inflammation within the pericardial space involving the pericardial surfaces that generally presents with sharp pleuritic chest pain. The mainstay of treatment is NSAIDs. The pain classically is pleuritic, radiates to the back, and tends to improve when the patient is sitting up. The diagnosis in this case is supported by the ECG findings of normal sinus rhythm, diffuse ST-seg- ment elevation, and diffuse PR segment depression. Leads I and aVR can show reciprocal ST-segment depression in acute pericarditis. Uncomplicated cases of pericarditis can be treated with NSAIDs in the outpatient setting. Glucocorticoids were previously recommended but should only be used if the patient cannot tolerate NSAIDs because they can increase the risk of recurrence. Colchicine can be used as an adjunct to NSAIDS or glucocorticoids, but it should be avoided if bacterial pericarditis is suspected. Pericarditis is often idiopathic or related to a viral infection, but it can be caused by various underlying disease states. There is often a prodromal period of low- grade fever, malaise, or flu-like symptoms. On examination, a pericardial friction rub can sometimes be appreciated. A bedside echocardiogram can be ob- tained to evaluate for an associated pericardial effusion. Patients with large effu- sions or pericardial tamponade benefit from inpatient evaluation and management. Incorrect Answer Explanations Although they were previously commonly recommended for the treatment of peri- carditis, glucocorticoids have been shown to be associated with recur- rence of pericarditis and should generally be avoided. Glucocorticoids should only be considered in rare cases in which the patient cannot tolerate NSAIDs. This presentation is most consistent with acute pericarditis because of the diffuse ST changes seen in essentially all leads. This is not a typical pattern indicating cardiac ischemia, which might have ST changes in contiguous leads consistent with specific cardiac vessels (inferior ischemia seen in leads II, III, and aVF). Thus, ni- trates would likely be of no benefit to this patient. Heparin is indicated in suspected pulmonary embolism or in certain ACS presenta- tions. Although pulmonary embolI can cause ECG changes, most commonly tachy- cardia and classically S1Q3T3, they are not expected to cause diffuse ST-segment el- evation, as is seen on this patient's ECG. Heparin should not be given to pa- tients with pericarditis. Pericarditis is often associated with pericardial effu- sion, which may be worsened by heparin.

Review notes: ["visual_reference_no_image_attached_in_jsonl"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريض عنده pericarditis، والالتهاب بيسبب ألم صدر sharp و pleuritic و بيحسن لما يجلس. الـ ECG بتظهر normal sinus rhythm مع diffuse ST-segment elevation و PR segment depression، وهاد يدعم التشخيص. العلاج الأساسي هو NSAIDs، والحالات البسيطة من غير مضاعفات ممكن تُعالج بالـ outpatient. Glucocorticoids كانت بينصح فيها بس لازم تنحصر في اللي ما بيقدر يتحمل NSAIDs لأنها بتزيد خطر رجوع الالتهاب.
الفخ: كتير من طلبة الطب بيختاروا glucocorticoids لأنهم بيسمّوها inflammation. الفرق إن الـ steroids بتزيد فرصة رجوع الـ pericarditis، ومكانها هي NSAIDs.

question: What is a criterion for hospital admission in a young, otherwise healthy person with newly diagnosed pericarditis?
englishExplanation: Patients with acute pericarditis (inflammation of the pericardium) present with sharp, pleuritic, retrosternal chest pain that radiates to the trapezius ridges and changes with body position (worse when lying down). The physical examination might reveal a pericardial friction rub. It can be an isolated condition or it can suggest underlying disease. Hospital admission is warranted for patients who also present with fever in order to actively investigate the etiology of the pericarditis and to closely monitor the patient's condi- tion. The hallmark of the early stage of disease is diffuse ST-segment elevation noted on an ECG; PR-segment depression can also occur but is not specific for pericarditis. The etiologies of pericarditis are vast and include infection (viral, bac- terial, fungal, parasitic), malignancy, medications, renal disease, connective tissue disease, myocardial infarction, trauma, and surgery. Reasonable indications for ad- mission include, again, fever or suspicion of a bacterial cause, as well as immuno- suppression, associated trauma, elevated biomarkers (myopericarditis), and hemo- dynamic instability. An effusion larger than 2 cm warrants admission to the hospital due to the risk of additional increase in size and the potential for cardiac tampon- ade. A history of active anticoagulant use is generally considered a poor prognostic factor and warrants hospital admission as well. In most patients, outpatient man- agement is appropriate, and symptoms resolve in days to weeks. Incorrect Answer Explanations Acute onset is not a criterion for admission. Most patients with pericarditis present in the acute stage of symptoms. Subacute course is an indication for admis- sion, not acute onset. Elevation of CRP, along with other inflammatory markers, is one of the diagnostic markers for pericarditis, but it does not predict increased severity of the dis- ease. An elevated WBC count can also be used to track the course of the disease. Any hemodynamic instability or hypotension — not hypertension — indicates the need for admission. Tachycardia out of proportion to pain or fever indicates my- ocarditis or myopericarditis.

ليش:شاب صحتو كويسة ومتشخّص عنده pericarditis حديثاً، لازم يتوظف لو معه fever. لأن وجود الحرارة يعني لازم نبيّن السبب الحقيقي للالتهاب، خاصة لو اشتباه بـ bacterial cause، ونتابع حالته عن قرب. indications تانية معقولة للدخول هي immunosuppression، أو رض مرافق، أو ارتفاع biomarkers اللي بتوحي بـ myopericarditis، أو عدم استقرار hemodynamically. وكمان effusion أكبر من 2 cm بتستوجب دخول بسبب خطر الـ tamponade.
