question: What is a classic ECG finding associated with pericarditis?
englishExplanation: Pericarditis is a condition whereby the pericardium becomes inflamed for a wide variety of reasons. Pericarditis causes ECG changes, such as PR-interval de- pression with diffuse ST elevations once the pericardial inflammation reaches the epicardium. Classically, the expected ECG changes associated with pericarditis progress through four stages: Stage one occurs within hours to days and is the classic “pericarditis” pattern, with diffuse PR depressions and ST elevations. The ST elevations may be difficult to separate from STEMI. Distinguishing features include small, upsloping ST eleva- tions that are generalized, have a diffuse distribution, do not have additional recip- rocal ST depressions aside from aVR and V1, and lack other ischemic changes (eg, T-wave inversions, Q waves, hyperacute T waves, etc.). Stage two occurs within 1 week and shows that the ST and PR segments have normalized. Stage three has no well-defined time frame, but it occurs after normalization of the ST and PR segments and shows diffuse T-wave inversions. Unlike with is- chemia, T-wave inversions and ST elevations that are associated with pericarditis usually do not exist simultaneously. Stage four also has no well-defined time frame but shows normalization of the ECG. Note that it is unnecessary for patients to progress through all four stages of classic ECG changes, and some may show rapid transition from stage one to stage four in mild cases. Changes like PR depressions and ST elevations may be tran- sient. Also, some patients will not follow this classic pattern and may demonstrate different morphologies. This can complicate the diagnosis of pericarditis, often making it a diagnosis of exclusion once ischemia has been ruled out. Incorrect Answer Explanations Coved ST-segment elevation is associated with Brugada syndrome, which is a congenital abnormality in cardiac sodium channels, not pericarditis. Pericarditis is strongly associated with diffuse PR depression and concave-upward ST elevation. Diffuse ST-segment depressions are associated with diffuse subendocar- dial ischemia or proximal left main coronary artery occlusion. ST eleva- tion in aVR is a common finding in this scenario as well. Pericarditis, however, is strongly associated with diffuse PR depression and ST elevation, with reciprocal ST depression in aVR and V1. Enlarged R wave in aVL is associated with left ventricular hypertrophy, which is most commonly caused by hypertension. Pericarditis, on the other hand, is strongly associated with diffuse PR depression and ST elevation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ pericarditis بيعمل تبدلات بالـ ECG، ومنها PR-interval depression مع diffuse ST elevation لما الالتهاب يوصل للـ epicardium. المرحلة الأولى، خلال ساعات لحد أيام، هي النمط الكلاسيكي، وفيها PR depressions و ST elevations منتشرة. الـ ST elevations ممكن تتشابه بـ STEMI، بس الفرق إنها صغيرة وصاعدة وتوزيعها منتشر، وما في فيها reciprocal drops غير في aVR و V1، وما في T-wave inversions ولا Q waves.
الفخ: coved ST-segment elevation هي نمط STEMI مو pericarditis. و diffuse ST depressions مش العلامة المميزة، لأن hallmark هي ST elevation مع PR depression.

question: What best distinguishes myopericarditis from pericarditis?
englishExplanation: Pericarditis is a condition wherein the pericardium becomes inflamed for a wide variety of reasons; this inflammation can also involve the myocardium, causing myopericarditis (alternatively, perimyocarditis). Unlike pericarditis, myopericarditis is associated with elevated cardiac biomarkers, such as troponin, as well as left ventricular dysfunction noted on echocardiogram. Unclear cases can also be distinguished with cardiac MRI, which will show focal myocardial inflammation. Patients with myopericarditis have a wide range of dis- ease severity; some present similarly to pericarditis — with positional chest pain and ECG changes — and others present as critically ill with florid cardiogenic shock. Due to this risk of severe decompensation, any patient with clinical findings concerning for myopericarditis should be admitted. Incorrect Answer Explanations Although myopericarditis can manifest different ECG findings than peri- carditis, ECG changes do not reliably distinguish pericarditis and my- opericarditis to the extent that cardiac biomarkers do. Pericarditis and myoperi- carditis may show similar ECG changes, but myopericarditis may also show territorial ECG changes that are not typically associated with pericarditis due to localized myocardial inflammation. Unlike pericarditis, myopericarditis is also asso- ciated with arrhythmias. The epicardium is the outermost layer of the visceral heart and is, more specifically, the visceral pericardium. Extension of pericarditis from the pari- etal pericardium to the visceral pericardium/epicardium is what results in the char- acteristic ECG changes associated with pericarditis. Generally, this is a benign process that does not result in severe illness. Only involvement of the my- ocardium results in biomarker elevation and ventricular dysfunction, leading to the diagnosis of the more dangerous myopericarditis. Positional chest pain is a classic finding for both pericarditis and my- opericarditis, so it does not help distinguish them. Patients with isolated my- ocarditis without pericardial inflammation may complain of a different type of chest pain that is constant, not positional, and more akin to ischemic chest pain. However, when the pericardium is involved, positional chest pain is an unreliable differentiator.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الفرق بين myopericarditis و pericarditis إن الالتهاب بيمسّ الـ myocardium كمان، وهاد بيسبب ارتفاع cardiac biomarkers مثل troponin. كمان بيظهر dysfunction بالـ left ventricle على echocardiogram، والحالات الغامضة بتقدر تتحدد بـ cardiac MRI اللي بتوضح inflammation بؤرية بالـ myocardium. لأن شدة المرض بتتفاوت، بعض الحالات بتبان مثل pericarditis العادي وبعضها بتيجي cardiogenic shock، فكل مريض suspected بـ myopericarditis لازم يتوظف.
الفخ: تغيّرات الـ ECG وألم الصدر اللي بيتغيّر مع الوضع موجودين بالاثنين، فما بيفرّقوا لحالهم. الـ biomarkers هي اللي بتفرّق بشكل موثوق.

question: A patient with end-stage renal disease presents with hypotension and altered mental status. The family noted the patient had been complaining of vague chest pain for the past week and has missed dialysis. What bedside echocardiogram finding should prompt emergent intervention?
englishExplanation: This patient is presenting with a pericardial effusion that is presumptively causing cardiac tamponade, which requires emergent pericardiocentesis. Based on the history, this patient likely has preceding uremic pericarditis that resulted in missed hemodialysis sessions and, consequently, worsening uremia, en- cephalopathy, and fluid accumulation. Patients presenting with uremic pericarditis and pericardial effusions without tamponade physiology should undergo urgent hemodialysis; dialysis alone resolves symptoms and pericardial effusions in most cases. Uremic pericarditis causes vague, usually positional chest pain, and it frequently causes pericardial effusions in patients with end-stage kidney disease; upwards of 50% of patients with uremic pericarditis have an associated pericardial effusion. Although any type of pericarditis can cause a pericardial effusion, uremic pericarditis is known for causing large effusions to form, likely due to the accumula- tion of metabolic wastes and fluid. Recurrent pericardial inflammation also results in a thickening of the pericardium, causing a restrictive pericarditis as well. Incorrect Answer Explanations End-point septal separation (EPSS) is a method of estimating left ven- tricular ejection fraction based on the movement of the mitral valve rel- ative to the interventricular septum. An EPSS of less than 5 mm is considered normal, whereas an EPSS greater than 7 mm is considered sensitive for a reduced ejection fraction of less than 50%. Although a mildly reduced ejection fraction war- rants consideration given the patient's hypotension, the presence of a large peri- cardial effusion and hypotension prompts greater concern for pericar- dial tamponade and the need for emergent pericardiocentesis. Pericardial fibrinous stranding is a classic echocardiographic finding associated with uremic pericarditis. These strands form due to chronic peri- cardial inflammation and scarring. The pericardium may also appear thickened. These fibrinous strands alone do not require any specific acute interven- tion, unlike a large effusion in the setting of likely cardiac tamponade. Regional wall-motion abnormalities would certainly be concerning findings in a pa- tient with a week of chest pain symptoms and hypotension. However, in this cir- cumstance, the presence of a large pericardial effusion and hypotension prompts greater concern for pericardial tamponade and the need for emergent pericardiocentesis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريض عنده end-stage renal disease، فاته dialysis، ومن أسبوع عنده ألم صدر غامض. هاي صورة uremic pericarditis اللي سبّبت worsening uremia و accumulation للسوائل و effusion كبيرة. وجود hypotension و altered mental status مع effusion كبيرة يعني cardiac tamponade، وهاد بده emergent pericardiocentesis. و uremic pericarditis معروفة إنها بتعمل effusions كبيرة عند أكثر من 50% من مرضى الـ ESRD. ولو ما في tamponade physiology، الـ hemodialysis لحالها بتحل الأعراض والـ effusion في أغلب الحالات.
الفخ: EPSS هو قياس الـ ejection fraction من حركة الـ mitral valve مقابل الـ septum، وما إلو علاقة بـ effusion. و fibrinous stranding و regional wall-motion abnormalities ما بيوصّلوا لكلام tamponade.

question: What is the first-line medication for managing acute viral pericarditis?
englishExplanation: NSAIDs such as ibuprofen, indomethacin, or aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) are first- line treatments for acute viral or idiopathic pericarditis; other causes, such as uremic pericarditis, are less common but may have their own specific treat- ments. Patients should be treated with full doses (eg, 600-800 mg of ibuprofen three times daily) for 2 to 4 weeks. The addition of colchicine can improve pain control and reduce recurrence rates. Incorrect Answer Explanations Acetaminophen is a reasonable adjunctive pain-control medication for patients with acute idiopathic or viral pericarditis but should not take the place of NSAIDs. NSAIDs and other anti-inflammatories have strong evidence supporting their effectiveness in the management of acute pericarditis. Methyl salicylate (otherwise known as oil of wintergreen) is a type of salicylate that is generally used as a topical pain reliever and, in very small quantities, a flavoring agent. Although aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is indicated for the manage- ment of acute viral or idiopathic pericarditis, methyl salicylate should not be used for this purpose. Steroids like prednisone are considered second-line agents and are only used for patients who are unable to take NSAIDs or whose symptoms are refrac- tory to NSAIDs. This is due to steroids' lower efficacy and side effect profile given duration of treatment (2-4 weeks).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: NSAIDs مثل ibuprofen و indomethacin و aspirin هي أول-line علاج للـ acute viral أو idiopathic pericarditis. لازم تعطى بجرعة كاملة مثل 600-800 mg من ibuprofen ثلاث مرات باليوم لمدة 2 إلى 4 أسابيع. وبنضيف colchicine كـ adjunct عشان نتحكم بالألم وننقّص rates الرجوع. الأدلة على فعالية الـ NSAIDs قوية، بينما الـ steroids أقل فعالية و side effects أعلى مع هالمدة من العلاج.
الفخ: Acetaminophen مسكن مفيد كـ adjunct بس ما بياخد مكان الـ NSAIDs. و methyl salicylate مسكن موضعي، و prednisone ثاني line لللي ما بيقدروا ياخدوا NSAIDs أو symptoms عندهم refractory.

question: A 56-year-old man presents with a severe headache, nausea with vomiting, and confusion. His vital signs include BP 201/135, P 102, and T 37°C (98.6°F); SpO is 99% on room air. A CT scan of the brain reveals bilateral white matter hypo- densities in the occipital and parietal regions consistent with vasogenic edema. What is the most appropriate treatment?

options.text: Hydralazine titrated to a target BP of 140/80
Metoprolol titrated to a target P of 60
Nicardipine titrated to a MAP of 126
Nitroprusside titrated to a diastolic BP less than 100

correctAnswer: Nicardipine titrated to a MAP of 126
englishExplanation: This patient's history, presentation, and CT findings are consistent with hypertensive encephalopathy, which is a true hypertensive emergency. Nicardipine, a peripherally acting calcium channel blocker given intra- venously, has consistent effects on dilating vascular beds and is considered first-line therapy for hypertensive encephalopathy. Therapy goals include lowering the MAP back into a range where cerebral autoregulation can occur. Generally, the MAP should be lowered by 20% in the first hour but by no 2 more than 25% in the first day. This formula can be used to estimate MAP: MAP = Diastolic BP + 1/3(Systolic – Diastolic pressure). Lowering the blood pressure too rapidly can provoke cerebral ischemia in a brain that is accus- tomed to higher blood pressures. These findings on CT, in combination with the hy- pertension, headache and confusion, are consistent with posterior reversible en- cephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Incorrect Answer Explanations Hydralazine is not considered first-line therapy for hypertensive en- cephalopathy. It can unpredictably lower cerebral perfusion pressure, precipitat- ing ischemia in the brain. Metoprolol is a beta-1 selective adrenergic receptor blocker. It primarily affects the heart rate with no vasodilatory properties. Although metoprolol can lower blood pressure, direct-acting vasodilator agents are considered better options. Additionally, therapy for hypertensive encephalopathy does not normally focus on heart rate. Nitroprusside, like hydralazine, can unpredictably lower cerebral perfu- sion pressure and paradoxically elevate intracranial pressure. It can be considered as second-line or third-line therapy but should not be used as a first-line agent.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الصورة هاي hypertensive encephalopathy، يعني hypertensive emergency حقيقية. الـ CT بتبيّن vasogenic edema في occipital و parietal، ومع صداع و ارتباك و BP 201/135 بتوافق PRES. Nicardipine حاصر قنوات الكالسيوم شغال peripherally، وبيوسّع vascular beds بشكل ثابت، وهاد счита first-line therapy. الهدف إنك تنزل الـ MAP 20% بالساعة الأولى بس ما أكثر من 25% خلال اليوم الأول، عشان ما تستفزّ cerebral ischemia. والـ MAP بتحسبه: diastolic BP زائد ثلث الفرق بين الـ systolic والـ diastolic.
الفخ: Hydralazine مو first-line لأنه بيخفّض cerebral perfusion pressure بشكل غير متوقع وممكن يسبب ischemia. و Metoprolol بيأثر على النبض وما إله vasodilating effect.

question: Which drug is safe for patients taking MAOIs?
englishExplanation: Monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors are used in the treatment of some patients with depression but can cause complications, such as serotonin syndrome and hypertensive crises, when taken in conjunction with other medications. Morphine is the only opioid that is safe for patients taking MAO in- hibitors. Patients who take MAO inhibitors are also at risk of developing severe hypertension if they ingest foods that contain large quantities of tyramine (eg, beer, cheese, bananas, processed foods, or soy products). Incorrect Answer Explanations Taking MAO inhibitors with amphetamines can potentiate the effects of amphetamines and cause a hypertensive crisis. Taking amphetamines with MAO inhibitors is contraindicated. When given to a patient taking an MAO inhibitor, meperidine can cause excita- tion, agitation, severe hypertension, and hyperthermia. However, seizures, coma, and even death can also result. A number of other over-the-counter and prescription drugs can cause severe inter- actions in patients taking MAO inhibitors. Tricyclic antidepressants, for instance, stimulate a release of norepinephrine and inhibit reuptake. Patients should be instructed to check with a pharmacist or physician before taking any new medication.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: MAO inhibitors بتستخدم مع بعض مرضى الـ depression، وبتسبب مشاكل مع أدوية تانية مثل serotonin syndrome و hypertensive crises. Morphine هو الـ opioid الوحيد الآمن لللي بياخدوا MAO inhibitors. كمان هالفئة من الناس معرّضة لـ severe hypertension لو أكلوا أطعمة فيها tyramine بكميات كبيرة مثل الجبن والموز والـ beer والأطعمة المصنّعة ومنتجات الصويا.
الفخ: Amphetamines مع MAO inhibitors بتضاعف مفعولاتها وبتعمل hypertensive crisis، فممنوعة. و Meperidine مع MAO inhibitors بتعمل excitation و agitation و severe hypertension و hyperthermia، وبتسبب seizures و coma وحتى موت.

question: A patient with hypertension and severe asthma presents with acute chest pain ra- diating to the back. Their vital signs include BP 210/140 in the right arm, BP 170/100 in the left, and P 110. There is moderate diffuse wheezing. A chest x-ray was performed and is shown below. What is the most appropriate pharmacologic intervention? Credit: Copyright 2024 Dr. Craig Hacking. Image courtesy of Dr. Craig Hacking and Radiopaedia.org, rID: 73356. Used under license.
englishExplanation:
The most appropriate pharmacologic intervention is diltiazem. This patient has a wide mediastinum, and their presentation is concerning for aortic dissection. The first-line impulse-control therapy for aortic dissection is a beta-blocker, such as esmolol or labetalol. However, in patients with a history of asthma, respiratory status must be closely monitored; beta-blockade can worsen asthma. In this case, the shear forces on the aorta must be reduced with intravenous antihypertensives with an alternate agent, targeting a systolic blood pressure of 100 to 120 mm Hg. Remember that the Stanford classification categorizes aortic dissections as either Type A or Type B. Type A can involve the ascending aorta, the arch, and thoracoabdominal aorta. Type B involves the descending thoracic aorta distal to the left subclavian artery without involvement of ascending aorta. The other common classification is the DeBakey system. Incorrect Answer Explanations This patient has findings concerning for an aortic dissection. Although la- betalol would help lower the blood pressure and heart rate, it could worsen the patient's asthma and respiratory status. Thus, an alternative agent, such as a cal- cium-channel blocker, is more appropriate. Nitroglycerin is the first-line therapy for flash pulmonary edema because it is pri- marily a venous dilator. It is only effective on arterial circulation at very high doses. There is no pulmonary edema noted on the x-ray in this case. This patient has findings concerning for an aortic dissection, and an alternative antihy- pertensive agent, such as a calcium-channel blocker, is more appropriate. This patient has findings concerning for an aortic dissection. Phentolamine is an alpha-1 and alpha-2 blocker, and its primary uses are in sympath- omimetic hypertension and hypertension secondary to pheochromocy- toma. It is rarely used in the emergency department and is not a recommended therapy for aortic dissection.

Review notes: ["visual_reference_no_image_attached_in_jsonl"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريض عنده widened mediastinum وألم صدر بينفّز للظهر، وهاد بيحكي عن aortic dissection. أول خط للـ dissection هو beta-blocker مثل esmolol أو labetalol، بس هالمريض عنده severe asthma، والـ beta blockade ممكن يخرب respiratory status. فبدنا نخفّض الـ shear forces على الـ aorta بـ intravenous antihypertensive من نوع تاني، ونستهدف systolic blood pressure بين 100 و 120 mm Hg. والـ Stanford classification بتقسم الـ dissection إلى Type A و Type B حسب الصوامل المصابة.
الفخ: Labetalol بينزّل الضغط والنبض بس ممكن ي加重 الـ asthma، فبنتجنّبه. و Nitroglycerin هو first-line لـ flash pulmonary edema لأنه venodilator، وأثره على الـ arterial circulation ضعيف.

question: A patient in the third trimester of pregnancy presents with headaches and leg swelling. Her vital signs include BP 170/130 and no fever. Her urine dipstick test result is positive for 3+ protein. Which medication is indicated?
englishExplanation: The patient's presentation is concerning for preeclampsia. It is important to rec- ognize preeclampsia, which affects 5% to 7% of all pregnant patients and is respon- sible for more than 70,000 maternal deaths and 500,000 fetal deaths worldwide every year. The presenting symptoms include new-onset hyper- tension and proteinuria during the third trimester, which can progress rapidly to serious complications. The first step is to reduce the systolic blood pressure to <140. There are three first-line medications for this condition: hydralazine IV, labetalol IV, and nifedipine PO. These medications are necessary to reduce blood pressure and en- sure maternal and fetal health. Magnesium is also added for preeclampsia with se- vere features. Incorrect Answer Explanations ACE inhibitors, such as enalapril, are contraindicated in pregnant pa- tients. ACE inhibitors have resulted in fetal malformations including renal failure, bony malformations, and pulmonary hypoplasia. Nitroprusside, in combination with esmolol or a beta-blocker, has historically been used in acute aortic dissection. Nitroprusside is contraindicated in pregnant patients because of potential cyanide toxicity. Valsartan is an angiotensin-receptor blocker and would not be used in the acute set- ting of preeclampsia. Valsartan's use in pregnant patients is also contraindicated be- cause it has been shown to be harmful to the fetus in the second and third trimesters.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة بالشهر التالت من الحمل عندها hypertension جديدة و 3+ protein بالـ dipstick، وهاد preeclampsia. أول خطوة هي ننزّل systolic pressure تحت 140. وفي ثلاثة أدوية first-line وهذي: hydralazine IV، و labetalol IV، و nifedipine PO. هدفها إننا ننزّل الضغط ونحمي الأم والجنين مع بعض. وبحالات preeclampsia مع severe features بنضيف Magnesium كمان للوقاية من التشنجات.
الفخ: Enalapril و Valsartan يعني الـ ACE inhibitors والـ ARBs ممنوعين بالحمل لأنهم بيسببوا تشوهات جنينية. و Nitroprusside ممنوع كمان بالحمل بسبب خطر cyanide toxicity.

question: What is a first-line medication for nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage?
englishExplanation: Nicardipine is an effective treatment for hypertension associated with intracerebral hemorrhage. This drug acts by blocking the influx of calcium into vascular smooth muscle and cardiac cells. The inhibition of calcium flux leads to va- sodilation. It is typically given as an infusion and can be titrated to achieve the de- sired effect. Incorrect Answer Explanations Nitroglycerin is not indicated in intracerebral hemorrhage. It is a first- line therapy in acute pulmonary edema and for anginal chest pain. It can be used in refractory hypertension particularly in those settings. Its mode of action is primarily on the venous system. With regard to the intracerebral vascular system in particular, nitroglycerin causes vasodilation of the basal intracranial arteries. Phentolamine is an alpha-1 and alpha-2 blocker. Its primary use is in sympath- omimetic hypertension and hypertension secondary to pheochromocytoma. Phentolamine is rarely used in the emergency department and is not part of the rec- ommended therapies for intracranial hemorrhage. Verapamil is not indicated. Medications for intracerebral hemorrhage due to hypertension include nicardipine, labetalol, and esmolol. Verapamil is not a first-line therapy for this condition.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: Nicardipine علاج فعّال للـ hypertension المصاحب لـ nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage. بيعمل block لدخول الكالسيوم داخل vascular smooth muscle و cardiac cells، و inhibition الـ calcium flux هذا بيؤدي إلى vasodilation. بينفع يعطى كـ infusion وبيتقدّم عليه بـ titration عشان نوصل للتأثير المطلوب بدون ما ننزّل الضغط فجأة.
الفخ: Nitroglycerin مش indicated بحد ذاته في الـ ICH، لأنه first-line في acute pulmonary edema و angina، وأثره الأساسي على الـ venous side. و Verapamil و Phentolamine مش من علاجات الـ ICH الموصى بها.

question: A patient arrives septic, and native valve infective endocarditis is suspected. Which antibiotic is the most appropriate initial choice for empiric treatment in the emergency department?
englishExplanation: Vancomycin is the most appropriate initial antibiotic choice for the emergency department treatment of suspected infective endocarditis. Definitive therapy should be tailored to blood culture results, and it may be appro- priate to obtain three sets of blood cultures and admit the patient pending results. In a patient who is septic, it is important to start empiric antibiotic therapy, and this should cover Staphylococcal, Streptococcal, and Enterococcal species. These are the most common causative pathogens in all types of infective endocarditis worldwide, and in the United States, Staphylococcus aureus is the most common causative organism. Vancomycin provides excellent antibiotic coverage and is a good initial choice for most patients. It also is the drug of choice for MRSA infections. Use of combination antibiotic therapy with regimens such as vancomycin and gentamicin is generally recommended for endocarditis, but vancomycin is the most appropriate first-line antibiotic for an emergency physician to start while considering the possible etiol- ogy and assistance from infectious disease consultation. Note that native valve en- docarditis and prosthetic valve endocarditis are treated differently depending on the culture results, but initial regimens include vancomycin, gentamicin, and rifampin. Most patients with endocarditis have either predisposing cardiac abnormalities (eg, prosthetic valve, mitral valve prolapse, bicuspid aortic valve, or calcific aortic stenosis) or risk factors for disease (eg, injected drug use, indwelling catheters, poor dental hygiene, or HIV). A history of intravenous drug abuse puts a patient at even higher risk of S. aureus infection (>50% cases). The diagnosis of infective endocarditis can be made using the modified Duke Criteria (sensitivity >90%), which involves the identification of: two major criteria; one major and three minor criteria; or five minor criteria. Incorrect Answer Explanations Cefepime is a cephalosporin commonly used in the treatment of pneu- monia, febrile neutropenia, UTIs, skin infections, and as an adjunct in the treatment of intraabdominal infections. It covers S. aureus infection, but studies indicate that its potential effectiveness against a MRSA infection lies in com- bination with another antimicrobial. For that reason, it is not a good solo empiric choice for endocarditis, and certainly not a better choice than vancomycin. Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside and often a first-line choice against in- fections with gram-negative organisms such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Proteus, Escherichia coli, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Serratia, and Citrobacter, as well as gram-positive staphylococcal infections. Like moxifloxacin, gentamicin does not provide adequate antistaphylococcal coverage for suspected in- fective endocarditis. Gentamicin is part of the treatment regimen for some types of infective native valve endocarditis but in combination with another antibiotic, such as penicillin, nafcillin, or vancomycin. In recent years, MRSA infection has become resistant to gentamicin. Moxifloxacin is a fluoroquinolone that has good coverage for strepto- coccal species and variable susceptibility with MRSA, but it does not provide adequate antistaphylococcal coverage for suspected infective endo- carditis. It is typically used in the treatment of community-acquired pneumonia, as well as skin infections, some abdominal infections, and bacterial bronchitis and sinusitis. Key Points Vancomycin is the most appropriate initial empiric antibiotic choice for suspected infective endocarditis. The most common pathogen causing infective endocarditis in the US is Staphylococcus aureus. Infective endocarditis is most commonly associated with either predisposing cardiac abnormalities or risk factors of disease, such as intravenous drug abuse, HIV, in- dwelling catheters, and poor dental hygiene. The Duke Criteria have a sensitivity higher than 90% for the diagnosis of infective endocarditis.

Vancomycin يعطي تغطية ممتازة وهو drug of choice لإحدوى MRSA. وبالنهاية العلاج لازم يتعدّل حسب نتائج الـ blood cultures، فلا بد من أخذ ثلاث sets منها.
الفخ: Gentamicin لحاله مش الخيار الأول للـ ED لأنه ما بيغطي Staph aureus بنفس الدرجة. و recommendation فعلاً هي استعمال combinaciones زي vancomycin مع gentamicin، بس أول دوا تبدأ فيه هو vancomycin.

question: In which population should antibiotic prophylaxis for endocarditis be recom- mended before a dental procedure?
englishExplanation: Prophylaxis is recommended in these populations: Patients with prosthetic valves; Patients with a history of endocarditis; Patients with valvular disease and a transplanted heart; and Patients with unrepaired congenital heart disease or repaired congenital heart dis- ease with residual defect or prosthesis. High-risk events in patients who require antibiotic prophylaxis for endocardi- tis include dental procedures that involve the gingiva, periapical region, or perforation of oral mucosa. Medications commonly used for prophylaxis should be provided before the dental procedure and include amoxicillin, ampicillin, cefazolin, ceftriaxone, clindamycin, and azithromycin. Antibiotic prophylaxis is no longer recommended for GI, genitourinary, and pulmonary procedures. Incorrect Answer Explanations Intravenous drug users have an estimated risk of developing endocarditis in the range of 2% to 5% per year, with mean age of diagnosis 30 years. Endocarditis is primarily found on the tricuspid valve in intravenous drug users. Organ transplant recipients demonstrate increased risk of endocarditis due to their immunocompromised state. However, prophylaxis is only required in patients with a cardiac transplant and history of valvular disease. Previous surgical repair of atrial or ventricular septal defect is not an indi- cation for prophylaxis. Valvular disease alone is also not an indication, but the presence of a prosthetic valve does require antibiotic prophylaxis for the first 6 months. Finally, if the surgical repair was incomplete or resulted in abnormal flow, antibiotic prophylaxis is required.

ليش: antibiotic prophylaxis قبل إجراءات الأسنان بتنصح بها لمجموعة من الناس، ومنهم اللي عندهم تاريخ previous endocarditis. كمان للمصابين بـ prosthetic valves، ولي عندهم valvular disease مع قلب متحوّل، ولي عندهم congenital heart disease غير مُصلّح أو مُصلّح مع defect أو prosthesis باقٍ. والإجراءات اللي بتستدعي هالـ prophylaxis هي اللي بتمسّ الـ gingiva أو الـ periapical region أو بتخترق الـ oral mucosa، والأدوية المستخدمة amoxicillin و ampicillin و cefazolin.
الفخ: تعاطي المخدرات الوريدية و transplant recipients معاهم increased risk، بس الـ prophylaxis بتنصح بس لو في heart transplant مع valvular disease. و repair سابق لـ ASD ما هو indication.

question: An otherwise healthy 30-year-old with a history of intravenous drug use presents with dyspnea, chest pain, and fever. Which heart valve is most likely to be affected?
englishExplanation: Intravenous drug use (IVDU) places this patient at particular risk for right-sided endocarditis. Right-sided endocarditis most commonly, but not ex- clusively, involves the tricuspid valve, although multiple valves can be involved. IVDU is considered a significant risk factor for developing endocarditis, espe- cially in younger, otherwise healthy patients (with an average risk of 2%-5% per year and an average age of 30 years at the time of diagnosis). It is thought that in- jection of particulates and other contaminants results in endovascular injury that then predisposes patients to endocarditis and other infections. The infecting organ- isms can come from a variety of sources, including normal oral and skin flora, in- testinal coliforms, and bacterial contamination of the drug used. Complications of native valve endocarditis include valvular/myocardial injury with secondary heart failure, dysrhythmias, and heart blocks due to in- volvement of the conduction system; paravalvular abscess; and distant infection(s) or ischemia from septic emboli. Incorrect Answer Explanations Native aortic valve endocarditis is less common with IVDU than tricus- pid valve, accounting for approximately 20% of cases. A baseline abnormal aortic valve, (eg, bicuspid or stenotic aortic valve or due to rheumatic valvular disease) generally predisposes to endocarditis. In this case, IVDU increases this patient's risk of right-sided endocarditis significantly, making the tricuspid valve the most likely affected valve. Native mitral valve endocarditis is less common with IVDU than tricus- pid valve, accounting for approximately 20% of cases. A baseline abnormal mitral valve, most commonly due to rheumatic valvular disease or mitral pro- lapse, predisposes to endocarditis generally. In this case, IVDU increases this patient's risk of right-sided endocarditis significantly, making the tricuspid valve the most likely affected valve. Although it is a right-sided valve, pulmonic endocarditis is the least commonly affected valve endocarditis. It is also rarely affected in isolation. It is unclear why this valve is less commonly affected than the other valves. In this case, IVDU increases this patient's risk of right-sided endocarditis significantly, making the tricuspid valve the most likely affected valve.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: تعاطي المخدرات الوريدية بيحط هالمريض بخطر واضح لـ right-sided endocarditis، وهالنوع من الـ endocarditis بتصيب الـ tricuspid valve أكثر من غيرها. الـ IVDU عامل خطر مهم خصوصاً عند الشباب الأصحاء، بمعدل خطر 2% إلى 5% سنوياً ومتوسط عمر التشخيص 30 سنة. الحقن بيسبب ضرر endothelial، وهاد بتهيّئ البيئة للمسبب البكتيري.
الفخ: Aortic valve endocarditis نادرة مع الـ IVDU وتوصل 20% بس، وعادة بتحتاج abnormal aortic valve من الـ baseline. و Pulmonic و Mitral أقل شيوعاً من الـ tricuspid.

question: Which presentation meets the modified Duke criteria for the definite diagnosis of infective endocarditis?

options.text: New valvular regurgitation on TEE with Staphylococcus aureus in a single blood culture
T 39°C (102.2°F), Roth spots, and new valvular regurgitation on TEE
T 39°C (102.2°F), Roth spots, new valvular regurgitation on TEE, and history of intravenous drug use
Two separate blood cultures positive for Staphylococcus aureus, history of IV drug use, and laboratory findings suggestive of glomerulonephritis

correctAnswer: T 39°C (102.2°F), Roth spots, new valvular regurgitation on TEE, and history of intravenous drug use
englishExplanation:
The modified Duke criteria has been shown to reliably risk-stratify pa- tients as having definite infective endocarditis (IE), possible IE, or re- jected IE. Fever, Roth spots, and history of intravenous drug use are mi- nor criteria, and new valvular regurgitation on TEE is a major criterion. Per the Duke criteria, to have a definite diagnosis of IE there must be any of the fol- lowing combinations of clinical criteria: Two major criteria, One major criterion and three minor criteria, or Five minor criteria. Incorrect Answer Explanations New valvular regurgitation on TEE and a single blood culture positive for Staphylococcus aureus are insufficient for the diagnosis of IE. Only one major Duke criterion (new valvular regurgitation on TEE) is met. S. aureus is a typical causative organism, but to satisfy a major criterion, there must be at least two separate positive blood cultures of typical pathogens. T 39°C (102.2°F), Roth spots, and new valvular regurgitation on TEE are insufficient for a definite diagnosis of IE per the Duke criteria. This an- swer choice includes only one major criterion (evidence of new valvular regurgita- tion on TEE) and two minor criteria (fever >38°C [100.4°F] and the immunologic phenomenon of Roth spots). For a definite diagnosis of IE, an additional major or minor diagnostic criterion is needed. Blood cultures positive for Staphylococcus aureus in two separate blood cultures, history of intravenous drug use, and laboratory findings suggestive of glomeru- lonephritis are insufficient for a definite diagnosis of IE according to the modified Duke Criteria. These presentation includes only one major criterion (positive blood culture of a typical pathogen) and two minor criteria: history of intravenous drug use and glomerulonephritis (a laboratory finding suggestive of an immunologic phenomenon).

Review notes: ["html_markup_or_entities"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ modified Duke criteria بتصنّف المريض definite infective endocarditis لو في واحد من هالتركيبات: two major criteria، أو one major criterion مع three minor criteria، أو five minor criteria. هالحالة فيها major واحد وهو new valvular regurgitation على TEE، ومعها تلات minor: fever أكثر من 38 درجة، و Roth spots، و تاريخ intravenous drug use. يعني واحد major مع تلات minor، وهاد satisfies criteria.
الفخ: blood culture واحدة بس موجبة لـ Staphylococcus aureus ما بتكفي major criterion، لازم اتنين separate cultures. و Option التانية فيها major واحد و minor اثنين، فبتطلع possible IE مو definite.

question: Which imaging modality is best to diagnose early infective endocarditis in a pa- tient with a history of intravenous drug use who does not have a prosthetic valve?
englishExplanation: Echocardiography is the imaging modality of choice for all patients suspected of having infective endocarditis (IE). TEE has been shown to be superior to transthoracic echocardiography in sensitivity and specificity for the di- agnosis of IE. TEE has a sensitivity of greater than 90% for the detection of valvu- lar vegetations. Findings from echocardiography constitute portions of the major and minor modified Duke criteria for diagnosis of IE. Incorrect Answer Explanations Cardiac CT with angiography (CTA) is not an early primary imaging modality for suspected IE. However, it can be useful in cases with high suspicion of IE but nega- tive TEE findings. Additionally, cardiac CTA is very useful in patients with prosthetic valves because these valves limit the utility of TEE. Chest x-ray is not a definitive imaging modality for the diagnosis of IE. However, chest x-ray can be useful in IE caused by intravenous drug use because 50% of these cases involve the right side of the heart. In cases of right-sided IE, the valvular vegetations often produce septic pulmonary emboli. Chest x-ray can help identify these pulmonary emboli and also show evidence of fluid overload in cases of left-sided IE with significant regurgitation. Transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) is less diagnostically useful than TEE because of its limited ability to detect signs of IE. The overall sensitiv- ity of TTE is 46% to 60%. TTE still plays a role in the emergent evaluation of sus- pected IE because it is likely to be the first diagnostic test performed in the emer- gency department other than chest x-ray, which has limited diagnostic value. The risk of IE is substantially reduced in the setting of normal valve morphology and function on TTE. Although the sensitivity of TTE is poor, its specificity is 94%. Diagnostic sensitivity improves as the size of the vegetation increases.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ echocardiography هي imaging modality of choice لكل مريض مشتبه فيه بـ infective endocarditis. و TEE اتضحت أحسن من TTE بالـ sensitivity و specificity لتشخيص الـ IE، وحساسيتها أكثر من 90% لكشف الـ valvular vegetations. ونتائج الـ echocardiography بتشكّل جزء من الـ major و minor criteria في modified Duke criteria، فبتحسب فعلياً في التشخيص.
الفخ: TEE هي الأدق، مو TTE لأن قدرة TTE محدودة برؤية علامات الـ IE. و Cardiac CTA مش أول imaging، بس بتنفع لو TEE سالبة وخصوصاً مع prosthetic valves. و Chest x-ray بيقدر يكشف pulmonary emboli بالـ right-sided IE.

question: An 84-year-old woman presents after an episode of dyspnea and near syncope. A systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur is noted on examination. Which phar- macotherapy should be avoided?
englishExplanation: Aortic stenosis (AS) is the third most common form of cardiovascular disease in de- veloped countries after hypertension and coronary artery disease. Significant care should be taken when treating AS patients with preload-reducing agents (nitrates) because the sudden decrease in preload can cause se- vere hypotension, which can lead to decreased coronary flow and worsened is- chemia and shock. Diuretics and inotropic agents can also be deleterious and should be used with caution. Managing AS is challenging; judicious use of fluids, maintenance of normal sinus rhythm, and avoidance of nitrates are recommended. The most common causes of AS are calcification of a normal trileaflet aortic valve and a congenital bicuspid aortic valve. AS usually progresses slowly, with symptoms taking decades to manifest in most cases. Auscultation re- veals a systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur associated with diminished and de- layed carotid pulses (parvus et tardus), a sustained left ventricular impulse on pal- pation, and a decreased or absent aortic component of the second heart sound. An ECG can show left ventricular hypertrophy with a repolarization abnormality, which is seen in 85% of patients with severe AS. Yearly echocardiography is indicated for patients with severe AS to assess condition severity, wall thickness, and left ventri- cle function. Exercise stress testing can lead to complications in patients with symp- tomatic AS and should not be performed. Once symptoms appear, the average sur- vival time in AS is 2 to 3 years, with a risk for sudden death (<1% per year). Syncope develops in 15% of AS patients, angina in 35%, and congestive heart failure in 50%. Incorrect Answer Explanations According to guidelines from the European Society of Cardiology and the European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery, digitalis is recommended for use in AS patients who are not candidates for surgery. Unlike beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers, digitalis can be used to control the heart rate of AS pa- tients because it is unlikely to cause hypotension. Lisinopril and other ACE inhibitors can be used to treat hypertension in patients with aortic valve disease. However, care should be taken with dosing to avoid hypotension. Beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers should be avoided. No medical treatment has been shown to decrease disease progression in the aortic valve leaflets. Although statins are currently being studied, they have not been shown to worsen symptoms of AS. Statins are used in patients with AS and atherosclerotic heart disease.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريضة عندها systolic crescendo-decrescendo murmur مع dyspnea و near syncope، وهاد بيحكي عن aortic stenosis. لازم ننتبه شديد مع أي دوا بيقلّل preload زي الـ nitrates، لأن نزول الـ preload فجأة بيسبب severe hypotension، وبيقلّل الـ coronary flow وبيزيد ischemia و shock. والتوصيات بـ AS هي judicious use of fluids، والمحافظة على normal sinus rhythm، وتجنّب الـ nitrates. و decompensation حاد بيجي من الـ reduction.
الفخ: الناس بتلخبط بين دوا بيقلّل afterload مثل Lisinopril ودوا بيقلّل preload مثل Nitroglycerin، والخطر هنا من نزول الـ preload. و Statins مش الإجابة لأن مرضى AS عندهم increased risk of CAD.

question: A 49-year-old man presents after fainting while running on his treadmill at home. He reports having exertional labored breathing and chest pain for the past several months. What cardiac disease is most likely to cause these symptoms?
englishExplanation: Aortic stenosis is a progressive disease that tends to become sympto- matic when the valve orifice narrows to 1 cm. This patient demonstrates the three classic symptoms of aortic stenosis: syncope, angina, and dyspnea. In pa- tients younger than 65 years, aortic stenosis is predominantly caused by a bicuspid aortic valve; in older patients, aortic stenosis results from calcific degenera- tion of the valve cusps. Ventricular outflow becomes severely restricted in aortic stenosis, and the left ven- tricle attempts to compensate for the outflow obstruction by becoming hypertro- phied. Evidence of left ventricular hypertrophy can be found on the 12- lead ECG and on chest x-ray. During rest, cardiac output is maintained, and the 2 patient is asymptomatic. However, during exertion, the left ventricle is unable to in- crease cardiac output resulting in dyspnea and syncope. Management of pa- tients with symptomatic aortic stenosis is complicated by the need to maintain both preload and afterload without causing acute decompen- sation from reduction. Symptomatic patients should be referred for possible surgical repair or replacement. Incorrect Answer Explanations Compared to aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation is less likely to cause symptoms of syncope with exertion because the regurgitation decreases with the shorter diastolic filling time during exercise. Dyspnea, on the other hand, is commonly seen in aortic regurgitation and can progress to symptoms of con- gestive heart failure. Mitral valve incompetence is most commonly caused by rheumatic heart disease worldwide and by mitral valve prolapse in the developed world. The chronic changes result in exertional dyspnea symptoms. The slow, chronic nature of this etiology results in maintained stroke volume, so syncope is uncom- mon. Acute mitral incompetence due to ischemia or infarct presents with pul- monary congestion and dyspnea due to the acute increase in left atrial filling pres- sures. Pulmonary edema is also common. Mitral stenosis, most commonly caused by rheumatic heart disease, produces symptoms of dyspnea and often orthopnea. The stenotic flow across the mitral valve leads to increased left atrial pressure and, eventually, to se- vere pulmonary hypertension if left untreated. Mitral stenosis does not typically lead to syncope.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريض عنده ثلاث أعراض كلاسيكية لـ aortic stenosis: syncope، و angina، و dyspnea مع الجهد. الـ AS مرض بيصير symptomatic لما الـ valve orifice يضيق لحد 1 cm. تحت سن الـ 65 السبب غالباً bicuspid aortic valve، وفوق الـ 65 بيكون calcific degeneration للـ cusps. الـ left ventricle بيتضخم وبيحاول يعوّض انسداد الـ outflow، وبالراحة الـ cardiac output ثابت، بس أثناء الجهد ما بيقدر يزيد.
الفخ: Aortic regurgitation أقل احتمالاً إنها تعطي syncope مع الجهد، لأن الـ regurgitation بتقل لما يقصر وقت الـ diastolic filling أثناء التمرين. و mitral stenosis و regurgitation عندهم أنماط ظهور مختلفة.

question: What finding is most common on chest x-ray in acute mitral regurgitation?
englishExplanation: Pulmonary edema is the most likely chest x-ray finding in patients with acute mitral regurgitation. Patients often will also have normal cardiac silhouettes, raising the suspicion for an acute process, because chronic mitral regurgitation of- ten shows an enlarged cardiac silhouette with left atrial and ventricular enlarge- ment. Echocardiogram with Doppler is the most helpful test in these patients, which will show mitral regurgitation. On examination, a systolic murmur best heard along the left sternal bor- der at the base of the heart can be noted in about 50% of patients with acute mitral regurgitation. Patients also may exhibit an S3 gallop. Patients of- ten have no history of heart failure at the time of initial presentation, which should raise suspicion for valvular injury. ECG in these patients may show signs of infarc- tion or ischemia. Incorrect Answer Explanations Acute mitral regurgitation does not cause cardiac enlargement and, thus, no enlarged cardiac silhouette would appear on chest x-ray. By comparison, chronic mitral regurgitation does lead to cardiac changes and would potentially show car- diac enlargement on chest x-rays. Normal x-ray under these circumstances is unlikely. Patients with acute mitral regurgitation would likely be exhibiting signs and symptoms of heart failure and pulmonary edema, causing them to come to the emergency department. Thus, they would most likely have evidence of pulmonary edema on a chest x-ray. A widened mediastinum on chest x-ray is unrelated to acute mitral regurgita- tion. It can be associated with an aortic aneurysm or dissection, which can lead to acute aortic regurgitation. In that case, pulmonary edema would also likely be present on the chest x-ray.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أكتر شي يظهر على الـ chest x-ray في acute mitral regurgitation هو pulmonary edema. وممكن cardiac silhouette يكون طبيعي، وهاد بيزيد الشك إن العملية acute، لأن chronic mitral regurgitation غالباً بتبيّن enlarged cardiac silhouette مع enlargement بالـ left atrium و left ventricle. و Doppler echocardiogram هي أكتر test مفيدة هنا لأنها بتبيّن الـ mitral regurgitation، وبالفحص ممكن نسمع systolic murmur على الـ left sternal border عند ثلث الحول.
الفخ: enlarged cardiac silhouette دليل على chronic process مو acute. و x-ray طبيعي غير مرجّح لأن المريض بيبان عليه heart failure و pulmonary edema. و widened mediastinum بيحكي عن مشكلة بالـ aorta مو بالصمامات.

question: What medication would be most helpful for acute mitral regurgitation?
englishExplanation: For patients with acute mitral regurgitation, afterload-reducing agents are most helpful. Nitrates (eg, nitroprusside) and diuretics can decrease regurgi- tation and improve aortic output. Patients with acute mitral regurgitation may rapidly develop hypotension. In that setting, an inotrope such as dobutamine may also be necessary. The hemodynamic changes that occur in acute mitral regurgitation are more severe than in chronic mitral regurgitation because the heart does not have time to adapt. If hypotension develops, they will likely require intra-aortic balloon pump counterpulsation placement for stabilization prior to surgical intervention, which is the definitive treatment for mitral valve regurgitation. Incorrect Answer Explanations Dopamine is contraindicated in cases of acute mitral regurgitation. Dopamine increases systemic vascular resistance, which increases afterload and leads to decreased aortic outflow. However, dobutamine causes vasodilation, which decreases afterload. Lisinopril is useful in managing patients with chronic mitral regurgitation because it decreases afterload. However, it is ineffective for emergent stabilization in the setting of acute mitral regurgitation. Norepinephrine increases systemic vascular resistance and, thus, increases af- terload. This increase leads to increased mitral regurgitation and decreased car- diac output, making it a poor choice for acute mitral regurgitation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في acute mitral regurgitation، أحسن دوا هو afterload-reducing agents زي nitroprusside، ومعها diuretics، عشان يقلّلوا الـ regurgitation ويحسّنوا الـ aortic output. والتغيرات الهيموديناميكية بالـ acute MR أشد من الـ chronic لأن القلب ما إله وقت يتأقلم. وقد يتطور hypotension بسرعة، وعندها ممكن تحتاج inotrope مثل dobutamine، مع IABP قبل تدخل الجراحة الذي هو العلاج النهائي.
الفخ: Dopamine و Norepinephrine ممنوعين لأنهم بيزودوا systemic vascular resistance، وهاد بيزود الـ afterload وبيزود الـ regurgitation وبيقلّل الـ cardiac output. و Lisinopril بيفيد بالـ chronic بس مش للاستقرار الطارئ.

question: Presence of which finding on the physical examination is most concerning for a potentially dangerous cause of dizziness?
englishExplanation: Symptomatic aortic stenosis generally occurs when the valve area is se- verely narrowed (<1 cm compared to normal = 3-4 cm). A patient presenting with dizziness (presyncopal symptoms) in the setting of an aortic steno- sis murmur likely has severe disease and should be evaluated for critical aor- tic stenosis. Echocardiography is the diagnostic modality of choice for 2 2 aortic stenosis. It is used to determine the degree of stenosis and evaluate for sys- tolic or diastolic dysfunction. Aortic stenosis classically presents as a systolic “crescendo-decrescendo” ejec- tion murmur heard best at the right sternal border of the second intercostal space that radiates into the carotids. Presence of a palpable thrill in this setting would im- ply significant blood flow turbulence and likely corresponds to severe stenosis. Delayed carotid pulsation is another significant finding. Patients classically develop anginal symptoms, then presyncopal/syncopal symptoms, followed fi- nally by development of secondary heart failure. The prognosis of untreated symptomatic aortic stenosis worsens with subsequent development of each. Admission, emergency department cardiology consultation, or discharge with close outpatient cardiology follow-up can be considered based on local resources and the severity of the patient's clinical presentation. Note that vasodilator agents should be avoided or used very cautiously in patients with severe aortic stenosis; these cause preload reduction that can result in decreased flow across the fixed ob- struction and thus reduced cardiac output. Patients should also be advised against significant exertion. Incorrect Answer Explanations Capillary refill is frequently used as a bedside metric of distal perfusion and volume status. Major causes of capillary refill prolongation include hy- povolemia and shock states. A normal capillary refill is 2 seconds or less, mak- ing this measure normal and, therefore, not dangerous. By contrast, dizziness (presyncope) in the setting of severe aortic stenosis is a dangerous circumstance and requires urgent additional evaluation. Nystagmus with lateral head movement occurs with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). BPPV is an uncomfortable but ultimately benign dis- order of the inner ear. It is treated with vestibular suppressants, such as meclizine, and vestibular therapy with the Epley maneuver. A patient presenting with this form of dizziness is not in danger and can be discharged once their symptoms are controlled. By contrast, dizziness (presyncope) in the setting of severe aortic steno- sis is a dangerous circumstance and requires urgent additional evaluation. Major causes of positional (or orthostatic) lightheadedness include de- hydration, medication side effects (diuretics, antihypertensives, alpha-1 antagonists), and autonomic dysfunction. Although orthostatic symptoms can certainly result in dangerous situations, such as falls, most causes are not dan- gerous. By contrast, dizziness (presyncope) in the setting of severe aortic stenosis is a dangerous circumstance and requires urgent additional evaluation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ symptomatic aortic stenosis بيصير لما مساحة الصمام تنضيق بشكل كبير، أقل من 1 cm مقابل 3 إلى 4 cm طبيعي. ومريض بيجي بدوار pre-syncopal ومعه murmur of aortic stenosis، غالباً عنده severe disease ولازم ينقيّم for critical aortic stenosis. الـ echocardiography هي modality المفضّلة للتشخيص لأنها بتحدد درجة الـ stenosis و functional status. والـ murmur crescendo-decrescendo بينسمع best بالـ right sternal border وبيـ radiates للـ carotids.
الفخ: capillary refill تين ساني و positional lightheadedness هادوا vasovagal أو orthostatic، ما بيوصّلوا لمرض قلبي خطير. و nystagmus مع حركة الرأس بيوحي بمشكلة دوار peripheral.

question: What is the most common etiology of aortic valve stenosis in the United States?
englishExplanation: The most common etiology of aortic valve stenosis is the gradual accumulation of calcium deposits on a normal tricuspid aortic valve. Senile degenerative calcification occurs slowly and is therefore more common in older patients. An activated inflammatory process causes the aortic valve to degenerate and become stiff, irregular, and fibrosed. This process shares the risk factors associated with coronary artery disease, such as male sex, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes, and smoking. Incorrect Answer Explanations Aortic valve stenosis may be triggered by an abnormal bicuspid aortic valve, but this is less common than age-related degeneration. A bicuspid valve has two cusps instead of the normal three, which results in turbulent flow, calcium buildup, and fibrosis. As expected, bicuspid aortic valve stenosis occurs at least a couple of decades earlier than tricuspid aortic valve stenosis. Although the prevalence of a bicuspid valve is less than 1% to 2% of the population, it accounts for nearly 50% of aortic valve replacements. Although radiation therapy to the mediastinum is associated with aortic valve stenosis, it is less common than age-related degeneration. Radiation-induced aortic valve stenosis involves progressive valve thickening and calcification in the decade following radiation therapy. Symptoms due to valve re- striction and dysfunction occur 5 years later, and valve replacement is common. Although rheumatic fever is the most common cause of aortic valve stenosis in developing countries, it is less common in the United States. An untreated group A Streptococcus throat infection may lead to acute rheumatic fever and chronic rheumatic heart disease, in which the aortic valve becomes thick- ened, fibrotic, and shrunken, with distinctive fused commissures. In 90% of cases, the aortic valve is affected along with the mitral valve.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أكتر سبب لـ aortic valve stenosis هو تراكم تدريجي للـ calcium على صمام aortic طبيعي بـ three cusps. هاي senile degenerative calcification بتصير ببطء، فاللي بتشوفها أكثر عند كبار السن. و process inflammatory بيتفعّل، فالصمام بيصير stiff و irregular و fibrosed. وهاد بيشارك عوامل الخطر نفسها بتاعت coronary artery disease زي الذكورة و hypercholesterolemia و diabetes و smoking.
الفخ: Bicuspid aortic valve أقل شيوعاً من الـ age-related degeneration، بس بيظهر sclerosis قبلها بـ عقدين أو تلاتة. و Radiation therapy للـ mediastinum و rheumatic fever كمان أقل شيوعاً.

question: What cardiac disorder is suggested by a systolic ejection murmur that radiates to the carotids?
englishExplanation: Aortic valve stenosis results in a midsystolic (systolic ejection) murmur as blood is ejected through a narrowed aortic valve. The murmur begins just after the first heart sound and terminates just before the second heart sound, so the first and second heart sounds are clearly audible. The murmur is a crescendo- decrescendo shape and is high-pitched due to the large pressure gradient between the left ventricle and aorta. It is best heard with the diaphragm of the stethoscope at the aortic valve post on the right upper sternal border. The murmur radiates to the carotid arteries. Leg raising accentuates the murmur by increasing preload, while handgrip attenuates the murmur. Incorrect Answer Explanations The murmur of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is similar to aortic valve stenosis in that it is high-pitched, crescendo-decrescendo, and midsystolic. However, unlike aortic valve stenosis, it is best heard in the left lower sternal border and it does not radiate to the carotids. The hypertrophic cardiomyopathy murmur is accentuated with standing and with the Valsalva maneuver, which de- creases preload. It is attenuated with squatting (which increases preload) and the handgrip maneuver (which increases afterload). Mitral valve regurgitation is caused by the retrograde flow of blood back through the mitral valve from the left ventricle into the left atrium. This results in a blowing, holosystolic murmur that begins with the first heart sound and ex- tends up to the second, making them difficult to hear. The murmur is heard best at the apex of the heart with the patient rolled onto their left side, and it radiates to the left axilla. The murmur increases with handgrip and decreases with inspiration and with the Valsalva maneuver. Ventricular septal defect is a defect in the ventricular septum that results in a holosystolic murmur with normal heart sounds. The murmur is best heard at the left lower sternal border and does not radiate. Smaller defects are associ- ated with a louder murmur and a palpable thrill. The murmur increases with hand- grip and decreases with the Valsalva maneuver.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ aortic valve stenosis بتعمل midsystolic ejection murmur لأن الدم بيطلع من صمام aortic ضيق. الـ murmur بيبدأ بعد S1 وبيخلص قبل S2، فصوتا القلب الأول والثاني واضحين. شكله crescendo-decrescendo وعالي الصوت بسبب فرق الضغط الكبير بين الـ left ventricle والـ aorta. بينسمع أحسن بالـ diaphragm على الـ right upper sternal border، وبيـ radiates للـ carotid arteries. و leg raising بيزوّد وضوحه بزيادة الـ preload.
الفخ: murmur بتاع hypertrophic cardiomyopathy عالي و crescendo-decrescendo مثله، بس بينسمع بالـ left lower sternal border و ما بيـ radiates للـ carotids، وبيزيد مع الوقوف ومع Valsalva. و Mitral regurgitation murmur نفخي best عند الـ apex.

question: What is the most likely cause of acute mitral valve regurgitation from papillary muscle rupture?
englishExplanation: Myocardial infarction (MI) is the most common cause of papillary mus- cle rupture, which can lead to acute mitral regurgitation. Acute mitral regurgita- tion most commonly occurs due to papillary muscle or chordae tendineae rupture, which is secondary to ischemia 2 to 7 days after an acute MI. Acute mitral re- gurgitation may also occur in endocarditis or trauma. Patients present with signs and symptoms of pulmonary edema, often of rapid onset, including signs of cardio- genic shock (eg, poor tissue perfusion and hypotension), and they may decompen- sate rapidly. Incorrect Answer Explanations Aortic dissection is an uncommon cause of acute mitral valve regurgitation. It can cause acute aortic regurgitation or insufficiency. Like mitral regurgita- tion, aortic regurgitation often presents with acute pulmonary edema and cardio- genic shock. However, an intra-aortic balloon pump is contraindicated for patients with aortic injury, so emergent surgical intervention will be necessary. Myocarditis is an uncommon cause of acute mitral regurgitation. Myocarditis is caused by cardiac muscle inflammation, which can lead to heart failure. Patients can also develop arrhythmias. Pulmonary embolism is an uncommon cause of acute mitral regurgitation. Large pulmonary emboli can lead to right ventricular strain and a dilated right ventricle. This can subsequently lead to tricuspid regurgitation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ myocardial infarction هو أكتر سبب لـ papillary muscle rupture، وهذي اللي بتسبب acute mitral valve regurgitation. الـ rupture بتصير بعد 2 إلى 7 أيام من الـ acute MI بسبب الـ ischemia. و acute MR ممكن تصير كمان بـ endocarditis أو trauma. المريض بيبان عليه pulmonary edema سريع الظهور مع signs of cardiogenic shock زي poor tissue perfusion و hypotension، وممكن ينهار بسرعة.
الفخ: Aortic dissection سبب نادر وهو بيسبب acute aortic regurgitation مش mitral. و Myocarditis و Pulmonary embolism نادرين، والـ PE غالباً بيسبب tricuspid regurgitation.

question: A patient presents with palpitations after the recent placement of a pacemaker. The ECG is shown. Which diagnosis most likely explains this patient's symptoms? Credit: Eric Shappell, MD, MHPE.
englishExplanation:
Undersensing describes a pacemaker's failure to detect intrinsic my- ocardial depolarization, resulting in inappropriate pacemaker impulses that occur soon after intrinsic depolarizations. The rhythm strip here shows a pacer spike during the ST segment of an intrinsic beat; this impulse should have been inhibited after the pacemaker sensed the preceding intrinsic de- polarization. Note that the second pacemaker impulse is not conducted because the ventricular myocardium is in the refractory period at this time. This nonconducted impulse, therefore, does not represent failure to capture. Etiologies of under- sensing include lead displacement or malfunction and changes in depolarization characteristics since the time of insertion (eg, myocardial fibrosis or infarc- tion, medication effects, or metabolic processes). Incorrect Answer Explanations Failure to capture is when the pacing stimulus does not result in my- ocardial depolarization. Failure to capture may be caused by many of the same mechanisms as undersensing, including lead displacement or malfunction, or changes in myocardial characteristics since the time of insertion (eg, myocardial fibrosis or infarction, medication effects, or metabolic processes). The ECG in a failure-to-capture scenario will show pacer spikes that lack an associ- ated depolarization (QRS) complex. The ECG in this question shows pacemaker spikes that are followed by depolarization complexes, which is not consistent with failure to capture. Oversensing is when low-voltage electrical signals (which may include nonmyocardial sources) result in inappropriate inhibition of pace- maker firing. Causes may include detection of T waves as intrinsic depolariza- tions, pectoralis muscle activation, or electrocautery devices. “Pacemaker syndrome” refers to new or worsening symptoms that pa- tients experience shortly after pacemaker placement caused by atri- oventricular dyssynchrony (ie, loss of atrial “kick”). Symptoms may include shortness of breath, exercise intolerance, and lethargy. Most patients have mild symptoms, although a small minority require pacemaker adjustment or replace- ment. Pacemaker syndrome is not associated with evidence of pacemaker malfunction on rhythm strips, as seen in this case. Key Points Common types of pacemaker malfunction include oversensing, undersensing, and failure to capture. Undersensing is when a pacemaker does not detect intrinsic depolarizations and re- sults in inappropriate asynchronous pacemaker impulses. Oversensing is when a pacemaker detects low-voltage signals as ventricular depolar- izations, resulting in the inappropriate inhibition of pacemaker impulses. Failure to capture is when pacemaker impulses fail to cause myocardial depolarization.

Review notes: ["visual_reference_no_image_attached_in_jsonl"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الـ pacemaker ما قدر يكتشف الـ depolarization الطبيعية اللي عم يصير بالقلب، فبعت impulse تاني بسرعة بدون ما يتوقف. اللي صار إنه الـ pacer spike طلع جوّا الـ ST segment بتاع الـ beat اللي قبله، يعني المفروض كان بيتحبط بعد ما sensed الديبولاريزيشن اللي قبله. والـ impulse التاني ما وصل لـ QRS لأنو الـ myocardium كان refractory بهالوقت، وهاد مو معناها failure to capture. أسباب الـ undersensing فيها lead displacement أو lead malfunction، أو تغيّر بخصائص الـ depolarization بعد الزراعة مثل myocardial fibrosis أو infarction.
الفخ: أغلب الطلاب بيختاروا failure to capture لأنو شافوا pacer spike بدون QRS تبعه. الفرق إنو في failure to capture الـ spike موجود وما في QRS بعده، أما هون الـ spike جاي جوّا الـ ST segment وما انطور QRS لأنو القلب كان refractory.

question: Which diagnostic study is most helpful in identifying the cause of automated im- plantable cardioverter-defibrillator failure?
englishExplanation: Approximately a quarter of AICD lead failures are due to lead fracture. Although re- mote interrogation is more sensitive for the diagnosis of lead fracture, a chest x-ray may show mechanically disrupted AICD leads. Other possible causes of AICD lead failure include insulation defects and artifact oversensing, each account- ing for around a quarter of lead failure incidents. Other AICDs complications re- lated to leads include tricuspid regurgitation due to damage to the tricuspid valve from lead insertion; impeded closure of the valve; and increased defibrillation threshold due to dislodgement of leads, inflammation at the lead tip, or pharmaceu- ticals, such as amiodarone. Incorrect Answer Explanations Chest MRI is relatively contraindicated in patients with AICDs or pace- makers. Research is ongoing into MRI-safe devices. A nuclear medicine bleeding scan is unlikely to reveal the cause of lead failure in a patient with an AICD. It is primarily used to assess sources of bleeding, particularly GI bleeding. A subclavian ultrasound is unlikely to reveal the cause of lead failure in a patient with an AICD. However, it may reveal lead-related DVT.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: حوالي ربع حالات فشل الـ leads بالـ AICD سببها fracture بالـ lead نفسه. الفحص عن بعد بـ remote interrogation أدق كتير بالتفريغ، بس الـ chest x-ray بيكشف leads متعطلة ميكانيكيًا أو انزاحة بتاعتها. فإذا الجهاز صار فيه خلل لازم تعمل أشعة للصدر لأنها سريعة ومجانية وبتبيّن الـ leads اللي متضررة بشكل واضح. كمان من كم سبب تاني للفشل هو defect بالـ insulation أو artifact oversensing، وكل واحد منهم حوالي ربع الحوادث.
الفخ: خيار الـ MRI والـ nuclear medicine bleeding scan ما بيساعدوا بهالسبب. الـ MRI ممنوع عملياً عند حدا عندو AICD أو pacemaker، والـ bleeding scan بينفع لفحص نزيف gastrointestinal، والـ subclavian ultrasound بيكشف الـ DVT بس وما بيوضح سبب فشل الـ lead.

question: A patient presents with erythema, swelling, warmth, and purulent drainage on the chest wall over an automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator device they have had for 8 years. The area around the device feels fluctuant. What is the definitive treatment for this clinical problem?

options.text: Incision and drainage of the abscess pocket
Needle aspiration of the abscess pocket
Removal of the device and associated hardware

correctAnswer: Removal of the device and associated hardware
englishExplanation: A patient with a pocket infection should have the device and all hard- ware removed. In the process of removing the device, the pocket should be well debrided. Antibiotics or incision and drainage of the abscess pocket are insufficient for treating pocket infections. Because of the propensity for formation of vegetation on the device or leads, pocket infections can cause endocarditis. TEE is piv- otal in the diagnosis of this additional complication. Incorrect Answer Explanations Empiric broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics are indicated for pocket infections but are not definitive treatment without removal of the device and hardware. Antibiotic choice should be guided by culture data, once available. Incision and drainage of the abscess without removal of the device and hardware is inadequate. In an infection with a nidus, such as an implantable de- vice or hardware, the nidus should be removed before or concurrently with treat- ment. By contrast, incision and drainage is often sufficient for treating an uncompli- cated abscess. Needle aspiration of the abscess pocket without removal of the device and hardware is inadequate. In an infection with a nidus, such as an implantable device or hard- ware, the nidus should be removed before or concurrently with treatment.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد بيتكلم عن infection بالـ pocket اللي حاوي الـ ICD، والعلاج الحقيقي هو إنك تشيل الـ device وكل الـ hardware معه. وقت الشيل لازم تنضف الـ pocket بشكل كامل، يعني debride. الـ antibiotics لوحدها أو incision and drainage ما بتكفي لأنو الـ nidus موجود جوا وبيعمل vegetation على الـ device أو الـ leads، وكمان الـ pocket infection ممكن يسبب endocarditis. وهون الـ TEE pivotal لتشخيص هالمضاعفة.
الفخ: الخيار اللي بيقفلهوا الـ antibiotics broad-spectrum intravenous والـ incision and drainage. هالاثنين لازم تسووا بس مع removal، لأنو وجود الـ device جوا بيعمل nidus وكل مرة بترجع الـ infection.

question: A patient with a permanent pacemaker achieves ROSC after intubation, chest compressions, and external defibrillation. Afterward, their pacemaker does not resume pacing spontaneously. Their vital signs are BP 68/43, P 34, R 12, and T 36.6°C (97.9°F); SpO is 93% on room air. An ECG is obtained and is shown be- low. What is the best next step? Credit: Mattu A, Tabas J, Brady w, eds. Electrocardiography in Emergency, Acute, and Critical Care. 2nd ed. American College of Emergency Physicians; 2019.
englishExplanation:
This patient has a complete heart block that is not being paced by their permanent pacemaker. Transcutaneous pacing is the best next step. Defibrillation at 200 J, 300 J, and 360 J is safe in patients with pacemakers if the anterior/posterior pad orientation is used or as long as the pad is placed approxi- mately 10 cm from the implanted pacemaker pulse generator. Immediate return of pacing may not occur after defibrillation. It is thought that there may be an increased pacing threshold related to ischemia, not a pacemaker malfunction. If, however, normal pacing does not resume sponta- neously, pacing will need to be reestablished. In this setting, transcutaneous pacing is the next best choice, and it is the safest approach to quickly resume pacing. Potential pacemaker complications that can occur after defibrillation are inhibition due to reversion to noise mode, damage to the circuit, re- programming, or myocardial damage at the site of the lead tip sec- ondary to current transmitted through the electrode. Incorrect Answer Explanations In the setting of chest compressions, it is important to verify that the pacemaker leads were not displaced. POCUS and chest x-ray may be helpful in deter- mining if there is displacement, but it would not be the next best step. Attempts at reestablishing pacing should occur first since the patient has unstable vital signs. After resuscitation, all pacemakers should be interrogated; however, it is important to reestablish pacing prior to interrogation. Transcutaneous pacing should be attempted first, as this is the quickest and safest way to reestablish pacing in this unstable patient. Transvenous pacing would be a way to reestablish pacing in this patient; however, it is not the quickest or safest approach. Additionally, attempts at temporary transvenous pacing may dislodge the permanent pacemaker leads. Transcutaneous pacing is the best initial approach to quickly reestablish pacing in this unstable patient.

Review notes: ["visual_reference_no_image_attached_in_jsonl"]
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريض عندو complete heart block وما الـ pacemaker الدائم عم pacing. الضغط عنده 68/43 والنبض 34 يعني هو unstable وبحتاج pacing فوراً. الـ transcutaneous pacing هو أحسن خطوة لأنه بيشتغل بسرعة وأمان وبيعيد الـ pacing من غير ما تستنى. والـ defibrillation بـ 200J و 300J و 360J آمن مع الـ pacemakers إذا حطيت الـ pads من قدام ولورا أو بعيد 10 cm عن الـ pulse generator.
الفخ: ناس بيختاروا pacemaker interrogation أو Cardiac POCUS عشان يتأكدوا من نزوح الـ leads. بس المريض unstable، لازم ترجّع الـ pacing الأول وبعدين تفحص، والـ transcutaneous هو أسرع طريقة تضمن النبض.

question: What is present in the rhythm strip below? Credit: Reproduced with permission from: Steven A. Pace, MD. In: Mattu A, Tabas J, Brady w, eds. Electrocardiography in Emergency, Acute, and Critical Care. 2nd ed. American College of Emergency Physicians; 2019.
englishExplanation: Failure to sense often appears as pacemaker spikes that occur earlier than the programmed rate (as is the case in this rhythm strip). With fail- ure to sense, the spike may or may not be followed by a QRS complex based on its relationship to the ventricular refractory period. Failure to sense can also be either complete or intermittent. It often occurs in the setting of fibrosis or cardiomy- opathies, as well as in acute right ventricular infarcts. Poor lead contact, lead fractures, or displacement can also lead to failure to sense. One should be cautious in the setting of a lack of QRS complex after a pacer spike during a refrac- tory period because it may be wrongly interpreted as failure to pace. Incorrect Answer Explanations Failure to pace (oversensing) occurs when there is interference from other electrical signals within the body (myopotentials), which is not present in this rhythm strip. Other electrical signals may be from MRIs or electro- cautery. When this occurs, the pacemaker incorrectly inhibits the pulse generator signal, and the patient may develop a bradycardic rhythm. Oversensing is seen most commonly when an intrinsic ventricular depolarization is followed by a T wave. Pacemaker with an inappropriate rate is not shown in this rhythm strip. Pacing rates below the programmed rate often occur in the setting of battery de- pletion. This is more rare with current lithium batteries, but in rare cases, it can lead to a rapid paced ventricular rate. In a normal ventricular paced rhythm, each pacemaker spike would be followed by a QRS complex, which is not the case in this rhythm strip. If an in- trinsic QRS complex occurs in the setting of a ventricular demand pacemaker, the pacemaker would sense it and inhibit a paced beat. In the absence of an intrinsic beat within a certain time interval (rate), the pacemaker would deliver a paced beat based on that rate interval.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بالـ strip اللي قدام نشوف pacer spikes بتيجي قبل الوقت المبرمج للـ pacing، وهاد تعريف الـ failure to sense. الـ pacemaker ما التقط الـ depolarization الطبيعية فبعت spike بدري. الـ spike ممكن يصير بعده QRS أو لا، حسب علاقته بالـ refractory period، والـ failure to sense بيصير كـ complete أو intermittent. الآسباب فيها fibrosis و cardiomyopathies و acute right ventricular infarcts، وفيه كمان poor lead contact أو lead fracture أو displacement.
الفخ: بعضهم بيختاروا failure to pace أو oversensing لأنو شافوا pacer spike بدون QRS تبعه. بـ oversensing بيصير الجهاز يوقف pulse generator لأنو قاس إشارات ثانية بالـ body، وهاد مو موجود بالـ strip.

question: A 57-year-old man with a history of severe ischemic cardiomyopathy presents with fever and chills. He had an LVAD implanted 5 weeks ago as a bridge therapy to cardiac transplantation. No obvious source of infection is noted on examina- tion. Which component of the assist device is the most likely source of the infection?
englishExplanation: Infection is a common adverse event following placement of an LVAD. Infection most often occurs between 2 weeks and 2 months after implantation. The various sites of LVAD-related infection include the incision site, pump pocket, driv- eline, and the various cannulas. The driveline is the most common site of in- fection. This line exits the chest wall protected by a skin seal and is thus most sus- ceptible to infection. Empiric antibiotic therapy should cover staphylococ- cal species as well as various gram-negative organisms, including Pseudomonas. Outpatient oral antibiotic therapy is appropriate for most patients with an LVAD driveline infection. Antibiotics should be continued for 2 to 4 weeks, with discontinuation based on the clinical picture. Incorrect Answer Explanations The various cannulas of the LVAD circuit can be involved in the infectious process, but they are not the most common site of infection. Driveline infection is a more common site for infection after LVAD placement. The site of the incision is also susceptible to infection, but it is not the most com- mon site of infection following LVAD placement. Driveline infection is more common. The pump pocket is the second most common area of infection after LVAD place- ment. The driveline goes into the pump, which is contained within a pocket in the chest wall. This pocket may become infected.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ infection من أشهر المضاعفات بعد زراعة الـ LVAD، وبيصير غالبًا بين أسبوعين وشهرين بعد العملية. الـ driveline هي أكثر جزء بيصاب لأنو الخط هذا بيطلع من جدار الصدر مكشوف للبيئة ومكسوه غير بـ skin seal. كمان الـ treatment بيكون antibiotics بتغطي staphylococci و gram-negatives زي Pseudomonas، وأغلب الحالات بتنعالج بالـ oral outpatient antibiotics من 2 لـ 4 أسابيع.
الفخ: الـ pump pocket والـ cannulas والـ incision site كلهم ممكن يصيبهم infection، بس الـ driveline هو الأكثر شيوعاً. الـ pump pocket ثاني أكثر مكان بعد الزراعة، ومع ذلك الـ driveline تتقدم عليه.

question: EMS calls about a patient with an LVAD who became unresponsive and apneic while being transported for altered mental status. EMS noted device alarms on initial assessment. All connections were found to be in place, and the batteries were exchanged without improvement. There are currently no device sounds in the chest. The patient's airway was secured en route. What action should be taken next?

options.text: Perform a needle decompression of the chest

englishExplanation: Prompt and full BLS/ACLS is recommended for LVAD patients in car- diac arrest if no readily correctable cause is identified.
