ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ ECG بيبين narrow complex tachycardia منتظمة بدون موجات P واضحة، وهاد غالباً AVNRT وهي أكثر tachycardia شائعة عند أصحاب القلوب الطبيعية. والمريضة مستقرة يعني ما في hypotension ولا شحوب ولا تغير ذهني، فالخطوة الأولى vagal maneuvers. الـ modified Valsalva، يعني blowing جوا سرنجة 10 mL لمدة 15-20 ثانية مع passive leg raise، أكثر فعالية من الـ maneuvers العادية، وحياتنا فيها ice water immersion و carotid massage.
الفخ: أكثر خطأ هو القفز على adenosine أو diltiazem مباشرة. هاد الـ drugs بتنفع، بس الترتيب غلط لأنه لازم تجرب vagal maneuvers أولا عند المريض المستقر. وبعدين carotid massage بنتجنبه عند كبار السن بسبب خطر تفجر plaque.

question: A 55-year-old man in cardiac arrest is being treated by paramedics. Which of the following is most important in positively affecting the chance of survival in the pre-hospital setting?
englishExplanation:
A significant amount of research has evaluated cardiac arrest in the pre-hospital setting and all aspects of advanced cardiac life support. The most important aspect contributing to improved survival in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest is high-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation, particularly compressions. The American Heart Association reports that there are five critical components of high-quality CPR: minimize interruptions in chest compressions, provide compressions of adequate rate, provide compressions of adequate depth, avoid leaning between compressions, and avoid excess ventilation.



Antidysrhythmic drugs (B) have not shown long-term benefits in most large resuscitation trials. Some drugs have actually been associated with worsened outcomes. Epinephrine (C) has shown only minimal short-term benefit in most trials and rarely a survival benefit that does not appear to have as much impact as high-quality compressions. The establishment of a definitive airway (D) is not associated with improvement of survival in the pre-hospital setting. Most suspect this is because of the interruption of compressions that often occurs while attempts at intubation are made. Many clinicians have moved to the establishment of a temporary supraglottic airway or bag mask ventilation only until the patient has a return of spontaneous circulation.

One Step Further
Question:
What rate of compressions is recommended in adult patients?

Reveal Answer:
100–120 compressions per minute.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Adult Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation

Compression position: lower half of sternum
Compression depth: at least 2 inches (5–6 cm)
Compression rate: 100–120/min
30 compressions → 2 breaths without advanced airway
10–12 breaths/minute with advanced airway
High-quality chest compressions: 10–20 mm Hg ETCO2
Factors that worsen CPR: compression interruption, excessive ventilation, poor technique
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه أكتر عامل بيأثر على النجاة في cardiac arrest خارج المستشفى هو CPR عالي الجودة، وخصوصاً الضغطات على الصدر. الـ AHA بتذكر خمسة عناصر أساسية: تقليل انقطاع الضغطات، وسرعة مناسبة، وعمق كافي، وعدم ميلان الجسم بين الضغطات، وعدم تنفس زيادة. أما الـ antidysrhythmic drugs فما أثبتت فائدة طويلة الأمد، و epinephrine فايدته بسيطة وقصيرة، وتأمين airway دائم ما حسن النجاة لأن الـ intubation بيقطع الضغطات، فبينصحوا بـ supraglottic airway أو bag-mask لحد ما يرجع النبض.
الفخ: أكثر خطأ هو اختيار epinephrine أو establishment of a definitive airway. هاد الاثنين ما أثبتوا تحسين النجاة قبل المستشفى، وأقوى عامل هو جودة الضغطات. فلا تخلّي الـ intubation يوقف الضغطات، وابتعد عن التنفس الزايد.

question: Which of the following congenital disorders results in a cyanotic child?
englishExplanation:
Cyanotic heart disease results from either right-to-left shunting of desaturated blood flowing into the systemic circulation or from decreased pulmonary blood flow. Tetralogy of Fallot is the classic CHD, but this group also includes truncus arteriosus, dextroposition (or transposition) of the great arteries, tricuspid atresia, and total anomalous pulmonary venous return. Most of these disorders are identified when patients are still in the nursery. The abnormalities seen in Tetralogy of Fallot include right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, over-riding aorta, ventricular septal defect (VSD), and right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH). An easy mnemonic to remember this is "PROVe" (Pulmonary stenosis, RVH, Overriding aorta, and VSD).

Patients typically present with cyanosis that is worse during feeding and crying. They often have poor feeding and in older children, they may squat to relieve symptoms. Patients may experience “tet spells” characterized by acute respiratory distress due to increased right outflow tract obstruction. Patients with severe right ventricular outflow obstruction may present early after birth with profound cyanosis requiring reopening of the patent ductus arteriosus. Patients will have a systolic ejection murmur along the left sternal border. Chest radiography typically shows the classic boot-shaped heart. Cyanosis can be recreated by any Valsalva maneuver, as this results in an increase in the right-to-left shunt across the VSD. Definitive treatment is surgical correction.



Atrial septal defect (A), coarctation of aorta (B), and ventricular septal defect (D) are all noncyanotic lesions.

One Step Further
Question:
What drug can be administered to reopen a recently closed ductus arteriosus?

Reveal Answer:
Prostaglandin E1.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Tetralogy of Fallot

Most common cyanotic congenital heart disease in childhood
History: episodes of cyanosis (tet spells) and squatting for relief (decreases R ➔ L shunt, increases oxygenation)
Echocardiogram: pulmonic stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy, overriding aorta, and VSD
CXR: boot-shaped heart
Mnemonic: PROVe: pulmonic stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy, overriding aorta, VSD
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه Tetralogy of Fallot هي أشهر أمراض القلب congenital اللي بتسبب زراق عند الطفل، وهي بتجمع أربع تشوهات: RV outflow tract obstruction و overriding aorta و ventricular septal defect و right ventricular hypertrophy، وبتحفظهم بـ mnemonic اسمه PROVe. عادةً الطفل بيظهر معاه زراق بيزيد وقت الرضاعة والبكاء، وفيه poor feeding، و squatting لما يكبر عشان يخفف الأعراض، وممكن تجيه tet spells مع ضيق تنفس حاد. وفيه systolic ejection murmur على الـ left sternal border، والـ CXR بتبين قلب بشكل الحذاء.
الفخ: الخيار D يعني VSD بس لحاله، وهاد مش زراقي لأنه بيعمل shunt من اليسار لليمين. و ASD و coarctation of the aorta برضو ما بيسببوا زراق لحالهم. الزراق بيحصل لما يصير shunt من اليمين لليسار أو ينقص الدم للرئتين.

question: Which of the following is the most common physical finding in patients with infective endocarditis?
englishExplanation:
Infective endocarditis occurs when pathogens introduced to the systemic circulation invade the endocardial surface of the heart, including the heart valves. Staphylococcal and streptococcal bacteria are the most common culprits.

The clinical signs and symptoms of endocarditis are varied. Symptoms include fever, chills, dyspnea, weakness, nausea, vomiting, cough, and chest pain. Regarding physical findings, fever is the most common abnormality seen in 90% of patients. Most patients with endocarditis will have a heart murmur (85%). Approximately half of patients with endocarditis develop embolic phenomena, where septic microemboli break off and lodge in downstream tissues. Characteristic skin findings, such as Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, and splinter hemorrhages, are somewhat less common.

The treatment of infective endocarditis involves antibiotic therapy targeted to the suspected pathogen and stabilization of any hemodynamic instability.



Janeway lesions (B), nontender erythematous lesions on the extremities, are seen in 10% of patients with endocarditis.

Osler nodes (C), tender lesions on the pads of the fingers, are seen in 10–23% of patients with endocarditis.

Retinal lesions, such as Roth spots (D), are seen in 2–10% of patients with endocarditis. Roth spots are hemorrhagic lesions with pale centers found on the retina.

Splinter hemorrhages (E), linear lines under the nail bed, are seen in 15% of patients.

One Step Further
Question:
Which gram-negative organisms that are difficult to culture can cause endocarditis?

Reveal Answer:
Haemophilus, Actinobacillus, Cardiobacterium, Eikenella, and Kingella, known as the HACEK group.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Bacterial Endocarditis

Risk factors: injection drug use, valvular heart disease
Sx & syndromes:
Mild and nonspecific febrile illness - fever, rash, cough, and myalgias
Acute heart failure
Focal neurological deficit from septic cerebral embolus
Altered mental status
Axial spine pain from osteomyelitis
Pneumonia from septic pulmonary emboli
PE: fever, Roth spots, Osler nodes, murmur, Janeway lesions, anemia, nailbed hemorrhages, emboli (FROM JANE)
Dx: echocardiography and Duke criteria
Most commonly caused by:
IVDA: Staphylococcus aureus, tricuspid
Native valve: Staphylococcus aureus, viridans streptococci (most common in previously diseased), mitral
GI malignancy: Streptococcus gallolyticus (formerly S. bovis)
Tx: antibiotics
Dental prophylaxis indicated in some cases
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه أكثر فحص سريري شائع عند مرضى infective endocarditis هو الـ heart murmur، وبيظهر عند حوالي 85% منهم، بينما الـ fever هي أكثر شذوذ شائع عند 90%. أما علامات الجلد زي Osler nodes و Janeway lesions و Roth spots و splinter hemorrhages فأقل شيوعاً. واللي بيحصل عند حوالي نص المرضى هو явيات embolic من الميكروبات السامة.
الفخ: أكثر خطأ هو اختيار Osler nodes أو Janeway lesions لأنهم بيبدوا كلاسيكي ومرتبطين بالـ endocarditis. الحقيقة إن الـ murmur أكثر شيوعاً بكثير، و Osler nodes مؤلمة في بطن الأصابع بينما Janeway lesions غير مؤلمة بالأطراف، وكلهم نادرين.

question: A patient presents with a holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border. Which of the following best explains this exam finding?
englishExplanation:
Murmurs are often discovered incidentally during routine examination in the ED. Sometimes they are deliberately explored through investigation of presenting symptoms. Regardless of their discovery, a murmur should be further evaluated if it is diastolic in nature, associated with chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, stroke signs or symptoms, or fever, or is a new systolic murmur with symptoms at rest. Emergency echocardiography is indicated in these instances. Additionally, patients with a new murmur and an abnormal electrocardiogram or chest X-ray should have an echocardiogram performed.

Transesophageal echocardiography is the most sensitive for detecting right-sided valvular defects. Tricuspid regurgitation may be normal or pathologic. Pathologic tricuspid regurgitation usually results from increased right heart pressure due to valvular incompetence and backflow of blood from strains on the natural pressure gradient within the cardiovascular system. Conditions that may result in increased right heart pressure include volume overload states such as pulmonary hypertension, atrial septal defects, pulmonary emboli, and chronic lung disease.

Signs of right heart failure (e.g., jugular venous distension, hepato- or splenomegaly, peripheral edema) or sepsis may be present depending on the etiology of the valvular deficiency. Tricuspid regurgitation sounds like a soft, blowing holosystolic murmur heard best at the left lower sternal border and increases with inspiration.

Treatment is aimed at the underlying cause (e.g., antibiotics for endocarditis, anticoagulation for pulmonary embolus). Severe tricuspid regurgitation may necessitate valve replacement.



Mitral regurgitation (A)is best heard at the cardiac apex near the left fifth intercostal space in the midclavicular line, radiates to the axilla, and sounds like a high-pitched holosystolic murmur.

Pulmonic stenosis (B) presents with a harsh systolic murmur heard at the left upper sternal border in the second intercostal space.

Tricuspid stenosis (D) creates a crescendo-decrescendo diastolic murmur preceded by an opening snap and is best heard in the left lower sternal border.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most likely cause of acute-onset symptomatic tricuspid disease?

Reveal Answer:
Bacterial endocarditis.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Tricuspid Regurgitation

Causes: tricuspid ring stretching from RV dilation > pulmonary hypertension, endocarditis, rheumatic heart disease
PE: signs of right-sided heart failure (ascites, fatigue, LE edema), JVD
Holosystolic murmur best heard at the left sternal border that becomes louder during inspiration
Dx: echocardiogram
Complication: atrial fibrillation
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ murmur عند الـ left lower sternal border وهو holosystolic، وهاد هو الشكل الكلاسيكي لـ tricuspid regurgitation اللي صوتها soft و blowing. الـ TR ممكن طبيعي أو مرضي، والمرضي بيصير بسبب ارتفاع ضغط القلب الأيمن مثل pulmonary hypertension أو atrial septal defect أو pulmonary emboli أو مرض رئوي مزمن. ولأن الصمام على اليمين، فالـ Transesophageal echocardiography هو الأدق لكشف عيوب الصمامات على اليمين.
الفخ: mitral regurgitation هو الفخ لأنه برضو holosystolic، بس أقوى عند الـ apex وبيشع للـ axilla، مو عند الـ left lower sternal border. وبدون سبب واضح ل increased right heart pressure، هاد الـ murmur ممكن يكون TR طبيعي.

question: A 66-year-old man presents to the ED in respiratory distress. The patient is unable to have a conversation as he is gasping for breaths. He has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes. In the ED, his vital signs are BP 150/92 mm Hg, HR 112 bpm, RR 24/min, and SpO2 92% on room air. On physical exam, the patient is in moderate distress, crackles are auscultated bilaterally halfway up the lung fields, 3+ pitting edema is appreciated bilaterally, and the patient is coughing frothy sputum. An ECG is performed that shows sinus tachycardia. A chest X-ray demonstrates an enlarged cardiac silhouette with bilateral interstitial infiltrates. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Acute congestive heart failure with pulmonary edema

correctAnswer: Acute congestive heart failure with pulmonary edema
englishExplanation:
This patient presents with classic signs of acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) and pulmonary edema, including dyspnea, tachycardia, hypertension, bilateral lung crackles, peripheral edema, and pink, frothy sputum. Pulmonary edema occurs due to elevated left ventricular filling pressures leading to fluid extravasation into the alveolar spaces. Risk factors for developing acute congestive heart failure (CHF) exacerbation include a history of hypertension, diabetes, ischemic heart disease, and noncompliance with medications or dietary restrictions.

The pathophysiology of acute pulmonary edema in CHF involves left ventricular dysfunction, which increases left atrial pressure and leads to pulmonary venous congestion. This congestion raises hydrostatic pressure, causing transudation of fluid into the interstitial and alveolar spaces, impairing gas exchange and leading to hypoxia. Chest X-ray findings of cardiomegaly, bilateral interstitial infiltrates, and pulmonary vascular congestion further support the diagnosis. In the emergency department, initial treatment includes noninvasive positive pressure ventilation to improve oxygenation, diuretics such as furosemide to reduce volume overload, and vasodilators like nitroglycerin for preload and afterload reduction in hypertensive patients.



While acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) (B) can present with respiratory distress and bilateral infiltrates, it typically occurs in the setting of sepsis, trauma, or aspiration and is characterized by a noncardiogenic cause of pulmonary edema. This patient’s history of hypertension, signs of volume overload (pitting edema), and cardiomegaly on chest X-ray suggest a cardiac etiology rather than ARDS.

Pneumonia (C) can cause dyspnea, cough, and infiltrates on chest X-ray, but it is usually associated with fever, focal lung findings, and leukocytosis. This patient lacks fever and has signs of volume overload (peripheral edema, cardiomegaly), making pneumonia less likely.

Pulmonary embolism (PE) (D) can cause acute dyspnea, tachycardia, and hypoxia, but it is usually associated with pleuritic chest pain and an absence of significant volume overload findings. The bilateral pulmonary edema seen on chest X-ray is not a common feature of PE, which more typically presents with clear lung fields or focal infarcts. Moreover, the presence of hypertension rather than hypotension makes massive PE less likely.

One Step Further
Question:
What are the classic chest X-ray findings in heart failure?

Reveal Answer:
Kerley B lines and cephalization of flow.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Decompensated Heart Failure

Sx: exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea
PE: crackles, pitting edema, S3 heart sound
Labs: ↑ BNP
CXR: cardiomegaly, cephalization, Kerley B lines, effusions
Dx: ECHO (most useful study)
Tx
NIPPV: ↑ oxygenation, ↓ work of breathing, ↓ preload, afterload
Nitroglycerin: ↓ preload, afterload
Furosemide: diuresis
Hypotension without signs of shock: dobutamine (but may worsen hypotension)
Severe hypotension with signs of shock: norepinephrine (↑ systemic vascular resistance, ↑ HR, ↑ BP, ↑ myocardial oxygen demand)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه هاد المريض عنده acute decompensated heart failure مع pulmonary edema، وعنده كل العلامات الكلاسيكية: ضيق نفس، tachycardia، ضغط مرتفع، crackles بالجانبين، وذمة محيطية مع sputum وردي رغوي. السبب إن ضغط امتلاء البطين الأيسر ارتفع، فالسائل طلع من الأوعية الرملية للج interstitial والـ alveolar spaces، وهاد بيخرب تبادل الغازات ويسبب hypoxia. لخطر أعلى عند من عنده hypertension و diabetes و ischemic heart disease ومع عدم التزامه بالأدوية، والـ CXR بتبين cardiomegaly مع bilateral interstitial infiltrates، والعلاج بيبدأ بـ non-invasive positive pressure ventilation و furosemide و nitroglycerin.
الفخ: ARDS و pneumonia و pulmonary embolism هادوا الفخ لأنهم برضو بيسببوا ضيق نفس و crackles. بس عنا cardiomegaly و sputum وردي رغوي وذمة محيطية وضغط مرتفع، وهاد كله يميل لـ acute CHF. الـ PE ما بيسبب sputum رغوي.

question: What is the most common presentation in patients who are diagnosed with an abdominal aortic aneurysm?
englishExplanation:
Most abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are picked up incidentally on physical examination or imaging studies, such as ultrasound or CT scan, that are being done for other reasons. These patients are usually asymptomatic. It is estimated that up to 3% of men older than 50 years of age have an occult AAA. Most aneurysms > 5 cm can be palpated. However, few are associated with an audible bruit. The risk of rupture for AAAs < 4 cm is minimal. However, once the diameter is > 5–5.5 cm, the risk of rupture increases, and consultation with a vascular surgeon is warranted. The greatest risk of rupture is seen in rapidly expanding AAAs. The classic triad of a ruptured AAA is pain, hypotension, and a palpable pulsatile abdominal mass. The associated pain is usually in the abdomen, back, or flank and can mimic other common conditions such as renal colic, constipation, and musculoskeletal back pain. Bleeding from rupture is typically retroperitoneal. The diagnosis can be made by bedside ultrasound, which has a high sensitivity for detecting AAAs. However, ultrasound poorly detects rupture due to bleeding into the retroperitoneum. A CT scan is highly sensitive for detecting AAAs and is the test of choice in hemodynamically stable patients.



Back pain (B), particularly dull low-back pain that radiates into the legs; flank pain (C), usually on the left side that radiates into the groin; and hypotension (D) are associated with AAA rupture.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the first main branch off the aorta distal to the arch?

Reveal Answer:
Celiac artery.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA)

Risk factors: male sex, older age, smoking, HTN
Sx: often asymptomatic but may present with abdominal pain
PE: pulsatile abdominal mass
If ruptured: hypotension
If arteriovenous fistula formation: abdominal bruit, signs of fluid overload and heart failure
Dx: U/S (consider CT if symptomatic and hemodynamically stable)
Tx
Monitor progression (Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines)
4.0–4.9 cm: U/S annually
5.0–5.4 cm: U/S every 6 months
Can also use CT or MRI (MRI is preferred over time due to less radiation)
Surgical repair indicated for
Symptomatic aneurysms
Asymptomatic aneurysms with a diameter ≥ 5.5 cm (some sources consider the threshold ≥ 5 cm in female patients) or with a rapid rate of expansion
The USPSTF recommends one-time screening for AAA by ultrasonography in men aged 65–75 who have ever smoked
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه أغلب الـ abdominal aortic aneurysms بنكتشفوا بالصدفة وقت فحص سريري أو imaging لسبب تاني، وهاد مرضى غالباً بدون أي أعراض. بيقدر إن 3% من الرجال فوق 50 سنة عندهم AAA مخفي، واللي أكبر من 5 cm ممكن تحسه باللمس، وقلة فيهم عندهم bruit مسموع. خطر التمزق شبه معدوم تحت 4 cm لكنه بيرتفع فوق 5-5.5 cm وهيك لازم استشارة vascular surgeon، والتمزق عنده triad كلاسيكية: pain و hypotension و كتلة بطنية نابضة.
الفخ: الخيارات B و C و D بتوصف التمزق مو الشكل الأكثر شيوعاً وقت التشخيص. الـ back pain غالباً dull منخفض في الظهر بينزل للرجلين، والـ flank pain غالباً باليسار بينزل للـ groin. لو طلع الـ triad كلو مع بعض فهاد تمزق.

question: Which of the following is a cause of torsades de pointes?

options.text: Drugs that shorten the QT interval

englishExplanation:
Torsades de pointes may be caused by electrolyte disturbances (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hypocalcemia), antidysrhythmic drugs that prolong the QT interval (procainamide, quinidine, disopyramide), N-acetyl procainamide, droperidol, amiodarone, phenothiazines, haloperidol, tricyclic antidepressants, terfenadine, astemizole, ketoconazole, erythromycin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Torsades de pointes is also associated with hereditary long QT interval syndromes.

It is a form of ventricular tachycardia manifested by episodes of alternating electrical polarity, with the amplitude of the QRS complex twisting around an isoelectric baseline resembling a spindle. The rhythm usually starts with a premature ventricular contraction and is preceded by a widening of the QT interval. Treatment involves intravenous infusion of magnesium sulfate and defibrillation.



Drugs that prolong the QT interval, not those that shorten the QT interval (A), can lead to torsades de pointes.

Hypokalemia, not hyperkalemia (B), leads to torsades de pointes.

Hypomagnesemia, not hypermagnesemia (C), can lead to torsades de pointes.

Cocaine and high-dose methadone, not marijuana (E), are a cause of torsades de pointes.

One Step Further
Question:
What can be used to treat hemodynamically stable torsades de pointes that is refractory to magnesium?

Reveal Answer:
Transvenous overdrive pacing.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Torsades de Pointes

ECG: polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with QT prolongation and QRS complex twisting around the isoelectric line
Most commonly caused by acquired or congenital long QT interval syndrome
Treatment
Unstable: immediate defibrillation
Stable: intravenous magnesium sulfate and discontinuation of the offending drug
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه torsades de pointes سببو اختلالات الأملاح، وأهمها hypocalcemia مع hypokalemia و hypomagnesemia، أو أدوية بتطول الـ QT interval، أو متلازمة QT الطويل الوراثية. وهي ventricular tachycardia تبين QRS complexes بتلف حول خط الـ isoelectric بشكل spindle، وبتبدأ عادة بـ premature ventricular contraction بعد ما يطول الـ QT. العلاج هو magnesium sulfate وريدي مع defibrillation.
الفخ: الخيارات A و B و C و E كلها معكوسة للصح. اللي بيسبب torsades هو hypokalemia و hypomagnesemia و hypocalcemia مو الـ hyper منها، والأدوية اللي بتطول QT مو اللي بتقصّره. وكمان السبب الحقيقي هو cocaine و high-dose methadone مو marijuana.

question: A 19-year-old man presents to the ED with headaches, leg fatigue, and exertional dyspnea. On examination, his blood pressure is 170/90 mm Hg in both arms but 110/70 mm Hg in both legs. Femoral pulses are weak compared to the brachial pulses. A systolic murmur is auscultated over the left upper back. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
This patient has coarctation of the aorta, a congenital narrowing of the aortic lumen, most commonly located just distal to the left subclavian artery near the ligamentum arteriosum. This results in elevated blood pressure in the upper extremities and decreased perfusion to the lower extremities. Patients often present with secondary hypertension, exertional fatigue, claudication, and diminished femoral pulses. A systolic murmur or continuous murmur may be heard over the left scapular region due to collateral circulation. If undiagnosed, complications such as heart failure, aortic rupture, or intracranial hemorrhage due to associated aneurysms (e.g., berry aneurysms) can occur.

In the emergency department, diagnosis is suspected based on clinical findings and confirmed with imaging. A chest X-ray may show rib notching due to collateral vessel formation and the classic “3 sign” representing aortic narrowing with post-stenotic dilation. A CT angiogram or echocardiography with Doppler can provide definitive confirmation. Management depends on the severity and stability of the patient. Hypertension should be treated with intravenous agents such as esmolol or nicardipine. Definitive management includes surgical repair or balloon angioplasty with stenting. In critically ill neonates with severe coarctation of the aorta, prostaglandin E1 infusion may be necessary to maintain ductal patency and systemic perfusion.



Although aortic dissection (A) can present with hypertension, it typically causes severe chest or back pain described as tearing in nature. Furthermore, coarctation of the aorta is a congenital condition often diagnosed in young patients, whereas aortic dissection is more common in older individuals with hypertension, connective tissue disorders, or atherosclerosis.

Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) (C) typically presents with a continuous “machinery” murmur heard best at the left infraclavicular area, not a systolic murmur over the back. Additionally, PDA is more likely to cause volume overload and symptoms of heart failure rather than hypertension with pulse differentials.

While the patient presents with hypertension, primary hypertension (D) typically occurs without significant differences in upper and lower extremity pressures. The presence of weak femoral pulses and differential blood pressure strongly suggest a secondary cause of hypertension, such as coarctation of the aorta.

Takayasu arteritis (E) affects large arteries, including the aorta, but it typically presents with systemic symptoms like fever, weight loss, and night sweats, along with vascular symptoms such as limb claudication or diminished pulses. The murmur over the left scapula and rib notching on imaging are more characteristic of coarctation of the aorta.

One Step Further
Question:
What valvular abnormality is often found in patients with coarctation of the aorta?

Reveal Answer:
Bicuspid aortic valve.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Coarctation of the Aorta

Narrowing of descending aorta
Critical coarctation of the aorta: neonate, presents before 2 weeks when PDA closes with poor feeding, absent femoral pulses
Sx: headaches, dyspnea, leg claudication
PE: higher blood pressure in the arms than the legs, delayed femoral pulse
ECG: LVH
CXR: notching of ribs, three sign (indentation of aorta)
Dx: echocardiogram
Tx: prostaglandin E1 infusion to keep PDA open (neonate, critical coarctation), balloon angioplasty with stent placement or surgical correction
Associated with Turner syndrome, bicuspid aortic valve, and intracranial aneurysms
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الفرق الكبير بين ضغط الذراعين والساقين مع ضعف الـ femoral pulses يبين coarctation of the aorta، وهي تضيق خلقي في الـ aortic lumen غالباً بعد الـ left subclavian artery قرب الـ ligamentum arteriosum. لهيك بنشوف secondary hypertension وتعب مع المجهود و claudication، والـ murmur يطلع فوق الكتف الأيسر بسبب الـ collateral circulation، والـ CXR بتبين rib notching و علامة الـ 3. العلاج النهائي هو surgical repair أو balloon angioplasty مع stenting، والـ hypertension بتعالج بالـ esmolol أو nicardipine.
الفخ: primary hypertension أو aortic dissection هادوا الفخ لأنهم برضو بيسببوا صداع وضغط عالي. الفرق إن عند coarctation الضغط بين الذراعين والساقين مختلف والـ femoral pulses ضعيفة، وهاد ما بيحصل مع primary hypertension.

question: Which of the following best describes the finding seen in the ECG above?
englishExplanation:
Bundle branch blocks are abnormal conduction abnormalities (not rhythm disturbances) in which the ventricles depolarize in sequence rather than simultaneously, thus producing a wide QRS complex (> 120 msec) and an ST segment with a slope opposite that of the terminal half of the QRS complex. A left bundle branch block is a bifascicular block in which ventricular activation is by way of the right bundle branch. The impulse travels down the right bundle, activating the septum and the free wall of the right ventricle, and then continues on in the same direction to activate the free wall of the left ventricle. Because the dominant forces are traveling in the same direction, there is a tendency toward monophasic QRS complexes. The ECG in an LBBB will show a large wide R wave in lead I and a negative wave (QS or rS) in lead V1.



Atrioventricular block (A) produces PR interval lengthening, not R-R’ complexes.

The ECG in a right bundle branch block (C) will show a wide S wave in lead I and an RSR’ pattern in lead V1.

Sinoatrial block (D) is represented electrocardiographically by a missed cycle or beat within otherwise normal appearing P waves and QRS complexes.

One Step Further
Question:
List some causes of left bundle branch block?

Reveal Answer:
Fibrosis of the conduction system, chronic hypertension, chronic cardiac ischemia, chronic congestive heart disease, and valvular disease.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Left Bundle Branch Block (LBBB)

Prevalence increases with age
Associated with acute myocardial insults
ECG findings
Wide QRS > 0.12 sec
Broad, slurred R in I, aVL, V5, and V6
Absent Q waves in I, V5, and V6
ST and T waves opposite direction to QRS
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ left bundle branch block هو اختلال توصيل مو اختلال نظم، لأن البطينات بتستقطب بشكل متسلسل مو مع بعض، فبيطلع QRS عريض فوق 120 msec مع ST segment ميله عكس نهاية الـ QRS. وفيه التنشيط بيصير عن طريق الـ right bundle branch، فالـ ECG يبين موجة R كبيرة وعريضة في lead I وموجة سالبة QS أو rS في lead V1. أما AV block و right bundle branch block و sinoatrial block فبيبدوا أشكال تانية، والـ LBBB بيسببه fibrosis نظام التوصيل مع chronic hypertension.
الفخ: right bundle branch block هو الفخ لأنه كمان wide QRS، بس يبين موجة S عريضة في lead I و RSR في V1، مو R في lead I. و AV block بيطول الـ PR interval، و sinoatrial block معناه نبضة ضايعة بين موجات P طبيعية.

question: A 30-year-old woman presents with palpitations, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea for 3 days. Her ECG is shown above. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her ECG findings?
englishExplanation:
A prolonged QT interval can be an inherited genetic disorder (long QT syndrome) or secondary to hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, myocarditis, and medications (e.g., procainamide, erythromycin, and antipsychotics).

Before puberty, the reference range for the QTc interval is similar in girls and boys. A QTc < 450 msec is considered normal, and ≥ 460 msec is prolonged. After puberty, references can vary on what is considered a prolonged QTc. Some consider the QTc prolonged at 440 msec in men and 460 msec in women, while others say that a QTc ≥ 470 msec in men and ≥ 480 msec in women is considered prolonged.

Patients may experience palpitations, chest pain, syncope, or dizziness. Patients with long QT syndrome should not participate in sports or vigorous activities. Beta-blockers may be useful in the treatment of congenital long QT syndrome, but the definitive treatment is placement of an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator.

In patients with other causes of prolonged QT syndrome, the underlying cause should be treated. Electrolyte deficiencies should be corrected, and medications that cause QT prolongation should be discontinued.



Hypercalcemia (A) and hyponatremia (D) cause a shortened QT interval on ECG. Hypercalcemia can also cause a prolonged PR interval and heart block.

Characteristic ECG findings of hyperkalemia (B) are dependent on the potassium level and include tall, peaked T waves and widened QRS complexes.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the safest medication to use in the treatment of QT prolongation-induced ventricular fibrillation?

Reveal Answer:
Lidocaine. Amiodarone and procainamide can prolong the QT interval.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Prolonged QT Syndrome

Presentation: syncope, seizure, palpitations
ECG: QT interval prolonged for age and sex
Prepubertal: QT interval > 460 msec
Men: QT interval > 440 msec
Women: QT interval > 460 msec
More commonly caused by medications > familial prolongation, low magnesium, potassium, calcium
Romano-Ward is most common inherited long QT syndrome (autosomal dominant)
Treatment
Congenital: beta-blocker, cardiology consult, consider genetic testing and counseling
Acquired: stop offending medications, correct electrolyte disturbances, give IV magnesium or pacing for torsades de pointes
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه المريضة عندها QT interval مطول بسبب نقص الأملاح، ومع الـ nausea و vomiting و diarrhea لمدة 3 أيام فقدت magnesium و potassium. الـ prolonged QT ممكن يكون وراثي أو ثانوي بسبب hypocalcemia و hypokalemia و hypomagnesemia أو myocarditis أو أدوية مثل procainamide و erythromycin و antipsychotics. والمعيار إن QTc فوق 460 msec يعتبر مطول، والعلاج هو تصحيح نقص الأملاح وإيقاف الأدوية اللي بتطول الـ QT.
الفخ: hypercalcemia و hyponatremia بيسببوا QT قصير مو مطول، فليست سبب. و hyperkalemia له ECG findings خاصة حسب مستوى البوتاسيوم، مو QT مطول. انتبه إن الـ vomiting و diarrhea عندها هي السبب بنقص الأملاح.

question: A 35-year-old man presents to the emergency department after an episode of near syncope while working as a landscaper. He has no significant medical history and does not smoke or drink alcohol. Physical exam is notable for flushed skin with clothing that is saturated with sweat. The patient is eating well and states he feels alright. The patient’s heart rate is 90 bpm after 2 L of normal saline, and he states he feels better. An ECG is subsequently performed and reveals normal sinus rhythm with no ST or T wave changes other than a single premature ventricular contraction. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
englishExplanation:
Premature ventricular contractions occur secondary to pacemaker cells that are in the conducting system that can spontaneously depolarize. Typically, these pacemaker cells are suppressed by electrical activity that is occurring at a faster rate from the upstream pacemaker cells. However, if an ectopic focus depolarizes prior to the arrival of the next sinus impulse, it can produce a premature ventricular contraction. These premature contractions are classified as atrial, junctional, or ventricular. If the focus is the ventricle, a premature ventricular contraction occurs, which can lead to asynchronous activation of the ventricles, which presents on ECG with QRS complexes with a prolonged duration and abnormal morphology. Premature ventricular contractions are a normal electrophysiological variant that typically do not require further workup or treatment. Potential etiologies of premature ventricular contractions include anxiety, medications, illicit drugs, caffeine, electrolyte derangements, and myocardial ischemia. If the patient has a history concerning for myocardial ischemia, further cardiac workup should be performed.



Cardiac catheterization (A) would be indicated in a patient presenting with new-onset chest pain with ST elevation on ECG. It would not be indicated for a premature ventricular contraction with no other symptoms supporting cardiac ischemia.

Cardiac stress testing (B) is typically indicated in uncertain cases of chest pain in a patient with risk factors such as diabetes and hypertension. If a patient has a normal workup including a normal ECG and troponins, stress testing may be ordered to attempt to provoke myocardial ischemia with exertion in order to unmask the most likely diagnosis and inform further management (such as cardiac catheterization).

Cardiac troponins (C) are typically indicated for a patient presenting with a chief concern of chest pain for whom it is important to rule out an ST elevation myocardial infarction or non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. This patient’s premature ventricular contractions in the setting of dehydration make an ischemic etiology an unlikely cause of his presentation.

One Step Further
Question:
Should cardiac stress testing be performed in Wellens syndrome?

Reveal Answer:
No, it is an electrocardiographic manifestation of severe proximal left anterior descending coronary artery stenosis, and the patient should not exert themselves.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Premature Ventricular Contractions (PVCs)

Early beats originating from the ventricular myocardium
Often wider-than-normal QRS duration with atypical morphology
No preceding P wave
Deflection of the ST segment and T wave is opposite that of the QRS
Often followed by a compensatory pause
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ ECG يبين sinus rhythm طبيعي مع premature ventricular contraction وحدة، وهاد غالباً variant كهربائي طبيعي ما بيحتاج عمل أو علاج. بيصير لأن focus من pacemaker cells في نظام التوصيل يستقطب قبل ما يوصله الـ sinus impulse التالي، وبيظهر على الـ ECG كـ QRS مطول بشكل غير طبيعي. الأسباب بتشمل anxiety و medications و اختلال الأملاح، بس ما في تاريخ ولا أعراض بتشير لـ ischemia. فـ cardiac catheterization و cardiac stress test و cardiac troponins مو لازمين، وأفضل خطوة هي discharge مع outpatient follow-up.
الفخ: أكثر خطأ هو طلب cardiac troponins أو cardiac stress test أو cardiac catheterization لأن الـ PVC بتوهمك إن في ischemia. لا، الـ PVC لحالها ما بتشير لـ ischemia، والـ troponins بتطلب فقط عند ألم صدر جديد مع ST elevation.

question: An 80-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by EMS after being found unresponsive in his yard by a neighbor. He has no palpable pulse and his rhythm strip is shown above. Which of the following medications should be administered first?
englishExplanation:
This patient is in cardiac arrest with a rhythm of monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia. There are no identifiable P waves and the QRS complexes are wide (> 0.16 msec), suggesting that this is most likely ventricular in origin. Advanced Cardiac Life Support algorithms propose that for the management of pulseless ventricular tachycardia, early defibrillation, chest compressions at a rate of 100 bpm, and administration of epinephrine 1 mg IV every 3–5 minutes are indicated as needed until the return of spontaneous circulation is established or until resuscitative efforts are deemed unsuccessful. Wide-complex tachycardia may be ventricular in origin, resulting in monomorphic, polymorphic (e.g., torsades de pointed), or bidirectional (e.g., digoxin toxicity) waveforms. It may also be supraventricular with aberrancy, indicating a conduction abnormality such as a bundle branch block, or it may be associated with a pre-excitation syndrome such as Wolff-Parkinson-White. If unsure whether the rhythm is ventricular or supraventricular in nature, treat it as if it is ventricular, especially if the patient is hemodynamically unstable.



Adenosine (A) is an endogenous nucleoside that inhibits adenylate cyclase and is used diagnostically and therapeutically for narrow-complex supraventricular tachycardia and is not efficacious for wide-complex tachycardia during cardiac arrest.

Amiodarone (B) is a class III antidysrhythmic that may be administered in patients with stable supraventricular tachycardia. It may also be administered during cardiac arrest resuscitation for initial rhythms of ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia, but this should only be given after one dose of epinephrine has been administered and defibrillation has been attempted.

Procainamide (D) may be given for stable wide-complex tachycardia or for stable dysrhythmias associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White.

One Step Further
Question:
Defibrillation is indicated for what cardiac dysrhythmias?

Reveal Answer:
Ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Ventricular Tachycardia

More than three consecutive ectopic ventricular beats
Monomorphic, polymorphic
Wide complexes
Bidirectional: digoxin toxicity
Brugada criteria can help differentiate ventricular tachycardia and supraventricular tachycardia with aberrancy
If unsure about the rhythm, manage all wide complex tachycardias as ventricular tachycardia
Tx
Pulseless: immediate defibrillation
Unstable: synchronized cardioversion
Stable: procainamide, amiodarone, synchronized cardioversion (especially if refractory)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه هاد المريض arrest والـ rhythm strip يبين monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia بدون موجات P، والـ QRS عريض فوق 0.16 ثانية، فهاد غالباً ventricular. حسب خوارزميات ACLS، لازم early defibrillation مع ضغطات بسرعة 100 بالدقيقة و epinephrine 1 mg IV كل 3-5 دقائق لحد ما يرجع ROSC. و wide-complex tachycardia ممكن تكون supraventricular مع aberrancy أو pre-excitation زي Wolff-Parkinson-White، فلما نكون مش متأكدين لازم نعالجها كأنها ventricular خاصة إذا المريض غير مستقر، و Adenosine ما بتنفع هنا.
الفخ: Adenosine هي الفخ لأنها بتنفع بس مع narrow-complex SVT، ومبينفعش مع wide-complex tachycardia أثناء arrest. وبما إنها بتاخد وقت، بتاخد من فرصك الـ defibrillation. القاعدة: إذا ما متأكد ventricular ولا supraventricular، عامله كـ ventricular.

question: A 12-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with palpitations and a high heart rate. She has had similar symptoms previously and is sure she is having the same event again. Vital signs show HR 192 bpm, BP 114/68 mm Hg, RR 12/min, and T 37.6℃. Her physical examination is otherwise unremarkable. As you are awaiting completion of the electrocardiogram, you start to think about your medication options to treat this patient. What medication is likely to be the clinician’s first-line agent for the treatment of this patient’s disorder?
englishExplanation:
Although you do not have an electrocardiogram for confirmation, this pediatric patient is most likely presenting with an atrial tachydysrhythmia. A heart rate of > 180 bpm in a child is likely supraventricular tachycardia (SVT). Supraventricular tachycardia is the most common rhythm disturbance in children. The first step in treating these patients is to decide whether the girl is hemodynamically stable or unstable. Unstable patients, such as those with hypotension, cardiogenic shock, or altered mental status, should undergo cardioversion immediately. This girl is stable, so additional time can be given to evaluate the rhythm, attempt vagal maneuvers, and prepare to medically treat the patient.

Adenosine (0.1 mg/kg) is the drug of choice to terminate episodes of atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia, and it is successful 80–95% of the time. Atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia can also be associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. It is important to remember that in patients with Wolff-Parkinson-White who have a wide-complex (antidromic) rhythm, adenosine can precipitate atrial fibrillation that can degrade to ventricular fibrillation, but these events are extremely rare. Patients with narrow-complex tachydysrhythmias associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White can be safely treated with adenosine.



Digoxin (B) is not routinely used for acute SVT treatment because of its delay in achieving therapeutic levels and its narrow therapeutic margin with serious toxicity.

SVT that is refractory to adenosine may respond to procainamide (C), and its use in Wolff-Parkinson-White is safe as it works by slowing conduction within the myocardium itself rather than blocking reentry at the atrioventricular node. However, this medication can have negative effects including precipitating heart block, negative inotropic effects, and prolongation of the QT interval if given too quickly. It is considered second-line therapy in children with SVT.

Verapamil (D) can be effective in older children and adults but it is not recommended due to its serious side effects including precipitating cardiovascular collapse, particularly in young children and those with preceding heart failure.

One Step Further
Question:
What are the electrocardiogram findings that suggest underlying Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome?

Reveal Answer:
A short PR interval (< 0.12 seconds), a prolonged QRS complex (> 0.12 seconds), and a delta wave or slurred upstroke of the QRS complex.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Supraventricular Tachycardia (SVT) or Paroxysmal Supraventricular Tachycardia (PSVT)

Common types include
Atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT)
Atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT)
Atrial tachycardia
Most commonly caused by a reentrant pathway in the atrioventricular node
Clinical
Infants: poor feeding, fussiness, irritability
Older children: palpitations, chest pain, fatigue
Adults: palpitations, chest pain, shortness of breath
PE: abrupt onset of tachycardia
Ventricular rate often 160–220 bpm in adults
HR > 180–220 bpm in children
HR up to 300 bpm in infants
Dx: ECG shows regular narrow complex tachycardia (P waves can be obscured at high HRs)
Stress testing or ambulatory monitoring may be needed
Tx: vagal maneuvers, drug therapy (adenosine), cardioversion
Can be associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه بنت عندها 12 سنة و pulse 192 مع palpitations، وأول شي لازم نعرفه هو إذا هي مستقرة ولا لأ. هي مستقرة، فبتاخد وقت نحلل الـ rhythm ونجرب vagal maneuvers وبعدين نعالج دوائيا. و Adenosine (0.1 mg/kg) هو drug of choice لوقف AV reentrant tachycardia، ونسبة نجاحه 80-95%. و SVT هي أكثر اضطراب نظم عند الأطفال، و pulse فوق 180 بالطفل غالباً SVT.
الفخ: أكثر خطأ هو القفز على digoxin أو verapamil لطفل مستقر. Digoxin ما بتستخدم بشكل روتيني لحالة SVT acutely لأن تأخيرها كبير، و verapamil خطر على الطفل. لازم تجرب vagal maneuvers وبعدين adenosine، و cardioversion الفورية إذا صار غير مستقر.

question: A 67-year-old woman presents with gradually worsening exertional dyspnea and lower extremity edema. She is diagnosed with constrictive pericarditis. Which of the following is the definitive treatment for this condition?
englishExplanation:
Constrictive pericarditis occurs when the normally elastic pericardium becomes thickened and fibrotic. This can occur from episodes of viral, inflammatory, or idiopathic pericarditis and can also result from radiation damage to the pericardium. In constrictive pericarditis, the normally separate and easily distensible parietal and visceral layers of the pericardium thicken and fuse, and this scarred pericardium impairs venous return to the heart, diastolic filling, and late in the course, cardiac output. Symptoms of constrictive pericarditis are similar to heart failure, especially right-sided heart failure, with dyspnea, dependent edema, and jugular venous distension. The definitive treatment for constrictive pericarditis is surgical resection of the pericardium, known as pericardiectomy.



Diuretics (A) are used in the treatment of heart failure and are ineffective in constrictive pericarditis.

NSAIDs (B) are the treatment for pericarditis caused by infection and inflammation, not constrictive pericarditis.

Pericardiocentesis (D) removes fluid from a large pericardial effusion. The issue in constrictive pericarditis is a thickened and scarred pericardium, not excess fluid.

One Step Further
Question:
What nerve overlies the pericardium and must be carefully avoided at surgery?

Reveal Answer:
Phrenic nerve.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Constrictive Pericarditis

Caused by thickening and scarring of the pericardium
Risk factors: history of viral or idiopathic pericarditis, prior radiation therapy or cardiac surgery, prior infection (e.g., tuberculosis), autoimmune conditions, malignancy
PE: increased JVP, pericardial knock, Kussmaul sign, pulsus paradoxus (rare)
Tx options (depending on whether early or chronic disease) include anti-inflammatory agents, Tx of the underlying cause, pericardiectomy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه في constrictive pericarditis الـ pericardium اللي كان مرنبقى سميك وفيبروز ويلتحم، فبيمنع الرجوع الوريدي للقلب والملء diastolic وبعدين بيأثر على الـ cardiac output. والأعراض بتطلع على شكل failure من ناحية اليمين: dyspnea وذمة معتمدة و distension في الـ jugular veins. والعلاج الحاسم هو استئصال الـ pericardium جراحيا وبيسمى pericardiectomy، أما الـ diuretics فبتعالج heart failure وما بتنفع هون، و NSAIDs للـ pericarditis الالتهابي، و pericardiocentesis لسحب سائل effusion كبير مو لتضخيم.
الفخ: pericardiocentesis هو الفخ لأن الناس بتخيل أي مشكلة بالـ pericardium معناها سائل. لا، المشكلة هون تضخيم وتليف مش سائل، فسحب السائل ما بيعالج المشكلة. وبنفس السبب الـ diuretics و NSAIDs ما هادو الحل.

question: A 4-year-old boy presents with apnea, hypoxia, and bradycardia. He is intubated, and several attempts at intravenous and intraosseous access are unsuccessful. Which of the following medications can be administered through the endotracheal tube while ongoing attempts to obtain vascular access are made?
englishExplanation:
While the ideal route of medication administration during resuscitation is via intravenous or intraosseous line, endotracheal administration of certain medications can be life-saving when vascular access is delayed. Medications that can be safely administered through an endotracheal tube (ETT) in pediatric patients include lidocaine, atropine, naloxone, and epinephrine. Absorption occurs across the alveolar-capillary membrane but may be impaired in states of ventilation-perfusion mismatch. Studies have also demonstrated a biphasic pattern of absorption that results in a depot effect of certain medications. Although the optimal dose is unknown, guidelines recommend using 2–2.5 times the usual dose for endotracheally administered medications. In order to achieve rapid drug absorption while minimizing pulmonary damage, medications should be diluted in distilled water or 0.9% normal saline to a total of 5 mL in pediatric patients (10 mL in adults and 1 mL in neonates). Complications related to endotracheal drug delivery include impaired gas exchange and prolonged absorption of certain medications, leading to unwanted effects after resuscitation, such as dysrhythmias from epinephrine. Despite the potential complications, endotracheal drug delivery is indicated when immediate pharmacologic intervention is required to stabilize a patient who lacks vascular access. The patient above is at imminent risk of cardiac arrest and should be given epinephrine via the ETT.



Amiodarone (A) and sodium bicarbonate (D) may have direct negative effects on the lung parenchyma and should not be delivered via ETT. Calcium chloride (B) is not effective when administered endotracheally.

question: A 44-year-old man presents in cardiac arrest. He is found to have ventricular fibrillation and is successfully defibrillated. A post-return of spontaneous circulation ECG is performed and shown above. The patient remains unresponsive. When should targeted temperature management be instituted?

options.text: After a head CT is performed
As soon as return of spontaneous circulation is achieved
Targeted temperature management should not be applied to patients with ST elevation myocardial infarction after cardiac arrest

correctAnswer: As soon as return of spontaneous circulation is achieved
englishExplanation:
Patients with cardiac arrest, no matter the rhythm or the location, should have targeted temperature management instituted immediately after the return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), and protocol initiation should not be delayed for either diagnostic studies or procedures. Targeted temperature management has been shown to improve survival and functional outcomes in prospective randomized trials. In the two major studies upon which the recommendations for therapeutic hypothermia were based, patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with an initial rhythm of ventricular fibrillation were eligible for a targeted temperature cooling protocol if they achieved ROSC. However, newer evidence indicates no significant difference in outcomes between those cooled versus those maintained at a temperature of 36–37.5°C. Thus, the 2023 guidelines recommend targeted temperature management by maintaining a temperature between 32°C and 37.5°C for at least 72 hours after cardiac arrest and attaining normothermia. Post-ROSC care should also focus on identifying and treating acute coronary syndromes or other potential causes. The ECG in the above patient shows an anterior wall myocardial infarction with ST elevations in leads V1–V5, I, aVL, and reciprocal changes in II, III, and aVF.



In patients with suspected intracranial pathology, targeted temperature management protocols should be initiated before a CT scan (A).

If cardiac catheterization (B) is indicated, it can be done while the patient is monitored for temperature rise. It is essential to avoid temperatures > 37.5°C.

Targeted temperature management protocols should be applied in patients with ST elevation myocardial infarction (D) after ROSC.

One Step Further

What ECG finding can be found in patients with severe hypothermia?

Reveal Answer:
Osborn waves or J waves, a deflection at the J point.

Inclusion criteria

Comatose
Best location for temperature probe: esophagus
Maintain temperature: 32.0–37.5°C (89.6–99.5°F)
There is insufficient evidence to recommend a specific therapeutic temperature for different subgroups of patients with cardiac arrest
Goals of care
Prevent fever
Provide comprehensive critical care
Neuroprognostication at a minimum of 72 hours after normothermia

الفخ: أكثر خطأ هو تأخير الـ TTM لحد ما يعمل head CT أو cardiac catheterization. لا، ما في داعي تستنى، فالبروتوكول يبدأ فور ROSC وبعدين-post-ROSC care بيستمر بالتوازي. وخلي بالك: ST elevation myocardial infarction ما بيلغي الـ TTM.

question: A 68-year-old man presents with dyspnea and fatigue and is found to have a cardiac tumor on bedside echocardiogram. What is the most likely etiology?
englishExplanation:
While cardiac tumors in general are very rare, metastatic disease involving the heart is over 20 times more common than primary cardiac tumors. Carcinoma can metastasize via lymphatic spread, direction extension, or hematogenous seeding. Melanomas, renal cell carcinoma, sarcomas, and leukemias are most likely to metastasize to the heart. Symptoms are often nonspecific and depend in part on the location of the mass. They can obstruct the flow of blood or heart valves resulting in symptoms of heart failure or regurgitation, embolize into pulmonary or systemic circulation, or invade the myocardium resulting in impaired function, pericardial effusion, heart blocks, or dysrhythmias.



Atrial myxomas (A)are the most common benign primary cardiac tumor and arise from the left atrium 80% of the time, with most of the remaining myxomas arising from the right atrium. They can range in size from 1 to 15 cm. Cardiovascular symptoms predominate but patients may also present with evidence of embolization, primarily to the systemic circulation, and constitutional symptoms. Myxomas are typically found in patients 30 to 60 years of age. Treatment is surgical resection.

Fibroelastomas (B) are the third most common primary tumors of the heart and most patients are over 60 years of age.

Approximately a quarter of all primary tumors of the heart are malignant, and sarcomas (D), including angiosarcomas, rhabdomyosarcomas and fibrosarcomas, are the most common. Malignant primary cardiac tumors are much less common than both metastatic disease to the heart or benign primary cardiac tumors.

One Step Further
Question:
Other than a murmur, what auscultatory finding may be present in patients with an atrial myxoma?

Reveal Answer:
A “tumor plop,” heard early in diastole.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Cardiac Tumors in Adults

Most common is benign atrial myxoma
Malignant tumors are rare and are mainly sarcomas
Metastatic disease is more common than primary malignancy
Lung cancer, melanoma, breast cancer
Sx: depends on tumor location
Dx: echo, cardiac MRI
Angiography and biopsy as needed
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه metastatic disease اللي بتوصل للقلب أكثر من 20 مرة شائعة من primary cardiac tumors، حتى مع إن tumors القلب نادرة. بتوصل عن طريق lymphatic spread أو direct extension أو hematogenous seeding، وأكثرها melanoma و renal cell carcinoma و sarcomas و leukemias، والأعراض غير نوعية وتظهر كـ heart failure أو regurgitation أو emboli أو pericardial effusion و heart block. و Atrial myxoma هو أكثر الورم الحميد الأساسي شيوعا ويبدأ من الـ left atrium بـ 80%، بينما Fibroelastoma هو الثالث شيوعا ومعظم مرضاه فوق 60 سنة.
الفخ: atrial myxoma و fibroelastoma هادوا الفخ لأنهم أشهر primary cardiac tumors، بس metastatic disease للقلب أكبر بـ 20 مرة. والـ myxoma بتنشأ من الـ left atrium عند عمر 30-60، بينما Fibroelastoma معظم مرضاه فوق 60 سنة، وهاد ما بينطبق على مريض عمره 68.

question: Nitrate infusion therapy works by which of the following mechanisms?
englishExplanation:
Nitrates work by reducing both preload and afterload. Nitroglycerin was the first treatment for angina pectoris and dates back to the 1800s. It still remains the first-line drug therapy for many patients with acute cardiac disease. Nitrates dilate veins (especially at low doses like a sublingual tab), coronary arteries, and to a lesser extent, systemic arteries by relaxing vascular smooth muscle. Thus, nitrates reduce preload by increasing venous capacitance and improve coronary blood flow by coronary vasodilatation. Decreased preload lowers left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, thereby decreasing wall stress. This causes a decrease in myocardial oxygen demand.

At higher doses that are typically used for infusion therapy, the added afterload effects cause a drop in systemic blood pressure, further decreasing wall stress and oxygen demand. Nitrates do not have a direct effect on cardiac chronotropy or inotropy. The primary adverse effects induced by nitrate therapy include hypotension, headache, and tachycardia. Nitrates should not be administered to patients with hypotension or to those who received a phosphodiesterase inhibitor in the last 24 hours. They should be administered with caution to patients with right ventricular infarction, as these patients can be preload dependent.



Nitrate infusion therapy does not work by increasing preload (A). Instead, the purpose of nitrates is to decrease the volume of blood returning to the heart, which is the opposite effect.

While reducing afterload (B) might be a component of treatment, focusing solely on this aspect overlooks other important mechanisms. Therefore, attributing the effect of nitrates exclusively to afterload reduction is incomplete.

Nitrates do not act by reducing cardiac contractility (D). Their mechanism does not involve altering the heart’s contractile strength, unlike other medications that specifically target this function.

Focusing only on reducing preload (E) with nitrates misses the broader therapeutic effects intended by their use. It is important to understand that nitrates have a more comprehensive role beyond just this single action.

One Step Further
Question:
What medication class both reduces cardiac contractility and can worsen bronchospasm?

Reveal Answer:
Beta-blockers.

Only use for severe pain refractory to nitroglycerin
Can be associated with negative outcome

Choice of specific P2Y12 inhibitor (e.g., ticagrelor, prasugrel, clopidogrel) and duration of use depends on the type of ACS, management strategy, and bleeding risk

Additional nonstatin lipid-lowering agents (e.g., ezetimibe) as needed

ليش: اللي صار إنه الـ nitrates بتقلل الـ preload والـ afterload مع بعض. هي بتوسع العروق، خصوصا بجرعات الصغيرة مثل الـ sublingual tablet، وبتوسع الـ coronary arteries، وبشكل أقل الـ systemic arteries، عن طريق ارتخاء الـ vascular smooth muscle. رفع الـ venous capacitance بيقلل الـ preload فينزل الـ LV end-diastolic pressure والـ wall stress، و بالتالي بنقص myocardial oxygen demand، وبالجرعات العالية المستخدمة بالـ infusion بينزل الـ systemic blood pressure كمان فتقل الـ wall stress أكتر.
الفخ: الخيار E يعني preload بس، والخيار B يعني afterload بس، وهاد غلط لأن الـ nitrates بتعمل الاثنين مع بعض حسب الجرعة. وهي ما إلها تأثير مباشر على الـ chronotropy أو الـ inotropy، فما بتسبب زيادة في الـ contractility.

question: A 75-year-old man presents to the ED with fatigue, melena, and dizziness for 2 days. He has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and colonoscopy performed during a recent hospitalization showed angiodysplasia of the ascending colon. Vital signs show a BP of 96/60 mm Hg, HR of 120 bpm, and RR of 20/min. Physical exam reveals conjunctival pallor and a heart murmur. ECG is shown above. Laboratory studies reveal hemoglobin of 7.9 g/dL. Which of the following cardiac valvular abnormalities is most likely present in this patient based on the overall presentation?
englishExplanation:
This patient has GI bleeding from angiodysplasia in the setting of chronic cardiovascular disease risk factors. The most likely associated valvular abnormality is aortic stenosis (AS). This relationship, known as Heyde syndrome, is due to shear stress across the stenotic valve causing degradation of high-molecular-weight von Willebrand factor multimers, predisposing to recurrent bleeding in those with intestinal angiodysplasia. Recognition is important because patients may continue to bleed until the underlying valve disease is corrected.

The most common cause of AS is calcific degeneration in patients > 65 years, though it can also occur earlier in patients with a bicuspid aortic valve or in those with rheumatic heart disease. Progressive narrowing of the valve area < 1 cm2 increases left ventricular afterload, causing hypertrophy that initially maintains output but predisposes to ischemia even without coronary artery disease. Over time, left ventricular dysfunction, atrial enlargement, atrial fibrillation, pulmonary hypertension, and right heart failure may develop. Patients with severe stenosis are preload dependent and highly vulnerable to acute decompensation when volume status or rhythm is disturbed. Severe disease is defined by peak velocity ≥ 4 m/s, mean pressure gradient ≥ 40 mm Hg, or valve area < 1 cm2, and up to one-third of patients have preserved ejection fraction.

AS often presents gradually with exertional dyspnea, angina, syncope, or heart failure, but may also decompensate abruptly with triggers like sepsis or anemia. The classic finding is a crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border radiating to the carotids, sometimes with an S4 gallop, diminished carotid pulses, or left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG (as is seen in this patient's ECG). Echocardiography is the diagnostic standard and allows staging. Asymptomatic patients may be treated medically with antihypertensives and risk factor control, but once symptoms develop, valve replacement is required since prognosis worsens rapidly. Surgical or transcatheter approaches are chosen based on surgical risk and comorbidities, with balloon valvuloplasty reserved as a temporary bridge. In the ED, treatment of acute decompensation centers on cautious fluids, correction of anemia, rhythm control, and vasopressors such as phenylephrine or norepinephrine, while avoiding aggressive diuresis, vasodilators, and inotropes unless necessary.



Aortic regurgitation (AR) (A) manifests with wide pulse pressure, bounding pulses, and a blowing diastolic murmur. Acute AR can cause pulmonary edema and shock, while chronic AR leads to left ventricular dilation and dysfunction. There is no known association with acquired von Willebrand disease or bleeding due to GI angiodysplasia.

Mitral regurgitation (MR) (C) causes a holosystolic murmur at the cardiac apex radiating to the axilla, often due to leaflet prolapse or ischemic damage. Chronic MR leads to left atrial dilation, pulmonary hypertension, and atrial fibrillation, but it is not associated with angiodysplastic GI bleeding related to acquired von Willebrand disease.

Mitral stenosis (MS) (D) is caused by rheumatic heart disease. MS produces elevated left atrial pressures, pulmonary edema, and atrial fibrillation. Its complications include pulmonary hypertension and right heart failure, not recurrent GI bleeding.

Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) (E) is commonly due to pulmonary hypertension or right-sided heart failure. TR presents with jugular venous distension, hepatomegaly, and peripheral edema. It is a volume overload condition of the right heart and does not predispose to bleeding from GI angiodysplasia.

One Step Further
Question:
Why is stress cardiac testing contraindicated in those with severe aortic stenosis?

Reveal Answer:
The fixed outflow obstruction prevents augmentation of cardiac output and can precipitate syncope, ischemia, or sudden death.

PE: crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur that radiates to the carotids, paradoxically split S2, S4 gallop
Murmur decreases with Valsalva
Most commonly caused by degenerative calcification

Anemia
Thromboembolism

arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه هاد المريض عنده نزيف من الـ angiodysplasia وعنده 75 سنة وعوامل خطر قلبية، وهاد يميل لـ aortic stenosis ضمن متلازمة Heyde. الآلية إن الـ shear stress على الصمام الضيق بيحلل الـ von Willebrand factor، فبتزيد النزيف المتكرر، ولازم نعالج الصمام وإلا النزيف بيرجع. والسبب الأكثر شيوعا هو calcific degeneration بعد 65 سنة، ويمكن يصير أبكر مع bicuspid valve أو rheumatic heart disease، ومع تضيق الصمام زاد الـ LV afterload وحدث hypertrophy، ولما تتطور المشكلة بتصير LV dysfunction و atrial fibrillation و right heart failure.
الفخ: aortic regurgitation و mitral stenosis هادوا الفخ لأنهم كلهم valves. الفرق إن Heyde syndrome بتجمع نزيف من الـ angiodysplasia مع صمام ضيق هو aortic stenosis، والـ regurgitation ما بتسبب الـ shear stress اللي بيحلل الـ von Willebrand factor.

question: A 32-year-old woman presents to the ED reporting right calf swelling for 1 week. She is 1 week postpartum, following an uneventful full-term vaginal delivery. She reports no chest pain, dyspnea, or cough. On examination, her right calf is 16 inches in circumference, and her left calf is 10 inches. Which of the following is the most accurate test to confirm the diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Duplex ultrasonography is currently the first-line imaging study to diagnose deep vein thrombosis (DVT) because of its relative ease of use, the absence of irradiation or contrast material, and a high degree of accuracy. In patients with clinically suspected disease, compression ultrasonography is 95–99% sensitive for proximal venous thrombus.



Computed tomography (A) can identify intravascular thrombi through demonstration of a filling defect with contrast enhancement. There are few studies evaluating the true sensitivity of this test, but the current studies show that it can be as sensitive as 95% in diagnosis of DVT. D-dimer (B) levels remain elevated in DVT for about seven days. Patients presenting late in the course, after clot organization and adherence have occurred, may have low levels of D-dimer. Similarly, patients with isolated calf vein DVT may have a small clot burden and low levels of D-dimer below the analytic cutoff value of the assay. This accounts for the reduced sensitivity of the D-dimer assay in the setting of confirmed DVT. In some countries, impedance plethysmography (D) has been the initial noninvasive diagnostic test of choice and has been shown to be sensitive and specific for proximal vein thrombosis. However, impedance plethysmography has several limitations, including insensitivity for calf vein thrombosis, nonoccluding proximal vein thrombus, and iliofemoral vein thrombosis above the inguinal ligament.

One Step Further
Question:
What diagnostic test has the highest sensitivity for diagnosing a deep vein thrombosis?

Reveal Answer:
Venography.

Most commonly caused by stasis, hypercoagulable state, endothelial dysfunction (Virchow triad)
Risks: smoking, immobilization, surgery, oral contraceptive use
Central line placement in upper extremity DVT

PE: extremity swelling and pain, may show a positive Homans sign
Dx: made by ultrasound, gold standard is venography
D-dimer used in low-risk cases
Pretest probability by modified Wells score

Warfarin is contraindicated in pregnancy

الفخ: D-dimer assay هو الفخ لأنه سهل وسريع، بس مستواه بضل مرتفع حوالي سبعة أيام، والـ DVT المحدود بساق بنفسه ممكن يعطيك D-dimer طبيعي. و Computed tomography بيحتاج إشعاع ومادة تباين، و impedance plethysmography ما بتكشف الـ calf vein thrombosis.

question: A 68-year-old man with a history of hypertension, chronic kidney disease, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation who is on anticoagulation presents after syncope. His spouse states that he came into their house after gardening reporting lightheadedness, and then he collapsed. She did not notice any convulsions at the time. He now reports shortness of breath and cannot tolerate sitting up due to lightheadedness. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), heart rate is 45 bpm, respirations are 24/min, blood pressure is 80/50 mm Hg, and SpO₂ is 97%. His ECG reveals a rate of 42 bpm with a junctional rhythm, a narrow QRS complex, and retrograde P waves. Which medication is most likely causing his clinical condition?
englishExplanation:
Digoxin, a cardiac glycoside that is sometimes prescribed for patients with symptomatic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction or atrial fibrillation, enhances cardiac inotropy and slows conduction through the sinoatrial (SA) and atrioventricular nodes. Unfortunately, digoxin has a narrow therapeutic index, and toxicity is common in situations such as when kidney impairment leads to decreased elimination. This patient with heart failure is likely also taking diuretics, and he may have higher serum digoxin levels due to superimposed hypovolemia and acute kidney insufficiency. Digoxin can result in a variety of cardiac dysrhythmias when serum concentrations increase beyond therapeutic dosing. Junctional rhythms occur when the pacemaker function of the SA node is suppressed, which may occur with digitalis toxicity. Junctional rhythms are a sequence of junctional escape beats, usually at a rate of 40–60 bpm. The QRS complex is usually narrow in junctional rhythms, and the P wave is usually absent or retrograde. Digitalis toxicity in patients with atrial fibrillation may present with accelerated junctional rhythms, although these are usually not symptomatic. Bradycardia can be managed with atropine, but definitive treatment of digoxin toxicity involves the administration of antibody (antigen-binding) fragments.



Amlodipine (A) is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that is selective for smooth muscle, making it an effective blood pressure medication with a negligible effect on the heart rate. Apixaban (B) is a factor Xa inhibitor that is used to anticoagulate patients with conditions that predispose them to embolic disease, such as atrial fibrillation. Anticoagulant medications increase the risk of bleeding complications, from epistaxis and heavy menses to intracranial hemorrhage and gastrointestinal bleeding. Lisinopril (D) is an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor that is used as an antihypertensive medication and has beneficial effects in minimizing cardiac remodeling. The most common adverse reactions for this class of medication, especially in overdose, are hypotension and dizziness.

One Step Further
Question:
What treatment is generally indicated for junctional bradycardia unrelated to digoxin toxicity or metabolic derangements?

Reveal Answer:
Pacemaker placement.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Digoxin Toxicity

Hypokalemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity
Sx: nausea, vomiting, vision changes (yellow halos)
ECG: PVCs, atrial tachycardia with AV block, slow Afib, bidirectional ventricular tachycardia
Dx: digoxin level, kidney function, hyperkalemia is associated with a poor prognosis
Tx: digoxin-specific antibody fragment
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللي صار إنه هاد المريض عنده syncope مع ضغط 80/50 ونبض 42 مع junctional rhythm و QRS ضيق و P wave رجعية، وهاد جوهر digoxin toxicity. الـ Digoxin بيزيد الـ contractility وبيبطئ التوصيل في الـ SA node والـ AV node، ومعاه index علاجي ضيق، فـ kidney impairment مع الـ diuretics وفقدان حجم بيزودوا serum level. الـ junctional rhythm بيصير لما الـ SA node يتوقف عن كونه Pacemaker، والـ QRS بيضل ضيق مع P wave غايب أو رجعية، والعلاج الحاسم هو antibody fragments.
الفخ: أكثر خطأ إن الطالب يختار amlodipine أو apixaban أو lisinopril. Lisinopril و amlodipine ما بيسببوا bradycardia من نوع junctional rhythm. digoxin هو اللي بيعمل toxicity بهالشكل، والعلاج بيكون digoxin antibody fragments.

question: What is the best next step in the management of the finding shown in the ECG above in a patient who presents with transient palpitations that have resolved?
englishExplanation:
On an ECG, the P wave indicates atrial depolarization. The PR interval measures conduction between the atria and ventricles. A normal PR interval is 120–200 msec. First-degree atrioventricular (AV) block is indicative of delayed or slowed conduction through the AV node and is seen when the PR interval is > 200 msec, as is demonstrated in the ECG above.

This can be seen as a normal variant in young, healthy adults. There are no specific signs or symptoms that are attributed to a first-degree AV block. Most cases are noted incidentally on an ECG performed for another reason. No specific treatment is required, as this is a stable rhythm. Some sources recommend avoiding AV nodal blocking agents.



Defibrillation (A) is used in the resuscitation of unstable cardiac dysrhythmias, including unstable ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, and torsades de pointes (none of which are shown above). Because a first-degree AV block is a stable rhythm, defibrillation would not be needed and would likely cause cardiac arrest.

Indications for the placement of an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) (B) include ischemic heart disease with unexplained syncope, cardiac arrest from ventricular fibrillation or ventricular tachycardia, sustained ventricular tachycardia, nonischemic cardiomyopathy, depressed left ventricular ejection fraction, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, long QT syndrome, Brugada syndrome, and other congenital heart diseases. However, a first-degree AV block is benign, and ICD placement is not necessary.

Magnesium (C) is the treatment of choice for torsades de pointes, which is an unstable polymorphic ventricular tachycardia that is commonly caused by electrolyte disturbances such as hypomagnesemia. It is often seen in the setting of a prolonged QT interval and is characterized by a twisting of the QRS complexes that shift around the baseline.

Placement of a permanent pacemaker (E) is often the treatment of choice for patients with high-grade AV blocks, including Mobitz II second-degree AV block and third-degree AV block.

One Step Further

What rare dysrhythmia is most commonly associated with digoxin toxicity?

Reveal Answer:
Bidirectional ventricular tachycardia.
