550.   What type of isolation does this patient require?
englishExplanation:
550.  The answer is e. EVD spreads through direct contact (mucous
membranes, breaks in skin, and needles) with blood or body fluids of
patients infected with EVD disease. Given the high pathogenicity (fatality
rate) and virulence of the disease (ease of spread), high-level contact
precautions are recommended alongside airborne precautions when
there is a chance of generating aerosols. The CDC recommends full-body
coverage (including eye protection) by PPE and the use of either N95
masks or personal air purifying respirators (PAPRs) for protection from
aerosols. Health care workers who are potentially at risk for exposure to
EBV should be trained and observed on the donning and doffing of PPE as
this is a high-risk activity.
Airborne isolation alone (a), contact isolation alone (b), droplet
isolation (c), and contact and droplet isolation (d) are not adequate for
preventing the spread of EBV.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض suspected EVD، ومرضه بينتشر بالتماس المباشر مع الدم أو سوائل الجسم عبر الـ mucous membranes وأي كسر بالجلد، وكمان بالـ needles. ولأن المرض عنده pathogenicity و virulence عالية، الـ CDC بتنصح بـ high-level contact precautions مع airborne precautions مع وقت ما في احتمال تتولد aerosols. ولازم يكون فيه PPE بغطّي الجسم كله مع eye protection، و N95 أو PAPR، وتدريب على donning و doffing.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على airborne بس أو على contact و droplet، لأنهم سمعوا إن respiratory illness بتنقل بالقطيرات. الفرق إن EVD مش droplet، هي direct contact مع الدم وسوائل الجسم، ولما يصير فيه احتمال توليد aerosols لازم نجمع الاتنين مع بعض.

question:
A patient presents to the emergency department with 8 months 
of progressive dyspnea. There is no recent change in the patient’s 
symptoms. On exam, there is a prolonged expiratory phase without 
wheezing, no rales, no pedal edema. The electrocardiogram is normal. The chest x-ray revealed hyperinflation with a flattened diaphragm. The diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease 
(COPD):

options.text: Can be made clinically in this patient
Can be made radiographically with demonstration flattening of
Requires demonstration of spirometry-proven airflow limitation
Requires genetic testing and historical features including

correctAnswer: Requires demonstration of spirometry-proven airflow limitation
englishExplanation:
The diagnosis of COPD requires spirometry-proven airflow limitation defined as a ratio of FEV1 divided by FVC after bronchodilators of less 
than 0.7. Patients who have normal spirometry with chronic symptoms and 
possible emphysema on CT scan are not considered to have COPD.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ COPD مو تشخيص سريري من symptoms و chest x-ray، لا، لازم يثبت بـ spirometry. التعريف إنه يبقى فيه airflow limitation مثبت، يعني نسبة FEV1 مقسومة على FVC بعد الـ bronchodilator أقل من أو تساوي 0.7. والمرضى اللي عندهم symptoms مزمنة بس spirometry عنده طبيعي، حتى لو في emphysema على الـ CT scan، ما بنعتبرهم عندهم COPD.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على إن التشخيص بينعمل سريري من symptoms، لأن المريض عنده 8 شهور dyspnea و hyperinflation و flattened diaphragm على الـ X-ray. الفرق إن الصور ما بتكفي، لازم spirometry-proven airflow limitation بعد الـ bronchodilators.

question:
In a patient with a diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), increased dyspnea, sputum production, and sputum 
purulence worse than baseline day-to-day variations for the past 
three days requiring evaluation in the emergency department is 
defined as:
englishExplanation:
COPD exacerbation can be defined as a worsening of symptoms from baseline day-to-day variations that requires treatment. The 
most common symptoms include increased dyspnea, cough, increased 
sputum production and increased sputum purulence.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض عنده COPD معروف، ومعه تغيّر بالأعراض عن الـ baseline اليومي لثلاثة أيام، ومعه زيادة بـ dyspnea و increased sputum production و increased sputum purulence. هاي هي الـ COPD exacerbation بالظبط. المهم إن الـ exacerbation هي تجاوز للـ baseline اليومي بشكل يحتاج تدخل وعلاج، مو مجرد continuation للأعراض نفسها. وبالتعريف داك: worsening of symptoms from baseline that requires treatment.
الفخ: الطلاب بيسقطوا على emphysema أو chronic bronchitis لأنهم شافوا زيادة dyspnea وبلغم. الفرق إن الـ emphysema و chronic bronchitis تشخيصات ثابتة للمريض، أما هاي حالة تغيّر مؤقت عن الـ baseline وبيحتاج معالجة، فبنسمّيها exacerbation.

question:
This bacterium is frequently implicated in non-GAS pharyngitis and is also most commonly implicated in suppurative jugular 
thrombophlebitis:
englishExplanation:
Fusobacterium necrophorum is an anaerobic gram-negative 
rod that is part of the normal oral flora and causes pharyngitis in patients 
15 to 45 years old with a similar presentation to GAS. Fusobacterium 
is the primary causative agent in septic jugular vein thrombophlebitis 
(Lemierre syndrome). Fusobacterium should be considered in young 
adults with ongoing severe symptoms.
   	 C H A P T E R 6 1 : Q U E S T I O N S AND ANS WERS —cont’d

838.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: F. necrophorum هو anaerobic gram-negative rod جزء من الـ normal oral flora، وبيسبب pharyngitis عند الناس اللي بأعمار 15 لـ 45 سنة، والpresentation بتاعتها بتكون شبيهة بالـ GAS. وهو السبب الأول لحدوث suppurative jugular thrombophlebitis اللي بينعرف باسم Lemierre syndrome. ولما يكون عندك شاب عنده symptoms مستمرة وشديدة كما هون، لازم تفكر فيها ولا تستبعدها بسرعة.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على Arcanobacterium haemolyticum لأنه بيسبب pharyngitis بمظهر شبيه، بس الفارق إن F. necrophorum هو اللي مربوط بشكل وثيق بـ suppurative jugular thrombophlebitis و Lemierre syndrome.

question:
Which of the following statements is true regarding the treatment 
of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP)?

options.text: Amoxicillin monotherapy is not an option as it does not effectively cover atypical pneumonia.
Macrolide resistance almost always prohibits azithromycin
The most common atypical pneumonia in CAP is Chlamydophila.
Clinical history and prodrome often lead to the identification of

correctAnswer: Macrolide resistance almost always prohibits azithromycin
englishExplanation:
The 2020 American Thoracic Society/Infectious Disease 
Society of America (ATS/IDSA) guidelines no longer recommend 
macrolide monotherapy as Streptococcus pneumoniae resistance is 
greater than 30% in most settings in the United States. Amoxicillin 
is now recommended as a first-line agent in the treatment of CAP in 
healthy patients without comorbidities.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاي الـ guidelines الحديثة بتغيّرت، وما عادت تنصح بـ macrolide monotherapy لـ CAP. السبب إنه مقاومة S. pneumoniae على الـ macrolides تجاوزت 30% في أغلب المناطق بأمريكا. وعشان هيك صارت amoxicillin الخيار الأول في علاج CAP عند المريض الصحي بدون comorbidities. يعني الاعتماد على azithromycin لحاله صار مش مبرر، خصوصاً لما تكون الـ resistance عالية بالـ setting اللي عم تعمل فيه.
الفخ: الطلاب بيروحوا على Chlamydophila لأنهم سمعوا إن أكثر atypical pneumonia في CAP هي اللي فيها Chlamydophila. الفرق إن هاي مو نقطة الحسم، والحسم بيتم على نسبة الـ resistance للـ macrolides فوق 30%.

question:
A 68-year-old man with a history of esophageal cancer presents 
with progressive fever, chest pain, and shortness of breath over 24 
hours. Chest radiography demonstrates a possible left lower lobe 
pneumonia and large left pleural effusion. Pleural fluid analysis 
reveals pH of 6.95, glucose level of 47 mg/dL, 11,500 white blood 
cells (WBCs)/mm3 (82% neutrophils), and protein level 75% of 
plasma levels. What are the indicated next steps in management?

options.text: Antibiotics, tube thoracostomy, and esophageal oral contrast
One-time pleural aspiration for fluid analysis

correctAnswer: Antibiotics, tube thoracostomy, and esophageal oral contrast
englishExplanation:
This is an exudative pleural effusion as defined by Light’s 
criteria (see Box 63.3). A pH less than 7.0 suggests emphysema or 
esophageal rupture. This patient is at risk for both; hence, the need to 
assess esophageal integrity. A pH less than 7.0 with glucose level less 
than 50 mg/dL are indications for tube thoracostomy. Normal pleural 
fluid has a WBC count of less than 1,000/mm3.
   

PART III  Emergency Medicine by System
889.e2
arabicExplanation:
ليش: السائل المسؤول عن الـ effusion طلع exudate حسب Light's criteria، والـ pH تاعه 6.95 يعني أقل من 7.0، والـ glucose 47 يعني أقل من 50 mg/dL، والـ WBC count 11,500 يعني أعلى من الحد الطبيعي 1,000/mm3. و pH تحت 7.0 هاد بيرجّع لاحتمال emphysema أو esophageal rupture، والمريض عنده تاريخ esophageal cancer. لازم كل هاد الـ pleural fluid ينشف بالـ tube thoracostomy، ومعاها antibiotics طول الوقت، ويصير لازم تقيّم سلامة الـ esophagus.
الفخ: الطلاب بيسقطوا على one-time pleural aspiration لأنهم شافوا pneumonia وبيفتكروا إن سحب السائل مرة وحدة بكفّي. الفرق إن الـ pH تحت 7 مع glucose تحت 50 هاد مؤشرات على tube thoracostomy، وعنده خطر esophageal rupture فلازم نعمل esophageal oral contrast.

question:
A 44-year-old man complains of swollen legs. He just finished two 
courses of prednisone for wheezing related to asthma. The first 
course was prescribed 6 weeks ago in the emergency department 
(ED), where he was diagnosed with new onset asthma and normal 
chest radiograph. The second course was prescribed by his family 
physician 2 weeks ago. The patient denies fever and chest pain and 
is still mildly short of breath, which is worse at night or with exertion. Examination shows bibasilar rales in his lungs, normal heart 
sounds, and 1+ edema in both legs up to his knees. What is his 
diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
The patient is unlikely to have a new diagnosis of asthma. 
He most likely had a viral process leading to reactive airway disease initially and viral myocarditis later. He unfortunately now has a DCM and 
symptoms of heart failure. Treatment is supportive. Prednisone-related 
end-organ damage usually does not occur this quickly.

References
976.e2
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض هاد ما عنده ربو جديد على الأرجح، بس كان عنده مرض فيروسي انطلق منه التهاب مجاري هوائية تفاعلية، وبعدين صار عنده التهاب عضلة القلب الفيروسي. وهلأ طور قلب متمدد من نوع DCM مع أعراض فشل قلب، والعلاج الداعم هو الصح. أضرار الـPrednisone على الأعضاء الهدفية ما بتظهر بهالسرعة القصيرة، يعني ما تكون هي السبب.
الفخ: كتير ناس بتختار التورم المسبب من الـPrednisone لأنه أخذ كورسين، بس التسمم الستيرويدي ما يصير هالسريعة؛ انتبه للمريض اللي بيحس بضيق نفس بالليل أو بالمجهود مع أصوات رئة بالأساس.

question:
What percentage of cases of acute bacterial prostatitis eventually 
develop into chronic bacterial prostatitis?
englishExplanation:
Chronic bacterial prostatitis will eventually develop in 10% 
of patients with acute bacterial prostatitis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الحقيقة هون بسيطة ومباشرة، وهي إنه من مرضى الـprostatitis البكتيرية الحادة، بس 10% منهم بيفضلوا بعدين عندهم شكل مزمن من المرض. يعني أغلب الحالات الحادة بتروح، بس جزء صغير بس، واحد من كل عشرة، بيصير مزمن وبيحتاج علاج ومتابعة أطول. ولازم نعرف إنه لما ييجي مريض بيحكي إنو الألم رجعله بعد فترة من التهاب حاد، احتمال يكون صار عنده الشكل المزمن، والنسبة المعروفة هي عشرة بالمية بس.
الفخ: الأرقام الثانية مثل 20% أو 5% بتتخدش لأنها بتوهم، بس الرقم المعتمد طبيًا هو عشرة بالمية ولازم يتحفظ زي ما هو بالضبط.

question:
Which one of the following findings, in conjunction with low back 
pain, indicates a benign cause of pain?

options.text: Negative sitting but positive supine straight leg raise test

correctAnswer: Negative sitting but positive supine straight leg raise test
englishExplanation:
A positive supine SLR test but a negative sitting SLR test 
suggests a nonphysiologic cause for the pain. Low back pain and 
fever suggest an epidural abscess or osteomyelitis. Saddle anesthesia 
and post-void residual greater than 100 mL are indicative of cauda 
equina syndrome (CES). Children complaining of back pain must be 
investigated. They may have spondylolysis with varying degrees of 
spondylolisthesis, Scheuermann disease (kyphosis and osteochondritis 
of the vertebral end plates), infectious diseases, or neoplastic etiologies.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: إيجاب الـstraight leg raise مع الاستلقاء وسلبيه مع الجلوس بيشير إلى إنو الألم مش عضوي، يعني سبب غير فسيولوجي وبنعتبرو حميد. بعكسه، ألم الظهر مع الحمى ممكن يكون خراج بالجوف الوركي أو التهاب عظم، والتخدير بمنطقة السرج وباقي البول فوق 100 مل بيشير إلى متلازمة الأعصاب الظهرية السفلية. وكمان لازم تعرف إنه أطفال بيحكيهم ألم ظهر لازم يتم تقييمهم لأن ممكن يكون في مشاكل بالعمود الفقري أو التهابات أو أورام.
الفخ: كتير ناس بتختار التخدير بمنطقة السرج أو باقي البول 500 مل لأنها تفصيلات مهمة، بس هدول مؤشرات على متلازمة الأعصاب الظهرية السفلية اللي هي حالة طارئة مش حميد.

question:
Which of the following findings would decrease the likelihood that 
a patient’s pleurisy is related to a lupus flare?
englishExplanation:
The general approach to assessing whether a symptom is 
caused by SLE disease activity is to look for signs and symptoms of the 
disease in other organs or systemically. Patients experiencing an SLE 
flare are likely to have other signs or symptoms of disease (e.g., arthralgias, fever, malaise, elevated ESR, low complement levels) beyond an 
isolated chief complaint (in this case, pleurisy). PR depression can be 
suggestive of pericarditis, which may occur during flares of SLE.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطريقة المعتادة لحكم إذا العرض بسبب نشاط مرض الـSLE هي نشوف إذا في أعراض وعلامات بأعضاء تانية أو أعراض عمومية. المرضى اللي عندهم نوبة SLE غالبًا بيكون عندهم أعراض ثانية مثل ألم مفاصل، حمى، توعك، ESR مرتفع، ومكملات منخفضة، مش مجرد شكوى معزولة مثل التهاب الجنب. وكمان انخفاض على الـECG ممكن يشير إلى التهاب التامور اللي ممكن يصير وقت نوبات الـSLE.
الفخ: خيارات مثل ESR المرتفع، المكملات المنخفضة، التهاب المفاصل المتعدد، وانخفاض على الـECG كلها بتدل على نشاط المرض، يعني لما تكون مراجعة الأنظمة سلبية بتنقي احتمال اللوبيوس.

question: In evaluating a patient with severe neutropenia, which of the following is false?

options.text: If the patient is febrile, basic isolation techniques and specific
If the patient is febrile, urine and blood cultures should be
The clinician should ask about medications, history of neutropenia, family history, and also review information regarding recent
The classic physical findings associated with infection will be
The review of systems focuses on bleeding problems, generalized

correctAnswer: The classic physical findings associated with infection will be
englishExplanation:
The classic physical signs of infection may be blunted in 
severe neutropenia, because the inflammatory or purulent response 
may be hampered by the limited numbers of neutrophils.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: السؤال بدو الجواب الكاذب، والحقيقة إنه بالذات الحاد، العلامات الكلاسيكة للعدوى ممكن تكون مطموسة ومبهتة. السبب هو إنو الاستجابة الالتهابية أو القيحية بتنحجز لأن عدد الخلايا المتعادلة قليل جدًا، فما بتبان الأورمة والاحمرار والقيح زي ما متوقع. عشان هيك الجواب هو إنو العلامات ستكون واضحة، وهاد هو الكلام الكاذب.
الفخ: كتير بيفكروا إنه المريض الحاد النتروبيني لازم يكون عنده حمى وعلامات عدوى واضحة، بس بالعكس العدوى عندهم ممكن تكون مخفية ومبهتة بسبب قلة النيوتروفيلات.

question: What are classic CXR findings of SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19)?
englishExplanation:
Ground-glass opacities, particularly in the lower lobes, 
are the most common findings of COVID-19 on CXR and on CT scans. 
In fact, early diagnosis of COVID-19 in many areas relied on radiographs because the results of PCR testing were often delayed.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الشائع بالـCXR والـCT للمرضى المصابين بمرض الكوفيد هو تعتيمات من نوع ground-glass، وخاصة بالقصبات السفلية. وكمان في مناطق كثيرة كان التشخيص المبكر للمرض يعتمد على الأشعة لأن نتائج الـPCR غالبًا كانت تتأخر. عشان هيك هاد هو الجواب الصح.
الفخ: كتير بيفكروا إنو الـlobar consolidation هي الصورة الكلاسيكية، بس هاد أكتر شي بيمشي مع الالتهاب الرئوي البكتيري، مش مع مرض الكوفيد.

question:
A 35-year-old man with AIDS presents with fever and a productive 
cough for 1 day. His last known CD4+ count 1 month ago was 538 
cells/μL. He has a lobar pneumonia in the left lower lobe on his 
chest radiograph. There is no evidence of lymphadenopathy. What 
is the most likely culprit pathogen in this case?
englishExplanation:
It is critical to have an understanding of diseases relative to 
the absolute CD4+ T cell count. Patients with CD4 counts higher than 
500 cells/μL typically develop illnesses similar to the general population. 
This patient presents with a lobar pneumonia, and S. pneumoniae is the 
most common cause. PCP is the most common opportunistic pathogen 
in AIDS patients, usually occurring in those with a CD4+ T cell count 
lower than 200 cells/μL. It would be extremely unusual for PCP to cause a 
lobar pneumonia in someone who is immune-reconstituted. Tuberculosis can occur at any stage of HIV infection. However, the symptoms tend 
to be more gradual in onset, and a lobar pneumonia is unlikely.
   

1673.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده CD4 فوق 500، والمرضى بهالمستوى بيعانوا أمراض شبيهة بالعامة السكانية. وبالتصوير عنده التهاب رئة بlobe محدد، وأشيع مسبب هو Streptococcus pneumoniae. الـPCP بتصيب اللي CD4 تحت 200 ونادر جدًا تكون سبب التهاب رئوي محدد بlobe بجسم متعافي مناعة. والـTB ممكن تصيب بأي مرحلة من الـHIV، بس أعراضها بتبدأ بالتدريج والتهاب بlobe واحد مش معتاد.
الفخ: كتير بيفكروا أي التهاب رئة بمريض AIDS هو PCP، بس القصة والأشعة والـCD4 المرتفع كلها بتدل على الـStreptococcus pneumoniae.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding chest radiography 
findings in pulmonary tuberculosis is true?

options.text: Adenopathy may distinguish TB from bacterial pneumonia.
Primary TB typically appears as an upper lobe cavity lesion.
The false-negative rate is 10% in immunocompetent patients.
The false-negative rate is 40% in HIV-infected patients.

correctAnswer: Adenopathy may distinguish TB from bacterial pneumonia.
englishExplanation:
Hilar adenopathy may be the only way to suspect TB as 
opposed to a typical bacterial pneumonia. Primary TB is usually a 
single-lobe infiltrate with a homogenous appearance. It is postprimary TB that has a predilection for the upper lobes, with or without 
cavitation. The false-negative rate for chest radiography in immunocompetent patients is very low, 1%. The rate increases to 7% to 15% in 
HIV-infected patients and those with endobronchial disease.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: تضخم الغدد اللمفية بالجذر الرئوي ممكن يكون الشي الوحيد اللي يميز الـTB عن الالتهاب الرئوي البكتيري المعتاد. الـprimary TB عادة بتظهر كاختراق متجانس بlobe واحد، أما الـpostprimary فهي اللي بتهاجم القصبات العليا مع أو بدون تشقق. ومعدل النتيجة الكاذبة بالأشعة قليل جدًا، حوالي 1% عند العديمين المناعة، ويرتفع إلى 7 لـ15% عند مرضى الـHIV.
الفخ: خيال إنو الـprimary TB بتظهر كتجويف بالlobe العلوي غلط لأن هاد وصف الـpostprimary، والأرقام 10% و40% لمعدل النتيجة الكاذبة مش صحيحة.

question:
An 18-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 
(ED) after submersion in his swimming pool. Per witnesses, once 
the patient was brought out from the water, he initially had severe 
coughing and complained of shortness of breath. On arrival to the 
ED, the patient denies shortness of breath and is not coughing. Vital 
signs as well as oxygen saturation are all within normal limits. Electrocardiogram (ECG) and chest radiographs are normal. What is 
the appropriate disposition of this patient?

options.text: Admission to the general hospital for 23-hour observation
Admission to the intensive care unit for 23-hour observation
Discharge home after observation in the ED for 8 hours

correctAnswer: Discharge home after observation in the ED for 8 hours
englishExplanation:
Any symptomatic patients or patients with a history 
of apnea, unconsciousness, or hypoxia should be admitted. Likewise, 
patients with dysrhythmias or abnormal chest radiographs should be 
admitted. Some effects of drowning can be delayed, so asymptomatic 
patients should be observed for 8 hours in the ED but can be safely discharged if they continue to be asymptomatic and can maintain normal 
room air oxygen saturation. They should be discharged in the care of a 
responsible family member or friend.
   	 C H A P T E R 1 3 3 : Q U E S T I O N S AND ANS WERS —cont’d.

1826.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض بعد الغرق عمل سعال وضيق نفس، بس هلأ العلامات الحيوية والتشبع بالأكسجين والـECG والأشعة كلها طبيعية. بس في آثار متأخرة ممكن تصير من الغرق، عشان هيك المرضى بلا أعراض لازم يراقبوا 8 ساعات بالطوارئ. وإذا فضل بلا أعراض ويقدر يحافظ على تشبع طبيعي بجو الغرفة، بيخرج تحت مسؤولية شخص بالغ مسؤول من العيلة أو الأصحاب.
الفخ: كتير بيختاروا الإخراج فورًا لأنه حاليًا طبيعي، بس هاد مبكر؛ والدخول للمستشفى مبرر بس إذا في أعراض أو نقص أكسجين أو اضطراب نظم أو أشعة غير طبيعية.

question:
Given that brief intervention and screening (SBIRT—screening, 
brief intervention, and referral to treatment) can reduce alcohol 
consumption and is feasible and effective in the emergency department, which of the following interventions are particularly effective 
and preferred for college students?
englishExplanation:
Studies show that providing internet-based interventions 
is more effective to reduce binge drinking among college students. The 
Internet could be an economic and acceptable form of delivering brief 
interventions and is a preferred approach to reach binge drinkers in 
college. AA Meetings, counseling, and pharmacologic treatment are 
likely to occur later in the treatment process.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الأبحاث أثبتت إنو التدخلات عن طريق الإنترنت فعالة أكثر لتقليل الشرب المفرط بين طلاب الجامعة. الإنترنت وسيلة اقتصادية ومقبولة لتقديم التدخلات المختصرة، وهي الطريقة المفضلة للوصول لهدول الطلبة. وكمان التدخل المختصر والفحص والتحويل للعلاج مثبت إنه بيقلل استهلاك الكحول وقابل للتطبيق بالطوارئ.
الفخ: كتير بيختاروا العلاج الدوائي أو جلسات الـAA لأنها معروفة، بس هدول بيجوا بعدين بمسار العلاج، مش الخطوة المفضلة مع طلاب الجامعة.

question:
A healthy 26-year-old female was helping her great aunt clean out 
her home when she spilled a large tray of old mercury thermometers on the floor. She then attempted to vacuum up the mercury. She 
is now presenting to the emergency department 3 hours later with 
cough, fever, and shortness of breath. Her oxygen saturation is 93% 
on room air and her respiratory rate is 24 breaths per minute. A 
chest x-ray shows bilateral patchy infiltrates. Which of the following 
would be the most appropriate initial management?

options.text: Provide supplemental oxygen and intravenous fluid resuscitation and admit for further monitoring.
Consult nephrology for potential acute kidney injury.
Administer antibiotics and admit for further monitoring.
Call the department of public health to evaluate the home for

correctAnswer: Provide supplemental oxygen and intravenous fluid resuscitation and admit for further monitoring.
englishExplanation:
This patient is exhibiting acute inhalation elemental mercury toxicity. After an inhalation exposure where mercury is volatilized 
and inhaled, patients can have fever, shortness of breath, and cough 
that can rapidly progress to ARDS. This may occur hours after exposure. Later, as the mercury is absorbed patients are at risk for inorganic 
mercury poisoning resulting in nephrotoxicity. The best approach to 
these patients is supportive care and close monitoring of their respiratory status. There are no roles for activated charcoal or antibiotics as 
activated charcoal does not bind heavy metals and this is a pneumonitis. Nephrology may ultimately need to be consulted but now the focus 
should be on the patient’s cardiorespiratory status. Answer choice E 
is also reasonable to prevent further exposure at the home given the 
large amount of elemental mercury spilled, however it is not the most 
emergent management step.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده تسمم حاد بالزئبق عن طريق الاستنشاق، واللي بيسبب حمى وسعال وضيق نفس ممكن يتقدم بسرعة إلى ARDS بعد ساعات من التعرض. الأفضل هو الدعم وإعطاء أكسجين وسوائل وريدية مع مراقبة وثيقة للوضع التنفسي. الـactivated charcoal ما بيربط المعادن الثقيلة مثل الزئبق، والمضادات الحيوية ما إلها دور لأنه هاد التهاب رئوي مش عدوى.
الفخ: كتير بيختاروا الـactivated charcoal لأنها أول خطوة بأي تسمم، بس هي ما بتربط المعادن الثقيلة أصلًا، والاستشارة بخصوص الكلى ممكن تصير بعدين مش هلأ.

question:
A 52-year-old man is brought to the emergency department (ED) after 
being rescued from a house fire. He has not suffered any cutaneous 
burns. He complains of a sore throat, hoarse voice, and cough. Vital 
signs are normal. Physical examination reveals soot in his oropharynx 
and carbonaceous sputum. What therapy should be instituted first?
englishExplanation:
Endotracheal intubation should be performed early in 
patients with signs and symptoms of significant airway burns (as with 
this patient). Corticosteroids are not beneficial and can worsen associated injuries. Inhaled beta-agonists are commonly used, but there is no 
evidence of improved outcome. Inhaled sodium bicarbonate plays no 
role in the management of smoke inhalation. Bronchoalveolar lavage 
can be performed if there is suspicion of inhaled debris or toxins, but 
the airway should first be secured.

1947.e2
PART IV  Environment and Toxicology
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده إصابات مقصورة بأعلى الهواية، يعني ألم الحلق وبحة الصوت وسخام بالبلعوم وباقٍ كربوني بالبلغم، وهدول علامات على حروق تنفسية مهمة. عشان هيك لازم نؤمن الهواية أول، بعمل Endotracheal intubation مبكر، قبل أي علاج تاني. لأن هالمنطقة ممكن تنتفخ وتنسد بعد الحرق، والتأمين المبكر بيحافظ على سلامة الهواية.
الفخ: كتير بيفكروا إنو الـnebulized albuterol أو الـcorticosteroids هي الخطوة الأولى، بس هدول مش أولوية؛ الستيرويدات أصلاً ما إلها فائدة، ولازم نؤمن الهواية قبل الغسيل الرئوي.

question:
A worker at a chemical plant was exposed to a cloud of chlorine 
gas (Cl2). On examination in the emergency department you note a 
normal oxygen saturation, increased respiratory rate, and wheezing 
on lung auscultation. In addition to administration of inhaled betaadrenergic agonists, which of the following can be administered for 
symptomatic relief?
englishExplanation:
This patient was exposed to chlorine gas which is an intermediate water-soluble gas that combines with water in the respiratory tract to form hydrochloric acid. Patients may have improvement 
of their symptoms with the administration of nebulized 2% sodium 
bicarbonate solution. Systemic corticosteroids have not shown a benefit in these patients. Antibiotics should not be administered routinely 
in these patients unless an overlying infectious process is suspected.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: غاز الـCl2 بيتجمع مع الماء بجهاز التنفس ويعمل حمض الهيدروكلوريك، وهاد بيسبب تهييج وضيق نفس وصفير. العلاج المضاف على الـbeta-agonists المبخرين هو محلول صوديوم بيكربونات بنسبة 2% مبخّر، واللي بيخفف أعراض هدول المرضى. الستيرويدات الجهازية ما أظهرت فائدة، والمضادات الحيوية ما بتعطى بشكل روتيني إلا إذا اشتبه بعدين بعوى معدية فوقية.
الفخ: كتير بيختاروا الستيرويدات النظامية لأنها مألوفة بحالات الالتهاب، بس ما بتنفع هون؛ والمضادات الحيوية مش خطوة أساسية إلا إذا في عوى ثانية.

question:
You are about to treat a child with acute asthma with albuterol. 
Which of the following factors is most important when considering 
the method of aerosolized drug delivery?

options.text: About 20% to 30% of nebulized drug reaches the alveoli.
Children receiving β-agonists by nebulizer (NEB) have similar
Children weighing >20 kg should receive a maximum of four
MDI-S therapy is more costly than NEB therapy.
The use of MDI-S for acute asthma is not supported by national

correctAnswer: Children receiving β-agonists by nebulizer (NEB) have similar
englishExplanation:
Clinical trials and systematic reviews have repeatedly 
shown these two forms of therapy to be equivalent. With NEB treatment, less than 10% of nebulized drug reaches the alveoli. A recommended MDI-S dose for older children is eight puffs. Most studies 
demonstrate that MDI-S therapy is more cost-effective because of a 
slightly reduced need for hospitalization. National guidelines support 
the use of MDI-S to deliver albuterol to children with acute asthma.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: التجارب السريرية والمراجعات الدليلية أثبتوا أكثر من مرة إنو الـnebulizer والـMDI-S بيعطوا نفس النتائج العلاجية عند الأطفال. وكمان أقل من 10% من الدواء المبخّر بيصل إلى الحويصلات الهوائية، والجرعة الموصى بها بالـMDI للأطفال الأكبر هي ثماني نقرات. أغلب الدراسات بتوضح إنو الـMDI-S أقل تكلفة، والإرشادات الوطنية بتدعم استخدامه لإعطاء الـalbuterol.
الفخ: كتير فاكرين إنه الـnebulizer أقوى وأكفأ، بس هاد غلط؛ والأرقام مثل إنو 20 لـ30% من الدواء بيصل الحويصلات مش صحيحة، والجرعة مش أربع نقرات.

question:
Which of the following findings is an indication for admission to 
the hospital in children with a diagnosis of pneumonia?

options.text: Abnormal chest radiograph showing pulmonary infiltrates
Decreased breath sounds in a lower lung field

englishExplanation:
Many children with pneumonia can be managed as an 
outpatient with appropriate therapy. Clinical dehydration or inability 
to orally maintain hydration should prompt admission for ongoing 
treatment and monitoring. Abnormal lung auscultation or findings on 

PART V  Special Populations
2108.e2
a chest radiograph by themselves would not be contraindications to 
outpatient treatment.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أغلب الأطفال المرضى بالتهاب الرئة بيتعاملوا كمرضى خارج مع مراعاة علاجية مناسبة. العلامة اللي بتطلب دخول المستشفى هي الجفاف السريري أو إنو الطفل ما يقدر يحافظ على ترطيبه عن طريق الفم، لأنو محتاج علاج ومراقبة مستمرة. بس سماعات الرئة الغير طبيعية أو الصورة بالأشعة وحدها مش سبب يمنع العلاج بالخارج.
الفخ: كتير بيختاروا التهاب الرئة أو صورة أشعة غير طبيعية كسبب للدخول، بس هدول وحدها مش مؤشر؛ اللي بيفرض الدخول هو الجفاف وعدم القدرة على شرب السوائل.

question:
Which of the following medications prescribed on discharge is 
most likely to interact in an older patient taking warfarin?
englishExplanation:
Studies of harmful drug interactions in older adults have 
shown that the initiation of antibiotics in patients taking warfarin can 
lead to bleeding. Ciprofloxacin can lead to an elevation in the international normalized ratio (INR) due to disruption of vitamin K synthesis in patients taking warfarin. Thus, more frequent monitoring is 
required when ciprofloxacin is initiated. The other options listed do 
not interact with warfarin. However, oxycodone and promethazine 
can be harmful because of central nervous system effects, potentially 
leading to falls.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: دراسات التداخلات الدوائية الضارة بالكبار أثبتت إنو بدء المضادات الحيوية مع الـwarfarin ممكن يسبب نزيف. الـciprofloxacin بيرفع الـINR لأنه بيقطع تصنيف فيتامين K بالمعوي عند مرضى الـwarfarin، وعشان هيك لازم مراقبة أكتر كثافة لما تبدأو. الخيارات الثانية ما بتنتفاعل مع الـwarfarin بشكل مباشر.
الفخ: كتير بيختاروا الـoxycodone أو الـpromethazine لأنها تأثيرها على الجهاز العصبي المركزي وممكن تسبب سقوط، بس التفاعل اللي بيحدث مع الـwarfarin هو مع المضادة الحيوية الـciprofloxacin.

question:
A 49-year-old man with diabetes who has been receiving chemotherapy for non-Hodgkin lymphoma presents with fever and facial 
pain. Six weeks ago, he was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics for fever but had negative cultures of blood and urine. He is 
taking ciprofloxacin as prophylaxis against infection. Examination 
is normal except for a purple-black lesion on his hard palate that 
looks like dried blood. A complete blood count shows severe neutropenia. In addition to blood cultures and chest radiography, what 
action should be taken immediately?

options.text: Observe in the emergency department (ED) because he may be
Obtain a computed tomography (CT) scan of the paranasal

correctAnswer: Obtain a computed tomography (CT) scan of the paranasal
englishExplanation:
This patient has invasive aspergillosis or mucormycosis 
until proven otherwise. These fungi invade tissues and produce lifethreatening necrotizing infections in cancer patients with neutropenia, as well as in diabetic patients, especially those who have received 
broad-spectrum antibiotics. CT scan will often show deep extension of 
the infection into the sinuses, orbit, or brain. The initial lesion in the 
palate or nose is often mistaken for a benign process. The antibiotics 
listed in A and B are incorrect. The most appropriate empirical antibiotic regimen is cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam, with or without 
an aminoglycoside, in addition to antifungal therapy. He is not a candidate for home therapy.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده نتروبينيا حاد وسكري وكيماوي، وبيشتكي حمى وألم بالوجه مع آفة بنفسجية سوداء بالحنك، هدول يخلونا نشتبه بـinvasive aspergillosis أو mucormycosis لحد ما يتأكد العكس. هالفطريات بتغزوا الأنسجة وتعمل عدوى نخرية مهددة للحياة، والـCT للجيوب غالباً بيكشف امتداد العدوى للجيب أو الحجاج أو الدماغ. عشان هيك لازم نعمل CT للجيوب ونبدأ مضادات فطرية وريدية بالمستشفى.
الفخ: كتير بيفكروا إنها عدوى بكتيرية بيعطوا الـclindamycin أو الـlevofloxacin، بس هدول غلط؛ والعلاج المبكر هو تشخيص بالأشعة وبدء مضادات فطرية.

question:
A 27-year-old man presents to the emergency department (ED) 
with acute onset of fever, chills, headache, myalgias, vomiting, 
mild abdominal cramping, and diarrhea for 8 hours. A splenectomy was performed 15 years earlier when he was treated for lymphoma, which has been in remission since then. He is not taking 
any medications and has been well. Vital signs are as follows: pulse, 
125 beats/min; blood pressure, 110/60 mm Hg; respiratory rate, 20 
breaths/min; and temperature, 39.5°C. His mental status is normal 
and he has mild generalized abdominal tenderness. What is the 
most appropriate treatment for this patient at this time?

options.text: Blood cultures followed by immediate administration of ceftriaxone or cefotaxime, with or without vancomycin
Hydration, antipyretic, antiemetic, and observation in the ED
Immediate hospital admission with observation and frequent

correctAnswer: Blood cultures followed by immediate administration of ceftriaxone or cefotaxime, with or without vancomycin
englishExplanation:
This patient is at high risk for overwhelming postsplenectomy sepsis, usually caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. Persons who 
have undergone splenectomy for a hematologic disorder or lymphoma 
are at much higher risk for overwhelming postsplenectomy infection 
than are those undergoing splenectomy for trauma. The initial prodromal symptoms may be misdiagnosed as a viral illness, gastroenteritis, 
or food poisoning before there is abrupt deterioration with development of septic shock with disseminated intravascular coagulation, purpura, and multiorgan dysfunction. After blood cultures are obtained, 
he should immediately receive antimicrobials active against pneumococci, meningococci, and Haemophilus influenzae. He can be investigated for other possible etiologies of his symptoms after this initial 
critical action is taken.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض اتعمله splenectomy من 15 سنة بسبب لمفوما، وهاد يخلو بخطر عالٍ على إنتان ساحق بعد استئصال الطحال، والسبب الأشهر هو Streptococcus pneumoniae. الأعراض المبكرة ممكن تتوهم إنها فيروس أو التهاب معوي أو تسمم غذائي، وبعدين بيهجم انحلال دم إنتاني مع اضطراب تخثر منتشر وبقع وفشل بعضا أعضاء. عشان هيك ناخد مزارع دم ونعطي مضادات حيوية فورية ضد pneumococcus وmeningococcus وH. influenzae.
الفخ: كتير بيختاروا إعادة الترطيب والخافض للحرارة والمضاد للغثيان مع المراقبة، بس هاد تأخير خطير؛ هدول المرضى بيحتاجوا مضادات حيوية فورية بعد أخذ المزارع.

question:
A senior attending asks a resident to discharge a young patient 
with abdominal pain. The resident has noted lab abnormalities 
she believes merits further work-up, but assumes the attending has 
seen these results and defers to the attending’s judgment. These 
abnormalities had in fact been overlooked by the attending and 
the patient gets sent home without appropriate work-up. This is an 
example of which potentially negative process?
englishExplanation:
The hierarchical nature of medicine can lead to authority 
gradients which may contribute to errors. If a more junior member of 
the team does not feel empowered to voice a concern regarding patient 
safety, it can potentially have adverse consequences.
arabicExplanation:

question: A 55-year-old man with a history of alcohol-related cirrhosis presents a few days after having a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt procedure performed. Which of the following is most likely to be exacerbated by this procedure?
englishExplanation:
The transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) procedure bypasses blood flow past the cirrhotic and high-resistance liver. Bypassing the liver subsequently stops the metabolic function of the liver on the blood that normally travels through this region. This results in postshunt encephalopathy, which occurs secondary to hyperammonemia that cannot be detoxified by the liver. The treatment of postshunt encephalopathy includes the administration of lactulose (which acidifies stool contents and leads to ammonia loss in the stool) and rifaximin (an antibiotic that eliminates ammonia-producing flora). Other complications associated with a TIPS procedure include hyperbilirubinemia, congestive heart failure with flash pulmonary edema (from the increased blood volume delivery to the heart), hemolytic anemia, and infection.



Ascites (A) occurs secondary to decreased hepatic synthetic function and a decreased circulatory osmotic pressure and is less likely to be altered by a TIPS procedure.

Coagulopathy (B) is associated with hepatic synthetic function, which will not be significantly affected by a TIPS procedure. A worsening of the underlying liver function, such as with continued alcohol consumption, could worsen the patient’s coagulopathy.

Variceal bleeding (D) would actually be improved with a TIPS procedure, as blood is now shunted around the cirrhotic and high-resistance liver. Similarly, a patient’s hemorrhoids may improve, as well, for the same reason.

One Step Further
Question:
What medication is indicated in variceal bleeding and acts by decreasing splanchnic vascular pressure?

Reveal Answer:
Octreotide.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt (TIPS)

Relieves portal hypertension by creating a shunt between portal vein and hepatic vein
Diverts blood flow away from liver into systemic circulation
Can precipitate hepatic encephalopathy

question: A 68-year-old man presents to the ED with 1 week of progressively worsening abdominal pain, distention, nausea, and constipation, stating he has not had a bowel movement in the past 3 days. He has no history of prior abdominal surgery or any significant medical history, but he also does not have a primary care provider and has not seen a doctor in over 20 years. Physical examination is notable for marked abdominal distention with tympany to percussion and diffuse tenderness without guarding. Abdominal X-ray is shown above. What is the most common etiology of this condition?
englishExplanation:
The most common etiology of this patient’s condition, which is a large bowel obstruction based on his symptoms and abdominal X-ray findings, is colorectal cancer (CRC).

CRC is one of the world’s most lethal malignancies, accounting for > 145,000 new cases and > 50,000 deaths annually in the United States. Despite effective screening strategies and strong multidisciplinary advocacy, the disease often presents insidiously, with symptoms such as changes in bowel habits, visible or occult blood in the stool, unexplained iron deficiency anemia, or less commonly, a palpable abdominal or rectal mass. Alarmingly, large bowel obstruction is the initial presentation in nearly one-third of cases, underscoring the importance of timely diagnosis. The American Cancer Society recommends screening for CRC starting at age 45 years, but lack of access to primary care and preventive screening often leads to delayed diagnoses, as illustrated by this patient who has not seen a physician in decades. This delay contributes to advanced presentations, including obstruction caused by tumor masses.

CRC is by far the most common cause of large bowel obstruction. Abdominal X-rays are a key initial diagnostic tool, with findings such as peripheral dilation of the large bowel, haustral markings, and minimal small bowel gas if the ileocecal valve remains competent. Cecal dilation > 10 cm or diffuse large bowel dilation > 8 cm is particularly concerning. If X-rays are nondiagnostic, abdominal CT imaging should follow, offering high sensitivity and specificity for both the detection and characterization of colorectal malignancy and associated complications. In cases of suspected obstruction, timely evaluation and intervention are critical, not only to relieve the obstruction but also to identify and manage the underlying malignancy.



Adhesions (A) are the most common etiology of small bowel obstructions, and though they may potentially cause large bowel obstructions, this occurs much less frequently than cases initiated by CRC.

Internal abdominal hernias (C) are a rare cause of large bowel obstructions, representing approximately 2% of all cases, and are more often implicated in small bowel obstructions.

Sigmoid volvulus (D) is the most common nonmalignant etiology of large bowel obstruction, accounting for 10% of all presentations, which is still far fewer than those caused by CRC.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common site of colorectal cancer metastases?

Reveal Answer:
The liver.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Large Bowel Obstruction

Most commonly caused by colorectal cancer
Most common location is sigmoid colon
Presentation: abdominal distension, obstipation, progressive changes in bowel habits
PE: high-pitched bowel sounds
Treatment is NGT, surgery

question: A 68-year-old man presents to the emergency department reporting diarrhea and dehydration. He reports that he had a dental procedure 2 weeks prior for which he took antibiotics. A week later, he began having crampy abdominal pain and foul-smelling diarrhea 6–7 times a day that is watery and contains mucus. His blood pressure is 102/68 mm Hg, heart rate is 103 bpm, temperature is 100.8°F (38.2°C), and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On examination, he has diffuse mild crampy abdominal pain. His lab work is notable for white blood cells of 13,000/µL and positive fecal leukocytes. What is the most appropriate oral treatment?
englishExplanation:
Clostridioides (formerly Clostridium) difficile is an anaerobic spore-forming bacteria that causes a toxin-mediated gastrointestinal infection ranging from mild diarrhea to severe pseudomembranous colitis. A common presentation is a patient who develops diarrhea within 2 weeks of discontinuing an antibiotic. The most frequently implicated antibiotics are clindamycin, fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins, penicillin combinations, carbapenems, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. These antibiotics reduce the normal anaerobic fecal flora, which break down bile acids and carbohydrates and allow Clostridioides difficile to predominate. Excess carbohydrates contribute to the watery diarrhea due to their osmotic effects, while excess bile acids result in a secretory mucus component.

Symptoms typically include foul-smelling, watery diarrhea with mucus, which when severe may also cause crampy abdominal pain, fever, leukocytosis, and dehydration. Mild disease is associated with a white blood cell count ≤ 15,000/µL. Moderate disease is associated with a white blood cell count > 15,000/µL while maintaining the ability to tolerate oral antibiotics. The presence of fecal leukocytes helps distinguish Clostridioides difficile from other benign antibiotic-associated diarrhea. In addition, specialized stool assays that detect the toxin, or stool cultures in a specialized medium, may assist in making a diagnosis. Individuals with severe or complicated disease require hospitalization. In very severe cases, patients may develop toxic megacolon.

Patients with nonsevere or severe disease may be treated with oral vancomycin or oral fidaxomicin. While previously recommended for patients with nonsevere disease, the use of metronidazole is now limited to patients with fulminant disease unless vancomycin or fidaxomicin are unavailable. Recurrence occurs in 20–30% of patients. Recent hospitalization or residence in a long-term care facility raises the risk, as 20–50% of hospitalized patients and up to 70% of long-term care residents may be colonized with Clostridioides difficile. Also, recent antibiotic use, gastrointestinal surgery, chemotherapy, the use of proton pump inhibitors or histamine type-2 blockers, underlying medical disease, and advanced age increase the risk of pseudomembranous colitis.



Ciprofloxacin (A) is used in the treatment of several infectious diarrheal illnesses, but it is not sufficient to treat Clostridioides difficile, rather, fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin have been implicated as a cause.

While clindamycin (B) is used to treat anaerobic infections, it is not indicated in this case since it is one of the antibiotics commonly associated with causing Clostridioides difficile.

Paromomycin (C) is an antiprotozoal agent used in the treatment of Giardia and intestinal amebiasis but not in the case of Clostridioides difficile colitis.

One Step Further
Question:
True or false: antibacterial hand sanitizer is effective and recommended over soap and water for eliminating Clostridioides difficile spores.

Reveal Answer:
False.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Clostridioides difficile Colitis (Pseudomembranous Colitis)

Risk factors: history of recent antibiotic use (clindamycin most common), hospitalization, age > 65 years
Sx: loose stools (more than three over 24 hours), abdominal pain
Diagnosis made with two-step testing to distinguish from colonization: sensitive test initially (NAAT or GDH) followed by specific test (toxin EIA)
Treatment
Nonsevere or severe: oral vancomycin or oral fidaxomicin
Fulminant: oral vancomycin with parenteral metronidazole
Patients with at least two Clostridioides difficile infection recurrences treated with appropriate antibiotic therapy: guidelines recommend use of fecal microbiota transplantation

question: A 71-year-old man presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain. His medical history is notable for diabetes and dyslipidemia. He smokes one pack of cigarettes per day. He has experienced recurrent episodes of abdominal pain for the past year that have been gradually worsening. He had a bloody, diarrhea bowel movement earlier in the week but has not had another episode recently. Symptoms only occur while and shortly after eating. Exam reveals a nontender abdomen, though the patient reports a 5/10 abdominal pain that has improved since onset. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Ischemic colitis is typically caused by underlying atherosclerosis that limits blood flow to the colon. Symptoms occur when there is reduced blood supply to the colon (such as when exercising) or increased oxygen demand from the colon (such as when eating). The classic history includes postprandial abdominal pain, diarrhea, and possibly bloody stools. Chronic, crampy abdominal pain is also a common presentation. The diagnosis can be supported with CT angiography of the abdomen and pelvis. Management involves medical optimization, including weight loss, smoking cessation, blood pressure control, lipid control, and antiplatelet agents such as aspirin. Chronic, severe symptoms refractory to medical management may warrant surgical intervention.



Irritable bowel syndrome (B) presents with recurrent episodes of abdominal pain that include constipation, diarrhea, or constipation that alternates with diarrhea. This diagnosis can only be made once other diagnoses have been ruled out. Often, CT imaging, colonoscopy, and testing for autoimmune and allergic conditions is indicated before assuming the diagnosis is irritable bowel syndrome.

Acute mesenteric ischemia (A) presents with sudden-onset, severe abdominal pain. Patients often have pain out of proportion to the exam, meaning that the patient is in severe pain yet has a relatively nontender abdomen. This condition occurs secondary to complete (or near-complete) arterial occlusion, often from an embolus, thrombus, or atherosclerotic plaque rupture.

Ulcerative colitis (D) presents with episodes of recurrent abdominal pain, grossly bloody stools, anemia, and weight loss. This condition only affects the colon, unlike Crohn disease, which affects any part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus. Ulcerative colitis is usually diagnosed at a younger age and symptoms are not necessarily associated with food intake.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common underlying condition that causes acute arterial occlusion mesenteric ischemia?

Reveal Answer:
Atrial fibrillation.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Ischemic Colitis

Most commonly caused by inadequate blood flow through the mesenteric vessels
Risks: atherosclerotic disease, aortoiliac surgery, cardiopulmonary bypass
Sx: acute onset of crampy abdominal pain, bloody bowel movement
Dx: CT imaging can show bowel wall edema
Tx: most cases resolve with supportive care
Add antibiotics for severe disease
Confirmed with colonoscopy

question: A 45-year-old man presents to the emergency department with epigastric abdominal pain with associated nausea that awoke him from sleep at 2 AM. The patient has previously had similar episodes of pain and had a positive outpatient urea breath test but has not started treatment yet. What medication is the best to be prescribed as part of the treatment regimen for this condition, in addition to antibiotics?
englishExplanation:
Gastritis is caused by inflammation of the gastric mucosa. Patients with gastritis often present with burning epigastric abdominal pain, which may be associated with nausea, abdominal fullness, and bloating. The clinical symptoms of gastritis are often difficult to distinguish from those of peptic ulcer disease. Patients with peptic ulcer disease most often develop pain several hours after eating a meal and at nighttime when gastric acid secretion is greatest.

Helicobacter pylori is a bacteria whose natural habitat is in the human stomach. Infection with Helicobacter pylori can occur in all age groups, is the most common cause of gastritis, and can lead to severe gastritis or peptic ulcer disease. It causes mucosal inflammation and leads to ulcerations. Diagnosis is often with a urea breath test. Medication regimens for the treatment of Helicobacter pylori infection include a combination of antibiotics and acid-suppressing agents with a proton pump inhibitor via either triple therapy or quadruple therapy. A triple therapy regimen typically includes clarithromycin plus either amoxicillin or metronidazole and a proton pump inhibitor. A quadruple therapy regimen typically involves bismuth-subsalicylate plus metronidazole, tetracycline, and a proton pump inhibitor. Treatment of the infection results in faster healing of ulcers, fewer recurrences, and a decreased risk of complications.



Calcium carbonate (A) is a type of antacid that may help relieve pain associated with gastritis and peptic ulcer disease, but it is not part of the triple or quadruple therapy treatment regimens for Helicobacter pylori.

Histamine H2 blockers (B) inhibit gastric acid production and are effective in treating peptic ulcer disease and gastritis. However, proton pump inhibitors are more effective and are recommended as part of the treatment regimens for Helicobacter pylori infection.

Misoprostol (C) is a prostaglandin analog that helps protect the gastric mucosa by decreasing acid secretion and reducing the amount of cyclic adenosine monophosphate that forms in response to histamine. Misoprostol may be used to prevent the development of NSAID-associated gastritis in patients with a high risk and is not part of the treatment regimen for Helicobacter pylori infections.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the condition that occurs in patients who consume excess amounts of calcium carbonate, characterized by hypercalcemia, alkalosis, and kidney insufficiency?

Reveal Answer:
Milk-alkali syndrome.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Gastritis

Inflammation associated with gastric mucosal injury
Causes include H.pylori, NSAIDs, alcohol, autoimmune disease
Dx: evaluation of biopsy specimen obtained from EGD
Tx: varies based on the underlying cause (e.g., stopping the offending agent)

question: An 85-year-old patient who resides in a nursing home presents with diffuse abdominal pain with nausea but no vomiting. Vital signs include a BP of 142/88 mm Hg, HR of 68 bpm, RR of 18/min, SpO2 of 95%, and T of 36.9°C (98.4°F). On physical examination, the abdomen is distended and tympanic to percussion. The above abdominal radiograph is obtained. What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Nasogastric tube placement and bowel rest

englishExplanation:
The radiograph demonstrates a markedly dilated single loop of colon consistent with sigmoid volvulus, often referred to as a bent inner tube sign without visible haustral markings. This is a closed-loop obstruction that results from the twisting of a mobile segment of bowel.

Sigmoid volvulus occurs almost entirely in two populations: older patients (mean age of 70 years) with debilitating, comorbid diseases who are bedridden and patients of any age with profound neurologic or psychiatric illness. Almost all patients have a history of chronic severe constipation. Patients present with progressive abdominal pain, abdominal distension, nausea, vomiting, and constipation. Fever is uncommon.

Although spontaneous reduction of a sigmoid volvulus can occur, it is infrequent enough to mandate procedural intervention. Sigmoidoscopy is used to decompress and detorse the bowel.



An enema (A) can be used in patients with constipation to help expel stool from the colon, but this is not useful in patients with a known volvulus and can delay definitive therapy.

Though often used, nasogastric tube placement and bowel rest (B) are usually inadequate. Decompression with a sigmoidoscope or even surgery may be necessary for definitive treatment.

Oral vancomycin and intravenous metronidazole (C) are used to treat fulminant Clostridioides difficile, which can present with toxic megacolon. Patients with toxic megacolon have signs of systemic toxicity, which are represented by some combination of fever, heart rate > 120 bpm, leukocytosis > 10,500/µL, anemia, dehydration, altered mental status, electrolyte disturbances, and hypotension. Additionally, the colon will be dilated on radiographic imaging.

Surgical resection (E) and fixation are reserved for when attempts at decompression with sigmoidoscopy are ineffective or when there is evidence of peritonitis or perforation.

One Step Further
Question:
How does a cecal volvulus appear on plain X-ray?

Reveal Answer:
A coffee bean shape with haustral markings.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Sigmoid Volvulus

Loop of bowel that twists around itself and its associated mesentery
Risk factors: advanced age, residence in long-term care facility, neurologic or psychiatric disease due to alterations in colonic motility, chronic constipation
Sx: gradual-onset diffuse abdominal pain, distention, constipation
Abdominal X-ray: U-shaped dilated loop of colon (coffee bean sign)
CT: whirl sign with a bird’s beak
Tx: endoscopic decompression to reduce volvulus, surgery for gangrene or inability to reduce volvulus
Elective surgery to prevent recurrence recommended
Complications: ischemia, gangrene, perforation

question: An 8-year-old girl is brought into the ED by her parents for a sore throat. She was seen by her pediatrician last week for a cold. She appears ill and her oral temperature is 103.6°F (39.8°C). She has a hoarse voice, frequent cough, stridor, and tracheal tenderness to palpation. There is no wheezing on auscultation. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Acute bacterial tracheitis is an obstructing infection of the upper airway primarily affecting children between 5 and 8 years, although it can occur in younger and older patients. It creates an inflammatory obstruction of the larynx, trachea, and upper bronchi that can be life-threatening. Patients present appearing toxic and have a mucopurulent sputum or cough, which differentiates it from similar conditions such as croup and epiglottitis. Fever, cough, and stridor may be a prodromal syndrome with airway obstruction rapidly following. When asked where the pain is the most, patients often point to the trachea. The trachea is often tender to palpation or manipulation. Plain film of the neck may show a hazy, irregular tracheal density with subglottic narrowing but is not needed for diagnosis. Staphylococcal species are most commonly implicated. Others include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus pyogenes, Moraxella catarrhalis, Haemophilus influenzae, and anaerobes. Management involves early airway control (preferably in the operating room), keeping the patient calm, intravenous fluids, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. In addition to intubation in a controlled setting, bronchoscopy may be therapeutic by removing purulent debris and relieving airway obstruction. Ampicillin-sulbactam or a combination of clindamycin and a third-generation cephalosporin (e.g., ceftriaxone) are recommended first-line antibiotics.



Epiglottitis (A) is historically seen in preschool-aged children unimmunized against Haemophilus influenzae type B. However, it is now most commonly caused by staphylococcal or streptococcal species. It presents with an abrupt onset of fever, dysphagia, dysphonia, and stridor without an antecedent viral prodrome.

An airway foreign body (B) usually causes acute symptoms in the absence of fever or purulent airway discharge in children ages 1–3 years with hyperorality (i.e., exploring items with their mouths).

Laryngotracheobronchitis (C), or croup, is seen in children ages 6 months to 3 years in the colder months with symptoms that get worse at night. Patients often have a classic seal-like “barking” cough and are nontoxic appearing.

One Step Further
Question:
What role does racemic epinephrine play in the management of acute bacterial tracheitis?

Reveal Answer:
None.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Bacterial Tracheitis

Causes: Staphylococcus aureus (most common), Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus pyogenes, Moraxella catarrhalis, Haemophilus influenzae, MRSA
Mean age range is 5–7 years, but most cases occur in patients under 6 years
High fever, barking cough, stridor
Presentation: looks like croup but in toxic-appearing child
X-ray: subglottic narrowing (steeple sign), tracheal irregularities or membranes in the lumen
Treat as airway emergency!

الفخ: أغلب الناس بيختاروا epiglottitis أو croup لأنهم بيسمعوا stridor مع حمى. الفرق إن الـ Tracheitis بتميّزه السعال مع sputum mucopurulent والـ trachea المؤلمة، والـ epiglottitis بيجي مع drooling وصعوبة بلع، والـ croup بتكون أصغر سناً وبتطلع مع barking cough.

question: A 5-month-old girl with no significant medical history and no allergies presents with fever and nasal congestion for 1 day. Examination reveals an uncomfortable but well-appearing infant with a fever to 102.7°F. Otoscopic evaluation reveals bilateral nonmobile, bulging tympanic membranes. Which of the following treatment regimens is appropriate?

options.text: Observation and close follow-up without initial antibiotics
Oral high-dose amoxicillin with clavulanic acid

englishExplanation:
This patient has bilateral acute otitis media (AOM), evidenced by the nonmobile, bulging tympanic membranes and fever. AOM is common in pediatric patients and a common indication for antibiotics.

AOM is commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis. Oftentimes, the infection can resolve without further intervention. Patients who are ≥ 6 months old with unilateral AOM and severe symptoms, as well as patients who are < 24 months with bilateral AOM, should receive antibiotic therapy. High-dose amoxicillin is the initial treatment of choice in patients without penicillin allergy.



Intramuscular ceftriaxone (A) is indicated for the treatment of AOM if first-line therapy is ineffective or if the patient has a history of a mild penicillin reaction (e.g., rash).

Observation and close follow-up without initial antibiotics (B) has recently become a treatment option endorsed by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) in select groups. The AAP recommends observation and repeat evaluation in 48–72 hours for patients 6 months to 2 years old with unilateral AOM without otorrhea and in children > 2 years of age with unilateral or bilateral AOM without otorrhea.

Oral azithromycin (C) can be used as an alternative to amoxicillin in patients with a severe penicillin allergy (e.g., anaphylaxis).

High-dose amoxicillin with clavulanic acid (E) can be used in patients who have received a beta-lactam antibiotic in the past 30 days.

One Step Further
Question:
What defines severe acute otitis media?

Reveal Answer:
Moderate to severe otalgia, otalgia for at least 48 hours, otorrhea, or temperature > 39°C (102.2°F).

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Otitis Media in Pediatrics

Most often infant or young child
Most common bacteria isolated include H. influenzae (nontypable), S. pneumoniae, and M. catarrhalis (there is decreased incidence of S. pneumoniae due to PCV13 vaccination)
Sx: ear pain, middle ear effusion + signs of infection or inflammation (fever, otorrhea, pus)
PE: erythema, bulge and decreased mobility of TM, purulent fluid
Tx: amoxicillin, consider amoxicillin-clavulanate in otitis-conjunctivitis syndrome
Consider period of observation if patient ≥ 2 years old and immunocompetent with mild symptoms
