question: A 54-year-old man with alcohol use disorder from southern Arizona presents secondary to cough, shortness of breath, and fever for the last 2 days. Chest radiograph shows a patchy right lower lobe infiltrate, and lab results reveal a normal eosinophil count. Which of the following is the most likely organism causing this patient’s pneumonia?
englishExplanation:
Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common bacteria to cause community-acquired pneumonia worldwide. The most common symptoms a patient may present with include dyspnea, cough, pleuritic chest pain, rust-colored sputum, and fever. Chest radiograph typically reveals a lobar infiltrate and antibiotic therapy is based upon severity and the most likely organism.



Blastomyces dermatitidis (A) is a fungal infection characterized by broad-based budding yeast. Alveolar infiltrates are characteristic on chest radiography.

Coccidioides immitis (B) is also a fungal infection that can cause pneumonia and is typically seen in the Southwestern United States. On laboratory evaluation, patients will typically have eosinophilia, which is reported normal in this patient.

Klebsiella pneumoniae (C) is more commonly a cause of pneumonia in people with alcohol use disorder. An upper lobe infiltrate is characteristic on chest radiography.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the recommended antibiotic treatment for Streptococcus pneumoniae in a patient without comorbidities?

Reveal Answer:
Amoxicillin, doxycycline, or a macrolide.

الفخ: أكثر إجابة غلط هي Klebsiella pneumoniae، لأن المريض عنده alcohol use disorder وكأنها البوابة. الفرق إن الـ CXR عند Klebsiella بيطلع upper lobe infiltrate، وهون الكيسة بنقص مع infiltrate عادي، و eosinophil count طبيعي بيقصي الفطريات زي Coccidioides.

question: A 21-year-old woman with a history of cystic fibrosis presents with a fever, increasing cough, and increasing sputum production. Her X-ray shows a right lower lobe infiltrate. She has not been hospitalized in the last 6 months. Which of the following medications should be included in her treatment regimen?
englishExplanation:
Cystic fibrosis is an autosomal recessive disease causing a mutation in the chloride transport system on the surface of exocrine glands. In the pulmonary organ system, patients develop a large amount of thick secretions. These thick secretions impair the normal function of the respiratory system, particularly, in the ability to expectorate mucous. Patients develop acute pulmonary exacerbations when they have a bacterial infection causing additional inflammation within the lung. The chest X-ray is often of limited utility in the diagnosis of pneumonia because of its baseline irregularities in patients with longstanding disease. When patients with cystic fibrosis develop pneumonia, broad-spectrum antibiotics are required to cover Staphylococcus aureus, Haemophilus influenzae, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. By the time patients reach 18 years of age, there is an 80% prevalence of Pseudomonas in pulmonary infections, and antibiotics like ciprofloxacin with activity against this organism must be administered. These patients should receive double coverage for Pseudomonas (e.g., piperacillin-tazobactam plus ciprofloxacin or an aminoglycoside). Patients also require aggressive chest physical therapy during the course of an acute pulmonary illness.



Amphotericin (A) is an antifungal agent. Patients with cystic fibrosis are not typically at risk for fungal infections treated with amphotericin unless there has been an environmental exposure. Other patients at risk for fungal infections include transplant recipients, patients on chemotherapy, or patients with advanced HIV.

Cefazolin (B) is a first-generation cephalosporin with good activity against gram-positive organisms. This agent is sometimes used in younger patients with cystic fibrosis. However, it is not commonly used in older patients.

Erythromycin (D) can be used for atypical pneumonia caused by atypical bacteria such as Mycoplasma pneuomoniae. However, it is not recommended in the treatment of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

One Step Further
Question:
What vitamin deficiencies do patients with cystic fibrosis develop?

Reveal Answer:
Vitamin A, D, E, and K deficiencies from gastrointestinal malabsorption.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Cystic Fibrosis

Autosomal recessive, CFTR gene
History of multiple recurrent respiratory infections or failure to thrive
Dx: newborn screen, elevated quantitative sweat chloride test
Pseudomonas aeruginosa most common infecting bacteria in recurrent pulmonary infections
Malabsorption (vit ADEK), steatorrhea, pancreatic insufficiency
Tx: airway clearance therapy, bronchodilators, DNase, pancreatic enzymes, empiric antibiotics (antipseudomonal), CTFR modulators (in patients with approved mutations), lung transplantation

question: What is the most common type of lung cancer in those who do not smoke?

options.text: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung

englishExplanation:
Responsible for over 150,000 deaths annually in the United States and almost 2 million deaths worldwide every year, lung cancer carries the greatest mortality of all malignancies, and excluding skin cancer, is outnumbered only by breast cancer in women and prostate cancer in men. To facilitate appropriate staging and treatment, lung cancer is further subdivided into small cell lung cancer (SCLC), which constitutes approximately 15% of diagnosed pulmonary malignancies, and nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which encompasses > 80% of lung malignancies and includes squamous cell carcinoma, large cell lung cancer, and adenocarcinoma of the lung, which is the most common type of lung cancer in both those who smoke (35% of cases) and those who do not smoke (70% of cases). The greatest risk factor for all classes of lung cancer remains smoking, with evidence showing a decrease in the incidence of all lung malignancies when patients quit, particularly before the age of 30. This further highlights the importance of providing counseling about the benefits of smoking cessation to patients who present to the emergency department, especially if their presentation is related to tobacco use. Other risk factors of note that should raise concern for lung cancer in the context of patient symptoms include radiation exposure, environmental toxins such as asbestos and radon, pulmonary fibrosis, alcohol use, and genetic predispositions based upon gathered family history.



Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung (D) is a form of NSCLC and is the second most common type of lung cancer, accounting for approximately 25% of cases.

Small cell lung cancer (C) represents approximately 15% of all lung malignancies and is known for more rapid growth but greater responsiveness to chemotherapy in comparison to NSCLC.

Large cell lung cancer (B) is far less frequently encountered than other types of lung cancer, constituting only about 10% of cases of NSCLC.

One Step Further
Question:
Individuals infected with what virus have approximately a fourfold increased incidence of lung cancer compared with noninfected individuals?

Reveal Answer:
Human immunodeficiency virus.

Non-small cell lung cancer (most common)
Adenocarcinoma, squamous cell, large cell
Tx depends on staging: surgical resection, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or tyrosine kinase inhibitors if positive for ALK or EGFR mutations
Small cell lung cancer
Associated with neuroendocrine and paraneoplastic syndromes
Metastasizes early, Tx may include chemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunotherapy, cranial irradiation
Leading cause of cancer-related death among men and women
Screening (USPSTF 2021)
Screen adults aged 50–80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years with an annual low-dose CT scan
Discontinue screening once the individual has not smoked for 15 years or has a limited life expectancy

Smoking أهم عامل خطر لكل الأنواع، وكل ما quit قبل سن 30 قلّت احتمالية المرض، فلازم تنصح أي مريض في الـ ED يquit.
الفخ: أكثر إجابة غلط هي squamous cell carcinoma أو small cell lung cancer، لأن الناس بتفكر اللي ما بيدخن بيوصله squamous. الفرق إن adenocarcinoma هي الأكثر شيوعاً عند اللي ما بيدخنوا وعند المدخنين كمان، و small cell بتمثل بس حوالي 15% من سرطانات الرئة.

question: A 13-year-old boy with a history of Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and spastic cerebral palsy who is nonverbal and nonambulatory and depends on a gastrostomy tube presents to the emergency department after an episode of vomiting at home 2 days ago. He has frequent visits to the hospital for his seizures and was intubated for status epilepticus 1 month ago. Today, his HR is 120 bpm, BP is 110/70 mm Hg, and SpO2 is 89%. After placing the patient on oxygen and obtaining a chest radiograph, you remain concerned about the possibility of aspiration pneumonia as a diagnosis. Which of the following should be considered in your treatment plan?
englishExplanation:
This patient is at risk for developing aspiration pneumonia, a complication of aspiration pneumonitis, which refers to chemical injury of lung tissue from aspiration of foreign material. Direct contact with the material causes injury to the alveolar-capillary membranes that can result in the destruction of surfactant and exudation of fluid and protein. This, in turn, can lead to atelectasis, alveolar hemorrhage, or the formation of consolidations like a granuloma or focal pneumonia. In certain patient populations, aspiration pneumonia may occur secondary to bacterial seeding of the damaged lung tissue.

This patient is chronically neurologically impaired with impaired swallowing and airway reflexes, which places him at a greater risk for aspiration during vomiting episodes. In uncomplicated cases of aspiration pneumonitis, the choice to start empiric antibiotics is controversial and should be tailored to the individual patient and clinical status. Some aspiration events will heal without the need for antibiotics. If a decision is made to treat with antibiotics, coverage against aerobes with ampicillin or clindamycin would be reasonable. Patients who are neurologically impaired or at risk for ventilator-associated infections should be given broad-spectrum antibiotics with coverage against Pseudomonas species. This patient is neurologically impaired, has frequent hospital admissions, and was recently intubated, putting him at risk for hospital-acquired infections. Therefore, this patient should receive piperacillin-tazobactam. If obtained, findings on a chest radiograph may initially be normal and should not be relied upon for patients highly suspected of having aspiration pneumonitis. This patient should also be admitted for continued monitoring, management of his hypoxia, and ongoing airway clearance.



Ampicillin-sulbactam (A) or clindamycin (B) are reasonable choices for treating aspiration pneumonia in an otherwise healthy patient without concerns for nosocomial infection. However, antibiotic use is generally reserved for patients with significant respiratory symptoms or signs of empyema.

There is no role for corticosteroids (C) in the treatment of aspiration pneumonia.

One Step Further
Question:
Aspiration of which toxic substances can lead to severe pneumonitis?

Reveal Answer:
Hydrocarbons.

Rapid Review

Risks: impaired consciousness, dysphagia, or seizure disorder
Sx: productive cough, fever, dyspnea on exertion
CXR: most common right upper lobe, posterior lobes
Polymicrobial (aerobic and anaerobic bacteria)
Tx
Amoxicillin-clavulanate
Ampicillin-sulbactam (inpatient, IV)
Clindamycin (penicillin allergy)
Moxifloxacin (adolescents)
Piperacillin-tazobactam (if neurologic impairment or tracheostomy)

الفخ: أكثر إجابة غلط هي clindamycin أو ampicillin-sulbactam أو corticosteroids. هالـ antibiotics البسيطة بتغطي aerobes وبتكون مقبولة في aspiration pneumonitis البسيط، بس هالطفل neurologically impaired وعنده admissions متكررة، فالـ broad-spectrum مع تغطية Pseudomonas هو الأنسب، والـ steroids مالهاش داعي.

question: What is the most common organism cultured from tracheal secretions in adult patients with cystic fibrosis?
englishExplanation:
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the most commonly recovered organism from respiratory cultures obtained in patients with cystic fibrosis. By 18 years of age, 80% of patients are colonized with Pseudomonas aeruginosa. When colonization is established, it is generally considered permanent. Therefore, antibiotic coverage should include a broad-spectrum penicillin in combination with an aminoglycoside for synergy.



Aspergillus fumigatus (A) and nontuberculosis Mycobacterium are also frequently encountered in patients with cystic fibrosis. However, they are not the most common organisms found.

Haemophilus influenza (B) and Staphylococcus aureus (D) are common organisms cultured in those newly diagnosed with cystic fibrosis but are found less often in those with chronic cystic fibrosis.

question: A 64-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a cough and shortness of breath that has progressively been worsening over the last several weeks. He has also been more fatigued and is unable to get around the house anymore. He reports no fever or night sweats. The patient has a history of hypertension and takes lisinopril daily. He emigrated from Argentina, where he used to work as a miner. He reports no tobacco use. What is the most likely diagnosis, based on the chest radiograph above?
englishExplanation:
This radiograph demonstrates bilateral diffuse ground-glass opacities. Many diseases are capable of mimicking this radiograph appearance and include mycobacterial and fungal infections, malignancy, occupational lung diseases, and autoimmune lung diseases. Other risk factors need to be taken into consideration when determining the most likely diagnosis so treatment can begin appropriately. Based on the information given, this patient is most likely presenting with pneumoconiosis, an occupational restrictive lung disease caused by inhalation of dust, often in mines, and from agriculture and construction work. Pneumoconiosis encompasses many occupational lung diseases, including coal workers’ pneumoconiosis, silicosis, and asbestosis. As a miner, this patient is at risk for pneumoconiosis. Diagnosis is based on risk factors, computed tomography imaging, biopsy, bronchoscopy, and lack of improvement after treatment for infectious causes. Treatment is largely supportive and includes reducing further lung insults by limiting exposures. Corticosteroids have been used to decrease inflammation, but no large randomized trials have been performed to truly know their benefit. The best way to avoid occupational lung disease is by prevention. Occupational Safety and Health Administration laws have been enacted in the United States since the 1970s to help prevent these illnesses, but these regulations are not necessarily followed in other countries.



Histoplasmosis (A)is a fungal lung disease that can also present with these radiograph findings. However, patients at risk for histoplasmosis include those at the extremes of age, immunocompromised individuals, and people who live in areas where histoplasmosis is found in the soil. These areas of the United States generally include the Ohio and Mississippi River valleys.

Miliary tuberculosis (B) is generally found in those with risk factors for tuberculosis, including immunocompromised individuals, those with previous tuberculosis, and individuals from endemic areas. Argentina is not one of those areas. Additionally, patients with long-standing tuberculosis more often present with low-grade fever and night sweats.

Sarcoidosis (D) usually presents between the ages of 20 and 40 years. Although it can be difficult to differentiate sarcoidosis from other entities, the mining risk factor leads the clinician toward pneumoconiosis instead of sarcoidosis in this patient.

One Step Further
Question:

Reveal Answer:
Amphotericin B.

question: An 11-month-old girl presents to the ED in February with symptoms including coughing and mild difficulty breathing. The parent states that the cough is getting worse and the baby sometimes gags while coughing but has not vomited. She has had nasal congestion and discharge and low-grade fever for about 2 days and is eating less than usual but still drinking fluids well. She has no significant medical history and is up to date with immunizations, including the first two doses of influenza vaccine. She attends daycare. The infant is alert and appropriately interactive but fussy. Her respiratory rate is 45 breaths/minute, her oxygen saturation is 97% on room air, her temperature is 38°C, and she has scattered mild expiratory wheezes and mild intercostal retractions. According to the American Academy of Pediatrics Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention of Bronchiolitis, which of the following is the most appropriate next step for this patient?

options.text: The patient can be discharged home with close follow-up without diagnostic testing or medication delivery in the ED
The patient does not require radiography or lab tests but should receive albuterol via metered dose inhaler or aerosol in the ED
The patient should receive a chest radiograph and oral steroids in the ED
The patient should receive aerosolized racemic epinephrine and be admitted

correctAnswer: The patient can be discharged home with close follow-up without diagnostic testing or medication delivery in the ED
englishExplanation:
This patient can be discharged home with close follow-up without diagnostic testing or medication delivery in the ED. Bronchiolitis is primarily a clinical diagnosis when an adequate medical history and examination can be obtained. This patient has no high-risk medical history (including prematurity, underlying cardiopulmonary disease, or immunodeficiency) or acute high-risk symptoms (such as severe respiratory distress, inability to maintain good hydration status, difficulty feeding, or apnea) and is maintaining adequate oral hydration. Her physical findings indicate mild to moderate illness severity. The American Academy of Pediatrics Guidelines for Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention of Bronchiolitis recognize the clinical nature of the diagnosis and recommend against routine usage of radiography and lab testing because they usually do not alter treatment or disposition unless severe respiratory distress or risk factors for severe illness are present or the diagnosis is unclear. In general, the guidelines also do not recommend prescribed medications in the ED or at home for this low-risk patient. Clinical studies have not found sufficient benefits from any medications to outweigh their potential risks. The guidelines also stress the importance of good hand hygiene practices to decrease the likelihood of disease transmission.



This patient does not require radiography or lab tests and she does not benefit from albuterol via metered dose inhaler or aerosol in the ED (B). Studies have not found clear significant or consistent benefits from short-acting beta agonist administration.

This patient does not require a chest radiograph and oral steroids in the ED (C). Chest radiography identifies an alternate diagnosis in < 1% of clinically diagnosed bronchiolitis patients and steroids have no proven benefit.

Racemic epinephrine and hospital admission (D) may be indicated in cases of severe croup, which presents with a barking cough and stridor. Aerosolized racemic epinephrine does not improve outcomes in patients with bronchiolitis. Additionally, admission is only indicated if the child cannot maintain oral fluid intake, severe respiratory distress or failure is present, or there are known high-risk factors for rapid progression of the disease.

One Step Further
Question:
What hand cleansing method do the World Health Organization, Centers for Disease Control, and American Academcy of Pediatrics all recommend if hands are not visibly soiled?

Reveal Answer:
Alcohol-based hand rubs are recommended because they remove organisms more effectively, require less time, and irritate skin less than other cleansing methods such as soap and water.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Bronchiolitis

Signs: 1- to 3-day prodromal URI symptoms
PE: tachypnea, retractions, polyphonic wheezing, rales
Diagnosis is made by history and physical exam
Most commonly caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)
Tx: supportive care (oxygen, fluids, nutrition, nasal suctioning), HFNC

ليش: حسب إرشادات American Academy of Pediatrics، التشخيص سريري بس لما التاريخ والفحص يكونوا كافيين. هي الطفلة مخاطرها منخفضة: ما عندها خلل قلبي رئوي ولا خلل مناعي، وبتحافظ على شربها، ونسبتها 97% مع مجهود خفيف بس. عشان هيك ما بحاجة أشعة مخبرية أو أدوية بالإدارة، والمطلوب متابعة ضيقة بالبيت، وكمان لازم نغسل إيدينا جيدًا عشان نقلّل انتقال المرض.
الفخ: الطلاب بيطلبوا أشعة صدر أو يعطوا albuterol بالإدارة، بس الإرشادات ما بتنصح فيهم بحالات الخطر المنخفض لأنهم ما بيغيّروا القرار، والعلاج الأساسي داعم ومتابعة.

question: A 54-year-old man who is intubated for respiratory failure has a worsening pulse oximetry. An X-ray is obtained in the supine position as seen above. Which of the following is demonstrated on this X-ray that supports a reason for his deteriorating oxygenation?
englishExplanation:
This X-ray demonstrates a secondary sign of pneumothorax called a deep sulcus sign. In some scenarios, most commonly when a patient is supine, a pneumothorax may not be visible on plain film. The deep sulcus sign is the deep lateral costophrenic angle on the side of the pneumothorax.



The silhouette sign (B) is seen on an X-ray when two substances of similar density touch each other, and as a result, the edges between them are blurred. This is classically seen in the presence of a right middle lobe pneumonia on a chest X-ray when the right heart border becomes obscured.

The spine sign (C) is seen on the lateral projection of a chest X-ray in the presence of pneumonia. Typically, the vertebrae become more lucent when moving inferiorly. In the presence of pneumonia in the posterior portion of the lung, the overlying infiltrate will make the vertebrae appear hyperdense.

Westermark sign (D) may be seen in a pulmonary embolism and is represented by the abrupt cut-off of vascular markings in the vessel where the clot is lodged, representing localized oligemia.

One Step Further
Question:
What ultrasonographic signs are associated with pneumothorax?

Reveal Answer:
Bar code sign on M-mode caused by the lack of lung sliding.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Spontaneous Pneumothorax

Risk factors: tall, thin, male sex, age 10–30 years, Marfan syndrome, cigarette smoking, COPD, tuberculosis, cystic fibrosis, ILD, Pneumocystis pneumonia
Primary is without underlying lung disease
Secondary is with underlying lung disease
Sx: acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain
PE: decreased breath sounds, decreased fremitus, hyperresonance to percussion
Dx
Upright CXR: absence of lung markings along lung periphery
Pleural U/S: absence of lung sliding
Tx
Small ≤ 2–3 cm (or < 25% pleural space), no respiratory compromise: observation with oxygen administration
Large > 2–3 cm, symptomatic: needle aspiration or chest tube thoracostomy
Recurrent: VATS, pleurodesis in a healthy patient
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض مربوط بالتنبيب ومستلقي على ظهره، والأشعة بتبين علامة ثانوية لـ pneumothorax اسمها deep sulcus sign، يعني الزاوية الحدّية الجانبية بصير أعمق على نفس الجانب. هاي بتظهر بالضيق لأنه لما يكون المريض مستلقي الـ pneumothorax ما بيكون مبين بالأشعة العادية، فبندوّر على هاي العلامة بدل ما نعتمد على الهواء الظليل الكلاسيكي.
الفخ: الطلاب بيفسّروا العلامة بـ silhouette sign أو spine sign، بس الـ silhouette معناها اختفاء حدود القلب، والـ spine sign بتشوفها بأشعة الصدر الجانبية بمرض الـ pneumonia.

question: A 70-year-old man with known COPD presents to the ED with his chronic COPD shortness of breath that occurs while walking on level ground. He often needs to stop to catch his breath. He has had no exacerbations or hospitalizations in the past year. How should this patient be categorized, according to the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease classification?
englishExplanation:
The Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) 2026 ABE classification system stratifies patients with COPD based on symptom burden and exacerbation history. Symptom severity is assessed using either the modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale or the Chronic Airway Assessment Test (CAAT), with high symptom burden defined as an mMRC score ≥ 2 or a CAAT score ≥ 10.

The mMRC dyspnea scale ranges from 0 to 4 and reflects the degree of functional limitation caused by dyspnea. An mMRC score of 0 describes dyspnea only with strenuous exercise. A score of 1 indicates shortness of breath when hurrying on level ground or walking up a slight hill. A score of 2 reflects walking slower than peers on level ground because of dyspnea or needing to stop when walking at one’s own pace. A score of 3 describes stopping for breath after walking approximately 100 meters or after a few minutes on level ground. A score of 4 indicates being too breathless to leave the house or experiencing dyspnea while dressing.

Within the GOLD ABE framework, Group A comprises patients with a low symptom burden (mMRC score 0 or 1 and CAAT score < 10) and low exacerbation risk. Group B includes patients with a high symptom burden (mMRC score ≥ 2 or CAAT score ≥ 10) but without frequent exacerbations or prior hospitalization. Group E includes patients with frequent exacerbations or a history of hospitalization, regardless of symptom severity.

This patient is classified as Group B because he has significant dyspnea reflected by an mMRC score of at least 2 or a CAAT score of at least 10, indicating a high symptom burden, but does not have a history of frequent exacerbations or hospitalization.

The GOLD classification can be useful in the ED, as it helps clinicians identify higher-risk patients, anticipate future exacerbations, and make safer admission versus discharge decisions once the acute episode is stabilized. It also informs appropriate outpatient maintenance therapy, vaccination review, and follow-up planning at ED discharge, thereby reducing early relapse and readmission.



Group A (A) includes patients with low symptom burden, usually corresponding to an mMRC score of 0 to 1. This patient's functional limitation and breathlessness with mild exertion suggest an mMRC score of at least 2, excluding group A.

Group C (C) and group D (D) were included in the earlier GOLD ABCD classification but were excluded from the updated ABE model because group C was rare and offered no distinct treatment advantage, with treatment and outcomes largely overlapping with those of patients with a high risk.

Group E (E) includes any patient with a history of at least one moderate or severe exacerbation in the past year, regardless of symptom severity. This patient has not experienced any exacerbations and so does not meet the criteria for group E.

One Step Further
Question:
What factors are included in the Chronic Airway Assessment Test score?

Reveal Answer:
Cough, sputum production, chest tightness, breathlessness with activity, activity limitation, confidence leaving home, sleep quality, and energy level.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)

Closely associated with chronic bronchitis and emphysema
Dx requires
Pulmonary symptoms (dyspnea, cough, or sputum production), clinical context (smoking), and airflow limitation
Postbronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.7 on spirometry
Patients with hypoxemia should be given supplemental oxygen with SpO2 goal of 88–92%
Management options include bronchodilators, anticholinergics, steroids, supplemental oxygen, noninvasive ventilation, smoking cessation, vaccinations, and antibiotics for severe disease, infection present, or those requiring ventilation
arabicExplanation:
ليش: حسب تصنيف GOLD الجديد ABE، التصنيف بيعتمد على شدة الأعراض وسجل التفاقم. هاد المريض بيمشي على أرض مستوية وبيضطر يتوقف ليتنفّس، وهاد بيوافق درجة 2 بقياس mMRC اللي بيوصف المشي ببطء أو التوقف عند المشي، يعني عنده عبء أعراض عالي. بس ما عنده تفاقم ولا دخول مستشفى بالسنة الماضية، عشان هيك ينحط بالمجموعة B مش E.
الفخ: الطلاب بيفكّروا بالمجموعة A لأنه ما في تفاقم، بس المجموعة A للعبء الأعراضي المنخفض بس ودرجة mMRC أقل من 2، والمشي ببطء والوقوف باستمرار هو اللي بيدل على الشدة العالية.

question: A 67-year-old man who weighs 80 kg and has a history of COPD presents to the emergency department with dyspnea, wheezing, and hypoxia. He is given broad-spectrum antibiotics, albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers, and methylprednisolone, but his respiratory status deteriorates and he is intubated. His ventilator settings include TV 640 mL, RR 12/min, and PEEP 5 cm H2O. His current oxygen saturation on the ventilator is 90%. Poor air movement with wheezes is heard bilaterally, and there is ventilator dyssynchrony. The patient’s pH is 7.00. Which of the following would be the most appropriate initial change to the ventilator settings?

options.text: Increase the fraction of inspired oxygen

englishExplanation:
COPD is associated with chronic smoking that results in increased mucus production and loss of alveolar elasticity, leading to air trapping and poor ventilation. Management of an acute COPD flare should be centered on maximal medical therapy to avoid intubation and includes albuterol-ipratropium bronchodilators, corticosteroids, magnesium sulfate (albeit only sometimes, with evidence only supporting its use in asthma, though it is a safe medication often given in COPD flares), and antibiotics that cover for community-acquired pneumonia (for moderate and severe exacerbations). Early use of high-flow oxygen therapy and bilevel positive airway pressure may reduce work of breathing and thus respiratory muscle fatigue.

In patients who must be intubated due to respiratory failure, careful management of the ventilator with a focus on lung-protective strategies is critical. In ventilated COPD exacerbations, ideal management is focused on low TVs (6–8 mL/kg) to avoid lung injury and pneumothorax, a prolonged expiratory phase to allow for full exhalation and to avoid breath stacking (which can be evident by ventilator dyssynchrony), a decreased respiratory rate again to avoid breath stacking, reduced peak pressures to avoid injury to the lung parenchyma, and use of a fraction of inspired oxygen that avoids hyperoxia and hypoxia. Permissive hypercapnia is employed to avoid the increased danger of breath-stacking and barotrauma with a target pH above 7.20. Ventilated patients should be admitted to the intensive care unit with early pulmonology consultation for further care and careful titration of the ventilator.



Increasing the fraction of inspired oxygen (A) should be avoided in this patient to prevent hyperoxia. Patients with COPD typically have hypoxia at baseline, and an oxygen saturation of 88–92% is appropriate. Increasing the TV (B) further should be avoided in ventilated patients with COPD. Their lungs are friable, and high TVs may cause pneumothoraces. Rather, lower TVs should be used. This patient’s current TV is 8 mL/kg if he is an 80 kg man. His TV should not be increased further. Reducing the respiratory rate (D) may be necessary to allow for full exhalation and to prevent breath stacking. However, patients with COPD exacerbations often have respiratory acidosis that requires increased minute ventilation through an increased respiratory rate. It is generally preferred to first prolong the expiratory phase in a patient with bronchospasm and then choose a respiratory rate that allows for proper exhalation while managing the patient’s pH. It would be helpful to increase the respiratory rate in this patient to increase the minute ventilation and treat the acidosis.

One Step Further
Question:
What can be done to immediately relieve peak pressure in a patient with significant breath stacking?

Reveal Answer:
Disconnect the ventilator and apply pressure to the chest.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Mechanical Ventilation

Pulmonary contusion: low TV
Asthma or COPD: low TV, low RR, decreased I:E ratio
ARDS: high PEEP, low TV, lowest tolerated FiO2
Pregnancy: avoid hypoxia, control hypercarbia
Neonates: pressure-controlled ventilation
Acidosis: higher TV, higher RR
Head injury: avoid hypercapnia
Complications
Volutrauma
Barotrauma
Ventilator-associated pneumonia
Hemodynamic instability (high RR or PEEP → ↓ venous return → ↓ cardiac output → hypotension)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده COPD وصار في ventilator dyssynchrony، وهاد بيدل على تكدّس هواء breath stacking. الحل إنه نمدّ مرحلة الزفير عشان الرئة تفرّغ كل هواها قبل ما تيجي دفعة جديدة، وهاد بيمنع التكدّس. وكمان بنخفّض معدل التنفّس وبنمسك الـ TV منخفض وبنضبط الـ FiO2 عشان نحمي الرئة من الإصابة ونتجنّب نقص الأكسجين وفائضه.
الفخ: الطلاب بيفكّروا برفع نسبة الأكسجين أو الـ TV عشان يحسّنوا القراءة، بس هدول ما بحلّوا مشكلة الزفير القصير، والدليل على تكدّس الهواء هو عدم تزامن الجهاز مع المريض.

question:
A 65-year-old patient presents to the Emergency Department with acute respiratory failure requiring high-flow
oxygen therapy.
Which of the following represents the duration a CD oxygen cylinder will last when delivering oxygen at 15L/min?
englishExplanation:
30 minutes
Explanation

A CD cylinder has 460L oxygen.
To calculate how long an oxygen cylinder will last, use the formula: Duration (minutes) = Cylinder volume (L) ÷ Flow
rate (L/min) = 460L ÷ 15L/min = 30.6 minutes
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اسطوانة CD بتحتوي 460 لتر أكسجين، وبحسب المعادلة نقسم الحجم على معدل التدفق لنتعرف على المدة بالدقائق. يعني 460 لتر مقسومة على 15 لتر بالدقيقة بتعطينا تقريبًا 30.6 دقيقة. ولو كلنا نحسبها بطريقة تانية، كل 15 لتر بتنفد بدقيقة واحدة بالضبط، فحتى نخلص الـ 460 لتر بدها حوالي نص ساعة.
الفخ: الطلاب بيلقوا على 15 دقيقة لأنهم بيخلطوا معدل التدفق بساعة، أو على 60 دقيقة لأنهم بيفكّروا الأسطوانة أكبر؛ بس لازم نقسم 460 لتر على 15 لتر بالدقيقة بدون ما نغيّر الوحدات.

question:
A 65-year-old male with acute exacerbation of COPD is initiated on NIV. His pre-NIV ABG shows pH 7.18, pCO2
11.0 kPa, and pO2 8.9 kPa. After 1 hour of NIV at 15/3, his ABG is unchanged. His saturations are 90% on a FiO2 of
0.21.
Which of the following NIV adjustments would be most appropriate?

options.text: Increase EPAP to 12 cm H2O, maintain IPAP at 15 cm H2O
Decrease IPAP to 12 cm H2O, maintain EPAP at 3 cm H2O
Increase IPAP to 20 cm H2O, maintain EPAP at 3 cm H2O
Decrease EPAP to 2 cm H2O, increase IPAP to 18 cm H2O
Maintain both IPAP at 15 cm H2O and EPAP at 3 cm H2O

correctAnswer: Increase IPAP to 20 cm H2O, maintain EPAP at 3 cm H2O
englishExplanation:
Increase IPAP to 20 cm H2O, maintain EPAP at 3 cm H2O
Explanation
The patient has a hypercapnic respiratory failure (elevated CO2) with acidosis, requiring increased ventilatory
support.
IPAP-EPAP difference (driving pressure) controls ventilation and CO2 removal; increasing IPAP while maintaining
EPAP increases this pressure difference, improving CO2 clearance.
EPAP does not need reduction as oxygenation is adequate.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده فشل تنفسي هيبركابني مع حموضة ومش متحسّن بعد ساعة على NIV، فلازم نزيد الدعم التهوييلي. الفرق بين الـ IPAP والـ EPAP هو ضغط الحركة اللي بيتحكّم بالتهوية وإخراج CO2، عشان هيك نزيد الـ IPAP ونخلّي الـ EPAP ثابت. التأكسد عنده كافي، فما في داعي نغيّر الـ EPAP، والهدف هو تحسين إخراج CO2 وتصحيح الحموضة.
الفخ: الطلاب بينزّلوا الـ EPAP أو ينزّلوا الـ IPAP خوفًا من الضغط، بس هيك بتصير فرق الضغط أقل وبيرجع CO2 يزيد؛ المطلوب زيادة الدفع مش نقصانه.

question:
A 67-year-old male presents to the Emergency Department with acute exacerbation of COPD. His vital signs show
RR 28, HR 110, BP 145/85, and SpO2 88% on room air.
Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for initiating NIV?

options.text: Recent facial trauma with unstable fractures

correctAnswer: Recent facial trauma with unstable fractures
englishExplanation:
Recent facial trauma with unstable fractures
Explanation
Recent facial trauma with unstable fractures is an absolute contraindication for NIV as:
The mask interface cannot form an adequate seal on the damaged facial structures
Pressure from the mask may worsen injuries and cause further displacement of fractures
Risk of compromising the airway due to unstable facial structures
Absolute contraindication to NIV
Severe facial deformity
Facial burns
Fixed upper airway obstruction
Relative contraindication to NIV
pH <7.15
GCS < 8/15
Confusion/ Agitation
Cognitive impairment
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الكسور غير المستقرة بالوجه مانع مطلق لبدء الـ NIV، لأنه القناع ما بقدر يعمل إغلاق محكم على الأنسجة المكسورة. وضغط القناع ممكن يزيد إزاحة الكسور ويخسّر الطريق الهوائي، فالمخاطرة عالية جدًا. وفي مانعات نسبية تانية مثل الـ pH أقل من 7.15 أو الـ GCS أقل من 8، وهدول بس بيأجّلوا القرار مش بيمنعوه نهائيًا.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا الـ pH 7.08 أو الـ GCS 10/15 لأنهم أرقام مقلقة، بس هدول مانعات نسبية، والمانع المطلق المذكور هو كسور الوجه غير المستقرة بس.

question:
A 45-year-old female with BMI 42 presents to the Emergency Department with worsening breathlessness. Her arterial blood gas shows pH 7.32, pCO2 7.2 kPa, and pO2 8.1 kPa on room air. She is a non-smoker and has no respiratory history.
Which I:E ratio setting would be most appropriate when initiating NIV?
englishExplanation:
1:1
Explanation

In obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OHS), patients often have increased airway resistance and reduced chest wall
compliance.
A 1:1 ratio allows equal time for inspiration and expiration, which helps prevent air trapping and reduces the work of
breathing.
An I:E ratio of 1:2-1:3 is recommended for COPD.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة سمينة وعندها obesity hypoventilation syndrome، والتهوية عندها صعبة بسبب قبّس الصدر المرتفع ومقاومة الممرات الهوائية. نسبة شهيق لزفير 1:1 بتعطي وقت متساوي للشهيق والزفير، وهاد بيساعد يمنع تكدّس الهواء وينقص مجهود التنفس. وبنستعمل 1:2 لحدة 1:3 بحالات الـ COPD مش بهالحالة، فالمطلوب هون تهوية كافية بدون تكدّس أو إرهاق لعضلات التنفس.
الفخ: الطلاب بيلقوا على 1:2 أو 1:3 لأنهم متعودين عليها بمرض الـ COPD، بس هون المريضة عندها obesity hypoventilation syndrome مش COPD، ولو استخدمنا 1:3 راح يصير عندها تكدّس هواء لأن الزفير ما بيكمل.

question:
A 25-year-old woman presents to the Emergency Department with worsening shortness of breath over the last 24
hours. She is able to complete sentences, has a respiratory rate of 22/min, a heart rate of 105/min, and her peak
flow is 65% of her best. She has no accessory muscle use.
What is the severity of this patient's asthma flare?
englishExplanation:
Moderate acute asthma
Explanation
This patient has moderate acute asthma based on her presenting symptoms and signs. 
Peak flow 65% (within the 50-75% range for moderate asthma)
Able to complete sentences (no severe breathlessness)
Mild tachycardia (HR 105) but not severe (>110)
No features of severe asthma
https://bnf.nice.org.uk/treatment-summaries/asthma-acute/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة بتقدر تكمّل جملها ودرجة peak flow عندها 65%، وهاد بنطاق 50-75% اللي بيشمل الربو الحاد المتوسط. نبضها 105 بس مش شديد لأنه ما تعدّى 110، وما في استعمال عضلات مساعدة. عشان هيك ما في علامات ربو حاد ولا مهدّد للحياة، والتصنيف بيحصل بجمع peak flow والأعراض معًا مش على الرقم لحاله.
الفخ: الطلاب بيلقوا على acute severe asthma لأنه النبض مرتفع وpeak flow ناقص، بس الشدة بتصير شديدة لما peak flow ينزل تحت 50% أو لما المريض ما يقدر يكمّل جمل أو يستعمل عضلات مساعدة.

question:
A 28-year-old male presents to the Emergency Department with sudden onset right-sided chest pain and mild
shortness of breath following 3 days of upper respiratory tract infection symptoms. Chest X-ray shows a 2cm (at
the hilum) pneumothorax on the right side.
Observations are HR 89, RR 18, saturations 98% on room air, BP 127/71, Temperature 36.8. The patient has no
past medical history and wants to avoid a procedure.
Which is the most appropriate management plan?
englishExplanation:
Follow-up in 2-4 days
Explanation
According to current guidelines, conservative management with observation is appropriate for a small (2cm) primary
spontaneous pneumothorax in a stable patient with minimal symptoms and no high-risk features.

question:
A 45-year-old male presents to the Emergency Department with shortness of breath after a house fire.
Which of the following statements regarding pulse oximetry readings is correct?

options.text: Pulse oximetry will accurately reflect oxygen saturation in carbon monoxide poisoning
Hypothermia will not affect pulse oximetry readings
Carboxyhaemoglobin causes falsely elevated SpO2 readings
Methemoglobinemia typically causes SpO2 readings around 85-90%
Hypovolemia always leads to inaccurate pulse oximetry readings

correctAnswer: Carboxyhaemoglobin causes falsely elevated SpO2 readings
englishExplanation:
Carboxyhaemoglobin causes falsely elevated SpO2 readings
Explanation
Carboxyhaemoglobin causes falsely elevated SpO2 readings because pulse oximeters cannot distinguish between carboxyhaemoglobin and oxyhaemoglobin, as they both absorb light similarly at the wavelengths used (660nm and
940nm). This makes pulse oximetry unreliable in carbon monoxide poisoning.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: جهاز الـ pulse oximetry ما بيقدر يفرّق بين الـ carboxyhaemoglobin والـ oxyhaemoglobin، لأنهم بيمتصوا الضوء بنفس الطريقة عند الموجات المستخدمة 660nm و940nm. عشان هيك القراءة بتطلع أعلى من الحقيقة بالمسموم بأول أكسيد الكربون، وهاد بيخلي القياس غير موثوق به بهالحالات. وعشان هيك لازم نتشكّك بالرقم العالي ونكمل التقييم السريري بدل ما نعتمد عليه لحاله.
الفخ: الطلاب بيصدّقوا قراءة الـ SpO2 العالية ويفكّروا المريض مستقر، بس هاد المريض مسموم بأول أكسيد الكربون؛ عشان هيك الرقم العالي بيبينه مستقر والحقيقة مش هيك.

question:
A 32-year-old experienced scuba diver presents to the Emergency Department with sudden onset chest pain and
shortness of breath after surfacing from a 30-meter dive. His observations are normal. He has increased vocal resonance on the right.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Pneumothorax
Explanation
According to Boyle's Law, gas expands as pressure decreases during ascent from a deep dive. If a diver holds their
breath during ascent, the expanding air can cause alveolar rupture, leading to pneumothorax.
The sudden onset of chest pain and dyspnoea after surfacing, along with the examination, is classic for this
presentation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: حسب قانون Boyle، الهواء بيتوسّع لما الضغط بيقل أثناء الصعود من غطس عميق، وإذا الغطّاس مسك أنفاسه الهواء المتوسّع بيكسر الحويصلات وبيسبّب pneumothorax. وفجأة ضغط الصدر وضيق النفس بعد ما طلع مع زيادة الرنين الصوتي على اليمين هي الصورة الكلاسيكية لهالتشخيص. ومؤشراته الطبيعية ما بتنفي التشخيص، لأن الـ pneumothorax الصغيرة ممكن تظل خفيفة وما تسبّب نقص أكسجة كبير.
الفخ: الطلاب بيلقوا على Pulmonary Barotrauma لأنه مصطلح غطس شائع، بس هاي بيشمل كسر الحويصلات نفسه؛ والعلامة المميزة هون هي زيادة الرنين الصوتي على نفس الجانب اللي بتدل على تجمع هواء بالتجويف الجنبي.

question:
A 40-year-old patient is found down, without identification or medical alert bracelet. No history is available. Vital signs are T 39°C, HR 110, BP 140/76, RR 
28, and SpO2 79% on RA. Physical examination is 
notable for rhonchi on the right. An Emergency Medical Technician applies 100% O2 by nonrebreather 
and the patient’s SpO2 rises to 85%. Which of the following is the MOST LIKELY cause of this patient’s 
presentation?
englishExplanation:
3.  The answer is C. (Chapter 62) This patient has a partial but incomplete response to supplemental oxygen, 
which is the hallmark of shunt physiology. Patients with 
a right-to-left shunt, whether intracardiac, vascular, or 
intrapulmonary, will always transmit some percentage 
of deoxygenated blood from the right to left circulation, 
resulting in persistent desaturation since some fraction 
of blood never encounters pulmonary oxygen. Asphyxia 
presents with desaturation, but the hypoxia resolves with 
increased oxygenation. Chronic obstructive pulmonary 
disease (COPD) can present with some degree of intrapulmonary shunting, but it generally presents as ventilation/
perfusion (V/Q) mismatch, which responds completely 
to inhaled oxygen. Additionally, a COPD patient would 
be expected to present with wheezes and air trapping, 
while this patient presents with focal rhonchi. Pneumonia 
creates an intrapulmonary shunt, during which exudate 
fills the alveoli and prevents gas exchange. The picture is 
typically a mix of V/Q mismatch and shunt, depending 
on the degree of consolidation. In a case of pneumonia, 
some portions of the disease demonstrate V/Q mismatch, which leads to the partial response to oxygen but 
the shunt fraction remains, which prevents a complete 
response. Note, shunt physiology presents with either no, 
OR partial, response to oxygen. Pulmonary embolus typically presents with V/Q mismatch, given the obstruction 
to blood flow.

![Tintinalli-2023-00153 source page 70](images/Tintinalli-2023-00153-Tintinalli-2023-p0070.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00153 source page 71](images/Tintinalli-2023-00153-Tintinalli-2023-p0071.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00153 source page 81](images/Tintinalli-2023-00153-Tintinalli-2023-p0081.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده نقص أكسجة ما بستجيب كامل للأكسجين العالي، وهاد هو العلامة المميزة لـ shunt physiology. بالتهاب الرئة بيملأ الحويصلات بانصباب ويمنع تبادل الغازات، فبيصير خليط بين V/Q mismatch وshunt، عشان هيك الرد بيبقى جزئي مش كامل. أما الـ COPD فالتهوية فيها المشكلة مش التروية فبتجاوب كاملة مع الأكسجين، والاختناق بيزول نقص الأكسجين فيه مع زيادة الأكسجين.
الفخ: الطلاب بيفكّروا بـ pulmonary embolus أو COPD لأنها أسباب شائعة لنقص الأكسجة، بس الرد الجزئي على الأكسجين بيميّز الـ shunt اللي بيعمله التهاب الرئة مش الرد الكامل.

question:
A 20-month-old infant with family history of asthma 
and atopic disease presents to the emergency department with 3 days of worsening upper respiratory congestion, cough, wheezing, and fevers. The parents say 
there have been many sick contacts at daycare this 
winter. Vital signs reveal T 38°C, HR 140, BP 96/50, 
RR 40, and SpO2 94% on RA. Physical examination 
is notable for scattered end-expiratory wheezing in 
all fields, crackles in the bilateral central lung fields, 
occasional cough, and supraclavicular retractions. 
There is no stridor. The patient is treated with albuterol with limited response. Which of the following 
is the MOST LIKELY diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
4.  The answer is B. (Chapter 127) While this patient has 
risk factors and features of many of these conditions, his 
wheezing without response to albuterol plus crackles, and 
absence of stridor and nontoxic appearance make bronchiolitis the most likely diagnosis. Bronchiolitis presents 
in children younger than 2 years, with a changing clinical 
examination with variable features, including wheezing, 
rhonchi, and crackles, with variably borderline oxygen 
saturation. It has no specific treatment beyond supportive care, and most often the work of breathing responds 
to high flow oxygen by nasal cannula. Asthma is a distracting answer given the family history of asthma and the 
clinical picture of wheezing in the setting of a respiratory 
infection. Age 2 years, however, is the threshold at which 
asthma is diagnosed; prior to this age, reactive airway disease is the clinical diagnosis. Both asthma and reactive 
airway disease have a hallmark response to albuterol, and 
the absent response in this case argues strongly against 
a reactive airway component. Croup, characterized by 
upper airway narrowing, is typically accompanied by 
stridor, and an overall clinical picture with cyanosis and 
respiratory distress is absent in this patient. There may 
be a component of airway narrowing in young children 
due to anatomical reductions in airway caliber, which limits tolerability of swelling, but this patient has no symptoms to suggest it. Epiglottitis is characterized by upper 
airway swelling, and the patient has no symptoms of 
upper airway obstruction.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عمره أقل من سنتين وعنده سعال وصفير وأصوات رجيج بالرئتين وما استجاب للـ albuterol. هاد مهم لأنه الربو وreactive airway disease بتجاوب مع الـ albuterol، فعدم الاستجابة بتنفيهم، وكمان ما في stridor فمش croup. وعمره تحت حد تشخيص الربو، فالتشخيص الأرجح هو bronchiolitis اللي ما إلها علاج محدد غير الرعاية الداعمة.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا Asthma بسبب تاريخ العائلة بالحساسية والربو، بس الحد لتشخيص الربو هو سنتين، وما قبلها اسمها reactive airway disease وبتجاوب حتمًا مع الـ albuterol.

question:
In adults, which of the following is the MOST common cause of pleural effusions with a pH of 7.3, pleural lactate dehydrogenase <200, and pleural protein 
<50% of serum protein level?
englishExplanation:
6.  The answer is B. (Chapter 62) By applying Light’s criteria, the pleural fluid is a transudate. In terms of overall 
prevalence of conditions, heart failure is the most common, and therefore causes the most transudative effusions. Cirrhosis, with less prevalence than heart failure, 
can also cause a transudative effusion, known as hepatic 
hydrothorax. Nephrotic syndrome, owing to the hypoalbuminemic state, can cause changes in oncotic pressure 
leading to fluid leakage from capillaries. Streptococcus 
pneumoniae, the most common pathogen in pneumonia, 
occasionally causes exudative pleural effusion.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بمقياس Light's criteria السائل بهالمواصفات بيطلع transudate، ومن بين كل الأمراض اللي بتعمل سوائل transudative الـ heart failure هي الأكثر شيوعًا بالبالغين عشان هيك بتسبب أكبر عدد منها. الـ cirrhosis بتعمل نفسه بس اسمه hepatic hydrothorax، والنفرتيك بتنقص الألبومين فيقلّ الضغط التناضحي فتسرّب السوائل من الشعيرات. أما التهاب الرئة بيعمل exudate مش transudate، فمش ضمن هالتصنيف.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا Nephrotic syndrome لأنه بيفكّروا بنقص الألبومين وتسرّب السوائل، بس الـ heart failure أكتر شيوعًا؛ والتمييز بيحصل بحساب Light's criteria أول شي عشان نعرف إنه transudate مش exudate.

question:
A 56-year-old woman presents to the emergency 
department with 4 days of multiple complaints. She 
visited a local spa with friends last week and had a 
massage, steam shower, and soaked in a hot tub. The 
patient has fever, chills, headache, muscle aches, 
shortness of breath, and dry cough. She has had 
a poor appetite associated with nausea, vomiting, 
and loose stools with some abdominal cramping. 
Past medical history includes hypertension, type 2 
diabetes, dyslipidemia, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. She smokes ½ pack of cigarettes per 
day, drinks two glasses of wine on the weekends, and 
does not use drugs. Recent travel includes one short 
trip to the local beach last month, on the first day of 
summer. She denies international travel or camping. 
She has had one sick contact, her friend from the spa 
weekend, who also recently became ill. She recalls 
that they had different meals at lunch that day. Physical examination demonstrates scattered rales. Chest 
x-ray is shown in Figure 6.2 and is read as diffuse 
patchy infiltrates and hilar adenopathy. What is the 
MOST COMMONLY performed test used to rapidly 
identify the likely pathogen?
FIGURE 6.2  J.E. Tintinalli, J.S. Stapczynski, O.J. Ma, D. Yearly, G.D. Meckler, D.M. Cline: 
Tintinalli’s Emergency Medicine: A Comprehensive Study Guide, 9th Edition: Copyright © 
McGraw-Hill Education. All rights reserved.
englishExplanation:
18.  The answer is D.  (Chapter 65) This patient most 
likely has Legionella pneumoniae. Risk factors for Legionella include tobacco use, chronic lung disease, being a 
transplant recipient (especially in the first 3 months posttransplant), and immunosuppression. Legionella can 
cause a wide array of symptoms, from benign disease to 
multisystem organ failure and acute respiratory distress 
syndrome. There is no seasonality to L. pneumoniae, but 
it is observed more frequently in the summer months as 
the frequency of other pathogens wanes. In about half of 
patients with community-acquired pneumonia, no specific pathogen is identified. A complete blood count would 
be nonspecific. The concurrent gastrointestinal distress in 
the setting of the confirmed pneumonia points to Legionella alone, rather than both a primary intestinal source 
and a respiratory source of infection. With no travel history, nor ingestion of freshwater (as occurs with campers), the likelihood of a parasite is also low. The sputum 
of patients with Legionella demonstrates few neutrophils 
and no predominant bacterial species. Although sputum 
culture detects all species of legionella, it is technically difficult, requires special agar media, and takes at least 5 days 
to obtain results. Therefore, sputum analysis in Legionella 
is inferior to the commonly available urinary antigen test 
for detection, which is rapid and yields same day results.

![Tintinalli-2023-00168 source page 73](images/Tintinalli-2023-00168-Tintinalli-2023-p0073.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00168 source page 74](images/Tintinalli-2023-00168-Tintinalli-2023-p0074.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00168 source page 84](images/Tintinalli-2023-00168-Tintinalli-2023-p0084.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الحالة بتتوافق مع التهاب رئة بـ Legionella، وأهم عوامل الخطر عندها هو التدخين والمرض الرئوي المزمن. التحليل السريع والشائع اللي بيستعمل لاكتشاف المسبب هو urinary antigen test، لأنه متوفر وعملي، بعكس زرع البلغم اللي بياخد 5 أيام وصعب تقنيًا ومحتاج وسايط خاصة، والـ CBC مش محدد. والإصابة بالجهاز الهضمي مع الرئوية بنفس الوقت هي اللي بترشدنا لـ Legionella مش مصدر معوي لحاله.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا sputum analysis لأنه منطقي لاكتشاف مسبب التهاب الرئة، بس بالـ Legionella زرع البلغم نتائجه بطيئة وغير عملية، وكمان بقلّ فيه الـ neutrophils وما فيه بكتيرية مسيطرة.

question:
Which of the following therapeutic regimens would 
be MOST acceptable for a 35-year-old, end-stage renal 
disease patient on hemodialysis, who was last admitted to the hospital and discharged 93 days prior, now 
presenting with fever, cough productive of green sputum, and the following chest radiograph (Figure 6.3)?
FIGURE 6.3  J.E. Tintinalli, J.S. Stapczynski, O.J. Ma, D. Yearly, G.D. Meckler, D.M. Cline: 
Tintinalli’s Emergency Medicine: A Comprehensive Study Guide, 9th Edition: Copyright © 
McGraw-Hill Education. All rights reserved.
englishExplanation:
21.  The answer is D. (Chapter 65) This patient, although 
discharged more than 3 months ago from the hospital, 
should be treated for healthcare-associated pneumonia 
because of her hemodialysis. Other conditions that qualify patients as having healthcare-associated pneumonia 
include being hospitalized for 2 or more days within the 
past 90 days, residing in a nursing home or long-term 
care facility, being on home IV antibiotics, receiving 
chronic wound care, receiving chemotherapy, and having an immunocompromised state. Acceptable regimens 
for healthcare-associated pneumonia consist of three drug 
regimens covering methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus 
aureus, gram-negative and resistant organisms including pseudomonas, and atypical organisms. Ceftriaxone 

72
TINTINALLI’S EMERGENCY MEDICINE EXAMINATION AND BOARD REVIEW, 9TH EDITION
and azithromycin would be acceptable for communityacquired pneumonia. Meropenem offers a broad-spectrum 
coverage, but it would not sufficiently cover all the recommended pathogens. The combination of vancomycin 
and ceftriaxone is a more suitable regimen for meningitis, 
and although it could cover many pneumonia pathogens, 
in this case some gram-negative pathogens (particularly 
pseudomonas) and atypical organisms would be not be 
covered.

![Tintinalli-2023-00171 source page 74](images/Tintinalli-2023-00171-Tintinalli-2023-p0074.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00171 source page 84](images/Tintinalli-2023-00171-Tintinalli-2023-p0084.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00171 source page 85](images/Tintinalli-2023-00171-Tintinalli-2023-p0085.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض بيعتبر عنده healthcare-associated pneumonia لأنه بيعالج غسيل كلوي منتظم، حتى لو مرّ على آخر دخول أكثر من 3 أشهر. ومن شروط هالتصنيف كمان إنه يكون مقيم بدار رعاية أو بياخد أدوية وريدية أو كيماوي، والغسيل الكلوي بيدخّله بهالفئة. هيك الحالات بدها ثلاث أدوية تغطي الـ MRSA والجراثيم سالبة الغرض بما فيها الـ pseudomonas والكائنات غير النمطية، وخليط Vancomycin مع cefepime وlevofloxacin بيمتثل هالمتطلبات بالضبط.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا Ceftriaxone مع azithromycin لأنها العلاج المعتاد للتهاب الرئة community-acquired، بس هون لازم نغطي الـ pseudomonas وMRSA كمان، وأي خليط أقل بيترك ثغرات بالعلاج.

question:
A 64-year-old undomiciled man presents intoxicated 
with fever, cough productive of rusty, brown sputum, 
and pleuritic chest pain. A chest x-ray is notable for a 
right lower lobe consolidation. Vitals are HR 110, RR 
24, BP 120/58, and SpO2 97% on RA. Labs include 
sodium 127, potassium 4.5, chloride 105, bicarbonate 22, blood urea nitrogen 35, creatinine 1.6, glucose 
126; white blood count 16 (8% bands), hemoglobin 
12, hematocrit 36, platelets 245; ethanol 254. Which 
of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE disposition plan?

options.text: Observation until sober, followed by discharge
Transfer to an alcohol detoxification program

englishExplanation:
22.  The answer is A.  (Chapter 65) This patient has 
pneumonia and is intoxicated. In addition, because the 
patient is undomiciled, there are social concerns and 
uncertainty how the patient will appropriately obtain care 
and resources outside of the hospital. Several pneumonia 
scoring systems help calculate risk among patients with 
pneumonia in the emergency department. The most wellstudied tools are the pneumonia severity index (PSI) and 
the CURB-65 rule. This patient’s data permits analysis by 
the CURB-65 system, and he scores a total of 3 points, 
1 each for confusion (although he is intoxicated, his risk 
must be assumed higher since a true mental status examination either cannot be conducted or is confounded), uremia (blood urea nitrogen >7 mmol/L), and blood pressure 
(diastolic below 60). He does not score points for 65 years 
or more, or respiratory rate. Having a CURB-65 score 
of 3 increases his risk of mortality in the outpatient setting. Additionally, even if his risk can be adjusted down 
for the confounding factor of intoxication, he is still at an 
increased risk given his homelessness and substance abuse 
and should be considered for admission. Discharging the 
patient would be risky. Observing him and reassessing 
once sober is an excellent idea; however, even without the 
sober reevaluation, his risk for progression of pneumonia 
combined with his social risk factors remains intermediate to high. Transferring him to a detox center would not 
address the actual medical problem of pneumonia.

![Tintinalli-2023-00172 source page 74](images/Tintinalli-2023-00172-Tintinalli-2023-p0074.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00172 source page 75](images/Tintinalli-2023-00172-Tintinalli-2023-p0075.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00172 source page 85](images/Tintinalli-2023-00172-Tintinalli-2023-p0085.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده التهاب رئة وهو سكران وبلا مأوى، ففي خطر على الرعاية والمتابعة بعد الخروج. حسب نظام CURB-65 بياخد 3 نقاط: تشوش بالوعي، وسموم كلوية بارتفاع الـ BUN، وانخفاض الضغط الانبساطي أقل من 60، وهاي بترفع خطر الوفاة بالرعاية الخارجية. وكمان انعدام البيت وإدمانه بيخلي خطره أعلى، عشان هيك الأفضل إدخاله على الجناح.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا مراقبته لحتى يفوق وينزله بعدها، بس المخاطرة الاجتماعية والتصنيف المرتفع لحاله كافي إنه يبقى بالمستشفى، وتصدّيه من المستشفى مخاطرة عالية لأنه مش ضامن يرجع.

question:
A 60-year-old farmer with prior medical history of 
heart failure, Hodgkin’s lymphoma, testicular cancer, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and arthritis presents to the emergency department with shortness of 
breath. Symptoms began 3 to 6 months prior to arrival, 
are worse with exertion, are accompanied by nonproductive cough, and have not been relieved through 
the use of his wife’s albuterol inhaler. He endorses 
occasional fevers and weight loss. He is currently 
undergoing active chemotherapy for his lymphoma. 
Bleomycin and dofetilide are on his medication list. 
Vital signs are T 37.4°C, HR 96, RR 20, BP 160/90, 
and SpO2 91% on RA. Physical examination reveals 
diffuse crackles and coarse breath sounds, without 
evidence of murmurs or peripheral edema. A bedside 
ultrasound reveals lung sliding, and no “B” lines. A 
chest x-ray reveals diffuse interstitial infiltrates and 
honeycombing, worse in the lower lobes. Which of 
the following is MOST LIKELY responsible for his 
current presentation?
englishExplanation:
25.  The answer is B. (Chapter 65) This patient presents 
with chronic cough and a clinical picture consistent with 
interstitial lung disease—crackles, interstitial infiltrates, 
and honeycombing on chest x-ray, and an ultrasound without suggestive features of airspace disease or effusion. He 
has a history of heart failure and malignancies. Bleomycin 
is commonly used to treat both lymphomas and testicular 
cancer, and is well known for causing pulmonary fibrosis 
and interstitial pneumonitis. Allergic bronchopulmonary 
aspergillosis is certainly something for which he is at risk, 
given his occupation; however, it typically resolves once 
exposure to the antigen is eliminated. Additionally, he has 
a chronic picture of lung disease without a clear exposure. 
Dofetilide is a class III antiarrhythmic and of the same 
class (generally) as amiodarone; however, it is not known 

CHAPTER 6  •  Thoracic-Respiratory Disorders
73
for specifically causing pulmonary fibrosis, unlike amiodarone. Heart failure typically presents with volume overload, pleural effusions, and interstitial/alveolar edema, 
which this patient lacks.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده صورة مرض رئوي بينسيجي مزمن: رجيجات بالرئتين وكثافات بينسيجية وخشونة عسلية بالأشعة بدون وذمة ولا سوائل جنب. هو بياخد علاج كيماوي للمليوما وسرطان الخصية، والـ Bleomycin شائع الاستعمال بهالعلاجين ومعروف إنه بيسبب الليفبروسيس الرئوي والتهاب البكريات. أما الـ dofetilide فهو مضاد اضطراب نظم من الفئة الثالثة وما معروف بالليفبروسيس، فالمشتبه به هو Bleomycin.
الفخ: الطلاب بيفكّروا بـ Heart failure لأنه عنده مرض قلبي سابق، بس الصورة هون جافة بدون وذمة أو سوائل جنب، والتشخيص بيشاور على مرض بينسيجي مش امتلاء وريدي.

question:
The majority of lung abscesses occur in which patient 
population?
englishExplanation:
26.  The answer is B.  (Chapter 66) The vast majority 
(80%) of lung abscesses are primary abscesses occurring 
in healthy patients or in patients with a risk of aspiration. 
Secondary lung abscesses, or those associated with malignancy, sepsis, or recent thoracic surgery, account for only 
20% of lung abscesses.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ lung abscesses الأولية بتصير بالمرضى الأصحاء أو بمين عنده خطر استنشاق، وهاد بيمثل 80% من الحالات. يعني استنشاق محتويات المعدة للرئتين هو السبب الأساسي بهالمجموعة، أما الحالات الثانوية المرتبطة بالخبيث أو الإنتان أو جراحة الصدر فما بتعدّي 20% بس. وهاد معناه إنه أول ما نشوف مريض فيه شك بخُراج رئة، لازم ندوّر على أسباب الاستنشاق قبل ما نفكر بالأسباب التانية.
الفخ: الطلاب بيفكّروا بالسرطان أو جراحة الصدر لأنه أسباب مألوفة، بس هدول بتمثل الثانوية بس ونسبة صغيرة جدًا؛ الأغلبية الساحقة خطر الاستنشاق، عشان هيك لازم نركّز على مخاطر الاستنشاق بالسؤال.

question:
A 3-year-old girl is brought by parents for evaluation 
of fever and poor oral intake. She recently immigrated 
to the United States from China, where she received 
the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin vaccine. Physical examination reveals she has cervical lymphadenopathy. Her 
vital signs are as follows: T 38.4°C, HR 146, BP 100/63, 
RR 36, and SpO2 100% on RA. Which of the following 
tests to evaluate for possible tuberculosis infection is 
MOST LIKELY to be positive in this patient?
englishExplanation:
31.  The answer is C. (Chapter 67) Patients who receive 
Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccination for tuberculosis prevention will often have a positive Mantoux skin 
test result even in the absence of infection. The appropriate tuberculosis blood test for use in patients with a history 
of BCG vaccine is an interferon-γ release assay (IGRA). 
Children with tuberculosis have a lower rate of pulmonary cavitary lesions, yielding lower rates of classic tuberculosis findings on the chest radiograph. Sputum cultures 
and acid-fast smears are also less likely to be positive in 
children, with positive sputum findings in only about 40% 
of pediatric patients ultimately treated for tuberculosis.

![Tintinalli-2023-00181 source page 77](images/Tintinalli-2023-00181-Tintinalli-2023-p0077.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00181 source page 86](images/Tintinalli-2023-00181-Tintinalli-2023-p0086.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالطفلة أخذت لقاح BCG، والمرضى اللي بيأخدوه بطلعوا Mantoux skin test إيجابية حتى بدون ما يكونوا مصابين. عشان هيك هاي العلامة بتكون إيجابية هون بالذات وتُعتبر الفحص الأرجح بالإيجاب بهالحالة. وأمراض الرئة بالمصغّرات مثل الـ tuberculosis نادرًا بتطلع صورة كلاسيكية بالأشعة، وزراعة البلغم والبقعة الحمضية قليلة الإيجابية بالأطفال.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا chest x-ray لأنه أول خطوة بأي شك بالعدوى، بس الأطفال نادرًا بيطلعوا صورة كلاسيكية؛ والـ Mantoux بيطلع إيجابي هون بسبب اللقاح مش العدوى.

question:
After unknowingly caring for a patient with active 
tuberculosis without proper respiratory protection, 
which is the MOST LIKELY way for a healthcare provider to respond on future tuberculosis tests?

options.text: Negative skin screening tests both 2 weeks later
Negative skin screening test in 2 weeks with positive chest radiograph within the next year
Negative skin screening test in 2 weeks with positive screening test 1 year later
Positive skin screening test in 2 weeks

correctAnswer: Negative skin screening tests both 2 weeks later
englishExplanation:
34.  The answer is A. (Chapter 67) Only 30% of patients 
become infected after a single droplet exposure. Of 
patients who do contract tuberculosis, the tuberculin skin 
test is negative until 1 to 2 months after exposure. Only 
1% to 13% of healthy patients with latent tuberculosis go 
on to develop active tuberculosis.

![Tintinalli-2023-00184 source page 77](images/Tintinalli-2023-00184-Tintinalli-2023-p0077.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00184 source page 87](images/Tintinalli-2023-00184-Tintinalli-2023-p0087.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بس 30% من الناس بتتعفّن بعد تعرّض واحد بالقطرات، والـ tuberculin skin test بيبقى سلبي لحد شهر أو شهرين بعد التعرّض. عشان هيك الفحص بعد أسبوعين بيرجع سلبي، وحتى الفحص بعد سنة كمان، وعشان هيك بنعيد الفحوصات لاحقًا بدل ما نعتمد على نتيجة وحدة بكّيرة. والسلف اللاتنكية بتطور لحال فعّالة بس بنسبة صغيرة جدًا.
الفخ: الطلاب بيفكّروا إنه الفحص بيطلع إيجابي فورًا بعد التعرّض لأن الجسم تعرّض للجرثومة السلية، بس الإيجاب المبكر مش مضمون، والفحص السليم بيرجع سلبي بعد أسبوعين مع تكراره بعد سنة.

question:
What is the MOST COMMON physical examination 
finding in a patient presenting for evaluation and treatment of a spontaneous, atraumatic pneumothorax?
englishExplanation:
36.  The answer is D. (Chapter 68) The most common 
physical examination finding in patients with pneumothoraces is sinus tachycardia. Because these pneumothoraces 
are small, decreased breath sounds and hyperresonance to 
percussion are often absent. Hypoxia can be present but is 
less prevalent than sinus tachycardia and more likely to be 
a feature of a tension pneumothorax.

![Tintinalli-2023-00186 source page 78](images/Tintinalli-2023-00186-Tintinalli-2023-p0078.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00186 source page 87](images/Tintinalli-2023-00186-Tintinalli-2023-p0087.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أكثر علامة فحص بتشوفها بمريض الـ pneumothorax التلقائي هي تسارع ضربات القلب من الجيب. هاي بتكون لأن الـ pneumothorax غالبًا صغيرة، فنقص الأصوات التنفسية وفرط الرنين بالقرع نادرًا بيبانوا. ونقص الأكسجة ممكن يكون موجود بس أقل شيوعًا من تسارع النبض، وكمان نقص الأكسجة أكثر ما بيتربط بـ pneumothorax متوتر.
الفخ: الطلاب بيفكّروا بنقص الأصوات التنفسية أو فرط الرنين بالقرع لأنها علامات كلاسيكية للـ pneumothorax، بس هون الـ pneumothorax صغيرة ومش دايمًا بتبان، فتسارع النبض هو الأكتر شيوعًا.

question:
Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE 
counseling to provide a patient upon discharge after a 
resolved pneumothorax?

options.text: High-altitude flying is not recommended until
Pleurodesis is recommended prior to any diving
Pulmonary function tests are recommended for
Reexpansion lung injury is a serious delayed

correctAnswer: Pleurodesis is recommended prior to any diving
englishExplanation:
38.  The answer is B. (Chapter 68) Patients who have had 
a pneumothorax are at high risk of recurrence and should 
be cautioned against diving prior to definitive management and prevention of future pneumothoraces by video 
assisted thorascopic surgery and pleurodesis. High-altitude 
flying is not recommended for at least 7 to 14 days after 
pneumothorax resolution but does not require cardiothoracic clearance. Pulmonary function tests are helpful 
measurements of contributing disease severity but have 
little bearing on management or prevention of future 
pneumothoraces. Reexpansion lung injury is uncommon 
and occurs shortly after pneumothorax resolution; this is 
usually mild and requires no treatment more than observation and supplemental oxygen.

![Tintinalli-2023-00188 source page 78](images/Tintinalli-2023-00188-Tintinalli-2023-p0078.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00188 source page 87](images/Tintinalli-2023-00188-Tintinalli-2023-p0087.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض اللي صار عنده pneumothorax معرض بشكل عالي لإنه يتكرر مرة ثانية، فلازم ننصحه إنه يتجنب ال diving تمامًا قبل ما يعمل العلاج النهائي والوقاية من أي pneumothorax جاي بعمل video assisted thoracoscopic surgery مع pleurodesis. أما الطيران على ارتفاعات عالية فممنوع لفترة من 7 لـ 14 يوم بعد ما يتحسن ال pneumothorax، بس هذا ما بده cardiothoracic clearance. و pulmonary function tests بتساعدنا نقيس شدة المرض الكامن بس ما إلها تأثير كبير على العلاج أو منع التكرار.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختاروا إنه الطيران العالي ممنوع لحد ما ياخد clearance من القلب والصدر، بس هذا غلط لأن الطيران بس ممنوع 7 لـ 14 يوم وما بده clearance. التركيز لازم يكون إنه ال diving ممنوع نهائيًا لحد ما يعمل pleurodesis.

question:
In the patient with severe asthma, which of the following findings is MOST sensitive for impending 
respiratory failure?

options.text: Decreased respiratory rate with altered mentation
Forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) or

correctAnswer: Decreased respiratory rate with altered mentation
englishExplanation:
42.  The answer is A.  (Chapter 69) In the patient with 
acute asthma exacerbation, decreased respiratory rate 
and altered mentation are indicative of hypercarbia with 
associated respiratory fatigue and thus requires immediate intervention to prevent impending respiratory failure. 

CHAPTER 6  •  Thoracic-Respiratory Disorders
75
Other signs of respiratory compromise or severe exacerbation include a forced expiratory volume in 1 second 
(FEV1) or peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR) less than 25% 
of predicted or a PaCO2 over 42 mm Hg. Minimal breath 
sounds often indicate a significant exacerbation but are 
not specific for impending respiratory failure.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بمريض ال asthma الحاد، نقص respiratory rate مع altered mentation بيدلوا على إنه عنده hypercarbia مع تعب بالعضلات التنفسية، وهالحالة بدها تدخل فوري عشان نمنع respiratory failure وشيك. في علامات ثانية تدل على تفاقم شديد زي إنه ال FEV1 أو ال PEFR يصير أقل من 25% من المتوقع، أو إنه ال PaCO2 يطلع فوق 42 mm Hg.
الفخ: الطلاب كتير بيختاروا Very minimal breath sounds لأنهم بيحسوا إنه هاي علامة خطر، بس هي بتدل على تفاقم كبير وما هي specific لل impending respiratory failure. التمييز إنه نقص respiratory rate مع altered mentation هو الأكثر حساسية.

question:
A 7-year-old boy presents for evaluation of shortness of 
breath that began while exercising earlier in the day. The 
patient endorses some mild wheezing and improvement 
of the shortness of breath after cessation of activity and 
is currently asymptomatic. His vital signs and physical 
examination are otherwise within normal limits. What 
are MOST APPROPRIATE discharge instructions and 
medication to be prescribed for this patient?

options.text: Short-acting beta-agonist to be used as needed
Short-acting beta-agonist to be used as needed
Short-acting beta-agonist to be used as needed

correctAnswer: Short-acting beta-agonist to be used as needed
englishExplanation:
43.  The answer is B. (Chapter 69) This patient, who is 
experiencing exercise-related shortness of breath that 
improves after cessation of activity, has exercised-induced, 
mild intermittent asthma. These exacerbations should 
improve quickly with a short-acting beta-agonist and 
should require no other therapy. Corticosteroid inhalers 
should be prescribed for exacerbation prevention only in 
patients with mild or moderate persistent asthma. Oral 
corticosteroids are recommended only in the case of acute 
exacerbation, which this patient denies.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده exercise-induced mild intermittent asthma، لأن ال shortness of breath بتحسن بعد ما يوقف الرياضة وهو حاليًا asymptomatic وكل الفحوصات طبيعية. هالحالات بتتحسن بسرعة مع short-acting beta-agonist وما بتدها أي علاج ثاني. أما corticosteroid inhalers فبتنوصف للوقاية من التفاقم بس لمرضى mild أو moderate persistent asthma، وال oral corticosteroids بتستعمل بس بالحالة الحادة.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا daily corticosteroid inhaler لأنهم بفكروا إنه أي asthma بده ستيرويد مستمر، بس هذا غلط لأن الحالة intermittent خفيفة وما حصل عندها exacerbation حاد. العلاج الصحيح هو ال short-acting beta-agonist عند الحاجة.

question: Which of the following is the MOST COMMON complication of patients intubated for status asthmaticus?
englishExplanation:
44.  The answer is B. (Chapter 69) Mechanical ventilation is a necessary intervention for asthma patients in 
severe respiratory distress, but it has multiple complications. All of the above complications can occur in patients 
intubated for severe asthma exacerbation, but the majority of these complications, such as pneumothorax, hemodynamic impairment and barotrauma, are direct results 
of the elevated peak airway pressures caused by airflow 
obstruction. Poor airway movement can also contribute 
to increased mucus plugging, which in turns put patients 
at risk for atelectasis and pulmonary infection.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لما نضع مريض status asthmaticus على mechanical ventilation، ال elevated peak airway pressures الناتجة عن انسداد مجرى الهواء هي المشكلة الأساسية وأكثر اختلاط شائع. وهالضغوط العالية هي السبب المباشر لمعظم الاختلاطات الثانية زي ال pneumothorax وال hemodynamic impairment وال barotrauma. كمان قلة حركة الهواء بتزيد ال mucus plugging اللي بيحط المريض بخطورة atelectasis وعدوى رئوية.
الفخ: الطلاب كتير بيختاروا pneumothorax لأنه أخطر، بس السؤال بيسأل عن الأكثر شيوعًا مو الأخطر. التمييز إنه ال peak airway pressures هو المصدر اللي بيتفرع منه باقي الاختلاطات.

question:
Which of the following is the MOST CONCERNING 
risk factor for mortality associated with asthma 
exacerbation?

options.text: More than two hospitalizations for asthma within

correctAnswer: More than two hospitalizations for asthma within
englishExplanation:
45.  The answer is D.  (Chapter 69) Risk factors for 
asthma-exacerbation-related death are as follows: more 
than two hospitalizations or three emergency department 
visits for asthma within the past year, using more than 
two canisters per month of short-acting beta-agonist, difficulty perceiving airway obstruction or its severity, and 
social features such as low socioeconomic status or illicit 
drug use. History of corticosteroid use, associated temperature, and early age of onset do not reliably predict 
mortality from asthma exacerbation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: من عوامل الخطورة للموت بسبب asthma exacerbation إنه يكون عنده أكثر من دخولتين للمستشفى أو ثلاث زيارات للطوارئ بسبب ال asthma خلال السنة الماضية. كمان استعمال أكثر من علبتين شهريًا من short-acting beta-agonist، وصعوبة إدراك شدة انسداد مجرى الهواء، وعوامل اجتماعية زي الوضع الاقتصادي الضعيف أو تعاطي المخدرات. أما تاريخ استعمال ال corticosteroids والحرارة وبداية المرض بعمر صغير فما بتتوقع الموت بشكل موثوق.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا History of corticosteroid use لأنهم بفكروا إنه بيدل على مرض شديد، بس هذا ما بيعتبر predictor موثوق للوفاة. المفتاح هو عدد الدخولات للمستشفى والزيارات للطوارئ خلال السنة.

question:
A 77-year-old male with Parkinson disease is brought to the hospital with obstipation. His 
abdomen is distended and mildly tender with decreased bowel sounds. His abdominal x-ray is 
shown below . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
The image indicates sigmoid volvulus. Abdominal radiography lacks sensitivity for 
small bowel ischemia and signs such as thumbprinting and pneumatosis are rare. Viscus 
perforation would be suspected if there were free air seen under the diaphragm, but abdominal 
radiography is incompletely sensitive for evaluation of perforation. Swallowed air would be 
unlikely to cause abdominal distention and obstipation. Gastric outlet obstruction might not 
demonstrate any findings on x-ray. Of all the answer choices, sigmoid volvulus is the only 
diagnosis that can be made solely relying on abdominal radiography.

![subjects1200-12f7fc222f05180e source page 132](images/subjects1200-12f7fc222f05180e-p0132.jpg)

![subjects1200-12f7fc222f05180e source page 133](images/subjects1200-12f7fc222f05180e-p0133.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الصورة بتدل على sigmoid volvulus، وهو اللي الوحيد من بين كل الخيارات اللي ممكن يتشخص اعتمادًا على abdominal radiography لحاله. المريض عنده Parkinson disease مع obstipation وبطن منتفخ ومؤلم شوي وأصوات معوية قليلة، وهاي الصورة السريرية بتتوافق مع ال volvulus. أما باقي التشخيصات فما بتنبين بشكل موثوق على صورة البطن العادية.
الفخ: الطلاب بيختاروا Viscus perforation لأنهم بيدوروا على free air تحت الحجاب، بس ال abdominal radiography غير حساسة كفاية لتقييم ال perforation وما ظهر عندنا free air. التمييز إنه ال volvulus هو التشخيص اللي بيعتمد على الصورة البسيطة لحاله.

question:
A 68-year-old female presents with a 2-day history of left lower quadrant pain. CT reveals 
diverticulitis. Which of the following is true?

options.text: The recurrence rate of diverticulitis after a single, uncomplicated episode is 75%.
Avoiding nuts, seeds, and corn has not been shown to decrease recurrence.
Patients younger than 40 years with diverticulitis should have resection of the diseased
She should be admitted for colonoscopy to exclude colon cancer.
The mortality rate of hospitalized patients with acute diverticulitis is 35%.

correctAnswer: Avoiding nuts, seeds, and corn has not been shown to decrease recurrence.
englishExplanation:
The recurrence rate after a single episode of uncomplicated diverticulitis is 20% to 
30%. Furthermore, a high-fiber diet may help prevent further episodes. There is no evidence 
that avoiding nuts, corn kernels, popcorn, or seeds is associated with an increased rate of 
recurrence, despite the fact that patients are commonly advised against ingesting these 
substances. Young patients with diverticulitis are a special population because they tend to have 
more aggressive disease and the recurrence rate of diverticulitis is higher. Although resection of 
the disease segment remains elective, some authors recommend resection in all young patients 
due to their higher risk of recurrence. CT is the study of choice in the ED because it reliably 
visualizes the site of inflammation and is very useful for detecting various complications (e.g., 
abscesses, perforation, fistulas). Colonoscopy is useful to exclude colon cancer but is deferred 
until the acute illness is treated. The mortality rate of hospitalized patients with diverticulitis is 
1% to 6% for those requiring only medical management and 12% to 18% for those requiring 
surgery.
arabicExplanation:
