الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا CT scan لأنه الأدق بشكل عام. الفرق إنه بالحمل بنتجنب الإشعاع، وهذا السبب إنه الـ ultrasound هو الفحص الأول المفضّل، والـ MRI يكون الخيار التالي فقط إذا كان الـ ultrasound غير حاسم.

following an uncomplicated cesarean section. She has normal vital signs but ap-
pears uncomfortable. She reports constant pain and difficulty voiding but no dy-
suria or hematuria. She has tenderness in the suprapubic region and a palpable

options.text: Administer tamsulosin and repeat a void trial

englishExplanation: This patient has acute urinary retention given her difficulty voiding and distended bladder on bedside ultrasound (bladder volume ≥300 mL). question:
What is the best first step in management for eclamptic seizures?
9/20/26, 1:17 AM
PEER for Physicians - Case Series 2026-1 — Answered

Page 117 of 974

options.text: Protect the airway and maintain oxygenation

correctAnswer: Protect the airway and maintain oxygenation
englishExplanation: Ensuring maternal oxygenation is maintained and the patient is protected from trauma due to the seizure are of paramount importance early in the care of the eclamptic patient. The patient can be placed in a left lateral position to avoid aspiration, oxygen can be administered at 8 to 10 L/min via a nonre- breather mask, and bed rails can be raised and padded to avoid trauma. Eclampsia is diagnosed with the onset of a generalized tonic-clonic seizure in a woman with known preeclampsia when other diagnoses are less likely. Eclamptic seizures occur in 2% to 3% of patients with severe preeclampsia not receiving anti- seizure prophylaxis and 0% to 0.6% of those with preeclampsia. Fetal bradycardia for 3 to 5 minutes is common after an eclamptic seizure.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الخطوة الأهم أول شي بتدبير eclamptic seizures وهي تأمين أكسجة الأم وحمايتها من الرض بسبب التشنج. بنقدر نحط المريضة بوضعية left lateral لتجنب الشفط، ونعطي أوكسجين 8 لـ 10 لتر بالدقيقة عبر non-rebreather mask، ونرفع حواجز السرير ونبطّنها لتجنب الرض. الـ eclampsia تتشخص بحدوث نوبة تشنج tonic-clonic معممة بمريضة عندها preeclampsia، والـ fetal bradycardia لمدة 3 لـ 5 دقائق شائعة بعد النوبة.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا ولادة الجنين فوراً أو معالجة الضغط. الفرق إنه ولادة الجنين ما هي الخطوة الأولى ولا هي عملية سريعة، والأهم بالبداية هو الـ airway والأكسجين وحماية الأم من الرض، وبعدها نعالج الضغط ونمنع تكرار التشنج.

question:

was 11.2 a month ago. Her vital signs are stable. One unit of packed RBCs is

Administering which medication intravenously is the best next step in this
patient's care?
englishExplanation: Patients with concern for an upper GI bleed should be treated with an intravenous proton-pump inhibitor (PPI), such as pantoprazole, while waiting for endoscopy. PPIs can decrease the rate of rebleeding in those with peptic ulcer disease. These patients also require good intravenous access for admin- istration of fluids and likely blood. Additionally, consideration must be given to an- ticoagulation reversal.

A 72-year-old woman with a history of cirrhosis presents with large-volume he-
matemesis and profound hemodynamic instability that is not rectified with the
infusion of octreotide, administration of crystalloid fluids, and initiation of the
massive transfusion protocol. She requires intubation, which is performed suc-
cessfully. Repeat vital signs after 4 units of packed RBCs and 2 units of fresh
frozen plasma include BP 60/40 and P 140.
What would be the most important next step in management?

options.text: Place an esophageal balloon tamponade device

correctAnswer: Place an esophageal balloon tamponade device
englishExplanation: Given this patient's history of cirrhosis and significant upper GI bleed, it's most likely this patient has bleeding esophageal varices. The most important intervention at this time is to stop the bleeding, which is most likely to be accomplished by using 9/20/26, 1:17 AM PEER for Physicians - Case Series 2026-1 — Answered  Page 125 of 974 an esophageal balloon tamponade device (eg, the Sengstaken-Blakemore tube or Minnesota tube) to place direct pressure against the bleeding vessels. This can be used as a temporizing measure while awaiting definitive management via endoscopy.
arabicExplanation:

A 72-year-old woman presents with epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. The
patient's initial laboratory values revealed a lipase of 542 units/L (normal range
0-65 units/L) and no evidence of GI bleed or anemia. Her vital signs are BP
90/60, P 115, R 18, and T 37.5°C (99.5°F); SpO  is 95% on room air.
What would be the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Conduct an oral challenge and, if tolerated, start oral rehydration
Consult radiology for a right upper quadrant ultrasound

englishExplanation: Crystalloid resuscitation is indicated in a patient with pancreatitis and unstable vital signs. Pancreatitis leads to inflammation and third spac- ing of fluids. Also, most individuals with pancreatitis will have decreased oral in- take and vomiting, leading to dehydration and further intravascular volume losses. Either normal saline or Lactated Ringer solution can be used for resuscitation, ex- cept in the case when hypercalcemia is present. In patients with hypercalcemia, nor- mal saline should be used for resuscitation since Lactated Ringer solution contains 3 mEq/L of calcium.

الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا ultrasonography للربع العلوي الأيمن أو مضادات حيوية أو تحدي فموي. الفرق إنه التشخيص واضح من الـ lipase، والأهم أول شي هو تثبيت العلامات الحيوية بالسوائل، وما في دلالة على التهاب صفراوي أو عدوى تحتاج مضادات حيوية بهذه المرحلة.

question:
A 68-year-old man experienced a mechanical fall onto his left side 3 days ago. He
was seen at urgent care and diagnosed with three left lower rib fractures on chest
x-ray. Today, he presents with persistent left upper quadrant pain radiating to
his left flank and left shoulder as well as generalized weakness. His vital signs are
BP 95/55, P 105, R 22, and T 37.8°C (100°F); SpO  is 90% on room air.
Which test should be performed first to determine the cause of this patient's
symptoms?
englishExplanation: This patient has a recent trauma to his left lower ribs, which overlie the spleen. He has an elevated pulse that is greater than his systolic blood pressure. A shock in- dex (heart rate divided by systolic blood pressure) >1 is associated with higher mortality in emergency department patients. Given his history of hypertension and BP 95/55 mm Hg, especially with reported weakness, this presen- tation could be a sign of significant anemia. Lastly, left upper quadrant pain radiat- ing to the shoulder could be a sign of a splenic injury, as hemoperitoneum can irritate the diaphragm and cause referred pain to the shoulder. A bedside FAST examination can immediately evaluate for free fluid in the abdomen, can be done rapidly, and would quickly address the critical threat to life that this presentation suggests.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده كسور بالأضلاع السفلية اليسرى قبل 3 أيام، وهذه الأضلاع فوق الـ spleen مباشرة، والنبض عندها أعلى من الضغط الانقباضي فمؤشر الصدمة shock index أكبر من 1 ومرتبط بوفيات أعلى. ألم الربع العلوي الأيسر اللي ينتشر للكتف الأيسر ممكن يكون علامة إصابة طحال، لأن hemoperitoneum يهيّج الحجاب فيسبب ألم منقول للكتف. فالـ bedside FAST هو الأسرع لتقييم وجود سائل حر بالبطن.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا CBC أو urinalysis أو تكرار صورة الصدر. الفرق إنه التحاليل مخبرية بتأخذ وقت وما بتحل تهديد الحياة الفوري، والـ FAST بالسرير يعطي جواب فوري عن النزيف داخل البطن وهاد اللي يحدد التدخل السريع.

A 26-year-old woman presents with altered mental status after intentional inges-
tion 1 hour prior to arrival. The patient is toxic appearing. Her vital signs are BP
70/40, P 46, R 18, and T 37.6°C (97.9°F); SpO  is 91% on nonrebreather mask.
Her blood glucose is 89 mg/dL. The patient is awaiting admission to the medical
ICU and 12 hours later is noted to have rising ALT and AST. Coingestion is a
concern.
Which intervention could have mitigated the rise in ALT and AST?
englishExplanation: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is the primary therapy for acetaminophen over- dose. Although this patient's initial presentation is consistent with beta-blocker toxicity (propranolol), it is important to screen for concomitant ingestions, such as acetaminophen and salicylate toxicity. NAC is most effective when adminis- tered within 8 to 10 hours from the time of ingestion to decrease the chance of the patient developing hepatotoxicity. The difficulty with acetaminophen is that there is not a unique toxidrome presenta- tion. Unless explicitly disclosed, acetaminophen ingestion can go unnoticed until delayed transaminase elevation, which underscores the need for routine ac- etaminophen concentration screening. Universal screening of suicidal ingestions found 0.3% of cases had a potentially toxic acetaminophen concentration, and 0.16% had a toxic salicylate ingestion not suggested by history. Although these per- 2 9/20/26, 1:17 AM PEER for Physicians - Case Series 2026-1 — Answered  Page 162 of 974 centages are low, they represent an intervention that can change future morbidity and mortality for these patients. Screening laboratory tests and studies rou- tinely done for ingestions include acetaminophen concentration, salicylate concentration, glucose level, BMP, ECG, and pregnancy testing for all pa- tients who can get pregnant. Other studies may be indicated based on history and physical examination.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ N-acetylcysteine (NAC) هو العلاج الأساسي لحالة acetaminophen overdose، وكان لازم يعطى عشان يمنع ارتفاع الـ ALT والـ AST المتأخر. العرض الأولي للمريضة يوحي بتسمم beta-blocker (propranolol) بضغط منخفض ونبض بطيء 46، بس لازم دايماً نسوي فحص للمواد المأخوذة معه زي acetaminophen و salicylate. والـ NAC يكون أكثر فعالية لما نعطيه خلال 8 لـ 10 ساعات من وقت الأخذ لأنه يقلل خطر hepatotoxicity.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا magnesium sulfate أو sodium bicarbonate أو methylene blue. الفرق إنه الـ acetaminophen ما عنده toxidrome مميز، فبدون طلب مستوى الدواء بالدم ممكن ما ينكشف إلا لما تطلع الـ transaminases متأخرة، والـ NAC هو الترياق الوحيد اللي يمنع هذا الضرر الكبدي.

A 27-year-old man presents with altered mental status, nausea, and vomiting.
His vital signs are BP 102/56, P 130, R 30, and T 38.3°C (100.9°F); SpO  is 92%
on room air. About a week ago, the patient was seen at an outside hospital after
an intentional ingestion, but he was cleared by the psychiatric team at that time.
The differential diagnosis includes toxic ingestion with a delayed presentation
and sepsis with an intra-abdominal source. An abdominal and pelvic CT scan
with contrast is ordered to rule out an infectious etiology.
Because ingestion with a delayed presentation is in the differential diagnosis,
what pharmacotherapy should be considered prior to the CT scan?
englishExplanation:
This patient's delayed tachycardia and fever are concerning for ingestion of levothy- roxine, leading to hyperthyroidism. Administration of a large iodide load can lead to an increased secretion of thyroid hormones that can be seen with iodinated contrast studies such as CT scans or coronary angiogra- phy. This effect on thyroid function is known as Jod-Basedow phenomenon. In vulnerable patients, this administration can result in a delayed presentation of hy- perthyroidism that usually spans 2 to 12 weeks. Therefore, physicians should con- sider administration of a thionamide derivative such as methimazole or propylth- iouracil to block excess iodide transport to the thyroid. In acute treatment of life- threatening thyroid storm, propylthiouracil is preferred due to inhibition of tetraiodothyronine (T ) to triiodothyronine (T ) conversion.

question:
A 48-year-old man with a past medical history of hepatitis C and
cirrhosis presents to the ED complaining of abdominal pain and chills. His
BP is 118/75 mm Hg, HR is 105 beats/minute, RR is 16 breaths/minute,
temperature is 101.2°F, and oxygen saturation is 97% on room air. His
abdomen is distended and diffusely tender. You perform a paracentesis and
retrieve 1 liter of cloudy fluid. Laboratory analysis of the fluid shows a
neutrophil count of 550 cells/mm3. Which of the following is the most
appropriate treatment?
englishExplanation:
76.  The answer is e. This patient with known liver disease has
spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP). Diagnostic criteria for SBP
include an ascitic fluid neutrophil count greater than 250 cells/mm3.
Pathogens associated with SBP include gram-negative rods like E. coli and
Klebsiella, as well as Streptococcus sp, and Streptococcus pneumoniae.
Therefore, the most appropriate antibiotic for treatment is a thirdgeneration cephalosporin such as cefotaxime.
All other answer choices (a, b, c, and d) are inappropriate antibiotic
choices.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده مرض بالكبد و cirrhosis، يعني اللي صار إنه تجمّع سائل بالبطن وفيه التهاب peritonitis عفوي، والسبب لأنه عدد الـ neutrophils بالسائل كان ٥٥٠ خلية، وهو أعلى من الحد التشخيصي اللي هو أكثر من ٢٥٠ خلية. الجراثيم المسؤولة عن SBP عادة تكون عصيات سلبية الغرام مثل E. coli و Klebsiella، وكمان Streptococcus sp و Streptococcus pneumoniae. عشان هيك العلاج المناسب هو cephalosporin من الجيل الثالث مثل cefotaxime.
الفخ: في ناس تختار Metronidazole أو Vancomycin، بس هاي مو مناسبة لأنها ما تغطي الجراثيم المسؤولة عن SBP. لازم تتذكر إن تغطية الـ gram-negative rods بدها cephalosporin من الجيل الثالث.

question:
A 40-year-old woman presents to the ED complaining of fever and 1
day of increasing pain in her RUQ. She denies nausea or vomiting or
worsening of pain after eating. The patient returned from a trip to Mexico 6
months ago. About 2 weeks ago, she experienced intermittent diarrhea with
blood-streaked mucus. Her BP is 130/80 mm Hg, HR is 107 beats/minute,
RR is 17 breaths/minute, and temperature is 102°F. Physical examination
reveals decreased breath sounds over the right lung base. Abdominal
examination is notable for tenderness to palpation in RUQ. Murphy sign is
negative. Her WBC is 20,500/μL. Chest radiograph reveals a small right
pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
86.  The answer is a. Amebic abscesses are common in countries with
tropical and subtropical climates and areas with poor sanitation.
Entamoeba histolytica causes an intestinal infection, and the liver is
seeded via the portal system. The clinical presentation includes abdominal
tenderness in the RUQ, leukocytosis, and fever. Diagnosis is supported by
identification of the pathogenic protozoan in the stool. Treatment includes
metronidazole and supportive care measures. If medical therapy is
unsuccessful, percutaneous catheter drainage is required.
Cholecystitis (b) presents with fever, leukocytosis, and RUQ pain, and a
positive Murphy. Cryptosporidium (c) is the most common cause of chronic

diarrhea in individuals with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)
and presents with profuse watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, anorexia,
nausea, and flatulence. In immunocompetent individuals, the illness is selflimited, with symptoms persisting for 1 to 3 weeks. Patients with
enterobiasis (d), also known as pinworms, complain of itching in the anal
region, particularly at night, as the adult worm lays eggs in the anus.
Pyogenic abscess (e) is the most common type of liver abscess; however,
the history of travel and lack of primary source for the pyogenic abscess
make it less likely a diagnosis. Most cases of pyogenic liver access occur in
the setting of ascending cholangitis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ amebic abscess شائع بالدول الاستوائية وشبه الاستوائية والمناطق اللي فيها صرف صحي سيئ، والمريضة رجعت من Mexico قبل ٦ أشهر. Entamoeba histolytica تعمل التهاب بالأمعاء وبعدها الكبد يتلوث عن طريق portal system، والعرض يشمل وجع بالـ RUQ و leukocytosis و fever. التشخيص يتدعم بوجود الطفيلي بالبراز، والعلاج metronidazole، وإذا ما نجح لازم percutaneous catheter drainage.
الفخ: كثير طلاب يختاروا cholecystitis، بس عندها Murphy sign سلبي وهنا الـ Murphy كان سلبي، ونفس الشي pyogenic abscess أقل احتمال لأنه ما فيه مصدر أولي. الفرق إنه الـ amebic أسفار وإسهال دموي، والـ pyogenic عادة بعد ascending cholangitis.

question:
A 68-year-old man presents to the ED by EMS from his nursing home
for abdominal pain and abdominal distension. He appears chronically
debilitated and uncomfortable. He is not obese, but his abdomen appears
moderately distended. A digital rectal exam reveals no gross blood and an
empty rectal vault. An abdominal radiograph is obtained and shown below.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
88.  The answer is b. The patient’s clinical presentation and abdominal
radiograph are consistent with a diagnosis of sigmoid volvulus. A volvulus
is kinking or twisting of the bowel that leads to intestinal obstruction and
can lead to tissue ischemia or necrosis. Sigmoid volvulus occurs most
commonly in elderly, debilitated, or institutionalized patients. The classic
triad of symptoms includes abdominal pain, abdominal distension, and
constipation. If the bowel becomes gangrenous, the mortality rate exceeds
50%. Percussive tympany may be present as well. Plain abdominal
radiographs demonstrate distended large bowel loops without haustra and
may resemble a bent inner tube. A contrast enema may help distinguish this
from other causes of bowel obstruction.

Patients with an SBO present with diffuse, crampy abdominal pain.
They may also report a lack of recent bowel movement or passage of flatus.
However, on abdominal films you will see distended loops of small bowel
and air-fluid levels in a stepladder appearance. (a). Gastric outlet
obstruction (c) is a type of SBO and usually occurs at the pylorus or
duodenum. Causes may include traumatic or spontaneous duodenal
hematomas, pyloric stenosis (in children), or pancreatic malignancy.
Patients present with vomiting and failure to thrive. Irritable bowel
syndrome (d) is more common in younger patients and can present
predominantly with diarrhea, predominantly with constipation, or
alternating diarrhea and constipation accompanied by severe abdominal
cramping that is relieved with defecation. Pneumoperitoneum (e) is a
surgical emergency. Patient will have peritonitis on examination (eg,
rebound tenderness, rigidity, involuntary guarding). Free intra-abdominal
air under the diaphragm is best seen on an upright chest X-ray.

![PreTest-5e-00088 source page 125](images/PreTest-5e-00088-PreTest-5e-p0125.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: العيان كبير بالعمر و debilitated ومن nursing home، وهذه الفئة هي الأكثر عرضة للـ sigmoid volvulus اللي هو التفاف أو انثناء بالأمعاء يؤدي لانسداد وأحياناً ischemia أو necrosis. الثلاثي الكلاسيكي هو وجع بالبطن وانتفاخ وإمساك، وعند الفحص ممكن نلاقي percussive tympany. صورة البطن البسيطة تبين حلقات قولون كبيرة ومنتفخة بدون haustra وتبدو مثل bent inner tube، والـ contrast enema ممكن تساعد بالتفريق.
الفخ: في ناس تختار SBO، بس بالـ SBO بنشوف حلقات الأمعاء الدقيقة منتفخة و air-fluid levels بترتيب stepladder، وهنا الحلقات كانت قولون كبيرة. الفرق إنه الـ volvulus فيه التفاف وحلقة قولونية كبيرة.

question:
A 21-year-old woman presents to the ED complaining of diarrhea,
abdominal cramps, fever, anorexia, and weight loss for 3 days. Her BP is
127/75 mm Hg, HR is 91 beats/minute, and temperature is 100.8°F. Her
abdomen is soft and nontender without rebound or guarding. WBC is 9200/
μL, β-hCG is negative, and urinalysis is unremarkable. Stool is guaiac
positive. She tells you that she has had similar symptoms four times over
the past 2 months. Which of the following extraintestinal manifestations is
associated with Crohn’s disease but not ulcerative colitis?
englishExplanation:
96.  The answer is c. Crohn’s disease is an autoimmune condition
characterized by chronic inflammation extending through all layers of
the bowel wall. The onset is generally between the ages of 15 and 40 years.
Crohn’s disease should be suspected in any patient whose symptoms show a
picture consistent with chronic inflammatory colitis. Extraintestinal
manifestations are seen in 25% to 30% of patients, and include aphthous
ulcers, erythema nodosum, iritis or episcleritis, arthritis, gallstones, and
thromboembolic disease. The incidence of these extraintestinal

manifestations is similar for Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis.
Nephrolithiasis is seen as a result of hyperoxaluria because of increased
oxalate absorption in patients with ileal disease.
Because ulcerative colitis affects only the large bowel, nephrolithiasis is
seen only in patients with Crohn’s disease. All other answer choices (a, b,
d, and e) are seen in both conditions.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ Crohn's disease هو مرض مناعي ذاتي فيه التهاب مزمن يمتد بكل طبقات جدار الأمعاء، وممكن يصيب أي جزء من الفم للشرج. عند مرضى Crohn اللي فيهم مرض بالـ ileum بيزيد امتصاص الـ oxalate، وهذا يعمل hyperoxaluria وبالتالي nephrolithiasis. بما إنه الـ ulcerative colitis يصيب القولون الكبير بس، فالـ nephrolithiasis بنشوفها بس بالـ Crohn، وعشان هيك هي المظهر اللي يميزه.
الفخ: الطلاب كثير يختاروا erythema nodosum أو uveitis أو thromboembolic disease، بس هاي كلها تنشوف بنفس النسبة بالـ Crohn والـ ulcerative colitis. الفرقة الوحيدة اللي تنحفظ هي nephrolithiasis بسبب الـ hyperoxaluria من مرض الـ ileum.

question:
Shared scenario:
A 41-year-old alcoholic man with a history of cirrhosis and hepatitis C
presents to the ED with bright red emesis. His temperature is 99.4°F, BP is

91/50 mm Hg, HR is 122 beats/minute, RR is 26 breaths/minute, and
oxygen saturation is 95% on room air.

98.   Which of the following conditions is the most common cause of upper
gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding?
englishExplanation:
98.  The answer is e. GI bleeding is a common presenting complaint in the
ED. Upper GI bleeding, defined as hemorrhage proximal to the ligament
of Treitz (located at the junction of the duodenum and the jejunum), is more
common than lower GI bleeding, representing approximately 75% of cases.
Gastric and duodenal ulcers are the most commonly identified sources of
upper GI hemorrhage. Other common causes of upper GI hemorrhage
include gastritis, Mallory-Weiss tears, and esophageal varices. Patients may
present with hematemesis and/or melena. Hematochezia is usually
associated with lower GI bleeding, though it may be seen in cases of a brisk
upper GI bleed. Early aggressive resuscitation with large bore IV access,
fluids, and blood products, if needed, is critical in reducing mortality from

upper GI bleed. Endoscopy is diagnostic in determining the source of an
upper GI bleed, and is often therapeutic as well, as bleeding vessels can be
cauterized of ligated.
Esophageal varices, gastritis, and Mallory-Weiss tears (a, b, and c) are
common causes of upper GI bleeding, but less common than peptic ulcer
disease. Gastric adenocarcinoma (d) is a rare cause of upper GI
hemorrhage.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: النزيف من الجهاز الهضمي العلوي هو الأكثر شيوعاً من السفلي، ويشكل حوالي ٧٥٪ من الحالات، والـ upper GI bleeding معناه نزيف قبل ligament of Treitz عند وصلة الـ duodenum مع الـ jejunum. أكثر مصدر محدد للنزيف هو قرحات المعدة والـ duodenum، يعني peptic ulcer disease هي السبب الأكثر شيوعاً. المريض ممكن يجي بـ hematemesis أو melena، والـ endoscopy تشخّص المصدر وغالباً تعالج كمان.
الفخ: في ناس تختار esophageal varices لأن المريض عنده cirrhosis، بس الـ varices شائعة أقل من الـ peptic ulcer disease. تذكّر إنه الـ varices والـ gastritis والـ Mallory-Weiss tears كلها أسباب شائعة بس أقل من قرحات الـ peptic.

question:
A 20-year-old man presents to the ED with fever and severe right
lower quadrant (RLQ) pain for 1 day. Prior to this episode, he reports 2
months of crampy abdominal pain, generalized malaise, a 10-lb weight loss,
and occasional bloody diarrhea. On examination, his BP is 125/70 mm Hg,
HR is 115 beats/minute, RR is 18 breaths/minute, and temperature is
100.8°F. His only significant past medical history is recurrent perirectal
abscesses. He appears uncomfortable and has a tender mass in the RLQ,
without guarding or rebound. Rectal examination is positive for trace heme-

positive stool. An abdominal computed tomographic (CT) scan reveals no
periappendiceal fat stranding. There is inflammation of the distal ileum and
several areas of the colon. There are no rectal inflammatory changes. Which
of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
256.  The answer is a. IBD refers to chronic inflammatory disease of the
GI tract. There are two major types—Crohn’s disease and ulcerative
colitis. Crohn’s disease can involve any part of the GI tract, from mouth to
anus, and is characterized by segmental involvement. The distal ileum is
involved in the majority of cases; therefore, acute presentations can mimic
appendicitis. Crohn’s disease spares the rectum in 50% of cases. There is a
bimodal age distribution, with the first peak occurring in patients 15 to 22
years of age and a second in patients 55 to 60 years of age. Definitive
diagnosis is by upper GI series, air-contrast barium enema, and
colonoscopy. Segmental involvement of the colon with rectal sparing is the
most characteristic feature. Other findings on colonoscopy include
involvement of all bowel wall layers, skip lesions (ie, interspersed normal
and diseased bowel), aphthous ulcers, and cobblestone appearance from

submucosal thickening interspersed with mucosal ulceration. Extraintestinal
manifestations are seen in 25% to 30% of patients with Crohn’s disease.
Ulcerative colitis (b) primarily involves the mucosa only with formation
of crypt abscesses, epithelial necrosis, and mucosal ulceration. Rectal pain
and bloody diarrhea are more common in ulcerative colitis than in Crohn’s
disease. Ulcerative colitis begins in the rectum, and fails to progress beyond
this point in one-third of patients. Colonoscopy demonstrates inflammation
of the mucosa only and continuous lesions of the GI tract. Although blood
loss from sustained bleeding may be the most common complication, toxic
megacolon must not be missed. While appendicitis (c) may be in the
differential diagnosis, the acute chronic nature of this disease and a normalappearing appendix on abdominal CT rules it out. Pseudomembranous
enterocolitis (d) is an IBD that results from toxin-producing Clostridium
difficile, a spore-forming obligate anaerobic bacillus. The disease typically
begins 7 to 10 days after the institution of antibiotic therapy, most often in
hospitalized patients. However, incidence in the community is rising.
Diverticulitis (e) is an acute inflammatory disease caused by bacterial
proliferation within existing colonic diverticula. The most common
presentation is pain, often in the LLQ. Abdominal CT demonstrates
inflammation of pericolic fat, presence of diverticula, bowel wall
thickening, or peridiverticular abscess.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ Crohn's disease ممكن يصيب أي جزء من الجهاز الهضمي من الفم للشرج، ويتميز بإصابة segmental، والـ distal ileum متأثر بأغلب الحالات عشان هيك ممكن يشبه appendicitis. الـ Crohn يستثني الـ rectum بحوالي ٥٠٪ من الحالات، وعند المريض كان في inflammation بالـ ileum ومناطق بالقولون بدون تغيرات بالـ rectum. كمان الـ perirectal abscesses المتكررة والـ CT اللي ما فيه periappendiceal fat stranding يدعموا التشخيص.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا appendicitis بسبب الوجع بالـ RLQ، بس الـ CT ما بيّن periappendiceal fat stranding. والفرقة عن ulcerative colitis إنه الـ Crohn يستثني الـ rectum ويسوي skip lesions.

question:
A 62-year-old woman with known history of coronary artery disease
on aspirin and clopidogrel presents to the ED with bright red blood per
rectum. Patient reports that she has had intermittent blood in her stool for
the past 2 days. Just prior to arrival, she had two episodes of large volume
bright red bloody stools. Her temperature is 98.6°F, HR is 98 beats/minute,
and BP is 115/74 mm Hg. She reports mild cramping that resolved and is
not having any pain at this time. A hemoglobin in the ER is 8.6 mg/dL
(hematocrit 26%) and white blood cell (WBC) count 7000/μL. Previous
colonoscopy records show colonic diverticula. She does not have any
bloody bowel movements during her stay in the emergency room (ER).
Which is the most appropriate diagnostic work-up for this patient?

options.text: Admit for bowel clean out and colonoscopy

correctAnswer: Admit for bowel clean out and colonoscopy
englishExplanation:
257.  The answer is b. This patient should be admitted for bowel clean
out and colonoscopy. Patient likely has bleeding from diverticulosis.
Diverticula are small outpouchings in the wall of the colon. They can
become inflamed and cause diverticulitis which is painful and typically
associated with an elevated inflammatory marker (WBC). Diverticulitis
does not usually cause painless bleeding.
The patient is hemodynamically stable and does not have any active
bleeding therefore might be eligible for outpatient follow-up (c). However,
she is anemic and on aspirin and clopidogrel, therefore it would not be safe
for her to be discharged without further evaluation. A CT abdomen and
pelvis (a) would be more useful in the setting of acute abdominal pain or
concern for inflammation, such as colitis or diverticulitis. A tagged RBC
scan (d) is useful when a patient is continuing to have active bleeding.
Evaluation of the small bowel with capsule endoscopy (e) may ultimately

be necessary if no other source is identified but is not the first step in
evaluation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها diverticula بالقولون، والنزيف اللي صار غالباً من diverticulosis لأنه الـ diverticulitis عادة يجي مع وجع و WBC مرتفع، وهنا الوجع خفيف وذهب والـ WBC طبيعي. المريضة مستقرة hemodynamically وما عندها نزيف نشط، بس عندها anemia والـ hemoglobin ٨.٦ وهي على aspirin و clopidogrel، وعشان هيك مو آمن نصرّفها بدون تقييم. فالقرار المناسب هو تنويم لعمل bowel clean out و colonoscopy.
الفخ: في ناس تختار discharge للـ outpatient follow-up، وهذا غلط لأنها anemic وعلى مضادات صفيحات. والـ tagged RBC scan بيتعمل بس لما يكون في نزيف نشط مستمر، وهنا النزيف وقف.

question:
If the adverse event rate of performing endoscopy with sclerotherapy
alone is 50% and the adverse event rate of administering octreotide
followed by endoscopy with sclerotherapy is 30%, what is the number of
patients you need to treat with octreotide to prevent one bad outcome?
englishExplanation:
263.  The answer is d. To calculate number needed to treat (NNT), you
must first devise the absolute risk reduction (ARR). In order to do this,
you must subtract the experimental event rate (EER) from the control event
rate (CER). The CER is 50% (0.5) and the EER 30% (0.3) in this question.
Thus, the ARR is 20% or 0.2 (0.5 – 0.3 = 0.2). The NNT is 1/ARR; in this
question it is 1/0.2 = 5. Thus, the NNT is five patients.
All other answer choices (a, b, c, and e) are incorrect based on the
previous calculation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لحساب الـ NNT لازم أول شي نجيب الـ absolute risk reduction، وهذا بنجيبه لما نطرح الـ experimental event rate من الـ control event rate. عندنا الـ CER هو ٥٠٪ يعني ٠.٥ والـ EER هو ٣٠٪ يعني ٠.٣، فبيطلع الـ ARR يساوي ٠.٢. والـ NNT هو ١ مقسوم على الـ ARR، يعني ١ على ٠.٢ يساوي ٥، وعشان هيك الجواب خمس مرضى.
الفخ: في ناس تختار عشرة أو سبعة لأنهم يقلبوا المعادلة أو يجمعوا الأرقام بدل ما يطرحوا. تذكّر إنه الـ NNT دايماً ١ على الـ ARR، والـ ARR هي الفرق بين النسبتين.

question:
Shared scenario:
A 76-year-old woman with a history of congestive heart failure, coronary
artery disease, and an “irregular heart beat” is brought to the ED by her
family. She has been complaining of increasing abdominal pain over the
past several days. She denies nausea or vomiting and bowel movements
remain unchanged. Vitals are BP of 110/75 mm Hg, HR of 114
beats/minute, and temperature of 98°F. She appears to be in significant pain.
Her HR is irregular with no murmur detected. The abdomen is soft,
nontender, and nondistended. The stool is heme-positive.

265.   What is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
265.  The answer is d. Patients with coronary artery disease, valvular heart
disease, and arrhythmias, particularly atrial fibrillation, are at high risk for
mesenteric ischemia. In addition, age greater than 50 years, congestive
heart failure, recent myocardial infarction, critically ill patients with sepsis
or hypotension, use of diuretics or vasoconstrictive medications, and
hypercoagulable states place patients at higher risk. The most common
cause of acute mesenteric ischemia is arterial embolus, which accounts for
50% of cases. The classic finding is “pain out of proportion to
examination findings”; that is, a patient complains of severe pain but is not
particularly tender on examination. A high degree of suspicion for
mesenteric ischemia in an elderly patient with abdominal pain is warranted.
Perforated gastric ulcer (a) presents with acute onset of severe
epigastric pain and bleeding, generally in someone with PUD. Diverticulitis
(b) presents as LLQ pain that is usually described as dull and constant.
Acute cholecystitis (c) occurs with an obstruction of the cystic duct with
gallstones and is often accompanied by fever, chills, nausea, and a positive
Murphy sign. It is the most common surgical emergency in elderly patients.
The classic triad for sigmoid volvulus (e) includes abdominal pain,
abdominal distention, and constipation. Nausea and vomiting are often
present, and diagnosis can be made on plain radiograph in 80% of cases.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها coronary artery disease و congestive heart failure ونبض غير منتظم، وهذه العوامل بتخليها بخطورة عالية للـ mesenteric ischemia، والسبب الأكثر شيوعاً هو arterial embolus. العلامة الكلاسيكية هي أن الوجع يكون أكبر بكثير من نتائج الفحص، يعني المريضة تشتكي من وجع شديد بس البطن لين وغير مؤلم عند الفحص، وعندها كمان stool heme-positive. كبار العمر مع وجع بطن لازم نفكر فوراً بالـ mesenteric ischemia.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا perforated ulcer أو cholecystitis، بس الـ perforation يجي بوجع epigastric حاد، والـ cholecystitis معه fever وحمى و Murphy sign إيجابي. الفرقة إنه هون الوجع شديد والفحص طبيعي.

question:
Shared scenario:
A 27-year-old man presents to the ED with significant epigastric abdominal
pain. He is generally healthy, but did recently sustain an ankle sprain
playing soccer. He reports that he has been having worsening heartburn for
the past several days, but tonight it became severe and he was nauseous. He
had one episode of coffee ground emesis prior to arrival. On further
questioning, he admits his stools have become black and tarry over the past
few days as well. He has an HR of 110 beats/minute and BP of 110/75 mm
Hg. His hemoglobin is 9.8 mg/dL. You start IV fluids and call for a GI
consult as you think he may need an upper endoscopy.

267.   Which medication should you consider starting in the ED?
englishExplanation:
267.  The answer is d. Pantoprazole is a PPI and should be given as he
has an upper GI bleed most likely due to PUD or gastritis. Acutely,
pantoprazole decreases the pH of the stomach and improves the ability
of clotting. PPIs have also been shown to decrease the chance of rebleeding
after endoscopy.
Octreotide (a) is a somatostatin analog and should be given for
suspected variceal hemorrhage. Esophageal variceal hemorrhages can be
very dangerous and should be considered in patients with liver disease.
Calcium carbonate (b) is an antacid and although it is useful to treat
symptoms of heartburn, it is not useful in acute GI bleeding. Famotidine (c)
is an H2 blocker and would also decrease the pH of the stomach. However,
it has not been shown to decrease the risk of rebleeding after endoscopy;

therefore, PPIs are preferred. Acetaminophen (e) is a nonopioid analgesic
and antipyretic that would not have a role in acute management of upper GI
bleeds.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده نزيف علوي بالجهاز الهضمي، وغالباً السبب peptic ulcer disease أو gastritis، والدليل هو الـ coffee ground emesis والـ black tarry stools والـ hemoglobin المنخفض. الـ pantoprazole هو PPI ولازم نعطيه لأنه يقلل حموضة المعدة ويحسّن قدرة التخثر، وكمان الـ PPIs أثبتت إنها تقلل خطر إعادة النزيف بعد الـ endoscopy. عشان هيك هو الخيار المناسب بالطوارئ.
الفخ: في ناس تختار famotidine لأنه كمان يقلل الحموضة، بس الـ H2 blocker ما ثبت إنه يقلل إعادة النزيف بعد الـ endoscopy. والـ octreotide بينحفظ لـ variceal hemorrhage عند مرضى الكبد، وما عند هذا المريض دليل عليه.

question:
A 6-week-old full-term boy presents with concern for yellowing of
the eyes. His mother reports that he has been feeding well and acting
normally. The child has been solely breastfed since birth and had normal
urine output and stool output but noted lightening stool color from seedy
yellow to pale, yellow/gray in appearance. Birth history reveals an
uncomplicated normal spontaneous vaginal delivery without vacuum assist.
Hepatitis B immunization and Vitamin K injection were given at birth.
Newborn screen and patient’s transcutaneous bilirubin level at birth
discharge were normal. No recent travel or animal exposures. Vital signs on
presentation show temperature 98.9°F, BP 96/44 mm Hg, HR 164
beats/minute, RR 32 breaths/minute, and pulse oximetry 99%. Patient is
calm with scleral icterus bilaterally and mild jaundice to face and chest.
Heart sounds are normal and lungs clear. Abdomen soft and nontender with
liver edge 1 cm below the costal margin. Capillary refill is brisk. No
bruising noted on skin exam. Initial labs are notable for elevated total
bilirubin level of 14.1, and direct bilirubin 9.2, with elevation in
transaminases with AST 85 and ALT 101. CBC shows a slightly low
hemoglobin of 10.4, but otherwise normal. What is the next best step in
management?

options.text: Obtain a right upper quadrant ultrasound to evaluate the biliary tree
Discharge home with recommendation to switch to formula feed
Consult Pediatric Infectious Diseases to evaluate for infectious hepatitis
Consult Pediatric Gastroenterology to evaluate for inherited disorder of
Consult Pediatric Hematology to evaluate for autoimmune hemolytic

correctAnswer: Obtain a right upper quadrant ultrasound to evaluate the biliary tree
englishExplanation:
379.  The correct answer is a. This infant is resenting with high concern
for symptoms and laboratory findings of biliary atresia. Biliary atresia is a
condition that occurs due to abnormal development of the biliary system.
Without a proper biliary system for bile to be excreted from the liver, it
builds up within the liver tissue leading to secondary cirrhosis and
eventually liver failure. Clinical signs often include jaundice and a history
of “clay colored stool.” Laboratory findings will be consistent with a
primary cholestatic process and varying degrees of transaminitis depending
on how early the disease is caught. A right upper quadrant ultrasound is
needed to evaluate the liver and for abnormalities of the biliary system.
Gastroenterology consult (d) is prudent for medical management and
evaluation of alternative causes of hepatitis; however, rare inherited
disorders of bile excretion and metabolism less commonly cause elevated
transaminases. Consultation with an infectious disease specialist (c) can be
considered if concern for primary hepatitis or TORCH (toxoplasmosis,

rubella, cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex) infection from birth, though the
patient in this scenario had no concerning birth history, fevers, or known
exposures. Hemolysis can be a source of elevated bilirubin and AST.
However, the elevation in bilirubin would be indirect or unconjugated
which is opposite of the direct hyperbilirubinemia that this patient has.
Therefore, consultation with hematology is not indicated (e). Breast milk
jaundice (b) is a cause of hyperbilirubinemia directly related to breast
milk’s effect on bilirubin metabolism; however this would cause an indirect
hyperbilirubinemia.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الرضيع عنده علامات ومختبرات توحي بـ biliary atresia، وهي حالة بسبب تطور غير طبيعي للجهاز الصفراوي، فالصفراء تتجمع داخل نسيج الكبد وتؤدي لـ cirrhosis ثانوي وفشل كبدي لاحقاً. العلامات تشمل اليرقان وقصة clay colored stool، والمختبرات تدعم عملية cholestatic مع ارتفاع بالـ transaminases. والخطوة التالية هي عمل right upper quadrant ultrasound لتقييم الكبد وتشوهات الجهاز الصفراوي.
الفخ: في ناس يختاروا consult Pediatric Hematology لتقييم hemolysis، بس بالانحلال الـ bilirubin يكون غير مباشر، وهنا الـ direct bilirubin مرتفع ٩.٢. الفرقة إنه الـ cholestasis تعمل ارتفاع بالـ direct bilirubin.

question: What is a characteristic of visceral abdominal pain?
englishExplanation:
Midline. Visceral pain is classically midline, poorly localized, and less easily described than somatic pain, which is often referred 
to as “sharp.”

226.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ visceral abdominal pain تتميز إنها تكون midline، يعني بمنتصف البطن، وتكون poorly localized ومو واضحة الوصف. بالفرق بينها وبين الـ somatic pain اللي تكون sharp ويكون المريض يحدد مكانها بدقة. عشان هيك لما نسأل عن صفة الـ visceral pain الجواب إنها midline ومو محدد المكان.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا well-localized أو sharp، بس هاي صفات الـ somatic pain مو الـ visceral. تذكّر إنه الـ visceral مبهمة ووسط البطن، والـ somatic حادة ومحددة عشان الالتهاب وصل للـ peritoneum.

question:
A 43-year-old female presents with 1 month of painless abdominal 
swelling. On examination she has a diffusely swollen abdomen with 
a fluid wave. To help determine the etiology, you obtain the serum 
ascites albumin gradient (SAAG). Which value is consistent with 
cirrhosis?
englishExplanation:
A (SAAG) value of greater than or equal to 1.1 g/dL is 
found in patients with portal hypertension. There are many causes of 
portal hypertension, including cirrhosis, liver failure, or heart failure. 
A SAAG value of less than 1.1 g/dL may be found in patients with conditions such as lupus or pancreatitis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ serum ascites albumin gradient أو SAAG بتساعدنا نعرف سبب الاستسقاء، والقيمة اللي تساوي أو تزيد عن ١.١ g/dL تشير لوجود portal hypertension. وأسباب الـ portal hypertension كثيرة وتشمل cirrhosis وفشل الكبد وفشل القلب، وعشان هيك القيمة ١.٥ g/dL هي اللي تتوافق مع cirrhosis. بالقابل قيمة أقل من ١.١ ممكن تنشوف بـ lupus أو pancreatitis.
الفخ: في ناس تنخدع وتختار قيمة صغيرة زي ٠.٥ أو ١ g/dL، بس هاي تحت الحد ١.١ وبتشير لحالات مو portal hypertension. الفرقة إنه الـ SAAG العالي يعني portal hypertension زي cirrhosis.

question:
A 55-year-old female presents with 1 month of diffuse abdominal 
swelling and pain. She reports a long history of alcohol use. In evaluating this patient for jaundice, at what bilirubin level does jaundice 
typically become clinically apparent?
englishExplanation:
Clinical jaundice is usually not evident until the total 
serum bilirubin concentration rises above 2.5 mg/dL. Jaundice is first 
apparent sublingually, in the conjunctiva or on the hard palate.

239.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اليرقان السريري عادة ما يبين للعين إلا لما يرتفع الـ total serum bilirubin فوق ٢.٥ mg/dL. وأول مكان ينشوف فيه اليرقان هو تحت اللسان أو بالـ conjunctiva أو على الـ hard palate، وعشان هيك الفحص السريري لازم يشمل هذه المناطق. القيمة ٤ mg/dL أعلى من الحد فهي اللي بتخلي اليرقان واضح سريرياً.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا ١ أو ٢ mg/dL لأنهم يخمنوا إنه أي ارتفاع يبين، بس تحت ٢.٥ اليرقان ما يكون ظاهر. تذكّر إنه الحد هو ٢.٥ mg/dL، وأي قيمة أعلى منه تعمل يرقان مرئي.

question: Antihistamines would most effectively control the nausea and vomiting caused by which of the following conditions?
englishExplanation:
Antihistamines are particularly useful in nausea and vomiting associated with labyrinthitis, motion sickness, and vestibular 
disorders by directly inhibiting vestibular stimulation and vestibularcerebellar pathways. The anticholinergic effect may also contribute to 
their effectiveness in vertigo and motion sickness.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: مضادات الهيستامين فعّالة بشكل خاص بالغثيان والاستفراغ المصاحب للـ labyrinthitis و motion sickness واضطرابات الـ vestibular، لأنها تثبط مباشرة التحفيز الدهليزي والمسارات الـ vestibularcerebellar. كمان التأثير المضاد للكولين ممكن يساهم بفعاليتها بالـ vertigo و motion sickness. عشان هيك هي الأنسب لحالة الـ labyrinthitis.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا gastritis أو gastroparesis، بس الغثيان بهالحالات سببه معدي ومو دهليزي، ومضادات الهيستامين أقل فعالية فيه. الفرقة إنه الغثيان الدهليزي هو اللي يستجيب للـ antihistamines.

question:
Appropriate pharmacologic therapy in the emergency department 
for most acute upper gastrointestinal bleeds (UGIB) includes which 
of the following agents?
englishExplanation:
PPIs decrease rebleeding, surgery, and mortality in patients 
with an acute UGIB from an ulcer. Because peptic ulcer disease is the 
most common cause of UGIB, it is appropriate to administer PPIs for 
most acute UGIB.

251.e2
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ proton pump inhibitor بيقلل إعادة النزيف والعمليات الجراحية والوفيات عند مرضى الـ acute upper GI bleeding الناتج عن قرحة. وبما إنه الـ peptic ulcer disease هو أكثر سبب للـ UGIB، فإعطاء الـ PPIs مناسب لأغلب حالات الـ acute UGIB بالطوارئ. عشان هيك هو العلاج الدوائي المناسب لمعظم حالات النزيف العلوي.
الفخ: في ناس تختار somatostatin لأنه مرتبط بنزيف الـ varices، بس هذا خاص بحالات الـ variceal bleeding مو كل النزيف العلوي. والـ erythromycin و antibiotics مو العلاج الأساسي إلا بحالات محددة.

question: In which of the following patients would Clostridioides difficile testing be least useful?

options.text: Patient with diarrhea who is taking omeprazole for known peptic ulcer disease.
Patient with diarrhea after recent tonsillitis treated with amoxicillin.
Patient with diarrhea who is a long-term resident of a skilled
Patient with acute vomiting and watery diarrhea following contact with a toddler with similar symptoms.
Patient with uncontrolled HIV and acute watery diarrhea.

correctAnswer: Patient with acute vomiting and watery diarrhea following contact with a toddler with similar symptoms.
englishExplanation:
Patient in answer D likely has a viral gastroenteritis, and C. 
difficile testing is more likely to result in false positive result or identify 
chronic colonization. Risk factors for C. difficile colitis include antibiotic or gastric acid suppressive therapy, skilled nursing facility residence, and chronic medical conditions.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض اللي عنده استفراغ حاد وإسهال مائي بعد مخالطة طفل عنده نفس الأعراض غالباً عنده viral gastroenteritis، وفي هذه الحالة فحص الـ C. difficile أقل فائدة. لأنه غالباً بيعطي false positive أو بيكشف colonization مزمن مو مرض حقيقي. وعوامل الخطورة للـ C. difficile colitis هي المضادات الحيوية أو مثبطات حمض المعدة، والإقامة بـ skilled nursing facility، والأمراض المزمنة.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا المريض اللي على omeprazole أو المقيم بـ nursing facility، بس هدول فعلاً عندهم عوامل خطورة والفحص عندهم مفيد. الفرقة إنه الانتقال من طفل لطفل يوحي بفيروس مو C. difficile.

question:
In which of the following patients is loperamide a safe treatment 
option?

options.text: Adult patient with acute watery diarrhea of unknown etiology
Adult patient with sepsis and bloody diarrhea
Elderly patient with a history of bowel obstruction with watery
Pediatric patient with acute watery diarrhea from norovirus

correctAnswer: Adult patient with acute watery diarrhea of unknown etiology
englishExplanation:
Loperamide, a bowel-selective opioid agonist, is an effective 
tool to reduce diarrhea severity. Although generally safe, it has been 
associated with toxic megacolon and obstruction in select groups, such 
as the elderly, pediatric patients (especially younger than age 3), and 
patients with a severe inflammatory colitis. Adult patients in which the 
risk of obstruction or severe inflammatory colitis is low are candidates 
for loperamide treatment.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ loperamide هو opioid agonist انتقائي للأمعاء وفعّال لتخفيف شدة الإسهال، وهو آمن بشكل عام لمعظم المرضى. بس ارتبط بالـ toxic megacolon والانسداد بفئات معينة مثل كبار السن والأطفال خصوصاً أقل من ٣ سنوات ومرضى الـ severe inflammatory colitis. عشان هيك البالغ اللي عنده إسهال مائي حاد مجهول السبب وما فيه خطورة عالية هو المرشح الآمن للـ loperamide.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا مريض الـ sepsis مع bloody diarrhea أو الطفل، بس هدول عندهم خطر colitis شديد أو أعمار صغيرة والـ loperamide ممنوع. الفرقة إنه البالغ المستقر بدون دم هو الآمن.

question: Which of the following is true regarding constipation?

options.text: The diagnosis of constipation requires lab testing and imaging in
Most patients with constipation and a normal examination can
Constipation is less common in the elderly due to low fiber,
Chronic constipation occurs when a patient experiences

correctAnswer: Most patients with constipation and a normal examination can
englishExplanation:
The term constipation refers to a multitude of symptoms, 
not a medical diagnosis. Patients often have different personal definitions for the term “constipation.” Chronic constipation refers constipation symptoms for 3 or more months. Constipation is more common in 
the elderly due to sedentary lifestyles and low-fiber, mechanically soft 
diets. In the ED, lab testing and imaging is often unnecessary for patients 
with a normal physical exam. Most well-appearing patients with constipation and a normal examination can be discharged home with empiric 
management.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: مصطلح الـ constipation بيشير لمجموعة أعراض ومو تشخيص طبي، والناس غالباً عندهم تعريفات شخصية مختلفة له. الـ chronic constipation يعني وجود الأعراض لمدة ٣ أشهر أو أكثر، وهي أكثر شيوعاً بكبار السن بسبب قلة الحركة والحمية القليلة الألياف. بالطوارئ الفحوصات المخبرية والتصوير غالباً مو ضرورية إذا الفحص السريري طبيعي، وأغلب المرضى اللي حالتهم مستقرة وفحصهم طبيعي بينصرّفوا للبيت مع علاج تجريبي.
الفخ: في ناس تختار إنه الـ constipation تتطلب labs و imaging دايماً، وهذا غلط لأن الفحص الطبيعي يكفي غالباً. الفرقة إنه المريض اللي شكله منيح وفحصه طبيعي ما بدو تصوير.

question: Which of the following is an initial management option for esophageal food bolus impactions in the ED?
englishExplanation:
Although none of the medical therapies are as good as 
endoscopy, Glucagon is likely more efficacious than nitroglycerin and 
nifedipine. Enzymatic degradation of an impacted meat bolus using 
the proteolytic enzyme papain, should not be performed because of 
risks of esophageal perforation. The gold standard intervention strategy for esophageal foreign body removal is endoscopy.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ Glucagon هو خيار علاجي أولي معقول بالطوارئ لانسداد الـ esophagus بسبب لقمة طعام، لأنه أكثر فعالية من الـ nitroglycerin والـ nifedipine. بس بالحقيقة ما في علاج دوائي أفضل من الـ endoscopy، وهي التدخل الذهبي لإزالة الأجسام الغريبة من الـ esophagus. والـ papain ممنوع استخدامه لأنه يحمل خطر perforation للـ esophagus.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا papain لأنه يحلل اللحمة، بس هذا غلط كبير لأنه يسبب خطر ثقب الـ esophagus. والـ sublingual nitroglycerine أقل فعالية من الـ glucagon، والـ endoscopy تبقى المعيار الذهبي.

question:
If the patient in the previous question instead had a BP of 200/125, 
and was diuretic naïve, which of the following would be the best 
management approach?

options.text: BiPAP, nitroglycerin 1–2 mg IV push repeated until SBP 150 mm
BiPAP, morphine 4 mg IV push, furosemide 40 mg IV push
BiPAP, isosorbide mononitrate 60 mg PO, furosemide 40 mg PO
BiPAP, nitroglycerin 1–2 mg IV push repeated until SBP <150,

correctAnswer: BiPAP, nitroglycerin 1–2 mg IV push repeated until SBP 150 mm
englishExplanation:
In this variation of question two, the patient is diuretic 
naïve and has features suspicious for the vascular phenotype of AHF. 
Furosemide should therefore be dosed at 40–80 mg IVP, and a 25% 
or less reduction in SBP should be targeted with repeated IV push 
nitroglycerin, 1–2 mg per dose. In patients with less distress or less 
severe hypertension who still show the vascular phenotype, sublingual 
nitroglycerin is a useful alternative because absorption and bioavailability are similar to IV. Transdermal and PO nitrates are not currently 
thought to be useful in AHF, by contrast, because of less favorable 
kinetics.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بالمريض اللي ضغطه ٢٠٠ على ١٢٥ وهو diuretic naïve وفيه صفات vascular phenotype من الـ acute heart failure، لازم نعطيه furosemide 40 mg وريدي مع BiPAP و nitroglycerin وريدي ١-٢ mg بشكل متكرر. والهدف إنه نخفض الـ systolic blood pressure بحوالي ٢٥٪ أو أقل. ولما يكون المريض أقل ضيق وضغطه أقل شدة مع نفس النمط، ممكن نستخدم الـ sublingual nitroglycerin لأنه امتصاصه قريب من الوريدي.
الفخ: في ناس يختاروا nitrates بالفم أو transdermal، بس هدول ما بينفعوا بالـ acute heart failure بسبب حركية الدواء غير المناسبة. كمان الـ furosemide بالفم أبطأ من الوريدي، والـ IV push هو الأسرع بهالحالة.

question: What percentage of esophageal foreign bodies require a nonoperative intervention to facilitate removal?
englishExplanation:
Most foreign bodies pass spontaneously. Approximately 10% 
to 20% require intervention, but less than 1% require surgery for removal.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أغلب الأجسام الغريبة بالـ esophagus تمر spontaneously بدون تدخل. بس حوالي ١٠٪ إلى ٢٠٪ من هذه الحالات تحتاج تدخل غير جراحي عشان نساعد بإزالتها. وأقل من ١٪ بس تحتاج عملية جراحية للإزالة، عشان هيك النسبة الصحيحة هي ١٠٪ إلى ٢٠٪.
الفخ: في ناس تختار نسب عالية مثل ٥٠٪ أو ٧٥٪ لأنهم يخمنوا إنه أغلب الحالات تحتاج تدخل، بس هذا غلط لأن الأغلبية تمر لحالها. الفرقة إنه بس نسبة صغيرة تحتاج intervention والجراحة نادرة جداً.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding the use of glucagon in 
esophageal obstruction from a food bolus is true?

options.text: Glucagon should be administered by the oral route.
Glucagon can facilitate passage of a food bolus localized anywhere in the esophagus.
Glucagon is relatively contraindicated with sharp-edged foreign
The success rate of glucagon approaches 90% when used with a

correctAnswer: Glucagon is relatively contraindicated with sharp-edged foreign
englishExplanation:
Glucagon is a smooth muscle relaxant, so it is theoretically 
useful only for distal esophageal foreign bodies. There are only anecdotal reports of success with glucagon, but a literature review shows 
no statistical benefit of glucagon in treating esophageal foreign bodies. 
There are many adverse effects, including flushing, nausea, and vomiting, that can potentially increase the risk of aspiration. It is contraindicated for use with sharp or damaging foreign bodies. There is only 
low-level evidence to support the use of effervescent agents, and they 
are relatively contraindicated after 24 hours because of perforation 
concerns.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ Glucagon هو مرخي للعضلات الملساء، وعشان هيك نظرياً مفيد بس للأجسام الغريبة بالجزء البعيد من الـ esophagus. بس الأدبيات ما بينت أي فائدة إحصائية للـ glucagon بعلاج الأجسام الغريبة بالـ esophagus، وفي تقارير نادرة بس عن نجاحه. وعند استعماله مضار كثيرة مثل flushing والغثيان والاستفراغ اللي ممكن تزيد خطر aspiration، وعشان هيك هو ممنوع نسبياً مع الأجسام الغريبة حادة الحواف.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا إنه نجاحه يقارب ٩٠٪، بس هذا مو صحيح لأن الفائدة ما ثبتت إحصائياً. الفرقة إنه مع الأجسام الحادة أو المؤذية الـ glucagon ممنوع نسبياً لأنه ممكن يعمل إصابة.

question: Which of the following is an indication for urgent endoscopy?

options.text: Chest pain due to foreign body
Object failing to pass out of the esophagus after 12 hours

englishExplanation:
A coin that remains lodged in the proximal esophagus 
should be removed. Other indications are inability to handle secretions, sharp objects, esophageal button battery (alkaline), and impactions that fail to pass after 24 hours.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ endoscopy العاجلة بتنبعت لما يكون في indication واضح، والعملة المعدنية أو الـ coin اللي تعلق بالجزء القريب من الـ esophagus لازم تنشال. ومن الاستطبابات الثانية عدم القدرة على التعامل مع الإفرازات، والأجسام الحادة، و esophageal button battery لأنها قلوية وخطيرة، والانسدادات اللي ما تمر بعد ٢٤ ساعة. عشان هيك وجود coin بالـ proximal esophagus هو الاستطباب الصحيح.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا button battery بالمعدة أو الجسم اللي ما مر بعد ١٢ ساعة، بس الـ battery بالمعدة مو بالـ esophagus وما تحتاج endoscopy عاجلة. والفترة المعتمدة للانسداد هي ٢٤ ساعة مو ١٢.

question:
Ulcers in which portion of the upper GI tract are most likely to 
perforate?
englishExplanation:
Duodenal ulcers account for 60% of all perforations, followed 
by antral gastric ulcers (20%) and gastric body ulcers (20%). Various 
upper gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms may lead to esophageal ulcerations and severe odynophagia, although perforation is infrequent.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: قرحات الـ duodenum هي المسؤولة عن ٦٠٪ من كل حالات الـ perforation، وبعدها تجي قرحات الـ antrum بالمعدة بحوالي ٢٠٪ وقرحات جسم المعدة بحوالي ٢٠٪. والقرحات بالـ esophagus ممكن تعمل أعراض علوية شديدة و odynophagia، بس الـ perforation فيها نادر. عشان هيك الجزء الأكثر عرضة للانثقاب هو الـ duodenal.
الفخ: في ناس تختاروا gastric أو esophageal، بس الـ esophageal نادراً ما تنثقب والـ gastric أنترال وجسم أقل من الـ duodenal. الفرقة إنه الـ duodenal لوحده مسؤول عن ٦٠٪ من الانثقابات.

question:
A 26-year-old man presents with complaints of pruritus and a raised 
rash for 7 days. The rash has been associated with nausea and painful 
symmetrical swelling of both wrists and metacarpophalangeal joints. 
He has no past medical history and takes no medications. He works 
in a retail store. Vital signs are normal, and the physical examination 
is remarkable for right upper quadrant tenderness, bilateral mild wrist 
effusion with minimal warmth and no erythema, and diffuse skin 
urticaria. The remainder of the examination is negative. Blood count, 
chemistries, and liver studies are remarkable for WBC of 11,800 cells/
mm3, AST of 212 IU/L, ALT of 395 IU/L, normal alkaline phosphatase 
level, and total bilirubin of 2.3 mg/dL. Which of the following diagnostic modalities would be most likely to yield the causative diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
A small number of patients with hepatitis B develop a prodrome of arthralgias and arthritis (symmetric small joints) and dermatitis. The dermatitis is typically urticarial but may be macular, popular, 
or petechial.
arabicExplanation: ليش: هذا المريض عنده التهاب كبد وبائي مع مفاصل مؤلمة وطفح جلدي، وهذي أعراض بتصير قبل ما يطلع اليرقان. نسبة قليلة من مرضى hepatitis B بتجيهم مرحلة بدائية فيها ألم بالمفاصل الصغيرة المتماثلة والتهاب جلد على شكل urticaria. عشان هيك الفحص اللي بيعطي التشخيص السببي هو Hepatitis B surface antigen. الطفح ممكن يكون urticarial أو macular أو popular أو petechial. الفخ: كثير طلاب يختارون Joint aspiration لأنهم يفكرون بالتهاب المفاصل الجرثومي، بس هنا المفصل دافي بدون احمرار وبلا حمى، والمفاصل المتماثلة مع ارتفاع الإنزيمات توحي بالسبب الفيروسي.

question:
Scleral icterus becomes clinically apparent at approximately which 
serum bilirubin level?
englishExplanation:
Icterus is often first noted in the sublingual or subungual areas when the serum bilirubin level is above approximately 
2.5 mg/dL.
arabicExplanation: ليش: اليرقان أو scleral icterus بيصير ملحوظ سريرياً لما يرتفع مستوى الـ serum bilirubin لمستوى معين. حسب المصدر فإن الـ icterus غالباً يلاحظ أول شي في المناطق تحت اللسان أو تحت الأظافر لما يكون البيليروبين فوق حوالي 2.5 mg/dL. بالحالة هذي المستوى الصحيح هو 2.5 mg/dL. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون 2 mg/dL لأنهم يخلطون بين حد اليرقان المخاطي وحد الملاحظة الصبغية تحت اللسان، فالتمييز يعتمد على أن 2.5 mg/dL هو الرقم اللي بيصير فيه اللون ملحوظ.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding the typical laboratory 
profile for a patient with acute viral hepatitis is true?

options.text: AST is generally elevated in excess of ALT.
Direct and indirect bilirubin levels are elevated in almost equal
Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels are almost always normal.
The alkaline phosphatase level is generally elevated 5 to 10 times
The WBC always shows a marked polymorphonuclear leukocytosis.

correctAnswer: Direct and indirect bilirubin levels are elevated in almost equal
englishExplanation:
The alkaline phosphatase level is rarely elevated more 
than 2 or 3 times normal, and LDH levels are modestly elevated. The 
WBC count may range from low, with lymphocytic predominance, 
to a polymorphonuclear (PMN)-predominant leukocytosis. ALT is 
almost always elevated in excess of AST in the setting of acute viral 
hepatitis.
arabicExplanation: ليش: في التهاب الكبد الفيروسي الحاد، البروفايل المخبري عنده نمط معين لازم نعرفه. المصدر يقول إن البيليروبين المباشر وغير المباشر بيرتفعان بنسب متقاربة جداً، يعني الجواب صحيح. كذلك الـ alkaline phosphatase نادراً يرتفع أكثر من مرتين إلى ثلاث أضعاف الطبيعي، والـ LDH يرتفع بشكل متوسط فقط. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون أن AST أعلى من ALT، بس العكس هو الصح في التهاب الكبد الفيروسي الحاد، حيث ALT غالباً أعلى من AST، وهذا فرق مهم كتير بالتمييز.

question:
A 39-year-old man presents with a 4-day history of abdominal pain 
and nausea. He has no significant past history and takes no medications. Vital signs include a temperature of 37.7°C (99.9°F) oral, 
pulse of 98 beats/min, respiratory rate of 20 breaths/min, and a 
blood pressure of 119/68 mm Hg. The physical examination reveals 
scleral icterus, a normal cardiopulmonary examination, moderate 
right upper quadrant tenderness without rebound, and guaiacnegative stool. Laboratory assessment reveals the following:
Total bilirubin
9.8 mg/dL
Conjugated bilirubin
4.6 mg/dL
Unconjugated bilirubin
5.2 mg/dL
AST
5300 IU/L
ALT
8400 IU/L
Alkaline phosphatase
750 IU/L
Albumin
3.9 mg/dL
INR
1.2
Hematocrit
42%
Platelet count
396,000/mm3
WBC
9900/mm3
Blood urea nitrogen (BUN)
53 mg/dL
Creatinine
0.9 mg/dL
Which of the following courses of action is most appropriate?

options.text: Admission for observation and GI consultation
CT scan of the abdomen with contrast

correctAnswer: Admission for observation and GI consultation
englishExplanation:
Altered sensorium and prolongation of the PT beyond 5 
seconds or INR beyond 1.5 suggests fulminant hepatic failure. Similarly, an unexplained elevation of the BUN or creatinine level may 
portend hepatorenal syndrome, which is associated with significant 
morbidity. The laboratory derangements warrant admission or transfer for hydration, close observation, and gastroenterology evaluation. 
Interferon has demonstrated some success in symptomatic hepatitis B patients but does not affect the early course. There is no role for 
corticosteroids.
arabicExplanation: ليش: هذا المريض عنده التهاب كبد حاد شديد مع AST وALT مرتفعين جداً وبيليروبين عالي، مع ارتفاع غير مبرر في الـ BUN. المصدر يقول إن ارتفاع الـ BUN أو creatinine غير المبرر ممكن ينذر بـ hepatorenal syndrome المرتبط بمراضة كبيرة. هذي الاختلالات المخبرية تستدعي الدخول للمستشفى أو التحويل للسوائل والمراقبة الدقيقة وتقييم gastroenterology. الفخ: كثير طلاب يختارون interferon therapy لأنه سمعوا عنه بالتهاب الكبد B، بس الـ interferon ما يأثر على المسار المبكر للمرض، وما في دور للـ corticosteroids، والإجابة الصح هي الدخول للمراقبة.

question:
The risk of liver injury in men increases as daily consumption of 
alcohol exceeds which of the following?
englishExplanation:
80 g of alcohol consumption is equivalent to a six-pack of 
beer, four to six glasses of wine, or three or four mixed drinks. For 
women, the risk increases with daily consumption of more than 20 g 
of alcohol.
arabicExplanation: ليش: خطر إصابة الكبد عند الرجال يزيد لما يتجاوز استهلاك الكحول اليومي كمية معينة. حسب المصدر فإن الـ 80 g من الكحول تعادل ست علب بيرة أو أربع إلى ست كاسات نبيذ أو ثلاث إلى أربع مشروبات مخلوطة. عند النساء الخطر يزيد لما يتجاوز الاستهلاك اليومي 20 g. الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون 40 g أو 60 g لأنهم يظنون أن الحد أقل، بس الرقم المعتمد للرجال هو 80 g بينما 20 g هو حد النساء، فانتبه للفرق بين الجنسين.

question:
A 63-year-old man with history of alcohol abuse presents with 
altered mental status. His family reports 3 days of decreasing ambulation and increasingly nonsensical conversation. He has no other 
known past medical history and takes no medications. Vital signs 
are unremarkable. Physical examination reveals a thin, unkempt 
man who is oriented to person only but is cooperative and follows 
commands. He falls asleep easily. There is no scleral icterus, and 
cardiopulmonary, abdominal, stool guaiac, and neurologic examinations are otherwise normal. A noncontrast CT scan of the head 
is negative for acute pathology. Pertinent laboratory findings are as 
follows:
Hematocrit (HCT)
34%
Hemoglobin
11.4 g/dL
Platelet count
108,000/mm3
WBC
9300/mm3
AST
148 IU/L
ALT
86 IU/L
Total bilirubin
2 mg/dL
Albumin
2.2 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase
158 IU/L
INR
1.8
BUN
38 mg/dL
Creatinine
2.1 mg/dL
Ethanol
0 mg/dL
Bicarbonate
30 mmol/L
Sodium
133 mEq/L
Potassium
3.6 mEq/L
Chloride
95 mEq/L
What is the most appropriate intervention?

options.text: Admission for lactulose, 30 to 60 g daily, titrated to modest diarrhea
Determination of further therapy, admission, and treatment
Discharge with the family; neomycin, 500 mg every 4 to 6 hours
Oral metronidazole, 250 mg PO every 6 hours

correctAnswer: Admission for lactulose, 30 to 60 g daily, titrated to modest diarrhea
englishExplanation:
Ammonia accumulates in severe liver disease and 
crosses the blood-brain barrier to eventually form glutamine. 
Ammonia levels correlate poorly with encephalopathy. Lactulose 
is an osmotic cathartic that acidifies colonic contents, causing 
ammonia trapping. Neomycin is a poorly absorbed aminoglycoside 
that reduces colonic bacteria but is relatively contraindicated in 
cases of renal insufficiency. Therapies for hepatic encephalopathy 
that have been under clinical investigation include metronidazole, 
zinc, flumazenil, and eradication of Helicobacter pylori. Vitamin 
K would have modest benefit due to loss of hepatic synthetic 
abilities.

arabicExplanation: ليش: هذا المريض عنده اعتلال دماغي كبدي hepatic encephalopathy مع تخليط وتشوش وارتفاع INR وانخفاض albumin. المصدر يقول إن الـ lactulose هو ملين أسموزي بيحمض محتوى القولون فيحبس الأمونيا داخل الأمعاء ويمنع امتصاصها. الجواب الأنسب هو الدخول للمستشفى وإعطاء lactulose بجرعة 30 إلى 60 g يومياً تتراوح حسب حدوث إسهال خفيف. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون neomycin لأنه يقلل بكتيريا القولون، بس المصدر يحذر إنه مضاد حيوي أمينوغليكوزيد ضعيف الامتصاص وممنوع نسبياً عند وجود renal insufficiency، وهنا الكرياتينين مرتفع.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding acute pancreatitis is 
true?

options.text: Esophageal ultrasound is the diagnostic imaging of modality of
Hypertriglyceridemia is the likely etiology of acute pancreatitis
The most common cause of acute pancreatitis is alcohol abuse.
Acute pancreatitis is the most lethal pancreatic disease globally.
Pancreatic pseudocysts form within the first week of symptom

correctAnswer: Hypertriglyceridemia is the likely etiology of acute pancreatitis
englishExplanation:
Serum triglyceride levels greater than 1000 mg/dL with 
no other clear causes of acute pancreatitis points to hypertriglyceridemia as the etiology. Imaging is not routinely recommended in the 
diagnosis of acute pancreatitis. CT is the diagnostic modality of choice; 
endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) is invasive and not recommended as a 
first line imaging test. Although acute pancreatitis is the most common pancreatic disease globally, pancreatic cancer carries the highest 
mortality. Pancreatic pseudocysts generally form after 4 weeks from 
symptom onset.
arabicExplanation: ليش: السؤال عن التهاب البنكرياس الحاد وأي عبارة صحيحة. المصدر يقول إن ارتفاع الـ serum triglyceride فوق 1000 mg/dL بدون أسباب واضحة تانية للالتهاب البنكرياسي يوجّه إلى أن hypertriglyceridemia هي السبب. عشان هيك العبارة إن hypertriglyceridemia هي الأتيولوجيا المحتملة صحيحة. الفخ: كثير طلاب يختارون أن السبب الأكثر شيوعاً هو alcohol abuse، لكن المصدر يقول إن gallstones هي السبب الأكثر شيوعاً، والـ pancreatic cancer هو الأعلى وفيات مو التهاب البنكرياس، والأكياس الكاذبة تتشكل بعد 4 أسابيع مو بأسبوع.

question:
Which of the following statements about serum lipase and amylase 
levels is true?

options.text: Lipase is an enzyme which aids in the digestion of carbohydrates.
In acute pancreatitis, amylase levels rise in 1 or 2 hours and normalize in 2 days.
Higher lipase and amylase levels are correlated with more severe
Amylase is a less specific test than the serum lipase level for the
Testing for both lipase and amylase enzymes improves the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for acute pancreatitis.

correctAnswer: Amylase is a less specific test than the serum lipase level for the
englishExplanation:
Lipase is more specific than amylase in the diagnosis of 
acute pancreatitis as amylase is produced by multiple organs other than 
the pancreas and lipase is produced predominantly by the pancreas. 
Lipase aids in the breakdown of dietary triglycerides into free fatty 
acids while amylase aids in the breakdown of carbohydrates. Levels 
rise within 6 to 24 hours and normalize in 3 to 7 days. Higher enzyme 
levels have not been found to correlate with disease severity. Testing for 
both enzymes has not been found to improve diagnostic sensitivity and 
specificity in the diagnosis of acute pancreatitis.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المقارنة بين serum lipase و amylase مهمة بتشخيص التهاب البنكرياس. المصدر يقول إن الـ lipase أكثر نوعية من الـ amylase لأن الـ amylase تنتجها أعضاء كثيرة غير البنكرياس بينما الـ lipase ينتجها البنكرياس بشكل أساسي. كمان الإنزيمات ترتفع خلال 6 إلى 24 ساعة وتتطبع خلال 3 إلى 7 أيام، والـ lipase بيساعد بتكسير الدهون الثلاثية والـ amylase بالكربوهيدرات. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون أن عمل الفحصين مع بعض يحسن الحساسية والنوعية، بس المصدر يقول إن عمل الإنزيمين معاً ما حسّن الحساسية والنوعية، والمستويات الأعلى ما ترتبط بمرض أشد.

question:
After eating undercooked ground beef, a patient develops fever, 
abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and rectal tenesmus. Local health 
authorities are investigating a common source from a local diner, as 
10 other patrons have presented with the same symptoms. Which of 
the following organism is likely to produce this dysentery outbreak?
englishExplanation:
This patient is most likely infected with Shiga toxin– 
producing E. coli (ETEC) which often results from eating undercooked 
ground beef. Watery diarrhea that becomes bloody with significant 
abdominal pain is typical. The diarrhea may be grossly bloody and mimic 
inflammatory bowel disease or intestinal ischemia. Toxin assays are recommended. Endoscopic findings would be identical to those of any other 
severe colitis. Antibiotics are not effective and may increase the risk of 
hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) in children. Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is a risk in older children and adults. Norovirus 

References
1131.e2
typically causes watery non-bloody diarrhea without severe abdominal 
pain. S. aureus causes the classic food poisoning with abdominal cramping 
and vomiting 1 to 6 hours after ingestion the preformed toxin.
arabicExplanation: ليش: هذا المريض أكل لحم مفروم غير مطبوخ جيداً وبعدها جاءه حمى وألم بالبطن وإسهال دموي وtenesmus، وانفجار وبائي بين عشرة زبائن بمطعم واحد. المصدر يقول إن المريض على الأغلب مصاب بـ Shiga toxin–producing E. coli اللي غالباً تنتج عن أكل لحم مفروم غير مطبوخ، والإسهال المائي يتحول لدموي مع ألم بطني شديد. الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون Norovirus لأنهم يشوفون وباء مطعم، بس المصدر يقول إن Norovirus يسبب إسهال مائي غير دموي بدون ألم بطني شديد، والـ S. aureus يسبب قيء بعد 1-6 ساعات، وهذا لا يناسب الصورة الدموية.

question:
A patient presents with non-bloody diarrhea for 5 days, crampy 
abdominal pain, and bloating. The white blood cell (WBC) is 
16,000/mL. Which of the following types of patient and scenario is 
most likely to put the patient at high risk for Clostridium difficile?

options.text: Nurse who works in the emergency department
Traveler on vacation returning from Mexico

englishExplanation:
Elderly nursing home patients have the highest risk for 
acquiring C. difficile. These patients are in close quarters and have multiple daily contacts with staff members, making person to person transmission more likely. Antibiotics and antacids are frequently utilized 
in these patients, which are risk factors for C. difficile. The C. difficile 
spores are highly resistant to heat, acid, and antibiotics, making them 
highly contagious for person to person or surface to person infections. 
The WBC is generally greater than 15,000/mL.

1150.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation: ليش: السؤال عن أي مجموعة عندها أعلى خطر للإصابة بـ Clostridium difficile. المصدر يقول إن مرضى دور المسنين هم الأعلى خطر لأنهم في أماكن ضيقة وعندهم اتصال يومي متكرر مع الطاقم، فانتقال العدوى من شخص لشخص أسهل بكتير. كمان بيتستخدمون المضادات الحيوية ومضادات الحموضة بكثرة وهذي عوامل خطر للـ C. difficile. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون الممرضة أو المسافر، لكن الـ traveller مرتبط بإسهال المسافر، والـ C. difficile ترتبط بالمسنين والمضادات الحيوية، وأبواغها مقاومة للحرارة والحمض فبتكون معدية جداً.

question:
A 59-year-old man with a past history of diverticular disease presents with his second episode of left lower quadrant (LLQ) abdominal pain. He is afebrile, and laboratory examination is remarkable 
for a leukocytosis of 13,800/mm3. Physical examination reveals 
moderate LLQ tenderness without masses or rebound. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen reveals a small (4 cm) 
abscess adjacent to the sigmoid colon, with moderate diverticulitis. 
Which of the following would be the most appropriate treatment?

options.text: Discharge on oral antibiotics with 2-day follow-up

englishExplanation:
Abscesses smaller than 5 cm are typically treated with 
intravenous antibiotics followed by an outpatient oral regimen. Larger 
abscesses may be drained surgically or percutaneously.
arabicExplanation: ليش: هذا المريض عنده diverticulitis مع خراج صغير بحجم 4 cm جنب الـ sigmoid colon وارتفاع بالكريات البيض. المصدر يقول إن الخراجات الأصغر من 5 cm تتعالج عادةً بمضادات حيوية وريدية وبعدها نظام فموي خارج المستشفى. عشان هيك الأنسب هو الدخول للمستشفى وإعطاء المضادات الحيوية عن طريق الوريد. الفخ: كثير طلاب يختارون percutaneous drainage أو laparotomy لأنهم يشوفون خراج، بس هذي الطرق للخراجات الأكبر من 5 cm، والخراج هنا 4 cm فبيتعامل معه بالمضادات الحيوية الوريدية فقط.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding colonic ischemia is 
true?

options.text: CT scanning of the abdomen is diagnostic
It is rarely associated with bloody stool.
It is typically due to nonocclusive disease.
Isolated right-sided ischemic colitis is associated with comparatively lower mortality.
Specific serum biomarkers may be helpful.

correctAnswer: It is typically due to nonocclusive disease.
englishExplanation:
Colonic ischemia is typically due to nonocclusive microvascular disease. It occurs due to low-flow conditions related to congestive heart failure (CHF), renal failure, hypovolemia, or recent illness 
or surgery. Bloody stools are predictable. It may also occur in younger 
patients with collagen vascular disease, hematologic abnormalities, or 
cocaine abuse. Isolated right-sided ischemic colitis is associated with 
comparatively higher mortality. There are no sensitive or specific laboratory tests, and although sometimes suggestive, CT scanning primarily rules out alternative processes.

1162.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation: ليش: السؤال عن colonic ischemia وأي عبارة صحيحة عنه. المصدر يقول إن إقفار القولون عادةً سببه nonocclusive microvascular disease، ويصير بسبب حالات قلة التدفق مثل congestive heart failure أو renal failure أو hypovolemia أو مرض أو جراحة حديثة. كمان ممكن يصير عند مرضى أصغر سناً مع collagen vascular disease أو اضطرابات دموية أو تعاطي cocaine. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون أن الـ CT هو الفحص التشخيصي، بس المصدر يقول إنه بالدرجة الأولى يستبعد الحالات البديلة، وما في اختبارات دم حساسة أو نوعية، وإقفار القولون الأيمن المعزول مرتبط بوفيات أعلى مو أقل.

question: What is the most common cause of sudden-onset rectal pain?
englishExplanation:
Anal fissures typically result from superficial tears in the 
anoderm, usually occurring in the posterior midline. The pain is 
heightened by secondary spasm of the anal sphincter.
