ليش: المريض عنده ألم جانبي بالخصر ببداية مفاجئة خلال 45 دقيقة، ويرجع للأعلى بالمنطقة الخصية، مع بيلة دموية بالفحص المجهري بأكثر من 50 كرية حمر بالحقل، وهاد كلاسيكي لـ nephrolithiasis. الصورة الافتراضية هي CT scan بدون contrast، لأنها تعطي معلومات عن حجم الحصاة ومكانها ووجود hydronephrosis. وأهم شي إن إضافة الـ IV contrast بتحجب رؤية الحصاة وبتخلي الفحص قليل الفائدة تشخيصياً.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون KUB أو renal ultrasound، لكن الـ KUB يبيّن حوالي 60 بالمئة من الحصيات فقط ولا يعطي معلومات عن الـ hydronephrosis. الفرق إنه الـ CT بدون صبغة هو الأدق لحصيات المسالك.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 35-year-old man with a history of diabetes mellitus comes to the emergency department because he has had severe left-sided flank and abdominal pain for the past 10 hours. Temperature is 102.2°F (39.0°C), pulse rate is 105/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 104/60 mmHg. Physical examination shows left-sided costovertebral angle tenderness to palpation. Urinalysis is significant for hematuria, nitrites, and leukocyte esterase. Bedside ultrasonography shows moderate left-sided hydronephrosis. A CT scan confirms the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
englishExplanation:
Antibiotic therapy
Expl anation
A. Antibiotic therapy
This patient's presentation is concerning for an infected stone which is an indication
for admission and urology consultation. Many of these patients will require urologic
intervention such as stent placement or percutaneous nephrostomy tube placement.
Empiric therapy with a broad-spectrum antimicrobial regimen is indicated in patients with an infection and urinary tract obstruction, especially when sepsis criteria
are met. Options include intravenous imipenem 500 mg every six hours or intravenous meropenem 1 g every eight hours in addition to vancomycin (or daptomycin
and linezolid) for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus coverage.
Further information:
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21292654/
Germann CA. Chapter 85. Urologic Disorders. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
B. Cystoscopy with retrograde pyelography
This is a procedure done to unblock an obstructed ureter and for ureteral stent
placement which may be an option for this patient. However, initiation of antibi-
Otics and urology consultation need to occur first.
C. Foley catheter insertion
Foley catheter insertion may be indicated for monitoring urinary output, urinary retention, irrigating clots, and relieving bladder outlet obstruction. None of these indications are present in this patient, nor would they necessitate Foley placement prior
to initiating antibiotics.
D. Percutaneous nephrostomy
Consulting urology is indicated for this patient given he is presenting with an infected stone. While percutaneous nephrostomy may be appropriate, antibiotics
must be initiated first.

ليش: المريض عنده ألم شديد بالخاصرة والبطن مع حمى وت tenderness للزاوية الضلعية الفقرية، والتحليل البولي يبيّن دم ونيتريت واستيراز leukocyte، والسونار بالسرير يبيّن hydronephrosis متوسط. هالصورة هي حصاة مصابة infected stone مع انسداد، وهاد استطباب للتنويم واستشارة جراحة المسالك، لأن كثير من المرضى بيحتاجوا تدخل مثل دعامة أو percutaneous nephrostomy. وبما إنه في عدوى مع انسداد لازم يبدأ فوراً علاج مضادي حيوي واسع الطيف، خصوصاً إذا تحققت معايير الإنتان.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون percutaneous nephrostomy أو Foley كخطوة أولى، لكن المضاد الحيوي هو اللي لازم يبدأ بأسرع وقت. الفرق إنه عند عدوى مع انسداد نبدأ العلاج الدوائي فوراً ثم يقرر الجراح الشكل التداخلي.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 39-year-old woman presents with painful, frequent, urgent urination that is relieved with voiding for the past three days. These symptoms started after she returned from a trip for her wedding anniversary, and this is the first time she has had these symptoms this year. Medical history includes an allergy to sulfa drugs. The patient is afebrile. Physical examination shows suprapubic tenderness. No vaginal discharge or lesions are noted. Urinalysis is positive for leukocyte esterase, nitrites, blood, and protein. Which of the following is the most appropriate therapeutic agent?
englishExplanation:
Oral fosfomycin
Expl anation
A. Intramuscular/intravenous ceftriaxone
Uncomplicated cystitis does not require IV/IM medications. If the patient is febrile
and has irritative voiding symptoms, consider acute bacterial pyelonephritis, which
does require IV antibiotics at least initially. Ceftriaxone is an example of an appropriate antibiotic for acute pyelonephritis. The IV dose would be followed by a 7- to
14-day course of the appropriate oral antibiotic.
B. Oral amoxicillin-clavulanate
Amoxicillin-clavulanate is not first-line therapy for uncomplicated cystitis in nonpregnant patients. It is used in treating UTI in pregnant women. Given this patient's
sulfa allergy, nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin are excellent choices.
C. Oral ciprofloxacin
The FDA advised restricting fluoroquinolone use for uncomplicated infections due
to risk of collateral damage from the use of fluoroquinolones. In recurrent or complicated UTI (e.g. structural abnormality), use of fluoroquinolones may be
appropriate.
D. Oral fosfomycin
The vignette describes uncomplicated acute bacterial cystitis. First-line therapy is
trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS for 3 days (if local antibiotic resistance is
<20%), nitrofurantoin for 5-7 days, or fosfomycin, 3 g packet x 1. Given this
patient's sulfa allergy, nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin are excellent choices.
Further information:
Germann CA. Chapter 85. Urologic Disorders. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.

arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها حرقة وتبول متكرر وإلحاح من ثلاث أيام، وهاد uncomplicated acute bacterial cystitis بالمرأة غير الحامل. الخط الأول هو trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole لثلاثة أيام، أو nitrofurantoin من خمس لسبع أيام، أو fosfomycin جرعة واحدة ثلاث غرامات. وبما إنه عندها حساسية على أدوية الـ sulfa فيستبعد الـ TMP-SMX، فبيبقى الـ fosfomycin أو الـ nitrofurantoin خيارين ممتازين.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون oral ciprofloxacin، لكن الـ FDA أوصت بتقييد الـ fluoroquinolones بالعدوى غير المعقدة بسبب الضرر الجانبي. والـ amoxicillin-clavulanate مو خط أول بهالحالة. الفرق إنه الـ fosfomycin جرعة واحدة مناسبة مع تحسس السلفا.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 34-year-old man comes to the emergency department complaining of testicular pain and heaviness in the left hemiscrotum for the past five days. He tells you that the pain radiates up to his left flank. He has a history of cryptorchidism. Temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse rate is 80/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 128/87 mmHg. Oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On examination, he feels less pain with elevation of the scrotum. Which of the following is the most likely based on this patient's symptoms and physical exam findings?
englishExplanation:
Epididymitis
Expl anation
A. Epididymitis
This is the classic presentation of epididymitis. Epididymitis is the most common
cause of acute scrotal pain in adults. Patients present with testicular pain and
swelling. Common causative organisms include Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria
gonorrhea, and E. coli. A positive Prehn sign is relief of pain with elevation of the
scrotum, and indicates this disease state. In testicular torsion, there will be a negative Prehn sign and no relief of pain with scrotal elevation.
Reference:
Germann CA. Chapter 85. Urologic Disorders. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
B. Orchitis
Orchitis is inflammation of the testis secondary to infection, classically from
mumps, but also commonly due to chlamydia and gonorrhea. On examination, the
testicle will be large and tender with scrotal erythema and edema. Isolated orchitis
is uncommon, as it usually occurs with epididymitis.
C. Testicular appendage torsion
This generally presents with acute onset of testicular pain. VVhile patients with this
condition may have a normal examination, a small firm nodule may be palpable on
the superior aspect of the testes and a corresponding blue dot may be seen on the
scrotum. However, given the indolent presentation and location of tenderness, it is
more likely epididymitis.
D. Testicular neoplasm
Testicular cancer presents as a solid, firm, painless testicular mass. The mass will
not transilluminate. This can be diagnosed with scrotal ultrasound. Testicular cancer is the most common solid tumor in men ages 15-45 years.

arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده ألم وثقل بالشق الصفني الأيسر من خمس أيام، والألم بيشعّ للأعلى بالخاصرة اليسرى، وفحصه يبيّن ارتياحاً من الألم عند رفع الصفن وهذه علامة Prehn إيجابية. هالصورة هي epididymitis، وهو أشهر سبب لألم الصفن الحاد عند البالغين، والأعراض تشمل ألم وتورم بالخصية. والمسببات الشائعة Chlamydia trachomatis وNeisseria gonorrhoeae وE. coli. وعكس ذلك، بالـ testicular torsion تكون علامة Prehn سلبية وما في ارتياح عند رفع الصفن.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون testicular torsion أو neoplasm، لكن الألم بدأ قبل خمس أيام تدريجياً مع ارتياح بالرفع. الفرق إنه علامة Prehn الإيجابية توجه بشكل واضح للتشخيص epididymitis.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 34-year-old man presents complaining of testicular pain and heaviness in the left hemiscrotum for three days. He tells you that the pain radiates up to his left flank. The patient has a positive Prehn sign on physical examination. Which of the following is the most likely pathogen?
englishExplanation:
Chlamydia trachomatis
Expl anation
A. Chlamydia trachomatis
This patient is presenting with the classic presentation of epididymitis, the most
common cause of acute scrotal pain in adults. Patients present with testicular pain
and swelling. A positive Prehn sign is relief of pain with elevation of the scrotum,
and indicates this disease state. The most common causative organism in men under the age of 40 years is C. trachomatis, accounting for 50% of cases, followed by
N. gonorrhoeae. In patients older than 40, the most common organism is
Escherichia coli.
Reference:
https : / ,/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430814/
Germann CA. Chapter 85. Urologic Disorders. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
B. Escherichia coli
E. coli is the most common cause of acute epididymitis in children and men over the
age of 40 years. In older men, presence of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) increases the risk for epididymitis due to urinary obstruction. Treatment is with a
fluoroquinolone.
C. Klebsiella species
Klebsiella is another, but less common, cause of acute epididymitis in men over the
age of 40 years.
D. Neisseria gonorrhoeae
N. gonorrhoeae is the second most common cause of acute epididymitis in patients
under the age of 40 years. Treatment should involve coverage for both C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae with ceftriaxone plus doxycycline.

ليش: المريض عنده ألم وثقل بالشق الصفني الأيسر من ثلاثة أيام والألم بيشعّ للخاصرة اليسرى، وفحصه يبيّن علامة Prehn إيجابية وهاد نمط epididymitis. وتشخيصه epididymitis هو أشهر سبب لألم الصفن الحاد عند البالغين، والأعراض تظهر على شكل ألم وتورم بالخصية. أما المسبب الأكثر شيوعاً عند الرجال تحت سن الأربعين فهو Chlamydia trachomatis وبيشكّل حوالي 50 بالمئة من الحالات، ويتبعه Neisseria gonorrhoeae. وفي المرضى فوق الأربعين يصير المسبب الأكثر شيوعاً هو Escherichia coli.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون Neisseria gonorrhoeae لأنه مسبب منتشر، لكنه الثاني وليس الأول بهذه الفئة العمرية. والـ E. coli أشيع لدى من فوق أربعين. الفرق هو العمر: تحت الأربعين يغلب C. trachomatis.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 20-year-old male college football player presents with severe muscle pain in his thighs and lower back, weakness, and dark urine. Earlier in the afternoon, the patient and his teammate had an intense weightlifting workout that he states "almost made me pass out." He has no significant past medical history or allergies. He denied taking any performance-enhancing drugs or supplements. He has a urine cup with brown urine at the bedside. The point-of-care urine dipstick is positive for blood but negative otherwise. What is the most appropriate initial step in the management of this patient?

options.text: CBC, complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy, IV normal saline 2 liter bolus
CBC, complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy, creatinine kinase, sodium bicarbonate in 1L D5W
CBC, complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy, tamsulosin, IV normal saline 2L bolus
Complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy, creatinine kinase, IV normal saline 2 liter bolus

correctAnswer: Complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy, creatinine kinase, IV normal saline 2 liter bolus
englishExplanation:
Complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy, creatinine kinase, IV
normal saline 2 liter bolus
Expl anation
A. CBC, complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy, IV
normal saline 2 liter bolus
It is important to get a creatinine kinase level on this patient with a classic presentation for rhabdomyolysis.
B. CBC, complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy,
creatinine kinase, sodium bicarbonate in IL D5W
This patient likely has rhabdomyolysis. No studies have shown alkaline diuresis to
be more effective than saline diuresis, and as such bicarbonate is not indicated as an
initial treatment in the emergency department.
C. CBC, complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy,
tamsulosin, IV normal saline 2L bolus
This patient's history is most suggestive of rhabdomyolysis, not nephrolithiasis.
Tamsulosin may be considered in cases of renal stone.
D. Complete metabolic panel, urinalysis with microscopy, creatinine
kinase, IV normal saline 2 liter bolus
This patient's presentation is likely the result of rhabdomyolysis. The urine dipstick
interprets myoglobin and hemoglobin similarly, thus giving a positive result for
blood. A urinalysis with microscopy can better distinguish between the two.
Appropriate evaluation and diagnosis will require a creatinine kinase level, which is
typically five times the upper limit of normal in rhabdomyolysis. IV normal saline is
the most important and appropriate initial step in management.
Further information: http://www.emdocs.net/emdocs-cases-evidence-based-recommendations-for-rhabdomyolysis/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: اللاعب عنده ألم عضلي شديد بالفخذين وأسفل الظهر مع ضعف وبول بني غامق بعد تمرين رفع أثقال عنيف، والـ dipstick إيجابي للدم، وهاد كله rhabdomyolysis. الـ dipstick بيفسّر myoglobin وhaemoglobin بنفس الطريقة فبيعطي نتيجة إيجابية للدم، فالتحليل مع الفحص المجهري بيساعد نفرّق بينهن. والتقييم الصحيح لازم يتضمن creatinine kinase لأنه عادة بيكون خمس مرات فوق الحد الأعلى بالـ rhabdomyolysis، مع جرعة سائلة وريدية من normal saline حجمها لترين. وما بينلزم CBC للخطة الأولية، ولا بيكربونات لأن الدراسة ما أثبتت أفضلية الإدرار القلوي على الإدرار بالسلاين.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون خيار البيكربونات أو التامسولوسين، لكن التامسولوسين للحصيات مش للـ rhabdomyolysis. الفرق إنه العلاج الأولي هو الإرواء بالسلاين مع قياس الـ CK.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 65-year-old male with a history of Hodgkin’s lymphoma who recently started chemotherapy presents to the emergency department with flank pain and hematuria. Physical exam shows a male in moderate distress. Bedside ultrasound shows hydronephrosis. Which of the following is most likely to be the composition of this patient’s stones?
englishExplanation:
Uric acid
Explanation
A. Calcium oxalate
In tumor lysis syndrome, rapid cell turnover can lead to the release of large amounts
of uric acid, calcium, phosphates, potassium, and urea into the body. This can result
in an obstructive uropathy caused both by uric acid stones as well as calcium phosphate stones. Tumor lysis syndrome is best prevented through hydration, monitoring, and allopurinol or rasburicase.
B. Magnesium oxalate
In tumor lysis syndrome, rapid cell turnover can lead to the release of large amounts
of uric acid, calcium, phosphates, potassium, and urea into the body. This can result
in obstructive uropathy caused both by uric acid stones as well as calcium phosphate stones. The risk of magnesium oxalate is not increased due to TIS.
C. Struvite
In tumor lysis syndrome, rapid cell turnover can lead to the release of large amounts
of uric acid, calcium, phosphates, potassium, and urea into the body. This can result
in an obstructive uropathy caused both by uric acid stones as well as calcium phosphate stones. Struvite stones are classically associated with bacterial infection.
D. Uric acid
In tumor lysis syndrome, rapid cell turnover can lead to the release of large amounts
of uric acid, calcium, phosphates, potassium, and urea into the body. This can result
in obstructive uropathy caused both by uric acid stones as well as calcium phosphate stones.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK459218/

question: A 42-year-old male presents to the emergency department with an itchy penile rash as shown in the image. He reports it is the second time he has had this infection this year. In addition to the appropriate management of his infection, which of the following laboratory tests will likely reveal the underlying cause for his condition?
englishExplanation:
Blood glucose
Expl anation
A. Blood glucose
The patient image demonstrates balanitis which is a common initial presenting
symptom in males with undiagnosed diabetes. Although appropriate treatment with
topical antifungals should be administered, given that the patient has had recurrent
infections and the etiology is likely Candidiasis, he should be tested for diabetes.
Candidal balanitis is defined as inflammation of the glans penis, often also involving
the prepuce (balanoposthitis), in the presence of Candida species and in the absence of other infectious etiology. Candidal balanitis is generally sexually acquired
and is often associated with the presence of diabetes mellitus. The appearance of
balanitis or phimosis in an otherwise healthy man can be the first presentation of
diabetes mellitus. Balanitis is more common in males who are uncircumcised. The
symptoms may include redness, swelling, pain, itching, and a discharge. Treatment
involves practicing good hygiene and using topical creams or ointments. In severe
cases, circumcision may be recommended.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537143/
B. RPR
This patient is presenting with recurrent balanitis, most likely due to undiagnosed
diabetes. RPR would be positive in cases of syphilis. Patients with primary syphilis
present with painless genital lesions, also called a chancre. Treatment is with
penicillin.
C. VDRL
This patient is presenting with recurrent balanitis, most likely due to undiagnosed
diabetes. VDRL would be positive in cases of syphilis.
D. Viral culture
Viral culture suggests a diagnosis of herpes which are vesicular. This patient's histow and exam is more consistent with balanitis.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 62-year-old male presents to the emergency department with bilateral flank pain radiating to his abdomen as well as difficulty urinating. An abdominal ultrasound is performed, which reveals a normal aorta but bilateral moderate hydronephrosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Prostate enlargement
Expl anation
A. Bilateral obstructing renal calculi
In an older male patient with bilateral hydronephrosis, an enlarged prostate or prostatic mass must be considered. In a female patient with bilateral hydronephrosis,
an obstructing pelvic mass should be on the differential.
B. Prostate enlargement
In an older male patient with bilateral hydronephrosis, an enlarged prostate or prostatic mass is the most common and likely In a female patient with bilateral hydronephrosis, an obstructing pelvic mass should be on the differential. Other
common causes to consider include medications that cause urinary retention.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK538499/
Germann CA. Chapter 85. Urologic Disorders. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
C. Renal artery stenosis
Renal artery stenosis does not cause bilateral hydronephrosis.
D. Urethral stricture
While urethral strictures may cause bilateral hydronephrosis, benign prostate hyperplasia (BPH) is the most common cause.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: عند رجل كبير بالعمر مع bilateral hydronephrosis لازم نفكر أول شي بتضخم البروستات أو كتلة بروستاتية لأنها السبب الأكثر شيوعاً واحتمالاً لانسداد المجاري البولية عنده. لو كانت المريضة أنثى بنفس الصورة كان التفكير يتجه لكتلة حوضية تسدّ الحالبين. ومن الأسباب الشائعة الثانية اللي لازم ننتبه لها الأدوية اللي تسبب urinary retention.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختاروا bilateral obstructing renal calculi لأنها تسدّ الجهتين وتعمل hydronephrosis، بس وجود difficulty urinating عند رجل كبير يرجّح تضخم البروستات مو الحصيات.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 55-year-old female with a history of multiple presentations for pyelonephritis presents to the emergency department with left-sided flank pain and dysuria. Temperature is 39ºC(102.2ºF), pulse rate is 110/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 124/80 mmHg. Urinalysis is significant for hematuria but is negative for leukocyte esterase or nitrites. CT scan shows a left-sided staghorn calculus. Which of the following is the most likely composition of this patient’s stone?
englishExplanation:
Struvite (magnesium ammonium phosphate)
Expl anation
A. Calcium oxalate
Most patients with nephrolithiasis form calcium stones (80%), composed primarily
of calcium oxalate or calcium phosphate. This patient's multiple episodes of
pyelonephritis and large staghorn calculus make a struvite stone more likely.
B. Calcium phosphate
Most patients with nephrolithiasis form calcium stones (80%), composed primarily
of calcium oxalate or calcium phosphate. This patient's multiple episodes of
pyelonephritis and large staghorn calculus make a struvite stone more likely.
C. Struvite (magnesium ammonium phosphate)
Patients with recurrent pyelonephritis are particularly at risk for struvite renal calculi, which are formed as a result of urinary tract infection by urease-forming
organisms. They grow rapidly and can occupy the entire collecting system. Ureaseproducing organisms include Proteus, Klebsiella, Staphylococcus, Pseudomonas,
Providentia, Serratia, and Morganella. The optimal treatment for struvite stones is
the complete surgical removal of all stone material.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK568783/
Germann CA. Chapter 85. Urologic Disorders. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
D. Uric acid
Uric acid stones are typically associated with dehydration, gout, leukemia, and tumor lysis syndrome. This patient's multiple episodes of pyelonephritis and large
staghorn calculus make a struvite stone more likely.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها نوبات متكررة من pyelonephritis وهذا يخليها معرّضة بشكل خاص لـ struvite renal calculi اللي تتكوّن بسبب عدوى urinary tract بميكروبات تنتج urease مثل Proteus وKlebsiella وPseudomonas. هالحصيات تكبر بسرعة كبيرة وممكن تشغل كل الـ collecting system، ولهيك تتشكل staghorn calculus. والعلاج الأمثل لها هو الإزالة الجراحية الكاملة لكل مادة الحصاة.
الفخ: أكثر خيار بيوقعون فيه هو calcium oxalate لأنه أشيع حصية بالمجتمع بشكل عام بنسبة 80%، بس تكرار pyelonephritis مع staghorn يرجّح struvite.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: Which of the following is the most effective means for preventing contrast-induced nephropathy in patients with chronic kidney disease?
englishExplanation:
Isotonic volume expansion
Expl anation
A. ACE inhibitor
While ACE inhibitors are generally beneficial in the prevention of long-term renal
disease, there is no evidence to suggest that they help prevent acute contrast-induced nephropathy.
B. Beta-blocker
While beta-blockers are generally beneficial in the prevention of long-term renal
disease, there is no evidence to suggest that they help prevent acute contrast-induced nephropathy.
C. Hypertonic volume expansion
Hypertonic saline is not currently recommended for CIN prophylaxis. Isotonic solutions such as normal saline and lactated ringers are preferred.
D. Isotonic volume expansion
The most widely accepted treatment to help prevent contrast-induced nephropathy
(CIN) is peri-procedure volume expansion with 0.9% normal saline infusion at a
rate of 1 ml/kg/hr for 6 to 12 hours before the procedure and continuing after the
procedure. Evidence also suggests that hydration with sodium bicarbonate is more
protective than normal saline alone. Weaker evidence suggests N-acetylcysteine
(NAC) will also decrease CIN.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK448066/
Wolfson AB. Chapter 83. Renal Failure. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS, Gausche-
Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice. 10th ed.
Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: العلاج الأكثر قبولاً لمنع contrast-induced nephropathy هو توسيع الحجم حول الإجراء بمحلول 0.9% normal saline بمعدل 1 ml/kg/hr لمدة 6 إلى 12 ساعة قبل الإجراء والاستمرار بعده. يعني لازم نستخدم محلول isotonic وليس hypertonic، لأن hypertonic saline غير موصى فيه حالياً. وفي دليل إن hydration مع sodium bicarbonate أكثر حماية من normal saline لوحده، ودليل أضعف إن N-acetylcysteine يقلل CIN.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختاروا hypertonic volume expansion لأنهم يظنوا تركيز أعلى يعني حماية أقوى، بس الصحيح إننا نستخدم isotonic solutions.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 32-year-old woman with a history of intravenous drug use is undergoing in-patient treatment with intravenous antibiotics for infective endocarditis. Eight days after starting nafcillin and gentamicin, her serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen became elevated. Microscopic analysis of urinary sediment shows muddy brown casts. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these laboratory findings?
englishExplanation:
Acute tubular necrosis
Expl anation
A. Acute tubular necrosis
This patient has acute tubular necrosis, for which muddy brown granular casts are
pathognomonic. Creatinine and blood urea nitrogen will be elevated due to kidney
injury. Aminoglycoside antibiotics, such as gentamicin, have nephrotoxic side effects and are one cause of acute tubular necrosis. Direct toxicity (from medications)
or ischemic injury are the most common causes of acute tubular necrosis.
Reference: https://wwrw.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK507815/
Wolfson AB. Chapter 83. Renal Failure. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS, Gausche-
Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice. 10th ed.
Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
B. Chronic kidney injury
Broad waxy casts can be seen in chronic kidney injury. These casts are larger than
other types because they form in dilated, diseased tubules in an environment of renal stasis. Muddy brown granular casts are pathognomonic for acute tubular
necrosis.
C. Glomerulonephritis
Red blood cell casts are seen in urine in the setting of glomerulonephritis but can
also occur after strenuous exercise. Muddy brown granular casts are pathognomonic for acute tubular necrosis.
D. Nephrotic syndrome
Fatty casts indicate nephrotic syndrome with a high amount of urinary protein.
Under a polarizing microscope, a "Maltese cross" pattern can be seen. Muddy brown
granular casts are pathognomonic for acute tubular necrosis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها acute tubular necrosis، والـ muddy brown granular casts في الـ urinary sediment هي الـ pathognomonic لها. الـ creatinine والـ blood urea nitrogen مرتفعين بسبب إصابة الكلى، والـ aminoglycoside antibiotics مثل gentamicin عندها آثار nephrotoxic وهي سبب معروف للـ acute tubular necrosis. وأشيع أسباب الـ acute tubular necrosis هي السمية المباشرة من الأدوية أو الإصابة الإسكيمية.
الفخ: في ناس تختار glomerulonephritis لأنها تصيب الكلى وتعمل ارتفاع creatinine، بس الـ muddy brown casts خاصة بالـ ATN مو بالـ glomerulonephritis.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 16-year-old boy presents because he feels something strange in his right testicle that he describes as lumpy. He has no testicular pain, abdominal pain, or difficulty urinating. Physical examination shows palpable distended veins on the lateral aspect of the right testicle that are accentuated with Valsalva maneuver while standing and diminished when supine. No palpable testicular masses or pain on palpation is noted. Which of the following complications is most likely if this patient's condition is not surgically corrected?
englishExplanation:
Decreased fertility
Expl anation
A. Decreased bone mass
While osteopenia is possible if a severe varicocele causes decreased Leydig cell function and low testosterone, this is not a common effect,
B. Decreased fertility
An unrepaired varicocele can impair sperm structure, function, and production and
cause impaired fertility. It is thought that — 40% of infertile men have varicoceles.
References:
https:/,/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK448113/
Germann CA. Chapter 85. Urologic Disorders. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
C. Testicular cancer
Varicocele is not a risk factor for testicular cancer; however, cryptorchidism, or an
undescended testicle, is.
D. Urinary retention
Structural changes associated with varicoceles in the testicles do not cause abnormalities in urinary function.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هذا المريض عنده varicocele غير معالج، والـ varicocele اللي ما يتصلح ممكن يضرّ بتركيب ووظيفة وإنتاج الحيوانات المنوية ويسبب impaired fertility. والدراسات تشير إن حوالي 40% من الرجال العقيمين عندهم varicoceles. يعني إن أهم مضاعفة محتملة إذا ما تصحح جراحياً هي decreased fertility.
الفخ: في طلاب يختاروا testicular cancer لأنهم يخلطوا بينها وبين cryptorchidism، بس الـ varicocele ليس عامل خطر لسرطان الخصية إطلاقاً.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: Which of the following is not a typical complication of a peripheral arteriovenous fistula?
englishExplanation:
Venous hypotension
Expl anation
A. Dialysis-associated steal syndrome
Steal syndrome is due to a high-flow fistula causing distal ischemia. These patients
may present with severe pain, swelling, or signs of ischemia distal to the fistula. A
normal compensatory mechanism to the fistula is to increase overall flow to the affected extremity, which will provide adequate blood flow to the higher resistance
distal capillary beds. When this mechanism fails, steal syndrome results which
draws blood through the lower resistance fistula instead of supplying distal tissue.
In the evaluation for steal syndrome, the pathognomonic finding is a diminished or
absent distal radial pulse, palpable only with compression of the dialysis access site.
B. Infection
Infection is a common complication of AV fistulas. Patients are at risk for infection
at the site, and also at higher risk for bacteremia due to frequent dialysis.
C. Pseudoaneurysm formation
Pseudoaneurysm formation is a known complication of AV fistula formation.
D. Venous hypotension
Complications of AV fistula include thrombosis, Infection, steal syndromr, formation of true pseudoaneurysms, high-output heart failure, and venous hypertension.
Venous hypertension is thought to be due to central vein stenosis. It occurs most
commonly with forearm fistulas and is manifested by swelling of the hand. In extreme cases, it can lead to gangrene. Treatment is surgical.
Venous hypotension is not a common complication of an AV fistula.
Further information:
Wolfson AB. Chapter 83. Renal Failure. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS, Gausche-
Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice. 10th ed.
Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.

arabicExplanation:
ليش: مضاعفات الـ AV fistula تشمل thrombosis وinfection وsteal syndrome وتكوّن pseudoaneurysms وhigh-output heart failure وvenous hypertension. الـ venous hypertension سببها central vein stenosis وتحصل أكثر مع forearm fistulas وتظهر كانتفاخ باليد وممكن توصل للغرغرينا بأقصى الحالات. أما venous hypotension فهي ليست من المضاعفات النموذجية أبداً.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يخلطوا بين venous hypertension وvenous hypotension ويختاروا hypertension كجواب، بس السؤال يبحث عن الشي اللي مو من المضاعفات.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 16-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his father because of erect, rigid, and painful penis for the past two hours. Medical history is significant for sickle cell disease. He denies any trauma. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Exchange blood transfusion should be initiated immediately

englishExplanation:
Intracavernous injection of phenylephrine
Expl anation
A. Administration of sildenafil
This option is incorrect as it is a cause of priapism. While there is some data to suggest that low dose sildenafil may be effective for chronic preventive treatment, it is
not indicated in the acute management of this patient.
B. Arterial embolization
Arterial embolization or surgical ligation is indicated for recalcitrant cases of highflow (non-ischemic) priapism. This patient's presumptive etiology of priapism is
sickle cell disease which is typically a low-flow, ischemic process.
C. Exchange blood transfusion should be initiated immediately
An exchange blood transfusion may be considered in sickle cell patients presenting
with priapism if the priapism is refractory to aspiration, irrigation, and phenylephrine instillation. However, exchange transfusion therapy in sickle cell patients
has been associated with acute neurologic events such as headache, seizure, or mental status changes (ASPEN syndrome: Association of Sickle cell disease, Priapism,
Exchange transfusion, Neurologic events).
D. Intracavernous injection of phenylephrine
Priapism in sickle cell is due to ischemic (low-flow) vasooclusive events. In low-flow
priapism, the penis is fully erect, rigid, and painful. Treatment options of low-flow
priapism include aspiration of the corpus cavernosum with saline irrigation and intracavernous phenylephrine.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK459178/
http://www.emdocs.net/priapism-in-children/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ priapism عند مريض sickle cell سببه أحداث vasoocclusive إسكيمية من نوع low-flow، وفيها القضيب يكون منتصب بشكل كامل وصلب ومؤلم. العلاج للـ low-flow يشمل aspiration من الـ corpus cavernosum مع irrigation بمحلول ملحي وحقن intracavernous من phenylephrine، ولهيك هي الخطوة التالية المناسبة.
الفخ: في طلاب يختاروا administration of sildenafil لأنه يخص الانتصاب، بس الـ sildenafil هو سبب للـ priapism وليس علاجه بالحالة الحادة.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A previously healthy 33-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of worsening left-sided scrotal pain for the past five days. He denies any trauma or fever. However, he does notice mild irritation with urination. Physical examination shows an erythematous and swollen left scrotal sac, as well as diffuse tenderness to palpation of the left scrotal contents. Ultrasound study shows increased flow to the left epididymis. Which of the following best characterizes this patient’s condition?

options.text: Ceftriaxone and doxycycline should both be given as treatment
Ciprofloxacin is the drug of choice

correctAnswer: Ceftriaxone and doxycycline should both be given as treatment
englishExplanation:
Ceftriaxone and doxycycline should both be given as treatment
Expl anation
A. Associated with negative Prehn's sign
A negative Prehn's sign indicates no pain relief with lifting the affected testicle,
which points towards testicular torsion as a cause of testicular pain. Positive Prehn's
sign indicates there is pain relief with lifting the affected testicle, which points towards epididymitis. This clinical finding is inferior to a Doppler ultrasound.
B. Ceftriaxone and doxycycline should both be given as treatment
Testicular pain, swelling, and asymmetric hyperemia of epididymis on ultrasound
are suggestive of epididymitis. Epididymitis is a clinical diagnosis combined with ultrasound examination and urinalysis. The choice of antibiotics follows an arbitrary
division at age 35. Younger than 35 years of age, patients are treated with ceftriaxone and doxycycline for presumed Chlamydia and Gonorrhea infection. After 35
years of age, patients are treated with a fluoroquinolone for presumed E. coli infection. Analgesics and scrotal elevations should be recommended.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430814/
Germann CA. Chapter 85. Urologic Disorders. In: Walls RM, Hockberger RS,
Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and Clinical Practice.
10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
C. Ciprofloxacin is the drug of choice
In young adults, sexually transmitted infections are the most common cause of epididymitis and orchitis. Empiric antibiotics covering Chlamydia trachomatis and
Neisseria gonorrhea should be administered. Ciprofloxacin is no longer considered
the first-line for gonorrhea, given its increasing resistance rates.
D. Emergent urology consultation is indicated
Epididymo-orchitis is not emergent unless severe infection, abscess formation, or
associated with Fournier's gangrene.

arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ testicular pain والتورم و asymmetric hyperemia للـ epididymis على الـ ultrasound تشير للـ epididymitis. وتقسيم المضادات الحيوية يعتمد على عمر 35، فالأصغر من 35 سنة يُعالج بـ ceftriaxone وdoxycycline لاحتمال Chlamydia وGonorrhea، والأكبر من 35 يُعالج بـ fluoroquinolone لاحتمال E. coli. ويُنصح أيضاً بالـ analgesics ورفع الـ scrotum، والمريض عمره 33 سنة.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختاروا ciprofloxacin لأنه دوا شائع للـ epididymitis، بس عند المرضى تحت 35 سنة الـ fluoroquinolone مو الخيار الأول.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: Testicular torsion is a urologic emergency that requires immediate care by a surgeon. Which of the following age groups are most commonly associated with this diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Expl anation
A. Infants
Young males through late teens
Extravaginal testicular torsion occurs in neonates and occurs when the tunica vaginalis has not adhered to the gubernaculum, so the tunica vaginalis and spermatic
cord twist together. This is not as common as intravaginal torsion in teenage boys.
B. Males age 20 to mid thirties
This is the most common age for incidence of primmy testicular tumors (testicular
cancer). Testicular torsion has a bimodal age of distribution: at birth and 12-18
years of age. The majority of cases occur in teenage boys.
C. Middle-aged males
Erectile dysfunction can be a part of the aging process as well as a sequela of multiple disease processes. Testicular torsion is most common in young males, but rarely
can be seen in older individuals.
D. Young males through late teens
Testicular torsion has a bimodal age of distribution: at birth and 12-18 years of age.
The majority of cases occur in teenage boys. 14% of cases occur in adults; older patients have worse outcomes.
There are two forms of torsion: intravaginal and extravaginal. Intravaginal torsion
occurs in adolescents and young adults and is due to an abnormal attachment of the
tunica vaginalis. Extravaginal torsion occurs in neonates and occurs when the tunica vaginalis has not adhered to the gubernaculum, so the tunica vaginalis and
spermatic cord twist together.
