Prostatitis (C) can also cause dysuria and urethral discharge but is often accompanied by pelvic pain and fever.

Pyelonephritis (D) is uncommon in young men. However, it is characterized by dysuria, fever, and flank pain.

One Step Further
Question:
What antibiotics are recommended in the treatment of pelvic inflammatory disease?

Reveal Answer:
Ceftriaxone, doxycycline, and metronidazole.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Urethritis

Inflammation of the urethra
Most frequently caused by an infectious etiology
Common causative organisms: Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Mycoplasma genitalium
Noninfectious causes (e.g., irritation from chemicals, trauma) may occur
Sx: dysuria, discharge, pruritus, dyspareunia
Some patients may be asymptomatic
Dx: Hx, PE, laboratory testing as needed (e.g., microbiologic studies)
Tx options (depending on the underlying etiology): antibiotics, irritant avoidance (for noninfectious causes)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض شب عنده dysuria حادة بعد نهاية أسبوع شرب وتُعدد شركاء جنسي، وعند الفحص في إفراز أصفر من الـ urethral meatus، وهذي الصورة الكلاسيكية للـ urethritis. الـ urethritis يتميز بإفراز إحليلي وحكة أو وخز بالعضو والتبول المؤلم والإلحاح والبيلة الدموية، والفحص ممكن يبيّن قرحات بالعضو وتضخم بالغدد الإربية. المسبب هو انتقال عدوى جنسية، وغالباً Neisseria gonorrhoeae أو Chlamydia trachomatis، والمشتبه به الأساسي هو gonococcal urethritis.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار cystitis، لأن كلمة dysuria تخلي الطالب يفكر بالتهاب المثانة مباشرة. بس الـ cystitis تُرجَّح أكثر لما يكون في إلحاح وتبول متكرر، ووجود إفراز إحليلي واضح بالفحص يرجّح urethritis. كذلك balanitis ما ترافقها إفرازات إحليلية.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 16-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with painful urination and urethral discharge. He is sexually active. On exam, he has a urethral discharge when gentle pressure is applied proximally to the penile meatus. His testicular exam is normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his illness?
englishExplanation:
Painful urination usually indicates inflammation or injury to the external genitalia or distal genitourinary tract. Penile or vaginal discharge is suggestive of urethritis in men and vulvovaginitis in women. The most common cause of urethritis in adolescent boys is a sexually transmitted infection. Neisseria gonorrhoeae or Chlamydia trachomatis are the usual culprits. Additional sexually transmitted pathogens known to cause urethritis include Trichomonas and Mycobacterium genitalium.

The diagnosis is made clinically and supported by using nucleic acid amplification tests for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis on first-catch urine. These results generally take several hours to a day to complete, so presumptive treatment for both Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis is appropriate in sexually active postpubertal male patients with urethritis. Doxycycline and ceftriaxone is the preferred regimen. Reinfection is common unless the partner is also notified and treated. Urethritis can also be caused by chemical irritation (e.g., bubble baths), medications (e.g., ceftriaxone, ticarcillin, penicillin), local injury, hypercalciuria, labial adhesions, or urethral strictures. A thorough history and exam are especially needed for prepubertal children with urethritis to evaluate for the possibility of sexual abuse.



Epstein-Barr virus (A) is an uncommon cause of urethritis.

Escherichia coli (B) can cause epididymitis in adolescent boys who practice insertive anal intercourse but is an uncommon etiology for urethritis.

Herpes simplex virus (C) may cause urethritis but typically presents with penile vesicles or ulcers.

One Step Further
Question:
What are the causes of orchitis in boys who are not sexually active?

Reveal Answer:
Bacterial brucellosis and many viruses (mumps, rubella, coxsackie, parvovirus, echovirus).

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Gonococcal Urethritis

Caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae
Gram-negative diplococci
Sx: purulent urethral discharge, dysuria
Dx: NAAT preferred (urine or urethral swab)
Sensitivity and specificity of NAAT is superior to culture
Tx: ceftriaxone IM (500 mg for individuals < 150 kg or 1 g for individuals ≥ 150 kg)
Add doxycycline 100 mg twice a day for 7 days if C. trachomatis not ruled out
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض مراهق نشيط جنسياً عنده تبول مؤلم وإفراز إحليلي عند الضغط القريب من الـ meatus مع فحص خصية طبيعي، وهذا يشير بقوة للـ urethritis. أكثر سبب للـ urethritis عند المراهقين هو عدوى منقولة جنسياً، والمسببان المعتادان هما Neisseria gonorrhoeae و Chlamydia trachomatis. التشخيص يُبنى سريرياً ويُدعم بفحص nucleic acid amplification للاثنين على أول بول، وبما إن النتيجة تتأخر ساعات، فالمعالجة التجريبية للاثنين ب ceftriaxone و doxycycline مناسبة.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون herpes simplex virus لأنهم يربطون أي عرض تناسلي بالـ HSV. بس الـ HSV عادة يعمل قرحات وحويصلات مؤلمة، مش إفراز إحليلي قيحي بدون قرحات، وفحص المنطقة يرجّح وجود إفرازات بدون تقرحات. المسبب الأشهر هنا gonorrhoeae.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 73-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia presents with a failure to void for 3 days and lower abdominal pain. Physical examination reveals lower abdominal distension and moderate tenderness to palpation. His blood urea nitrogen to creatinine is 20:1.6. What management is indicated?
englishExplanation:
The patient presents with symptoms and signs consistent with acute urinary obstruction requiring the placement of a Foley catheter to relieve the obstruction. Postrenal or obstructive kidney failure is a reversible cause of acute kidney injury (AKI) and should always be considered in patients with new azotemia. Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a common cause of urinary obstruction. Treatment of obstructive uropathy focuses on relieving the obstruction. There is no contraindication to placing a Foley catheter in patients with BPH, and it should be done emergently to relieve the obstruction.



Emergency dialysis (A) should only be undertaken for pulmonary edema, severe uncontrollable hypertension, hyperkalemia, severe electrolyte or acid-base disturbance, specific overdoses, and severe symptomatic uremia. Intravenous fluids (C) to restore circulating volume are unnecessary in obstructive kidney failure. Suprapubic catheterization (D) should be attempted if the placement of a Foley catheter fails.

One Step Further
Question:
What other lab findings aside from blood urea nitrogen to creatinine ratio are consistent with prerenal acute kidney injury?

Reveal Answer:
A urine sodium < 20 mEq/L and a fractional excretion of sodium (FENa) < 1%.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Urinary Retention

Etiologies
Obstructive
Male: BPH
Female: prolapse, tumor
Neurogenic (diabetes)
Drug-induced (alpha-agonists)
Diagnostic tests: bladder ultrasound, catheterization, urinalysis, urine culture, serum creatinine
Management: observe (low-risk), catheterization, alpha-1 antagonists such as tamsulosin, antibiotics, surgery
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده benign prostatic hyperplasia مع احتباس بول 3 أيام، وبالفحص في انتفاخ وتخشخشة أسفل البطن، والنسب بترتفع بشكل يوحي بفشل كلوي بعد كلوي أو انسدادي. العلاج هنا هو إدخال Foley catheter لإزالة الانسداد، وهذا يجيب فائدة فورية للكلية الحاجزية. ما في أي مانع من إدخال Foley عند مريض BPH، والإجراء لازم يتم بشكل إسعافي، والـ suprapubic catheterization يُلجأ لها فقط إذا فشل وضع الـ Foley.
الفخ: كثير طلاب يختارون suprapubic catheterization لأنهم يخافون من الـ BPH. لكن الـ suprapubic هي الخطوة البديلة فقط عند فشل إدخال Foley، بينما الـ Foley هو الخيار الأول ولا يوجد مانع منه. مو ضروري أيضاً إعطاء سوائل وريدية هنا، لأن المشكلة انسدادية.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: An 18-year-old sexually active man presents with testicular pain for 3 days. The pain is constant and accompanied by fever. Examination reveals a mildly tender right testicle with a normal lie and no urethral discharge. Urinalysis shows 2+ leukocyte esterase, negative nitrites, and 10–25 WBC/hpf. What treatment is indicated?

options.text: Ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscular once and doxycycline 100 mg twice a day for 10 days
Ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscular once and levofloxacin 500 mg once daily for 10 days
Ciprofloxacin 250 mg twice a day for 3 days
Levofloxacin 500 mg once daily for 10 days

correctAnswer: Ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscular once and doxycycline 100 mg twice a day for 10 days
englishExplanation:
This patient has signs and symptoms consistent with epididymitis, which results from infection of the vas deferens, causing edema from passive congestion and inflammation. It usually presents with a gradual onset of scrotal pain, unlike torsion, which presents with a more abrupt onset of symptoms. Approximately 10–30% of patients present with urinary symptoms, and more than half of patients report fever. Early in the course, patients present with pain and tenderness localized to the epididymis, but symptoms quickly spread to the adjacent testicle. Classically, the Prehn sign (decrease in pain with elevation of the scrotum) is taught to indicate epididymitis, but this sign has a low sensitivity.

Urinalysis typically demonstrates signs of infection. Pyuria is common. If testicular torsion is suspected, scrotal ultrasound should be pursued. Antibiotic therapy should be tailored based on patient characteristics. In sexually active adults and adolescents, Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections are the most common cause of epididymitis, particularly in younger patients (< 35 years). Therefore, treatment includes ceftriaxone and doxycycline. Older patients are more likely to have urinary tract abnormalities, predisposing them to epididymitis from typical urinary tract pathogens (e.g., Escherichia coli). However, if they are sexually active, coverage of C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae is also indicated.



Ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscular (A) is insufficient treatment for both N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis.

Ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscular once and levofloxacin 500 mg once daily for 10 days (C) is an appropriate treatment regimen for a patient with acute epididymitis with a history of insertive anal intercourse or a patient with risk factors for both sexually transmitted infections and urinary pathogens, like having obstructive uropathy or a recent urologic procedure.

Ciprofloxacin 250 mg twice a day for 3 days (D) is a treatment option for patients with an uncomplicated urinary tract infection, though it should not be used as first-line treatment when other options are available, as it has a boxed warning (tendinitis or tendon rupture, CNS side effects, peripheral neuropathy).

Levofloxacin 500 mg once daily for 10 days (E) is an appropriate treatment for epididymitis in a patient who is not sexually active when only typical urinary pathogens are suspected.

One Step Further
Question:
What antibiotics are first-line treatment for acute prostatitis in the outpatient setting?

Reveal Answer:
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or a fluoroquinolone.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Epididymitis

Most common cause
Prepubertal: UTI, virus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae
Postpubertal: C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae
Sexually transmitted: C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae
Nonsexually transmitted: E. coli, Pseudomonas
Sx: gradual-onset unilateral scrotal pain
PE: scrotal erythema, relief with testicular elevation (Prehn sign), normal cremasteric reflex
Dx: clinical, U/S will show increased color flow on Doppler
Tx
Prepubertal: treat UTI (if present), supportive care
Postpubertal: ceftriaxone + doxycycline
Sexually transmitted: ceftriaxone + doxycycline
Nonsexually transmitted: fluoroquinolone
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض شب نشيط جنسياً عنده ألم خصي مستمر 3 أيام مع حمى وtenderness خفيفة وخصية بوضع طبيعي، وتحليل البول يبيّن leukocyte esterase موجب مع pyuria، وهذا يوافق epididymitis. عند البالغين والمراهقين النشيطين جنسياً، أكثر مسببين هما Chlamydia trachomatis و Neisseria gonorrhoeae، لذلك العلاج لازم يغطي الاثنين معاً. فالخيار الصحيح هو ceftriaxone بجرعة 500 ملغ عضلياً مرة واحدة مع doxycycline 100 ملغ مرتين يومياً لمدة 10 أيام.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار ceftriaxone لحاله، لأن الطالب يتذكر معالجة gonorrhea وينسى إنه لازم يغطي Chlamydia كمان. الـ ceftriaxone وحده ما يغطي chlamydia، والعلاج الناقص يؤدي لبقاء العدوى ومضاعفات. الحل تغطية الاثنين معاً دائماً.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: Which of the following is the most common presentation of testicular cancer?

options.text: Lower abdominal, perianal, and scrotal discomfort
Painless enlargement superior to the testicle that feels like a “bag of worms”
Swelling and tenderness of the entire testicle

englishExplanation:
Although testicular cancer is the most common solid malignancy in young male patients ages 15–35 years, it accounts for just 1% of all cancers in men. These tumors are more common in those with undescended testicles and infertile patients. The most common presentation is that of a palpable, nontender solid nodule or mass that cannot be separated from the testicle. A mass that is palpable is more likely to be malignant than one found only via imaging. Acute onset of scrotal pain is unlikely in testicular cancers and should prompt an evaluation for other causes, such as testicular torsion or epididymitis. Patients may also present with symptoms related to metastasis including regional lymphadenopathy (found in 15% of patients at the time of diagnosis) or bone pain. All patients with a scrotal mass should undergo ultrasound imaging for further evaluation and prompt referral to a urologist.



Approximately 30–40% of patients present with lower abdominal, perianal, or scrotal discomfort (A). However, the most common presentation is the finding of a focal nontender testicular mass.

Varicoceles present as painless enlargement superior to the testicle (B). Palpation of a varicocele is often described as feeling similar to a “bag of worms.”

Swelling and tenderness of the entire testicle (D) is concerning for orchitis. The most frequent bacterial causes of orchitis in adults include N. gonorrhoeae, C. trachomatis, E. coli, and Klebsiella.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common type of testicular malignancy?

Reveal Answer:
Germ cell tumor, accounting for 95% of all testicular tumors.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Testicular Cancer

Risk factors include cryptorchidism, age 15–35 years
Sx: testicular lump
PE: painless, hard, fixed mass
Lab results: beta-hCG, AFP, or LDH may be elevated based on tumor type
Diagnosis starts with ultrasound
Tx (varying based on factors such as type and stage): radical inguinal orchiectomy, radiation therapy or platinum-based chemotherapy in certain situations
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أكثر شكل سريري لسرطان الخصية هو وجود nodule أو mass صلبة غير مؤلمة لا تنفصل عن الخصية نفسها. سرطان الخصية هو أكثر أنواع الأورام الصلبة شيوعاً عند الشباب من عمر 15 إلى 35 سنة، لكنه يمثل فقط 1% من كل السرطانات عند الرجال. وجود كتلة محسوسة يزيد احتمال كونها خبيثة مقارنة بكتلة تُكتشف فقط بالتصوير، وفي حوالي 15% من المرضى يكون في تظاهر بالعقد اللمفية الإقليمية أو ألم بالعظام.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار a bag of worms اللي فوق الخصية، وهذي علامة varicocele وليست سرطان. في طلاب أيضاً يختارون انتفاخ وتندر كامل الخصية اللي يوحي orchitis. لكن السرطان يتظاهر بكتلة صغيرة غير مؤلمة، ومحسوسة، ومتباينة عن باقي الخصية.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: Which of the following examination findings is most suggestive of testicular torsion?

options.text: Erythema and warmth of the scrotum
Relief of pain with testicular elevation

englishExplanation:
Testicular torsion occurs when the spermatic cord twists, compromising blood flow to the testicle. The most suggestive physical examination finding is the absence of the cremasteric reflex—when stroking the inner thigh fails to cause ipsilateral testicular elevation. This reflex is mediated by the genitofemoral nerve and is usually present in healthy male patients. In torsion, ischemic nerve dysfunction leads to its loss. While not 100% sensitive, the absent cremasteric reflex is the most specific clinical finding for testicular torsion and should heighten suspicion for the diagnosis.

Testicular torsion classically presents with acute, severe scrotal pain, often accompanied by nausea and vomiting. The affected testicle is typically high-riding with a horizontal lie due to spermatic cord twisting. Color Doppler ultrasound is the preferred imaging modality and will show reduced or absent blood flow. However, emergency clinicians must prioritize clinical suspicion over imaging results. If torsion is strongly suspected, emergent urology consultation and surgical detorsion should not be delayed. The gold standard treatment is emergent surgical detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy, ideally within 6 hours to maximize testicular salvage. A delay in diagnosis can result in infarction and necessitate an orchiectomy.

Delayed recognition of testicular torsion can lead to complications such as testicular atrophy, infertility, and psychological distress. In pediatric and adolescent patients presenting with acute scrotal pain, emergency clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion for torsion and use clinical signs, including the absent cremasteric reflex, to guide decision-making.



While erythema and warmth (B) may be present in testicular torsion, they are more commonly associated with infectious processes such as epididymitis or orchitis. These inflammatory conditions usually have a more gradual onset, often with fever or urinary symptoms. In torsion, early findings tend to be pallor rather than erythema, as blood flow is obstructed rather than increased.

Mild tenderness without swelling (C) is more suggestive of minor trauma, early epididymitis, or referred pain from another source, such as renal colic. Testicular torsion typically causes severe tenderness and an acutely swollen testicle due to venous congestion and ischemia. Mild symptoms alone should not rule out torsion, but they are not the most suggestive finding.

A varicocele (D) is a dilation of the pampiniform venous plexus and presents as a soft, bag-of-worms-like mass that typically worsens with standing. It is not associated with testicular torsion. While large varicoceles can be associated with infertility, they do not present with acute, severe pain or the high-riding testicle seen in torsion.

Finally, relief of pain with testicular elevation (E) (Prehn sign) is classically associated with epididymitis, not torsion. Lifting the testicle may relieve pain in epididymitis due to reduced pressure on the inflamed epididymis. However, Prehn sign is unreliable and inconsistent in distinguishing torsion from epididymitis. Relying on this sign can lead to a missed or delayed diagnosis of torsion, increasing the risk of testicular loss.

One Step Further
Question:
At what age is testicular torsion most likely to occur?

Reveal Answer:
There is a bimodal distribution, with peak incidence in the neonate (within first few days of life) and preadolescence.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Testicular Torsion

Bimodal distribution: infants and young adults
Sx: intense scrotal pain
PE: exquisite tenderness of the testicle, hard testes, high-riding testes, absent cremasteric reflex
Dx: confirmed by ultrasound with Doppler
Tx: urgent surgery, manual detorsion if surgery delayed, pain control
Start detorsion techniques with medial-to-lateral rotation, as most cases of torsion rotate laterally to medially
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ testicular torsion يصير لما الحبل المنوي يلتف ويقطع تدفق الدم للخصية، وأكثر علامة فحص تشير له هي غياب الـ cremasteric reflex. هالفعل بوساطة genitofemoral nerve، ولما دلّك داخل الفخذ ما يرتفع نفس الخصية بشكل طبيعي بسبب اختلال عصبي إقفاري. هالعلامة رغم إنها مو 100% حساسة، تعتبر أكثر علامة سريرية محددة للـ torsion، ولازم ترفع الشك حتى لو التصوير ما كان متوفر فوراً، لأن التصوير لا يجب أن يؤخّر التدخل.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون ارتياح الألم عند رفع الخصية، وهي Prehn sign، وهذا خطأ شائع. علامة Prehn لها حساسية منخفضة أصلاً، وأحياناً توجد في epididymitis أكثر، فما تعتبر معتمدة لاستبعاد الـ torsion. تذكّر إن غياب الـ cremasteric reflex هو الفيصل هنا.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: An 18-month-old girl presents to the emergency department with a fever of 39°C. Her parents report decreased appetite but no vomiting or diarrhea. They report her urine smells foul. She appears ill but nontoxic, and the remainder of her examination is normal. Her urinalysis shows 2+ nitrites, 2+ leukocyte esterase, moderate bacteria, and white blood cells. A urine culture is pending. Which of the following represents the appropriate management of this patient’s illness?

options.text: Admit for intravenous ceftriaxone and supportive care
Admit for intravenous vancomycin and supportive care
Discharge home with oral cefpodoxime and close outpatient follow-up
Discharge home with reassurance and encourage hydration
Start empiric ciprofloxacin and discharge home

correctAnswer: Discharge home with oral cefpodoxime and close outpatient follow-up
englishExplanation:
This patient presents with possible pyelonephritis, or at least a febrile urinary tract infection. Pyelonephritis is a bacterial infection that involves the renal parenchyma. In pediatric patients, fever without a clear source is often the primary manifestation. Urinalysis findings, including positive nitrites, leukocyte esterase, and pyuria, support the diagnosis. While pyelonephritis in young children can be severe, not all cases require hospitalization. Patients who appear nontoxic, have no significant comorbidities, and demonstrate the ability to tolerate oral medications can be safely cared for as outpatients with oral antibiotics like cefpodoxime, cefixime, or even cefalexin if resistance to first-generation cephalosporins is low in the community, provided close follow-up is ensured.

Oral third-generation cephalosporins are effective first-line options for treating pyelonephritis caused by Escherichia coli and other common uropathogens. In this patient, the absence of signs of sepsis or dehydration makes outpatient treatment appropriate. A typical course for oral therapy lasts 7–14 days. Parents should be educated to monitor for worsening symptoms such as lethargy, poor oral intake, or persistent fever, which may necessitate a return to the emergency department.

Close outpatient follow-up is critical to ensure clinical improvement and adjust therapy based on urine culture results. Kidney ultrasound or additional imaging may be warranted in cases of recurrent infection, abnormal growth, or nonresponse to therapy to evaluate for underlying abnormalities, such as vesicoureteral reflux.



While intravenous ceftriaxone (A) is the standard for hospitalized patients with pyelonephritis, this patient does not meet the criteria for admission. She is nontoxic, is not dehydrated, and can likely tolerate oral antibiotics. Hospitalization would expose the patient to unnecessary interventions, increasing health care costs and potentially creating undue stress for the family.

Vancomycin (B) is inappropriate for this patient, as pyelonephritis is predominantly caused by gram-negative organisms like E. coli, which vancomycin is ineffective against. This choice also unnecessarily escalates treatment, which could lead to adverse effects and antibiotic resistance.

Although the patient appears nontoxic, her clinical presentation and urinalysis findings are consistent with bacterial pyelonephritis, which requires antibiotic therapy. Failing to treat her infection would place her at significant risk for complications, including kidney scarring and sepsis. Thus, discharging with reassurance and oral hydration (D) is not the best management strategy.

Ciprofloxacin (E) is generally avoided in pediatric patients due to concerns about its potential effects on cartilage development. Safer alternatives like cefpodoxime are preferred for treating urinary tract infections in children, especially in uncomplicated cases in which oral therapy is indicated.

One Step Further
Question:
Which group of children are at the highest risk of developing urinary tract infections and acute pyelonephritis?

Reveal Answer:
Children with urinary tract abnormalities.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Pyelonephritis in Pediatrics

Sx: fever, dysuria, flank pain, vomiting
PE: CVA tenderness
Diagnostic tests
UA + leukocyte esterase, nitrites, + WBC
Urine culture
Cause: Escherichia coli, Klebsiella, Proteus, Enterococcus, Staphylococcus spp
Tx: first-generation cephalosporin (uncomplicated), second- or third-generation cephalosporin (complicated, fever), gentamicin, ampicillin if concern for Enterococcus
Hospitalize/IV antibiotics: patient < 2 months old, toxic, immunocompromised, inability to tolerate oral meds, no benefit from outpatient therapy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفلة عندها fever بدون مصدر واضح، وتحليل البول موجب nitrites وleukocyte esterase مع bacteria وpyuria، وهذا يوافق pyelonephritis أو التهاب مسالك بولية مع حرارة. ليست كل حالة pyelonephritis بصغار السن تحتاج تنويم، فالطفلة تبدو غير توكسيك ولا يوجد علامات إنتان أو جفاف، وتقدر تتقبل الدواء الفموي. لذلك تخريج مع cefpodoxime فموي ومتابعة قريبة هو الخيار الصحيح، وcefpodoxime من cephalosporins الجيل الثالث الفعالة ضد Escherichia coli ومسببات التهاب المسالك الشائعة، ومدة العلاج من 7 إلى 14 يوماً.
الفخ: الفخ هو تنويم الطفلة وإعطاء ceftriaxone وريدي تلقائياً. في طلاب يخافون من pyelonephritis عند الأطفال فيختارون التنويم مباشرة، لكن التنويم مخصص للحالات اللي فيها إنتان أو جفاف أو عدم قدرة على تحمل الدواء الفموي. هنا المريضة نافعة ومستقرة.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 12-year-old boy presents with penile pain. On exam, you note the image above. What management is indicated?

options.text: Direct application of ice to the skin

englishExplanation:
This patient presents with paraphimosis, a urologic emergency requiring emergent reduction of the foreskin. Paraphimosis occurs when the foreskin cannot be returned to its anatomic position covering the glans penis. It can be caused by infection, trauma, or hair tourniquets. Subsequent venous congestion can lead to arterial compression, penile necrosis, and gangrene. The typical presentation is erythema and engorgement of the penis distal to the obstruction and proximal flaccidity.

Treatment is directed at reducing swelling and edema of the foreskin and reducing it to the neutral position. Parenteral anesthesia or a local nerve block may be necessary for manual reduction. Circumferential compression should be held starting at the glans to reduce edema. This should be followed by manual reduction by placing steady pressure on the glans with both thumbs while holding the shaft straight. If these attempts fail, urology should be consulted for a dorsal slit procedure. Patients may be discharged home after reduction if they are voiding without difficulty and have no signs of severe infection.



Although cold water (in a glove or bag) can be useful in reducing edema, ice (A) should not be directly applied.

Urology follow-up (B) is necessary after reduction has occurred, but patients should not be sent home with paraphimosis because of the risk of serious complications.

Injectable phenylephrine (C) is used in the treatment of priapism, or prolonged erection of the penis that does not resolve spontaneously. It is not indicated in the treatment of paraphimosis.

Topical clotrimazole (E) is used to treat fungal infections of the glans, like balanitis. While infection can be one cause of paraphimosis, topical clotrimazole is not the first-line treatment for paraphimosis.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the definitive treatment of paraphimosis?

Reveal Answer:
Circumcision.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Paraphimosis

Sx: penile pain
PE: foreskin that, once retracted, cannot be brought to the usual position
Tx: manual reduction or dorsal slit if reduction unsuccessful
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هذا مرضه paraphimosis، وهي حالة طارئة بالمسالك لما القلفة لا ترجع لتغطية الـ glans، والنتيجة احتقان وريدي ممكن يوصل لتضيق الشرايين و necrosis و gangrene. العلاج هو تقليل الورم والانتفاخ ثم الإرجاع اليدوي للقلفة للوضع الطبيعي، ويكون ذلك بالضغط الدائري بدءاً من الـ glans لتخفيض الانتفاخ، ثم ضغط ثابت بالإبهامين على الـ glans مع تثبيت الساق مستقيمة. ممكن نحتاج تخدير موضعي أو حصار عصبي قبل الـ manual reduction.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون وضع الثلج مباشرة على الجلد، وهذا خطأ واضح لأن الثلج المباشر ممنوع؛ ممكن نستعمل ماء بارد داخل قفاز أو كيس. ثاني فخ هو إرسال المريض للمتابعة مع urology بدون إجراء، وهذا خطر لأن الـ paraphimosis ما تروح بدون إرجاع فوري.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 69-year-old man presents to the emergency department with acute urinary retention for 14 hours. He reports a steadily decreasing stream and intermittent urinary hesitancy for several months, but thus far, he has refused to see a clinician for his symptoms. Presently, he has not had any urine output since yesterday. His vital signs are within normal limits, but he appears to be significantly uncomfortable and has a palpable bladder on exam. A Foley catheter is placed and 900 mL of urine is collected over the next hour. Laboratory studies and urinalysis are unremarkable. Which class of medication should be used to treat this patient while he is waiting to see a urologist?
englishExplanation:
Acute urinary retention is a painful emergency that typically occurs in older men with benign prostatic hyperplasia. Patients present with the inability to pass urine, lower abdominal distention, and pain. It is uncommon in women. Prolonged bladder outlet obstruction can lead to acute kidney injury, so it must be treated expeditiously. Patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia often report urinary frequency, hesitancy, nocturia, and a weak urinary stream. Eventually, patients can develop bladder outlet obstruction and acute urinary retention unless treated appropriately with medications. This patient’s previous history suggests the development of benign prostatic hyperplasia. After relieving the obstruction with a Foley catheter and ensuring that there are no complications associated with the obstruction, this patient should be referred to an outpatient urologist. However, he will also benefit from the medical management of his prostatic hyperplasia. There are several treatment options available, but alpha-1 adrenergic antagonists provide more immediate therapeutic benefits and are the recommended first-line therapy. Examples of this medication include tamsulosin, doxazosin, and terazosin. They work to relax the smooth muscle in the bladder neck, prostate capsule, and prostatic urethra. Side effects include hypotension and dizziness, but frequently, older men with benign prostatic hyperplasia have concomitant hypertension that will also improve with this therapy.



5-alpha reductase inhibitors (A) are considered second-line therapy for the treatment of benign prostatic hyperplasia. Examples of this medication include finasteride and dutasteride. This class of medication is generally not recommended for patients with acute urinary retention because the benefits from the use of 5-alpha reductase inhibitors require long-term treatment.

Anticholinergic agents (C), such as oxybutynin or tolterodine, can be used as an alternative monotherapy, but they have been more effective as dual therapy with alpha-1 adrenergic antagonists and are contraindicated in acute urinary retention.

Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (D) can be used in patients with mild symptoms and erectile dysfunction. An example is tadalafil. However, this class of medication has not been shown to be as effective as alpha-1 adrenergic antagonists or 5-alpha reductase inhibitors.

One Step Further
Question:
What initial volume of urine returned after placement of a Foley catheter for acute urinary retention should concern the clinician for the development of postobstructive diuresis and significant volume loss with electrolyte abnormalities?

Reveal Answer:
1,000–1,500 mL.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH)

Most common in older male patients (aged > 50–60 years)
Caused by stromal and epithelial cell growth in the transitional zone of the prostate
Sx: hesitancy, intermittence or incontinence, frequency or fullness, urgency, nocturia (HI FUN)
Some patients may be asymptomatic
PE: nontender, enlarged prostate without nodules or indurations
Dx: based on Hx, digital rectal exam
UA typically performed to rule out alternate causes
Tx options: lifestyle interventions (e.g., fluid avoidance before bedtime), alpha-blockers, 5-reductase inhibitors, surgery (e.g., TURP)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده احتباس بول مع BPH، وتم إدخال Foley وإخراج البول، وبعد التأكد من عدم وجود مضاعفات ينحال لمتابعة urology خارجياً. لكن قبل ذلك يستفيد من علاج طبي للـ BPH، والـ alpha-1 adrenergic antagonists هي الخط الأول لأنها تعطي فائدة علاجية أسرع من غيرها. أمثلة هالأدوية tamsulosin وdoxazosin وterazosin، وتعمل على إرخاء العضلة الملساء في رقبة المثانة ومحفظة البروستات والإحليل البروستاتي.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار 5-alpha reductase inhibitor لأن الطلاب يعرفون إنه علاج BPH. بس هذا الدواء يحتاج أسابيع إلى شهور حتى يعطي فائدته، وما ينفع للحالة اللي بدها تأثير سريع، بينما الـ alpha-1 antagonists تعمل بسرعة على إرخاء العضلة وتخفيف الانسداد. الانتباه كذلك لأثاره مثل هبوط الضغط والدوخة.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 21-year-old man presents to a rural emergency department with no available consulting specialties with severe testicular pain. His symptoms started suddenly 1 hour ago while jogging. He tried to control his pain with acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and oxycodone that he had left over from a previous surgical procedure, but he continues to have severe pain. He has experienced several episodes of emesis. The patient’s vital signs are notable for a heart rate of 120 bpm. Physical exam is notable for a tender left testicle that has an elevated horizontal lay, negative cremasteric reflex, and no relief of symptoms with elevation of the testicle. Which of the following is the best next step in treatment?
englishExplanation:
Testicular torsion occurs when the testicle twists around its blood supply, leading to ischemia. This can manifest as severe testicular pain, scrotal edema, and an absence of a cremasteric reflex (L1 and L2 spinal root) with a horizontal and high-riding testicle. The pathophysiology is related to inadequate fixation of the lower pole of the testis to the tunica vaginalis, thus allowing the testicle to rotate. The diagnosis can be confirmed with a testicular ultrasound. However, this diagnostic test should not delay treatment (such as manual detorsion or surgery), as the diagnosis can be made on clinical grounds.

If there is any delay for a urology consultation and surgical treatment (such as a rural hospital without consulting services), then manual detorsion should be attempted. The definitive treatment of testicular torsion is an emergent surgical intervention to detorse the testicle and bilateral fixation to prevent torsion in the contralateral testicle. Any intervention that delays detorsion should not be performed, as it is thought that the testis sustains irreversible damage after 12 hours of ischemia from torsion.



Administering ceftriaxone and doxycycline (A) could be appropriate treatment of epididymitis, which in a young patient is typically caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis. This pathology would present with a tender posterior testicle, pyuria, and possibly a positive Prehn sign (pain relief with elevation of the testicle) without symptoms that are sudden in onset, which is not this patient's presentation.

Testicular ultrasound (B) would be indicated to confirm the diagnosis of testicular torsion, particularly in cases in which the diagnosis is uncertain. In this case, there is plenty of clinical evidence to suggest the most likely diagnosis and a testicular ultrasound would not change management. Arranging for a testicular ultrasound would also likely delay the ultimate necessary care.

Emergency surgery (D) is the best initial step in management for testicular torsion if there is no delay to surgery. This patient is in a rural hospital without consulting services. Thus, this treatment is not plausible. The time it would take to transfer the patient could result in further testicular injury.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the appendix testis?

Reveal Answer:
A pedunculated and small vestigial structure on the testis that is an embryological remnant of the Müllerian duct system that can twist and cause pain.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Testicular Torsion

Bimodal distribution: infants and young adults
Sx: intense scrotal pain
PE: exquisite tenderness of the testicle, hard testes, high-riding testes, absent cremasteric reflex
Dx: confirmed by ultrasound with Doppler
Tx: urgent surgery, manual detorsion if surgery delayed, pain control
Start detorsion techniques with medial-to-lateral rotation, as most cases of torsion rotate laterally to medially
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده testicular torsion من قصة الألم المفاجئ الشديد مع استفراغ وتسارع قلب، والفحص يبيّن خصية مرتفعة بوضع أفقي، وغياب الـ cremasteric reflex، وعدم ارتياح عند رفع الخصية. الأهم إنه موجود بريف بدون استشاريين، والتصوير التشخيصي ما يجب أن يؤخّر العلاج لأن التشخيص سريري. في هالحالة اللي فيها تأخير للتدخل الجراحي، الخطوة الصحيحة هي manual detorsion بمحاولة فك الالتواء، لأن الخصية تتعرض لضرر لا رجعة فيه بعد 12 ساعة من الإقفار.
الفخ: أكبر فخ هو اختيار testicular ultrasound، لأن الطالب يحب يثبت التشخيص قبل التدخل. بس الطلب واضح إن أي إجراء يؤخّر فك الالتواء ممنوع، والتصوير لا ينبغي أن يسبق العلاج هنا. كذلك ceftriaxone وdoxycycline هذي معالجة epididymitis مش torsion.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 54-year-old man presents with abdominal pain, vomiting, and fever. Physical examination reveals an ill-appearing man with a mass in the right groin as seen above. Which of the following is the most immediate next step required?

options.text: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis

englishExplanation:
This patient presents with signs and symptoms concerning for a strangulated hernia and should have an emergent surgical consultation for possible operative management. A hernia occurs when part of the viscus protrudes from its surrounding tissue walls. There are three presentations seen with hernias. The first is a reducible hernia where the hernia is soft and nontender (or minimally tender) and can easily be reduced through the neck of the defect. An incarcerated hernia is firm and painful and cannot be reduced through its defect. Lastly, a strangulated hernia occurs after incarceration and involves impairment of blood flow (arterial, venous, or both) to the viscus. Patients with strangulated hernias typically present with bowel obstruction and are toxic appearing. The hernia site itself is firm and extremely painful to palpation. There are often changes to the overlying skin. A strangulated hernia is a true surgical emergency. Emergent surgical consultation should be obtained prior to imaging as patients will require operative management. A delay in definitive treatment can lead to bowel ischemia or infarction.



An abdominal X-ray (A) may show signs of a bowel obstruction but this will not aid much in further diagnosis.

A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis (B) will show obstruction as well as the origin of the hernia sack. Neither of these modalities should delay surgical consultation and prompt treatment is critical.

A scrotal ultrasound (C) may show the presence of bowel in the scrotum but is not needed for diagnosis.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction?

Reveal Answer:
Adhesions from prior surgery.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Inguinal Hernias

Bimodal: < 1 and > 40 years old
Direct
Protrudes directly through the Hesselbach triangle and medial to the inferior epigastric artery (IEA)
Bulge decreases upon reclining
Indirect
​​Most common type
Protrudes through internal ring, lateral to IEA
Mnemonic: MDs don’t lie
​Medial to IEA: direct
Lateral to IEA: indirect
Strangulation risk: indirect > direct
Strangulated or incarcerated hernias: emergent surgery consultation
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده ألم بالبطن وقيء وحرارة، وبالفحص بادئ ill-appearing مع كتلة بالمنطقة الإربية اليمنى، وهذا يوافق strangulated hernia. الفتق الـ strangulated يصير بعد incarceration، وفيه اختلال تدفق الدم للعضو، والمريض يتظاهر عادة بانسداد أمعاء وبمظهر توكسيك، والفتق يكون قاسياً ومؤلماً جداً مع تغيرات بالجلد فوقه. هالحالة طارئة جراحية حقيقية، والخطوة الفورية هي الحصول على surgical consultation قبل أي تصوير، لأن المريض بدّه تدخل جراحي عاجل، وأي تأخير ممكن يؤدي لإقفار أو احتشاء الأمعاء.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار CT scan للبطن والحوض لأنه يبيّن الانسداد وأصل الفتق. لكن التصوير ما يجب أن يؤخّر الاستشارة الجراحية أبداً، والحالة تشخيصها سريري مع كتلة إربية ومظهر توكسيك. الاستشارة الجراحية تسبق التصوير.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: Which of the following is a major extrarenal manifestation of polycystic kidney disease?
englishExplanation:
Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is a common autosomal dominant genetic disorder primarily involving the kidneys but also affecting multiple organ systems. It is caused by mutations in the PKD1 or PKD2 genes, with PKD1 mutations typically leading to earlier and more severe disease. The hallmark of PKD is the bilateral development of numerous kidney cysts, which enlarge over time and progressively impair kidney function. Patients often present in adulthood with flank or abdominal pain, hypertension, gross or microscopic hematuria, urinary tract infections, or nephrolithiasis. Hypertension is frequently the earliest manifestation and may precede any noticeable decline in kidney function.

Progressive cyst growth leads to kidney enlargement and parenchymal destruction, ultimately resulting in chronic kidney disease. Nearly 50% of affected individuals will develop end-stage kidney disease requiring dialysis or kidney transplantation by 60 years old. Proteinuria may be present but is usually non-nephrotic in range.

PKD is a systemic disorder, and extrarenal manifestations are common. One of the most serious complications is the development of intracranial (cerebral) aneurysms, particularly in the circle of Willis. The risk of aneurysm formation increases with age and is significantly higher in individuals with a family history of aneurysm or subarachnoid hemorrhage, larger aneurysms, or poorly controlled hypertension. Rupture of a cerebral aneurysm presents with the sudden onset of a thunderclap headache, often described as the worst headache of the patient’s life, and may be accompanied by nausea, vomiting, photophobia, neck stiffness, and altered mental status.

Other notable extrarenal manifestations include hepatic cysts, which are common and often asymptomatic but may cause hepatomegaly or pain. Pancreatic cysts may also occur but are usually clinically insignificant. Cardiac valvular abnormalities, particularly mitral valve prolapse and aortic regurgitation, are more common in patients with PKD. Additionally, there is an increased incidence of colonic diverticulosis, which may lead to diverticulitis or bleeding, particularly in patients with advanced kidney disease.

Diagnosis is made by kidney imaging, most commonly ultrasound, but CT or MRI may provide more detail. Genetic testing is available but is generally reserved for atypical cases or for family planning. Treatment focuses on blood pressure control, with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin II receptor blockers, infection prevention and treatment, and kidney protection through lifestyle modification and monitoring. Regular surveillance for complications, including aneurysms in individuals at high risk, is an important part of long-term care.



Abdominal aortic aneurysm (A) is not a common feature of PKD. It is more associated with atherosclerosis and connective tissue disorders like Marfan syndrome.

Aortic stenosis (B) is a valvular disorder unrelated to cystic diseases. PKD may involve mitral valve prolapse more commonly than aortic valve issues.

Ovarian cyst (D) is a common benign finding and is not directly related to PKD, which involves cyst formation in the kidney and liver, not the ovaries.

One Step Further
Question:
What is a simple kidney cyst?

Reveal Answer:
A benign, fluid-filled sac that forms in the kidney. It is asymptomatic and is characterized by thin walls, clear fluid, and no internal septations or solid components on ultrasound or CT.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Polycystic Kidney Disease

Most commonly autosomal dominant inheritance pattern due to PKD1 or PKD2 gene mutations
Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease less common and often caused by PKHD1 gene variants
Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
May be asymptomatic or present with flank pain, hematuria
PE: hypertension
Dx: ultrasound (most common), CT, MRI
May be incidentally discovered on imaging
Tx: BP control (e.g., ACEIs, ARBs), increased fluid intake
Associated with increased risk for liver or pancreatic cysts, intracranial aneurysm, intracerebral hemorrhage
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ polycystic kidney disease مرض وراثي autosomal dominant يصيب الكلى والعديد من الأعضاء الأخرى، والعلامة المميزة فيه تكوّن أكياس ثنائية الجانب بالكلى تكبر مع الوقت وتدمر النسيج وتؤدي لفشل كلوي مزمن. هو مرض جهازي، والتظاهرات خارج الكلية شائعة، وأخطرها هو تطوّر intracranial أو cerebral aneurysms بالتحديد في circle of Willis. خطر تكوّن الأكياس الوعائية يزيد مع العمر، ويكون أعلى بوجود تاريخ عائلي لأم دم أو نزف تحت العنكبوتية.
الفخ: في طلاب يختارون abdominal aortic aneurysm لأن كلمة aneurysm تخلّيهم يتوقعون الأبهر. بس التظاهر الشهير والمهم بمرض الكلى المتعددة الأكياس هو cerebral aneurysm في circle of Willis، وخصوصاً لما يكون في تاريخ عائلي للنزف تحت العنكبوتية. تذكّر هالربط.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: What is the most common cause of pain related to testicular malignancies?
englishExplanation:
Male patients presenting for evaluation of testicular pain or masses should be assessed for genital emergencies, particularly testicular torsion, testicular appendageal torsion, epididymitis, orchitis, scrotal abscess, and Fournier gangrene.

Testicular malignancy is not a true genital emergency, but should be considered in any patient with a testicular mass of unknown etiology. Testicular cancer accounts for only 1% of all male cancers, but it is the most common solid cancer in men ages 15 through 35 years. The vast majority are germ cell tumors.

Most patients with testicular malignancies are actually asymptomatic and pain-free. Symptoms may include a dull ache or heavy sensation in the lower abdomen, scrotum, or perianal region. The mass is indurated or firm. Those that do present with pain are usually secondary to intratumoral hemorrhage. This may be mistaken for orchitis.

Testicular malignancies are often insidious and may present with supraclavicular adenopathy, gynecomastia, chronic dry cough or dyspnea (from lung metastasis), nausea, vomiting, anorexia, an abdominal mass, gastrointestinal bleeding (from retroduodenal metastasis), bone pain, low back pain, nervous system involvement, or unilateral leg swelling from venous thrombosis.

A complete physical inspection, including a testicular exam, may reveal the primary tumor. Identification of a testicular mass warrants urgent urology referral for additional diagnostic testing and staging.



Avascular necrosis (A) is not a recognized cause of pain in testicular malignancies. While testicular infarction can occur, this is distinct from avascular necrosis and is grouped with intratumoral hemorrhage as a cause of pain.

Orchitis (C) is an infectious or inflammatory condition unrelated to testicular malignancy. While orchitis is more common than testicular tumors and may initially be suspected, it is not caused by the malignancy itself.

Torsion (D) can occur in association with testicular tumors, but it is explicitly described as a rare cause of pain in testicular malignancies, whereas hemorrhage and infarction are the most likely causes

One Step Further
Question:
What should be offered to men with testicular cancer who wish to preserve fertility prior to instituting cancer therapy?

Reveal Answer:
Cryopreservation of sperm.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Testicular Cancer

Risk factors include cryptorchidism, age 15–35 years
Sx: testicular lump
PE: painless, hard, fixed mass
Lab results: beta-hCG, AFP, or LDH may be elevated based on tumor type
Diagnosis starts with ultrasound
Tx (varying based on factors such as type and stage): radical inguinal orchiectomy, radiation therapy or platinum-based chemotherapy in certain situations
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الغالبية العظمى من مرضى أورام الخصية يكونون بدون أعراض وبدون ألم أصلاً، وأعراضهم ممكن تكون مجرد ثقل أو وجع خفيف بالبطن السفلي أو الكيس أو المنطقة حول الشرج، والكتلة تكون صلبة. أما اللي يجيهم ألم فعلاً، فالسبب الأشهر هو intratumoral hemorrhage، أي نزف داخل الورم نفسه. هالتظاهر ممكن يُشتبه به خطأً كحالة orchitis، ولهذا لازم ننتبه، لأن أي كتلة خصية مجهولة السبب تستدعي تقييماً جاداً.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار orchitis، لأن المريض بده ألم وورم ممكن يشبه التهاب الخصية. بس الـ orchitis يعطي انتفاخ وتندر بكامل الخصية مع أعراض إنتانية، بينما الألم بأورام الخصية سببه نزف داخل الورم على خلفية كتلة صلبة. انتبه لهذا الفرق.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: An 18-year-old presents to the emergency department with severe pain in his penis. He indicates he has had some mild irritation to the glans and foreskin areas recently. After intercourse tonight he was unable to reduce the foreskin and now has severe pain in the tip of his penis. On examination, the penis is flaccid and the foreskin is retracted proximally. There is swelling to the tip of the penis with mild erythema. What is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
This patient has a story and exam consistent with paraphimosis. Paraphimosis is a true urologic emergency of the uncircumcised penis. It is the inability to reduce the proximal edematous foreskin distally over the glans penis into its natural position. The resulting glans edema and venous engorgement can progress to arterial compromise and gangrene. Paraphimosis can be caused by infection, masturbation, trauma, or hair or clothing tourniquets. Patients typically appear very anxious, and the history reveals that the patient retracted the foreskin and could not replace the foreskin over the glans. Physical examination reveals a flaccid proximal penis with erythema and engorgement distal to the obstruction. The foreskin is retracted and cellulitis may be present. The diagnosis of paraphimosis is based on clinical findings and should be intervened on immediately. Paraphimosis can often be reduced by compression of the glans for several minutes to reduce edema and allow for successful reduction of the now smaller glans through the foreskin.



A penile fracture (B) occurs when the tunica albuginea of one or both corpora cavernosa ruptures due to direct trauma to the erect penis. The most common cause is sexual intercourse, but other causes include animal bites, stabbing, bullet wounds, and self-mutilation. On examination, the penis is acutely swollen but flaccid, discolored, and tender.

Phimosis (C) is the inability to retract the foreskin proximally. Infection, poor hygiene, and previous preputial injuries with scarring are common causes of pathologic phimosis. Scarring at the tip of the foreskin can occlude the preputial meatus, infrequently causing urinary retention.

Priapism (D) is a urologic emergency that is characterized by a persistent, painful, pathologic erection in which both corpora cavernosa are engorged with stagnant blood. Many cases of priapism are related to oral antihypertensive agents, neuroleptic medications, or oral agents related to erectile dysfunction.

One Step Further
Question:
What emergent procedure needs to be performed in a patient with paraphimosis when all reduction techniques have failed and ongoing ischemia is clearly evident?

Reveal Answer:
Superficial dorsal slit incision of the constricting band.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Paraphimosis

Sx: penile pain
PE: foreskin that, once retracted, cannot be brought to the usual position
Tx: manual reduction or dorsal slit if reduction unsuccessful
arabicExplanation:
ليش: القصة والفحص واضحين لـ paraphimosis، لأن المريض غير مختون ومرّ بشد على القلفة، وبعد الجماع ما قدر يرجع القلفة، وصار عنده ألم شديد بالطرف مع انتفاخ واحتقان. الـ paraphimosis هي عدم القدرة على إرجاع القلفة المتورمة فوق الـ glans لوضعها الطبيعي، مما يؤدي لتورمه واحتقانه الوريدي اللي ممكن يوصل لتضيق شرياني وغرغرينا. الفحص يبيّن قضيب flaccid بالجزء القريب، مع احتقان وانتفاخ بالجزء البعيد من منطقة الانسداد، والتدخل لازم يكون فوري.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار phimosis، وهي فعلاً عدم القدرة على سحب القلفة للخلف، بس هي حالة مختلفة تماماً وغير طارئة بهالشكل. الفرق المهم إن بالـ paraphimosis القلفة مسحوبة وما ترجع، بينما بالـ phimosis القلفة ما تنسحب أصلاً. تذكّر هالتفريق لأنه يغير الطارئية.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: Which of the following represents a reason for emergent dialysis in a patient with end-stage kidney disease and on dialysis?

options.text: Missed dialysis with normal serum potassium level

englishExplanation:
Although the decision to institute dialysis in a patient with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is complicated, the indications for emergent dialysis in the emergency department are not. Pulmonary edema represents one of the most common problems patients with CKD present to the emergency department with. Patients will typically have worsening dyspnea on exertion or shortness of breath, but body weight significantly greater than dry weight may be the best indicator. Initial emergency treatment of pulmonary edema in the dialysis patient is similar to that in the nondialysis patient, but the dialysis patient is less likely to respond to diuretic therapy. Supplemental oxygen should be given and nitroglycerin (sublingual or intravenous) should be started. Regardless of the response to oxygen and vasodilators, dialysis arrangements should be made for the dialysis patient. Dialysis is the most effective approach to reducing circulating volume when the patient lacks kidney function. Medical treatment may temporarily stabilize a patient while awaiting dialysis. Other emergent indications for dialysis include severe uncontrollable hypertension, hyperkalemia, severe electrolyte or acid-base disturbance, specific overdoses, and severe symptomatic uremia.



Hyperphosphatemia, not hypophosphatemia (A), is a trigger for dialysis.

Patients may miss a scheduled dialysis treatment (B) without developing complications requiring emergent dialysis.

Severe uremia without symptoms (D) does not require emergent dialysis. However, the presence of symptoms, including altered mental status or bleeding, would qualify the patient for emergent dialysis.

One Step Further
Question:
What blood urea nitrogen and creatinine are considered triggers for the initiation of dialysis in patients with chronic kidney disease?

Reveal Answer:
A blood urea nitrogen of 100 mg/dL and a creatinine of 10 mg/dL.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Indications for Kidney Replacement Therapy (Dialysis)

Acidosis: pH < 7.1
Electrolyte abnormalities: refractory hyperkalemia (> 6.5 mEq/L) or rapidly rising levels
Dialyzable ingestions: substances that can be effectively removed through dialysis
Volume overload: unresponsive to diuretics
Symptomatic uremia: significant symptoms due to kidney failure
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ pulmonary edema من أشهر الأسباب اللي تجيب مرضى الفشل الكلوي المزمن للطوارئ، وغالباً يشتكون من ضيق نفس مع الجهد، وأفضل مؤشر هو وزن أعلى بكثير من الوزن الجاف. العلاج الأولي يشمل الأكسجين وnitroglycerin تحت اللسان أو وريدياً، بس مريض الدياليز أقل استجابة للمدرات البولية، والديلزة هي الأكثر فعالية لتقليل الحجم الدوري عند غياب وظيفة الكلية. لذلك pulmonary edema هي من الاستطبابات الواضحة للديلزة الإسعافية، ومؤشرات أخرى تشمل فرط ضغط غير مسيطر، وفرط بوتاسيوم، واضطراب كهارل أو حموضة، وجرعات زائدة محددة، ويوريميا شديدة بأعراض.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار missed dialysis مع بوتاسيوم طبيعي، لأن في مرضى يفوّتون جلسة ولا تتطور عندهم مشاكل حادة، فغياب الجلسة لوحده ما هو استطباب. كذلك hypophosphatemia خيار غلط، لأن hyperphosphatemia هي اللي تعتبر محرضاً للديلزة وليس نقص الفوسفات. المعيار هو الشدة والعلامات السريرية.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A parent brings her 1-year-old uncircumcised boy to the emergency department after realizing while bathing the child that his foreskin was not retractile. He has no fever and is still having copious wet diapers. Examination reveals a normal, intact foreskin overriding the glans, and urine can be seen coming out of the meatus. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Retraction of the foreskin to expose the distal glans penis
Topical hydrocortisone applied to the distal penis

englishExplanation:
This patient’s presentation is consistent with physiologic phimosis. Phimosis is the inability to retract the foreskin proximal to the glans. It is important to differentiate phimosis from paraphimosis (inability to reduce the foreskin back over the glans), as paraphimosis is a medical emergency that can lead to necrosis of the glans due to the obstruction of venous flow. Phimosis is due to adhesions between the prepuce and glans, which lyse over time, leading to the ability to retract the foreskin. This physiologic phimosis often resolves spontaneously by age 3 years and does not require additional management unless the stenosis becomes pathologic and severe enough to impede urinary flow, causing obstruction or infection. This patient is still having wet diapers, is at the age of physiologic phimosis rather than pathologic phimosis, and urinary flow is noted on exam. Thus, reassurance and discharge is the appropriate care plan. Additionally, parents should be advised to clean under the foreskin to reduce the risk of local or urinary infections.



Retraction of the foreskin to expose the distal glans (B) should not be attempted, as this will not benefit the patient and can potentially lead to paraphimosis, a much more serious condition.

Topical hydrocortisone (C), or other steroid cream, may be used for those with pathologic phimosis, which would be a higher consideration after age 3 years. This patient likely has physiologic phimosis.

Urology consult (D) is not recommended for this benign condition unless symptoms persist into older childhood and do not resolve with topical treatments.

One Step Further
Question:
What is often used to reduce swelling to aid reduction of paraphimosis?

Reveal Answer:
Ice applied to the distal penis.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Phimosis

Often benign in infants and children < 3 years old
Sx: inability to retract foreskin over the glans penis
Tx: hygiene, topical steroids, dorsal slit (if signs of ischemia), or circumcision
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده physiologic phimosis، وهي عدم القدرة على سحب القلفة للخلف بسبب التصاقات بين القلفة والـ glans. هالتصاقات تتحلل مع الوقت وتذوب تدريجياً، والـ physiologic phimosis عادة تحل من حالها بعمر 3 سنوات. الطفل عنده حفاضات مبللة بشكل جيد، وما في حرارة، ومشاهدة البول يخرج من الـ meatus، فما في دليل على انسداد أو انتان، ولهذا reassurance and discharge هو الخيار الصحيح مع نصح الأهل بتنظيف تحت القلفة لتقليل خطر الالتهاب.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار سحب القلفة لإظهار الـ glans البعيد، وهذا خطأ لأن سحب القلفة بهالعمر وبهالتصاقات ما يفيد الطفل إطلاقاً، وممكن يسبب paraphimosis اللي حالة أخطر بكثير. كذلك الستيرويد الموضعي يُستعمل فقط للـ pathologic phimosis وليس هنا.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 33-year-old woman with a history of frequent urinary tract infections presents to the ED with right flank pain and dysuria that started acutely today. The pain is associated with a low-grade fever, nausea, and vomiting. Urinalysis is positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrites. Microscopic examination reveals 26 WBC/hpf and 2+ bacteria. A noncontrast abdominal computed tomography scan shows a staghorn calculus in the right kidney. Which of the following is the likely composition of the staghorn calculus?
englishExplanation:
Urologic stone formation is the result of the supersaturation of dissolved salts in the urine, which then condense into a solid. Struvite (magnesium-ammonium-phosphate) stones account for about 10–15% of all stones. They occur almost exclusively in patients with urinary tract infections caused by urea-splitting bacteria such as Proteus, Klebsiella, Providencia, Pseudomonas, and Staphylococcus species. They are also the most common cause of staghorn calculi (large stones that cause a cast of the renal pelvis). Treatment of staghorn calculi is difficult as antibiotic penetration of the stone is poor and the risk for urosepsis exists as long as the stone remains.



Most stones are comprised of calcium oxalate (A), either alone or in combination with calcium phosphate. Although these stones are common, this patient's concomitant urinary tract infection suggests a struvite stone.

Cystine (B) stones are rare and occur in patients with cystinuria, an autosomal recessive genetic disorder affecting amino acid transport that is not present in this patient.

Uric acid (D) stones account for about 10% of cases of urolithiasis. These stones are radiolucent on an abdominal radiograph and are related to underlying illnesses such as gout and diabetes that are not present in this patient.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common condition resulting in hypercalciuria and subsequent kidney stone formation?

Reveal Answer:
Hyperparathyroidism.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Ureterolithiasis and Renal Colic

Most commonly caused by calcium oxalate
Struvite: staghorn calculi, urease-producing bacteria
Uric acid: radiolucent on X-ray, gout
Cystine: children with metabolic diseases
Sx: flank pain that radiates to groin
PE: patient won’t lie still, hematuria
Dx: noncontrast helical CT, most common location is the ureterovesical junction (UVJ)
U/S can be used to diagnose hydronephrosis in those not eligible for CT imaging
Tx: pain control (NSAIDs, opioids) and antiemetics
< 5 mm: likely to pass spontaneously
> 5 mm: medical expulsive therapy (tamsulosin), urology consultation in certain cases
> 10 mm: urology consultation, shock wave lithotripsy, ureteroscopy
Admission: intractable pain or vomiting, infected stone or urosepsis, single kidney with significant obstruction, hypercalcemic crisis, urinary extravasation
Prevention
Lifestyle modifications: increased fluid intake, dietary adjustments
Options for prevention of recurrent calcium stones despite lifestyle modifications: thiazides, allopurinol, citrate
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها التهاب مسالك بولية متكرر واليوم التهاب حاد، وتحليل البول موجب للـ leukocyte esterase وnitrites، والتصوير أظهر staghorn calculus بالكلية اليمنى. الـ struvite stones، اللي تركيبها magnesium-ammonium-phosphate، تشكّل تقريباً 10 إلى 15% من كل الحصوات، وتصير تقريباً حصراً عند مرضى التهاب المسالك البولية الناتج عن بكتيريا مكسّرة لليوريا مثل Proteus وKlebsiella وProvidencia وPseudomonas. وهي كذلك أكثر سبب شائع لحصوات الـ staghorn، ومعالجتها صعبة لأن المضادات ما تخترق الحصوة جيداً وخطر urosepsis موجود ما دامت الحصوة موجودة.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار calcium oxalate، لأنها فعلاً أكثر أنواع الحصوات شيوعاً بشكل عام. لكن وجود التهاب مسالك بولية مرافق هو المفتاح اللي يرجّح struvite وليس calcium oxalate. كذلك uric acid وcystine لهما سياقات خاصة غير موجودة بهالمريضة، مثل النقرس والسكري أو cystinuria.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 50-year-old man presents to the emergency department with testicular pain. He states his symptoms started yesterday and have progressively worsened. He reports no new sexual activity. On physical exam, his right testicle and epididymis are edematous and tender to palpation. Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy?
englishExplanation:
Levofloxacin is recommended for the treatment of acute epididymo-orchitis in nonsexually active patients who are low-risk for sexually transmitted infections. Acute epididymo-orchitis is one of the most common causes of scrotal pain in male patients. It is characterized by testicular pain, swelling, and tenderness. In rare cases, patients may present with fever, rigors, and lower urinary tract symptoms, including increased frequency, urgency, and dysuria. Epididymo-orchitis is commonly caused by bacterial infections but can occur secondary to trauma or autoimmune diseases. The most common infectious etiologies vary by age and risk factors. In patients who are sexually active, Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis are the most common. However, in nonsexually active patients, urinary pathogens such as Escherichia coli are the most likely organisms. The diagnosis of epididymo-orchitis is often suspected based on history and physical exam. Urinalysis, urine culture, and testing for sexually transmitted infections can help support the presumptive diagnosis through identification of causative organisms.



Ceftriaxone (A) and doxycycline (C) are recommended for patients who are sexually active and have symptoms of epididymo-orchitis. The preferred treatment is ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscularly plus doxycycline 100 mg orally twice a day for 10 days. However, for patients who are unable to tolerate doxycycline, azithromycin may be given as an alternative.

Ceftriaxone and levofloxacin (B) are recommended for patients of any age who practice insertive anal intercourse. Ceftriaxone is given as a one-time dose of 500 mg intramuscularly, and levofloxacin is prescribed at a dose of 500 mg orally once daily for 10 days.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most likely cause of bilateral orchitis in an unvaccinated child?

Reveal Answer:
Mumps.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Epididymitis

Most common cause
Prepubertal: UTI, virus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae
Postpubertal: C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae
Sexually transmitted: C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae
Nonsexually transmitted: E. coli, Pseudomonas
Sx: gradual-onset unilateral scrotal pain
PE: scrotal erythema, relief with testicular elevation (Prehn sign), normal cremasteric reflex
Dx: clinical, U/S will show increased color flow on Doppler
Tx
Prepubertal: treat UTI (if present), supportive care
Postpubertal: ceftriaxone + doxycycline
Sexually transmitted: ceftriaxone + doxycycline
Nonsexually transmitted: fluoroquinolone
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده epididymo-orchitis واضح من الألم المتدرج مع تورم وتندر بالخصية والبربخ، وما عنده أي نشاط جنسي جديد، فهو غير معرّض لعدوى منقولة جنسياً. عند المرضى غير النشيطين جنسياً، المسببات الأكثر احتمالاً هي مسببات المسالك البولية مثل Escherichia coli، ولهذا levofloxacin هو الخيار الصحيح. أما المرضى النشيطون جنسياً فأكثر مسببين عندهم Neisseria gonorrhoeae و Chlamydia trachomatis، وهذول بدهم ceftriaxone و doxycycline.
الفخ: الفخ هو اختيار ceftriaxone وdoxycycline لأنها العلاج الشائع لالتهاب البربخ عند الشباب. بس المريض صرح إنه ما عنده نشاط جنسي جديد، فالتغطية المطلوبة هون لمسببات المسالك البولية، والـ levofloxacin يغطيها بشكل مناسب. ارجع دائماً لحالة النشاط الجنسي قبل اختيار المضاد.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 24-year-old man presents to the emergency department with an erection that has lasted for the past 6 hours and has not been improving. His vital signs are within normal limits, and physical exam is notable for an erect penis that the patient states is painful. Which of the following is the best initial treatment for this patient?
englishExplanation:
Priapism is defined as a persistent erection of the penis or clitoris that is not associated with sexual stimulation or desire. Priapism typically occurs in male individuals with an erection that lasts ≥ 4 hours and is commonly associated with sickle cell disease. The condition can be classified as ischemic and nonischemic, with ischemic priapism being a urologic emergency.

The cause of priapism is related to smooth muscle relaxation of the cavernosal arteries, which leads to increased blood entry to the penis with decreased venous outflow. Ischemic priapism is when increased blood entry ultimately leads to a compartment syndrome with increased hypoxia and acidosis in the cavernous tissue. Untreated ischemic priapism can lead to permanent damage and erectile dysfunction.

The treatment of acute ischemic priapism involves reducing blood inflow, increasing blood outflow, and removal of blood to decrease compartment pressure. The management of ischemic priapism is via emergent urological consultation, with aspiration of the corpora cavernosa and intracavernosal phenylephrine.



Emergent surgical decompression (B) would be indicated in cases of priapism refractory to initial medical management and aspiration.

Phenylephrine (C) should be injected into the corpora cavernosa and is not given intravenously for priapism.

Observation (D) is inappropriate, as persistent priapism can lead to permanent impotence if untreated.

One Step Further
Question:
What nerve block should be performed prior to attempting aspiration in priapism?

Reveal Answer:
A penile block (with injection of bupivacaine or lidocaine without epinephrine at the base of the penis).

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Priapism

Low-flow: venous, painful, emergency
Highest risk in individuals with sickle cell disease
Tx: corpora cavernosa aspiration, intracavernous phenylephrine
Use dorsal penile nerve block
Injection and aspiration performed at 2 o’clock or 10 o’clock position
High-flow: arterial, semierect, painless
Often related to trauma
Tx: observation, arterial embolization
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الحالة هاي priapism إسكيمي، يعني انتصاب مستمر صارله 6 ساعات ومو مرتبط برغبة جنسية، وهاد يعتبر طارئ مسالك بولية. السبب إنه في ارتخاء لعضلات الsmooth muscle بشرايين cavernosal، فبدخول الدم للpenis أكثر والخروج الوريدي يقل، وهاد يوصل لcompartment syndrome مع hypoxia و acidosis بالcavernous tissue. إذا ما عالجناه ممكن يصير ضرر دائم و erectile dysfunction، فالعلاج الأول هو aspiration of the corpora cavernosa مع intracavernosal phenylephrine بعد استشارة urology طارئة.
الفخ: في ناس يختاروا Phenylephrine بس عن طريق الوريد، وهاد غلط لأنه الدواء لازم ينجق داخل الcorpora cavernosa. وفي كمان من يختار Emergent surgical decompression، وهاد بس للcases اللي ما استجابت للعلاج الطبي الأولي والaspiration.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 56-year-old man without any reported medical history and without a primary care clinician for over 20 years presents to the emergency department with 4 days of worsening pain and tenderness over the head of his penis and foreskin, as well as a thick, white discharge in the region of his pain. The patient has no fevers, dysuria, hematuria, urethral discharge, or difficulty urinating. He also reports no testicular tenderness or swelling and has not had a recent change in his hygienic routine. He has been sexually inactive for > 5 years. Physical exam is notable for the findings seen in the image above. Based on his history and presentation, along with appropriate antimicrobial treatment, which of the following diagnostic tests is most indicated for this patient?
englishExplanation:
Inflammation of the glans of the penis, which is termed balanitis, affects up to 3% of uncircumcised men worldwide. This incidence increases when cases of balanoposthitis, or inflammation of both the glans and foreskin, are also included. In patients in which an etiology is clearly identified, the most common cause of both balanitis and balanoposthitis is candidal infection, with a predisposition for infection related to poor hygiene or overcleaning of the glans and foreskin. Patients may also have bacterial, dermatologic, autoimmune, and neoplastic sources, though in far fewer amounts than fungal cases, which typically present with pain, tenderness, and swelling along the glans and foreskin and clumps of white exudate overlying the area. This is in contrast to bacterial causes of balanitis, which more commonly have a thicker, malodorous, and purulent exudate. If untreated, ongoing inflammation and worsening edema can lead to phimosis of the foreskin, with resultant voiding difficulty and sexual dysfunction, necessitating foreskin dilation or emergent circumcision. Children typically develop balanitis for hygienic reasons, with the buildup of sweat, skin debris, and urine within their foreskin as a fertile ground for fungal growth. Cases in children are treated with topical antifungals, and typically no further diagnostic workup is indicated. In adults who develop balanitis without any identifiable risk factors for the condition, a fingerstick glucose should be performed as this is sometimes the presenting concern of patients who are newly diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. This is because hyperglycemia is correlated with increased fungal growth at the glans and foreskin due to increased levels of glucose in urine that is not properly cleaned out of the area.



A rapid plasma reagin (B) would be an appropriate initial screening test for syphilis in the proper clinical setting, but this patient’s symptoms and findings do not raise concern for this condition.

Given that the patient is urinating without any difficulty and not reporting hematuria or retention, there is no indication for a retrograde urethrogram (C).

With no evidence of fever, dysuria, hematuria, flank pain, or suprapubic pain, and with localization of symptoms and findings to the patient’s glans and foreskin, the performance of a urinalysis (D) is not necessary.

One Step Further
Question:
What multisystem condition, which can manifest with balanitis, affects the eyes, joints, and genitourinary tract?

Reveal Answer:
Reactive arthritis.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Balanoposthitis

Balanitis - inflammation of the glans penis
Posthitis - inflammation of the prepuce or foreskin
Most commonly caused by Candida
Risks: uncircumcised penis
Sx: burning and itching of the penis
PE: erythema and inflammation with scant white discharge
Tx: topical antifungal
Recurrent balanitis is seen in patients with diabetes
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الصورة والحكاية توحي بbalanitis، يعني التهاب رأس الpenis، وهاد يصيب حتى 3% من الرجال غير المختونين، وإذا انضاف التهاب الforeskin صار balanoposthitis. السبب الأشهر لما يكون في white exudate متكتل هو candidal infection، وهاد يصير عادة بسبب poor hygiene أو overcleaning. والمريض هون عنده سكري غير مشخص ممكن، لأنه من 20 سنة ما زار طبيب، فلازم نعمل fingerstick glucose لأن الcandidal infection بتنذر بhyperglycemia غير مكتشفة.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختاروا Urinalysis أو Rapid plasma reagin لأنهم يفكروا بالSTI، بس المريض sexually inactive من 5 سنين وما عنده urethral discharge ولا dysuria، فالاحتمال الأشهر سكري مو مرض جنسي.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A 21-year-old man presents to the emergency department for a penile lesion that has been present for 1 week. He is sexually active with multiple partners and is inconsistent with condom use. Examination reveals a painless 2 cm ulcerative lesion on his dorsal penis and painless inguinal lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is the appropriate treatment for this patient?

options.text: Single dose of intramuscular ceftriaxone and oral doxycycline for 1 week

englishExplanation:
This patient’s presentation is most consistent with a diagnosis of primary syphilis. This sexually transmitted disease is caused by Treponema pallidum, a spirochete organism that enters the affected individual via direct contact. At the site of primary contact, a painless chancre will present 2–3 weeks after initial contact. The chancre can present at any site of direct contact, including the penis, vagina, rectum, and mouth. Patients may also have painless regional lymphadenopathy. Diagnosis for primary syphilis is typically made clinically. Darkfield microscopy can be used to directly visualize the organism, but its sensitivity is not sufficient as a rule-out test. Blood tests such as venereal disease research lab (VDRL) and rapid plasma reagin (RPR) can also be obtained, but these tests also have high false-positive and false-negative results. The initial, painless chancre will resolve without treatment, but failure to treat puts the patient at risk of advancing to secondary and tertiary syphilis, which can have serious cardiac or neurological implications. Management of primary syphilis is a single dose of intramuscular penicillin for most patients. Oral doxycycline for 2 weeks is recommended for patients allergic to penicillin. Later stages of syphilis are also treated with penicillin but require extended dosing.



Oral penicillin for 1 week (A) is not the correct treatment for syphilis because one-time intramuscular therapy is preferred.

A single dose of oral azithromycin (C) is the correct treatment for chancroid, a sexually transmitted disease that presents with a painful chancre caused by Haemophilus ducreyi.

A single dose of intramuscular ceftriaxone and oral doxycycline for 1 week (D) is part of the correct treatment for urethritis or purulent urethral discharge in men. It should likely also be prescribed to this patient, but his presentation also requires treatment for syphilis. Doxycycline would be continued twice daily for 7 days for correct treatment. This is most often caused by Neisseria gonorrhea and Chlamydia trachomatis.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the treatment for syphilis in pregnant patients with penicillin allergies?

Reveal Answer:
Penicillin desensitization followed by penicillin treatment.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Primary Syphilis

Sx: painless ulcer that forms 3 weeks after sexual activity and disappears in 3–6 weeks
PE: vaginal, anal, or oral chancre (painless, punched-out lesion with a raised margin, lymphadenopathy)
Dx: darkfield microscopy, RPR/VDRL confirmed by FTA-ABS
Caused by spirochete Treponema pallidum
Tx: single IM injection of benzathine penicillin
Mnemonic: syphilis is painless ulcer
arabicExplanation:
ليش: القصة chancre مؤلم؟ لأ، هي painless ulcerative lesion 2 سم مع painless inguinal lymphadenopathy، وهاد بالضبط primary syphilis الناتج عن Treponema pallidum اللي يدخل بالcontact مباشر. الchancre يظهر بعد 2-3 أسابيع من التعرض، وممكن يصير بالpenis أو vagina أو rectum أو mouth. وما إنه الchancre يشفى لحاله بدون علاج، بس عدم العلاج بيخلي المرض يتقدم لsecondary وtertiary syphilis مع مضاعفات قلبية وعصبية، فالأساس بالنسبة لأغلب المرضى هو single dose of intramuscular penicillin.
الفخ: في طلاب يختاروا Oral penicillin لمدة أسبوع، بس الدواء الفموي مش الجواب القياسي، والخط الأول هو جرعة واحدة عضلية. والبديل الفموي بس للحساسية للpenicillin وهو doxycycline لمدة أسبوعين.

chapterTitle: Renal, Electrolyte, Acid–Base and Endocrine Emergencies
question: A patient presents with small-volume bleeding from an arteriovenous fistula used for dialysis. Which of the following is the most appropriate first step in managing the bleeding?

options.text: Apply tourniquets proximal and distal to the fistula site
Hold direct pressure with a finger for 5–10 minutes
Tightly apply a pressure dressing and leave in place for 1 hour
