question: A 28-year-old patient comes to the emergency department for evaluation of a "bump on my vagina" that has slowly increased in size over the past two months. For the past two weeks, it has caused them some discomfort when engaging in intercourse. Physical examination of the vulva shows mild distention of the right inferior labia majora. Palpation of the labia minora and this area via the vaginal introitus shows a 3 cm non-tender, soft mass located at the eight o'clock position. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Bartholin gland cyst
Expl anation
A. Bartholin gland cyst
Bartholin gland cysts are mucus-filled and occur on either side of the vaginal opening (4 0'clock or 8 0'clock positions). They are the most common large vulvar cysts.
Symptoms of larger cysts include vulvar irritation, dyspareunia, pain during walking, and vulvar asymmetry. Cysts can be managed conservatively with sitz baths and
analgesics. Patients can also get Bartholin gland abscesses, which are usually
painful, fluctuant, and red. Diagnosis is by physical examination. Large cysts and
abscesses require drainage and sometimes excision; abscesses may require antibi-
Otics.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK532271/
B. Gartner duct cyst
Gartner duct cysts develop from embryologic remnants of the Wolffian
(mesonephric) duct. They are located in the anterolateral wall of the proximal (superior) portion of the vagina and are typically located above the level of the inferiormost aspect of the pubic symphysis. They are typically small, asymptomatic cysts
that follow the course of the duct. However, they can enlarge to substantial proportions and be mistaken for urethral diverticulum or other structures.
C. Skene duct cyst
Skene duct cysts develop adjacent to the distal urethra, sometimes causing perineal
discharge, dyspareunia, urinary obstruction, or abscess formation. Cysts form if the
duct is obstructed, usually because the gland is infected. They occur mainly in
adults. Cysts may form abscesses or cause urethral obstruction and recurrent UTIs.
Most cysts are < 1 cm and asymptomatic. Some are larger and may cause
dyspareunia.
D. Vulvar cancer
Vulvar cancer is a malignant, invasive growth in the vulva. The disease accounts for
5% of gynecologic cancers in the United States with the majority (90%) being squamous cell carcinoma. The labia majora are the most common site involved representing about 50% of all cases, followed by the labia minora. Typically, a lesion
presents in the form of a firm lump or ulcer on the labia majora and may be associated with itching, irritation, local bleeding, or discharge, in addition to dysuria or
Page 2535 of 4185
dyspareunia. The labia minora, clitoris, perineum, and mons are less commonly
involved.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريضة عندها كتلة ناعمة 3 cm غير مؤلمة بمكان الساعة الثامنة عند فتحة المهبل، وهاد هو Bartholin gland cyst. الكيسة تتكون إما بجهة الساعة الرابعة أو الثامنة، وهي أشهر كيسة كبيرة بالفرج وتسبب dyspareunia وعدم تناسق بالفرج. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون Skene duct cyst أو Gartner، بس كيسة سكين تكون قريبة من الإحليل، وBartholin بالضبط عند الـ introitus، والفحص السريري يكفي للتشخيص.

question: A 17-year-old female presents with three days of vaginal pruritus and white vaginal discharge. It has worsened every day, and she is having a hard time sleeping from the discomfort at night. Body mass index is 23 kg/m². Temperature is 36.8°C (98.3°F), pulse rate is 74/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 124/78 mmHg. Which of the following laboratory tests is most likely to be abnormal?
englishExplanation:
KOH prep
Expl anation
A. Endocervical cultures
Endocervical cultures are typically used when there is a suspected bacterial infection (like a sexually transmitted infection) to determine the causative bacteria.
B. Gram stain
Gram stain is the laboratory method that can be used to test for bacterial vaginosis
and other vaginal infections, although it is rarely used in practice. Endocervical cultures or a saline wet mount are more commonly used for the diagnosis of vaginal
infections.
C. KOH prep
A KOH prep test will help to confirm the diagnosis of vaginal candidiasis, the most
likely cause of these clinical symptoms.
References: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK459317/
McKinzie J. Chapter 84. Sexually Transmitted Infections. In: Walls RM,
Hockberger RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and
Clinical Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
D. Tzanck smear
Tzanck smear would be indicated if this case presented with a lesion and herpes
simplex was suspected. The scrapings collected from the lesion could be viewed under a microscope for identification.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريضة عندها حكة وإفراز أبيض لثلاث أيام، وهاد يوحي vaginal candidiasis، والفحص الأنسب للتأكيد هو KOH prep. الـ KOH يبين budding yeast وhyphae ويأكد التشخيص، وهاد المرض هو الأكثر بهالأعراض. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون endocervical cultures، بس هذي للعدوى الجرثومية مثل الأمراض المنقولة جنسياً، أما الفطريات فتشخص بالـ KOH مش بالزرع.

question: A 24-year-old pregnant female at 22 weeks gestation with a history of migraine presents to the emergency department with 48 hours of headache. The headache came on gradually but has continued to progress, prompting her to seek evaluation. She denies fever, infectious symptoms, or trauma. Temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse rate is 85/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 145/80 mmHg. Oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Physical exam, including a complete neurologic exam, is unremarkable. The fetal heart rate is 140/min. The patient is given acetaminophen in triage with the resolution of her headache and is completely asymptomatic at this time. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
englishExplanation:
Expl anation
A. CT head
Urinalysis
This patient's elevated blood pressure is most concerning for pre-eclampsia and
should prompt further laboratory studies.
B. Discharge home with supportive care
This patient's elevated blood pressure is concerning for pre-eclampsia and should
prompt further studies.
C. MRI brain
This patient's elevated blood pressure is most concerning for pre-eclampsia and
should prompt further studies.
D. Urinalysis
Preeclampsia should be a consideration in all pregnant patients presenting with
headaches. The diagnostic workup should include a urinalysis to evaluate the presence of proteinuria, a complete blood count to evaluate for thrombocytopenia, and a
complete metabolic panel to assess for impaired liver function and renal function.
Elevated blood pressure with proteinuria is typically thought to be diagnostic
of preeclampsia, but it may not always be present. For those with new-onset hypertension but no proteinuria, other new-onset symptoms such as thrombocytopenia,
renal insufficiency, pulmonary edema, impaired liver function, or new-onset
headache may be used for diagnosis.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK570611/
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريضة حامل بـ 22 أسبوع وعندها صداع وضغط 145/80، وهاد يوحي preeclampsia فلازم نعمل urinalysis لنشوف proteinuria. التقييم كمان يشمل CBC للصفيحات وmetabolic panel لوظائف الكبد والكلى، لأن البروتين مع الضغط العالي هو الأساس للتشخيص. الفخ: في طلاب يطلبون MRI brain أو CT head، بس الضغط المرتفع هو الأهم هنا، والصداع بنت سياق يوجهنا لـ preeclampsia مش لسبب عصبي.

question: A 31-year-old gravida 3, para 2 woman who is at 28 weeks gestation presents to the ED because her blood pressure was elevated when she checked it at home. Temperature is 36.8°C (98.3°F), pulse rate is 74/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 156/100 mmHg. Oxygen saturation is 100%. Blood pressure at her most recent examination was 144/96 mmHg. Prior blood pressure readings were within normal limits. The patient does not have headaches, visual disturbances, or a history of seizures. Physical examination shows tenderness to palpation of the abdomen. The lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Physical examination also shows 2+ pitting edema and 2+ reflexes bilaterally. Results of complete blood cell count are within normal limits. A urine dipstick test shows 2+ protein. Based on this patient's presentation, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Preeclampsia
Expl anation
A. Essential hypertension
Given that this patient is pregnant and has not had prior blood pressure elevations
recorded prior to her pregnancy, she is best classified with the hypertensive disorder in pregnancy called preeclampsia.
B. Gestational hypertension
Given this patient's proteinuria, preeclampsia is the more correct answer choice.
Most women who have gestational hypertension, however, eventually develop
preeclampsia.
C. HELLP syndrome
Though this may be considered a subtype of preeclampsia, this patient's normal
liver enzymes and platelets make this an incorrect answer choice.
D. Preeclampsia
This patient has two elevated blood pressure readings (systolic blood pressure
greater than or equal to 140 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure greater than or
equal to 90 mm Hg) on two different occasions and greater than 1+ proteinuria after
20 weeks' gestation, which meets the criteria for preeclampsia.
References:
https:/,/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK570611/
Henn M, Lall M. Chapter 173. Complications of Pregnancy. In: Walls RM,
Hockberger RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and
Clinical Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريضة بقراءتين مرتفعتين للضغط فوق 140/90 بعد الأسبوع العشرين مع proteinuria 2+ بالـ urine dipstick، وهذا ضبط معايير preeclampsia. إضافة إن عندها 2+ pitting edema و2+ reflexes، والتحاليل CBC طبيعية فما في HELLP. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون gestational hypertension، بس وجود البروتين يرجح preeclampsia، وفيه طلاب يختارون HELLP بس الإنزيمات والصفيحات طبيعية.

question: A 31-year-old female with no past medical history presents with persistent, aching low back pain for 5 weeks. She denies trauma, fever, or constitutional symptoms, and states that the pain is constant and nonradiating. She has associated nausea but no vomiting. She denies urinary symptoms, vaginal bleeding, or discharge. She denies weakness, numbness, or incontinence. She has been taking acetaminophen with temporary relief. Vital signs are within normal limits. Abdominal and back exam are unremarkable. Neurologic exam, including strength, sensation, coordination, and gait is unremarkable. Urine pregnancy test results positive, of which patient was unaware. Pelvic exam is unremarkable. Blood type is O, Rh positive. Serum beta-hCG results 6200mIU/mL. Transabdominal ultrasound reveals an intrauterine yolk sac within a gestational sac. What is the next best step in management of this patient?
englishExplanation:
Supportive care
Expl anation
A. Lumbosacral xray series with shielding
There is no indication for lumbosacral plain radiographs in this patient with an unremarkable exam, lack of red flags, and alternate explanation for low back pain.
B. RhoGAM administration
There is no indication for RhoGAM administration in an Rh-positive patient, especially without concern for bleeding.
C. Supportive care
This patient is presenting with an incidental intrauterine pregnancy without vaginal
bleeding and without concern for ectopic pregnancy. There is no suspicion of appendicitis, urinary tract infection, spinal infection, or trauma in the question stem
to suggest further workup. Supportive care with acetaminophen for pain control
and appropriate follow-up is reasonable at this time.
Further information: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2684210/
D. Transvaginal ultrasound
There is no indication for transvaginal ultrasound in a patient with a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy by transabdominal ultrasound.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريضة عندها ألم أسفل الظهر وطلع حمل داخل الرحم بالصدفة، شفناه بالـ transabdominal ultrasound على شكل yolk sac داخل gestational sac. ما في نزيف مهبلي ولا شك بأكتوبي، وعندها blood type موجب Rh فما في داعي لـ RhoGAM، فالمتابعة الداعمة مع acetaminophen كافية. الفخ: في طلاب يطلبون transvaginal ultrasound لنفي ectopic، بس صار في دليل على intrauterine pregnancy بالفحص الحالي فخلص الموضوع.

question: A 17-year-old girl presents because she has had recurrent pelvic pain for the past 15 months that worsens each month prior to menstruation and improves afterward. Ibuprofen has not provided relief from the pain. The patient had menarche at 12 years of age and generally has regular menstrual periods. She is not sexually active. Temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), pulse rate is 82/min, and blood pressure is 98/55 mmHg. Physical examination of the abdomen and the external genitalia are normal. The vaginal mucosa and cervix appear normal. A tender nodule is palpated in the rectovaginal fascia. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line therapy for this patient's condition?
englishExplanation:
Combined oral contraceptive pills
Expl anation

This patient is presenting with endometriosis, a common benign disorder in which

the uterus. Endometrial tissue is most often found on the pelvic peritoneum,
ovaries, and uterosacral ligaments, although endometrial implants can occur anywhere in the abdomen or pelvis. Symptoms of chronic pelvic pain are common.

question: An 18-year-old female presents to the emergency department with vaginal bleeding for three days. Her urine pregnancy test is positive. Which of the following ultrasound findings would allow you to send this patient home with appropriate obstetrics-gynecology follow-up?

Intrauterine gestational sac with a yolk sac

A. Corpus luteal cyst
The patient has a positive pregnancy test and abdominal pain. The important diagnosis that needs to be ruled out in the emergency department is an ectopic pregnancy. An ectopic pregnancy is effective ruled out by positive identification of an intrauterine pregnancy, of which a gestational sac and a yolk sac need to be visualized
on ultrasound.
B. Free fluid in the pouch of Douglas
The pouch of Douglas is an anatomical structure that is a bag-shaped extension of
the peritoneum located between the posterior wall of the uterus and the
rectum. Free fluid in the pouch of Douglas would be highly concerning for a ruptured ectopic pregnancy.
C. Intrauterine gestational sac with a yolk sac
The patient has a positive pregnancy test and abdominal pain. An ectopic pregnancy
is an important diagnosis that needs to be ruled out in the emergency department.

on ultrasound.

question: A 19-year-old woman, gravida 1 para 0, at 32 weeks' gestation is brought to the emergency department by ambulance because of vaginal bleeding and cramping abdominal pain for the past hour. There is no history of any trauma. She smokes 5-10 cigarettes per day. Temperature is 37ºC (98.6º), pulse rate is 90/min, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg. Which of the following conditions is the most likely given this patient's clinical manifestations?
englishExplanation:
Abruptio placentae
Explanation
A. Abruptio placentae
Abruptio placentae (placental abruption) is defined as the premature separation of
the placenta from the uterus. Patients with abruptio placentae typically present with
vaginal bleeding, uterine contractions, and fetal distress. A significant cause of third
trimester bleeding associated with fetal and maternal morbidity and mortality, placental abruption must be considered whenever bleeding is encountered in the second half of pregnancy. Some risk factors include maternal hypertension (44% of
cases), trauma, smoking, alcohol and cocaine use. Before a pelvic examination can
be safely performed, an ultrasonographic examination should be performed to ex-
Clude placenta previa.
Reference:
Henn M, Lall M. Chapter 173. Complications of Pregnancy. In: Walls RM,
Hockberger RS, Gausche-Hill M, et al. Rosen's Emergency Medicine Concepts and
Clinical Practice. 10th ed. Philadelphia: Elsevier; 2023.
B. Placenta accreta
Placenta accreta is an abnormally adherent placenta, resulting in delayed delivery of
the placenta. Placental villi are not contained by uterine decidual cells, but rather
extend to the myometrium. Placental function is normal, but trophoblastic invasion
extends beyond the normal boundary (Nitabuch layer). In such cases, unless meticulous manual removal of the placenta is performed, massive postpartum hemorrhage may result. Prenatal diagnosis is by ultrasonography. Treatment is usually
with scheduled cesarean hysterectomy between 34 0/7 to 35 6/7 weeks' gestation,
before the patient goes into labor on her own.
C. Placenta previa
Placenta previa is a condition that classically presents as painless vaginal bleeding
in the second or third trimester and is secondary to an abnormal placentation near
or covering the internal cervical os.
D. Vasa previa
Vasa previa is a complication in which fetal blood vessels cross or run near the internal cervical os. These vessels are at risk of rupture when the supporting mem-
Page 2591 of 4185
branes rupture, as they are unsupported by the umbilical cord or placental tissue.
The classic triad of vasa previa is membrane rupture, painless vaginal bleeding, and
fetal bradycardia.

question: An 18-year-old woman complains of dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and abnormal vaginal discharge. Cultures are performed and return showing Gram-negative diplococci. question: A 22-year-old patient, currently 16 weeks pregnant, presents complaining of burning with urination and increased frequency over the last few days. options to treat acute cystitis in pregnancy include amoxicillin-clavulanate and
cefpodoxime.

question: A 20-year-old woman presents asking to be tested for an STI. She was recently with a new sexual partner and has noticed some mild discharge. The pelvic examination reveals no cervical motion tenderness. What is the most appropriate management at this time?

question: What is the most common risk factor for developing cervical cancer?
englishExplanation: Cervical cancer is most commonly associated with HPV infection. HPV is detected in 99.7% of cervical cancers. question: A 47-year-old patient presents with abnormal vaginal bleeding. CT shows probable advanced cervical cancer with spread to the bladder and rectum. What is the best initial approach to starting a conversation with the patient about the CT results?

question: What is the most common risk factor for developing pelvic inflammatory disease?

question: What is the most appropriate disposition for a well-appearing patient who is 10 weeks' pregnant and has been diagnosed with pelvic inflammatory disease?

question: Which combination of antibiotics is appropriate when treating perihepatitis?

The regimen of cefotetan and doxycycline is recommended by the CDC to treat severe PID in the inpatient setting. Cefotetan covers N. gonorrhoeae and anaerobes; doxycycline covers C. trachomatis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: علاج الـ perihepatitis بيعتمد على الـ antimicrobial therapy لعلاج الـ pelvic inflammatory disease الأساسي. والـ regimen الموصى فيه من الـ CDC لعلاج الـ PID الشديد في الـ inpatient setting هو cefotetan مع doxycycline. والـ cefotetan بيغطي N. gonorrhoeae والـ anaerobes، بينما الـ doxycycline بيغطي C. trachomatis.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون levofloxacin مع metronidazole لأنه option معروف للـ PID، بس هاد للـ outpatient، والـ regimen المطلوب هون للـ severe inpatient PID هو cefotetan مع doxycycline.

question: Which complication is associated with the underlying cause of perihepatitis?
englishExplanation: Perihepatitis is a complication of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) that ascends from the genital tract into the peritoneal cavity. Other associated complications of PID include pyosalpinx, hydrosalpinx, pyometra, tubo-ovarian abscess, tubal damage resulting in ectopic pregnancy or infertility, and adhesions.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ perihepatitis هي مضاعفة للـ pelvic inflammatory disease اللي تصعد من الـ genital tract على الـ peritoneal cavity. ومن مضاعفات الـ PID التانية الـ pyosalpinx والـ hydrosalpinx والـ pyometra والـ tubo-ovarian abscess، بالإضافة لتلف الـ fallopian tube اللي بيؤدي لـ ectopic pregnancy أو infertility، والـ adhesions.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون cirrhosis أو hepatocellular carcinoma لأنهم يربطوا المرض بالكبد، بس الـ perihepatitis ما بتسبب تلف كبدي، والمضاعفة المرتبطة بالمرض الأساسي هي الـ tubo-ovarian abscess.

question: A 21-year-old woman presents with right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She states she was exposed to chlamydia in the past but it never bothered her. The patient is stable, and the pain and nausea are well-controlled. A pregnancy test is negative, and CT imaging is unremarkable. What is the appropriate disposition for this patient?
englishExplanation: This patient has signs, symptoms, and physical examination findings that are consistent with perihepatitis (also known as Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome) as a result of untreated pelvic inflammatory disease. The mainstay of treatment is similar to the treatment of PID: antibiotics, analgesia, and antiemetics. Disposition decisions are based on the patient's clinical condition. She can be discharged with oral antibiotics if stable.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها علامات وأعراض وفحص سريري متوافقة مع perihepatitis أو Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome ناتجة عن pelvic inflammatory disease غير معالجة. والعلاج الأساسي شبيه بعلاج الـ PID وهو antibiotics مع analgesia و antiemetics. وقرار الـ disposition بيعتمد على الحالة السريرية للمريضة، وبما إنها مستقرة والألم والغثيان مسيطر عليهم فبتنصرف مع oral antibiotics.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون admit with intravenous antibiotics لأنهم يربطوا الالتهاب الكبدي بالخطورة، بس الاستقرار السريري وعدم وجود abscess أو sepsis بيسمح بالعلاج الفموي بالبيت.

question: What is the most common symptom in patients presenting with epithelial ovarian cancer?
englishExplanation: Bloating, abdominal or pelvic pain, early satiety or decreased appetite, and urinary urgency or frequency are the most common presenting symptoms in epithelial ovarian cancer. Patients at highest risk for ovarian cancer are those over the age of 40 with a family history of ovarian cancer.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: من أكثر الأعراض شيوعاً في الـ epithelial ovarian cancer هو الـ bloating، مع ألم في الـ abdomen أو الـ pelvis، والشبع المبكر أو قلة الشهية، والurgency أو frequency بالتبول. والمرضى الأكثر عرضة للـ ovarian cancer هم اللي أعمارهم فوق 40 سنة وعندهم family history of ovarian cancer.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون vaginal bleeding لأنهم يربطوا أورام الـ gynecologic بالنزيف، بس النزيف مش من أكثر الأعراض، والـ bloating هو الأكثر شيوعاً بالـ epithelial ovarian cancer.

question: A 64-year-old has a CT scan showing a 10-cm mass on the right ovary that is concerning for epithelial ovarian cancer. Although the pain was initially minimal, the patient suddenly reports an abrupt worsening of severe right pelvic pain with worsened tenderness to palpation on the right. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Give the patient a prescription for oral pain medication
Obtain a pelvic ultrasound with ovarian Doppler
Obtain a serum beta hCG test
Repeat the CT of the abdomen and pelvis

correctAnswer: Obtain a pelvic ultrasound with ovarian Doppler
englishExplanation: Given this patient's large ovarian mass and abrupt worsening of abdominal pain, there should be concern for ovarian torsion. The diagnostic modality of choice in this setting would be ovarian Doppler ultrasound.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها كتلة كبيرة على الـ right ovary بحجم 10 سم، ومع التدهور المفاجئ والشديد بالألم لازم نفكر بالـ ovarian torsion. والفحص التشخيصي الأمثل في هالحالة هو الـ pelvic ultrasound مع الـ ovarian Doppler. وهذا بيفرق بين وجود torsion أو احتباس دم بالكتلة قبل أي إجراء تاني.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون مسكنات فموية أو إعادة الـ CT، بس الـ CT ما بيقيم التدفق الدموي، والـ Doppler ultrasound هو اللي بيشخص الـ torsion وبيغير قرار العلاج فوراً.

question: Consideration of what diagnosis is necessary in adolescents who present with abnormal heavy uterine bleeding soon after menarche?
englishExplanation: Heavy uterine bleeding in the adolescent age group at the time of menarche may indicate a bleeding disorder and possibly be the patient's first sign of this diagnosis. Physicians should inquire about a family history of bleeding disorders and a history of excessive bleeding or bruising.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: النزيف الرحمي الشديد عند المراهقات وقت الـ menarche ممكن يكون علامة على وجود bleeding disorder، وممكن يكون أول عرض للتشخيص. فلازم نسأل المريضة عن تاريخ عائلي لأمراض النزيف وعن تاريخ نزيف زائد أو كدمات سهلة. وهذا مهم جداً حتى ما نفوّت التشخيص ونعالج السبب من بدايته.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون polyps أو leiomyomas لأنهم أسباب شائعة للنزيف، بس بعمر المراهقة وقرابة الـ menarche، الـ bleeding disorders هي الاحتمال اللي لازم نفكر فيه أول.

question: Which medication is the first-line treatment for pelvic pain due to endometriosis?
englishExplanation: The first-line treatment for pelvic pain due to endometriosis is an estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive. Endometriosis is the implantation of endometrial tissue outside the endometrial cavity, and it is a common cause of pelvic pain in women.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: العلاج الأول لآلام الحوض الناتجة عن endometriosis هو estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive. والـ endometriosis هي انغراس نسيج الـ endometrium خارج تجويف الـ endometrium، وهي سبب شائع لألم الحوض عند النساء. والـ oral contraceptive بيقلل نمو النسيج المنغرز وبيخفف الأعراض بشكل فعال.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون الـ gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist أو aromatase inhibitor، بس هدول خط تاني أو للحالات اللي ما استجابت، والـ first-line هو الـ estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive.

question: An 80-year-old woman presents with pressure in her pelvis that is worsened by standing up or bearing down. She has not had any surgeries and has four grown children. She is otherwise asymptomatic; she denies dysuria, urinary dribbling, vaginal bleeding, and abdominal pain. A descending soft circular mass is discovered within the vagina on pelvic examination. What is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation: Patients with uterine prolapse typically complain of pelvic pressure that is worse with standing up or bearing down. The symptoms get better when the patient lies down. On pelvic examination, the uterus is seen coming down into the center of the vagina.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: مريضات الـ uterine prolapse عادةً يشتكون من ضغط بالحوض بيزيد مع الوقوف أو الشد، وبيتحسن لما تستلقي المريضة. وعند الفحص البطني الحوضي، الـ uterus بينشاف نازل على مركز الـ vagina، وهاد متوافق مع كتلة نازلة دائرية طرية داخل الـ vagina عند مريضة عندها أربع أولاد وما عملت جراحات.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون cystocele أو rectocele لأنها prolapse تانية، بس النازل هون بالمركز وبيعطي كتلة دائرية طرية، وهذا بيميز الـ uterine prolapse عن الـ cystocele اللي تكون أمامية.

question: A hemodynamically stable 36-year-old woman with a history of uterine leiomyomas presents with heavy vaginal bleeding and a Hgb of 5.2. She is a Jehovah's witness and declines blood transfusion. She demonstrates understanding of the risk of refusing transfusion, including death, and shows you an advance directive stating her wishes. What should be included in the documentation regarding the discussion with the patient?

options.text: Case was discussed with elders from the patient's church
Discussion was held and patient has capacity to understand risks, including death
Informed consent is unnecessary, as the patient will likely die

correctAnswer: Discussion was held and patient has capacity to understand risks, including death
englishExplanation: When a patient refuses a recommended treatment, the physician must document that a conversation was had with the patient, explaining treatment options and risks and benefits, and that the patient appeared to have capacity to understand the risk of refusing treatment, including death if applicable.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لما يرفض المريض علاج موصى فيه، لازم الطبيب يوثق إنه صار نقاش مع المريض وشرح خيارات العلاج والفوائد والمخاطر. ولازم يكون مكتوب إن المريض باين إنه عنده capacity يفهم خطر رفض العلاج، وبيشمل ذكر الوفاة إذا كان هذا الاحتمال موجوداً. عندنا مريضة Jehovah's witness رافضة نقل الدم وواضحة وقادرة تفهم المخاطر.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون إنه informed consent غير ضروري لأن المريضة غالباً رح تموت، بس هاد غلط لأن موافقة المريض القادر موثقة هي الأساس القانوني بتصرف الطبيب.

question: Which finding is most consistent with a molar pregnancy?

options.text: Elevated fetal heart rate on Doppler assessment
Uterus that is larger than expected based on dates

correctAnswer: Uterus that is larger than expected based on dates
englishExplanation: A molar pregnancy is a type of gestational trophoblastic disease characterized by disordered proliferation of chorionic villi. Clues to the diagnosis include a uterine size that is larger than expected based on dates, preeclampsia before 24 weeks' gestation, higher-than-expected levels of serum beta-hCG, and lack of audible fetal heart tones.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ molar pregnancy هي نوع من الـ gestational trophoblastic disease وبتتميز بفرط تكاثر غير منظم بالـ chorionic villi. ومن الأدلة على التشخيص إن حجم الـ uterus أكبر من المتوقع حسب الـ dates، بحيث بيجي قبل 24 أسبوع من الحمل، مع مستويات serum beta-hCG أعلى من المتوقع وبغياب أصوات قلب الجنين.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون إن الـ beta-hCG أقل من المتوقع، بس العكس صحيح، بالـ molar pregnancy بيكون الـ beta-hCG أعلى، والفرق هون بيميز المرض بشكل مباشر.

question: What is the most common organism isolated from Bartholin gland abscesses?
englishExplanation: Although many Bartholin abscesses are polymicrobial, Escherichia coli is the most common pathogen isolated. Bacteria that cause STIs, such as Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, are also frequently isolated.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: على الرغم من إن أغلب abscesses الـ Bartholin gland بتكون polymicrobial، لكن أكثر pathogen بينعزل هو Escherichia coli. والجراثيم اللي بتسبب الـ STIs متل Chlamydia trachomatis و Neisseria gonorrhoeae بتنعزل بتردد عالي كمان، لكنها ما هي الأكثر بينعزل بالـ Bartholin abscesses.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون Neisseria gonorrhoeae أو Chlamydia trachomatis لأنهم يربطوا المنطقة بالـ STIs، بس الأكثر عزل هو E. coli، فانتبه لكلمة most common بالـ stem.

question: What is the best management for a painless Bartholin cyst that is less than 3 cm in size?
englishExplanation: Small Bartholin cysts, which are usually painless, may be managed expectantly. Sitz baths and warm compresses may encourage drainage. If the cyst is large or painful, it may be treated with incision and drainage.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ Bartholin cysts الصغيرة اللي عادةً تكون غير مؤلمة ممكن تدار بشكل expectant. وكمادات دافئة وحمامات sit baths ممكن تشجع على التصريف. وإذا كان الكيس كبيرة أو مؤلم، وقتها ممكن نعالجه بـ incision and drainage. والمريضة هون عندها كيس غير مؤلم وحجمه أقل من 3 سم، فالـ expectant management هو الأنسب.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون marsupialization أو word catheter placement، بس هدول للإجراءات الأكثر تدخلاً وبينلجأوا لهم إذا كان الكيس كبير أو متكرر أو مؤلم.

question: An 18-year-old woman has been diagnosed with pelvic inflammatory disease. She has an IUD in place, and she is not pregnant. Her vital signs are stable, and she is able to tolerate oral medications. What is the correct next step in management?

options.text: Leave the IUD in place; discharge after giving intramuscular and oral antibiotics
Leave the IUD in place; hospitalize and give intravenous antibiotics
Remove the IUD; discharge after giving intramuscular and oral antibiotics
Remove the IUD; hospitalize and give intravenous antibiotics

correctAnswer: Leave the IUD in place; discharge after giving intramuscular and oral antibiotics
englishExplanation: According to the CDC, there is insufficient evidence to support IUD removal in cases of PID. The presence of an IUD does not change the recommended antibiotic regimen. Stable patients with PID can be discharged with intramuscular and oral antibiotics.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: حسب الـ CDC ما في أدلة كافية بتدعم إزالة الـ IUD في حالات الـ pelvic inflammatory disease. ووجود الـ IUD ما بيغير الـ antibiotic regimen الموصى فيها. والمريضة الـ stable واللي بتتحمل الأدوية الفموية ممكن تنصرف مع intramuscular and oral antibiotics بدون ما نشيل الـ IUD.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون إزالة الـ IUD لأنهم يعتقدوا إنه مصدر الالتهاب، بس التوصية الحديثة هي تركه مكانه لأن إزالته ما بتغير النتائج والعلاج واحد.

question: A 20-year-old woman presents with nausea, vomiting, and lower abdominal pain. She underwent methotrexate treatment for an ectopic pregnancy 7 days earlier. At that initial visit, her beta-hCG level was 12,121 mIU/mL. What is the next step in this patient?

options.text: Consult OB for likely ruptured ectopic pregnancy from treatment failure
Discharge home as this is the normal response to methotrexate therapy
Give a second dose of methotrexate
Treat supportively with pain control and antiemetics

correctAnswer: Consult OB for likely ruptured ectopic pregnancy from treatment failure
englishExplanation: Methotrexate is a nonsurgical treatment option for unruptured ectopic pregnancies and should be given to patients with beta-hCG levels less than 5,000 mIU/mL. When given to patients with higher levels, the risk of treatment failure is much greater. Any patient presenting with abdominal pain following methotrexate therapy requires an ultrasound to rule out a ruptured ectopic pregnancy.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ methotrexate هو خيار علاج غير جراحي للـ unruptured ectopic pregnancy، ولازم ينعطى لمرضى مستويات الـ beta-hCG أقل من 5,000 mIU/mL. وهنا كان مستوى المريضة 12,121 mIU/mL وهو مرتفع، فخطر فشل العلاج أكبر بكثير. وأي مريضة تجي بألم بطني بعد علاج الـ methotrexate لازم تعمل ultrasound لاستبعاد ruptured ectopic pregnancy.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون مسكنات و antiemetics ويعتبرون الألم جزء طبيعي من العلاج، بس الألم بعد الـ methotrexate بينبهنا لاحتمال rupture ولازم استشارة OB فوراً.

question: What history and examination findings are most common in a patient with ectopic pregnancy?
englishExplanation: Abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding are the most common symptoms of ectopic pregnancy, with 90% of patients presenting with abdominal pain. Risk factors include history of PID, STI, ectopic pregnancy, smoking, tubal surgery, or pharmacologic abortion; IUD in place; age >35; and assisted reproductive technologies.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: ألم البطن والنزيف المهبلي هما أكثر الأعراض شيوعاً في الـ ectopic pregnancy، بحيث 90% من المريضات بيجوا بألم بطني. ومن عوامل الخطر تاريخ الـ PID أو الـ STI أو ectopic pregnancy سابقة أو التدخين أو جراحة الـ tubal أو الإجهاض الدوائي، ووجود IUD، والعمر فوق 35 سنة، وتقنيات الإنجاب المساعدة.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون missed menstrual period أو shoulder pain، بس انقطاع الدورة مش من أكثر العروض الموثقة هون، وألم الكتف بيشير لتهيج بريتوني متأخر، والأكثر شيوعاً هو ألم البطن.

question: A 38-year-old G1P0 woman who is 6 weeks pregnant presents with vaginal bleeding and cramping. What is the most likely diagnosis based on this ultrasound image?
englishExplanation: This ultrasound shows an adnexal mass, which is concerning for ectopic pregnancy. Ectopic pregnancy is one of the most important things to consider in a female patient of reproductive age with vaginal bleeding or abdominal pain. Risk factors include history of PID, STI, ectopic pregnancy, smoking, tubal surgery, or pharmacologic abortion.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ ultrasound بيبين adnexal mass، وهذا مقلق جداً لوجود ectopic pregnancy. والـ ectopic pregnancy من أهم التشخيصات اللي لازم نفكر فيها عند أي أنثى بعمر الإنجاب عندها نزيف مهبلي أو ألم بطني. ومن عوامل الخطر تاريخ الـ PID أو الـ STI أو ectopic pregnancy سابقة أو التدخين أو جراحة الـ tubal أو الإجهاض الدوائي.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون threatened miscarriage بسبب النزيف والتقلصات، بس وجود الكتلة بالـ adnexa وعدم وجود حمل داخل الرحم هو اللي بيرجح الـ ectopic pregnancy.

question: When discharging a patient for pregnancy of unknown location, what is most important to document to support a plan of outpatient expectant management?

options.text: No intrauterine pregnancy was identified on ultrasound
Patient has had previous miscarriages and in vitro fertilization
Patient is willing and able to comply with close follow-up care
Serum beta hCG level is low

correctAnswer: Patient is willing and able to comply with close follow-up care
englishExplanation: Some pregnant patients with undiagnosed vaginal bleeding or abdominal pain are referred to as patients with “pregnancy of unknown location.” It is important to have a discussion with the patient to determine that she understands the clinical implications and risks of ectopic pregnancy and that she has access to close follow-up care.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بعض الحوامل اللي عندهم نزيف مهبلي غير مشخص أو ألم بطني بينسموا مرضى pregnancy of unknown location. والمهم هون إنه يصير نقاش مع المريضة نتأكد فيه إنها فاهمة المضاعفات السريرية ومخاطر الـ ectopic pregnancy، وإنها قادرة توصل لمتابعة قريبة. فالتوثيق الأهم هو رغبة المريضة وقدرتها على الالتزام بالـ close follow-up care.
الفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون إن مستوى الـ beta-hCG منخفض أو عدم رؤية حمل داخل الرحم، بس هدول نتائج فحص ما بتدعم خطة الـ outpatient expectant management، واللي بيدعمها هو التزام المريضة بالمتابعة.

question: What is a laboratory finding of HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets) syndrome?
englishExplanation: HELLP syndrome consists of hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets. Evidence of hemolysis can be seen on the peripheral blood smear with the presence of schistocytes, elevated LDH, and increased bilirubin. Increases in the transaminases are also noted.
arabicExplanation: ليش: متلازمة HELLP معناها hemolysis وانزيمات كبد عالية وصفيحات قليلة، وعلامات التحلل الدموي بتظهر على شريحة الدم المحيطي بشكل schistocytes، وكل هاد يرفع الـ LDH ويزيد البيليروبين. فرفع الـ LDH هو أحد الفحوصات المخبرية المتوقعة، لأنه بيدل على تكسر الكريات الحمراء الي بصير بالمرض. كذلك بيلاحظ ارتفاع في إنزيمات transaminases، وهاد كله بيمشي مع الصورة السريرية للمريضة. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون Normal antithrombin III لأنه بفكروا إنها علامة مميزة للمتلازمة، لكن الحقيقة إنها ما بتدل عليها، والعلامة الأدق هي ارتفاع LDH مع التحلل الدموي.

question: A 31-year-old woman presents with seizures. She is 3 weeks postpartum. Her vital signs include BP 160/110, P 95, and T 37.1°C (98.8°F); SpO2 is 94% on room air. What medication should be given first?
englishExplanation: This patient's presentation is suggestive of eclampsia, which can occur in the third trimester of pregnancy or up to 4 weeks postpartum. The initial treatment of eclampsia is magnesium sulfate 4 to 6 g IV, followed by infusion at 1 to 2 g/hr.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريضة عندها تشنجات مع ضغط 160/110 وهي بعد الولادة بثلاث أسابيع، وهاد بيمشي مع eclampsia الي بتصير بالثلث الثالث أو لحتى أربعة أسابيع بعد الولادة. والعلاج الأولي للـ eclampsia هو magnesium sulfate بجرعة أربعة لستة غرامات وريدياً، وبعدها تسريب بمعدل واحد لاثنين غرام بالساعة. فلهيك magnesium sulfate هو الدواء الأول قبل أي شي تاني. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Phenytoin لأنه مضاد اختلاج معروف، لكنه ما هو العلاج الأول للـ eclampsia، والـ magnesium sulfate هو الأساس لضبط التشنجات.

question: A previously healthy, nulliparous 32-year-old woman at 35 weeks' gestation presents with a new-onset headache. She has no vision changes, confusion, or abdominal pain, and acetaminophen provided no relief. Her vital signs are BP 165/95, P 87, R 14, and T 36.9°C (98.4°F), and her neurologic examination is normal. What is the best next step?

options.text: Confirm blood pressure and then administer labetalol 20 mg IV
Consult obstetrics to perform an emergency cesarean section
Order a STAT CT scan of the brain

correctAnswer: Confirm blood pressure and then administer labetalol 20 mg IV
englishExplanation: Preeclampsia with severe features needs to be treated emergently. Women who present after 20 weeks' gestation with severe hypertension have preeclampsia with severe features. Labetalol, hydralazine, nifedipine, and nicardipine are all appropriate. Magnesium sulfate infusion should also be initiated for seizure prophylaxis.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريضة حامل بـ 35 أسبوع وعندها صداع جديد وضغط 165/95، وهاد بيمشي مع preeclampsia with severe features، والحالة لازم تتعالج بشكل طارئ. فلازم أول شي نتأكد من قراءة الضغط ومن ثم نعطي labetalol 20 mg وريدياً، لأنه من الأدوية المناسبة مع hydralazine وnifedipine وnicardipine. كذلك لازم نبدأ تسريب magnesium sulfate للوقاية من التشنجات. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون CT للدماغ بسبب الصداع، لكن الضغط العالي بالحمل هو الأهم، وقراءة الضغط لازم تتأكد قبل إعطاء الدواء.

question: In a pregnant trauma patient, administration of Rh(D) immune globulin helps prevent which complication?
englishExplanation: Any pregnant patient who is Rh negative and who presents following abdominal trauma should receive a dose of Rh(D) immune globulin. This intervention prevents Rh isoimmunization from a fetal-maternal hemorrhage. This complication can lead to fetal hydrops, a life-threatening accumulation of excessive fluid.
arabicExplanation: ليش: أي حامل Rh negative بتجي بعد رض على البطن لازم تاخد جرعة Rh(D) immune globulin، لأنها تمنع Rh isoimmunization الناتجة عن نزف بين الجنين والأم. وهالمضاعفة بتقدر توصل لـ fetal hydrops الي هو تجمع خطير للسوائل بالجنين ويهدد حياته. فإعطاء الجلوبيولين بيمنع هالتسلسل من أصله. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Placental abruption لأنها مضاعفة رض شائعة، لكن الجلوبيولين ما يمنعها، هو بالتحديد يمنع التحسس عند الجنين الي بيسبب fetal hydrops.

question: A 26-year-old woman presents with 2 hours of mild vaginal bleeding and abdominal cramping pain. She is 6 weeks and 5 days pregnant. Her beta-hCG level is 1,756 mIU/mL. What is the most appropriate diagnostic test?
englishExplanation: This patient requires an emergent ultrasound to rule out an ectopic pregnancy. A transvaginal approach is most appropriate because her beta-hCG level is above the discriminatory zone for visualization of an intrauterine pregnancy by transvaginal ultrasound.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريضة عندها نزيف مهبلي خفيف ومغص وعمر الحمل ستة أسابيع وخمسة أيام، ورقم الـ beta-hCG هو 1,756، وهالرقم فوق الـ discriminatory zone لرؤية الحمل داخل الرحم. فالحالة بدها ultrasound طارئ لاستبعاد ectopic pregnancy، والطريق المهبلي هو الأنسب لأنه يعطي رؤية أوضح بهالعمر المبكر. لهيك transvaginal ultrasound هو الفحص الأنسب. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون Urinalysis لأنها سهلة وسريعة، لكنها ما بتشوف مكان الحمل، والهدف الأساسي هنا نفي الحمل خارج الرحم بالتصوير.

question: A 29-year-old patient at 20 weeks' gestation is newly diagnosed with diabetes for high blood sugar. What best describes this patient's diabetic condition?
englishExplanation: According to the American Diabetes Association (ADA), gestational diabetes is diabetes that is newly diagnosed during pregnancy (typically after 15 weeks gestation) that was not present prior to pregnancy. Typically patients are screened early with Hgb A1C and undergo a glucose tolerance test around 24 weeks.
arabicExplanation: ليش: حسب الـ ADA، الـ gestational diabetes هي السكري الي يتشخص لأول مرة أثناء الحمل بالعادة بعد 15 أسبوع، وما كان موجود قبل الحمل. وهالمريضة تشخصت بسكري جديد بعمر حمل 20 أسبوع، فالوصف الأدق لحالتها هو gestational diabetes. بالعادة يتم الفحص المبكر بـ HbA1c وبعدها glucose tolerance test حول 24 أسبوع. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Type II diabetes لأن السكر مرتفع، لكن السكري ما كان موجود قبل الحمل، ولهيك التصنيف الصح هو سكري الحمل.

question: A 37-year-old patient who is G3P2003 with a single-gestation pregnancy is being evaluated. She has a history of seasonal allergies, irritable bowel syndrome, and a prior full-term twin pregnancy. What feature makes this patient's pregnancy high risk?
englishExplanation: High-risk criteria for pregnancy include age of 35 years or older, current multiple gestation pregnancy, significant preexisting conditions, development of a condition during pregnancy, history of complications with prior pregnancies or deliveries, and substance abuse during pregnancy.
arabicExplanation: ليش: معايير الحمل عالي الخطورة تشمل عمر 35 سنة أو أكثر، وحمل متعدد حالي، وأمراض مزمنة مهمة، وحدوث حالة مرضية أثناء الحمل، ومضاعفات بحمل سابق، وتعاطي مواد أثناء الحمل. والمريضة عمرها 37 سنة، فهاد لحاله بيعتبر عامل خطورة أساسي حتى لو كانت حامل بجنين واحد وهي G3P2003. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون حمل التوأم السابق لأنهم بفكروا إنه خطورة، لكنه كان سابق وليس الحمل الحالي، والمعيار المطبق هنا هو العمر فوق 35.

question: If a pregnant patient has preexisting obesity, which complication is most likely to occur with the baby?
englishExplanation: Fetal macrosomia (increased fetus size) is a well-established risk associated with maternal obesity. Maternal obesity is associated with numerous pregnancy complications and birth defects, including miscarriage, gestational diabetes, pregnancy-associated hypertension, preeclampsia, fetal macrosomia, congenital abnormalities, and increased risk of requiring a Cesarean section.
arabicExplanation: ليش: السمنة عند الأم مرتبطة بمضاعفات حمل متعددة وعيوب خلقية، ومن ضمنها الإجهاض وسكري الحمل وارتفاع الضغط المرتبط بالحمل والـ preeclampsia. كمان بترتبط بـ fetal macrosomia الي معناه زيادة حجم الجنين، وهي من المضاعفات المتوقعة على الطفل. كذلك بترفع احتمالية الولادة القيصرية. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Gastroschisis أو عيوب خلقية، لكن السؤال بيسأل عن الأكثر ارتباطاً، والـ fetal macrosomia هي الأكثر ثباتاً مع سمنة الأم.

question: What finding is most strongly associated with rupture of the amniotic sac?
englishExplanation: The approach to confirming rupture of membranes has three components: pooling of amniotic fluid in the vaginal vault, a positive nitrazine test result, and crystallization (or "ferning") revealed on microscopic analysis of amniotic fluid. Ferning is the most specific for amniotic sac rupture.
arabicExplanation: ليش: تشخيص تمزق أغشية السائل الأمنيوسي بعتمد على ثلاث مكونات، وهي تجمع السائل بالمهبل، وإيجابية test النيترازين، وظهور التبلور أو ferning عند فحص السائل بالميكروسكوب. والفيرنينغ هو الأكثر خصوصية لتمزق كيس السائل الأمنيوسي، يعني لو ظهر بنكون شبه متأكدين من التشخيص. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون Nitrazine paper turning red، لكن ورقة النيترازين بتتحول للأزرق مع السائل الأمنيوسي وليست حمراء، وأيضاً هي أقل خصوصية من الفيرنينغ.

question: What is the most common etiology of uterine rupture?
englishExplanation: Uterine rupture is a complete division of all three layers of the uterus and is associated with high maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. Prior cesarean section is the most common etiology of uterine rupture.
arabicExplanation: ليش: تمزق الرحم هو انفصال كامل لطبقاته الثلاث، ومرتبط بنسبة عالية من الاعتلال والوفاة للأم والجنين. وأكثر مسبب شيوعاً لتمزق الرحم هو القيصرية السابقة، لأن مكان جرح الرحم السابق بكون منطقة ضعيفة بتقدر تنفتح تحت ضغط المخاض. فلهيك Prior cesarean section هو الجواب. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Trauma in pregnancy لأنه ببين سبب مباشر، لكنه أقل شيوعاً بكثير من القيصرية السابقة الي هي المسبب الأكثر انتشاراً لتمزق الرحم.

question: Which obstetrics diagnosis is suggested by this POCUS, right upper quadrant view?
englishExplanation: This POCUS in the right upper quadrant view is abnormal and shows free fluid in the intraperitoneal cavity. Uterine rupture is a complete division of all three layers of the uterus, resulting in the expulsion of the fetus, amniotic fluid, and blood into the peritoneal cavity.
arabicExplanation: ليش: صورة الـ POCUS بالمنظر الربع العلوي الأيمن غير طبيعية وبتبين سائل حر داخل تجويف البريتوان، وهاد بيدل على وجود دم او سائل خارج الرحم. وتمزق الرحم هو انفصال كامل لطبقاته الثلاث، وبيؤدي لخروج الجنين والسائل الأمنيوسي والدم لتجويف البريتوان، وهاد يفسر السائل الحر بالصورة. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون Placental abruption لأنها سبب نزيف معروف، لكن الـ abruption ما بتخرج الجنين للبريتوان، والسائل الحر هنا بمشي مع تمزق الرحم.

question: Which finding distinguishes uterine rupture from placental abruption?
englishExplanation: Uterine rupture is a complete division of all three layers of the uterus, which interrupts normal uterine contractions. Physical examination may reveal an oddly shaped, flaccid uterus or a fetal body part in an unexpected location outside the uterus. In placental abruption, an intact uterus vigorously and continuously contracts.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الفرق الأساسي بين تمزق الرحم والـ placental abruption بظهر بالفحص الفيزيائي للرحم. بتمزق الرحم تكون الانقباضات متوقفة والرحم بشكل غريب وارتخائي، و ممكن نحس بجزء من جسم الجنين بمكان غير متوقع خارج الرحم. أما بالـ abruption فالرحم سليم وبيستمر بالانقباض بقوة وبشكل متواصل. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Vaginal bleeding أو الفرق بالوجع، لكن هاي صفات مشتركة بين الحالتين، والمميز الحقيقي هو نتيجة فحص الرحم نفسه.

question: A 30-year-old woman at 38 weeks' gestation presents with active contractions and vaginal leakage of fluid. She reports no complications during her pregnancy. Bedside ultrasonography shows positive fetal cardiac activity. Fetal heart tracings show variable decelerations and episodes of bradycardia. Bimanual examination is remarkable for a palpable, pulsating, cordlike structure that protrudes 3 cm past the cervix. What is the most appropriate initial management?

options.text: Push the fetus back into the uterus

englishExplanation: Umbilical cord prolapse is a rare obstetric emergency that requires prompt delivery of the fetus, but the most appropriate initial action is to elevate the presenting fetal part to reduce compression on the cord. Once done, the examiner must leave their hand in place in the patient's vagina, even during transport to the operating room.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الحالة عندها تدلي الحبل السري بعد تمزق الأغشية، والحبل محسوس نابض بيخرج ثلاث سنتيمتر خارج عنق الرحم مع تباطؤات بالقلب الجنيني. وهالحالة طارئة توليدية بدها ولادة سريعة للجنين، لكن أول إجراء لازم هو رفع الجزء المقدم من الجنين لتقليل الضغط على الحبل. وبعد كده لازم الفاحص يخلي ايده داخل المهبل وما يشيلها لحتى الوصول لغرفة العمليات. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Push the fetus back into the uterus، لكن دفع الجنين للداخل ممنوع تماماً، والإجراء الصحيح هو رفع الجزء المقدم فقط لتخفيف الضغط.

question: What is considered the first-line treatment for amniotic fluid embolism?

options.text: Supportive care with no definitive first-line therapy

correctAnswer: Supportive care with no definitive first-line therapy
englishExplanation: Amniotic fluid embolism is a rare but life-threatening complication of pregnancy and delivery. Currently, there is no single first-line treatment. The standard of treatment is centered around supportive care, correction of abnormal vitals, airway and respiratory support, and cardiac support as required.
arabicExplanation: ليش: انسداد السائل الأمنيوسي حالة نادرة بس مهددة للحياة أثناء الحمل والولادة، وما في حالياً علاج وحيد يعتبر خط أول. ولهيك الأسلوب المعياري هو supportive care مع تصحيح العلامات الحيوية غير الطبيعية، ودعم الطريق الهوائي والتنفس، ودعم القلب حسب الحاجة. يعني ما في دواء محدد يوقف المشكلة من جذورها. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون Massive transfusion لأن النزف شائع، لكن نقل الدم بيدعم الحالة وما هو علاج أولي نوعي، والعلاج الأساسي يبقى الرعاية الداعمة.

question: What laboratory finding is most consistent with the coagulopathy associated with amniotic fluid embolism?
englishExplanation: DIC is the most common coagulopathy associated with amniotic fluid embolism and is classically associated with elevated D-dimer, thrombocytopenia, low fibrinogen, elevated PT, and elevated activated PTT. Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with schistocytes may also be seen.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الـ DIC هو أكثر اعتلال تخثر مرتبط بانسداد السائل الأمنيوسي، وبيتميز بشكل كلاسيكي بارتفاع الـ D-dimer ونقص الصفيحات وانخفاض الفيبرينوجين مع ارتفاع PT وaPTT. كذلك ممكن نشوف فقر دم انحلالي دقيق الأوعية مع schistocytes بالمسحة الدموية. فلهيك ارتفاع الـ D-dimer هو الفحص المتوقع. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Elevated fibrinogen، لكن بالـ DIC يكون الفيبرينوجين منخفض بسبب استهلاك عوامل التخثر، وليس مرتفع كما بيفكروا.

question: A patient presents a few hours postpartum and is noted to have significant hemodynamic instability. There is concern for amniotic fluid embolism, and the patient seems to be developing DIC. What laboratory abnormalities would be expected?

options.text: Elevated platelets, prolonged aPTT, elevated D-dimer, and low fibrinogen
Normal PT, normal aPTT, low platelets, and elevated D-dimer
Normal PT, prolonged aPTT, low platelets, and normal fibrinogen
Prolonged PT, prolonged aPTT, elevated D-dimer, and low fibrinogen

correctAnswer: Prolonged PT, prolonged aPTT, elevated D-dimer, and low fibrinogen
englishExplanation: DIC is characterized by severe and extensive clotting, particularly the formation of microthrombi in small blood vessels. This causes consumption of clotting factors, leading to low platelets, low fibrinogen, and prolonged coagulation times. Extensive clotting leads to elevated D-dimer levels.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الـ DIC بيتميز بتخثر شديد وواسع مع تشكل خثرات دقيقة بالأوعية الصغيرة، وهاد بيؤدي لاستهلاك عوامل التخثر. فبيصير عندنا انخفاض الصفيحات وانخفاض الفيبرينوجين مع طول زمني PT وaPTT، والتخثر الواسع برفع الـ D-dimer. والتخثر الحاصل عند المريضة بعد الولادة بمشي مع تطور الـ DIC. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون الخيار الي فيه صفيحات مرتفعة، لكن الصفيحات بالـ DIC تكون منخفضة بسبب الاستهلاك وليست مرتفعة.

question: What is the best treatment for a stable patient with postpartum pulmonary embolism who is currently breastfeeding?
englishExplanation: Either unfractionated heparin or low-molecular-weight heparins such as enoxaparin are appropriate therapy for a stable patient with postpartum pulmonary embolism. Direct oral anticoagulants such as dabigatran and rivaroxaban should be avoided during breastfeeding.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريضة بعد الولادة وعندها pulmonary embolism وهي مرتاحة وترضع طفلها. والعلاج المناسب هو heparin غير المجزأ أو low-molecular-weight heparin مثل enoxaparin، لأنهم آمنين بالرضاعة. ولهيك enoxaparin بجرعة واحد ملغ لكل كيلوغرام تحت الجلد هو الخيار الأفضل بهالحالة. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون dabigatran أو rivaroxaban لأنهما مضادات تخثر حديثة، لكن لازم نتجنبهما أثناء الرضاعة، وهالشي بيميز الخيار الصحيح.

question: A 30-year-old woman presents complaining of a “typical” migraine headache. She is 4 weeks' postpartum and is currently breastfeeding. Which medication is contraindicated?
englishExplanation: Many drugs can be detected in breastmilk. Ergotamine has been reported to be associated with vomiting, diarrhea, and seizures in infants at dosages typically used to treat migraine headaches. It should be avoided in breastfeeding patients.
arabicExplanation: ليش: كثير أدوية بتنتقل لحليب الأم، والـ ergotamine ممنوع أثناء الرضاعة لأنه مرتبط بحدوث تقيؤ وإسهال وتشنجات عند الرضع بالجرعات المستخدمة لعلاج صداع الشقيقة. فلهيك لازم نتجنبه تماماً بالمرضعة الي عندها migraine. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون Morphine لأنه مسكن قوي وبخافوا منه، لكن الأفيونيات بتستخدم بحذر تحت الإشراف، والدواء الممنوع صراحة هو ergotamine بسبب آثاره الخطيرة على الرضيع.

question: An 18-year-old woman presents with abdominal pain and a foul-smelling, bloody vaginal discharge 6 days after an uncomplicated cesarean delivery. This physical examination reveals lower abdominal tenderness with uterine and adnexal tenderness. Her incision is clean, dry, and intact with no evidence of dehiscence. Both breasts are mildly swollen with minimal tenderness, but no warmth is noted. Her vital signs are significant for P 110 and T 39°C (102.2°F). Which diagnosis best explains the cause of the fever?
englishExplanation: Pelvic infection is one of the most common serious postpartum complications. This patient's presentation is consistent with endometritis, which is an infection of the endometrium. Classic findings are fever, tachycardia, foul-smelling and profuse bloody discharge, uterine and adnexal tenderness, and abdominal pain.
arabicExplanation: ليش: التهاب بطانة الرحم هو أحد أشهر المضاعفات الخطيرة بعد الولادة، وعلاماته الكلاسيكية هي الحمى وتسرع القلب وإفرازات مهبلية دموية كريهة الرائحة مع ألم وإيلام بالرحم والملحقات. والمريضة عندها كل هاي العلامات بعد القيصرية بستة أيام، والجرح نظيف وسليم والثدي شبه طبيعي. فالتشخيص الأنسب endometritis. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Mastitis لأن الثدي متورم قليلاً، لكن ما في دفء ولا إيلام واضح، والإفراز الكريه وألم الرحم هو الي يرجح التهاب بطانة الرحم.

question: What is the most common cause of postpartum hemorrhage?
englishExplanation: Primary postpartum hemorrhage is most commonly caused by uterine atony. After delivery of the placenta, the uterus should become firm to palpation. If the uterus does not contract effectively, mechanical hemostasis is impaired, and postpartum hemorrhage results.
arabicExplanation: ليش: النزف بعد الولادة الأولي أكثر أسبابه شيوعاً هي uterine atony. بعد نزول المشيمة المفروض الرحم يصير متماسك عند الجس، ولو ما انقبض بشكل فعال بتتأثر آلية الإرقاء الميكانيكي وبصير نزف. ولهيك ارتخاء الرحم هو السبب الأكثر شيوعاً لنزف ما بعد الولادة. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Retention of placental tissue أو تمزقات القناة التناسلية لأنها أسباب معروفة، لكنها أقل شيوعاً بكثير من الـ uterine atony الي هي السبب الأول.

question: What organism most commonly causes puerperal mastitis?
englishExplanation: Puerperal mastitis is an inflammation of the breast, typically suppurative, that occurs in the immediate postpartum period. Staphylococcus aureus, which is found commonly on the skin, is the typical pathogen.
arabicExplanation: ليش: التهاب الثدي النفاسي هو التهاب بالثدي غالباً قيحي، وبيصير بفترة ما بعد الولادة مباشرة. والعامل المسبب النموذجي هو Staphylococcus aureus، لأنه موجود بشكل شائع على الجلد وبيوصل للثدي بسهولة. فلهيك هو الجرثومة الأكثر تسبباً بالتهاب الثدي النفاسي. الفخ: في طلاب يختارون Escherichia coli لأنها جرثومة شائعة بالالتهابات، لكنها ما هي المسبب الأشيع هنا، والـ Staphylococcus aureus هو الي بيطغى على غيره بالتهاب الثدي.

question: Which antibiotic is the first-line treatment for uncomplicated mastitis?
englishExplanation: Mastitis is inflammation and infection of breast tissue. The first-line antibiotic treatment for uncomplicated mastitis is cephalexin or dicloxacillin. This covers Staphylococcus aureus, which is the most common pathogen implicated in mastitis.
arabicExplanation: ليش: التهاب الثدي هو التهاب وعدوى بنسيج الثدي، والعلاج الأولي بالمضادات الحيوية لحالات التهاب الثدي غير المعقدة هو cephalexin أو dicloxacillin. وهالمضادات بتغطي Staphylococcus aureus الي هو المسبب الأشيع لالتهاب الثدي. فلهيك cephalexin هو الخيار الأول. الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون Vancomycin لأنه قوي ضد الجراثيم المقاومة، لكنه ما هو خط أول للالتهاب غير المعقد، والـ cephalexin كافي وبيغطي المسبب المعتاد.

question: A 55-year-old postmenopausal woman who is an active smoker presents for evaluation of a breast infection. The examination shows mastitis without abscess, which is her third episode of mastitis to this breast in the past year. In addition to antibiotics, what is the most appropriate follow-up plan that should be recommended?

options.text: Follow-up with a breast surgeon within 1 month
Follow-up with primary care in 4 to 6 months

correctAnswer: Follow-up with a breast surgeon within 1 month
englishExplanation: Prompt follow-up with a breast surgeon should be recommended as soon as possible. This patient likely has nonlactating periductal mastitis, which is the result of subareolar ductal inflammation. Periductal mastitis is often seen in smokers. It is essential that the patient see a breast surgeon to rule out an underlying malignancy.

question: A 23-year-old woman presents after a witnessed syncopal episode. She is 1 week postpartum and has had a mild generalized headache and vision disturbances since delivery. Her vital signs include BP 126/82 and P 90. Laboratory test results include Na 119, K 4.2, and glucose 68. What is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation: Postpartum pituitary gland necrosis (Sheehan syndrome) affects patients who lose a significant amount of blood and suffer pituitary hypoperfusion and necrosis after childbirth. Laboratory abnormalities can include hyponatremia, hypoglycemia, and anemia secondary to resulting adrenal insufficiency.

question: A 78-year-old woman presents with a 3-day history of weakness and dysuria. She is noted to be tachycardic, febrile, and hypotensive. What is the best initial fluid for resuscitation?
englishExplanation: Current recommendations are to use an isotonic fluid for resuscitation, and given that this patient is septic and likely will require multiple boluses of fluid, Making lactated Ringer solution the correct choice since it is a balanced isotonic crystal- loid fluid. Normal saline has a risk of hyperchloremic acidosis. Although there has long been controversy over the use of balanced crystalloids versus normal saline, there is now good evidence that balance crystalloid should be used as the preferred crystalloid for resuscitation. A recent large study demonstrated a reduc- tion in composite outcome of death, renal dysfunction, and renal replacement in the critically ill. Another study also demonstrated a reduction in acute kidney injury in the non–critically ill patients with the use of balanced crystalloids compared to nor- mal saline. Incorrect Answer Explanations Like lactated Ringer solution, 0.9% normal saline is an isotonic crystalloid fluid; however, saline is not a balanced isotonic crystalloid fluid, as is lactated Ringer. Although crystalloids are the preferred choice for vol- ume resuscitation, normal saline has been shown to be linked with a hy- perchloremic metabolic acidosis. When compared with balanced crystalloids (eg, lactated Ringer solution), normal saline is also shown to have an increased risk of acute kidney injury. Albumin is a colloid solution that can expand intravascular volume, but it is considerably more expensive than crystalloid solutions and has not shown a benefit in studies. With no benefit and considerable more expense, current recom- mendations are to use crystalloids for initial resuscitation fluid choice. Packed RBCs are the mainstay of resuscitation in hemorrhagic shock. However, in the absence of bleeding, blood transfusions are not recommended as the first-line of intravascular volume expansion because they can carry risk of trans- fusion reactions and infections. This patient does not present with obvious bleeding and is instead showing a picture of likely sepsis; lactated Ringer solution would be the fluid of choice for volume expansion in this patient.

question: What is the recommended first-line single agent used to treat gestational hyper- tension in pregnancy?
englishExplanation: Labetalol is a first-line agent for gestational hypertension in pregnancy. Stage 1 is defined by the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) as BP 130-139/80-89 mm Hg, and stage 2 as any BP ≥140/80 mm Hg. The measurements must be taken on two or more separate occasions and must be before 20 weeks' of gestation or persist longer than 12 weeks' postpartum. Severe chronic hypertension is defined as systolic BP >160 mm Hg or diastolic BP >110 mm Hg and warrants prompt treatment. If a pregnant patient presents to the emergency department first, one must rule-out preeclampsia. Once preeclampsia has been ruled out and discussion with OB has been done, patients can be sent home on a medication for their hypertension. First- line options are labetalol, hydralazine, or nicardipine, with labetalol preferred. For emergency management of severe hypertension in pregnancy, labetalol IV, hy- dralazine IV or IM, or nifedipine PO may be used for acute management if needed. Pregnant patients with chronic hypertension are at increased risk for pla- cental abruption, preeclampsia, low birth weight, cesarean delivery, premature birth, and fetal demise. Incorrect Answer Explanations Hydralazine can be used to treat hypertension in pregnancy. However, due to reflex tachycardia, oral hydralazine is not recommended for use as a single agent. Hydralazine may be combined with methyldopa or labetalol if needed as adjunctive therapy. Hydralazine IV can also be used emergently to treat severe hypertension in pregnancy (BP >160/110), but labetalol is still considered by many to be first line. All antihypertensive medications cross the placenta. ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril are contraindicated in pregnancy because of their teratogenic ef- fects on fetal scalp, lungs, and kidneys. Similar to ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers (eg, valsartan) are contraindicated because of their teratogenic effects in pregnancy. The FDA has added a boxed warning to use of these medications: "Drugs that act on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. Discontinue as soon as possible once pregnancy is detected."

question: Which finding best distinguishes ectopic pregnancy from pelvic inflammatory disease?
englishExplanation: Although it is possible for a patient with pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) to be on her menses or have bleeding due to irritation of the cervix, vaginal bleeding is the finding that best distinguishes between ectopic pregnancy and PID. Obstetric emergencies (eg, ectopic pregnancy, acute abruption, and uterine rupture) comprise the most frequent life-threatening gynecologic causes of pelvic pain in adolescent females. All three typically present with vaginal bleeding. Ectopic pregnancy usually presents with vaginal bleeding and crampy abdominal pain around 6 to 8 weeks after the patient's last menstrual period and can lead to large-volume intraperitoneal hemorrhage. Crampy pain and bleeding in the setting of a positive pregnancy test can be signs of other pregnancy- related emergencies. Placental abruption is most common at 24 to 26 weeks' gestation and can lead to severe DIC, compromising both the patient and the fetus. Uterine rupture usually occurs during labor and is most common in patients who have had a prior cesarean section or uterine surgery. The diagnosis of pregnancy is central to the diagnosis of obstetric emergencies. It is critical for the physician to remember that an adolescent will not always know if they are pregnant and will not always endorse sexual activity, even if they have en- gaged in it. Thus, urine (or serum) pregnancy testing is critical in men- struating patients with abdominal or pelvic pain and should be considered in those who are near age of menarche (median age of menarche is 11-12, depending on demographics) with ambiguous abdominal pain. Incorrect Answer Explanations Because PID is an infectious process and ectopic pregnancy is not, fever is more likely to occur in PID than in ectopic pregnancy. However, fever cannot reliably distinguish between the two conditions, as half of patients with PID do not have a fever. In patients with PID, high fever is one of the indicators of severe disease. Peritonitis is a nonspecific finding that can be found in both PID and ec- topic pregnancy. Peritonitis may also be present in patients with pelvic pain due to other disease processes, such as appendicitis or intestinal perforation. In PID, peritonitis may be a sign of a ruptured tubo-ovarian abscess. In ectopic pregnancy, peritonitis may be a sign of intraperitoneal blood. Shock can be present in both PID and ectopic pregnancy. Although PID and ectopic pregnancies can both present with normal vital signs, they can both also lead to shock. PID (especially cases with a tubo-ovarian abscess) can lead to septic shock, which is often characterized by high fever and peritonitis. Ectopic pregnancy can lead to hemorrhagic shock due to large-volume, brisk intraperitoneal bleeding.

question: In the evaluation of a 30-year-old healthy patient with back pain and normal vi- tal signs, which feature most likely indicates a reassuring and non-serious under- lying pathology?
englishExplanation: The onset of back pain associated with heavy lifting suggests a mechani- cal cause, of which the vast majority of episodes are self-limiting and do not indi- cate a more serious pathology. In the evaluation of a patient with back pain, some historical features point toward serious causes. Abnormal vital signs in a pa- tient with back pain are particularly concerning, especially in older pa- tients. Additional red flags that point to significant underlying pathology include age older than 50 years and a history of cancer, immunosuppression, parenteral drug use, or recent trauma; pain that is unrelieved by rest or analgesia; pain that keeps the patient awake at night; pain associated with nausea or diaphoresis; neurologic findings; and pain that is grad- ual in onset. Broadly, serious pathologies that can present as back pain include occult fractures, congenital anomalies, tumors, vascular catastrophes, infections of the vertebral disc or spinal cord meninges, and space-occupying lesions within the canal that lead to spinal cord or nerve root compression. Nearly all patients with se- rious underlying pathologies have associated risk factors or other symptoms to cor- relate to the diagnosis. Incorrect Answer Explanations Leg weakness is a neurologic finding that may indicate the presence or development of spinal cord compression or cauda equina syndrome. Multiple underlying pathologies can cause cord compression, with a herniated disc being the most common cause. Other etiologies include trauma, tumor, and infec- tion. Further workup is indicated for the possibility of a serious cause. Progressive pain or pain that has been present over 1 month should prompt consideration of a more serious underlying pathology. Often pa- tients with vertebral osteomyelitis present with pain that has been present for weeks to months. The presence of fever is inconsistent. Most patients are over age 50 years. These patients may also have focal spinal tenderness to palpation, signs of cord compression, or even signs of an epidural abscess if the infection has spread. Malignancy should also be considered, especially in those with constitutional symp- toms such as weight loss, fevers, and night sweats or with a history of malignancy. Although chronic pain may ultimately be from a benign cause, vertebral osteomyeli- tis and cancer should first be considered and evaluated appropriately with inflam- matory markers and an MRI, if available. Constitutional symptoms such as weight loss, fevers, and night sweats may point to the possibility of cancer. In patients with back pain and one or more of these symptoms, consideration of malignancy or metastasis should be con- sidered and evaluated.

question: A 62-year-old woman is seen for intermittent vaginal bleeding over the past 2 months. Pelvic ultrasound shows an endometrial stripe greater than 5 mm. What is the next best step in management?

options.text: Begin oral hormone therapy and discharge

englishExplanation: This patient's endometrial thickness is abnormal, which is concerning for malignancy. In women older than 35, the most concerning diagnosis for abnor- mal uterine bleeding is endometrial cancer. Pelvic ultrasound is the imaging modal- ity of choice for abnormal uterine bleeding in older patients and can generally be deferred to outpatient workup. If there is a concern for cancer and a patient is un- able to obtain timely follow-up, this study may be performed in the emergency de- partment. An endometrial lining of 4-mm thickness or more has greater than 99% negative predictive value for endometrial cancer, and this finding can generally be used to exclude endometrial cancer. However, patients still need fol- low-up care with gynecology, as an endometrial biopsy may be performed for ongo- ing bleeding or at the provider's discretion. Incorrect Answer Explanations Postmenopausal patients with vaginal bleeding should not be started on oral hormone therapy in the emergency department. Outside the setting of ma- lignancy, postmenopausal vaginal bleeding is generally light and self-limited. Exclusion of cancer is the primary objective, and treatment is usually unnec- essary once malignancy has been excluded. Moreover, appropriate follow-up care must be ensured versus simply discharging the patient home. Emergent dilatation and curettage is not part of the treatment algorithm for postmenopausal vaginal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy may ultimately be required as part of this patient's evaluation; however, the biopsy can be performed on an out- patient basis. Endometrial ablation is a treatment option for patients with heavy menstrual bleeding (ie, premenopausal patients) after malignancy has been excluded. It is gen- erally not performed in postmenopausal patients.

question: A 4-year-old girl is brought in by her parents because she has foul-smelling vagi- nal discharge mixed with blood. She has no history of recent fever or UTI. Detailed questioning of the patient and her parents eliminates concern for sexual abuse. What is the expected finding on vaginal examination?
englishExplanation: Vaginal foreign bodies are a rare cause of pediatric vulvovaginitis and are likely under-reported in the pediatric and adolescent literature. Blood-stained vagi- nal discharge is the most common presenting symptom, occurring in approximately 80% to 90% of all cases. Wads of tissue paper are the most common re- tained vaginal foreign body and comprise approximately 80% of all cases. Obtaining an accurate history from pediatric patients can be challenging, so a sub- jective history is most commonly obtained from the parents. Importantly, a high level of suspicion must be maintained for possible sexual abuse in all pe- diatric patients presenting with vulvovaginitis. Very young pediatric patients are generally unaware of the vagina, but later in child- hood, during the process of self-exploration, they sometimes insert larger objects or toys. Placing the patient in the supine position, knees to chest, often allows for optimal physical examination of the vaginal vault. If a vaginal foreign body can be directly visualized, attempted removal using either forceps or irrigation with warmed saline is a reasonable first approach. Vaginal foreign bodies that cannot be directly visualized or are not amenable to simple removal in the emergency depart- ment require further workup, including vaginal ultrasonography, x-rays, vaginoscopy, examination under general anesthesia, or consultation with a pediatric gynecologist, depending on the resources immediately available. Incorrect Answer Explanations A normal examination is certainly possible, but if parents bring a child in because of discharge, finding discharge on examination is likely. Although examining the genitals of a young child is difficult, care must be taken to look for foreign bod- ies, lacerations, and other trauma to localize the source of the blood. Urethral prolapse presents with spotting on underwear and is identified as a red-purple mass at the opening of the urethra. However, urethral prolapse is far less common than retained foreign bodies. Vaginal neoplasms are relatively rare in children. When they occur, they are usually rhabdomyosarcomas, but they can occasionally present as germ cell tu- mors or clear cell adenocarcinoma.

question: A patient presents 2 days postoperatively from laparoscopic appendectomy with moderate abdominal discomfort and right-shoulder pain. The patient has no prior medical history. The operative record reveals an uncomplicated procedure. A CT scan is shown below. What is the most likely cause of this patient's condition? Credit: Copyright 2024 Dr. Mohammad Farghali Ali Tosson. Image courtesy of Dr. Mohammad Farghali Ali Tosson and Radiopaedia.org, rID: 50037. Used un- der license.

options.text: De novo perforation of a peptic ulcer
Deep surgical site infection with gas-forming organisms

englishExplanation:
In the early postoperative period (up to 5 days), the most common cause of pneumoperitoneum is incomplete resolution of intraoperative insuffla- tion from laparoscopic surgery. This may cause some abdominal discomfort due to peritoneal irritation or referred right-shoulder discomfort from di- aphragmatic irritation. Ileus or constipation may also cause abdominal pain in the postoperative period. Although hollow organ perforation and necrotizing deep sur- gical site infection are possible, they are much less likely. Possible indications of pathology in the setting of early postoperative pneumoperitoneum are large amounts of air, fever, leukocytosis, and evidence of peritoneal in- flammation. Surgical consultation is warranted in the emergency department for patients with evidence of pathologic free air. Insufflation may also result in more serious complications, such as mediastinal or subcutaneous air, pneumothorax, cardiac arrhythmia, or air em- bolism. These complications may be caused by a malpositioned insufflation needle or physiologic changes from insufflation. Incorrect Answer Explanations De novo perforation of a peptic ulcer is a possible cause of pneumoperi- toneum, but retained air from insufflation is more likely in this early postoperative period. Peptic ulcer perforation would be more likely in a critically ill patient or a patient with a history of peptic ulcer disease. Deep surgical site infection with gas-forming organisms is a possible cause of pneumoperitoneum, but retained air from insufflation is more likely in this early postoperative period. Necrotizing surgical site infections are seen in the early postoperative period, but they are rare. Laparoscopic perforation of the bowel is a possible cause of pneumoperi- toneum, but retained air from insufflation is more likely given the uncomplicated surgery and small amount of free air. The patient's history is also consistent with in- complete resolution of insufflation. Although iatrogenic injury to the intestine is al- ways a possibility, it is a rare complication.

question:
A 38-year-old woman presents to the ED with abdominal pain. She
reports that over the past 2 days she gets pain in her right-upper quadrant
(RUQ) shortly after eating. As you palpate her abdomen, you notice that
she stops her inspiration for a brief moment due to increased pain. Her
vitals include a BP of 130/75 mm Hg, HR of 95 beats/minute, RR of 16
breaths/minute, and temperature of 100.4°F. What is the initial diagnostic
test of choice for this condition?
englishExplanation:
72.  The answer is e. The patient’s history and physical examination is
consistent with acute cholecystitis. Because of the poor predictive value of
the history, physical, and laboratory findings in cholecystitis, the most
important initial imaging test is RUQ ultrasound. Ultrasound findings
suggestive of acute cholecystitis include gallstones, gallbladder wall
thickening and distention, and pericholecystic fluid.
CT scanning (b) may be useful when other intra-abdominal disorders
are being considered. However, the sensitivity of a CT is less than that of
ultrasound for acute cholecystitis. MRI (c) is not a first-line test for acute
cholecystitis. HIDA scan (d) has a higher sensitivity and specificity than
ultrasound, making it the most accurate study for cholecystitis; however, it
is reserved for cases where ultrasound is negative or equivocal. Plain film
radiographs (a) demonstrate stones in the gallbladder less than 25% of the
time.
