question:
A 7-year-old boy presents to the ED 1 hour after slipping and landing
on his right outstretched hand. He was evaluated and splinted by emergency
medical technicians (EMTs) and brought to the ED. On examination, you
note a deformity of his right wrist. There are no neurovascular deficits. A
radiograph of the wrist is shown in the figure. Which of the following is
true regarding physeal fractures in children?

(Reproduced, with permission, from Shah BR, Lucchesi M. Atlas of
Pediatric Emergency Medicine. New York, NY: McGraw Hill; 2006: Figure
19-3.)

options.text: Salter-Harris type IV is defined as a crush injury of the growth plate.
The most common type of fracture is the Salter-Harris type II.
This patient’s radiographic findings are consistent with Salter-Harris
Fractures through the physis, metaphysis, and epiphysis are classified as
The worst prognosis is seen with Salter-Harris type I fractures.

correctAnswer: The most common type of fracture is the Salter-Harris type II.
englishExplanation:
374.  The answer is b. The physis, or growth plate, is a common site of
fractures in pediatric patients. The most widely used system of
classification for these fractures is the Salter-Harris classification. In this
system, there are five classifications of injuries. In general, the higher the
Salter-Harris classification, the worse the prognosis and the higher the
chance for growth arrest. This X-ray reveals a Salter-Harris type II
fracture that involves the physis and metaphysis. Salter-Harris II is the most
common type, accounting for approximately 75% of fractures involving
the growth plate. Salter-Harris I occurs when the fracture involves the
growth plate. There may be no radiographic evidence of these fractures.
This injury should be suspected in any patient who is tender around the
physis of a bone in the absence of obvious radiographic fracture. Treatment
for this injury includes early immobilization and referral. Prognosis is
usually good. Salter-Harris III occurs when a fracture breaks through the
growth plate and into the epiphysis. Salter-Harris IV involves the
metaphysis, physis, and epiphysis. Salter-Harris V is a crush injury to the
growth plate and has a high potential for growth arrest (Figure).

(Reproduced with permission from Adam J. Rosh, MD, and Rosh Review.)
All other answer choices (a, c, d, and e) are incorrect based on this
information.

and rhinorrhea for the past 2 days. The rash started behind his ears the
previous night and in the morning of the day of presentation it spread
further to his neck and chest. On examination, he is ill-appearing, awake,
alert, and crying. A maculopapular rash is present on his head, neck, and
upper trunk. You also note scleral injection bilaterally. There are no lesions
in his mouth.

378.   The mother has also been taking care of her 10-month-old niece for
the past week while the infant’s parents are out of town. The infant is

afebrile and has not exhibited any similar symptoms. Which of the
following is the most appropriate management of the 10-month-old niece?
englishExplanation:
378.  The correct answer is c. For infants less than 1 year of age or those
who have a contraindication to receiving the measles vaccine, measles IG
should be administered within 72 hours.
Children older than 1 year of age who are not immunized against
measles should receive the vaccine (b) within 72 hours of exposure
provided there is no contraindication (ie, immunocompromised state,
previous reaction to the vaccine). Supportive care (a) and respiratory
isolation (d) are appropriate for individuals with active disease, but not
indicated for exposure. Obtaining a serum IgM level (e) is not an element of
postexposure prophylaxis and therefore not required for nonimmunized
individuals with recent measles exposure.

question:
A 15-year-old adolescent boy presents with new onset headache.
Patient states that the headache started during his second period class. He
describes initially having difficulty seeing the words on his paper due to
white spot being in the center of his vision. This has since resolved but he
now describes an 8/10 headache located in bilateral frontal regions, and
describes lights as very bright and sounds as very loud. He does play
football, but has not had a headache, dizziness, or nausea after playing.
Vital signs on presentation show temperature 97.9°F, BP 112/66 mm Hg,
HR 68 beats/minute, RR 14 breaths/minute, and oxygen saturation 99%.
HEENT exam is overall normal with equally reactive pupils and normal
tympanic membrane exam. Photophobia and phonophobia are present.
What is the best next step in the care of this patient?

options.text: IV prochlorperazine, ketorolac, diphenhydramine, and 20 mL/kg normal

correctAnswer: IV prochlorperazine, ketorolac, diphenhydramine, and 20 mL/kg normal
englishExplanation:
384.  The correct answer is e. The patient in this vignette is presenting
with acute onset headache associated with phonophobia and photophobia,
preceded by visual changes consistent with aura. This combination of
findings is most consistent with new onset migrainous headache. In status
migrainosus, IV therapy is recommended. A “cocktail” or combination
therapy has shown to be more effective than any single agent.
Diphenhydramine is used in combination with the prochlorperazine to

decrease its extrapyramidal side effects, such as akathisia, as this can be
uncomforting to the patient.
Mild migraine headaches can be treatment with oral therapies (b).
Administration of 100% oxygen therapy (a) is the treatment of cluster
headache. This patient’s headache description is more consistent with a
migraine. There are no indications for antibiotic therapy and LP (d) in this
afebrile patient with a normal neurologic exam. Opiate pain medications (c)
should not be used in the treatment of migraine headaches.

question:
Shared scenario:
A 70-year-old man presents to the ED complaining of dull, aching pain in
his left back and flank that began 1 day before presentation while watching
TV. The pain is constant and does not radiate. He denies history of trauma
or heavy lifting, and nothing seems to make the pain worse or better. His
BP is 170/95 mm Hg, HR is 88 beats/minute, RR is 17 breaths/minute,
temperature is 97.6°F, and oxygen saturation is 100% on room air. His
physical examination and laboratory studies are unremarkable.

416.   After you finish discussing the patient, your attending physician
leaves to examine the patient and you plan to return the ultrasound machine
to its original location in the ED. Which of the following statements is true
regarding cleansing procedures for an external ultrasound transducer?

options.text: All external transducers should be fully sterilized between each use
If the sonographer wears gloves while performing an examination, it is
The combination of soap and warm water is a safe and effective means
Alcohol-based products are safe to use to clean the ultrasound

correctAnswer: The combination of soap and warm water is a safe and effective means
englishExplanation:
416.  The answer is d. It is important to clean all external ultrasound
transducers between each use. Warm soapy water is a safe and effective
means to do this, as the rubber matching layer of the ultrasound transducer
will prevent any water or soap from reaching the piezoelectric crystals
housed inside the transducer.
Only internal transducers (eg, endocavitary or endovaginal probes)
require full sterilization in between each use (a). Ultrasound gel is neither
bacteriostatic nor bactericidal (b). The sonographer should always sanitize
his or her hands before and after an exam and wear gloves when performing
an ultrasound examination; whether or not they are worn does not change
the fact that the transducer should be cleaned after every use (c). Many
alcohol-based solutions are not safe to be used on ultrasound transducers as
the alcohol can penetrate the rubber matching layer and destroy the
piezoelectric crystals (e); manufacturer’s recommendations should guide
selection of cleaning products.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: تنظيف جميع الـ external ultrasound transducers بين كل استعمال وثاني مهم جداً، والماء الدافئ مع الصابون طريقة آمنة وفعالة للتنظيف. وطبقة المطابقة المطاطية بالـ transducer بتمنع الماء والصابون من الوصول للبلورات الكهربائية الموجودة جوّه الجهاز. والـ internal transducers فقط زي الـ endocavitary أو الـ endovaginal probes هي اللي بتحتاج تعقيم كامل بين كل استعمال. والـ ultrasound gel ليس bacteriostatic ولا bactericidal، ولازم نستخدم اللي بتوصي به الشركة المصنعة للمنتجات المنظفة.
الفخ: كتير طلاب بختاروا Alcohol-based products لأنها منظفات معروفة، أو إن لبس القفازات بيغني عن التنظيف. بس الكحول ممكن يخترق الطبقة المطاطية ويدمر البلورات، ولُبس القفازات ما بيغني إبداً عن تعقيم الـ transducer بعد كل استعمال.

question:
A 39-year-old man is transferred to the ED from an outside facility
for fever and altered mental status because the patient needed a higher level
of care. According to emergency medical services, the patient had
laboratory tests, urine studies, blood cultures, a chest X-ray, and lumbar
puncture performed at the sending facility. It is unknown if the patient
received antibiotics or intravenous fluids at the other facility. The patient
was not sent with any paperwork or imaging studies from the sending
facility. His vital signs on arrival are temperature 102.4°F, BP 90/54 mm
Hg, HR 118 beats/minute, RR 24 breaths/minute, and oxygen saturation
93% on 2 L/minute by nasal cannula. Which of the following is the next
best step in management?

options.text: Administer empiric antibiotics and admit the patient for sepsis
Administer empiric antibiotics and call the sending facility for
Arrange transportation back to the sending facility where his diagnostic
Repeat laboratory tests, blood cultures, urine studies, and chest X-ray
Repeat laboratory tests, blood cultures, urine studies, and chest X-ray

correctAnswer: Administer empiric antibiotics and call the sending facility for
englishExplanation:
566.  The answer is b. Patients are often transferred for higher level of care
or specialty evaluation. Transferring a patient is a complex and coordinated
effort between the sending and receiving facilities. Ideally, the patient’s
medical documentation and study results are made available to the
receiving facility for review upon patient arrival or shortly thereafter. This
aids in continuity of care, reduces redundancy of testing, reduces cost,
increases ED workflow and throughput, and improves patient satisfaction.
However, in the event that a patient arrives without any documentation
from the sending facility, the accepting physician has an obligation to care
for the patient regardless of the available information. Additionally,
attempts should be made to contact the sending facility to request
records and documentation to prevent unnecessary testing and reduce
medical errors from occurring. Therefore, given the limited information
available to the treating physician, the patient requires treatment of sepsis
including empiric antibiotics while the physician attempts to call the
sending facility for supplemental history and documentation.
Answer choice (a) is incorrect insomuch as it neglects the important
task of contacting the sending facility to gather information about care
provided to the patient (eg, fluid resuscitation, antibiotics, blood cultures
obtained, imaging studies) prior to transfer. Answer choice (c) is incorrect
because it is inappropriate to send a critically ill patient (or any patient for
that matter) from a higher level of care to a lower level of care.
Additionally, this sort of patient “dumping” or “shuffling” is fraught with
litigation potential under the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act

(EMTLA), which dictates that patients must be stable prior to discharge or
transfer to another facility. Answer choice (d) and (e) are incorrect because
this patient requires treatment for sepsis, including empiric antibiotic
administration, and the sending facility should be contacted to gain
additional information about the patient’s care.

question:
In infants, what is the most common cause of a depressed level of 
consciousness?
englishExplanation:
The most common causes of depressed consciousness vary 
with patient age. In infants, infectious causes are most common; however, trauma secondary to physical abuse and metabolic derangements 
from inborn errors of metabolism can also be seen. Accidental toxic 
ingestions are often seen in younger children but are very uncommon 
in infants. Young adults and adolescents are more likely to present with 
depressed consciousness after recreational drug use or trauma. Older 
adults are particularly vulnerable to infectious causes, medication 
effects, and alterations in their living environments.

ليش: أسباب نقص مستوى الوعي بتختلف حسب عمر المريض، وعند الرضع تكون الأسباب infectية هي الأكثر شيوعاً. ممكن كمان نشوف trauma الناتج عن إساءة جسدية واضطرابات استقلابية من أخطاء الاستقلاب الخلقية. أما الابتلاعات السامة العرضية فبتشوف غالباً عند الأطفال الصغار لكنها نادرة جداً عند الرضع. والبالغون الشباب والمراهقون بجيلوا غالباً بنقص الوعي بسبب المخدرات الترفيهية أو الصدمات، وكبار السن أكثر عرضة للأسباب Infective وتأثيرات الأدوية والتغيرات ببيئتهم.

question: A variety of brief screening tools may aid in the detection of confusion. All of these tests focus on which cardinal finding of confusion?
englishExplanation:
Inattention is the critical finding for diagnosis of confusion 
and delirium. All of the screening tools (brief Confusion Assessment 
Method [bCAM], Mini-Mental State Exam [MMSE], Quick Confusion 
Scale [QCS]) evaluate this abnormality, although other components of 
consciousness are tested in some models.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب الصحيح هو Attention impairment لأن عدم الانتباه هو العلامة الأساسية والمفتاحية لتشخيص الconfusion والdelirium، وكل أدوات الفحص القصيرة مثل brief Confusion Assessment Method و Mini-Mental State Exam و Quick Confusion Scale تركّز أساساً على تقييم هذا الخلل. صحيح إن بعض النماذج تفحص مكونات أخرى من الوعي، لكن العلامة الجوهرية والمشتركة بينها جميعاً هي ضعف الانتباه. يعني إذا بدك تصطاد التشخيص بسرعة، راقب قدرة المريض على تركيز انتباهه.\nالفخ: كثير طلاب يختارون Decreased level of arousal لأنهم يربطون الconfusion بالنعاس مباشرة، بس انخفاض مستوى اليقظة ليس العلامة المفتاحية التي تقيسها كل الأدوات، والتمييز يكون بالتركيز على ضعف الانتباه كمعيار أساسي.

question:
A mother arrives with her 10-year-old daughter (41 kg) who has 
been seizing for at least 10 minutes. The patient has a history of epilepsy, and a home dose of rectal diazepam has been ineffective. The 
mother states that the child has been in her usual state of good health 
until the seizure began, and there has been no history of trauma. 
Which of the following is the most appropriate initial action?

options.text: Consult neurology to obtain a bedside electroencephalogram.
Endotracheal intubation with vecuronium and etomidate.
Establish vascular access and administer 2 mg of lorazepam.
Obtain an immediate computed tomography scan of the head.

englishExplanation:
Early, aggressive benzodiazepine administration is associated with decreased morbidity and mortality in status epilepticus. 
Intramuscular midazolam is superior to intravenous lorazepam; in 
addition, the dose of lorazepam is inadequate. Endotracheal intubation 
may ultimately be required but is a secondary priority; use of a longacting neuromuscular blockade agent, such as vecuronium, should be 
avoided. Cranial computed tomography may or may not be needed in 
this patient, depending on the response to benzodiazepine therapy. 
Bedside electroencephalograms are most useful in diagnosing nonconvulsive status epilepticus.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الطفلة عندها status epilepticus وما زالت تتشنج عشر دقائق، و rectal diazepam بالبيت ما نفع، والإعطاء المبكر والقوي للbenzodiazepine مرتبط بنقص الاعتلال والوفاة. الintramuscular midazolam أفضل من الintravenous lorazepam، وهاد هو الإجراء الأولي الأنسب لأنه سريع وما بده وصول وريدي. أما الintubation فممكن يصير لاحقاً كأولوية ثانية، وتجنب الlong-acting neuromuscular blockade مثل vecuronium.\nالفخ: طلاب كتير يختارون lorazepam بجرعة 2 mg لأنهم يحفظون إنه benzodiazepine، بس الجرعة غير كافية بالوضع الحالي، والتمييز إنه الIM midazolam يتفوق على الIV lorazepam بأدلة أقوى.

question: A patient who normally wears contact lenses is diagnosed with bacterial conjunctivitis. Which of the following is the preferred treatment in this patient?
englishExplanation:
Patients who wear contact lenses are at increased risk for 
infections with Pseudomonas and, in the setting of bacterial conjunctivitis, should be prescribed a quinolone, barring any contraindications.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب Moxifloxacin لأن مريض الcontact lenses معرّض أكثر للعدوى بPseudomonas، وفي حالة bacterial conjunctivitis لازم يوصف له quinolone إذا ما في موانع. الMoxifloxacin من عائلة الquinolone وبيغطي الPseudomonas، وهاد اللي بيميّزه عن باقي الخيارات اللي ما بتعطي نفس التغطية. فالقاعدة إنه أي مريض عدسات لاصقة عنده التهاب ملتحمة جرثومي، فكر مباشرة بالquinolone.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون Erythromycin لأنه علاج شائع لالتهاب الملتحمة، بس المريض اللي يلبس contact lenses خطر الPseudomonas عنده أعلى، والتمييز إنه الquinolone هو اللي يغطي هالجرثومة.

question:
What is the most common cause of nausea and vomiting in the 
pediatric population?
englishExplanation:
In pediatrics, acute gastroenteritis is the most common 
cause of vomiting. Studies on management of vomiting in this population focus on children with this condition.

Questions and Answers
244.e2
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب acute gastroenteritis لأنه في الأعمار الصغيرة هو السبب الأكثر شيوعاً للاستفراغ، ولهذا السبب معظم الدراسات اللي تتكلم عن تدبير الاستفراغ عند الأطفال تركّز على هالحالة. يعني لما يجيك طفل باستفراغ، أول ما تفكر فيه هو التهاب المعدة والأمعاء الحاد. وهاد بيسهّل عليك التدبير لأنه غالباً self-limited ومعالجة الجفاف هي الأساس.\nالفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون motion sickness أو drug side effects لأنها أسباب معروفة للاستفراغ، بس هي أقل شيوعاً بكثير عند الأطفال، والتمييز إنه gastroenteritis هو الأكثر انتشاراً في هالفئة العمرية.

question:
Elevations in which of the following serum markers in the setting 
of an acute gastrointestinal bleed is predictive of increased 30-day 
mortality?
englishExplanation:
An initial lactate greater than 2.5 mmol/L is associated with 
the development of in-hospital hypotension and an increased rate of 
30-day mortality.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب Lactate لأنه ارتفاعه فوق 2.5 mmol/L في سياق acute gastrointestinal bleed بيرتبط بتطور هبوط الضغط داخل المستشفى وبزيادة معدل الوفيات خلال ثلاثين يوماً. فقياس الlactate من البداية بيعطيك مؤشر إنذار مبكر عن سوء النتيجة، وهاد اللي بيميّزه عن باقي المؤشرات المذكورة. يعني إذا كان مرتفع، اعتبر المريض عالي الخطورة وراقبه عن قرب.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون White blood cell count لأنه علامة شائعة للعدوى والنزف، بس ما ثبت إنه يتنبأ بالوفيات بنفس قوة الlactate، والتمييز إنه القيمة فوق 2.5 هي المؤشر المعتمد.

question:
A 3-year-old girl comes in from home with arm pain after being 
playfully swung by her parents. The child appears uncomfortable 
and refuses the move her arm. After manipulation and a palpable 
click, the child appears more comfortable however after 30 minutes 
will not range her arm for the provider. What is the most appropriate next step for this patient?

options.text: Obtain an XR to evaluate for fracture
Continue to observe the patient with frequent re-evaluations
Discharge home with parents with strict return precautions

correctAnswer: Discharge home with parents with strict return precautions
englishExplanation:
In children with radial head subluxation, the child, fearful 
for eliciting a pain response, may continue to hold their arm in protection while appearing more comfortable. Appropriate comfort and 
discharge may be appropriate with reliable caregivers and with instructions to return within 24 hours if the child does not return to normal.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الطفلة عندها radial head subluxation، وبعد المناورة ظهر click محسوس وصارت مرتاحة أكثر، لكن بقيت تحمي ذراعها لأنها خايفة من استرجاع الألم، وهاد سلوك طبيعي بهالحالة. فيمكن إخراجها مع أهل موثوقين مع تعليمات صارمة بالرجوع خلال 24 ساعة إذا ما رجعت لطبيعتها. يعني ما بتحتاج صورة أو استشارة عظمية إذا الفحص مطمئن والمناورة نجحت.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون طلب XR أو استشارة Orthopedics لأن الطفل ما بيحرّك ذراعه، بس هالحفاظ على الذراع وقائي وليس دليل إصابة، والتمييز إنه ما في حاجة لتصوير لما يكون الطفل مرتاح وأهله موثوقين.

question:
A 2-year-old previously healthy toddler presents with an avulsed 
tooth after hitting his mouth on the ground after a trip and fall. 
Physical examination is remarkable for a non-toxic appearing child 
who is crying and has an open slightly oozing pocket at the maxillary central incisor. The mother has brought the tooth stored in 
milk and the event occurred one hour ago. Which of the following 
statements regarding the patient’s management is true?

options.text: Set-up for conscious sedation should be arranged, because the
The mother should store the tooth in the patient’s mouth.
The tooth should be placed in Hank’s balanced salt solution.
The tooth should be replaced in the socket as soon as possible.
The tooth should not be reimplanted.

correctAnswer: The tooth should not be reimplanted.
englishExplanation:
Management of recovered avulsed teeth depends on the age 
of the patient and the length of time for which the tooth has been displaced. Avulsed primary teeth are not reimplanted. Reimplanted primary teeth ankylose or fuse to the bone, so although the dentofacial 
complex grows downward and forward, the reimplantation site does 
not. There also may be interference with the eruption of the permanent tooth. Cosmetic deformity results in either case. Thus, this patient 
should be referred to a specialist for consideration of a space maintainer or cosmetic appliance.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب الصحيح إنه السن ما لازم يُعاد زرعه، لأن الأسنان اللبنية المقلوعة primary teeth لا يُعاد زرعها؛ فلو زرعت بتلتحم بالعظم وتتثبت، وبينما تنمو المنطقة السنية للأمام والأسفل يبقى موضع الزرع ثابتاً، وممكن تعيق بزوغ السن الدائم. والنتيجة تشوّه شكلي بأي حال، ولهذا يُحوّل الطفل لأخصائي لتقييم space maintainer أو جهاز تجميلي.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون إعادة السن في مكانه بأسرع وقت لأنهم يطبقون قواعد الأسنان الدائمة، بس القاعدة تختلف مع primary teeth، والتمييز إنه عمر الطفل سنتان يعني سن لبني لا يُعاد زرعه.

question: Routine use of prophylactic antibiotics in patients treated with anterior packing for epistaxis has clearly demonstrated which of the following benefits?

options.text: Reduction in incidence of acute otitis media

englishExplanation:
Administration of prophylactic antibiotics in patients discharged with anterior nasal packing has not been shown to prevent 
the listed infectious complications and is not recommended in patients 
without immunocompromise, valvular disorders, or in those whose 
packing will be left in place for less than 48 hours.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب None of the above لأنه إعطاء المضادات الحيوية الوقائية للمرضى اللي يخرجون مع anterior nasal packing ما ثبت إنه يمنع أي من الاختلاطات المذكورة. وهاد العلاج غير موصى به عند غير مثبطي المناعة، ولا عند مرضى صمامات القلب، ولا عند اللي رح يبقى الpacking عندهم أقل من 48 ساعة. فباختصار ما في فائدة مثبتة من الاستخدام الروتيني.\nالفخ: بعض الطلاب يختارون prevention of toxic shock syndrome لأنها فكرة شائعة عن الpacking، بس الدليل ما أثبت هالفائدة، والتمييز إنه الجواب الصحيح هو إنه ما ثبت أي من الفوائد المذكورة.

question:
Of the following choices, which is the correct match between type 
of urine cast and pathologic condition?
englishExplanation:
Hyaline casts are associated with dehydration, exercise, and glomerular proteinuria. The following are the other correct 
associations:
 
• Fatty casts—nephrotic syndrome
 
• Red cell casts—glomerulonephritis
 
• White cell casts—renal parenchymal infection
 
• Granular casts—ATN
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب hyaline casts مع dehydration و exercise لأنه هالتطابق صحيح، فالhyaline casts ترتبط بالجفاف والرياضة والglomerular proteinuria. أما باقي الخيارات فمطابقتها خاطئة، فالfatty casts ترتبط بnephrotic syndrome، والred cell casts بglomerulonephritis، والwhite cell casts بالعدوى parenchymal الكلوية، والgranular casts بالATN. يعني الموضوع كله حفظ مطابقة نوع الcast مع المرض.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون red cell casts مع nephrotic syndrome لأنهم يخلطون بين أمراض الكلية، بس الred cell casts تدل على glomerulonephritis، والتمييز إنه الhyaline casts هي اللي ترتبط بالجفاف والرياضة.

question:
A 27-year-old juvenile-onset diabetic is brought by emergency 
medical services (EMS) for a hypoglycemic coma. Fingerstick 
glucose level is 30 mg/dL. The paramedics were not able to obtain 
intravenous (IV) access, and two immediate attempts at IV cannulation failed in the emergency department (ED). What should be 
the next step in the patient’s management?

options.text: Central venous catheter placement, then D50W IV

englishExplanation:
Intravenous dextrose (25 to 75 g for adults, 0.5to 1 g/kg for children) is preferable but, if unable to obtain IV access, administer glucagon, 
1 or 2 mg intramuscularly (IM) or subcutaneously (SC; 0.025 to 0.1 mg/kg 
IM or SC in children). The onset of action is 10 to 20 minutes. It is ineffective in cases of glycogen absence, such as alcohol-induced hypoglycemia.
arabicExplanation: ليش: المريض عنده hypoglycemic coma ومستوى السكر 30 mg/dL، والdextrose الوريدي هو الأفضل لكن فشلت محاولات الوصول الوريدي، فالخطوة التالية هي إعطاء glucagon بجرعة 1 أو 2 mg عضلياً أو تحت الجلد. الglucagon بيبدأ مفعوله خلال 10 إلى 20 دقيقة، وهاد الحل العملي لما ما في وريد. بس انتبه إنه غير فعّال في حالات غياب الglycogen مثل hypoglycemia الناتجة عن الكحول.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون Central venous catheter ثم D50W لأنهم يصرون على الطريق الوريدي، بس هالإجراء invasive ويأخذ وقت، والتمييز إنه الglucagon الIM هو البديل الموصى به عند فشل الوصول الوريدي.

question:
Which of the following clinical pictures is not seen with Lyme dis -
ease?
englishExplanation:
Clinical pictures consistent with hepatitis, conjunctivitis,
and meningitis may be seen with Lyme disease.
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب glomerulonephritis لأن داء Lyme ممكن يعطي صوراً سريرية تشبه hepatitis و conjunctivitis و meningitis، أما glomerulonephritis فليست من الصور المعروفة فيه. فالسؤال يطلب الشي اللي ما يُشاهد مع Lyme disease، وhadal هو الخيار الصحيح. يعني إذا شفت مريض Lyme عنده أعراض كلوية بشكل glomerulonephritis فكّر بسبب آخر.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون meningitis أو hepatitis لأنها أعراض مشهورة بالعدوى، بس هدول فعلاً ممكن يصيروا مع Lyme، والتمييز إنه الglomerulonephritis هي الصورة غير المرتبطة بالمرض.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding acute hematogenous 
osteomyelitis in children is not true?

options.text: Blood cultures are not usually positive.
Skeletal scintigraphy is indicated in neonates.
The most common site is the long-bone epiphysis.

englishExplanation:
Children may be ill but not usually toxic. There is a 2 : 1 
or 3 : 1 male predominance, with the most likely site being the distal 
metaphysis. Blood cultures are positive in 60% of cases. Scintigraphy is 
not useful in neonates due to a limited inflammatory response. Radiographs are more useful and sensitive early on than in adults.

1727.e2
PART III  Emergency Medicine by System
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب إنه child usually appears toxic هي العبارة غير الصحيحة، لأن الطفل بacute hematogenous osteomyelitis ممكن يكون مريضاً لكن عادة ليس toxic. والصحيح إنه في predominance ذكوري بنسبة 2:1 أو 3:1، وأكثر موقع إصابة هو distal metaphysis، والblood cultures إيجابية في 60% من الحالات. والscintigraphy ما بتفيد عند neonates بسبب محدودية الاستجابة الالتهابية.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون long-bone epiphysis كموقع شائع لأنهم يخلطون بين الmetaphysis و epiphysis، بس الموقع الأكثر إصابة هو الdistal metaphysis، والتمييز إنه العبارة الخاطئة هي ظهور الطفل بمظهر toxic.

question:
Which of the following patients meets the criteria for systemic 
inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS)?

options.text: 53-year-old man with respirations 30 breaths/min, white blood
74-year-old woman with chest pain, heart rate 130 beats/min
81-year-old man with WBC count, 2700 cells/mm3, heart rate,

correctAnswer: 53-year-old man with respirations 30 breaths/min, white blood
englishExplanation:
SIRS is defined as two or more of the following—tachycardia, tachypnea, temperature higher than 38°C (100.4°F) or lower 
than 35°C (95°F), high or low WBC count, or bandemia. Sepsis is SIRS 
with infection. Severe sepsis includes organ dysfunction. Septic shock 
involves systolic blood pressure below 90 mm Hg.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب الصحيح هو الرجل في 53 من عمره لأنه عنده respirations ثلاثين نفساً بالدقيقة مع WBC 16,000، وهاد بيعطيه معيارين على الأقل من معايير SIRS. فالSIRS يُعرّف بوجود اثنين أو أكثر من تسرّع القلب أو تسرّع التنفس أو حرارة أعلى من 38 أو أقل من 35 درجة أو ارتفاع أو انخفاض الكريات البيضاء أو bandemia. والsepsis هو SIRS مع عدوى، والsevere sepsis فيه اختلال وظيفي عضوي.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون الطفل المصاب بالpneumonia لأن عنده حرارة 39 درجة، بس الحرارة وحدها معيار واحد ولا تكفي، والتمييز إنه لازم معيارين على الأقل لتلبية تعريف SIRS.

question:
How long does a typical urine drug screen result remain positive 
after use of cocaine?
englishExplanation:
Urine drug screens typically detect the cocaine metabolite 
benzoylecgonine, which is typically present in the urine for 3 to 7 days 
after the last use.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب 3-7 days لأن فحوص المخدرات في البول عادة تكشف مستقلب الكوكايين benzoylecgonine، وهاد المستقلب يبقى ظاهراً في البول لمدة تتراوح بين ثلاثة وسبعة أيام بعد آخر استخدام. فإذا كان المريض يستخدم الكوكايين مؤخراً، لازم تتوقع نتيجة إيجابية خلال هالفترة. وهاد يفسر ليش الفحص يظل إيجابياً أياماً مو يوم واحد بس.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون 1 day لأنهم يفكرون إنه الكوكايين يقعد بالجسم فترة قصيرة، بس المستقلب يبقى أطول بكثير، والتمييز إنه الbenzoylecgonine هو اللي يُكشف ويبقى 3 إلى 7 أيام.

question: Which of the following is a correct formula for use in airway management of children?

options.text: Cuffed ETT size (1 to 10 years old) = 4 + (age in years/2)
Uncuffed ETT size (1 to 10 years old) = (16/age in years) + 4

englishExplanation:
Correct formulas are as follows:
Uncuffed ETT size = 4 + (age in years/4)
Cuffed ETT size = subtract 0.5 from formula for uncuffed ETT; (4 + 
(age in years/4)) − 0.5
ETT depth = 3 × uncuffed tube size
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب ETT depth = 3 × ETT size لأنه هالصيغة صحيحة، فعند الأطفال عمق الأنبوب الرغامي يساوي ثلاثة أضعاف حجم الأنبوب غير المنفوخ. والصيغ الأخرى الصحيحة هي أن حجم الuncuffed tube يساوي 4 زائد العمر بالأعوام مقسوماً على أربعة، وحجم الcuffed يُنقص منه 0.5. فانتبه للأرقام لأن الخيارات فيها صيغ مقلوبة ومغلوطة.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون ETT depth = 4 × ETT size لأنهم يخلطون بين الرقمين 3 و 4، بس المقام الصحيح هو ثلاثة، والتمييز إنه عمق الأنبوب دائماً ثلاثة أضعاف حجمه.

question:
Which of the following are appropriate methods to obtain urine as 
part of a fever evaluation in a non-toilet-trained child?
englishExplanation:
The only reliable method to obtain sterile urine in a 
non-toilet-trained child is bladder catheterization or suprapubic aspiration if a catheter specimen cannot otherwise be obtained. Bag collection has a high rate of false-positive results and is not preferred in a 
child who is not toilet trained.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب A and C وهو catheterized specimen و suprapubic aspiration، لأنهما الطريقتان الموثوقتان للحصول على بول معقّم عند طفل غير مدرب على الحمام. أما bag collection فنسبته عالية من النتائج الإيجابية الكاذبة ولا يُفضّل عند هالطفل. يعني إذا بدك تقييم حرارة عند رضيع وتحتاج بولاً موثوقاً، فالقثطرة أو الشفط فوق العانة هما الخيار.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون clean catch, midstream لأنه يبدو أسهل وأقل تدخلاً، بس الطفل غير المدرب ما بينفع معه هالأسلوب، والتمييز إنه القثطرة والشفط فوق العانة هما الطريقتان المعتمدتان.

question:
A 38-day old male infant presents to the emergency department 
(ED) after parents noted a fever at home today. In the ED, the temperature was noted to be 40.0°C. The child was born at 35 weeks 
gestation and 1 week ago was diagnosed with otitis media by his 
primary care physician and has been taking amoxicillin as treatment. Which of the following historical aspects places this child at 
higher risk for invasive bacterial infection?
englishExplanation:
Risk for serious bacterial infection (SBI) varies with age. 
Children less than 3 months are at high risk for SBI, with those less 
than 28 days of age at highest risk. Hyperpyrexia, prior treatment with 
antibiotics, and prematurity have also been identified as risk factors for 
SBI. Response to antipyretics has not been linked to SBI risk.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب B و C و D لأن الحرارة 40 درجة، والعلاج السابق بالمضادات الحيوية، والخداج كلها عوامل خطر للعدوى الجرثومية الغازية. والطفل عمره 38 يوماً أي أقل من ثلاثة أشهر معرّض أصلاً لخطر عالٍ، والأعلى خطراً هم أقل من 28 يوماً. أما الاستجابة للخافض فما ارتبطت بخطر العدوى الجرثومية.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون Fever responsive to acetaminophen كعامل خطر لأنهم يظنون إنه الحرارة اللي ما تنخفض أخطر، بس الاستجابة للخافض ما ثبت ارتباطها بالخطر، والتمييز إنه العوامل هي الحرارة العالية والعلاج المسبق والخداج.

question:
Which of the following statements regarding occult bacteremia in 
children younger than 36 months old is true?

options.text: Children with no obvious source of fever and a temperature
The most common pathogen is Neisseria meningitidis.
There has been a marked decrease in the incidence of occult bacteremia since the advent of universal vaccination against pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type B.
With pneumococcal bacteremia, most patients remain febrile

correctAnswer: There has been a marked decrease in the incidence of occult bacteremia since the advent of universal vaccination against pneumococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type B.
englishExplanation:
Children younger than 36 months old with a fever higher 
than 102.2°F (39°C) and no obvious source have an incidence of occult 
bacteremia of less than 1%. Most patients appear nontoxic. The most 
common pathogen in positive cultures is Streptococcus pneumoniae, and 
the incidence of infection has dropped dramatically since the advent of 
universal vaccination. With pneumococcal bacteremia, most patients 
become afebrile in 3 or 4 days with or without antibiotic therapy.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب الصحيح هو انخفاض incidence الoccult bacteremia بشكل ملحوظ بعد انتشار التطعيم الشامل ضد pneumococcus و Haemophilus influenzae type B. فالأطفال أقل من 36 شهراً مع حرارة أعلى من 39 درجة وبدون مصدر واضح صار احتمال الoccult bacteremia أقل من 1%، ومعظمهم غير toxic، وأكثر جرثومة هي Streptococcus pneumoniae. ومع pneumococcal bacteremia غالباً تنخفض الحرارة خلال 3 أو 4 أيام.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون Neisseria meningitidis كأكثر جرثومة لأنها خطيرة ومشهورة، بس الجرثومة الأكثر هي Streptococcus pneumoniae، والتمييز إنه الجواب الصحيح متعلق بالانخفاض الكبير بسبب التطعيم.

question:
What is the most common viral agent causing pneumonia in infants 
younger than 1 year?
englishExplanation:
RSV and parainfluenza are the most common viral agents 
in infants younger than 1 year. Viruses that may be responsible for the 
other agents may also cause viral pneumonia but are not as common 
as RSV.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب Respiratory syncytial virus لأن RSV و parainfluenza هما أكثر الفيروسات المسببة للpneumonia عند الرضع الأصغر من سنة. فإذا جاءك رضيع عنده التهاب رئوي والسبب فيروسي، فأكثر احتمال هو RSV. والفيروسات الأخرى المذكورة ممكن تسبب pneumonia فيروسية لكنها أقل شيوعاً بكثير من RSV في هالفئة العمرية.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون Adenovirus أو Enterovirus لأنها فيروسات معروفة بالجهاز التنفسي، بس شيوعها أقل من RSV عند الرضع، والتمييز إنه RSV هو الأكثر انتشاراً تحت عمر السنة.

question:
Which of the following increases the systemic vascular resistance 
(SVR), thus producing a left-to-right shunt through the ventricular 
septal defect (VSD) associated with Tetralogy of Fallot?
englishExplanation:
Squatting or knee-to-chest positions increase the SVR, 
thus improving tet spells by producing the left-to-right shunt. Acute 
hypovolemia, crying, defecation, and tachycardia are all events that 
suddenly lower the SVR and produce large right-to-left shunts across 
the VSD, beginning the vicious cycle of a hypoxic (tet) spell.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب Squatting لأن وضعية القرفصاء أو الضغط على الصدر بالركبتين ترفع الSVR، وهاد يحسّن tet spells عبر إحداث shunt من اليسار لليمين عبر الVSD المرافق لTetralogy of Fallot. أما نقص الحجم الحاد والبكاء والتبرز وتسرّع القلب فكلها تخفض الSVR فجأة وتنتج shunt كبير من اليمين لليسار تبدأ معه الحلقة المؤذية لنوبة hypoxia.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون Crying لأنه يزيد الجهد والانفعال، بس البكاء يخفض الSVR ويسوّئ النوبة، والتمييز إنه القرفصاء هو اللي يرفع الSVR ويحسّن الshunt.

question:
A 4-year-old child presents with moderate dehydration from gastroenteritis. He is still actively vomiting. Which of the following 
statements regarding this patient’s rehydration is correct?

options.text: A nasogastric tube should be placed for rehydration.
Oral rehydration should not be started.
Oral rehydration success can be determined in 2 or 3 hours.
Oral rehydration target volume is 80 mL/kg.
Target oral rehydration volume should be administered over 2

correctAnswer: Oral rehydration target volume is 80 mL/kg.
englishExplanation:
Oral rehydration can be effective even in the face of 
vomiting in cases of mild or moderate dehydration. Target oral volumes 
are 60 and 80 mL/kg, respectively. Nasogastric tubes may occasionally 
be useful but should not be used unless oral rehydration therapy (ORT) 
fails. The target oral volume should be given in doses of 25% of total 
replacement per hour over 4 hours.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب إنه الtarget oral rehydration volume هو 80 mL/kg لأن الجفاف متوسط الشدة، والهدف في الجفاف الخفيف 60 mL/kg والمتوسط 80 mL/kg. والإماهة الفموية ممكن تنجح حتى مع الاستفراغ، والأنبوب الأنفي المعدي يُستخدم فقط إذا فشلت الإماهة الفموية. ويُعطى الحجم على جرعات 25% من الإجمالي كل ساعة على مدى أربع ساعات.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون وضع nasogastric tube لأنه يستفرغ باستمرار، بس الأنبوب لا يُستخدم إلا بعد فشل الإماهة الفموية، والتمييز إنه الحجم الصحيح 80 mL/kg مع الاستمرار بالمحاولة الفموية.

question: Patients with nephrotic syndrome are at risk for which complication?
englishExplanation:
Thrombosis. Due to increased permeability of the basement membrane, patients lose antithrombin 3 molecules which predisposes them to thrombosis. Patients are also at risk for infections, 
fluid overload, and electrolyte abnormalities. In general, patients do 
not have increased risk of Henoch-Schönlein purpura, supraventricular tachycardia, or vascular malformations.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب Thrombosis لأنه بسبب زيادة نفاذية الغشاء القاعدي يفقد المرضى جزيئات antithrombin 3، وهاد يهيّئهم لتكوّن الخثرات. والمرضى كذلك معرّضون للعدوى وزيادة السوائل واختلالات الشوارد. أما Henoch-Schönlein purpura وsupraventricular tachycardia وvascular malformations فما في زيادة خطر لها بشكل عام. فإذا شفت nephrotic syndrome ففكّر بالخثار.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون Henoch-Schönlein purpura لأنها مرتبطة بأمراض الكلية، بس ما في زيادة خطر لها مع nephrotic syndrome، والتمييز إنه فقدان antithrombin 3 هو اللي يفسّر خطر الthrombosis.

question: What is a unique pharmacokinetic property observed in the pediatric population?

options.text: Infants have decreased absorption of topically applied medications.
Neonates and infants have higher total body water and larger
All drug metabolizing enzymes are at full capacity at birth.
All maternal drugs should be considered not safe when breast

correctAnswer: Neonates and infants have higher total body water and larger
englishExplanation:
Young children can have significant differences in the 
pharmacokinetic properties based on their physiology. Absorption 
can be impaired and delayed based on gut pH and motility. Metabolizing enzymes mature at different rates during the first year of life. 
Young children have a higher total body water and larger volumes 
of distribution and extracellular fluid. There are several factors to 
consider when assessing the risk/benefit profile of taking medications while breast-feeding, including limited human data, maternal 
comorbidities, therapeutic alternatives, properties of the drug, and 
the benefits of continued breast-feeding, when possible. LactMed 
is an excellent resource to determine the safety of the drug during 
breast-feeding.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب إنه neonates و infants عندهم total body water أعلى وحجوم توزيع وسوائل خارج خلوية أكبر، وهاد فرق فارماكوكينيتيكي مهم عند الأطفال. فالامتصاص ممكن يكون مضطوباً أو متأخراً حسب pH الأمعاء وحركيتها، والإنزيمات الأيضية تنضج بمعدلات مختلفة خلال السنة الأولى من العمر. يعني الجرعات عند الأطفال لازم تُحسب على أساس هالفروقات الفسيولوجية.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون إنه كل الإنزيمات الأيضية بكامل طاقتها عند الولادة، بس هالفكرة غلط لأن الإنزيمات تنضج تدريجياً، والتمييز إنه زيادة ماء الجسم وحجم التوزيع هو الخاصية الفريدة الصحيحة.

question:
A 12-month-old girl is referred to the emergency department (ED) 
because her daycare noticed that she cries whenever she is picked 
up and there was crepitus in the left side of the chest. They deny any 
witnessed trauma in the daycare facility. The mother arrives and 
appears concerned. On physical examination, you find some circular contusions on the inner aspects of both her upper arms. The 
mother states this occurred from a fall a week ago. Which of the 
following should be the next step(s) in the patient’s management?

options.text: Conduct a skeletal survey, and report to child protective services
Determine whether the arm contusions are of the same age.
Perform a dedicated retinal examination to determine if the
Perform a humerus x-ray to determine if there is a humerus

correctAnswer: Conduct a skeletal survey, and report to child protective services
englishExplanation:
Contusions on the inner aspect of the upper arm are atypical 
injuries in light of the mother’s claim of a fall for the child. This pattern 
of injury is often related to being held tightly around the arm. Chest wall 
pain in a child could indicate a rib fracture. Chest x-ray is insensitive 
for rib fractures, which are very uncommon at this age unless caused 
by inflicted trauma. This should raise your suspicion of child physical 
abuse. In general, children younger than 2 or 3 years old with suspected 
inflicted injuries should be evaluated with a skeletal survey.
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب إجراء skeletal survey والإبلاغ عن child protective services، لأن الكدمات على الجزء الداخلي من الذراعين إصابات غير نمطية لا تتوافق مع قصة السقوط، وعادة تنتج من الإمساك بالطفل بقوة. وألم جدار الصدر عند الطفل ممكن يدل على كسر ضلع، والكسر نادر بهذا العمر إلا بسبب إصابة متعمّدة. عموماً الأطفال أقل من سنتين أو ثلاث مع شك بإصابات متعمّدة لازم يُقيَّموا بskeletal survey.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون صورة humerus أو تقييم عمر الكدمات لأنها تبدو خطوات تشخيصية كافية، بس الشك بالإيذاء مع نمط الإصابة يستدعي skeletal survey وإبلاغ مباشر، والتمييز إنه هالتصوير الواحد ما يكفي.

question: In a 2-week-old infant that is not yet crawling, which of the following is most highly concerning for abuse?

options.text: Torn lingual frenulum with scant bleeding

correctAnswer: Torn lingual frenulum with scant bleeding
englishExplanation:
Lingual frenulum tears are very concerning for abuse in 
pre-mobile infants. These injuries heal quickly, and the presence of 
bleeding excludes the possibility of birth injury. Several self-limited 
injuries can result from the birth process, even in deliveries that are not 
recognized as particularly traumatic. These injuries can be clinically 
subtle and are not-uncommonly missed in the newborn nursery. Rib 
fractures are uncommonly seen from birth and are more common in 
larger infants or difficult deliveries. The presence of obvious callous on 
the rib fractures is consistent with a fracture that is at least 7 to 14 days 
old. Clavicle and skull fractures are not uncommon parturitional injuries. Unlike other fractures, skull fractures do not develop callous and 
their age cannot be estimated.
   

2261.e1
REFERENCES
arabicExplanation: ليش: الجواب Torn lingual frenulum with scant bleeding لأنه تمزق اللجام اللساني مقلق جداً للإيذاء عند الرضع غير المتحركين، وهالإصابات تشفى بسرعة ووجود النزف يستبعد احتمال إصابة الولادة. أما كسور الترقوة والجمجمة فليست نادرة كإصابات ولادية، وكسور الأضلاع نادرة من الولادة، ووجود callus واضح يعني إنه الكسر عمره أسبوع إلى أسبوعين على الأقل. والكسور الجمجية لا تشكّل callus ولا يمكن تقدير عمرها.\nالفخ: طلاب يختارون Lateral rib fracture with callous لأن كسر الضلع يوحي بالإيذاء، بس وجود الcallus يدل إنه قديم ويمكن أن يكون ولادياً، والتمييز إنه تمزق اللجام مع النزف عند رضيع غير متحرك هو الأكثر إثارة للشك.

1. A 28- year- old G2P1 woman at 26 weeks of gestation presents with a
recurrent asthma flare. Vital signs are temperature 36°C, heart rate
110 beats/min, blood pressure 120/60 mm Hg, respiratory rate 28
breaths per minute and O 2 saturation 96%. She has diffuse expi -
ratory wheezes. Arterial blood gas reveals P o2 90 mm Hg, P co 2
40 mm Hg, and pH 7.34. Which of the following statements best
describes the issues in management with this patient?

options.text: Most patients with asthma improve during pregnancy.
Inhaled beta- agonists are first- line therapy.

correctAnswer: Inhaled beta- agonists are first- line therapy.
englishExplanation:
Beta- agonists followed by corticosteroids are the mainstay
of asthma therapy during pregnancy. During pregnancy, one third of
asthmatics worsen, one third improve, and one third stay the same.
Blood gas interpretation must take into account the “normal” alke -
mia of pregnancy with a Pco 2 of 30 to 32 mm Hg and a compensatory
HCO3 level of 18 to 20 mEq/L. This patient has a relative “hypoventilation” and may indeed need admission for close observation.

question: A 2-week-old boy presents to the ED with feeding intolerance and abdominal distension. He was born 4 weeks premature. On physical exam, you note abdominal wall erythema. An abdominal radiograph reveals intramural air within the bowel wall. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment for this disease process?

options.text: Surgical consultation for immediate bowel resection

englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with signs and symptoms consistent with necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC). NEC is defined as bowel necrosis of an unknown etiology. Management is first with prolonged bowel rest, nasogastric decompression, and intravenous antibiotics that specifically target enteric bacteria. If that fails, surgical resection of the necrotic bowel must be pursued. NEC classically affects premature infants at a much higher rate than those born at term. Signs and symptoms of NEC include abdominal distension, poor feeding, vomiting, and bloody stool. Systemic illness may occur and presents with lethargy, apnea, fever, and shock. Diagnosis of NEC is with abdominal radiograph, which reveals pneumatosis intestinalis.



Broad spectrum intraperitoneal antibiotics (A) would be appropriate for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis in patients with a peritoneal dialysis catheter; however, this would not be appropriate to initiate in a neonate with NEC.

Rectal air enema (C) is the most appropriate initial treatment for intussusception.

Surgical consultation for immediate bowel resection (D) is the classic management of midgut volvulus and is the third phase of potential management of necrotizing enterocolitis.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the classic triad of presenting signs and symptoms of intussusception?

Reveal Answer:
Abdominal mass, colicky abdominal pain, and currant jelly stool.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review

ليش: الحالة هي necrotizing enterocolitis، وهو نخر بالأمعاء مجهول السبب يصيب الخدج بكثرة، وعلاجه الأولي راحة الأمعاء الطويلة مع nasogastric decompression ومضادات حيوية وريدية تستهدف بكتيريا الأمعاء. أعراضه انتفاخ بطن وسوء تغذية وتقيؤ ودم بالبراز، وقد يصير إنتان جهازي مع خمول وانقطاع نفس وحرارة وصدمة. التشخيص بالأشعة البطنية يبيّن pneumatosis intestinalis، وإذا فشل العلاج لازم استئصال جراحي للأمعاء المتنخرة.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختارون antibiotics داخل البريتوان أو bowel resection فوراً، وهاد غلط كخطوة أولى. تذكّر إن إزالة الضغط بالـ NG هي البداية، والاستئصال مرحلة ثالثة إذا فشل العلاج.

question:
A 6-day-old term female neonate is brought to the emergency department with jaundice. She was born via vaginal delivery at the gestational age of 39 weeks, with a birth weight of 3.5 kg. Jaundice started today without fever, diarrhea, or vomiting. The mother informs you that the baby is exclusively breastfed, but she feels pain and engorgement in her breasts and struggles with breastfeeding. The baby is not lethargic, her muscle tone is normal, she cries normally, and her weight is 3 kg. Vital signs are blood pressure 80/45 mm Hg, heart rate 160 bpm, respiratory rate 40/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, and temperature 37.2°C. Laboratory tests are presented below:

Hemoglobin: 15 g/dL

White blood cells: 4,900/µL

Platelets: 170,000/µL

C-reactive protein: 4 mg/L

Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dl

Blood urea nitrogen: 20 mg/dl

Potassium: 3.7 mEq/L

Sodium: 146 mEq/L

Alanine aminotransferase: 20 U/L

Aspartate aminotransferase: 25 U/L

Bilirubin:

Direct bilirubin: 1 mg/dL
Total bilirubin: 14 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase: 100 U/L

Albumin: 3.5 g/dL

Direct Coombs test: negative

What is the next step in management?

options.text: Expressed maternal milk with appropriate latching education

correctAnswer: Expressed maternal milk with appropriate latching education
englishExplanation:
This neonate has signs and symptoms of insufficient breastfeeding. The mother has had difficulty with breastfeeding, and the baby receives inadequate calories and is dehydrated (weight loss > 10% with a mild rise in sodium and blood urea nitrogen). As a result, enterohepatic circulation has increased, and the baby has developed unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Since the total bilirubin level is < 25 mg/dL, the neonate is not at risk of bilirubin-induced neurologic dysfunction (BIND). Also, she has normal vital signs, and her tone, crying, and mental status are normal, which means the BIND score is low. The BIND score identifies the presence of acute bilirubin encephalopathy (ABE). BIND score calculates the sum of scores for mental status (normal = 0, sleepy but arousable = 1, lethargic and irritable = 2, coma and seizure = 3), muscle tone (normal = 0, mild hypotonia = 1, moderate hypotonia = 2, retrocolic and opisthotonos = 3), and cry pattern (normal = 0, high pitched = 1, shrill = 2, inconsolable or absence of cry = 3). A BIND score of 1–3 is slight ABE, 4–6 is moderate, and 7–9 is advanced ABE. Risk factors for BIND in newborns are gestational age < 38 weeks (higher risk for lower gestational ages), hypoalbuminemia, hemolytic conditions, and sepsis. Since the baby has a low BIND score and has no risk factors for ABE, she should receive supportive care, including optimized breastfeeding and hydration. One of the causes of inadequate breastfeeding is breast engorgement and difficulty in latching, in which the baby cannot attach to the breast. Expressing milk and providing appropriate education on latching is the first step in management. If breast milk is insufficient, pasteurized donor milk would be another option. Formula feeding is discouraged as a primary replacement, but may be used if other methods are not preferred.



Exchange transfusion (A) is required if there are symptoms of ABE (hypotonia, lethargy, apnea, opisthotonos, and seizure) and the total serum bilirubin (TSB) is above the threshold for exchange transfusion, based on gestational age and the time elapsed since birth. ABE is generally not a concern when TSB is < 15 mg/dL.

Intravenous immune globulin (D) is indicated in hyperbilirubinemia and severe hemolysis, which is not found in this patient.

Intravenous antibiotics (C) are necessary when there is neonatal sepsis. This neonate is not presenting with signs and symptoms of sepsis.

Phototherapy (E) is indicated for unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia when the TSB is above the threshold. This threshold depends on the gestational age and the presence of the risk factors for BIND. Generally, treatment would not be indicated in a 7-day-old neonate with TSB < 15–20 mg/dL.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the difference between the pathophysiology of breastfeeding jaundice and breast milk jaundice?

Reveal Answer:
Breastfeeding jaundice is due to inadequate feeding, while breast milk jaundice is due to the block of bilirubin glucuronidation by unknown factors in the milk.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Suboptimal Intake Jaundice

Aka breastfeeding jaundice
Inadequate milk production or infant with poor milk transfer
Increased enterohepatic circulation of bilirubin
Clinical: jaundice, weight loss, dehydration, hypernatremia
Tx: lactation consultation, donated breast milk or formula supplementation, phototherapy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الوليد عندو علامات رضاعة غير كافية، الأم عندها صعوبة بالرضاعة والطفلة صارت تنقص كالوري ونقص سوائل، لأن نزول الوزن أكثر من 10% مع ارتفاع طفيف بالصوديوم والـ BUN. هاد أدى لزيادة الدورة الكبدية المعوية فصارت hyperbilirubinemia غير مباشرة، ومستوى البيليروبين أقل من 25 mg/dL فما في خطر على الدماغ. علاماتها الحيوية طبيعية وتوترها وبكاها ويقظتها طبيعية، يعني BIND score منخفض، فالعلاج دعمي مع تحسين الـ breastfeeding عن طريق الحليب المستخرج وتعليم الإرضاع السليم.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يقفزون نحو phototherapy أو exchange transfusion، بس هاد مش ضروري لأن البيليروبين تحت 25 والطفلة wellbeing. فرّق بينهن بقياس مستوى البيليروبين وتقييم BIND قبل أي تدخل.

question: A first-time mom brings in her 4-week-old son because she is concerned that her son has been having projectile, nonbilious vomiting after eating over the past 2 weeks. She had an uncomplicated, vaginal birth at 39 weeks following an uneventful pregnancy. The boy's weight at birth was 8 lbs 3 oz, and today he weighs 8 lbs 8 oz. He is exclusively fed milk-based formula, and his mother states that he seems to want to eat constantly yet never seems to be satisfied and is especially hungry after an episode of emesis. On physical exam, you note a well-developed male newborn child. On palpation of his abdomen, you feel a pronounced peristaltic wave from the left upper quadrant to the right upper quadrant and a 5 mm oval mass in the right upper quadrant. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Advise the mother to switch the child to a soy-based formula
Obtain a CT scan of the abdomen
Obtain an air or barium enema

englishExplanation:
Pyloric stenosis is characteristically associated with projectile vomiting that usually starts at 2–6 weeks of age (with symptoms being delayed in preterm infants), but some infants may begin with vomiting at birth. It is important to differentiate the baby spitting up versus having projectile postprandial vomiting. The pyloric sphincter is a muscle that controls the emptying of gastric contents into the duodenum. In pyloric stenosis, the muscle is hypertrophied and results in obstruction at the gastric outlet, causing distension and retrograde propulsion of stomach contents. Patients typically present with projectile, nonbilious vomiting because the gastric contents have not had a chance to mix with bile secreted distal to the gastric outlet obstruction. Physical exam findings can include a left to right peristaltic wave as the stomach tries to empty its contents against the hypertrophied muscle, as well as an oval-shaped mass with palpation of the hypertrophied muscle. Patients may also want to eat frequently and seemingly without satiety, be fussy, and may also present with dehydration (e.g. decrease or lack of tears with crying, a decrease in the number of wet diapers per day) and weight loss due to an inability to keep feedings down. Ultrasound is the initial diagnostic study of choice, as it is rapid, noninvasive, and free from radiation. It has a sensitivity and specificity close to 100%. If the ultrasound is equivocal, then an upper GI series will classically show a string sign as contrast travels through the narrowed pylorus.



Infants who are lactose intolerant typically present with abdominal bloating or cramping, gas, or diarrhea, especially within 30 minutes to 2 hours of having breast milk or milk-based formula, but they do not have projectile postprandial vomiting. Switching to a soy-based formula (A) would not help to improve this infant's symptoms.

A CT scan of the abdomen (B) may show pyloric stenosis but is not the best choice for the diagnosis of suspected pyloric stenosis, as it exposes the infant to unnecessarily large amounts of radiation.

An air or barium enema (D) is used for the diagnosis and treatment of intussusception, which typically presents as vomiting and diarrhea followed by bloody bowel movements with mucus (currant jelly stools). An abdominal mass in the right lower quadrant (as the telescoping of the bowel into itself typically occurs at the ileocecal junction) may also be palpated. An air or barium enema would not provide imaging of the pyloric sphincter.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the classic electrolyte abnormality seen in pyloric stenosis?

Reveal Answer:
Vomiting leads to hypokalemia, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Pyloric Stenosis

2–8 weeks of age, boys > girls
Sx: nonbilious projectile vomiting after feeding, early satiety
PE: dehydration, RUQ olive-like mass
Lab results: hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis
Dx: ultrasound or UGI series (string sign)
Tx: fluid and electrolyte replacement, pyloromyotomy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الوليد عندو pyloric stenosis، والعلامات projectile nonbilious vomiting وتظهر عادة بعمر 2 إلى 6 أسابيع، مع إمكانية بدء القيء عند الولادة عند بعض الأطفال. العضلة المتضخمة تسد مخرج المعدة وتعطي موجة peristaltic من الشمال لليمين وكتلة بيضوية بالربع العلوي الأيمن. الطفل بدو ياكل باستمرار وما يشبع، وقد يصاب بالجفاف ونقص بالوزن. الـ ultrasound هو الفحص التشخيصي الأول لأنه سريع وغير باضع وبدون إشعاع.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختارون CT أو air/barium enema، وهاد غلط لأن الـ ultrasound يكفي ويكشف الـ pylorus المتضخم. تذكّر إن الـ enema علاج الـ intussusception مش الـ pyloric stenosis.

question: A 3-week-old boy presents to the ED with his parents for problems with feeding. His parents note that he forcefully vomits after every feed but remains hungry. On physical exam, you palpate an olive-shaped mass in the upper abdomen. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic test?

options.text: Computed tomographic scan of the abdomen

englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with signs and symptoms associated with pyloric stenosis. Pyloric stenosis is caused by the idiopathic hypertrophy and elongation of the pylorus causing gastric outlet obstruction. Pyloric stenosis is best diagnosed with abdominal ultrasound. Risk factors for the development of pyloric stenosis include male sex, being firstborn, and exposure to erythromycin as a neonate. Patients with pyloric stenosis generally present within the first 3–6 weeks of life. Signs and symptoms include projectile nonbilious emesis with persistent hunger after vomiting. There may be a palpable olive-shaped mass in the epigastrium or right upper quadrant of the abdomen. However, it is not often palpable due to the patient crying during the exam. Treatment of pyloric stenosis is with surgical pyloromyotomy.



A CT of the abdomen (B) is generally not necessary to make the diagnosis of pyloric stenosis as it is typically easily seen with ultrasound alone. Ultrasound is also more desirable as it does not expose the child to radiation and is noninvasive.

An upper GI series (C) is used to diagnose malrotation and midgut volvulus, which presents with bilious emesis. The image produced shows a corkscrew appearance of the oral contrast, revealing the diagnosis.

An X-ray of the abdomen (D) is often sufficient to diagnose necrotizing enterocolitis, which presents with pneumatosis intestinalis and feeding intolerance in neonates.

One Step Further
Question:
What physical exam finding is classically associated with necrotizing enterocolitis?

Reveal Answer:
Abdominal wall erythema.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Pyloric Stenosis

2–8 weeks of age, boys > girls
Sx: nonbilious projectile vomiting after feeding, early satiety
PE: dehydration, RUQ olive-like mass
Lab results: hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis
Dx: ultrasound or UGI series (string sign)
Tx: fluid and electrolyte replacement, pyloromyotomy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد المريض عندو pyloric stenosis الناتج عن تضخم واستطالة مجهولة السبب بالـ pylorus تسبب انسداد مخرج المعدة ومنع تفريغ محتوياتها للاثني عشر. أفضل وسيلة تشخيصية هي الـ abdominal ultrasound، وعوامل الخطر هي جنس الذكر والطفل الأول والتعرض لـ erythromycin بالولادة. الأعراض تشمل قيء نافث غير صفراوي مع جوع مستمر بعد القيء وكتلة زيتونية بالإبيغاستريوم، والعلاج النهائي جراحي بالـ pyloromyotomy.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختارون upper GI series لأنهم يربطونها بالتشخيص، بس هي محددة للـ malrotation والـ midgut volvulus لأنها تبيّن شكل corkscrew. تذكّر إن الـ ultrasound أدق وأأمن وما يعرّض الطفل للإشعاع.

question: A 3-month-old infant presents to the emergency department with worsening vomiting for the last 2 months. His mother had received no prenatal care, and the family recently emigrated from a country with limited medical resources due to war. His mother reports that the baby has lost weight, vomits his milk shortly after every feed, and cries to be refed shortly afterward. His vital signs are within normal limits for age. His exam is normal, except that he has little subcutaneous fat, and intestinal peristalsis can be seen through his thin abdominal wall. Which of the following laboratory abnormalities are expected in this infant?

options.text: Metabolic acidosis with hypokalemia and elevated blood urea nitrogen
Metabolic acidosis with hyponatremia and hyperkalemia
Metabolic alkalosis with hypochloremia and hypokalemia
Metabolic alkalosis with hyponatremia and hypokalemia

correctAnswer: Metabolic alkalosis with hypochloremia and hypokalemia
englishExplanation:
This patient demonstrates the characteristic presentation of pyloric stenosis. Infants present with nonbilious vomiting that usually begins between 2 and 8 weeks of age. There are reports of this developing as late as 5 months of age, but this is rare. The vomiting becomes more forceful over time and may start intermittently but then occurs with each feed as the condition progresses. These patients may lose weight like this patient, and they often begin to cry to eat soon after vomiting. Exam findings may show intestinal peristalsis across their thin abdominal wall. Historically, the diagnosis was made by the palpation of an olive-like mass, which was more easily felt shortly after feeding.

This presentation is uncommon in countries where ultrasound is readily available as the diagnosis and interventions now occur earlier, preventing some of the metabolic complications of persistent vomiting. The olive-like mass is less frequently found by the clinician suspecting the diagnosis but can still be felt under sedation at the time of pyloromyotomy. Ultrasound criteria for pyloric stenosis are muscle thickness ≥ 3–4 mm and length ≥ 12–16 mm (depending on the reference text). However, younger infants or those early in their course may not yet have met these specifications. If ultrasound is unavailable, an upper GI series can be used as an alternative for evaluating the pylorus.

Patients with prolonged symptoms develop electrolyte disturbances. The loss of hydrochloric acid with repeated vomiting results in a hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis. When this occurs depends on the severity and frequency of vomiting. Hypokalemia is also a common finding, but only if the patient has had more than 3 weeks of symptoms, like the patient in this case. Treatment is pyloromyotomy after the correction of any electrolyte disturbances.



A metabolic acidosis with hypokalemia and elevated blood urea nitrogen (A) is more commonly seen in patients with diarrhea. Elevated blood urea nitrogen levels are typical but not universal in patients with severe dehydration and might be present in this patient. Acute diarrhea usually leads to a loss of bicarbonate and potassium in the stool, resulting in hypokalemia and metabolic acidosis.

A metabolic acidosis with hyponatremia and hyperkalemia (B) is more frequently seen in patients with diabetes-related ketoacidosis. The acidosis is due to the formation of ketones, and hyponatremia results from serum dilution secondary to the high osmotic pressure of glucose. The serum potassium levels in these patients can vary widely despite a significant total body potassium deficit, and they are often mildly elevated.

A metabolic alkalosis with hyponatremia and hypokalemia (D) is more commonly seen in patients on loop diuretic therapy. The increased delivery of potassium to the distal urinary tract increases its urinary excretion. The loss of sodium reflects the induced hypovolemia. Elevated aldosterone from the activation of the renin-angiotensin system also enhances hydrogen and potassium excretion, causing further hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis.

One Step Further
Question:
What techniques can be used to palpate the pylorus in an infant with suspected pyloric stenosis?

Reveal Answer:
After decompressing the stomach with an orogastric tube, help the infant relax by flexing the hips and using a pacifier with sugar water.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Pyloric Stenosis

2–8 weeks of age, boys > girls
Sx: nonbilious projectile vomiting after feeding, early satiety
PE: dehydration, RUQ olive-like mass
Lab results: hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis
Dx: ultrasound or UGI series (string sign)
Tx: fluid and electrolyte replacement, pyloromyotomy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الرضيع عندو pyloric stenosis، والقيء يبدأ عادة بين الأسبوع الثاني والثامن ويصير نافثاً مع كل رضعة مع فقدان وزن وجوع بعد القيء. الفحص يبيّن حركة معوية عبر جدار البطن الرقيق، والتشخيص كان تاريخياً بكسر الكتلة الزيتونية. مع الاستمرار بالقيء يفقد الرضيع الهيدروجين والكلوريد، ويقوم الكلى بمقايضة الهيدروجين بالبوتاسيوم فيتفاقم القلاء الأيضي. النتيجة هي metabolic alkalosis مع hypochloremia و hypokalemia.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختارون metabolic acidosis لأنهم يفكرون إن القيء يعطي حماضاً، وهاد غلط. فرّق بفهم إن فقدان حمض المعدة يعطي قلاء، ومع القيء المستمر يزول الكلور والبوتاسيوم.

question: A 10-month-old boy is brought to the ED by his parents for episodes of inconsolable crying for 3 hours. The episodes last a few minutes and then seem to resolve. He appears well between episodes. During the episodes, he curls his legs up to his chest and appears to be in pain. The parents report no current vomiting or diarrhea, but they say he is recovering from a recent viral GI illness. Vital signs are a T of 98.2°F (36.8°C), BP of 90/52 mm Hg, HR of 151 bpm, RR of 25/min, and SpO2 of 98% on room air. During the examination, the boy has vague abdominal discomfort, and a mass is palpated in the right upper quadrant. Examination of the stool reveals occult blood. An ultrasound is shown above. What is the most appropriate next step in care?
englishExplanation:
This patient’s presentation is classic for intussusception, characterized by intermittent episodes of severe abdominal pain, inconsolable crying, and the presence of a palpable sausage-shaped mass in the right upper quadrant. The stool test revealing occult blood supports the diagnosis. Ultrasound findings show a target sign, which is diagnostic for intussusception.

This condition occurs when a segment of the intestine telescopes into an adjacent segment, leading to bowel obstruction and compromised blood flow. It is most commonly seen in children between the ages of 6 months and 3 years, with a peak incidence around 1 year of age. The condition is often idiopathic, particularly in younger children, but in older children it is essential to investigate for pathologic lead points such as a Meckel diverticulum, intestinal polyps, lymphomas, or postinfectious Peyer patch hypertrophy.

Clinically, intussusception presents with intermittent episodes of severe, colicky abdominal pain. During these episodes, children often draw their knees up to their chest and cry inconsolably. Between episodes, they may appear relatively well. Vomiting is a common symptom, and it may initially be nonbilious, but as the obstruction progresses, bilious vomiting can occur. A classic late finding in intussusception is the passage of bloody, mucoid stools, described as currant jelly stool. Physical examination may reveal a palpable, sausage-shaped mass in the right upper quadrant, often associated with tenderness. The diagnostic test of choice is an abdominal ultrasound, which reveals the target sign or donut sign, representing the telescoped bowel segments.

Treatment involves nonoperative reduction using air or hydrostatic enemas, which are both diagnostic and therapeutic. These enemas are performed under imaging guidance (fluoroscopy or ultrasound) and have a high success rate in stable patients without signs of perforation or peritonitis. Surgery is required if enema reduction is unsuccessful, complications like bowel perforation occur, or a pathological lead point is suspected. Prompt recognition and management of intussusception are critical to preventing complications such as bowel ischemia, perforation, or peritonitis.



A CT scan of the abdomen (B) is unnecessary when the diagnosis is already established by clinical presentation and ultrasound.

A surgical intervention (C) is not yet indicated in this patient, but surgical consultation is indicated prior to proceeding with an air contrast enema. Patients require surgical reduction if an air contrast enema is unsuccessful or if they are in shock.

An upper GI series (D) is the study of choice to diagnose malrotation and volvulus. Malrotation presents at < 1 month old and results from abnormal rotation of the gut during embryological development. Children may be well appearing with a malrotation, but if the malrotation becomes a volvulus (twisting of the malrotated gut), they will typically have sudden constant abdominal pain, distention, and bilious vomiting and usually become ill appearing.

One Step Further
Question:
Which segments of the bowel most commonly telescope during intussusception?

Reveal Answer:
Ileum into colon.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Intussusception (Telescoping Bowel) in Pediatrics

RF: 6 months to 3 years old
Clinical: colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, and bloody stools (currant jelly)
Dx: ultrasound (target sign)
Important to be vigilant for pathologic lead points in children of any age
Tx: air or hydrostatic (contrast or saline) enema, surgical
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد مريض intussusception، ويتميز بنوبات ألم بطنية شديدة وبكاء لا يهدأ وكتلة sausage-shaped بالربع العلوي الأيمن، ووجود occult blood بالبراز يدعم التشخيص. الـ ultrasound يبيّن target sign وهو مؤكد للتشخيص، والحالة تحصل لما تنزلق قطعة أمعاء داخل قطعة ملاصقة مسببة انسداداً ونقص تروية. أكثر شيوعاً بين 6 أشهر و3 سنوات، والعلاج الأساسي هو air contrast enema.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختارون surgical intervention فوراً، بس العملية هي الخيار إذا فشل الـ enema. فرّق بأن الـ air enema هو العلاج الأول والناجح بأغلب الحالات، مع طلب استشارة جراحية قبله خوفاً من الانثقاب.

question: A 6-year-old boy presents to the ED after his parents found him drinking bleach. It is industrial strength, and they are unsure how much he drank. The patient has no other medical conditions. His T is 97.6°F (36.4°C), BP is 82/61 mm Hg, HR is 132 bpm, RR is 32/min, and SpO2 is 95% on room air. The patient is crying and drooling. He demonstrates a hoarse cry. He has burn marks around his mouth and on his chest. His clothes appear to be wet and have a chemical odor. The nursing staff has obtained IV access. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Administer a 10 cc/kg bolus of normal saline

englishExplanation:
Caustic ingestions can be life-threatening and are more common in the pediatric population. Exposures are typically acidic or alkaline. The extent of the injury is based on the concentration of the compound (and subsequently the pH), the volume ingested, and the duration of contact with tissues. Household beach is a common, relatively dilute alkali that many patients have access to. In contrast, industrial bleach is much more concentrated than household bleach and is more likely to cause significant injury. Alkaline agents cause liquefactive necrosis and tend to cause more damage than acidic agents. Patients with caustic agent exposure may present with gastrointestinal symptoms (burns in and around the mouth, odynophagia, dysphagia, drooling, and vomiting), dermatologic symptoms (burn marks where exposure occurred), respiratory symptoms (stridor, hoarse voice or cry, and hypoxia), and burning of the mucous membranes (such as tearing of the eyes and vision loss).

The first step in the management of a caustic exposure is to expose the patient, which involves removing all of the patient’s clothes. The patient’s airway should then be assessed. If there is any concern for airway loss, including hoarseness, stridor, and hypoxia, patients should be intubated before edema and swelling of the airway worsen and the procedure becomes technically challenging. Once the airway is secured, supportive therapy should occur, including the administration of IV fluids. It is important to check basic laboratory studies to assess for electrolyte derangements. Finally, gastroenterology should be consulted for endoscopy and further care. On the other hand, patients who appear well with a known caustic ingestion may not require intervention in the ED. However, they should still be admitted for an observation period.



Administering a 10 cc/kg bolus of normal saline (A) would be appropriate for this patient, as he is hypotensive. However, it would be more important to first remove the patient’s clothing to remove continued exposure and to intubate the patient (C), given his drooling (inability to tolerate oral secretions) and hoarse cry (suggesting airway involvement). Ultimately, consulting gastroenterology for endoscopy (B) will be needed after the patient is stabilized.

One Step Further
Question:
What type of necrosis is caused by acid exposure?

Reveal Answer:
Coagulative necrosis.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Caustic Ingestions

Presentation: chest pain, dysphagia, drooling
Alkali: corrosive damage with liquefactive necrosis
Acid: coagulation necrosis
Management: NPO, endoscopy, monitor airway
Monitor children with history of possible ingestion
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الطفل شرب bleach صناعي شديد التركيز، والمواد القلوية تسبب liquefactive necrosis وأشد ضرراً من الحوامض. الأعراض تشمل حروق حول الفم، وdrooling، وبحة بالصوت، وضيق نفس، وعلامات حرق على الصدر. أول خطوة بالعلاج هي expose المريض بواسطة إزالة كل ملابسه، لأنها مبللة بالمواد الكاوية ومستمرة بالتفاعل مع الجلد. بعدها يُقيّم المجرى الهوائي وينوب التنبيب إذا كان في بحة أو صرير أو نقص أكسجة.

question: A 5-day-old full-term girl presents to the emergency department with her parents for vomiting and feeding intolerance since discharge from the hospital 3 days ago. She has had decreased urine output and no stool output since yesterday. Her vital signs include rectal temperature 37.8°C, heart rate 180 bpm, blood pressure 74/42 mm Hg, respiratory rate 55/minute, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. On exam, she appears lethargic and her shirt is covered in green emesis. Her abdomen is soft and she weakly grimaces with palpation. An intravenous fluid bolus of 20 mL/kg is started and bloodwork is sent. Her abdominal X-ray is shown above. What is this patient’s most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Necrotizing enterocolitis is the most common neonatal gastrointestinal emergency. Risk factors include prematurity, congenital heart disease, and sepsis. Notably, 10% of patients with this disease are full-term. Abdominal X-rays are the gold standard for diagnosis but may only show nonspecific bowel loop dilatation. Findings of air within the portal venous system or the bowel wall (pneumatosis intestinalis) is pathognomonic but is only found in 75% of cases. The pathophysiology is not completely understood. It is thought to be due to direct injury or inflammation within the bowel wall that allows for translocation of gut flora into the wall layers leading to subsequent infection and necrosis. Despite treatment, this disease carries a mortality of 30%. Most commonly, patients present within the first 2–3 weeks of life. Patients will present with poor feeding and emesis with or without signs of a severe systemic infection. With such a high mortality, immediate and aggressive treatment is indicated at the time of clinical suspicion. Treatment includes intravenous fluid resuscitation, gastric decompression, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and immediate surgical consultation. Common antibiotic regimens are piperacillin-tazobactam and gentamicin or ampicillin, gentamicin, and metronidazole.



Duodenal atresia (A)is the congenital absence of the lumen connecting the foregut and midgut. It presents within hours of birth with bilious emesis, and the pathognomonic abdominal X-ray finding is the double bubble sign.

Malrotation volvulus (B) is a twisting of the midgut around itself due to a congenital failure of proper full rotation of the midgut itself. This malrotation leads to ischemia and gangrene of the intestines. The mainstay of diagnosis is an upper GI series, as abdominal X-rays rarely aid in the diagnosis.

Pyloric stenosis (D) is most common in first-born male patients and presents with nonbilious emesis. An abdominal exam may reveal an olive-like mass in the epigastric region. Abdominal ultrasound confirming this stenosis is the gold standard for diagnosis.

One Step Further
Question:
What are the doses of piperacillin-tazobactam and gentamicin for necrotizing enterocolitis treatment?

Reveal Answer:
Piperacillin-tazobactam 80 mg/kg every 6 hours and gentamicin 2.5 mg/kg every 8 hours.
