question: A 6-year-old boy presents with his parent for a cough. He is a previously healthy, fully immunized boy with a recent diagnosis of croup several days ago. At the initial visit, he was treated with nebulized epinephrine and oral dexamethasone and subsequently discharged home. His parent states he continued to improve until yesterday when he started developing higher fevers and noisy breathing, particularly at night. When the patient woke this morning, she noticed he had increased work of breathing and worsening noisy breathing. Vital signs are remarkable for a T of 102.2°F (39°C), HR of 140 bpm, RR of 45/min, BP of 90/50 mm Hg, and SpO2 of 93%. Exam is remarkable for a toxic-appearing young boy that is sitting upright but tolerating his secretions. Inspiratory stridor is noted on exam at rest with intercostal and suprasternal retractions. What is the most likely pathogen causing the patient's presentation?
englishExplanation:
Bacterial tracheitis is a serious infection that presents either as a primary or secondary infection. The mean age of presentation is between 5 and 7 years. The majority of cases occur in previously healthy children in the setting of a viral respiratory tract infection. Staphylococcus aureus is classically the most common causative organism. Typically, children will have prodromal signs and symptoms of a viral respiratory tract infection for 1–3 days before more severe signs of illness develop (secondary bacterial tracheitis). In a minority of children, the onset is fulminant, with progression to acute respiratory distress within 24 hours of the onset of symptoms (primary bacterial tracheitis). Most children with fulminant onset are toxic-appearing, presenting with fever and leukocytosis. Clinical features include significant respiratory distress, which will be more pronounced than with croup. Patients tend to appear toxic but can usually handle their oral secretions, which differs from epiglottitis. Securing the patient’s airway with endotracheal intubation is part of the typical management, as > 85% of patients require endotracheal intubation. Securing the airway is preferentially performed in the operating room or by the most experienced clinician available. Broad-spectrum antibiotics, such as ampicillin-sulbactam, should be started. If methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is a concern, vancomycin should be added to the regimen.



Haemophilus influenzae (A), Moraxella catarrhalis (B), and Streptococcus pneumoniae (D) are all potential causative organisms for the development of bacterial tracheitis. However, they are not as common as Staphylococcus aureus.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common predisposing illness to bacterial tracheitis?

Reveal Answer:
Despite croup being a common predisposing illness, influenza A is the most common associated viral infection.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Bacterial Tracheitis

Causes: Staphylococcus aureus (most common), Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus pyogenes, Moraxella catarrhalis, Haemophilus influenzae, MRSA
Mean age range is 5–7 years, but most cases occur in patients under 6 years
High fever, barking cough, stridor
Presentation: looks like croup but in toxic-appearing child
X-ray: subglottic narrowing (steeple sign), tracheal irregularities or membranes in the lumen
Treat as airway emergency!
arabicExplanation: ليش: الطفل عمره 6 سنين وعنده التهاب تنفسي فيروسي سابق متل الـ croup بعدها تدهورت حالته بحرارة أعلى وصوت تنفس أسوأ. هذا نمط bacterial tracheitis اللي غالباً بجي كالتهاب بكتيري ثانوي بعد عدوى فيروسية، ومتوسط العمر 5-7 سنوات. الـ Staphylococcus aureus هو الجرثوم الأكثر شيوعاً المسبب لهالحالة بشكل كلاسيكي. الطفل بيظهر toxic وبعاني من ضيق تنفس شديد بس عادة بيقدر يتحكم بالإفرازات، وهاد بيفرقه عن الـ epiglottitis. الفخ: في ناس بختاروا Haemophilus influenzae، بس هاد مرتبط بالـ epiglottitis عند غير المطعمين، والـ croup السابق وما بعده بيوجهنا ل Staphylococcus aureus.

question: A 5-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with difficulty breathing. According to his parent, he has had a fever of 102°F (38.9°C) for 2 days with a sore throat. He has not eaten anything since yesterday. Today he will not drink anything either, and he drools a lot. On examination, you find an ill-appearing child sitting straight up in bed. He grows very anxious when moved and does not want to lie down. He has tachycardia, tachypnea, and mild stridor on auscultation. What is the most appropriate next step for this patient?

options.text: Administer racemic epinephrine with humidified oxygen and oral steroids
Defer further agitation of the patient and consult anesthesiology or otolaryngology for emergent airway management
Obtain intravenous access and prepare for emergent endotracheal intubation

correctAnswer: Defer further agitation of the patient and consult anesthesiology or otolaryngology for emergent airway management
englishExplanation:
Although much less common in the era of vaccines, epiglottitis is a bacterial infection characterized by rapidly progressing inflammation around and of the epiglottis. If not treated appropriately, it can progress to life-threatening airway obstruction. Symptoms include respiratory distress in a patient preferring to maintain posture in the “sniffing” or upright position with dysphagia, muffled voice, and drooling. Patients with presumptive epiglottitis should be kept calm and all interventions that are anxiety-provoking, including intravenous access and use of a tongue blade for examination, should be deferred until appropriate resources and assistance are in place. In patients who appear to have impending airway compromise, specialists should be assembled to assist with airway management including anesthesiology or otolaryngology. Children < 6 years old or adults with > 50% obstruction of the laryngeal lumen on direct visualization or radiograph should have airway management performed in a controlled environment such as the operating room. If a patient cannot maintain oxygen saturation in the high 80s, even with the use of a bag-valve mask for ventilation, endotracheal intubation needs to be performed by the most experienced clinician with another clinician providing backup for an emergent needle cricothyrotomy in children or surgical cricothyrotomy in adults.



Administering racemic epinephrine with humidified oxygen and oral steroids (A) would be the appropriate treatment for croup. There was no report of cough to suggest croup in this patient, and the presence of anxiety out of proportion to respiratory distress should lead the clinician toward a diagnosis of epiglottitis instead of croup.

As already mentioned, patients with epiglottitis should have all anxiety-provoking procedures deferred until resources arrive. Therefore, obtaining intravenous access and preparing for emergent endotracheal intubation (C) would not be the best next step. Additionally, endotracheal intubation can be difficult in these patients and should generally be performed in a controlled environment or with backup assistance in place.

In patients with stridor and fever who appear to have impending airway obstruction, such as is the case in this patient, further evaluation and imaging should be deferred until the airway has been managed appropriately. This patient should not have a soft tissue neck radiograph (D) performed at this time.

One Step Further
Question:
For emergent airway management, a needle cricothyroidotomy should be performed in patients under what age?

Reveal Answer:
< 10–12 years of age.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Epiglottitis

Most commonly caused by H. influenzae (decrease since Hib vaccine), Streptococcus and Staphylococcus species
Sx: rapid onset of fever, muffled voice, dysphagia, respiratory distress
PE: sore throat, stridor, leaning forward, drooling, red swollen epiglottis on direct visualization
Imaging: enlarged epiglottis (thumbprint sign) on lateral neck X-ray
Tx: airway management and IV antibiotics (third-generation cephalosporin AND antistaphylococcal)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده epiglottitis، يعني التهاب بكتيري بيمتد بسرعة حول الـ epiglottis وممكن يسبب انسداد بالمجاري الهوائية ويهدد الحياة. الطفل هون قاعد مستقيم ويردّ ينام، وعنده drooling وصوت مخنوق، وهاد وضع خطير لازم نخلّيه هادي تماماً. لذلك الجواب الصح هو نأجّل أي إجراء يزعجه ونجيب anesthesiology أو otolaryngology ليتعاملوا مع المجرى الهوائي ببيئة مسيطر عليها.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (C) يعملوا IV وأدوات للـ intubation فوراً، بس هاد غلط لأن أي إزعاج أو وضع أنبوب ممكن يقفل المجرى الهوائي فجأة، فخلّيه هادي واستنّى الفريق المختص.

question: A 79-year-old woman presents to the ED with acute left thigh pain after tripping and falling at home. She did not hit her head or lose consciousness. Physical examination reveals left anteromedial thigh ecchymosis and irregular breast contours with skin thickening, nipple inversion, and areas of ulceration. An X-ray of her left femur reveals periosteal irregularity suggesting a pathological fracture. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Inflammatory carcinoma of the breast is an invasive type of breast cancer that is characterized by diffuse erythema and edema of the breast and thickened skin. This is due to dermal lymphatic invasion of cancer tissue and can lead to irregular breast contours and nipple inversion. The overlying skin can take on the appearance of orange peel (peau d’orange). A distinct underlying palpable mass may not be present. It accounts for 1–5% of all breast cancers in the US. Women are usually older at the time of diagnosis, in their 50s–60s. Given its invasive nature, metastatic lesions may be present at the time of diagnosis. This may include pathologic fractures, pulmonary involvement, or neurocognitive symptoms due to brain metastases. Risk factors for breast cancer include female sex, family history, older age, and increased levels of estrogen. Diagnosis is ultimately confirmed by biopsy. Medical therapy can be directed based on the expression of certain hormone receptors (e.g., estrogen, progesterone) and the overexpression of the human epidermal growth hormone receptor HER2/neu gene. The prognosis is poor, with a 5-year survival rate of around 50%.



Fibroadenoma (A) is a benign breast tumor that is small, firm, and mobile with sharp edges. It is common in women < 35 years old and is not a precursor to malignancy. Intraductal papilloma (C) is a small, benign subareolar tumor of the lactiferous ducts that typically causes a serous or bloody nipple discharge. Sclerosing adenosis (D) is in the category of fibrocystic breast disease, a benign condition in premenopausal women that typically causes premenstrual breast pain and lumps. It may mimic invasive carcinoma, but the difference can be appreciated microscopically.

One Step Further
Question:
What chemotherapy agent is used to treat breast cancer that overexpresses the HER2/neu gene?

Reveal Answer:
Trastuzumab.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Breast Cancer

Second most frequent cause of cancer death among female individuals in the United States
Risk factors: history of prior ovarian or breast cancer, a family history of breast or ovarian cancer, or a genetic predisposition such as BRCA1 or BRCA2
Dx: mammography and biopsy
Most common type is invasive ductal carcinoma
Tx: breast-conserving therapy (lumpectomy followed by radiation therapy) or mastectomy ± radiation therapy
Surgery should involve a sentinel lymph node biopsy
Adjuvant therapy depending on tumor and patient characteristics
Screening for patients with average risk:
USPSTF: biennial screening mammography for patients aged 40–74 years
NCCN: annual screening mammography with tomosynthesis starting at the age of 40
Breast self-examination should NOT be routinely encouraged
NCCN recommends patient breast awareness and reporting changes to a clinician
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ inflammatory carcinoma نوع invasive من سرطان الثدي، بيتميز باحمرار و edema منتشر بالثدي وجلد سميك، وهاد بسبب غزو الأوعية اللمفية الجلدية بالسرطان. هاد بيفسّر شكل الثدي غير المنتظم وانقلاب الـ nipple وظهور جلد مثل قشر البرتقال، وممكن ما يكون في كتلة محسوسة واضحة. وبما إنه invasive فممكن يكون في metastatic lesions وقت التشخيص مثل pathological fracture، وهاد مطابق لحالة المريضة.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (A) fibroadenoma لأنه شائع بالثدي، بس هو ورم سليم صغير وصلب ومتحرك وحدود حادة، وعادة عند نساء أصغر من 35 سنة وما بيسبب تغيّر بالجلد ولا كسور مرضية.

question: A 32-year-old man presents to the emergency department for dyspnea over the last 24 hours. He was seen 3 days ago in the same emergency department for a left leg injury due to a bicycle collision, at which time he was diagnosed with a tibia fracture. According to the medical record, he was neurovascularly intact at the time of the visit. The fracture was treated with closed reduction and posterior long leg splinting, and he was discharged with outpatient orthopedics follow-up. His current vital signs are a T of 97.4°F (36.3°C), BP of 122/82 mm Hg, HR of 108 bpm, RR of 22/min, and SpO2 of 91% on room air. Which of the following additional findings would most likely be present, given the most likely underlying cause of the patient’s current condition?

options.text: Diminished pedal pulses on the left
Tense anterior compartment of the left leg

englishExplanation:
Fat embolism is a complication of long bone fractures or major trauma that is characterized by fat globules in the peripheral circulation and lung parenchyma. Fat embolism syndrome is a rare, serious condition associated with acute respiratory failure, neurocognitive impairment, and possible death. It occurs most commonly after long bone fractures (e.g., tibia, femur) in young adults and hip fractures in older patients. It can also occur in cases of nonorthopedic trauma, burns, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Fat embolism syndrome is more common in male individuals and has a peak incidence between ages 10 and 40 years, likely reflecting the higher incidence of trauma in this age group. The exact pathogenesis is not known, but the prevailing theory suggests that mechanical disruption of bone marrow or adipose tissue releases fat globules into the peripheral circulation.

The most common and earliest manifestations of fat embolism syndrome are respiratory distress and hypoxemia, commonly followed by neurologic impairment (e.g., confusion, agitation) and thrombocytopenia with a petechial rash. Symptoms typically begin 24–72 hours after the initial insult. Other findings include fever, tachycardia, jaundice, and kidney involvement, which may be apparent by fat detected in the urine. CT imaging may show focal consolidation or ground-glass opacities. However, fat embolism syndrome is primarily diagnosed clinically, so there are no particular diagnostic imaging or laboratory findings.

Treatment of fat embolism syndrome is primarily supportive, aimed at treating the associated condition (e.g., long bone fracture) and supporting respiratory function. Exchange transfusion is often needed in cases of fat embolism syndrome in patients with sickle cell disease. Most patients with fat embolism syndrome will recover spontaneously when properly supported in the acute setting, but complications include ARDS and death. Generally, symptoms resolve within a few days or up to a week in more severe cases.



Diffuse bilateral crackles (A) can be appreciated in a variety of contexts, including ARDS, multifocal pneumonia, and cardiogenic pulmonary edema. While ARDS is possible after trauma, this patient’s isolated tibial fracture is less likely to be complicated by ARDS than by fat embolism. Vascular compromise in the setting of fractures, manifesting as reduced pedal pulses (B), can occur as a result of direct vascular injury or compartment syndrome. Neither of these would cause respiratory involvement and are thus unlikely to be occurring in this case. A tense muscular compartment (D) would signify that this patient’s fracture is complicated by compartment syndrome. However, this would not present with respiratory involvement and is less likely for this presentation.

One Step Further
Question:
What condition similar to fat embolism syndrome may present following cosmetic injections or surgical procedures?

Reveal Answer:
Silicone embolism syndrome.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Fat Embolism

Often presents in patients with hip or long bone fracture
Sx or findings: hypoxia, respiratory distress, neurological changes, petechial rash
Tx: supportive care
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده fat embolism syndrome، وهاد من مضاعفات كسور العظام الطويلة مثل الـ tibia، ومعظم المصابين شباب بعمر 10 لـ 40 سنة. الأعراض بتبدأ عادة بعد 24 لـ 72 ساعة من الإصابة، وأول وأشهر شي هو ضيق النفس ونقص الأكسجة. بعدها بتيجي أعراض عصبية مثل confusion وagitation، وكمان thrombocytopenia مع petechial rash، وهاد اللي بيميز المتلازمة فالجواب (C).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (D) tense anterior compartment لأنه فكّروا بالـ compartment syndrome بعد الكسر، بس هون في dyspnea وتدهور تنفسي 3 أيام بعد الإصابة وهاد يمشي مع fat embolism أكثر، والعلامة المميزة هي الـ petechial rash.

question:
A 5-year-old presents with fever, rash, and bilateral conjunctival injection for 6 days.
Which of the following is NOT part of the possible treatments for Kawasaki Disease?
englishExplanation:
Ceftriaxone
Explanation
Treatments fpr Kawasaki Disease include:
Aspirin - Initially high-dose for anti-inflammatory effect, then low-dose for antiplatelet effect
IVIG - Reduces inflammation and risk of coronary artery aneurysms
Corticosteroids - Particularly beneficial in high-risk patients
Infliximab - Used in IVIG-resistant cases
Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic which has no role in the treatment of Kawasaki.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: السؤال بيسأل عن العلاج اللي مش من ضمن علاجات Kawasaki disease، والعلاجات المعروفة هي aspirin بالبداية بجرعة عالية كمضاد التهاب وبعدها جرعة منخفضة كمضاد صفائح. كمان في IVIG لتقليل الالتهاب وخطر aneurysms الشرايين التاجية، وcorticosteroids للمرضى عاليي الخطورة، وinfliximab للحالات اللي ما استجابت للـ IVIG. أما ceftriaxone فمضاد حيوي وما إله أي دور في علاج Kawasaki لذلك هو الجواب.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (C) systemic corticosteroids لأنهم بيعرفوا إن الستيرويدات تُستخدم بأمراض التهابية، بس بالـ Kawasaki هي جزء من العلاج خصوصاً بالمرضى عاليي الخطورة، والصح إن ceftriaxone هو اللي ما إله دور.

question:
A 5-year-old boy presents with a purpuric rash on his lower extremities, abdominal pain, and joint swelling. He is
diagnosed with Henoch-Schönlein purpura (HSP).
Which of the following is the most common serious complication of HSP?
englishExplanation:
Renal impairment
Explanation
Renal impairment is the most common serious complication of HSP, occurring in approximately 30-50% of cases. It
can range from mild proteinuria and haematuria to severe nephritis and renal failure—the other options, while potential complications of HSP, are less common.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده Henoch-Schönlein purpura، والـ renal impairment هو أشهر مضاعفة خطيرة للمرض وبيصيب حوالي 30 لـ 50 بالمئة من الحالات. الإصابة بالكلى تتراوح من proteinuria و haematuria بسيطة لحد nephritis شديد وrenal failure. باقي الخيارات ممكن تصير مضاعفات لكنها أقل شيوعاً بكثير من إصابة الكلى، وهاد اللي بيخلي الجواب (D).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (B) intussusception لأنه عارفين إنه مرتبط بالـ HSP لما يصير ألم بالبطن، بس هو أقل شيوعاً من إصابة الكلى، فانتبه إن السؤال بيسأل عن الأشهر والأخطر مش أي مضاعفة ممكنة.

question:
A 7-year-old child is discharged from the Emergency Department following treatment for an acute asthma
exacerbation.
What is the most appropriate follow-up plan?

options.text: Follow-up with GP within 24 hours only
Follow-up with GP within 48 hours and specialist review in 1 month
Follow-up with GP within 1 week only
No follow-up is required if symptoms have resolved

correctAnswer: Follow-up with GP within 48 hours and specialist review in 1 month
englishExplanation:
Follow-up with GP within 48 hours and specialist review in 1 month
Explanation
The correct answer reflects the best practice guidelines for asthma follow-up care in children. The 48-hour GP review
is crucial for assessing the child's recovery, reviewing the inhaler technique, and ensuring the acute episode has fully
resolved. The 1-month specialist review allows for comprehensive asthma control assessment and medication adjustment if needed.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل طلع من الطوارئ بعد علاج acute asthma exacerbation، وأفضل خطة متابعة هي مراجعة الـ GP خلال 48 ساعة ومراجعة اختصاصي بعد شهر. مراجعة الـ 48 ساعة مهمة لتقييم تعافي الطفل ومراجعة طريقة استخدام الـ inhaler والتأكد إن النوبة خلصت بالكامل. ومراجعة الشهر مع الاختصاصي بتسمح بتقييم السيطرة على الربو وضبط الأدوية إذا لزم.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (E) ما في حاجة لمتابعة إذا خفّت الأعراض، وهاد غلط لأن الأعراض بترجع وممكن تكون السيطرة على الربو سيئة بدون مراجعة، فالمتابعة القريبة ضرورية حتى لو الطفل صار أحسن.

question:
A 3-year-old child presents to the Emergency Department with acute-onset respiratory distress after playing with
small toys. The child shows signs of respiratory compromise, with increased work of breathing, tachypnoea, and
oxygen saturation of 89% despite being on high-flow nasal oxygen. Chest examination reveals decreased air entry
on the right side with wheeze.
What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Perform chest X-ray before any intervention

englishExplanation:
Immediate rigid bronchoscopy
Explanation
In a child with suspected foreign body aspiration who is unstable despite high-flow oxygen, immediate rigid bronchoscopy is the definitive management. Delays in removing the foreign body can lead to complete airway obstruction,
tissue damage, and death.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده suspected foreign body aspiration وواضح إنه unstable رغم الـ high-flow oxygen، وهاد بيعني خطر انسداد كامل بالمجرى الهوائي. الجواب الصح هو immediate rigid bronchoscopy لأنها الإجراء النهائي اللي بيشيل الجسم الغريب، وأي تأخير ممكن يسبب tissue damage وموت. علامات مثل نقص دخول الهواء على جهة اليمين مع wheeze بتدعم وجود جسم غريب.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (D) nebulized bronchodilators لأنهم فكّروا بالربو من صوت الـ wheeze، بس الطفل unstable بعد الأكسجين وهاد جسم غريب مش تشنج قصبي، فتضييع الوقت بالموسعات خطر وممنوع.

question:
A 3-year-old child presents to the emergency department with a barking cough and mild respiratory distress. There
is no stridor at rest or on agitation. The diagnosis of croup is made, and you decide to administer dexamethasone.
What is the recommended single oral dose of dexamethasone for this patient?
englishExplanation:
0.15 mg/kg
Explanation
The recommended single oral dose of dexamethasone for croup is 0.15 mg/kg. This dosage is effective in reducing the
severity and duration of croup symptoms as much as 0.6mg/kg.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده croup مع كحة نباحية وضيق نفس بسيط وما في stridor وقت الراحة ولا عند الإزعاج. الجرعة الصحيحة من dexamethasone بالفم هي 0.15 mg/kg جرعة واحدة، وهاد الجواب (A). هالجرعة فعالة بتخفيف شدة ومدة أعراض الـ croup بقدر ما تفعل جرعة 0.6 mg/kg، فما في داعي نعطي جرعة أكبر.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (C) 0.6 mg/kg لأنهم شايفين رقم أكبر وأقوى، بس هالجرعة ما بتعطي فايدة إضافية عن الـ 0.15 mg/kg، والصح إن الجرعة الموصى بها هي الأقل لأنها بنفس الفعالية.

question:
A 5-year-old boy presents to the Emergency Department with an acute ankle injury requiring reduction. You are
considering procedural sedation with ketamine.
Which of the following is NOT a contraindication to ketamine use?
englishExplanation:
Controlled asthma
Explanation
Controlled asthma is not a contraindication to ketamine use.
Contraindications In addition to general contraindications:
• Pulmonary Hypertension

• Age less than 12 months due to an increased risk of laryngospasm and airway complications
• A high risk of laryngospasm (active respiratory infection, active asthma)
• Unstable or abnormal airway. Tracheal surgery or stenosis.
• Active upper or lower respiratory tract infection
• Proposed procedure within the mouth or pharynx
• Patients with severe psychological problems such as cognitive or motor delay or severe behavioural problems
• Significant cardiac disease (angina, heart failure, malignant hypertension)
• Intracranial hypertension with CSF obstruction
• Intra-ocular pathology (glaucoma, penetrating injury)
• Previous psychotic illness
• Uncontrolled epilepsy
• Hyperthyroidism or Thyroid medication
• Porphyria
• Prior adverse reaction to ketamine
• Altered conscious level due to acute illness or injury
• Drug / alcohol intoxication

question:
A 1-week-old infant presents with multiple small (1-2mm) pearly-white papules on the nose and cheeks.
Observations are normal, and examination apart from the papules is unremarkable.

Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
englishExplanation:
Reassurance
Explanation
Milia are benign, keratin-filled cysts that commonly occur in newborns and infants. They appear as small, white to
yellowish, dome-shaped papules typically on the nose, cheeks, and chin.
Milia in infants are self-limiting and typically resolve spontaneously within the first few months of life. No treatment
is necessary, and parents should be reassured about their benign nature.

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00738 source page 1454](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00738-frcem-p1454.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده milia، وهي أكياس كيراتين حميدة بتصير بالأطفال حديثي الولادة وتظهر كحبيبات بيضاء صغيرة على الأنف والخدين والذقن. الـ milia محدودة بذاتها وبتختفي لحالها خلال الأشهر الأولى من العمر بدون أي علاج. فالخطة الصح هي طمأنة الأهل، وهاد الجواب (C)، والفحص والملاحظات كلها طبيعية.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (B) topical retinoid لأنه فكّروا بمشكلة جلدية تحتاج علاج، بس أي علاج هون غير ضروري وممكن يضر بشرة الرضيع، والـ milia بتختفي لحالها فمجرد الطمأنة كافية.

question:
A 6-year-old child presents to the Emergency Department with an acute severe asthma exacerbation. Initial treatment with nebulized salbutamol and ipratropium has shown minimal improvement. The decision is made to start
IV aminophylline.
What is the correct loading dose of IV aminophylline for this child?
englishExplanation:
5 mg/kg over 20 minutes
Explanation
The correct loading dose of IV aminophylline for children with acute severe asthma is 5 mg/kg given over 20 minutes,
followed by a maintenance infusion.
https://bnfc.nice.org.uk/drugs/aminophylline/

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00739 source page 621](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00739-study-p621.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00739 source page 622](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00739-study-p622.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده acute severe asthma exacerbation وما تحسن بشكل واضح من nebulized salbutamol وipratropium، وهون نبدأ IV aminophylline. جرعة الـ loading الصحيحة للأطفال هي 5 mg/kg تُعطى على مدى 20 دقيقة، وبعدها maintenance infusion. هالجرعة المعطاة ببطء بتوصل للمستوى العلاجي بأمان، فهي الجواب (B).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (D) 10 mg/kg لأنهم بيظنوا إن الجرعة الأعلى أسرع بالتحسن، بس إعطاء جرعة كبيرة بسرعة ممكن يسبب سمية وأعراض جانبية خطيرة مثل اضطراب نظم القلب، والصح هو الـ 5 mg/kg.

question:
A 14-year-old male presents to the Emergency Department with anterior knee pain that has been present for 3
months. The pain is worse with physical activity, particularly running and jumping. On examination, there is tenderness and swelling over the tibial tuberosity.
Which of the following is the most appropriate management plan?

options.text: Complete rest from all physical activities for 6 months
Activity modification and quadriceps stretching exercises
Long-term knee immobilization with a cast
Emergency MRI scan of the knee

correctAnswer: Activity modification and quadriceps stretching exercises
englishExplanation:
Activity modification and quadriceps stretching exercises
Explanation
Osgood-Schlatter disease is a common cause of knee pain in adolescents during their growth spurt. It is an overuse injury affecting the tibial tuberosity where the patellar tendon attaches. The correct management involves activity modification to reduce pain while maintaining function, along with specific stretching exercises.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده anterior knee pain لفترة 3 شهور بتزيد مع الرياضة خصوصاً الجري والقفز، مع tenderness و swelling على الـ tibial tuberosity، وهاد Osgood-Schlatter disease. هي إصابة overuse بالمكان اللي بيتصل فيه الـ patellar tendon بعظم الظنبوب، وبتصير بالمراهقين خلال طفرة النمو. فالعلاج هو تعديل النشاط مع تمارين إطالة للـ quadriceps، وهاد الخيار (C).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (A) immediate knee arthroscopy أو (E) emergency MRI لأنهم متخوفين من إصابة داخلية، بس الحالة overuse مزمنة وما فيها علامات حادة، والصور والجراحة ما إلهم داعي بالبداية.

question:
An 8-year-old boy weighing 25kg presents to the Emergency Department with gastroenteritis. He requires maintenance fluid therapy.
What is the correct hourly maintenance fluid rate?
englishExplanation:
65ml/hr
Explanation
For calculating maintenance fluids in children, use the Holliday-Segar formula:
First 10kg: 4ml/kg/hr (10 × 4 = 40ml/hr)
Second 10kg: 2ml/kg/hr (10 × 2 = 20ml/hr)
Remaining kg: 1ml/kg/hr (5 × 1 = 5ml/hr)
Total = 40 + 20 + 5 = 65ml/hr
https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng29/chapter/recommendations
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل وزنه 25 kg ولازم نحسب الـ maintenance fluids بقاعدة Holliday-Segar. أول 10 kg بتاخد 4 ml/kg/hr يعني 40، وعشر الكيلو التانية بتاخد 2 ml/kg/hr يعني 20، والباقي 5 kg بتاخد 1 ml/kg/hr يعني 5. مجموع هالنواتج 40 زائد 20 زائد 5 بيعطي 65 ml/hr، وهاد الجواب (B).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (C) 85 ml/hr لأنهم بيحسبوا كل الوزن بمعدل موحّد بدل تقسيم الكيلوات، بس القاعدة بتقسّم الوزن لأجزاء بمعدلات مختلفة، واللي بيعطي الرقم الصح هو 65.

question:
A 3-year-old presents to the ED with fever, lethargy, and poor perfusion. Initial assessment reveals tachycardia,
prolonged capillary refill, and cool peripheries.

What is the most appropriate initial fluid management?
englishExplanation:
Balanced crystalloid 10ml/kg bolus
Explanation
According to the 2021 paediatric advanced life support guidelines regarding fluid choice in circulatory failure:
If available, use balanced isotonic crystalloids as the first choice of fluid bolus. If not, normal saline (0.9%) is an acceptable alternative.
https://www.resus.org.uk/print/pdf/node/11331
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده علامات shock من fever، lethargy، tachycardia، تأخر capillary refill وأطراف باردة. حسب guidelines الإنعاش المتقدم للأطفال لعام 2021، أول شي باختيار السوائل هو balanced isotonic crystalloid إذا متوفر، وإذا ما توفر فالـ normal saline مقبول كبديل. فالجواب الصح هو balanced crystalloid بجرعة 10 ml/kg bolus.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (A) normal saline 20 ml/kg لأنه الجرعة الكلاسيكية القديمة، بس الـ balanced crystalloid هو الأفضل بالاختيار، وبعض الحالات عندها خطر من جرعات كبيرة من الـ saline، فاختار الـ 10 ml/kg من الـ balanced.

question:
A 5-year-old female presents to the Emergency Department with widespread petechiae and epistaxis lasting more
than 5 minutes. Her observations are normal. Her platelet count is 15 x 10^9/L.
Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
englishExplanation:
Oral prednisolone 1mg/kg/day
Explanation
The first-line treatment is oral corticosteroids in ITP with platelets >10 x 10^9/L without significant bleeding.
IVIG (C) is reserved for emergencies with severe bleeding or very low platelets.
Platelet transfusion (A) is not routinely indicated unless life-threatening bleeding exists.

Splenectomy (D) is a second-line treatment after failure of medical management.
Observation (E) alone is inappropriate, given the low platelet count and symptoms.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: البنت عندها widespread petechiae و epistaxis و platelet count 15 x 10^9/L، وهاد ITP. العلاج الأول في الـ ITP مع صفائح أكبر من 10 وأعراض نزف بسيطة هو oral corticosteroids، يعني oral prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day. هاد الجواب (B) لأن الحالة ما فيها نزف مهدد للحياة ولا صفائح أقل من 10.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (C) IVIG لأنهم فاكرينه العلاج الأول، بس الـ IVIG محجوز للحالات الطارئة مع نزف شديد أو صفائح منخفضة جداً، وفي حالات مثل هون الستيرويدات الفموية أول خط، والـ platelet transfusion ما بيُعطى إلا بنزف مهدد للحياة.

question:
A 2-month-old infant presents to the Emergency Department with a 3-day history of cough, rhinorrhoea, and increasing work of breathing.
Which of the following factors puts this patient at highest risk for severe bronchiolitis?
englishExplanation:
Age under 3 months
Explanation
Age under 3 months is one of the most significant risk factors for severe bronchiolitis. Young infants in this age group
are particularly vulnerable due to their immature immune and pulmonary systems. Other risk factors are:
Chronic lung disease (including bronchopulmonary dysplasia).
Haemodynamically significant congenital heart disease.
Neuromuscular disorders.
Immunodeficiency.
The infant having been born prematurely, particularly before 32 gestational weeks.
https://cks.nice.org.uk/topics/cough-acute-with-chest-signs-in-children/management/bronchiolitis/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الرضيع عمره شهرين وعنده cough و rhinorrhoea مع زيادة بالجهد التنفسي، وهاد bronchiolitis. أهم عامل خطر ل bronchiolitis الشديد هو العمر أقل من 3 شهور، لأن الرضع بهالعمر عندهم جهاز مناعي ورئوي غير ناضج. لذلك الجواب (B)، وفي عوامل أخرى مثل chronic lung disease والـ congenital heart disease و prematurity والمناعة الضعيفة.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (E) exposure to second-hand smoke أو (D) family history of asthma، بس هذول عوامل مساعدة وليست الأقوى، والعمر أقل من 3 شهور هو العامل الأخطر لأنه بيجعل الرضيع أكثر عرضة للإصابة الشديدة.

question: Which one of these blood gas results from a child would be categorized as mild DKA?
englishExplanation:
pH 7.29 bicarb 15, glucose 33
Explanation
According to the British Society for Paediatric Endocrinology and Diabetes (BSPED), children who are diagnosed with
DKA should be classified as follows:
Mild DKA - A patient with a pH of 7.20-7.29 and/or bicarbonate <15 mmol/L,
Moderate DKA - A patient with a pH 7.10-7.19 and/or bicarbonate <10 mmol/L
Severe DKA - A patient with a pH <7.10 and/or bicarbonate <5 mmol/L
https://www.bsped.org.uk/media/1959/dka-guidelines.pdf
arabicExplanation:
ليش: السؤال عن تصنيف الـ DKA الخفيف حسب British Society for Paediatric Endocrinology and Diabetes. الـ mild DKA هو pH بين 7.20 و7.29 و/أو bicarbonate أقل من 15، والـ moderate هو pH من 7.10 لـ 7.19 و/أو bicarbonate أقل من 10، والـ severe هو pH أقل من 7.10 و/أو bicarbonate أقل من 5. فحسب هالتصنيف، pH 7.29 مع bicarbonate 15 هو الحد الفاصل للـ mild، وهاد الجواب (B).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (A) pH 7.30 مع bicarbonate 22 لأنه بيحسوه قريب من الطبيعي، بس هالقيم هي ضمن الطبيعي وما بشكل DKA من الأصل، والـ DKA الخفيف لازم pH أقل من 7.30 وبيكربونات منخفضة.

question:
A 14-year-old female presents to the Emergency Department with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). She has been vomiting for the past 24 hours and appears drowsy. Her vital signs show BP 135/85 mmHg (previously 110/70), HR 85
(previously 110), and she complains of a headache.
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Continue IV insulin infusion as per protocol

englishExplanation:
Give 3% hypertonic saline
Explanation
This patient shows multiple early warning signs of cerebral odema in DKA: headache, unexpected fall in heart rate
(from 110 to 85), and increased blood pressure (from 110/70 to 135/85). BSPED recommends 3% hypertonic saline or
mannitol. Hypertonic saline is preferred as mannitol has significant osmotic diuretic effects.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: البنت عندها DKA وظهرت علامات إنذار مبكر ل cerebral oedema وهي صداع، ونزول غير متوقع بنبض القلب من 110 لـ 85، وارتفاع ضغط الدم من 110/70 لـ 135/85. هالعلامات بتدعم بداية الوذمة الدماغية. الـ BSPED بتوصي بإعطاء 3% hypertonic saline أو mannitol، والـ hypertonic saline مفضّل لأن الـ mannitol إله تأثير مدر للبول تناضحي قوي، فالجواب (E).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (C) administer mannitol لأنه معروف بالوذمة الدماغية، بس الـ hypertonic saline هو المفضّل لأنه ما بيسبب الخسارة الكبيرة بالسوائل، والـ mannitol محجوز كبديل ثاني بالبروتوكول.

question:
A 3-month-old infant presents to the Emergency Department with
scaly patches on the scalp. The mother reports that the rash started 2
weeks ago. The infant is otherwise well, feeding normally, and has no
fever.

Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management
for this infant's condition?
englishExplanation:
Massage emollient onto the scalp
Explanation
The initial management of infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis involves
massaging a topical emollient onto the scalp to loosen scales, then removing them using an infant brush or fine-tooth comb before washing
with a suitable shampoo.
https://cks.nice.org.uk/topics/seborrhoeic-dermatitis/management/seborrhoeic-dermatitis-infants/

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00763 source page 634](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00763-study-p634.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00763 source page 1485](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00763-frcem-p1485.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00763 source page 1486](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00763-frcem-p1486.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00763 source page 1487](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00763-frcem-p1487.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الرضيع عنده scaly patches على فروة الرأس بعمر 3 شهور، وهاد infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis. العلاج الأولي هو تدليك emollient على فروة الرأس لتفكيك القشور، وبعدها إزالة القشور بفرشاة ناعمة أو مشط بأسنان دقيقة قبل الغسل بشامبو مناسب. فالطفل صح وحالته عامة جيدة وما في حاجة لعلاج جهازي، وهاد الجواب (D).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (B) oral antifungal أو (C) topical steroid، بس هاي الحالة بسيطة وتُعالج بشيء موضعي لطيف، والعلاج المضاد للفطريات أو الستيرويد ما إلهم داعي بالخطوة الأولى.

question:
A 4-year-old child presents to the Emergency Department after ingesting a single rare earth magnet while playing.
X-rays confirm that the magnet is in the stomach. The child is asymptomatic and tolerating oral intake, and the ingestion occurred 6 hours ago.
Which of the following is the most appropriate management plan?

options.text: Discharge home with safety-netting advice and follow-up X-rays

correctAnswer: Discharge home with safety-netting advice and follow-up X-rays
englishExplanation:
Discharge home with safety-netting advice and follow-up X-rays
Explanation
Discharge with appropriate safety-netting advice is appropriate for single magnet ingestion in an otherwise healthy
child who is asymptomatic, tolerates oral intake, and has reliable caregivers for observation. This is because single
magnets will typically pass through the gastrointestinal tract without complications.
Follow-up AXRs should continue to be performed until it can be demonstrated (and confirmed by a radiologist) that
the magnet has passed through the stomach and serial X-rays (at least 6-12hrs apart) show that it is progressing
through the small bowel or beyond.
https://rcem.ac.uk/wpcontent/uploads/2021/10/RCEM_BPC_Ingestion_of_Super_Strong_Magnets_in_Children_170521.pdf
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل بلع مغناطيس واحد وهو asymptomatic ويتحمل الأكل، والمغناطيس بالمعدة وصار 6 ساعات. المغناطيس الواحد عادة بيمشي بالجهاز الهضمي بدون مضاعفات، فالتصرف الصح هو discharge بآمان ونصيحة safety-netting مع متابعة X-rays. المتابعة بالأشعة بتبقى لحد ما نبين إنه تجاوز المعدة والأمعاء الدقيقة، وهاد الجواب (C).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (A) immediate surgical removal أو (E) endoscopic removal، بس هذول بيتعملوا عند وجود علامات انسداد أو مغناطيسات متعددة أو بلع جسم خطير، أما مغناطيس وحيد بحالة مستقرة فيُترك يمشي لحاله.

question:
A 6-month-old infant presents to the Emergency Department with anxious parents concerned about a bluish-grey
patch on the baby's lower back and buttocks noticed during a nappy change. The child's observations are normal,
and the examination is unremarkable, apart from the abnormality noted below.

Which of the following is the most appropriate management approach?

options.text: Skeletal survey and child protection referral

englishExplanation:
Reassurance and discharge
Explanation
Mongolian blue spots (Congenital dermal melanocytosis) are common birthmarks that appear as flat, bluish-grey
patches, typically on the lower back and buttocks. 
They are completely benign and:
Present in up to 90% of Asian, Native American, and African infants
Result from melanocytes trapped in the dermis during embryonic migration
Usually fades by school age
Require no treatment

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00771 source page 640](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00771-study-p640.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00771 source page 641](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00771-study-p641.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00771 source page 1499](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00771-frcem-p1499.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00771 source page 1500](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00771-frcem-p1500.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00771 source page 1501](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00771-frcem-p1501.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الرضيع عمره 6 شهور وعنده patch رمادي مزرق على أسفل الظهر والأرداف، وهاد Mongolian blue spots أو congenital dermal melanocytosis. هاي شامات حميدة شائعة جداً، بتصير عند نسبة كبيرة من الرضع من أصول آسيوية وأفريقية، ونتيجة لانحباس الـ melanocytes بالـ dermis أثناء الهجرة الجنينية. بتختفي لحالها غالباً بعمر المدرسة وما بتحتاج أي علاج، فالجواب (C) طمأنة وخروج.
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (D) skeletal survey و child protection referral لأنهم شايفين الشامات الزرقاء زي الكدمات، بس هي تشوهات جلدية حميدة ومحددة شكلها ومكانها، وما إلها علاقة بالإساءة.

question:
A 4-year-old unvaccinated child presents to the Emergency Department with fever, cough, and coryza for 3 days.
On examination of the mouth, you see a rash.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Measles
Explanation
Koplik spots are pathognomonic for measles. They appear as bluish-white spots on a red background on the buccal
mucosa, typically 2-3 days before the characteristic maculopapular rash. They are a valuable early diagnostic sign.

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00776 source page 644](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00776-study-p644.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00776 source page 1508](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00776-frcem-p1508.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00776 source page 1509](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00776-frcem-p1509.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00776 source page 1510](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00776-frcem-p1510.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل غير مطعّم وعنده fever و cough و coryza من 3 أيام، والفحص بالفم بيبيّن rash. الـ Koplik spots هي العلامة المميزة للـ measles، وتظهر كنقاط زرقاء بيضاء على خلفية حمراء على الـ buccal mucosa، وعادة قبل الـ maculopapular rash بيومين أو 3 أيام. فهي علامة تشخيصية مبكرة مهمة وبتحدد الجواب (C).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (A) scarlet fever أو (B) hand, foot and mouth disease لأنهم شايفين طفح، بس الـ Koplik spots خاصة بالـ measles، والطفل غير مطعّم وعنده أعراض الأنف والحلق اللي تمشي مع الحصبة.

question:
A 9-month-old infant is brought to the Emergency Department by
his anxious parents after choking while eating small pieces of apple.
The child is conscious but showing signs of ineffective cough and increasing respiratory distress.

After delivering 5 back blows between the shoulder blades, which
prove unsuccessful, what is the next most appropriate step in management?

options.text: Continue with back blows until effective
Attempt finger sweep of the mouth
Proceed directly to basic life support

englishExplanation:
Deliver 5 chest thrusts
Explanation
In infants under 1 year of age, after 5 unsuccessful back blows, the next
step is to deliver 5 chest thrusts. This is performed by turning the infant
supine and delivering 5 quick thrusts to the lower half of the sternum.
Chest thrusts create an artificial cough by suddenly forcing air out of
the lungs.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الرضيع عمره 9 شهور وبيلع جسم غريب وصار عنده ineffective cough وضيق تنفس متزايد، وهون always 5 back blows أول شي. بعدها إذا ما نفعت هالخمس، الخطوة الثانية عند الرضع أقل من سنة هي 5 chest thrusts، واللي بتتعمل بقلب الرضيع على ظهره وإعطاء 5 دفعات سريعة على النصف السفلي من القص. فالـ chest thrusts بتعمل كحة صناعية بتطرد الهواء بقوة، وهاد الجواب (C).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (B) abdominal thrusts أو (D) finger sweep، بس هذول ممنوعين بالرضع أقل من سنة بسبب خطر إصابة الكبد والأعضاء، والـ finger sweep ممكن يدفع الجسم الغريب أعمق، والصحيح هو الـ chest thrusts.

question:
A 4-year-old child presents to the Emergency Department with a fever of 39.2°C and severe ear pain.
Which of the following statements about paracetamol dosing is correct?

options.text: A loading dose of 20mg/kg oral paracetamol can be given, followed by maintenance doses of 15mg/kg every 4
A loading dose of 30mg/kg oral paracetamol should be given for rapid pain relief
The maximum daily dose should not exceed 60mg/kg/day
The loading dose should be given intravenously for better absorption
The loading dose should be calculated based on ideal body weight

correctAnswer: A loading dose of 20mg/kg oral paracetamol can be given, followed by maintenance doses of 15mg/kg every 4
englishExplanation:
A loading dose of 20mg/kg oral paracetamol can be given, followed by maintenance doses of 15mg/kg every 4 hours
Explanation
A loading dose of 20mg/kg oral paracetamol is safe and effective for initial pain management in children, followed by
maintenance doses of 15mg/kg every 4-6 hours. This regimen helps achieve therapeutic levels more quickly while
staying within safe limits. The maximum daily dose can be 75mg/kg/day in children (not exceeding 4g in 24 hours).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده fever و ear pain ومنحتاج نعرف الدوزينغ الصح للـ paracetamol. الجرعة الصحيحة هي loading dose من 20 mg/kg بالفم، وبعدها maintenance doses من 15 mg/kg كل 4 لـ 6 ساعات. هالنظام بيوصل للمستوى العلاجي أسرع وبأمان أثناء البقاء بالحدود الآمنة. والحد الأقصى اليومي ممكن يكون 75 mg/kg/day عند الأطفال بدون تجاوز 4 غرام خلال 24 ساعة، وهاد الخيار (A).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (C) الحد اليومي 60 mg/kg/day، بس هالرقم أقل من الحد الفعلي وهو 75 mg/kg/day، وأيضاً في ناس بيختاروا (B) 30 mg/kg كجرعة تحميل وهاد مبالغ فيه.

question:
A 4-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of fatigue, pallor, and bruising. His
mother reports he has been complaining of bone pain, particularly in his legs. On examination, he has cervical lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly. His blood tests show Hb 8.2 g/dL, WBC 32 x 10^9/L with blast cells
present, and Platelets 45 x 10^9/L.
What is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL)
Explanation

The correct answer is ALL because the presentation includes classic features: young age (peak 2-5 years), bone pain,
fatigue, bruising, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and characteristic blood findings (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukocytosis with blast cells).
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عمره 4 سنين وعنده fatigue و pallor و bruising من أسبوعين مع bone pain بالساقين. بالفحص في cervical lymphadenopathy و hepatosplenomegaly، والتحاليل بتبين Hb 8.2 وأبيض 32 بالألف مع وجود blast cells وصفائح 45. هاي كلها الصورة الكلاسيكية للـ acute lymphoblastic leukaemia، وأكثر عمر إصابة من 2 لـ 5 سنين، فالجواب (A).
الفخ: في ناس بيختاروا (C) ITP لأنهم شايفين الكدمات ونقص الصفائح، بس بالـ ITP ما بيكون في hepatosplenomegaly ولا blast cells ولا leukocytosis، ووجود الـ blast cells هو اللي بيوّجه للـ leukaemia.

question:
A 6-year-old boy presents to the Emergency Department with fever and lethargy.
Calculate his estimated weight.
englishExplanation:
20 kg
Explanation
 Using the WET FLAG formula [2 x age] + 8:
For a 6-year-old child: [2 x 6] + 8 = 12 + 8 = 20 kg
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الجواب 20 kg لأنو حساب وزن الطفل بهاد العمر يعتمد على فورمولا WET FLAG، وهي عبارة عن ضرب عمر الطفل بالسنة بـ 2 وجمع 8 على الناتج. هون الطفل عمره 6 سنين، فبيصير 2 ضرب 6 يساوي 12، وبعدين 12 زائد 8 يساوي 20. فوزنه التقديري الصحيح هو 20 كيلوغرام، وهاي الطريقة معتمدة لتقدير الوزن بسرعة لما يكون الطفل ما بينفع يتوزن أو بدنا نعطي أدوية بجرعات حسب الوزن.
الفخ: في ناس بيختارو 16 kg لأنهم بينسو يجمعو الـ 8 أو بيضربو العمر بـ 2 بس بدون زيادة، وهاد غلط واضح. لازم تتذكر إنو الفورمولا كاملة هي 2 ضرب العمر زائد 8 دايماً.

question:
A 6-year-old presents to the Emergency Department with polyuria, polydipsia, and lethargy. Blood tests show pH
7.25, bicarbonate 13 mmol/L, and glucose 25 mmol/L.
Which of the following is the correct initial fluid management for this patient?

options.text: Calculate deficit based on 10% dehydration and replace over 48 hours
Calculate deficit based on 7% dehydration and replace over 48 hours
Calculate deficit based on 5% dehydration and replace over 48 hours
Give 20ml/kg bolus immediately, followed by maintenance only
Calculate deficit based on 3% dehydration and replace over 24 hours

correctAnswer: Calculate deficit based on 5% dehydration and replace over 48 hours
englishExplanation:
Calculate deficit based on 5% dehydration and replace over 48 hours
Explanation
This patient has mild DKA as evidenced by pH 7.25 (between 7.2-7.29) and bicarbonate 13 mmol/L (less than 15).
According to the BPSED guidelines, mild DKA should be managed assuming a 5% fluid deficit, which should be replaced over 48 hours.
It is not possible to accurately clinically assess the degree of dehydration to calculate the deficit. Clinical methods are
unreliable. The fluid deficit should be estimated based on the initial blood pH. It should be replaced over 48 hours
alongside maintenance fluids.
Assume a 5% fluid deficit in children and young people with mild DKA (indicated by blood pH 7.2–7.29 and/or bicarbonate <15).

Assume a 7% fluid deficit in children and young people with moderate DKA (indicated by blood pH 7.1–7.19 and/or
bicarbonate <10).
Assume a 10% fluid deficit in children and young people with severe DKA (indicated by blood pH <7.1 and/or bicarbonate <5).
https://www.sort.nhs.uk/Media/Guidelines/BSPED-DKA-guideline-2020-update.pdf
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هاد الطفل عنده DKA خفيف لأنو الـ pH عنده 7.25 يعني بين 7.2 و 7.29، والبيكربونات 13 يعني أقل من 15، وهاي معايير الـ DKA الخفيف حسب BSPED. بالقواعد، الـ DKA الخفيف لازم نعتبره نقص سوائل بنسبة 5% ونعوّضه على مدى 48 ساعة مع سوائل الصيانة. ما بنقدر نقيّم درجة الجفاف سريرياً بشكل دقيق لأنو الطرق السريرية غير موثوقة، فبنعتمد تقدير النقص على الـ pH بالدم.
الفخ: كتير طلاب بيختارو 7% لأنهم بيخلطو بين الخفيف والمتوسط، بس المتوسط مربوط بـ pH ما بين 7.1 و 7.19 وبيكربونات أقل من 10، وهاد مش موجود هون. فخليك دقيق بقراءة الأرقام قبل ما تختار.

question:
An 8-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with a circular, expanding rash on his left thigh. The rash
has a characteristic "bull's-eye" appearance, with a central red spot surrounded by a clear area and an outer red
ring. The patient reports a tick bite at the site two weeks ago.
Which of the following is the most appropriate antibiotic treatment for this patient?
englishExplanation:
Amoxicillin
Explanation
The patient's presentation is consistent with erythema migrans, the characteristic rash of early Lyme disease. In children under 9 years old, amoxicillin is the first-line treatment for Lyme disease due to its effectiveness and safety profile. In children 9-12 NICE still has doxycycline as first line. 

https://cks.nice.org.uk/topics/lyme-disease/management/management/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الحالة واضحة إنها erythema migrans، وهي الطفح المميز لمرض Lyme المبكر، وبتجي على شكل حلقة متوسعة مع مركز أحمر ومنطقة فاتحة وحلقة خارجية حمراء، والطفل حكى عن قرصة tick قبل أسبوعين. للأسف الأطفال تحت 9 سنين، الـ amoxicillin هو الخيار الأول لعلاج Lyme لأنو فعّال وآمن. أما الأطفال من 9 لـ 12 سنة، فإن NICE لسا بتعتبر الـ doxycycline خط أول بالنسبة إلهم.
الفخ: في طلاب بيختارو doxycycline لأنها مشهورة بعلاج الـ tick-borne diseases بشكل عام، بس هون العمر عامل حاسم وما بنستخدمها للأطفال الصغار. لازم تربط الجواب بعمر المريض مش بس بالتشخيص.

question:
A 4-year-old boy presents to the Emergency Department with severe dehydration following 3 days of diarrhoea and
vomiting. After multiple failed peripheral IV attempts, an intraosseous line is placed in the proximal tibia. Blood
samples are drawn from both the IO line and a subsequently obtained peripheral venous line for analysis.

Which of the following laboratory values would show the MOST significant difference between the IO and venous
samples?
englishExplanation:
Calcium
Explanation
IO samples show a good correlation with venous samples for:
Haemoglobin/haematocrit
Chloride
Glucose
Urea
Creatinine
Albumin
IO samples poorly correlate with venous samples for:
WBCs
Platelets
Serum CO2
Sodium
Potassium
Calcium
https://litfl.com/intraosseous-access/

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00797 source page 661](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00797-study-p661.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00797 source page 662](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00797-study-p662.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00797 source page 1547](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00797-frcem-p1547.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00797 source page 1548](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00797-frcem-p1548.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00797 source page 1549](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00797-frcem-p1549.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00797 source page 1550](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00797-frcem-p1550.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الجواب Calcium لأنه عينات الـ IO بتعطي ارتباط ممتاز مع العينات الوريدية بقيم Haemoglobin و haematocrit و Chloride و Glucose و Urea و Creatinine و Albumin. في المقابل، في قيم بتترابط بشكل ضعيف مع الدم الوريدي، وهي WBCs و Platelets و Serum CO2 و Sodium و Potassium و Calcium. فالـ Calcium هو من القيم اللي بتختلف بشكل كبير بين عينة الـ IO والعينة الوريدية، وهاد مهم تعرفه لما تعتمد على نتائج سحب الدم من خط داخل العظم.
الفخ: في ناس بتختار Glucose لأنه شائع الاستخدام بالطوارئ، بس الـ Glucose من القيم اللي بتترابط بشكل جيد بين العينتين. الفرق الأكبر بيظهر بالقيم اللي ارتباطها ضعيف زي الـ Calcium والـ Sodium.

question:
A 4-year-old child presents to the Emergency Department in status epilepticus.
After two doses of benzodiazepines with no response, what is the most appropriate next step in management?
englishExplanation:
Administer Levetiracetam 40 mg/kg over 5 minutes
Explanation
In paediatric status epilepticus that has failed to respond to two doses of benzodiazepines, the options are:
Levetiracetam 30–60 mg/kg (over 5 min, max 3 g) OR
Phenytoin 20 mg/kg by slow IV infusion over 20 min with ECG monitoring OR
Phenobarbital 20 mg/kg by IV infusion over 5 min
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل بحالة status epilepticus وما استجاب لجرعتين من الـ benzodiazepines، فالخطوة الجاية حسب البروتوكول هي إعطاء Levetiracetam بجرعة 30 لـ 60 ملغ لكل كيلوغرام، وتُعطى خلال 5 دقائق وبحد أقصى 3 غرام. فخيار إعطاء Levetiracetam 40 mg/kg خلال 5 دقائق مطابق للجرعة والمدة المطلوبة. البدائل الأخرى المقبولة بنفس المرحلة هي Phenytoin 20 mg/kg بالتسريب الوريدي البطيء خلال 20 دقيقة مع مراقبة ECG، أو Phenobarbital 20 mg/kg بالتسريب خلال 5 دقائق.
الفخ: في طلاب بيختارو Phenytoin 40 mg/kg لأنه بيفكرو الجرعة الأعلى أقوى، بس الجرعة الصحيحة 20 mg/kg مش 40، وزيادتها بتزيد خطر السمية القلبية. انتبه للجرعة الصحيحة قبل ما تختار الدواء.

question:
A 4-month-old female infant presents to the paediatric clinic for routine examination. The mother mentions asymmetric skin folds in the thigh region. On examination, there is limited abduction of the right hip.
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
englishExplanation:
Immediate hip ultrasound
Explanation
In a 4-month-old infant with clinical signs suggestive of DDH (asymmetric skin folds, limited abduction), immediate
hip ultrasound is the most appropriate imaging modality. Ultrasound can effectively visualize the cartilaginous components and dynamic stability of the hip joint in infants under 6 months.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفلة عمرها 4 شهور وعندها علامات سريرية بتشكك بـ DDH، زي الطيات الجلدية غير المتناظرة بمحطة الفخذ ومحدودية الـ abduction بالورك الأيمن. بأعمار أقل من 6 شهور، الـ hip ultrasound هو الفحص الأنسب لأنه بقدر يشوف المكونات الغضروفية والثبات الديناميكي للمفصل بشكل واضح. فالإجراء الصحيح هو عمل ultrasound للورك فوراً لتأكيد التشخيص قبل أي تدخل.
الفخ: في ناس بتختار plain radiograph لأنه فحص سهل ومتوفر، بس بالأعمار الصغيرة العظام لسا غضروفية والـ X-ray ما بيعطي صورة كافية. الـ ultrasound هو الخيار الأول تحت 6 شهور.

question:
A 2-week-old infant presents to the Emergency Department with
poor feeding, tachypnoea, and excessive sweating during feeds. On
examination, you note a continuous "machinery" murmur best heard
at the left upper sternal border.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA)
Explanation
The correct answer is Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA) because the presentation includes classic symptoms of a left-to-right shunt with heart
failure in infancy and the pathognomonic continuous "machinery" murmur best heard at the left upper sternal border.
Why other answers are incorrect:
VSD typically presents with a harsh holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, not a continuous machinery murmur
ASD rarely causes symptoms in infancy and has a soft systolic ejection
murmur at the upper left sternal border
TOF typically presents with cyanotic episodes and has a systolic ejection murmur, not a continuous murmur
CoA typically presents with differential blood pressure between upper
and lower limbs and absent femoral pulses, not a continuous murmur
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الرضيع عمره أسبوعين وعنده تغذية سيئة وtachypnoea وتعرق زايد أثناء الرضعات، وهاد بيدل على فشل قلب بسبب shunt من اليسار لليمين. العلامة المميزة هون هي الـ continuous machinery murmur اللي بينسمع بأفضل شكل عند الحد القصي العلوي الأيسر، وهاي pathognomonic لـ Patent Ductus Arteriosus. فالتشخيص الأرجح هو PDA لوجود النفخة المستمرة مع أعراض فشل القلب بعمر الرضاعة.
الفخ: كتير طلاب بيختارو VSD لأنه أشهر عيب قلبي خُلقي، بس نفخة الـ VSD هي holosystolic harsh بتنسمع عند الحد القصي السفلي الأيسر مش مستمرة. النفخة المستمرة على شكل machinery هي المفتاح لـ PDA.

question:
A 2-year-old child presents to the Emergency Department with a 2-day history of ear pain and fever. On examination, there is visible discharge from the right ear canal.
Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
englishExplanation:
Oral amoxicillin
Explanation
In children with acute otitis media (AOM) presenting with otorrhea, immediate antibiotic therapy is recommended
rather than watchful waiting. Amoxicillin is the first-line treatment
Antibiotic criteria are
Otorrhoea in any child or young person
Under 2 years with infection in both ears

Is systemically very unwell
Has high risk of complications
https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng91/resources/visual-summary-pdf-4787282702
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عمره سنتين وعنده ألم بالأذن وحرارة مع وجود إفرازات من قناة الأذن، يعني otorrhoea. بوجود الـ otorrhoea عند أي طفل، التوصيات بتقول نبدأ مضاد حيوي فوراً وما نلجأ للـ watchful waiting. والـ amoxicillin هو خط العلاج الأول لحالات acute otitis media، فخيار Oral amoxicillin هو الأنسب كإدارة أولية. باقي الحالات اللي تحتاج مضاد حيوي فوري كمان هي الأطفال تحت سنتين بالإصابة بالأذنين مع بعض، أو اللي حالتهم العامة سيئة جداً، أو عندهم خطر مضاعفات عالي.
الفخ: في ناس بتختار watchful waiting لأنها شائعة بـ AOM الخفيف، بس وجود الإفرازات من الأذن بيلغي هالخيار. الـ otorrhoea بحد ذاتها معيار إعطاء مضاد حيوي فوري.

question:
A 2-year-old child presents to the Emergency Department with a displaced fracture of the left radius and ulna requiring manipulation, along with a head injury that currently does not meet NICE criteria for a CT head. The child
weighs 8kg and has no other medical problems.
Which of the following statements regarding intranasal diamorphine is correct?

options.text: Intranasal diamorphine is safe to use in this child
Head injury is not a contraindication to intranasal diamorphine
A recent dose of oral morphine would not affect the decision to give intranasal diamorphine
Intranasal diamorphine can be safely given if the child develops epistaxis
Intranasal diamorphine should be avoided as the child is under 10kg

correctAnswer: Intranasal diamorphine should be avoided as the child is under 10kg
englishExplanation:
Intranasal diamorphine should be avoided as the child is under 10kg
Explanation
A weight under 10kg is a contraindication for intranasal diamorphine.
Contraindications for IN Diamorph
Children <10kg
Administration of other opiates prior
Known Allergy
Children with a head injury / neurological problem
Epistaxis
Airway / respiratory problem
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل وزنه 8 كيلوغرام فقط، ووزن أقل من 10 كيلوغرام هو من موانع استخدام intranasal diamorphine تماماً. والطفل كمان عنده إصابة رأس، وإصابة الرأس أو أي مشكلة عصبية هي كذلك من موانع الاستخدام. غير هيك، من الموانع كذلك إعطاء أي opiates أخرى قبلها، والحساسية المعروفة، والـ epistaxis، ومشاكل بالمجاري التنفسية أو التنفس. فالجواب الصحيح هو أنو لازم نتجنب الـ intranasal diamorphine لأن الطفل أقل من 10 كيلوغرام.
الفخ: في طلاب بيختارو إنو الإعطاء آمن لأنه بيفكرو الجرعة الأنفية لطيفة وبسيطة، بس الوزن تحت 10 كيلو لوحده مانع كافي. تذكر إنو وزن الطفل وإصابة الرأس بيمنعوا الاستخدام هون.

question:
A 15-year-old male presents to the Emergency Department with sudden onset palpitations. His ECG shows a narrow complex tachycardia at 180 bpm. After confirming SVT, you decide to give adenosine.
What is the correct initial dose of adenosine for this patient?
englishExplanation:
3 mg IV
Explanation
Paediatric adenosine dosing in SVT
Up to 1 year: 150 mcg/kg initial dose, increase by 50–100 mcg/kg every
1–2 minutes. Maximum single dose: Neonates 300 mcg/kg, Infants 500
mcg/kg.
Ages 1–11 years: 100 mcg/kg initial dose, increase by 50–100 mcg/kg
every 1–2 minutes. Maximum single dose: 500 mcg/kg (maximum 12
mg).
Ages 12–17 years: 3 mg IV initially, increase to 6 mg after 1–2 minutes
if needed, then 12 mg after 1–2 minutes.
https://www.resus.org.uk/sites/default/files/2022-03/RCUK%20Paediatric%20emergency%20algorithms%20and%20resources%20-
Mar%2022%20V1.pdf

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00826 source page 1595](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00826-frcem-p1595.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00826 source page 1596](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00826-frcem-p1596.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00826 source page 1597](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00826-frcem-p1597.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عمره 15 سنة، والأعمار من 12 لـ 17 سنة إلها بروتوكول خاص بجرعة الـ adenosine لحالات SVT. الجرعة الأولية بهالفئة العمرية هي 3 ميليغرام وريدياً، وإذا ما استجاب بعد دقيقة أو دقيقتين بنرفعها لـ 6 ميليغرام، وإذا لسا ما استجاب بعد دقيقة أو دقيقتين بنرفعها لـ 12 ميليغرام. فالإجابة الصحيحة هي 3 mg IV كجرعة أولية.
الفخ: في ناس بتختار 6 mg أو 12 mg لأنهم بيعرفو هالأرقام من البروتوكول، بس هدول جرعات متتالية بتُعطى بعد فشل الجرعة الأولى مش بالبداية. الجرعة الأولية للفئة العمرية 12 لـ 17 سنة هي 3 ميليغرام.

question:
According to the SUDIC protocol, which of the following children should NOT be assessed in hospital following
sudden unexplained death?

options.text: A 6-month-old with sudden cardiac arrest at home
A 4-year-old pronounced dead at scene after drowning
A 1-year-old found deceased in their cot
None of the above - All cases should be assessed in hospital

correctAnswer: None of the above - All cases should be assessed in hospital
englishExplanation:
None of the above - All cases should be assessed in hospital
Explanation
According to the SUDIC (Sudden Unexplained Death in Children) protocol, ALL cases of sudden unexpected death in
children should be assessed in hospital, regardless of where death is confirmed.

Even in cases where death is obvious or pronounced at scene, the child should still be transferred to hospital for
proper assessment and management according to the protocol.

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00829 source page 681](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00829-study-p681.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00829 source page 682](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00829-study-p682.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: حسب بروتوكول SUDIC، وهو Sudden Unexplained Death in Children، كل حالات الوفاة المفاجئة وغير المبررة عند الأطفال لازم يتم تقييمها بالمستشفى. وهاد ينطبق بغض النظر عن المكان اللي تأكدت فيه الوفاة، يعني حتى لو كانت الوفاة واضحة أو تم تشخيصها بالموقع، لازم الطفل ينقل للمستشفى للتقييم والتدبير حسب البروتوكول. فعلياً ما في حالة واحدة يجب استثناؤها من تقييم المستشفى.
الفخ: في ناس بيختارو الحالة اللي تم إعلان الوفاة فيها بالموقع زي الغرق، بس البروتوكول واضح إنو كل الحالات لازم تنقل للمستشفى. لا تستثني أي حالة من التقييم.

question:
A 6-year-old presents to the Emergency Department with a fever, sore throat, and a characteristic sandpaper-like
rash.
Which of the following statements regarding notification is correct?

options.text: Notification must be made immediately by telephone
Notification should be made within 24 hours
Notification should be made within 3 days
Notification is only required if there is a cluster of cases
Notification is not required for scarlet fever

correctAnswer: Notification should be made within 3 days
englishExplanation:
Notification should be made within 3 days
Explanation
Scarlet fever is a notifiable disease in the UK. Healthcare professionals are legally required to report suspected cases
through the online notification system within 3 days of suspecting the diagnosis.
https://www.gov.uk/guidance/notifiable-diseases-and-how-to-report-them#list-diseases
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده حرارة والتهاب حلق وطفح مميز على شكل ورق الصنفرة، وهاد بيتوافق مع scarlet fever. والـ scarlet fever هو مرض notifiable بالمملكة المتحدة، يعني الأطباء والعاملين بالصحة ملزمين قانونياً بالإبلاغ عن الحالات المشتبهة. الإبلاغ بيتم من خلال نظام الإبلاغ الإلكتروني خلال 3 أيام من الاشتباه بالتشخيص، فالإجابة الصحيحة هي أن الإبلاغ لازم يصير خلال 3 أيام.
الفخ: في طلاب بيختارو الإبلاغ الفوري بالهاتف أو خلال 24 ساعة لأنه بيفكرو المرض خطير، بس المهلة المعتمدة للـ scarlet fever هي 3 أيام. انتبه للفرق بين الإبلاغ الفوري وبين الـ 3 أيام.

question:
A 4-month-old female infant presents with poor weight gain, recurrent chest infections, and intermittent bluish discolouration of the
lips.
Vital signs:
Temperature: 37.2°C
Heart rate: 140/min
Respiratory rate: 45/min
Blood pressure: 85/45 mmHg
Oxygen saturation: 94% on room air
Clinical examination:
• Fixed split of S2 on cardiac auscultation
• Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur at left upper sternal border
• Mild subcostal recession
• Clear lung fields on auscultation
• Capillary refill time 2 seconds
• No hepatomegaly
Past medical history: Born at term, normal delivery
Current medications: None

What is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Atrial septal defect (ASD)
Explanation
The key diagnostic feature here is the fixed split S2, which is pathognomonic for ASD. The left-to-right shunt creates volume overload of the
right heart, explaining the systolic ejection murmur. The fixed split occurs because the increased RV volume prolongs ejection time regardless
of the respiratory phase.
The mild cyanosis and recurrent infections are due to pulmonary overcirculation—classic presentation timing at 4 months, when pulmonary
vascular resistance has dropped enough to allow significant shunting.
Incorrect answers explained:
PDA: Would present with poor feeding, tachypnoea, and failure to
thrive. Clinical findings include a continuous machinery murmur below
the left clavicle, bounding pulses, and a wide pulse pressure
VSD: Typically presents with failure to thrive, frequent respiratory infections, and sweating during feeds. Clinical findings include a holosystolic murmur at LLSB, thrill common, normal S2
PS: Usually presents with exercise intolerance and fatigue. Clinical
findings include ejection click, crescendo-decrescendo murmur, and
normal split S2
TOF: Presents with cyanotic spells, squatting, and poor growth. Clinical
findings include significant cyanosis, right-sided hypertrophy, bootshaped heart on CXR, and no fixed split S2

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00841 source page 689](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00841-study-p689.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-00841 source page 690](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-00841-study-p690.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: العلامة المفتاحية هون هي الـ fixed split of S2، وهاي pathognomonic لـ Atrial Septal Defect. الـ shunt من اليسار لليمين بيعمل volume overload على القلب الأيمن، وهاد بيفسر وجود الـ systolic ejection murmur. والـ fixed split بيصير لأنو زيادة حجم البطين الأيمن بتطوّل وقت القذف بغض النظر عن مرحلة التنفس. الزرقة الخفيفة والالتهابات التنفسية المتكررة سببها فرط الدوران الرئوي، واللي بيظهر بعمر 4 شهور لما ينخفض ضغط الشرايين الرئوية.
الفخ: في ناس بتختار VSD لأنه أشهر عيب خلقي، بس نفخة الـ VSD هي holosystolic عند الحد القصي السفلي الأيسر وما فيها fixed split. الـ fixed split S2 هي المفتاح المميز لـ ASD.

question:
A 4-year-old child is brought to the Emergency Department by his mother with concerns about behavioural
changes. Over the past 2 months, he has become withdrawn, shows aggressive behaviour towards his younger sibling, and has started wetting the bed despite being previously toilet trained. During examination, you notice multiple bruises in different stages of healing on his upper arms and thighs.
What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Reassure the mother that this is normal behaviour for a 4-year-old and discharge
Refer directly to CAMHS for behavioural assessment
Initiate safeguarding procedures and inform the safeguarding lead
Prescribe bedwetting alarm and arrange follow-up with GP
Order blood tests to rule out organic causes

correctAnswer: Initiate safeguarding procedures and inform the safeguarding lead
englishExplanation:
Initiate safeguarding procedures and inform the safeguarding lead
Explanation
The combination of concerning behavioural changes (withdrawal, aggression, regression in toilet training) along with
unexplained bruising in different stages of healing raises significant safeguarding concerns that require immediate action. These are red flag signs that could indicate physical abuse.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هون في مجموعة علامات مقلقة مع بعض، وهي التغيرات السلوكية من انسحاب وعدوانية تجاه الأخ الصغير، وتراجع بالتدريب على الحمام بعد ما كان متدرب، ومع وجود كدمات بمواضع مختلفة وبمراحل شفاء مختلفة على الذراعين والفخذين. هالجمع بين العلامات بيعتبر red flags ممكن تدل على إساءة جسدية، فالخطوة الصحيحة هي البدء بإجراءات الحماية safeguarding وإبلاغ الـ safeguarding lead فوراً. هالحالات بتتطلب تحرك سريع وما بتتأجل.
الفخ: في ناس بتختار الطمأنة والإحالة لـ CAMHS أو طلب تحاليل لاستبعاد أسباب عضوية، بس الكدمات بمراحل شفاء مختلفة مع التراجع السلوكي بترجّح الإساءة. ما تطمّن وتصرف المريض بهاد السياق.

question:
A 4-year-old child presents to the emergency department with a severe femur fracture requiring immediate IO access for fluid resuscitation. After successful IO placement, the child experiences significant pain at the insertion
site.
What is the most appropriate management of IO-related pain in this situation?

options.text: Give 0.5mg/kg lidocaine IM near the IO site
Administer 0.5mg/kg lidocaine through the IO line, wait 1 minute, then flush with saline
Subcut 3mg/kg lidocaine near the IO site
Give 0.1mg/kg lidocaine through the IO line without flush
Apply topical lidocaine gel around the IO site

correctAnswer: Administer 0.5mg/kg lidocaine through the IO line, wait 1 minute, then flush with saline
englishExplanation:
Administer 0.5mg/kg lidocaine through the IO line, wait 1 minute, then flush with saline
Explanation
Lidocaine can be administered through the IO line for pain—dose 0.5mg/kg [max dose 20 mg]. Wait 60 seconds for
the medication to take effect, and then flush with saline. This approach effectively addresses the pain by targeting the
highly innervated medullary cavity.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ IO access بيسبب ألم لأنو تجويف النخاع العظمي غني جداً بالأعصاب. لعلاج هالألم، بنعطي lidocaine عبر خط الـ IO نفسه بجرعة 0.5 ملغ لكل كيلوغرام، وبحد أقصى 20 ميليغرام. بعد إعطاء الدواء لازم ننتظر 60 ثانية حتى ياخد مفعوله، وبعدها بنعمل flush بالمحلول الملحي. فالخيار الصحيح هو إعطاء 0.5mg/kg lidocaine عبر خط الـ IO والانتظار دقيقة ثم الـ flush بالسلاين.
الفخ: في ناس بتختار الطرق الموضعية أو الحقن العضلي أو تحت الجلد، بس الهدف هو التجويف النخاعي نفسه، فالدواء لازم يروح عبر نفس خط الـ IO. لا تنسى الانتظار والـ flush بعد الدواء.

question:
A 9-year-old boy presents to the Emergency Department in status epilepticus. After initial benzodiazepines fail to
terminate the seizure, phenytoin is prescribed. During rapid IV administration of phenytoin, the patient develops
severe bradycardia followed by cardiac arrest.
Which of the following statements best explains this adverse event?

options.text: The patient had an underlying cardiac conduction defect
The phenytoin dose was too high for the patient's weight
Rapid IV administration of phenytoin caused direct cardiac toxicity
The patient had an allergic reaction to phenytoin
The benzodiazepines given earlier potentiated phenytoin's cardiac effects

correctAnswer: Rapid IV administration of phenytoin caused direct cardiac toxicity
englishExplanation:
Rapid IV administration of phenytoin caused direct cardiac toxicity
Explanation
Rapid intravenous administration of phenytoin is a well-known cause of cardiac conduction abnormalities, including
bradycardia and asystole. This occurs due to the drug's direct effects on cardiac sodium channels and is independent
of the total dose.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل بحالة status epilepticus وبعد الـ benzodiazepines تم إعطاؤه phenytoin، وأثناء الإعطاء الوريدي السريع صار عنده بطء قلب شديد ثم توقف قلب. السبب هو إنو الإعطاء الوريدي السريع للـ phenytoin معروف إنه يسبب اضطرابات توصيل قلبية، ومنها الـ bradycardia والـ asystole. وهاد بيصير بسبب تأثير الدواء المباشر على قنوات الصوديوم بالقلب، وهو مستقل عن الجرعة الكلية. فلازم الـ phenytoin يُعطى بالتسريب البطيء مع مراقبة الـ ECG.
الفخ: في طلاب بيختارو إنو الجرعة كانت عالية أو إنو في عيب توصيل كامن، بس السبب الحقيقي هو سرعة الإعطاء وتأثيره القلبي المباشر. لا تربط الحادثة بجرعة عالية إذا الطفل استلم جرعة صحيحة.

question:
A 6-year-old boy is being managed for DKA as per the BSPED guidelines. 4 hours into treatment, he becomes
drowsy and develops a headache with vomiting.
What is the best treatment option?
englishExplanation:
2.7% Hypertonic Saline
Explanation
Although mannitol and 2.7% Hypertonic saline can be used for increased ICP due to mannitol’s diuretic effect, 2.7%
Hypertonic saline is preferred in DKA where patients are likely to be dehydrated.
www.bsped.org.uk
https://www.bsped.org.uk/media/zcwhmkei/dka-overview-algorithm-v2.pdf
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده DKA وبيتلقى علاجه حسب BSPED، وبعد 4 ساعات صار عنده خمول وصداع مع قيء، وهاد بيعمل شك بزيادة الضغط داخل القحف. للمعالجة، في خيارين هما mannitol و 2.7% Hypertonic Saline، بس الـ hypertonic saline هو المفضّل بحالات الـ DKA. والسبب إنو الـ mannitol عنده تأثير مدرّ للبول، وهاي المرضى بالأساس معرضين للجفاف، فمدرّ البول ممكن يزيد الجفاف سوءاً. فالأفضل هو 2.7% Hypertonic Saline.
الفخ: في ناس بتختار Mannitol لأنه معروف بمعالجة ارتفاع الضغط داخل القحف، بس بسياق الـ DKA المرضى جفافهم موجود والـ mannitol بزيده. الـ hypertonic saline هو الخيار الأأمن هون.

question:
A 3-year-old child presents to the emergency department with acute onset of bloody diarrhoea, vomiting, and decreased urine output. Laboratory tests reveal thrombocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, and acute kidney injury.
Which of the following is the most likely causative organism for this Haemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)
presentation?
englishExplanation:
Escherichia coli O157:H7
Explanation
Escherichia coli O157:H7 is the most common causative organism of typical or diarrhoea-associated Haemolytic
Uremic Syndrome (D+ HUS), especially in children. This strain of E. coli produces Shiga toxin, which damages the
endothelial cells of small blood vessels, particularly in the kidneys. This leads to the classic triad of HUS: microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الطفل عنده إسهال دموي مفاجئ وقيء وقلة إدرار بول، والتحاليل بتظهر thrombocytopenia و haemolytic anaemia و acute kidney injury، وهاد هو الثالوث الكلاسيكي لـ Haemolytic Uremic Syndrome. المسبب الأكثر شيوعاً للـ typical أو diarrhoea-associated HUS، خصوصاً عند الأطفال، هو Escherichia coli O157:H7. هالسلالة بتنتج Shiga toxin اللي بتضر الخلايا البطانية للأوعية الدموية الصغيرة، خصوصاً بالكلى، وهاد بيعمل الثالوث المميز.
الفخ: في طلاب بيختارو Shigella dysenteriae لأنها كذلك مرتبطة بالإسهال الدموي والـ HUS، بس هي سبب أقل شيوعاً. الأشهر بالـ D+ HUS عند الأطفال هو E. coli O157:H7.

question:
A 5-month-old child has tried a peanut butter flavoured Ella’s kitchen pouch for the first time. Unfortunately, this
is followed shortly by SOB, wheeze and a reduced level of consciousness. BM is 4.9. Observations are HR 141, Sats
94%, T 36.8, RR 30, BP 75/50.
What is the next stage in management?
englishExplanation:
100-150mcg IM Adrenaline
Explanation
According to the Resus Council 2021 guidelines for anaphylaxis the correct dosing of adrenaline is as follows:
Intramuscular (IM) adrenaline
Use adrenaline at 1 mg/mL (1:1000) concentration 
Adult and child >12 years: 500 micrograms IM (0.5 mL)
Child 6–12 years: 300 micrograms IM (0.3 mL)
Child 6 months to 6 years: 150 micrograms IM (0.15 mL)
Child <6 months:  100–150 micrograms IM (0.1–0.15 mL)
https://www.resus.org.uk/library/additional-guidance/guidance-anaphylaxis
https://www.resus.org.uk/sites/default/files/2021-04/Anaphylaxis algorithm 2021.pdf
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الرضيع عمره 5 شهور وتعرّض لمادة غذائية لأول مرة بعدها صار عنده ضيق نفس وwheeze وانخفاض بمستوى الوعي، وهاد بيمثل anaphylaxis. حسب إرشادات Resus Council 2021، الجرعة الصحيحة للـ adrenaline العضلي للأطفال من 6 شهور لـ 6 سنين هي 150 ميكروغرام عضلياً بتركيز 1 mg/mL. فالطفل هون عمره 5 شهور قريب من هالفئة، والجرعة المناسبة هي 100-150mcg IM Adrenaline، وهي الإدارة التالية الصحيحة.
الفخ: في ناس بتختار 10mls/kg fluid bolus أو 2mls/kg 10% dextrose لأنهم بيركزو على مستوى الوعي، بس الـ anaphylaxis بيتعالج بالـ adrenaline العضلي فوراً. الـ adrenaline هو الدواء المنقذ هون مش السوائل.

question:
You are walking by the resuscitation bay where the FY2 has been managing a patient with suspected neutropenic
sepsis. They have prescribed Tazocin as per the trust guidelines, which the nurse has just started. The patient has
then developed a widespread urticarial rash and wheeze.
Observations are as follows: HR 115, BP 100/40, RR 16, Sats 95% OA, T 37.6. They are lying flat on the trolley looking unwell.
What is your first step in management?

options.text: IV adrenaline infusion- dose as per the resus council guidelines

englishExplanation:
Stop Tazocin

Explanation
The patient has developed anaphylaxis to Tazocin- which has just been started. The question asks the first step in
management - which is to Remove the trigger as per the 2021 Anaphylaxis guidelines [linked]
https://www.resus.org.uk/library/additional-guidance/guidance-anaphylaxis
https://www.resus.org.uk/sites/default/files/2021-04/Anaphylaxis algorithm 2021.pdf
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض كان بيتلقى Tazocin لاشتباه sepsis، وبعد ما بدأ التسريب صار عنده طفح urticarial منتشر وwheeze، وهاد anaphylaxis ناتج عن الدواء اللي لسا بدأ للتو. بسؤالنا عن الخطوة الأولى بالإدارة، حسب إرشادات anaphylaxis لعام 2021، الخطوة الأولى هي إزالة المُحرّض remove the trigger. بالسياق هون، إزالة المُحرّض معناها إيقاف الـ Tazocin فوراً، فالجواب هو Stop Tazocin قبل أي شي تاني.
الفخ: في طلاب بيختارو IM Adrenaline أو السوائل لأنهو الخطوات المعروفة بالـ anaphylaxis، بس السؤال بيسأل عن الخطوة الأولى تحديداً بعد ظهور التفاعل مباشرة. إيقاف الدواء المُحرّض بجي قبل باقي الخطوات.
