ليش: الـcutaneous anthrax بيسببه Bacillus anthracis وهو الأكثر شيوعاً بين أنواع الجمرة الخبيثة. بيبلش بحبة pruritic papule وسريعاً بتتحول لقرحة غير مؤلمة وفيها eschar سوداء بمركزها، وغالباً بكون حولها وذمة nonpitting كبيرة. غياب الألم هو المميز بغياب الوجع رغم شكلها المرعب، والوذمة سببها سموم الجمرة الخبيثة اللي تزيد نفاذية الأوعية الدموية.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا Painful erythematous plaque with lymphangitis لأنها صورة الـcellulitis الشائعة بالامتحانات. الفرق إنه celery/spreading الليمفاوية والوجع هما من features cellulitis، وهون ما في وجع وفيه eschar سوداء ومحيط وذمة وذمة، وهذا اللي بيرجح anthrax.

question: A 51-year-old man with diabetes presents with perineal pain and fever. Physical examination reveals crepitus along the scrotum and left inner thigh. Which of the following is the best next step in management?

options.text: Clindamycin, vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, and surgical consultation
Immediate operative debridement followed by antibiotics
Urologic consultation plus broad-spectrum oral antibiotics

correctAnswer: Clindamycin, vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, and surgical consultation
englishExplanation:
Gas gangrene requires prompt diagnosis and early aggressive management to improve mortality and morbidity. Clindamycin, vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, and surgical consultation are appropriate and sufficient for patients with gas gangrene. It can be caused by Clostridium organisms (i.e., clostridial myonecrosis) or from polymicrobial deep soft tissue infection from wounds or other damage to soft tissue. Clostridium perfringens is the most common organism implicated in gas gangrene. Patients with diabetes or immune compromise who present with a perineal necrotizing soft tissue infection have Fournier gangrene. Patients with gas gangrene typically appear toxic and may report pain out of proportion to examination findings. Crepitus may also be palpated in the affected area, which indicates the presence of subcutaneous emphysema. Plain radiography may reveal subcutaneous gas produced by gas-forming bacteria. In addition to parenteral antibiotics and early surgical debridement, hyperbaric oxygen therapy may be considered for necrotizing soft tissue infections as it causes suppression of growth of anaerobic organisms.



Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (B) may be beneficial in the management of anaerobic soft tissue infections but is not sufficient as monotherapy. Parenteral broad-spectrum antibiotics and surgical debridement are paramount.

Immediate operative debridement followed by antibiotics (C) is not recommended for the management of gas gangrene as this delays the administration of antimicrobial therapy. Antibiotics should be initiated as soon as the diagnosis is suspected, and arrangements for operative intervention should occur simultaneously.

Urologic consultation plus broad-spectrum oral antibiotics (D) is inappropriate management because patients with gas gangrene should be treated with parenteral antibiotics. Urologic consultation for surgical debridement is appropriate.

One Step Further
Question:
True or false: piperacillin-tazobactam provides poor coverage for anaerobic bacteria.

Reveal Answer:
False.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Necrotizing Fasciitis and Myonecrosis

Necrotizing fasciitis
Type 1: polymicrobial
Type 2: a single organism (most commonly group A Streptococcus)
Myonecrosis
Traumatic (Clostridium perfringens)
Spontaneous (Clostridium septicum)
Pain out of proportion to exam
Systemic signs of infection
Cellulitis progresses to dusky blue with bullae or vesicles
Radiograph: subcutaneous emphysema
Emergent surgical debridement, broad-spectrum antibiotics
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده سكري وعندو ألم بالعجان وحمى، وبالفحص في crepitus بالصفن والفخذ الأيسر الداخلي، وهاد gas gangrene واللي ممكن يكون Fournier gangrene بمنطقة العجان. السبب ممكن Clostridium وبالأخص Clostridium perfringens، أو إنتان لخلايا عميقة متعدد الجراثيم. الإدارة الصحيحة هي Clindamycin plus vancomycin plus piperacillin-tazobactam مع استشارة جراحية عاجلة.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا Immediate operative debridement followed by antibiotics، أو Hyperbaric oxygen therapy كعلاج وحيد. الفرق إنه الـhyperbaric oxygen ممكن تفيد كإضافة للعلاج لكنها ما بتكفي لوحدها، والمضادات الجراحية والاستشارة الجراحية هي الأساس والخطوة التالية الصحيحة.

question: You have been asked to review blood culture results at the start of your morning ED shift. Which of the following is most likely to be a contaminant?
englishExplanation:
Contamination of blood culture specimens is not uncommon and can be the result of improper technique when obtaining the specimen or colonization of the skin or catheter from where the blood was drawn. Knowing which bacteria are likely to represent contamination versus actual infection is critical in avoiding unnecessary antibiotic use and the possible complications related to their use. Risk factors for true bacteremia include advanced age, corticosteroid use, immunosuppression, chronic liver or kidney disease, intravenous catheters, neutropenia, and parenteral nutrition. Factors that would favor contamination over true bacteremia include when typical organisms of the skin flora are isolated (e.g., coagulase-negative Staphylococcus), when only one of two cultures is positive, or when growth first occurs after 72 hours of incubation. Organisms with the highest false positive rates include Bacillus species, coagulase-negative Staphylococcus species, Propionibacterium species, and viridans streptococci.



The finding of certain organisms on blood culture should always be thought to represent true bacteremia when isolated. This includes Candida albicans (A), Enterobacteriaceae (C) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (D). Infections with Candida albicans can range from benign mucous membrane infections, such as candida vaginitis, to sepsis and multiorgan system failure. Enterobacteriaceae are a family of gram-negative bacteria that includes common pathogens such as Escherichia coli, Salmonella, Klebsiella, and Shigella. Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a gram-negative non-fermenting bacillus that is a leading cause of hospital-acquired infections, including ventilator-associated pneumonia, and catheter-associated urinary tract infections. It is also the most common pathogen isolated from patients with cystic fibrosis. Other organisms that suggest true bacteremia include Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae.

One Step Further
Question:
True or false: ceftriaxone provides adequate coverage for infections related to Pseudomonas aeruginosa?

Reveal Answer:
False. Cefepime, ceftazidime, piperacillin-tazobactam, and ciprofloxacin are all antibiotics that would provide adequate coverage.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Measles (Rubeola)

Risks: unvaccinated young child
Prodrome: high fever, cough, conjunctivitis, coryza
PE: red spots with blue or white center on buccal mucosa (Koplik spots) → maculopapular rash that starts on head and spreads toward feet
Dx: made clinically, but nasopharyngeal PCR can be used for definitive diagnosis
Tx: supportive care plus vitamin A if signs of vitamin A deficiency, severe symptoms, or child < 2 years
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لما نراجع نتائج زراعة الدم، في عوامل بترجح التلوث على العدوى الحقيقية. أهمها عزل جراثيم من فلورا الجلد الطبيعية زي Coagulase-negative Staphylococcus، أو لما تنمو واحدة بس من زراعتين، أو لما يظهر النمو بعد 72 ساعة من الحضن. وجراثيم ثانية زي Bacillus وPropionibacterium وviridans streptococci عندهن أعلى معدلات إيجابية كاذبة.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا Candida albicans أو Pseudomonas aeruginosa لأنهم يشوفوا إنها ممكن تكون ملوثات بالبيئة. الفرق إنه هاي الجراثيم لما تنعزل من الدم لازم تعتبر bacteremia حقيقية، بخلافCoagulase-negative Staphylococcus اللي بيعتبر من فلورا الجلد الملوثة.

question: A 45-year-old man with a history of recent kidney transplant presents with a painful vesicular rash. He is adherent to his antirejection therapy. He has an erythematous, vesicular rash extending from his left axilla to his left hip. A chest X-ray shows a left pleural effusion. You are concerned about disseminated disease. Which of the following is the most likely benefit of the recommended therapy for the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) is an extremely contagious viral infection that is responsible for both chickenpox (varicella) and shingles (herpes zoster). It is more common in the winter and spring months but occurs year-round. Risk factors include lack of immunization, increased age, immunosuppressive therapy, organ transplantation, lymphoproliferative disorders, and human immunodeficiency virus. Both children and patients older than 60 years old are able to receive vaccination to prevent zoster viral infections.

Herpes zoster usually begins with a prodrome of headache, malaise, and photophobia. Pain, pruritus, and paresthesias along one or two dermatomes usually precedes the appearance of a vesicular rash. The rash does not cross the midline and most commonly affects the face or chest, though any body region may be affected. Disseminated varicella can affect multiple dermatomes and can cause zoster pneumonitis, as is likely in this patient. Treatment involves acyclovir IV and medical admission. The goal of therapy is to prevent or reduce visceral complications of the disease. Concomitant corticosteroid therapy is not recommended.



Antiviral therapy for the treatment of disseminated varicella does not accelerate skin healing (A), prevent bacterial superinfection (B), or reduce pain (C).

One Step Further
Question:
What is shingles of the ear?

Reveal Answer:
Herpes zoster oticus (Ramsay Hunt syndrome).

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Herpes Zoster (Shingles)

Risk factors: immunosuppression, advancing age
Caused by reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus
Sx: painful, papulovesicular rash preceded by tingling or hyperesthesia
PE: rash with unilateral, dermatomal distribution that does not cross midline
Dx: based on clinical presentation, PCR if confirmation needed
Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells (not typically done)
Tx: antiviral therapy (best if started within 72 hours)
Postherpetic neuralgia: when pain persists beyond 3 months in the same distribution as a preceding documented episode of acute herpes zoster
Prevention: RZV two-dose series
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض بعد زراعة كبد وعندو rash حويصلي مؤلم من الإبط الأيسر للورك الأيسر، وكمان انصباب جنبي أيسر، وهاد disseminated varicella-zoster مع zoster pneumonitis. والعلاج هو acyclovir وريدي مع إدخال للمستشفى. الهدف من العلاج هو الوقاية أو تقليل المضاعفات الحشوية للمرض، لأن الفيروس المنتشر ممكن يوصل لالتهاب رئة والكبد والكلى وغيرهم.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا Reduces pain أو Prevents bacterial superinfection لأنهم يعرفوا إنه الشنكل بيوجع. الفرق إنه العلاج المضاد للفيروس ما بسرّع شفاء الجلد ولا بيمنع العدوى البكتيرية الثانوية ولا بيقلل الألم، بل هدفه الأساسي منع وإخماد المضاعفات الحشوية.

question: A 30-year-old man presents to the ED after a wild animal bit his finger. After obtaining history and completing the physical exam, the patient receives tetanus immunoglobulin and vaccine. While explaining rabies to the patient, he asks how the virus spreads from the bite area to his brain. Which of the following is the correct explanation?

options.text: Local toxin formation and hematogenous spread of toxin

englishExplanation:
Rabies is a viral zoonosis spread from mammals to humans. If not treated at initial exposure, it has near 100% fatality. The affected animal injects the virus at the bite site that amplifies in local muscle and then travels from there to the brain via retrograde axonal transport. Once it reaches the spinal cord, the virus infects the dorsal root ganglion up to the diencephalon and further brain regions. This neuronal transport is the cause of paresthesias that can be seen in subacute rabies infections.

Factors affecting the rate and likelihood of disease progression include the size of the inoculum, degree of innervation at the bite site (e.g., the face is highly innervated and at higher risk), and host immunity. Bats are responsible for almost 90% of rabies cases in the United States. Treatment requires injection of both immunoglobulin and vaccine in most patients, as they are previously not immunized. If there is an obvious bite site, the immunoglobulin should be administered at that site.



Hematogenous spread of the virus (A) is the common route of infection of the meninges in meningitis. Virus or bacteria enter the blood via direct contact, often at the nasal or respiratory tract, and cross the blood-brain barrier at the choroid plexus, where it is most susceptible.

Local toxin formation and spread (B) is the common form of transfer of toxin-mediated diseases such as tetanus or toxic shock syndrome. In these scenarios, the bacteria stay in the area of inoculation, but toxins are spread to cause systemic effects.

Macrophage distribution (C) occurs with HIV and John Cunningham (JC) virus, which then carry the virus across the blood-brain barrier.

One Step Further
Question:
When should a patient who finds a bat in their house be vaccinated for rabies?

Reveal Answer:
If a bite occurred, if contact occurred, if a bite cannot be ruled out, and when a patient is in the room and cannot rule out contact (sleeping, intoxicated, children, etc.).

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Rabies

Risks: exposure to raccoons, bats, or skunks
Sx: hydrophobia, agitation, spasms
Tx: supportive care (illness often fatal)
Prevention: wound care (scrubbing), rabies immune globulin at wound site (if indicated), vaccination
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الفيروس بيدخل بعضلة مكان العضّة وبيتكاثر فيها لفترة، وبعدها بينتقل من الموقع للدماغ عن طريق النقل المحوري retrograde axonal transport. لما يوصل للحبل الشوكي بيصيب الـdorsal root ganglion ويطلع للـdiencephalon وباقي مناطق الدماغ. وهاد النقل العصبي هو سبب الـparesthesias اللي بتظهر بالعدوى تحت الحادة بالـrabies.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا Hematogenous spread of the virus لأنهم يعتقدوا إنه أي فيروس بيوصل للدماغ بالدم. الفرق إنه الانتشار الدموي هو طريق التهاب السحايا، لكن rabiesneurotropic بيمشي على طول الأعصاب للأعلى، ولهيك فترة الحضانة بتعتمد على مكان العضّة ودرجة تعصيبها.

question: A 45-year-old man presents to the emergency department with stiffness in his neck, trunk, and extremities. His partner reports that he was reporting lockjaw and some muscle aches yesterday. He cut his hand with a hunting knife about a week ago, but it has been healing without issue. His vital signs are T 38.2°C, HR 120 bpm, BP 180/100 mm Hg, and RR 22/min. On physical examination, the patient’s muscles are rigid, and he appears to be in pain. Which of the following best describes the cause of this patient’s symptoms?
englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with muscle tetany and autonomic instability consistent with an infection with Clostridium tetani, the organism that causes tetanus. Any wound can become contaminated by C. tetani, but this organism can also infect burns, frostbite, and umbilical stumps. No wound is found in up to 10% of patients diagnosed with tetanus. The disease can present in three forms: generalized, cephalic, and local. Generalized is the most common and presents with violent muscular contractions, muscle stiffness, and autonomic instability. These symptoms are caused by bacterial release of the exotoxin tetanospasmin, which prevents the presynaptic release of the inhibitory neurotransmitters GABA and glycine. Loss of inhibition results in unchecked excitatory neurotransmission, leading to muscle contractions and stiffness. The loss of inhibition in the autonomic nervous system leads to autonomic instability. Treatment is largely supportive, with wound debridement, muscle relaxants (benzodiazepines), immunoglobulin, antibiotics (metronidazole is preferred), and support of the respiratory and circulatory systems as necessary. Infection does not induce immunity, so the patient should be vaccinated prior to discharge from the hospital.



Impairment of excitatory neurotransmitter release (A) describes the mechanism of the toxin produced by Clostridium botulinum, which causes botulism and presents with weakness and flaccid paralysis.

Promotion of excitatory neurotransmitter release (C) can cause muscle rigidity, such as is seen in sympathomimetic toxicity, but this patient’s presentation is more consistent with a tetanus infection, given his history of a contaminated wound.

Promotion of inhibitory neurotransmitter release (D) would result in flaccid muscles rather than the contractions and spasms seen in tetanus.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the function of the second exotoxin released by Clostridium tetani?

Reveal Answer:
In addition to tetanospasmin, Clostridium tetani also releases tetanolysin, which facilitates growth of the bacterium.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Tetanus

Caused by Clostridium tetani, which leads to neurotoxin production of tetanospasmin
Found in soil, dust, feces
Sx: weakness, myalgias, muscle cramps, dysphagia
PE: trismus (lockjaw), sardonic smile, rigidity and spasms of muscles, opisthotonos
Tx: benzodiazepines, metronidazole (preferred over penicillin), TIG, immunization
Strychnine poisoning can mimic
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده lockjaw وتصلب بالرقبة والجذع والأطراف مع ألم وتصلب عضلي وعدم استقرار أوتونومي، وقبل أسبوع جرح يده، وهاد tetanus سببه Clostridium tetani. البكتيريا بتفرز exotoxin اسمه tetanospasmin اللي بيمنع الإطلاق قبل التشابكي للناقلات العصبية المثبطة GABA وglycine. فقدان التثبيط يؤدي لإطلاق مفرط للإشارات المستثيرة، فتصير انقباضات وتيبّس بالعضلات وعدم استقرار الجهاز العصبي الأوتونومي.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا Impairment of excitatory neurotransmitter release، وهي حيلة لأنها تشبه وصف البوتوليزم. الفرق إنه botulinum بيمنع إطلاق الناقل المستثير وتيبّس مترهل، لكن tetanus يمنع الناقل المثبط ويسبب تصلب وتشنجات، والدليل هو lockjaw والجرح.

question: A 73-year-old woman with an indwelling Foley catheter is sent for evaluation from the nursing home because of fever. Which of the following is a criterion for systemic inflammatory response syndrome?
englishExplanation:
Sepsis is an increasingly common cause of ED visits and the tenth leading cause of death in the US. In response to the infectious insult, the host’s body activates a number of inflammatory cascades as part of the host response. Systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) occurs most commonly in response to an infection. SIRS plus a source of infection was historically used to define sepsis. Then, the definition changed to include the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA), which measures organ dysfunction to determine whether a patient has sepsis. The quick SOFA (qSOFA) has been a rapid way to determine a patient's mortality risk from sepsis, and the quick scoring system uses a patient's respiratory rate, blood pressure, and mental status to determine mortality risk.

However, the 2021 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines updated their recommendations for the screening of sepsis to not include the use of the qSOFA as a single screening tool over the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) criteria, National Early Warning Score (NEWS), or Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS) scores. Thus, it is important to know the components of SIRS, as SIRS is still often used to determine if a patient may have sepsis. A respiratory rate of 22/min fulfills one of the SIRS criteria.



A heart rate of 86 bpm (A) and temperature of 37.9°C (D) do not meet the criteria for SIRS.

Lactic acid (B) has become an important laboratory value in the care of patients with sepsis. Lactic acid levels > 4.0 mmol/L are associated with worsened outcomes. Aggressive resuscitation in the early stages of sepsis includes large volumes of intravenous fluid and early antibiotics. Lactate levels that fail to decrease after initial treatment are an ominous sign.

One Step Further
Question:
What bacterial species are most commonly implicated in the development of generalized erythroderma and rash in an ill-appearing patient?

Reveal Answer:
Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Sepsis and Septic Shock

Sepsis: life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection
Screening tools include quick SOFA (qSOFA), SIRS, NEWS, MEWS
SOFA score ≥ 2 indicates organ dysfunction and mortality risk ~10%
qSOFA positive if at least two of the criteria are met
Septic shock: sepsis + require vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥ 65 mg Hg despite adequate volume resuscitation + serum lactate level > 2 mmol/L (18 mg/dL)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـSIRS هي استجابة التهابية جهازية بترافق العدوى، وكتير بتستعمل لتحديد احتمال الإنتان رغم تغير التعريفات. معايير SIRS تتضمن معدل التنفس 22 بالدقيقة أو أكثر، أو PaCO2 أقل من 32، وهاد بيعتبر معيار كامل بذكرها. ومعدل نبض 86 وحرارة 37.9 لا يعدون ضمن معايير SIRS عند هذه العتبات. والمعايير القياسية هي حرارة أكثر من 38 أو أقل من 36، ونبض أكثر من 90، وتنفس أكثر من 20 أو PaCO2 أقل من 32، وكرات بيض أكثر من 12,000 أو أقل من 4,000.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا Lactic acid 4 mmol/L لأنهم يربطوه مباشرة بالإنتان. الفرق إنه اللاكتات هو مؤشر لنقص التروية وعلى قصور الأعضاء بالSEPSIS، لكنه مو من معايير SIRS الأربعة، وهون معيار التنفس 22 هو الصحيح.

question: A 63-year-old patient who is currently undergoing chemotherapy for breast cancer presents after being sent in by her oncologist for positive blood cultures. The blood cultures showed gram-positive cocci in clusters in two bottles. She had a fever 2 days ago when the cultures were drawn. Other than generalized fatigue and mild nausea, she has been asymptomatic. What is the best choice for empiric treatment?
englishExplanation:
A Gram stain showing gram-positive cocci in clusters often represents infection with Staphylococcus species, most notably S. aureus. Bacteremia may result as a complication of primary infection, such as cellulitis or pneumonia, or may be the result of an infected central venous catheter. A careful history and physical examination are necessary to uncover clues as to the possible source of infection. Particular care should be directed at evaluating for possible endocarditis, which may present with protracted fever and chills, new-onset murmur, Janeway lesions, Osler nodes, and Roth spots. In this patient, given her history of current chemotherapy treatment for breast cancer, bacteremia due to the presence of a central venous catheter is the likely cause. Empiric treatment should include coverage of methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) until susceptibility is available. Vancomycin (15–20 mg/kg/dose every 8–12 hours, not to exceed 2 grams per dose) is the antibiotic of choice. Daptomycin is an acceptable alternative. Once susceptibility results are available, antibiotics can be adjusted accordingly.



Cefepime (A) is a fourth-generation cephalosporin that provides gram-negative and some gram-positive coverage. While active against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, it does not provide coverage against MRSA.

Nafcillin (B) is an appropriate treatment for methicillin-sensitive S. aureus bacteremia. Given the risk of MRSA, it should not be used for empiric therapy prior to susceptibility results.

Piperacillin-tazobactam (C) is a broad-spectrum antibiotic but also does not provide coverage against MRSA.

One Step Further
Question:
True or false: blood cultures that show growth starting after 72 hours of incubation are more likely to represent contamination.

Reveal Answer:
True.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Sepsis and Septic Shock

Sepsis: life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection
Screening tools include quick SOFA (qSOFA), SIRS, NEWS, MEWS
SOFA score ≥ 2 indicates organ dysfunction and mortality risk ~10%
qSOFA positive if at least two of the criteria are met
Septic shock: sepsis + require vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥ 65 mg Hg despite adequate volume resuscitation + serum lactate level > 2 mmol/L (18 mg/dL)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: لما الـ Gram stain يطلع gram-positive cocci in clusters، هاد غالبا Staphylococcus وبالأخص S. aureus. المريضة عم تاخد chemotherapy لسرطان الثدي، فالأرجح إنه الـ bacteremia جايي من central venous catheter. لهيك لازم نغطي الـ MRSA تجريبيا لحد ما تطلع الـ susceptibility. الـ Vancomycin هو antibiotic of choice بجرعة 15-20 mg/kg/dose كل 8-12 ساعة وبدون ما يتجاوز 2 grams للجرعة، والـ Daptomycin بديل مقبول.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختاروا الـ Nafcillin لأنه مغطي لـ S. aureus، بس هو بس للميثيسيلين-حساس يعني ما يغطي الـ MRSA. أما الـ Cefepime فهو cephalosporin رابع جيل وما بيغطي الـ MRSA أصلا.

question: You have a patient in whom you suspect influenza. It is best to provide treatment within 48 hours of symptom onset, but treatment is recommended as early as possible for patients at high risk for complications from the illness. Which of the following patient risk factors might treatment > 48 hours from symptom onset be beneficial and is recommended according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention?

options.text: The patient has a body mass index of 35 kg/m 2
The patient has a history of diabetes
The patient has a sibling hospitalized for influenza
The patient is 4 years of age

correctAnswer: The patient has a history of diabetes
englishExplanation:
Influenza is a respiratory virus that occurs in distinct outbreaks each year, usually during the winter months. Antiviral medications such as oseltamivir, zanamivir, and peramivir have been helpful in reducing morbidity and mortality from influenza infections. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommend treatment as early as possible for hospitalized patients, those with complicated or progressive illness, and patients at high risk for complications from the disease. Early treatment (< 48 hours) is desired, but those at high risk should also be treated even if symptom onset was > 48 hours. Patients considered to have a high risk include children < 2 years old, those with chronic diseases (e.g., asthma, epilepsy, sickle cell disease, diabetes), those who are immunosuppressed or who currently take aspirin therapy, and those with a body mass index > 40 kg/m2. Evidence has shown American Indian, Alaska Native, Hispanic, and non-Hispanic Black patients seem to be at higher risk for hospitalization due to influenza, possibly due to less vaccine access and missed opportunities to vaccinate, which stem from a lack of access to health care and insurance, misinformation, and distrust. Deciding to treat is often complicated because of the number of other viruses that are circulating that have similar presentations, but recommendations are to not wait for laboratory confirmation before beginning treatment if the patient has symptoms consistent with influenza.



A body mass index > 40 kg/m2 is a risk factor, so if the patient has a body mass index of 35 kg/m2 (A), treatment is not necessarily indicated.

Response of family members to similar illness is not a risk factor, so treatment is not necessarily indicated if the patient has a sibling hospitalized for influenza (C).

Recommendations are to treat patients < 2 years old, so if the patient is 4 years old (D), treatment is not necessarily indicated.

The demographic information in the above explanation follows AMA Manual of Style terminology and may not match the language used in the references. Race is a social construct that is often correlated to certain medical conditions in the literature and evidence-based guidelines. Our hope is to inspire a change in the way race is used in the medical community.

One Step Further
Question:
Should you give oseltamivir to a patient in whom you suspect influenza and has a risk factor but has a negative rapid influenza test?

Reveal Answer:
Yes. Rapid influenza tests are specific but not sensitive, so false negatives are common.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Influenza

Presentation: sudden onset of fever, headache, cough, myalgia, sore throat, fatigue
Diagnosis is made clinically, can be confirmed with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) or viral culture
Treatment is mainly supportive or oseltamivir for patients at increased risk for severe disease
Start oseltamivir as early as possible, ideally within 48 hours (after, it will confer less benefit)
Most common cause of viral pneumonia in adults
New vaccine recommended yearly
Monitor patients for postinfluenza pneumonia
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ influenza virus بيجي بأوبئة موسمية بالشتا، والأدوية مثل oseltamivir وzanamivir وperamivir بتنقص الـ morbidity والـ mortality. القاعدة إنه نبلش علاج بأسرع وقت، بس مرضى الـ high risk لازم نعالجهم حتى لو صار أكثر من 48 ساعة من بداية الأعراض. من الـ high risk: الأطفال أقل من سنتين، وأصحاب الأمراض المزمنة مثل asthma وepilepsy وsickle cell وdiabetes، والمثبطين مناعيا، والـ BMI أكبر من 40.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا الـ BMI 35 لأنه ببالهم أي obesity تعتبر خطر، بس المطلوب بالـ CDC هو BMI أكبر من 40. والـ sibling hospitalized للـ influenza مجرد contact وما بيعتبر عامل خطر لعلاج متأخر.

question: Which of the following is the appropriate treatment for a 4-year-old child with suspected ehrlichiosis?
englishExplanation:
Human monocytic ehrlichiosis describes a disease caused by a small gram-negative intracellular bacteria, Ehrlichia chaffeensis. This is commonly spread by the Amblyomma americanum tick found across the southeastern, south-central, and mid-Atlantic states in the United States. Since its discovery in 1987, several additional bacteria from other ticks have been described to cause similar illnesses such as anaplasmosis and ewingii ehrlichiosis. Infection can occur within hours of tick attachment as opposed to the days needed for Borrelia burgdorferi infection.

Patients with ehrlichiosis generally present with an undifferentiated febrile illness and nonspecific symptoms of headache, myalgia, abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Rash and altered mental status are less common. Laboratory findings are nonspecific with leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, mild transaminitis, and mild hyponatremia in many cases. Many identified patients require hospitalization. The diagnosis is sometimes made upon finding Ehrlichia morulae (an intravacuolar aggregate of bacteria) in peripheral leukocytes, but this finding is infrequent, so many patients are treated empirically. A four-fold increase in immunoglobulin G titers over time is also diagnostic but takes time. Treatment is with tetracyclines, with doxycycline being the preferred agent, even in young patients. Delayed treatment is associated with morbidity and mortality, so early treatment is encouraged, even without a diagnosis. Short courses of doxycycline are unlikely to cause the adverse tooth discoloration known to occur in young children.



Amoxicillin (A) and other penicillins, ciprofloxacin (B) and other fluoroquinolones, clarithromycin (C) and other macrolides, and cephalosporins are not effective treatments against ehrlichiosis.

One Step Further
Question:
Which other tick-borne illness, besides ehrlichiosis, should be treated with doxycycline regardless of patient age?

Reveal Answer:
Rocky Mountain spotted fever.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Ehrlichiosis and Anaplasmosis

Vector: primarily tick-borne
Sx: fever, headache, myalgia, chills
Lab results: leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, elevated aminotransferases
Dx: whole blood testing (e.g., PCR)
Treatment: doxycycline (start empirically for suspected disease)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ ehrlichiosis سببه Ehrlichia chaffeensis، بكتيريا صغيرة gram-negative داخل الخلايا، وتنتقل عبر Amblyomma americanum tick بمناطق جنوب وجنوب-وسط وmid-Atlantic بأمريكا. المريض عادة يجي بحرارة غير محددة مع headache وmyalgia وألم بطن وغثيان وقيء، والـ rash والـ altered mental status أقل شيوعا. التشخيص ممكن نشوف Ehrlichia morulae داخل الـ peripheral leukocytes، والعلاج tetracyclines والـ doxycycline هو المفضل حتى عند الأطفال الصغار.
الفخ: أكثر غلطة إنه الطلاب يبعدوا الـ Doxycycline عن الأطفال لأنه بده يصبغ الأسنان، بس بالـ ehrlichiosis هو الـ preferred agent حتى بالمرضى الصغار. والـ Amoxicillin والـ Clarithromycin ما بيغطوا Ehrlichia أصلا.

question: Which of the following populations of patients has the greatest risk of severe neurologic complications from the influenza virus, such as encephalopathy, encephalitis, and aseptic meningitis?

options.text: Adolescent patients infected with an H1N1 strain of influenza
Children unvaccinated for influenza and naive to the virus
Patients who are immunocompromised after a solid organ transplant
Patients with asthma who need daily inhaled corticosteroids

correctAnswer: Children unvaccinated for influenza and naive to the virus
englishExplanation:
Infection by the influenza virus tends to be short and self-limited in most pediatric patients. However, complications can occur in some populations, a few of which are severe. The most common complication is a secondary bacterial infection like otitis media, sinusitis, or bacterial pneumonia. Lower respiratory infections, including from the virus itself, can occur along with a secondary bacterial infection. These are most common in children < 2 years of age. Asthma exacerbations are common in children > 2 years of age with asthma, especially if they need daily inhaled corticosteroids.

Common neurologic complications such as a febrile or nonfebrile seizure are typically short in duration, and most of these patients rapidly recover. Uncommon neurologic complications such as encephalopathy, encephalitis, and aseptic meningitis are confined almost exclusively to young children who have never been vaccinated for influenza and are naive to the virus. Another rare complication is Guillain-Barré syndrome, although this is usually seen a few weeks after recovery from the virus.

Extremely rare muscular complications of influenza include myocarditis and rhabdomyolysis. Additionally, Reye syndrome is life-threatening and associated with aspirin, especially during an influenza B infection. Children with suspected or confirmed influenza who have a high risk should be treated with influenza antivirals. This includes children < 5 years old, but especially < 2 years, children on chronic aspirin therapy, those with asthma who need daily inhaled corticosteroids, or those with neurodevelopmental conditions, chronic lung disease, heart disease, blood disorders (e.g., sickle cell disease), endocrine disorders, kidney disease, liver disease, metabolic disorders, or a weakened immune system.



An adolescent patient infected with an H1N1 strain of influenza (A) is more likely to develop a viral or bacterial lower respiratory tract infection.

Patients who are immunocompromised after a solid organ transplant (C) are more likely than others to develop a secondary fungal infection from invasive pulmonary aspergillosis.

Patients with asthma who need daily inhaled corticosteroids (D) are more likely than others to develop an asthma exacerbation, not severe neurologic complications of influenza.

One Step Further
Question:
Which bacterial pneumonia complicating an influenza infection can be particularly and rapidly fatal?

Reveal Answer:
Staphylococcus aureus.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Influenza

Presentation: sudden onset of fever, headache, cough, myalgia, sore throat, fatigue, nausea and vomiting, diarrhea
Winter months
Dx made clinically, can be confirmed with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) or viral culture
Tx: oseltamivir for children who
Are hospitalized
Have severe or progressive symptoms or complications
Have high risk of complications in any setting
Are in the outpatient setting if within 48 hours of onset of symptoms
Were exposed and are at high risk for complications for antiviral chemoprophylaxis
Complications: calf myositis, postinfluenza bacterial (S. aureus) pneumonia
arabicExplanation:
ليش: عدوى الـ influenza عند الأطفال عادة قصيرة ومحدودة، بس المضاعفات ممكن تصير ببعض الفئات. أكثر مضاعفة هي الـ secondary bacterial infection مثل otitis media أو sinusitis أو bacterial pneumonia، وأكثرها عند الأطفال أقل من سنتين. الـ asthma exacerbations شائعة فوق عمر سنتين خاصة يلي بياخدوا inhaled corticosteroids يومي. المضاعفات العصبية النادرة مثل encephalopathy وencephalitis وaseptic meningitis محصورة تقريبا بالأطفال الصغار يلي ما تطعموا أبدا للـ influenza وأجسامهم ما تعرفت على الفيروس.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا مرضى الـ asthma أو immunocompromised، بس هدول أكثر عرضة لتفاقم الـ asthma أو العدوى البكتيرية الثانوية، مو للمضاعفات العصبية. المضاعفات العصبية الشديدة محصورة بالأطفال غير المطعمين والـ naive للفيروس.

question: A 45-year-old man presents to the emergency department with swelling, pain, and a reddish-purple area over his lateral calf that has worsened over the last 4 hours. The patient and his family were caught in heavy evacuation traffic from severe river flooding in the Southeast and finally made it to a hospital. When leaving his home, the patient cut his leg on something in the mud. He attempted to clean the wound but did not have access to clean water or medical supplies. It has taken all day to exit the flooded area. Vital signs show HR 132 bpm, BP 103/62 mm Hg, RR 24/min, and T 39.1°C. The patient looks toxic. His lateral leg is exquisitely tender, is dark red and swollen, and has crepitus. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of this patient’s symptoms?
englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with signs and symptoms characteristic of a necrotizing soft tissue infection. These infections often have extensive soft tissue necrosis, systemic toxicity, and high mortality. Initially, the infection can appear benign, but it can quickly develop into severe infection and sepsis. People at greatest risk for a necrotizing soft tissue infection include those with diabetes, alcohol use disorder, kidney disease, heart disease, cancer, chronic skin infections, intravenous drug use disorder, and human immunodeficiency virus. However, necrotizing soft tissue infections can occur in healthy individuals, too. Because of improved hygiene in the United States, necrotizing soft tissue infections are most often polymicrobial with gram-positive cocci, gram-negative rods, and anaerobes. Clostridial infections have become less common, but they can still occur, most often in the setting of trauma with a dirty wound and lack of appropriate medical resources. Clostridium species and their spores are found in soil and marine environments. On physical exam, it can be difficult to differentiate a necrotizing infection due to Clostridium species versus more common organisms such as group A Streptococcus. However, the finding of crepitus on physical exam or air in the tissues found on radiographic imaging favors clostridial infection. This patient most likely has an infection with Clostridium perfringens. Prompt treatment with antibiotics and surgical debridement is required to prevent mortality in these patients. Often, they also require supportive measures for underlying sepsis.



Group A Streptococcus (B) is a common cause of necrotizing soft tissue infections, particularly in the United States where there are improved hygiene and sanitation practices. However, this patient’s history of a lack of medical resources, lack of clean water, traumatic wound that was exposed to soil, and crepitus on physical exam suggests Clostridium perfringens.

Staphylococcus aureus (C) is another common cause of necrotizing soft tissue infections, but again, this patient’s history is most consistent with Clostridium perfringens infection.

Vibrio vulnificus (D) is another important organism associated with necrotizing soft tissue infections, but this organism should be highly considered in patients who have been exposed to seawater environments.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the appropriate antibiotic regimen needed to treat a necrotizing soft tissue infection caused by Clostridium perfringens?

Reveal Answer:
A penicillin-based antibiotic plus clindamycin.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Necrotizing Fasciitis and Myonecrosis

Necrotizing fasciitis
Type 1: polymicrobial
Type 2: a single organism (most commonly group A Streptococcus)
Myonecrosis
Traumatic (Clostridium perfringens)
Spontaneous (Clostridium septicum)
Pain out of proportion to exam
Systemic signs of infection
Cellulitis progresses to dusky blue with bullae or vesicles
Radiograph: subcutaneous emphysema
Emergent surgical debridement, broad-spectrum antibiotics
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده necrotizing soft tissue infection: ألم شديد، toxaemia، لون أحمر-غامق، swelling وcrepitus. الـ clostridial infections صارت أقل شيوعا بس بتصير بالـ trauma مع جرح ملوث ونقص المصادر الطبية، وجراثيم Clostridium وأبواغها موجودة بالتربة والبيئات البحرية. تمييز الـ Clostridium عن group A Streptococcus صعب بالفحص، بس وجود الـ crepitus أو الهوا بالأنسجة بالتصوير بيميل لصالح الـ clostridial infection. فهون الجرح صار بالطين بعد الفيضان وما نظف بمي نظيفة، والأرجح Clostridium perfringens.
الفخ: في طلاب يختاروا الـ Vibrio vulnificus لأنه بالحالات يلي ذكر فيها الـ flood، بس هو مرتبط بالـ saltwater exposure وأكل seafood، مو بجرح ملوث بالطين. والـ Staphylococcus aureus بالعادة بيطلع abscess أو cellulitis بدون crepitus.

question: Which of the following is commonly seen in patients during the initial period of infection with yellow fever?
englishExplanation:
Yellow fever is difficult to distinguish from other possibly severe illnesses such as malaria, viral hepatitis, typhoid fever, leptospirosis, rickettsial infections, and Filoviridae (e.g., Ebola). It is a mosquito-borne illness that should be considered in patients returning from South America and Africa with sudden onset of nonspecific symptoms like fever, headache, and vomiting. While not specific for yellow fever, transaminitis is common. Other laboratory abnormalities are leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, prolonged clotting times, azotemia, and albuminuria. Cases that continue after the remission stage can present with severe gastrointestinal hemorrhage and multiorgan dysfunction. Prevention is key as vaccination is available. However, patients with confirmed yellow fever should be kept in mosquito-free areas to prevent transmission. Appropriate precautions are required as laboratory samples are also infectious.



Coma, delirium, hypoglycemia (A), hypotension, kidney failure (B), seizures (C), and gastrointestinal and other hemorrhages are generally only seen in yellow fever in cases that have progressed past the remission stage. Most cases are self-limited, and all are treated with supportive care.

One Step Further
Question:
How long before travel should a yellow fever vaccine be administered?

Reveal Answer:
10 days.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Yellow Fever

Transmitted via mosquitoes, endemic in tropical areas (Africa, South America)
Sx: begins as nonspecific febrile illness (fever, headache, myalgias), then a period of remission for ~24–48 hours
Some recover, but others can develop a severe illness with fever, vomiting, jaundice, acute liver injury, acute kidney failure, and hemorrhagic manifestations
Hallmark is jaundice with hemorrhagic fever
Dx: detected through IgM
Elevated LFTs, possibly DIC
Tx: supportive care
Prevention: vaccination before travel, mosquito avoidance precautions
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ yellow fever مرض منقول بالـ mosquito ولازم نفكر فيه لأي مريض راجع من أمريكا الجنوبية أو أفريقيا مع حرارة وصداع وقيء ببداية مفاجئة، وما بنقدر نفرقه عن malaria أو viral hepatitis أو typhoid أو leptospirosis. بالمرحلة الأولى الأولية، الـ transaminitis شائع مع إنه مو محدد للـ yellow fever. كمان ممكن نلاقي leukopenia وthrombocytopenia وprolonged clotting times وazotemia وalbuminuria.
الفخ: في طلاب يختاروا الـ hypoglycemia أو kidney failure أو seizures، بس هدول وComa والـ delirium والـ hemorrhage ما بتشوفها إلا بالحالات يلي تجاوزت الـ remission stage. أغلب حالات الـ yellow fever محدودة وعلاجها supportive care فقط.

question: A 4-year-old boy with hereditary spherocytosis presents to the ED with fever, rash, and fatigue. He had a fever for 4 days, which resolved before he developed the rash depicted above. During his evaluation, he is found to have a hemoglobin level of 5 g/dL and an undetectable reticulocyte count. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient’s illness?
englishExplanation:
Parvovirus B19 is a single-stranded DNA icosahedral virus that causes a wide range of symptoms. It most commonly presents with a fever for several days, followed by several weeks of profound reticulocytopenia. A characteristic raised, lacelike, or reticular rash appears after a few weeks, which is usually when the diagnosis is first considered. The rash can also be a fiery red or hyperpigmented rash on the cheeks (often called slapped cheek), worse with transitioning from outdoors into a warm room. Additional symptoms are less specific and less common, including arthritis, arthralgia, sore throat, headache, and decreased appetite. More serious illnesses include myocarditis and neonatal hydrops.

The profound drop in reticulocytes from parvovirus B19 is transient and normally tolerated well, but in patients whose hemoglobin has a short half-life, it can cause an aplastic crisis. This includes patients with sickle-cell disease, hereditary spherocytosis, thalassemia, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, and pyruvate kinase deficiency. Such patients may require hemoglobin transfusions until their bone marrow recovers.



HIV (A) also causes a wide range of symptoms, but associated rashes tend to be well circumscribed, oval or round, not lacelike or with a slapped-cheek appearance.

Iron deficiency (B) is an incredibly common cause of anemia but does not cause a fever or a rash.

Patients with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (C) typically have signs of intravascular hemolysis and less commonly have bone marrow dysfunction such as reticulocytopenia.

One Step Further
Question:
How does parvovirus B19 cause fetal hydrops in the fetus of an infected pregnant patient?

Reveal Answer:
Severe fetal anemia leads to cardiac failure and fetal hydrops.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Parvovirus B19

Nonenveloped, single-stranded linear DNA virus
Erythema infectiosum (fifth disease) is caused by parvovirus B19
Most common in children aged 4–10 years
Typically preceded by URI symptoms 3–4 days before rash onset
PE shows an erythematous, macular, slapped-cheek rash
Diagnosed clinically
Adults may develop arthropathy in small joints of the hands and feet, with or without a rash
Confirmed through serologic testing
Can cause a transient aplastic crisis due to a halt in erythropoiesis, leading to severe anemia, particularly in patients with underlying red blood cell dysfunction (e.g., sickle cell disease)
In immunosuppressed patients, can cause pure red blood cell aplasia due to the suppression of erythropoiesis, leading to severe chronic anemia
Fetal complications from maternal infection may include fetal anemia, cardiomegaly, hydrops fetalis, and growth restriction
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ Parvovirus B19 فيروس DNA وحيد السلسلة، وعادة بيجي بحرارة لعدة أيام وبعدها reticulocytopenia عميقة لأسابيع، ثم rash شبكي lacelike على شكل كف اليدين على الخدود (slapped cheek). النقص الشديد بالـ reticulocytes مؤقت وبيتحمل عادة، بس بالأمراض يلي فيها عمر كريات حمر قصير بيسبب aplastic crisis، ومنها hereditary spherocytosis وsickle-cell وthalassemia وG6PD deficiency، وهون الـ Hb نزل لـ 5 g/dL مع reticulocyte غير قابل للقياس بعد حرارة 4 أيام وrash.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا الـ iron deficiency لأنه أشهر سبب للفقر، بس ما بيسبب لا حرارة ولا rash ولا reticulocytopenia عميقة. والـ HIV والـ PNH ما بيعطوا هالـ lacelike rash مع aplastic crisis بهالعمر.

question: Which of the following is the first-line treatment for scabies in adults?
englishExplanation:
Topical permethrin 5% cream
Explanation
Topical permethrin 5% cream is considered the most effective first-line treatment for scabies in adults. It is safe, welltolerated, and has a high cure rate. Oral ivermectin is an alternative, especially in cases of widespread or severe infestations, but it's typically used as a second-line treatment. Antihistamines and corticosteroids may help with symptoms
but do not treat the infestation itself.
Advise the person and/or their parents/carers that: 
All members of their household, their sexual partners within the past month, and any other close personal contacts
(even if asymptomatic) should also be treated with topical permethrin 5% cream.
Referral to genito-urinary medicine (GUM) may be required for partner notification.
Their bedding, clothing, and towels (and those of all potentially infested contacts) should be decontaminated by
washing at a high temperature (at least 60°C) and drying in a hot dryer, or dry-cleaning, or by sealing in a plastic bag
for at least 72 hours.
Itching may continue for up to 4 weeks after successful treatment of scabies. People should seek medical advice if
itching persists for longer than 2-4 weeks after the last treatment application.
https://cks.nice.org.uk/topics/scabies/management/management-of-scabies/
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ scabies عند البالغين خط أول هو topical permethrin 5% cream لأنه آمن ومتحمل ومعدل الشفاء عالي. لازم ننبه إنه كل أفراد البيت والشركاء الجنسيين بآخر شهر وأي مخالط قريب يتعالجوا حتى لو ما في أعراض. كمان الفراش والملابس والمناشف تتغسل بحرارة 60 درجة أو أكثر وتنشف بمجفف حار أو تتحفظ بكيس بلاستيكي 72 ساعة. الحكة ممكن تكمل لـ 4 أسابيع بعد العلاج الناجح، ولازم نرجع للطبيب لو استمرت أكثر من 2-4 أسابيع.
الفخ: في طلاب يختاروا oral ivermectin كن علاج أول، بس هو بديل ويستخدم كخط ثاني خاصة بالحالات الواسعة أو الشديدة. الـ antihistamines والـ corticosteroids بيساعدوا بالأعراض بس ما بيعالجوا الـ infestation نفسه.

question:
A 28-year-old resident doctor presents to the Emergency Department after a needlestick injury that occurred 30 minutes ago while
taking blood from a known HIV patient who is not on any treatment.
They do not know their viral load.
The needle penetrated through their glove and caused a deep puncture wound on their right index finger. The patient has no significant
past medical history and is not on any regular medications. Their
tetanus status is up to date.

On examination, there is a small puncture wound on the right index
finger with minimal bleeding. The wound has been washed thoroughly with soap and water.
What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Start immediate prophylaxis with Tenofovir/Emtricitabine and Raltegravir
Start immediate prophylaxis with Tenofovir/Emtricitabine only
Obtain the source patient's viral load before starting prophylaxis
Start prophylaxis after obtaining baseline bloods from the healthcare worker
Defer prophylaxis until Occupational Health review in the morning

correctAnswer: Start prophylaxis after obtaining baseline bloods from the healthcare worker
englishExplanation:
Start prophylaxis after obtaining baseline bloods from the
healthcare worker
Explanation
In cases of high-risk needlestick injuries from known HIV-positive
source patients, post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) should be started as
soon as possible, ideally within 24 hours and no later than 72 hours.
The recommended regimen includes two nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (Tenofovir/Emtricitabine) plus an integrase inhibitor
(Raltegravir).
Baseline bloods should be taken first- as if the initial bloods show that
the recipient was HIV/Hep B/C negative and the repeat bloods show
that they are positive, then this can be identified as the event that
caused the infection. You do not need to wait for the results of the
bloods.

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01160 source page 859](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01160-study-p859.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01160 source page 860](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01160-study-p860.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01160 source page 861](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01160-study-p861.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بالإصابات عالية الخطورة من مريض HIV معروف وغير معالج، الـ post-exposure prophylaxis لازم يبلش بأسرع وقت، والأفضل خلال 24 ساعة وما بعد 72 ساعة. النظام الموصى فيه تنين nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors وهم Tenofovir/Emtricitabine مع integrase inhibitor وهو Raltegravir. القاعدة إنه ناخد الـ baseline bloods من الـ healthcare worker أولا لأنها لو طلعت سلبية وشوي بعدين صارت موجبة منعرف إنه هي الحدث يلي سبب العدوى، وما بنحتاج ننتظر النتائج لنبلش العلاج.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا يبلشوا العلاج فورا بالـ Tenofovir/Emtricitabine وRaltegravir من دون ما ياخدوا baseline bloods، فبينسوا الخطوة يلي بتحدد هل العدوى من هل حادثة. والـ defer للـ Occupational Health للصبح غلط لأنه بيأخر العلاج وما في داعي ننتظر.

question:
A 65-year-old male presents to the Emergency Department with
fever, headache, and neck stiffness for 2 days. Which antibiotic regimen would be most appropriate?
englishExplanation:
Ceftriaxone + Amoxicillin
Explanation
In adults over 50 years old or those who are immunosuppressed, empiric treatment for bacterial meningitis should include coverage for Listeria monocytogenes, which is covered by Amoxicillin. Ceftriaxone covers the most common causes of bacterial meningitis (S. pneumoniae
and N. meningitidis).
https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng240/chapter/Recommendations#antibiotics-for-bacterial-meningitis-in-hospital

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01161 source page 861](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01161-study-p861.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01161 source page 2069](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01161-frcem-p2069.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01161 source page 2070](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01161-frcem-p2070.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01161 source page 2071](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01161-frcem-p2071.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01161 source page 2072](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01161-frcem-p2072.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عمره 65 سنة وعنده fever وheadache وneck stiffness لمدة يومين، يعني bacterial meningitis محتمل. بالبالغين فوق الـ 50 سنة أو المثبطين مناعيا، العلاج التجريبي لازم يغطي Listeria monocytogenes، والـ Amoxicillin هو يلي بيغطيها. والـ Ceftriaxone بيغطي أشهر المسببات وهي S. pneumoniae وN. meningitidis. فالنظام المناسب لهالمريض هو Ceftriaxone مع Amoxicillin لأنه بيجمع تغطية الاثنين، وهاد يلي بيمنع تأخير العلاج لحالات Listeria الخطيرة.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا Ceftriaxone وحده لأنه منسي إنه فوق الـ 50 سنة لازم نضيف غطاء Listeria. والـ Vancomycin ما بينضاف إلا لو كان في خطر pneumococcal resistance، مو كغطاء روتيني بكل الحالات.

question:
A 45-year-old sheep farmer presents to the Emergency Department with a painless, erythematous, circular lesion
on his right thumb. The lesion has a central crust and raised edges.
Which of the following is the most appropriate management for this condition?
englishExplanation:
Supportive care and monitoring
Explanation
The clinical presentation described is consistent with orf, also known as contagious ecthyma or "shepherd’ sore." Orf
is a zoonotic viral infection caused by the parapoxvirus, commonly affecting sheep and goats. Humans can contract
the virus through direct contact with infected animals or contaminated fomites.
Orf is typically self-limiting and resolves spontaneously within 4-8 weeks.

The lesion is usually painless and does not require specific treatment.

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01162 source page 861](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01162-study-p861.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01162 source page 862](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01162-study-p862.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01162 source page 2072](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01162-frcem-p2072.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01162 source page 2073](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01162-frcem-p2073.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01162 source page 2074](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01162-frcem-p2074.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: القصة مزارع أغنام عنده lesion دائرية حمرا وغير مؤلمة على الإبهام مع central crust وحواف مرتفعة، وهاد بيتوافق مع orf المعروف بـ contagious ecthyma أو shepherd's sore. الـ orf عدوى zoonotic viral سببها parapoxvirus وبتنتقل من الأغنام والماعز أو الـ contaminated fomites بالتواصل المباشر. المرض عادة self-limiting وبيشفى لحاله خلال 4-8 أسابيع، والـ lesion غير مؤلم وما بيحتاج علاج خاص.
الفخ: بعض الطلاب يختاروا الـ oral antibiotics أو الـ surgical excision لأنهم مفكرينها عدوى بكتيرية أو خراج. القصة المهنية لمزارع الأغنام مع الـ painless lesion والـ crust هي المفتاح للـ orf، وعلاجه supportive care ومراقبة بس.

question:
A 28-year-old woman presents to the Emergency Department with a severe headache, fever, and neck stiffness.
She mentions that her university roommate was recently diagnosed with meningococcal meningitis. The patient is
diagnosed with probable meningococcal meningitis and admitted for treatment. Which of the following is the most
appropriate antibiotic for meningitis prophylaxis for her close contacts?
englishExplanation:
Ciprofloxacin
Explanation
Ciprofloxacin is the most appropriate antibiotic for meningitis prophylaxis in close contacts of patients with meningococcal meningitis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها احتمال meningococcal meningitis ورفيقتها بالجامعة مشخصية، فلازم نعطي prophylaxis للـ close contacts. الـ Ciprofloxacin هو الأنسب للـ prophylaxis بالمخالطين القريبين لمريض الـ meningococcal meningitis. الـ prophylaxis ضروري لأنه بيوقف انتقال العدوى وبيمنع تفشيها بين المخالطين، وبنعطيها للمخالطين حتى لو ما عندهم أي أعراض واضحة، وهاد أساس الوقاية من التفشي داخل المجتمع الجامعي المزدحم.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا الـ Ceftriaxone لأنه أقوى، بس للـ prophylaxis يلي موصى فيه هو الـ Ciprofloxacin أو rifampin أو ceftriaxone بجرعة واحدة، وهون الجواب الـ Ciprofloxacin. والـ Vancomycin والـ Amoxicillin ما إلهم دور بالـ prophylaxis هون.

question:
A 35-year-old woman presents to the Emergency Department complaining of itchy, red bumps on her skin. She reports noticing small, reddish-brown insects in her bedding at home. The patient is visibly anxious and concerned
about potential disease transmission. Which of the following statements is the most appropriate response to reassure the patient?

options.text: Bed bugs can transmit various blood-borne diseases
Bed bug bites often lead to severe allergic reactions
Bed bugs are not known to transmit diseases to humans
Bed bug infestations require immediate medical treatment
Bed bugs can cause long-term health complications

correctAnswer: Bed bugs are not known to transmit diseases to humans
englishExplanation:
Bed bugs are not known to transmit diseases to humans
Explanation
Bed bugs are not known to transmit diseases to humans. This statement provides accurate reassurance to the patient
without downplaying the discomfort and inconvenience of bed bug infestations.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها حكة وred bumps بشعرها ولاحظت حشرات صغيرة reddish-brown بالفراش، وهاد يعني bed bugs، وهي قلقانة من انتقال الأمراض. الحقيقة العلمية إنه الـ bed bugs غير معروفة بإنها تنقل أمراض للبشر، فهاد الكلام بيطمن المريضة بصدق من دون ما نقلل من انزعاجها ومشاكلها. فالرد المناسب هو إنه ما في داعي للخوف من عدوى منقولة من الحشرة نفسها.
الفخ: في طلاب يختاروا إنه الـ bed bugs تنقل أمراض blood-borne لأنهم بيخلطوا بينها وبين البعوض أو القراد. أو يختاروا إنه الحشرات تسبب مضاعفات صحية طويلة، وهالكلام غير مدعوم، لأن الضرر الأساسي هو الحكة والانزعاج.

question:
A 32-year-old primary school teacher presents to the Emergency Department with a 3-day history of fever and a widespread itchy rash.
The rash started on her trunk and has now spread to her face, scalp,
and extremities. She reports having had contact with a student who
was diagnosed with chickenpox last week.
Vital Signs:
Temperature: 38.2°C
Heart Rate: 92/min
Blood Pressure: 118/76 mmHg
Respiratory Rate: 16/min
SpO2: 98% on room air
General: Alert, oriented, mild distress due to itching Skin: Multiple
crops of vesicular lesions in different stages (macules, papules, vesicles, and crusted lesions) distributed over the face, trunk, and extremities. Approximately 30% of lesions are crusted.

What is the most appropriate next step in management regarding
this patient's return to work?

options.text: She can return to work immediately
She can return to work when all lesions have crusted over
She can return to work 5 days after the rash first appeared
She can return to work when she becomes afebrile
She can return to work when new lesions stop appearing

correctAnswer: She can return to work when all lesions have crusted over
englishExplanation:
She can return to work when all lesions have crusted over
Explanation
A person with chickenpox is considered infectious until all lesions have
crusted over, which typically takes 5 to 7 days after the rash first appears. This is the standard guideline for determining when isolation can
be discontinued.

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01166 source page 2078](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01166-frcem-p2078.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01166 source page 2079](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01166-frcem-p2079.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01166 source page 2080](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01166-frcem-p2080.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها chickenpox مع حرارة وrash منتشر بأطوار مختلفة، وعندها 30% من الـ lesions crusted. القاعدة إنه مريض الـ chickenpox يضل معدي لحد ما تكل الـ lesions كلها تعمل crust، وهاد بياخد عادة 5-7 أيام من بداية الـ rash. وهاد هو المعيار المعتمد لتوقيف الـ isolation، فترجع عالشغل بس لما تتقشر كل الـ lesions، وهي لسا بمرحلة معدية لأن 70% منها مو متقشرة.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا إنه ترجع للشغل لما تصير afebrile، بس انقطاع الحرارة ما بيعني انتهاء العدوى لأنه الفيروس ممكن ينتقل من الـ vesicles. كمان خيار إنه ترجع بعد 5 أيام أو لما توقف الـ lesions الجديدة غير كاف، لأن المعيار هو تقشر كل الـ lesions.

question:
A 45-year-old sheep farmer presents to the Emergency Department with a painless, erythematous, nodular lesion
on his right thumb. The lesion has been present for about a week and has gradually increased in size.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Orf virus infection
Explanation
Orf, also known as ecthyma contagiosum, is a zoonotic infection caused by a parapoxvirus primarily affecting sheep
and goats. Farmers, veterinarians, and others who handle infected animals are at risk of contracting the virus through
direct contact with infected animals or contaminated fomites.
Orf typically presents as a painless, erythematous, nodular lesion on exposed skin, often on the hands or fingers. The
history of a sheep farmer with an atraumatic finger ulcer is highly suggestive of this diagnosis. The infection is usually
self-limiting and resolves without scarring within 4-8 weeks.

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01167 source page 863](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01167-study-p863.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01167 source page 864](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01167-study-p864.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01167 source page 2080](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01167-frcem-p2080.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01167 source page 2081](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01167-frcem-p2081.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01167 source page 2082](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01167-frcem-p2082.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: القصة مزارع أغنام وعنده lesion erythematous nodular غير مؤلمة على الإبهام زاد حجمها أسبوع، وهاد بيتوافق مع orf المعروف كمان بـ ecthyma contagiosum. الـ orf عدوى zoonotic viral سببها parapoxvirus بتصيب الأغنام والماعز، والمزارعين والبيطريين الأكثر عرضة للعدوى بالتواصل المباشر مع الحيوان المصاب أو الـ fomites الملوثة. الـ lesion عادة غير مؤلمة وتخف لحالها بدون ندبة خلال 4-8 أسابيع، فالعرض المميز هو إبهام مزارع أغنام بلا ألم.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا cutaneous anthrax لأنه بيعطي ulcer سودا بالجزارين وصناعة الجلود مع edema شديد وتسمم، وهون المريض مستقر والـ lesion غير مؤلمة بس. والـ herpetic whitlow بيوجع كتير وبيطلع vesicles على الإصبع، والـ pyogenic granuloma بيطلع بسرعة بعد رضة وبينزف.

question:
A 72-year-old female presents to the Emergency Department with a 5-day history of profuse watery diarrhoea (>10
episodes/day), lower abdominal cramping, and fever. She completed a course of co-amoxiclav 2 weeks ago for a
chest infection.
Vital Signs:
Temperature 38.2°C
HR 102/min
BP 128/75 mmHg
RR 18/min
SpO2 97% on room air
On examination: The patient appears dehydrated with dry mucous membranes. Abdominal examination reveals
generalised tenderness, particularly in the left lower quadrant, without guarding or rebound. Bowel sounds are
hyperactive.
Blood tests:
WBC 15.2 x 10^9/L
CRP 85 mg/L
Creatinine 132 μmol/L (baseline 85)
Albumin 31 g/L.
The stool C. difficile toxin test is positive.

What is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Vancomycin 125mg orally four times daily for 10 days
Metronidazole 400mg orally three times daily for 10 days
Vancomycin 250mg orally four times daily for 14 days
Metronidazole 500mg orally three times daily for 14 days

correctAnswer: Vancomycin 125mg orally four times daily for 10 days
englishExplanation:
Vancomycin 125mg orally four times daily for 10 days
Explanation
According to current guidelines, oral vancomycin 125mg four times daily for 10 days is the first-line antibiotic for a
first episode of mild, moderate or severe C. difficile infection.
While metronidazole was previously used for mild cases, vancomycin has shown superior cure rates and is now preferred. Fidaxomicin is typically reserved for recurrent infections or as a second-line if vancomycin is ineffective.
https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng199/resources/visual-summary-pdf-9194639149

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01168 source page 864](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01168-study-p864.jpg)

![Study-FRCEM-2025-01168 source page 865](images/Study-FRCEM-2025-01168-study-p865.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة عندها إسهال مائي غزير مع fever وتشنج بطن بعد مضاد حيوي قبل أسبوعين، والـ C. difficile toxin test إيجابي، فهي عندها C. difficile infection بأول نوبة. بالدلائل الحديثة، الـ oral vancomycin بجرعة 125mg أربع مرات باليوم لمدة 10 أيام هو خط أول للمرحلة الخفيفة أو المتوسطة أو الشديدة من أول نوبة. الـ Metronidazole كان يستخدم زمان بالحالات الخفيفة، بس الـ vancomycin أظهر معدلات شفاء أفضل وصار مفضل، والـ Fidaxomicin عادة بنحفظه للعدوى المتكررة.
الفخ: كتير طلاب يختاروا الـ Metronidazole لأنه كان الخط الأول القديم، بس ما صار مفضل لأنه الـ vancomycin معدل شفائه أعلى. والـ Fidaxomicin والجرعة الأعلى من الـ vancomycin ما إلهن دور بأول نوبة غير معقدة.

question:
A 20-year-old man presents with a painless lesion on 
his penis (Figure 11.2). He states that he has had six sexual partners in the last 4 months, including both men 
and women, and he rarely uses protection. Which of the 
following is the MOST APPROPRIATE treatment?
englishExplanation:
4.  The answer is B.  (Chapter 153) Primary syphilis is 
characterized by a painless chancre with indurated borders on the penis, as in this case. Painless ulcers may be 
found on the vulva in women or other areas of sexual 
contact. Treponema pallidum, the spirochete that causes 
syphilis, remains very sensitive to penicillin and this is 
considered first-line treatment. Acyclovir is used to treat 
herpes simplex virus, which presents with painful genital 
ulcers. Metronidazole and clindamycin are used to treat 
bacterial vaginosis, which is not commonly associated 
with genital ulcers.

![Tintinalli-2023-00368 source page 150](images/Tintinalli-2023-00368-Tintinalli-2023-p0150.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00368 source page 151](images/Tintinalli-2023-00368-Tintinalli-2023-p0151.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00368 source page 159](images/Tintinalli-2023-00368-Tintinalli-2023-p0159.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض عنده painless chancre بحواف indurated على القضيب، وهاد الـ primary syphilis، والـ Treponema pallidum الـ spirochete المسبب بيضل حساس جدا للـ penicillin والـ penicillin هو العلاج الأول. الـ ulcers غير المؤلمة ممكن تكون على الـ vulva عند النساء أو مناطق أخرى من التواصل الجنسي. فالجواب المناسب هو الـ Benzathine penicillin G، وعنده كمان ستة شركاء جنسيين بأربع شهور وما يستخدم حماية.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا الـ Acyclovir لأنه بفكروا كل قرحة تناسلية هي herpes، بس الـ herpes بتعطي ulcers مؤلمة ومتكررة ومجموعة vesicles مو chancre واحد. والـ Metronidazole والـ Clindamycin للـ bacterial vaginosis وليس لها علاقة بقرحة القضيب.

question:
Which of the following medications used to treat sexually transmitted infections is considered safe for use 
during pregnancy?
englishExplanation:
8.  The answer is A. (Chapter 153, Table 11.2) Penicillin, ceftriaxone, azithromycin, cefixime, metronidazole, erythromycin, and acyclovir are thought to be safe for use during 
pregnancy. Tetracyclines and fluoroquinolones should be 
avoided during pregnancy. Tinidazole should be avoided 
in the first 3 months of pregnancy.

![Tintinalli-2023-00369 source page 151](images/Tintinalli-2023-00369-Tintinalli-2023-p0151.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00369 source page 159](images/Tintinalli-2023-00369-Tintinalli-2023-p0159.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بالحمل لازم نختار دواء آمن للجنين، والـ acyclovir من الأدوية الآمنة لعلاج الأمراض المنقولة جنسيا خلال الحمل. كمان الـ penicillin وceftriaxone وazithromycin وcefixime وmetronidazole وerythromycin بتعتبر آمنة بالحمل. أما الـ tetracyclines والـ fluoroquinolones فيجب تجنبها بالحمل، والـ tinidazole يفضل تجنبه بالثلاث شهور الأولى من الحمل. فالـ acyclovir هو الجواب لأنه آمن ومستخدم للأمراض المنقولة جنسيا بالحمل.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا الـ Doxycycline لأنه فعال بأمراض كثيرة، بس هو من الـ tetracyclines الممنوعة بالحمل لضررها على الأسنان والعظم. والـ Ofloxacin من الـ fluoroquinolones الممنوعة كمان، والـ Tinidazole يفضل تجنبه بالثلث الأول.

question:
A 55-year-old man with chronic kidney disease on 
hemodialysis presents to the emergency department 
for fever and increased weakness today. His wife has 
noticed that he seems confused about the events of 
the last 2 days. Vital signs reveal fever, tachycardia, 
and hypotension. Which of the following organisms 
is the MOST LIKELY cause of bacteremia in this 
patient?
englishExplanation:
15.  The answer is C.  (Chapter 151) Bacteremia from 
indwelling medical devices such as intraperitoneal or 
intravascular dialysis catheters may be a source of septic 
shock. The most prevalent causes of bacteremia are Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Neisseria 
meningitidis. Pseudomonas aeruginosa and other gramnegative bacteria are occasional causes of bacteremia in 
injection drug users. Streptococcus pyogenes is more commonly associated with necrotizing soft tissue infection 
leading to sepsis.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض على hemodialysis وعنده fever وtachycardia وhypotension مع confusion، فالأرجح septic shock من bacteremia من الـ dialysis catheter. الـ bacteremia من الأجهزة الطبية داخل الجسم مثل catheters ممكن تكون مصدر الـ septic shock. وأشهر مسببات الـ bacteremia هي Staphylococcus aureus وStreptococcus pneumoniae وNeisseria meningitidis، فالأكثر ترجيحا هون هو S. aureus لأنه الأشيع مع الـ indwelling catheters.
الفخ: في طلاب يختاروا الـ Pseudomonas aeruginosa لأنه مرتبط بالـ catheters، بس الصحيح إنه هو وباقي gram-negative bacteria مسببات متفرقة للـ bacteremia عند متعاطي المخدرات بالوريد. والـ Streptococcus pyogenes أكثر ارتباطا بالـ necrotizing soft tissue infection المؤدي للـ sepsis.

question:
A 22-year-old healthy man presents to the emergency 
department for “pimples” that are spreading on his 
body. He states that he otherwise feels well and has 
no medical history. He is afebrile and well appearing 
on examination. Examining the skin, you see a patch 
of carbuncles on the anterior chest wall and a wellcircumscribed 1-cm abscess on the inner left thigh 
without cellulitis. Bedside glucose is 88. Which of the 
following is the MOST APPROPRIATE management?

options.text: Incision and drainage and discharge with oral
Incision and drainage and discharge with wound
Warm compresses and discharge with oral
Warm compresses and discharge with wound care

correctAnswer: Incision and drainage and discharge with oral
englishExplanation:
18.  The answer is A. (Chapter 152) Incision and drainage is the recommended treatment for large furuncles, 
carbuncles, and skin abscesses. Antibiotics are recommended for patients with multiple lesions, extensive 
surrounding cellulitis, immunosuppression, or signs of 
systemic infection.

![Tintinalli-2023-00382 source page 153](images/Tintinalli-2023-00382-Tintinalli-2023-p0153.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00382 source page 163](images/Tintinalli-2023-00382-Tintinalli-2023-p0163.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض شاب سليم مع carbuncles على الصدر وabscess محدد 1 سم على الفخذ الداخلي بدون cellulitis، والحرارة طبيعية وسكر الدم 88 يعني ما في diabetes. الـ incision and drainage هو العلاج الموصى فيه للـ furuncles الكبيرة والـ carbuncles والـ skin abscesses. الـ antibiotics بتوصى فيها للمرضى عندهم lesions متعددة أو cellulitis واسعة أو نقص مناعة أو علامات عدوى جهازية، وهاد المريض عنده carbuncles متعددة فيعطى I&D مع oral antibiotics عند الخروج.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا warm compresses بدون شق وتفريغ، بس الـ abscess والـ carbuncle لازم يتفجروا بالـ incision and drainage وضغط الحرارة وحده ما بيكفي. أما الخروج بدون antibiotics ولا I&D فيغلط لوجود أكثر من lesion.

question:
A 35-year-old healthy female florist presents to the 
emergency department for a nonhealing nodule on 
her right arm despite daily warm soaks and topical 
antibiotic ointment (Figure 11.7). Which of the following organisms should be considered when choosing an appropriate antibiotic?
englishExplanation:
20.  The answer is C.  (Chapter 152) Sporotrichosis is 
a mycotic infection caused by the fungus Sporothrix 
schenckii and is commonly found in soil, sphagnum moss, 
and decaying vegetable matter. It is most common in tropical and subtropical zones but can be found among florists, gardeners, and agricultural workers. Inoculation is 
often secondary to penetrating trauma from plant thorns, 
wood splinters, or contaminated organic materials. After 
the fungus enters the body through a break in the skin, 
lesions restricted to the site of inoculation may appear as a 
crusted ulcer or verrucous plaque. The surrounding skin 
may then become erythematous and ulcerate, resulting in 
a chancre with local lymphadenitis. If left untreated, the 
initial painless nodule or papule at the site of inoculation 
can go on to develop subcutaneous nodules with skip 
areas along local lymphatic channels. Aeromonas hydrophilia is associated with freshwater laceration exposures. 
Mycobacterium marinum is associated with fish tanks. 
Vibrio parahaemolyticus is associated with saltwater exposure, lacerations from fish or fishbones, and underlying 
hepatic cirrhosis.

![Tintinalli-2023-00384 source page 153](images/Tintinalli-2023-00384-Tintinalli-2023-p0153.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00384 source page 154](images/Tintinalli-2023-00384-Tintinalli-2023-p0154.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00384 source page 163](images/Tintinalli-2023-00384-Tintinalli-2023-p0163.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريضة florist وعندها nodule ما بيشفى على الذراع رغم الكمادات الدافية والمرهم المضاد الحيوي. الـ sporotrichosis عدوى فطرية سببها Sporothrix schenckii وبتنتقل من التربة والـ sphagnum moss والمواد النباتية المتحللة، وأكثر شي عند بائعي الزهور والبستانيين والعاملين بالزراعة. العدوى عادة بعد رضة من شوكة نبات أو شظية خشب، وبتبلش كـ painless nodule أو papule بموقع الدخول، وبتكمل لـ subcutaneous nodules مع skip areas على طول الـ lymphatic channels.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا الـ Aeromonas hydrophila أو Mycobacterium marinum لأنهم فاكرين أي nodule ما تشفى هي عدوى atypical mycobacteria. الـ Aeromonas مرتبط بالجروح بالمياه العذبة والـ Mycobacterium marinum بحوض السمك، بس المهنة florist تودينا مباشرة للـ Sporothrix schenckii.

question:
A healthy 22-year-old man presents to the emergency 
department with 2 days of aching left shoulder pain 
after working out. On examination, you observe a 
rash (Figure 11.9). Which of the following statements 
regarding this condition is TRUE?

options.text: The patient also likely has oral lesions on
The patient should be tested for human immunodeficiency virus infection.
The rash commonly crosses the midline.
The rash is easily treated with topical antifungals.

correctAnswer: The patient should be tested for human immunodeficiency virus infection.
englishExplanation:
24.  The answer is B. (Chapter 154) The presence of herpes 
zoster in a young, otherwise healthy person may be a sign 
of human immunodeficiency virus infection or immune 
suppressed condition. Herpes zoster involving more than 
three dermatomes should also prompt consideration to an 
immunodeficient condition. Herpes zoster often begins 
with a prodrome of pain, itching, and paresthesias in one 
or more dermatomes. These symptoms are followed by 
the development of a maculopapular rash that becomes 
vesicular with lesions in different stages of development. 
The eruption of herpes zoster does not cross the midline 
and is not treated with topical antifungal treatments. Herpes simplex infections can present with oral lesions, but 
herpes zoster is not associated with oral lesions.

CHAPTER 11  •  Systemic Infectious Disorders
151

![Tintinalli-2023-00385 source page 154](images/Tintinalli-2023-00385-Tintinalli-2023-p0154.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00385 source page 163](images/Tintinalli-2023-00385-Tintinalli-2023-p0163.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00385 source page 164](images/Tintinalli-2023-00385-Tintinalli-2023-p0164.jpg)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض شاب سليم وعنده ألم بكتفه مع rash، أي herpes zoster (shingles). وجود الـ herpes zoster بشخص شاب وسليم ممكن يكون علامة على عدوى HIV أو حالة نقص مناعة. ولو الـ herpes zoster صار بأكثر من ثلاثة dermatomes لازم نفكر كمان بحالة نقص مناعة، فالصحيح إنه يفحص للـ HIV. الـ herpes zoster بيبلش عادة بألم وحكة وتنميل بديرمة واحدة ثم rash maculopapular بتصير vesicles بأطوار مختلفة، وما بيتعدى الـ midline أبدا.
الفخ: الطلاب يختاروا إنه الـ rash بيتعدى الـ midline أو إنه بيتعالج بمضاد فطري موضعي، وهاد غلط لأن الـ zoster بضل بديرمة واحدة وما بيتعدى الـ midline وما بيتعالج بمضاد فطري. خيار وجود lesions بالفم غلط كمان لأنه هاد أشهر بالـ herpes simplex مو الـ zoster.

question:
A 16-year-old boy presents for fever, headache, sore 
throat, and odynophagia, upper abdominal pain and 
fatigue. He is tolerating his secretions without difficulty and speaking clearly. On oropharyngeal examination, you note the following. Laboratory testing 
reveals lymphocytosis (Figure 11.10). Which of the 
following is TRUE regarding this condition?
englishExplanation:
25.  The answer is C.  (Chapter 154) Epstein-Barr virus 
(EBV) is the causative agent of heterophile-positive infectious mononucleosis. EBV infection is also associated 
with cancers such as B-cell lymphoma, Hodgkin’s disease, 
Burkitt’s lymphoma, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. 
There are two age-related peaks of infection: early childhood and young adulthood with college students and 
military recruits experiencing the highest morbidity. EBV 
requires close contact for transmission via salivary secretions. Rest and analgesia are the mainstays of treatment 
with supportive management and symptom control.

question:
Which patient characteristic is associated with the 
highest pretest risk of acquiring human immunodeficiency virus infection?
englishExplanation:
27.  The answer is A. (Chapter 155) African Americans 
represent only 14% of the total U.S. population, but this 
group accounted for almost half (44%) of new human 
immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infections in the year 
2010. The rate of new infections among black men was 
the highest of any group by race and sex, notably in men 
having sex with men. Risk factors associated with acquiring HIV infection include homosexuality or bisexuality, 
injection drug use, receipt of a blood transfusion prior to 
1985, and maternal HIV infection.

![Tintinalli-2023-00390 source page 155](images/Tintinalli-2023-00390-Tintinalli-2023-p0155.jpg)

![Tintinalli-2023-00390 source page 164](images/Tintinalli-2023-00390-Tintinalli-2023-p0164.jpg)
