الفخ: الطلاب يختارون alteplase لأنه علاج الـ stroke الحاد. لكن أعراض هالمريض رجعت طبيعية لحالها والفحص العصبي سليم والـ NIHSS صفر، فالـ thrombolytic ما له أي دور هنا وخطر النزف أكبر من فائدته. أما الـ heparin أو الإخراج بدون تقييم وعائي فما بمثّلوا الرعاية الصحيحة.

question: Which of the following is recommended as first-line treatment for patients with idiopathic intracranial hypertension?
englishExplanation:
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is caused by increased brain water content and decreased CSF outflow. Patients typically present with a generalized headache that is gradual in onset. The headache may be worsened by eye movements. Additionally, any Valsalva maneuver decreases cerebral venous return and can worsen the headache. Patients will often have visual symptoms, including transient vision loss secondary to ischemia of the visual pathways.

Other typical symptoms include nausea, vomiting, and lightheadedness. Funduscopic examination reveals papilledema. Diagnosis is made based on MRI findings or an increased opening pressure found on lumbar puncture. Treatment focuses on decreasing CSF production initially with acetazolamide. Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor used alone or in combination with furosemide. Weight loss is also recommended.



Corticosteroids (B) may be used on rare occasions as a temporizing measure but are not indicated in routine care of IIH.

Gabapentin (C) is an anticonvulsant and neuropathic pain medication sometimes used off-label in the management of IIH. It is not a first-line treatment for IIH but may be considered when patients experience persistent headache symptoms that do not respond adequately to primary therapies like acetazolamide.

Serial lumbar punctures (D) to remove excess CSF can be effective, but the procedures are invasive and painful. They are not generally recommended due to the rapid reaccumulation of CSF and the discomfort of serial lumbar punctures that can be associated with complications like post-lumbar puncture headache.

Ventricular shunt placement (E) and optic nerve sheath fenestration are the last lines of treatment.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common long-term complication of idiopathic intracranial hypertension?

Reveal Answer:
Vision loss.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri)

Risk factors: female sex, elevated BMI, medications (e.g., tetracyclines, growth hormone, retinoids)
Sx: diffuse headache, visual blurring, peripheral vision loss
PE: bilateral papilledema, CN VI palsy
LP: elevated opening pressure
Initial Tx options include acetazolamide, weight loss
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ idiopathic intracranial hypertension ناتج عن زيادة نسبة الماء بالدماغ ونقص تصريف الـ CSF. المرضى عادة يجوا بصداع معمم يبدأ تدريجياً، وممكن يزداد مع حركات العين، وأي Valsalva maneuver بتقلل الرجوع الوريدي الدماغي فتزيد الصداع. كتير مرضى عندهم أعراض بصرية ونقص بصر عابر بسبب ischemia بالمسارات البصرية، والفحص بقاع العين بوضّح papilledema. التشخيص بُبني على نتائج الـ MRI أو ارتفاع ضغط الفتح بالـ lumbar puncture، والعلاج يركّز أولاً على تقليل إنتاج الـ CSF بالـ acetazolamide، وهو carbonic anhydrase inhibitor يُستخدم لحاله أو مع furosemide، مع التوصية بإنقاص الوزن.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون corticosteroids لأنها خيار شائع بالقوائم. لكن الـ corticosteroids تُستخدم بحالات نادرة جداً كإجراء مؤقت وليست علاج روتيني للـ idiopathic intracranial hypertension. أما الـ gabapentin فبس للصداع المستمر اللي ما يستجيب، والـ shunt يُلجأ له بحالات مختارة فقط.

question: A 36-year-old man presents to the emergency department for back pain beginning this morning. He also reports chills and radiation of pain into both legs. He reports significant tobacco use with a 20 pack-year smoking history and current intravenous heroin use. Vital signs show T of 103°F (39.4°C), HR of 94 bpm, RR of 18/min, BP of 126/74 mm Hg, and SpO2 of 97% on room air. Physical examination shows point tenderness over the L2 vertebrae with 3+ patellar and Achilles reflexes bilaterally. There are no appreciable sensory deficits in the lower extremities. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein are elevated. MRI with contrast shows a fluid-filled lesion in the posterior epidural space at the level of the L2 vertebrae with peripheral rim enhancement. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient’s condition?

options.text: Administration of intravenous dexamethasone and consultation to neurosurgery and radiation oncology
Administration of intravenous vancomycin and cefepime and immediate neurosurgery consultation
Neurology consultation and administration of intravenous methylprednisolone

correctAnswer: Administration of intravenous vancomycin and cefepime and immediate neurosurgery consultation
englishExplanation:
Spinal epidural abscess (SEA) is an infectious condition in which purulence accumulates in the dorsal epidural space. The incidence has been increasing in recent decades, which is thought to be due to the higher prevalence of prominent risk factors, such as spinal surgery, intravenous drug use, and immunosuppression. SEAs can arise via hematogenous spread or direct extension from adjacent infected tissue, with the former being the more common route. Urinary tract, skin and soft tissue, and respiratory infections are frequent precursor infections. In this patient’s case, his history of intravenous heroin use is his most prominent risk factor. However, SEA can occur in patients without any specific risk factors, so a high index of suspicion should be maintained for patients presenting with classic findings.

SEA characteristically presents with the triad of back pain, fever, and neurologic deficits, though most patients do not present with the entire triad. The location of back pain is variable, depending upon the particular location of the SEA, with the thoracic and lumbar spine most commonly affected. Patients with SEA often progress through a range of symptoms with initially mild neurologic findings consisting of radicular pain and hyperreflexia. Incontinence, frank motor weakness, or paralysis represent advanced stages of disease. MRI with contrast is the gold standard imaging modality for SEA, but CT myelography is a reasonable alternative when MRI is not available. Radiographic features of SEA on MRI include fluid-equivalent T2 signal intensity with peripheral rim enhancement and a hypointense central area. Elevations in erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein are nonspecific, but sensitive, findings that support the diagnosis. Blood cultures should also be sent.

Management of all cases of SEA should involve immediate neurosurgical evaluation for potential decompression, as there is a significant risk of cord compression and permanent neurologic deficits if not promptly treated. Some patients may be candidates for CT-guided aspiration of the abscess, but decompressive laminectomy is the definitive surgical treatment. Patients not being taken for immediate surgical management of SEA should be started on empiric antibiotic therapy consisting of vancomycin and an antipseudomonal beta-lactam such as cefepime or meropenem. Some patients, such as those with no neurologic deficits at the time of presentation or those with deficits for > 72 hours, may be appropriate for conservative management with antibiotics and close observation. Complications of SEA are severe and include sepsis, permanent neurologic deficits, and death. Cervical SEAs carry a particularly high degree of morbidity and mortality.



Intravenous corticosteroids, such as dexamethasone, and consultations to neurosurgery and radiation oncology (A) are appropriate steps in the management of spinal cord compression due to oncologic processes. This patient’s clinical and imaging findings are much more suspicious for an SEA, so antibiotics and neurosurgery evaluation are warranted. Advanced AIDS can be complicated by myelopathy presenting with some features that overlap with SEA, and this would be treated with antiretroviral therapy (C), but a history of known, untreated HIV or presentation with an AIDS-defining illness would be expected in such cases. Exacerbations of multiple sclerosis are commonly treated with a neurology evaluation and intravenous corticosteroids (D), but this patient has no historical features to suggest the diagnosis, and his current presentation is classic for SEA. Vertebroplasty (E) is a surgical procedure performed by orthopedic specialists for vertebral compression fractures but has no role in the treatment of SEAs.

One Step Further
Question:
What recreational activity is associated with atraumatic myelopathy that can mimic symptoms of transverse myelitis?

Reveal Answer:
Surfing. The atraumatic myelopathy is thought to result from transient spinal cord ischemia from prolonged prone positioning with arms extended and head held upright.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Spinal Epidural Abscess

Most commonly caused by S. aureus
Risks: diabetes, IV drug use, recent back surgery, immunodeficiency, endocarditis, bacteremia
Sx: back pain, fever, and neurological deficits
Dx: elevated ESR or CRP
MRI
Tx: IV antibiotics, spine surgery consultation for drainage
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ spinal epidural abscess حالة معدية يتجمع فيها القيح بالـ dorsal epidural space، وانتشارها زاد بالسنوات الأخيرة بسبب شيوع عوامل الخطر مثل جراحة العمود الفقري والـ IV drug use والـ immunosuppression. هالمريض مدخّن وبمستخدم heroine وريدياً، وعنده حرارة 103 وألم أسفل الظهر مع انتشار للأرجل وتناقص بالحس، والـ ESR والـ CRP مرتفعين، والـ MRI أظهر lesion بالـ posterior epidural space مع peripheral rim enhancement. القاعدة إنه يجب البدء بمضادات حيوية تجريبية فوراً مع تقييم جراحي عصبي عاجل، ولهذا الـ vancomycin وcefepime مع استشارة جراحة عصبية فورية هو التصرف الصحيح.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون neurology مع methylprednisolone لأنهم يفكروا بالتهاب عصبي مناعي. لكن الـ spinal epidural abscess عدوى بكتيرية تحتاج مضادات حيوية تغطي المسببات الشائعة مع تصريف جراحي عاجل، وتأخير ذلك ممكن يسبب شلل دائم. أما dexamethasone مع radiation oncology فبتخص الأورام النقيلية.

question: A 16-year-old girl with a history of depression is brought to the ED and actively seizing. She is accompanied by her parent, who is a health care worker and is undergoing treatment for latent tuberculosis. They are concerned that the patient may have taken the parent’s medication. The parent reports she has been seizing for approximately 10 minutes. She is afebrile. The patient is atraumatic with upward gaze deviation, has tonic-clonic contractions of all extremities, and has sonorous respirations. Which of the following is the most effective therapy?
englishExplanation:
This patient is presenting with convulsive status epilepticus, defined as continuous generalized tonic-clonic seizure activity lasting > 5 minutes or recurrent seizures without return to baseline mental status. In such cases, prompt recognition and treatment are critical. The lack of trauma and absence of a known history of epilepsy or recent febrile illness make a primary seizure disorder, intracranial hemorrhage, meningitis, or encephalitis less likely.

Given her history of depression and the parent’s concern about a possible ingestion, an intentional overdose should be considered. Isoniazid, commonly used for the treatment of latent tuberculosis infection, is a potential culprit. Isoniazid toxicity causes seizures by depleting pyridoxine (vitamin B6), which is essential for the synthesis of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain. This deficiency leads to GABA depletion and lowers the seizure threshold, potentially resulting in refractory seizures and status epilepticus.

While benzodiazepines remain the first-line treatment for seizures, their effectiveness may be reduced in the setting of isoniazid-induced GABA depletion. In such cases, the antidote is intravenous pyridoxine, which replenishes GABA synthesis and directly addresses the underlying pathophysiology. Pyridoxine has a wide safety margin, making it an appropriate empiric therapy in cases of undifferentiated status epilepticus when isoniazid toxicity is a concern.



Fosphenytoin (A) is generally not effective in the treatment of drug- or medication-induced seizures, including those related to isoniazid.

Levetiracetam (B) is a medication used in patients with seizure disorders, and it is a second-line agent in status epilepticus.

Phenobarbital (C) is a barbiturate that may temporarily terminate seizures in this patient, but it will not ultimately resolve this patient’s underlying pyridoxine deficiency. Although it may be used as an adjunct or alternative medication in status epilepticus, it often results in profound sedation requiring endotracheal intubation.

One Step Further
Question:
Which lab test should be performed immediately in seizing patients?

Reveal Answer:
Point-of-care glucose.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Isoniazid (INH) Toxicity

At therapeutic doses, side effects include neuropathy and liver injury
AST or ALT > 3x upper limit of normal: consider discontinuing or temporarily holding INH
In overdose, ↓ B6 (pyridoxine) → ↓ GABA → refractory seizures with anion gap metabolic acidosis and protracted coma
Antidote: B6 (pyridoxine)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هالمريضة بمرحلة convulsive status epilepticus، ويُعرَّف كاستمرار نوبة tonic-clonic معممة أكثر من 5 دقائق أو تكرار النوبات بدون رجوع للوعي الطبيعي. غياب الرضّ والحرارة وتاريخ الصرع يقللوا احتمال الـ primary seizure disorder أو الـ intracranial hemorrhage أو الالتهاب السحائي. وجود تاريخ اكتئاب وقلق الأهل من تناول دواء أحد الوالدين يوجّه بقوة نحو ingestion متعمّد، و isoniazid المستخدم للـ latent tuberculosis هو الجاني المحتمل، لأن سُميته تتلف pyridoxine (فيتامين B6) المهم لتصنيع الـ GABA، فينخفض الـ GABA ويهبط عتبة النوبات. والـ antidote هو الـ intravenous pyridoxine.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون levetiracetam أو fosphenytoin لأنهما من مضادات الاختلاج المعتادة. لكن بالـ isoniazid toxicity فاعلية الـ benzodiazepines تقل بسبب نقص الـ GABA، والعلاج النوعي هو الـ pyridoxine اللي يعوّض ويرجع تصنيع الـ GABA، وله هامش أمان واسع فيُعطى تجريبياً.

question: Which of the following is suggestive of dementia rather than delirium?

options.text: Sudden onset and offset of symptoms
Symptoms associated with disturbance in the sleep-wake cycle

englishExplanation:
Dementia presents with gradual-onset memory loss. Early in the disease course, patients may present with minor forgetfulness that can be confused with normal memory loss of aging. As it progresses, patients will forget names and addresses and lose the ability to perform acts of daily living. Dementia is a gradual-onset process that slowly worsens over months to years. As the condition progresses, patients may struggle to find words and communicate. In contrast, delirium is a sudden-onset process. Patients with dementia are more prone to delirium, as are patients with advanced age. Infection, change in environment, loss of a hearing aid, dehydration, or any physiological disturbance can cause delirium. Delirium has a rapidly fluctuating course, and patients may be suddenly agitated and confused with possible delusions and hallucinations. Symptoms are more common at night and when the sleep-wake cycle is disturbed. Management is centered on treating any underlying medical cause. Regular sleep and a healthy diet are also protective. A familiar environment and family can also reduce delirium.



Sudden onset and offset of symptoms (B), symptoms associated with disturbance in the sleep-wake cycle (C), and symptoms associated with infection (D) would all be more suggestive of delirium rather than dementia.

One Step Further
Question:
What nutritional deficiency can cause confusion, ataxia, nystagmus, and ophthalmoplegia?

Reveal Answer:
Thiamine deficiency.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Dementia

Gradual loss of mental capacity
Preserved attention, motor function, speech
Irreversible causes: Alzheimer, vascular dementia, Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
Reversible causes: depression, B12 deficiency, syphilis, hypothyroidism, NPH, drug use, intracranial mass
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ dementia تبدأ تدريجياً مع فقدان ذاكرة بطيء، وبداية المرض ممكن تكون نسيان بسيط يتلخبط مع النسيان الطبيعي للعمر، ومع التقدم المريض ينسى الأسماء والعناوين ويفقد القدرة على القيام بأنشطة الحياة اليومية. الـ dementia عملية تدريجية تسوء على مدى أشهر إلى سنوات، ومع التقدم ممكن يواجه المريض صعوبة بإيجاد الكلمات والتواصل. أما الـ delirium فهو عملية مفاجئة البداية، ولهذا فإن gradual onset والأعراض اللي تسوء ببطء هي اللي تفرّق الـ dementia عن الـ delirium.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون sudden onset and offset لأنهم يحسبوا الاختلاف بالشدة فقط. لكن الـ sudden onset and offset والأعراض المرتبطة باختلال دورة النوم واليقظة والأعراض مع العدوى كلها توجّه للـ delirium وليس للـ dementia. المفتاح هو إن الـ dementia بدايتها gradual وتسوء ببطء.

question: A 61-year-old man presents to the ED with intermittent shock-like spasms of pain in his right cheek. The pain only lasts a few seconds at a time but recurs frequently. He notes that shaving each morning causes intense spasms of pain, as does chewing. What is the first-line treatment for his likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Trigeminal neuralgia is a chronic pain condition characterized by sudden, severe, unilateral, electric shock-like paroxysms of pain in the distribution of one or more branches of the trigeminal nerve, most commonly the maxillary (V2) and mandibular (V3) divisions. Episodes are brief, typically lasting seconds to minutes, and can occur spontaneously or be triggered by everyday activities such as chewing, brushing teeth, speaking, shaving, or exposure to wind or temperature changes. Pain is often described as stabbing or burning and may occur in clusters, with symptom-free intervals in between.

The condition is usually caused by vascular compression at the root entry zone of the trigeminal nerve, often by an aberrant loop of the superior cerebellar artery. This compression leads to demyelination and hyperexcitability of the nerve fibers. Less commonly, trigeminal neuralgia may result from multiple sclerosis, tumors, or brain stem infarcts, especially in patients < 65 years old or those with bilateral symptoms. Women are affected more frequently than men, and it typically presents after age 50.

Diagnosis is primarily clinical, based on a detailed patient history and characteristic features of the pain. A thorough evaluation is essential to exclude other causes of facial pain, such as dental infections, temporomandibular joint disorders, sinusitis, or postherpetic neuralgia. Neuroimaging, typically with MRI, is often performed to assess for secondary causes like tumors or multiple sclerosis plaques and to evaluate for vascular compression of the nerve root.

First-line pharmacologic treatment is carbamazepine, which is initiated at 100 mg twice daily and titrated as needed for symptom control, typically up to 1,200 mg/day. Oxcarbazepine is an alternative with a similar mechanism of action and fewer side effects. Patients on carbamazepine require periodic monitoring of complete blood counts and liver function tests due to the risk of hematologic toxicity and hepatotoxicity. If medication is ineffective or poorly tolerated, second-line options include other anticonvulsants (e.g., gabapentin, lamotrigine).

Overall, early recognition and effective treatment of trigeminal neuralgia are important to reduce the impact of this debilitating pain disorder on quality of life. Treatment plans should be individualized, with a focus on symptom control and minimizing adverse effects.



Baclofen (A) has been used in the treatment of trigeminal neuralgia, although there is limited evidence of its efficacy.

Botulinum injections (B) may be useful in patients with pain that is refractory to medical options.

Diazepam (D) is not used in the management of trigeminal neuralgia.

One Step Further
Question:
Does surgery play a role in the management of trigeminal neuralgia?

Reveal Answer:
Surgical options, including microvascular decompression and ablative procedures, may be considered if the condition is refractory to medical therapies.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Trigeminal Neuralgia (Tic Douloureux)

Sx: sudden unilateral electric shock-like pains in gums, cheek, chin, temporal forehead
PE: pain in V2 and V3 distributions, less commonly in V1
Tx: carbamazepine
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ trigeminal neuralgia حالة ألم مزمن تتميّز بنوبات وجع قصيرة وحادة كالصعقة الكهربائية، وحيدة الجانب، بتوزيع فروع الـ trigeminal nerve، وأكثرها الـ maxillary (V2) والـ mandibular (V3). النوبات قصيرة من ثوانٍ لدقائق وممكن تيجي تلقائياً أو تُحفَّز بأنشطة يومية مثل المضغ أو فرش الأسنان أو الحلاقة أو الكلام أو التعرض للهواء وتغير الحرارة. السبب عادة ضغط وعائي على منطقة دخول الجذر للـ trigeminal nerve، وغالباً عروة شاذة من الـ superior cerebellar artery. التشخيص سريري، والعلاج الأول هو الـ carbamazepine.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون baclofen أو botulinum injections أو diazepam لأنها تُستخدم كمان بالألم العصبي والتشنجات. لكن هالأدوية مو خط أول للـ trigeminal neuralgia، والـ carbamazepine هو العلاج الأول المثبت، والـ baclofen ممكن يُستخدم كمُكمّل بحالات مختارة فقط.

question: A 17-year-old girl with a history of migraines presents to the emergency department with a severe headache. She reports the pain is her typical migraine pain consisting of unilateral severe head pain with photophobia and flashes of light. Her trial of acetaminophen and sumatriptan at home has not resulted in any relief. Her physical exam is normal. Which of the following is the most effective next step in the management of her headache?
englishExplanation:
A migraine is a severe disabling recurrent headache often accompanied by photophobia, phonophobia, and vomiting. No genetic markers have yet been identified as the cause of migraines despite that such headaches frequently run in families. The once well-known theory of a vascular origin of migraines has been shown to be incorrect. The current leading theory is one of primary neuronal dysfunction but is yet to be proven. Treatment includes identifying triggers with a headache calendar, sleep, and a trial of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs which are often effective for mild symptoms. In the emergency department, one of the most effective solutions includes an intravenous normal saline bolus given with intravenous prochlorperazine and ketorolac.



Dexamethasone (A) and other corticosteroids have not been shown to be effective in the treatment of acute migraines in children in the emergency department setting.

Meperidine (B) and other opiates should be avoided in the treatment of headaches as they are less effective and have a strong potential to promote chronic migraines.

While sodium valproate (D) has historically been used in the treatment of migraines, there is limited evidence for its use in children.

One Step Further
Question:
Why is diphenhydramine often given with prochlorperazine for the treatment of migraines?

Reveal Answer:
Diphenhydramine is thought to prevent dystonic reactions associated with prochlorperazine.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Migraine Headache

Risks: female sex, family history
Sx: gradual onset, throbbing, pulsating headache
Adults: unilateral > bilateral
Children: bilateral > unilateral
Without aura: most common, nausea or vomiting, photophobia, phonophobia
Aura: scotoma, flashing lights, sounds
Dx: clinically
Tx:
Avoid triggers, adequate sleep and exercise, CBT
Abortive Rx: triptans, DHE, valproic acid, antiemetics, NSAIDs
Triptans, DHE: avoid in those with uncontrolled HTN or CV disease
Prophylaxis: TCAs, beta-blockers, anticonvulsants (valproic acid, topiramate), CCBs
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ migraine صداع شديد ونكسي متكرر يترافق غالباً مع photophobia وphonophobia وتقيؤ. ما في علامات جينية محددة معروفة كسبب، رغم إن الصداع النصفي منتشر بالعائلات، والنظرية القديمة عن منشأ وعائي ثبت إنها غير صحيحة، والنظرية الحالية هي خلل عصبي أولي. بالطوارئ أحد أكثر الحلول فاعلية هو إعطاء bolus من الـ normal saline وريدياً مع الـ prochlorperazine وريدياً مع ketorolac. والـ prochlorperazine يُعد من أفضل الخيارات لهالمريضة اللي ما استفادت من acetaminophen وsumatriptan بالبيت.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون meperidine أو أي opiate لتسكين الألم. لكن الـ opiates يجب تجنبها بعلاج الصداع لأنها أقل فاعلية وعندها قدرة قوية على دفع المريض نحو الـ chronic migraine. أما الـ dexamethasone فما ثبتت فاعليتها بالصداع النصفي الحاد، والـ sodium valproate دليلها محدود عند الأطفال.

question: A 48-year-old man with a history of hypertension and nonadherence to his medications presents with a severe headache that began 8 hours before arrival. His neurologic exam is nonfocal. CT scan is shown above. His pain is resolved after intravenous fluids and parenteral medications. Vital signs include a BP of 195/96 mm Hg, HR of 92 bpm, RR of 16/minute, and T of 98.6°F (37°C). Which of the following is the best next step in patient care?

options.text: Check an ECG, urinalysis, and basic metabolic panel

englishExplanation:
Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage is an important cause of headache with a 30-day mortality of almost 50% and potentially devastating complications. It is usually caused by a ruptured berry aneurysm, which is a focal arterial pouch in areas of bifurcation on the circle of Willis. Diagnosis within the first 6–12 hours can often be made by a noncontrast CT scan, which shows hyperdense material filling the subarachnoid space.

Blood pressure should be lowered immediately. Systolic blood pressure < 160 mm Hg is a reasonable initial target according to a national guideline. Definitive therapy involves urgent endovascular coil embolization or surgical clipping of the aneurysm to prevent rebleeding. If the patient has acute hydrocephalus with increased intracranial pressure, they may also require urgent ventriculostomy.

Even if symptoms resolve, patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage should be treated in the ICU due to the risk of complications, such as delayed vasospasm with ischemia. Other serious potential complications include seizures, hyponatremia, stress cardiomyopathy, dysrhythmias, and other organ dysfunction. Oral nimodipine is proven to improve neurologic outcomes if started within 4 days of symptom onset and continued for 21 days.



Checking an ECG, urinalysis, and basic metabolic panel (A) is sometimes done to screen for complications of poorly controlled hypertension. Obtaining a baseline creatinine prior to an angiogram is also reasonable. However, addressing the blood pressure is more important in the initial treatment of this patient with subarachnoid hemorrhage.

Discharging with close follow-up (B) would not be appropriate for this patient, even if asymptomatic, as he still needs evaluation for a possible ruptured aneurysm.

While lumbar puncture (D) could be performed in a patient highly suspected of having a subarachnoid hemorrhage after a negative head CT, this patient’s imaging shows a hemorrhage and requires further intervention.

One Step Further
Question:
Should patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage receive seizure prophylaxis?

Reveal Answer:
Not usually, unless hemorrhage is extensive with cortical involvement. Specifically, prophylaxis with phenytoin has been shown to cause worse outcomes.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage

Most commonly caused by a ruptured aneurysm
Sx: abrupt onset of the worst headache of their life or thunderclap headache
Dx: noncontrast CT scan, blood will appear white on CT
If CT unremarkable and performed within 6 hours of symptom onset, subarachnoid hemorrhage effectively ruled out
If CT unremarkable and suspicion high, lumbar puncture or CTA
Hunt and Hess scale classifies severity of subarachnoid hemorrhage to predict mortality
Treatment is supportive (blood pressure control with IV agents), euvolemia, and nimodipine (prevents vasospasm and other neurologic complications)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage سبب مهم للصداع ومعه وفيات خلال 30 يوم تقارب الخمسين بالمئة ومضاعفات مدمرة، وغالباً بسبب رشح berry aneurysm على الـ circle of Willis. التشخيص خلال أول 6 إلى 12 ساعة ممكن بالـ noncontrast CT اللي يوضّح مادة عالية الكثافة تملأ الـ subarachnoid space. القاعدة إنه يُخفَّض ضغط الدم فوراً، والمستهدف الأولي المعقول هو أقل من 160 mm Hg للـ systolic حسب الدليل الوطني. العلاج القاطع هو coil embolization أو clipping جراحي عاجل للـ aneurysm لمنع إعادة النزف، والمريض يبقى بالـ ICU حتى لو رجعت أعراضه.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون prepare for lumbar puncture لأنهم شافوا صداع شديد وCT، أو يختاروا الإخراج مع متابعة لأنه ما بيّن عليه شي. لكن بعد تشخيص الـ SAH بالـ CT المهم هو التحكم بالضغط فوراً لمنع إعادة النزف، والـ ICU ضرورية للمراقبة من vasospasm المتأخر.

question: A 72-year-old woman with a history of hypertension, diabetes, and atrial fibrillation on warfarin presents to a rural emergency department at 11:00 AM with a left-sided facial droop and left upper extremity weakness. She reports the symptoms began at 7:00 AM while making her coffee. Her National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale is calculated to be 10. Blood work is performed and significant for an INR of 2.5. A CT scan is performed and shown above. Which of the following is the best next step?

options.text: Administer tPA then transfer to a stroke center
Initiate aspirin and high-dose statin therapy
Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain
Transfer to a stroke center for possible mechanical thrombectomy

correctAnswer: Transfer to a stroke center for possible mechanical thrombectomy
englishExplanation:
This patient’s symptoms and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) are concerning for an acute cerebrovascular accident (CVA). Her CT scan shows focal hyperdensity of the middle cerebral artery (MCA), known as the dense MCA sign, an early indication of MCA ischemic occlusion. While her presentation puts her in the appropriate time window for tPA administration (0–4.5 hours), her daily warfarin use and INR ≥ 1.7 is an absolute contraindication for tPA administration. Patients with evidence of large artery occlusion, such as an internal carotid artery or MCA occlusion, who have absolute contraindications to tPA or are ineligible for tPA due to the time of symptom onset, are candidates for mechanical thrombectomy up to 24 hours from the time they were last seen well. Additional criteria depending on the time from onset include functional independence at baseline, and the area of ischemia should be < one-third the MCA territory. These patients should be transferred to a stroke center for a CT angiogram or MR angiogram to quantify the occlusion further and be evaluated for mechanical thrombectomy.



Patients presenting with an acute stroke within 4.5 hours of symptom onset who do not have any contraindications should receive tPA. Administering tPA and then transferring to a stroke center (A) is incorrect in this case as the patient has an absolute contraindication to tPA administration. Absolute contraindications include neurosurgery, head trauma, or stroke in the last 3 months; uncontrolled hypertension (> 185 mm Hg systolic BP or > 110 mm Hg diastolic BP); history of intracranial hemorrhage; known intracranial arteriovenous malformation, neoplasm, or aneurysm; active internal bleeding; suspected or confirmed endocarditis; blood glucose < 50 mg/dL; and known bleeding diathesis (platelet count < 100,000, heparin administration within last 48 hours and elevated aPTT, current use of oral anticoagulant with an INR ≥ 1.7, or current use of direct thrombin inhibitors or direct factor Xa inhibitors). Initiating aspirin and high-dose statin therapy (B) is incorrect. While these agents play a well-documented role in reducing the risk of recurrent CVAs, they are not indicated in the acute treatment phase. Inconclusive CT imaging (including CT angiogram) may be followed up with magnetic resonance imaging of the brain (C). This patient has a dense MCA sign on her CT imaging, highly specific for MCA occlusion.

One Step Further
Question:
Which patients treated with mechanical thrombectomy for an acute CVA have the best functional outcome?

Reveal Answer:
Those treated within 6 hours of symptom onset.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Ischemic Stroke

Anterior cerebral artery: frontal lobe dysfunction, apraxia, contralateral paralysis (lower > upper)
Middle cerebral artery: contralateral paralysis (upper > lower), aphasia
Posterior cerebral and vertebrobasilar arteries: LOC, nausea or vomiting, CN dysfunction, ataxia, visual agnosia
Dx: CT might reveal loss of gray-white interface, acute hypodensity
Rule out hypoglycemia
CTA to evaluate for large-vessel occlusion
NIHSS to evaluate severity of stroke
Acute Tx: thrombolytics within 4.5 hours, possible thrombectomy within 24 hours
DAWN or Defuse3 can help risk-stratify for mechanical thrombectomy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الأعراض ودرجة الـ NIHSS عند هالمريضة مقلقة لـ acute cerebrovascular accident، والـ CT أظهر focal hyperdensity بالـ middle cerebral artery، وهي علامة الـ dense MCA sign اللي تعتبر إشارة مبكرة لانسداد الـ MCA. رغم إنها بنافذة الـ tPA الزمنية من صفر إلى 4.5 ساعة، إلا إن استخدامها اليومي للـ warfarin مع INR 2.5 يعتبر مانع مطلق لإعطاء الـ tPA. المرضى اللي عندهم دليل على انسداد شريان كبير ومعهم مانع مطلق للـ tPA أو خارج نافذته يصيروا مرشحين للـ mechanical thrombectomy حتى 24 ساعة من آخر وقت كانوا فيه بخير، فالتصرف الصحيح هو تحويلها لمركز سكتات.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون administer tPA then transfer لأنهم بس يشوفوا النافذة الزمنية. لكن الـ warfarin مع INR عالي يعتبر مانع مطلق للـ tPA بسبب خطر النزف الدماغي، والبديل المناسب هو التحويل السريع لمركز سكتات لتقييم الـ thrombectomy.

question: A 40-year-old man presents to the emergency department with his spouse for a headache that began after sexual intercourse 3 hours ago. The pain is diffuse, severe, and pressure-like in nature. He has no focal neurologic deficits or meningismus on physical examination. The CT scan of his head is normal. Due to continued high clinical suspicion, a lumbar puncture is performed, and it does not show xanthochromia or measurable RBCs in the sample fluid. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in care?
englishExplanation:
Acetaminophen is an appropriate therapy for patients with acute headache. This patient likely has a postcoital headache, which could be a common inciting event for subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Therefore, an appropriate workup should be completed to rule out emergent and life-threatening causes of the headache. However, in the absence of focal neurologic findings, normal initial head CT imaging, and normal cerebrospinal fluid studies, SAH can reliably be ruled out. At this time, the best next step is pain control.



CT angiography (B) is an imaging modality that may be appropriate to identify cerebral aneurysms in lieu of performing a lumbar puncture, but its utility, in this case, is low given a negative noncontrast head CT, which has a high sensitivity for detecting SAH (~ 100% if performed within 6 hours of symptom onset), in addition to normal appearing cerebrospinal fluid analysis.

Intravenous thrombolysis (C) is indicated only for acute ischemic strokes in a very select patient population. Patients must have measurable neurologic deficits, which are absent in this case.

Neurosurgical consultation (D) is not indicated in the absence of surgical pathology.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the cutoff number of RBCs in CSF to reliably exclude subarachnoid hemorrhage?

Reveal Answer:
Currently, there is no consensus on a precise threshold number.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage

Most commonly caused by a ruptured aneurysm
Sx: abrupt onset of the worst headache of their life or thunderclap headache
Dx: noncontrast CT scan, blood will appear white on CT
If CT unremarkable and performed within 6 hours of symptom onset, subarachnoid hemorrhage effectively ruled out
If CT unremarkable and suspicion high, lumbar puncture or CTA
Hunt and Hess scale classifies severity of subarachnoid hemorrhage to predict mortality
Treatment is supportive (blood pressure control with IV agents), euvolemia, and nimodipine (prevents vasospasm and other neurologic complications)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: هذا المريض عنده صداع بعد الجماع، وهاد ممكن يكون من الأحداث اللي بتسبق الـ subarachnoid hemorrhage، فيجب إكمال تقييم مناسب لاستبعاد الأسباب الطارئة والمهددة للحياة. الـ acetaminophen علاج مناسب للألم الحاد. وهنا بعد غياب أي علامات عصبية بؤرية، مع CT دماغ طبيعي بدايته، ونتائج الـ CSF طبيعية بدون xanthochromia وبدون كريات حمراء قابلة للقياس، يصير بالإمكان استبعاد الـ SAH بثقة. لذلك الخطوة الأفضل حالياً هي السيطرة على الألم.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون CT angiography لأن الـ SAH شغلة خطيرة وبدهم يتأكدوا أكثر. لكن فائدتها هنا منخفضة جداً بعد CT غير ظليل حساسيته عالية جداً خلال أول 6 ساعات وتحليل CSF الطبيعي، والـ thrombolysis بتحتاج عجز عصبي قابل للقياس وهو غائب، والاستشارة الجراحية بلا سبب جراحي.

question: A 27-year-old woman presents with a concern about transient vision loss in her right eye. She states that she has had multiple similar episodes in the past 6 months. She also reports incomplete bladder emptying, intermittent tremors, and intermittent weakness in her left arm. Which of the following is the best diagnostic test for the suspected diagnosis?

options.text: CSF testing for myelin basic protein
CT scan of the brain and spine
MRI of the brain and spine

correctAnswer: MRI of the brain and spine
englishExplanation:
MRI of the brain and spine is the diagnostic modality of choice for multiple sclerosis (MS), a disease characterized by demyelination of axons within the CNS. Patients present with symptoms that are scattered in time and space, meaning that they have intermittent symptoms in anatomically disparate locations. Patients may have patchy motor and sensory deficits and bladder dysfunction. Optic neuritis is a common initial presentation. Spinal cord lesions typically involve the posterior columns, lateral spinothalamic tracts, and corticospinal tract. Brain and spinal MRI is the diagnostic modality of choice because it can be used to rule out causes of cord compression while also showing lesions diagnostic for MS.



CSF testing for myelin basic protein (A) can be used in an MS diagnosis but is of questionable accuracy, and no CSF test is entirely specific.

CT scan of the brain and spine (B) does not aid in diagnosis. MRI has a better sensitivity and specificity for detecting MS lesions.

CSF oligoclonal bands, not serum (D), are also helpful. Oligoclonal bands are found in the CSF of most patients with MS.

Evoked potentials (E) are infrequently used in the diagnosis of MS. Somatosensory evoked potentials assess the electrical conduction of sensory pathways in the CNS coming from the limbs to the brain.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the first-line treatment of multiple sclerosis exacerbations?

Reveal Answer:
High-dose IV steroids (e.g., methylprednisolone).

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Multiple Sclerosis

Demyelinating CNS lesions separated in space and time
Risk factors: female sex, aged < 50 years, birth at northern latitude (possibly linked to vitamin D deficiency)
Sx: pain with eye movement, monocular vision loss, diplopia with lateral gaze, sensory abnormalities
PE: afferent pupillary defect (Marcus Gunn pupil), spinal electric shock sensation with neck flexion (Lhermitte sign), impaired ocular adduction (bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia)
Dx
MRI: periventricular white matter lesions
CSF: oligoclonal IgG bands, WBC pleocytosis
Tx options (depending on factors such as disease subtype, severity, patient preference)
Acute exacerbation: corticosteroids (e.g., methylprednisolone)
Disease-modifying agents (e.g., natalizumab, ocrelizumab, glatiramer acetate†, interferon beta-1a†)
Note: natalizumab associated with PML, test for JC virus antibodies
† May be used during pregnancy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ MRI للدماغ والعمود الفقري هو الفحص التشخيصي المختار للـ multiple sclerosis، وهي مرض يتميّز بـ demyelination للمحاور داخل الـ CNS. المرضى يشتكوا من أعراض متفرقة بالزمن والمكان، يعني أعراض متقطعة بمواقع تشريحية مختلفة، وممكن يكون في نقص حركي وحسي متقطع وخلل بالمثانة. الـ optic neuritis من أشهر طرق الظهور الأولى، والآفات بالـ spinal cord غالباً تصيب الـ posterior columns والـ lateral spinothalamic tracts والـ corticospinal tract. الـ MRI للدماغ والعمود الفقري هو الخيار لأنه يستبعد أسباب ضغط النخاع وبنفس الوقت يبيّن الآفات المميزة للـ MS.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون CSF testing for myelin basic protein أو serum oligoclonal bands لأنهم سامعين عن الـ bands بالـ MS. لكن دقة تحليل الـ myelin basic protein مشكوك فيها، وما في فحص CSF نوعي تماماً، والـ oligoclonal bands المفيدة هي بالـ CSF وليست بالمصل، والـ CT أقل حساسية بكثير من الـ MRI لكشف آفات الـ MS.

question: What is the most likely cause of a patient presenting with bilateral facial nerve palsy?
englishExplanation:
Bell palsy is a paralysis of the peripheral seventh cranial nerve. Clinically, one is able to distinguish a peripheral from a central cause of facial motor weakness by involvement of the forehead in a peripheral palsy. The forehead receives bilateral innervation centrally and a stroke syndrome will not interfere with upper facial strength because of the contralateral innervation. In Bell palsy, the seventh nerve is affected after leaving the brainstem and weakness is seen on the entire side of the face. Bilateral Bell palsy occurs simultaneously very rarely. Borrelia burgdorferi is the causative organism of Lyme disease and Lyme is one of the few causes of bilateral Bell palsy. Other causes include Guillan-Barre syndrome, sarcoidosis, meningitis, or bilateral neurofibromas.





The list of possible causes of Bell palsy is quite extensive and includes infectious etiologies, structural abnormalities, trauma, and toxic etiologies. Herpes simplex virus (B), leukemia (C), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (D) are all possible causes of acute Bell palsy but Lyme disease is most likely to cause bilateral symptoms.

One Step Further
Question:
What syndrome causes a vesicular rash in or around the ear canal, facial paralysis, and hearing loss?

Reveal Answer:
Ramsay Hunt syndrome caused by herpes zoster.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Lyme Disease

Most commonly caused by Borrelia burgdorferi carried by Ixodes tick
History of being in the woods, hiking, or camping
Sx
Stage 1: erythema migrans (pathognomonic), viral-like syndrome (fever, fatigue, malaise, myalgia, headache)
Stage 2: myocarditis, bilateral facial nerve palsy (pathognomonic for Lyme disease)
Stage 3: chronic arthritis, chronic encephalopathy
PE: slightly raised red lesion with central clearing, erythema migrans (bull’s-eye) rash
Tx: doxycycline
Children: amoxicillin or doxycycline (if used for < 21 days)
Pregnant: amoxicillin
In severe disease (severe meningitis, encephalitis, carditis): ceftriaxone
Prevention after tick bite: doxycycline in a single dose if the following are true
Tick is identified as Ixodes
Tick is attached for ≥ 36 hours based on engorgement
Prophylaxis begins within 72 hours of tick removal
Doxycycline is not contraindicated
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ Bell palsy هو شلل في الـ peripheral seventh cranial nerve، ونفرّق سريرياً بين السبب المحيطي والمركزي بمشاركة الجبهة. الجبهة تأخذ تعصيب ثنائي مركزياً، فمتلازمة السكتة الدماغية عادة ما تأثر على قوة الوجه العلوي بسبب التعصيب المقابل، أما بالـ Bell palsy فيكون الضعف بكامل جانب الوجه. الـ bilateral Bell palsy نادر جداً بحصوله بنفس الوقت، والـ Borrelia burgdorferi اللي يسبب Lyme disease من الأسباب القليلة للـ bilateral Bell palsy، مع أسباب أخرى مثل Guillain-Barre syndrome والساركويد والالتهاب السحائي والـ bilateral neurofibromas.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون herpes simplex virus لأنه أشهر سبب للـ Bell palsy. لكن الـ HSV والـ leukemia والـ Mycoplasma pneumoniae كلها ممكن تسبب Bell palsy أحادي الجانب، بينما الـ Lyme disease هو الأكثر ترجيحاً لإحداث الشلل الوجهي الثنائي.

question: Which of the following is the most common cause of status epilepticus in a patient with known epilepsy?
englishExplanation:
The most common cause of status epilepticus in a patient with known epilepsy is discontinued medication. In patients with an established seizure disorder, abrupt withdrawal of antiseizure medications or subtherapeutic drug levels is the leading precipitating factor for breakthrough seizures and progression to status epilepticus.

Nonadherence may occur due to missed doses, inability to obtain medications, adverse effects, or intentional discontinuation. Loss of steady-state antiseizure medication levels lowers the seizure threshold and can result in prolonged or recurrent seizures without recovery of baseline mental status.

In contrast, in patients without a prior seizure history, acute structural, metabolic, or infectious etiologies are more frequently implicated.



Hypoglycemia (A) is a well-recognized cause of acute symptomatic seizures and can precipitate status epilepticus in patients with and without a prior seizure disorder. However, in patients with known epilepsy, it is not the most common cause of status epilepticus. Hypoglycemia is more frequently seen in patients with diabetes mellitus who use insulin or oral hypoglycemic agents or in those with critical illness, alcohol use disorder, or sepsis. While glucose should always be checked in any patient with seizures because it is a reversible and life-threatening cause, it is less common than discontinuing the medication in patients with established epilepsy.

Meningitis (C) can cause seizures due to cortical irritation from infection and inflammation, and it may lead to status epilepticus in severe cases. However, meningitis is more commonly a cause of new-onset seizures in patients without a prior seizure history rather than the most common cause of status epilepticus in patients with known epilepsy. Patients with meningitis present with additional findings such as fever, neck stiffness, altered mental status, or photophobia. In contrast, patients with known epilepsy who develop status epilepticus most often have a precipitating factor related to medication nonadherence or subtherapeutic drug levels rather than a new central nervous system infection.

Trauma (D) can precipitate seizures due to structural injury, intracranial hemorrhage, or cortical irritation. Acute trauma is a recognized cause of new-onset seizures and may lead to status epilepticus, particularly in patients with severe head injury. However, in patients with known epilepsy, trauma is not the leading cause of status epilepticus unless there is a clear history of recent head injury. In the absence of such a history, breakthrough seizures due to discontinued medication are much more common.

One Step Further
Question:
What is Todd paralysis?

Reveal Answer:
Transient focal neurologic weakness that occurs after a seizure and typically resolves within minutes to hours, though it may persist up to 36 hours or occasionally longer.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Status Epilepticus

PE will show ≥ 5 minutes of continuous seizure activity or more than one seizure without recovery from the postictal state between episodes
Most commonly caused by a change in the medication regimen of someone with a seizure disorder
Check fingerstick for hypoglycemia
Treatment
First-line: benzodiazepines (e.g., lorazepam)
Second-line: levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, valproate
Third-line: pentobarbital, propofol
arabicExplanation:
ليش: السبب الأكثر شيوعاً للـ status epilepticus عند مريض عنده صرع معروف هو إيقاف الدواء. بالمريض اللي عنده اضطراب نوبات مثبت، السحب المفاجئ لمضادات الاختلاج أو وجود مستويات دوائية تحت العلاجية هو العامل المُرجِّح الأساسي لنوبات الاختراق والتقدم للـ status epilepticus. عدم الالتزام ممكن يصير بسبب جرعات فائتة أو عدم القدرة على تأمين الدواء أو الأعراض الجانبية أو الإيقاف المتعمد. فقدان المستويات الثابتة للدواء بيخفض عتبة النوبات ويسبب نوبات مطوّلة أو متكررة بدون رجوع للوعي الطبيعي، والـ hypoglycemia رغم خطورتها ليست السبب الأكثر شيوعاً بهالمجموعة.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون hypoglycemia لأنهم اتعلموا إن السكر لازم يُفحَص بأي مريض عنده نوبة وهو سبب قابل للعلاج ومهدد للحياة. لكن الـ hypoglycemia أشيع عند مرضى السكري اللي بيستخدموا الإنسولين أو أدوية السكر الفموية، أو بحالات الخطورة والإنتان، وليست السبب الأول للـ status epilepticus عند مريض الصرع المعروف.

question: What is the most common tumor of the cerebellopontine angle?
englishExplanation:
The posterior cranial fossa, containing the cerebellum, pons, and medulla oblongata, with the foramen magnum at the center of the space, has the potential to house a multitude of benign and malignant neoplasms due to the diversity of structures with varying anatomic makeups within the region. Presenting signs and symptoms depend upon the etiology and location of the developing lesion, with the cerebellopontine angle as the most common site of tumors in the posterior fossa. The vast majority of tumors at this site are benign with approximately 90% of lesions at this location being vestibular schwannomas or acoustic neuromas.

Regardless of etiology, the most common presenting symptom of all cerebellopontine angle tumors is hearing loss, seen in over 95% of cases. Vestibular schwannomas similarly present in this manner with patients reporting gradual loss of hearing and tinnitus over a period of years due to cochlear nerve involvement. Additional symptoms may arise depending on further nerve involvement, including gait instability and vertigo associated with vestibular nerve disturbances, as well as facial numbness and pain resulting from trigeminal nerve disruption. If there is clinical suspicion based upon sensorineural hearing loss with or without concomitant cranial nerve abnormalities, MRI with gadolinium is the diagnostic study of choice with 1–2 mm sections through the internal auditory meatus, which will optimally visualize the region and determine the degree of cerebellopontine angle involvement.



An ependymoma (A) is a tumor arising from the neuroepithelial lining of the ventricular system of the brain and spinal cord. The majority of cases occur in the pediatric population, with half of these lesions seen in children < 3 years. They are most commonly seen in the fourth ventricle, where obstruction of the flow of cerebrospinal fluid may produce hydrocephalus.

Glioblastoma (B) is an aggressive malignant brain tumor that is most commonly located in the frontal and temporal lobes and may present with progressively worsening headaches, vomiting, neurologic deficits, and stark personality changes.

Of the malignant lesions that develop in the posterior fossa, medulloblastomas (C) are the most common primary brain malignancy in children, arising from the medullary velum and typically extending into the fourth ventricle, with symptoms developing due to worsening obstructive hydrocephalus.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the most common tumor of the central nervous system?

Reveal Answer:
Meningioma.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Brain Tumors

Etiologies: primary brain tumors, metastatic disease
Primary brain tumors classified according to the cell type of origin
Sx and findings: headache, focal neurologic deficits (depending on tumor location), seizures, cognitive dysfunction, nausea
Tx options (depending on tumor type): surgery, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, radiation therapy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ posterior cranial fossa يحتوي على الـ cerebellum والـ pons والـ medulla oblongata، وبيحتوي على أورام حميدة وخبيثة كثيرة بسبب تنوع البنى فيه، والـ cerebellopontine angle هو الموقع الأكثر شيوعاً للأورام بالـ posterior fossa. الغالبية العظمى من الأورام بهذا الموقع حميدة، وحوالي 90% منها تكون vestibular schwannomas أو ما يُعرف بالـ acoustic neuromas. أشيع عرض لكل أورام الـ cerebellopontine angle هو نقص السمع اللي يُرى بأكثر من 95% من الحالات، والـ vestibular schwannoma بيمشي بنقص سمع تدريجي وطنين على مدى سنوات، وإذا في شك سريري فالـ MRI مع gadolinium هو الفحص المختار.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون medulloblastoma أو ependymoma لأنهم أورام مشهورة بالـ posterior fossa. لكن الـ medulloblastoma أشيع بالطفال ومو بالـ cerebellopontine angle، والـ glioblastoma ورم نسيجي عالي الدرجة بقبّة الدماغ، بينما الـ cerebellopontine angle بالغالبية العظمى أورامه vestibular schwannoma حميدة.

question: Which of the following lumbar puncture results would you expect to find with the head CT seen above?

options.text: Tube 1: WBC 5/µL, RBC 4,000/µL; tube 2: protein 70 mg/dL, glucose 60 mg/dL; tube 3: RBC 50/µL
Tube 1: WBC 7/µL, RBC 4,000/µL; tube 2: protein 75 mg/dL, glucose 60 mg/dL; tube 3: RBC 3,200/µL
Tube 1: WBC 80/µL, RBC 3/µL; tube 2: protein 60 mg/dL, glucose 60 mg/dL; tube 3: RBC 0/µL
Tube 1: WBC 900/µL, RBC 10/µL; tube 2: protein 200 mg/dL, glucose 15 mg/dL; tube 3: RBC 1/µL

correctAnswer: Tube 1: WBC 7/µL, RBC 4,000/µL; tube 2: protein 75 mg/dL, glucose 60 mg/dL; tube 3: RBC 3,200/µL
englishExplanation:
The head CT scan shows a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Most SAHs are caused by a ruptured berry aneurysm in the circle of Willis. CT scan is the initial imaging modality to detect SAH and may (as with this example) show an accumulation of blood in the subarachnoid space. However, if the CT scan is negative after 6 hours from symptom onset, a lumbar puncture (LP) or CTA can be performed to better assess the presence of SAH. If LP is performed, comparing RBC count in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) across tubes helps diagnose SAH over a traumatic lumbar puncture.

If the first and last tubes both have a significant number of RBCs, SAH is most likely. A large difference in RBC numbers (first tube >> last tube) indicates a traumatic tap. No definitive number of RBCs needs to be present in the CSF to diagnose SAH. The pathology can also be detected by identification of xanthochromia, a yellow appearance of the CSF due to blood breakdown and release of bilirubin. Xanthochromia may take up to 12 hours to develop and remains present for several weeks. Xanthochromia can be detected by direct visualization or, preferably, via spectrophotometry.



Tube 1: WBC 5/µL, RBC 4,000/µL; tube 2: protein 70 mg/dL, glucose 60 mg/dL; tube 3: RBC 50/µL (A) is most likely due to a traumatic LP. There is a large difference in the number of RBCs from tube 1 to tube 4.

Tube 1: WBC 80/µL, RBC 3/µL; tube 2: protein 60 mg/dL, glucose 60 mg/dL; tube 3: RBC 0/µL (C) is CSF indicative of aseptic meningitis, with elevated WBCs, mildly elevated protein, and normal glucose.

Tube 1: WBC 900/µL, RBC 10/µL; tube 2: protein 200 mg/dL, glucose 15 mg/dL; tube 3: RBC 1/µL (D) is CSF indicative of bacterial meningitis. There are many WBCs, few RBCs, high protein, and low glucose.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the target blood pressure goal in patients who present with hypertension and acute subarachnoid hemorrhage?

Reveal Answer:
SBP < 160 mm Hg.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage

Most commonly caused by a ruptured aneurysm
Sx: abrupt onset of the worst headache of their life or thunderclap headache
Dx: noncontrast CT scan, blood will appear white on CT
If CT unremarkable and performed within 6 hours of symptom onset, subarachnoid hemorrhage effectively ruled out
If CT unremarkable and suspicion high, lumbar puncture or CTA
Hunt and Hess scale classifies severity of subarachnoid hemorrhage to predict mortality
Treatment is supportive (blood pressure control with IV agents), euvolemia, and nimodipine (prevents vasospasm and other neurologic complications)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ CT المرفق بوضّح subarachnoid hemorrhage، وأغلب الـ SAH بتنتج من رشح berry aneurysm بالـ circle of Willis. الـ CT هو الفحص الأول لكشف الـ SAH وممكن يوضّح تجمع الدم بالـ subarachnoid space، وإذا كان سلبي بعد 6 ساعات من بدء الأعراض ممكن نعمل lumbar puncture أو CTA. وعند عمل الـ LP، مقارنة عدد كريات الدم الحمراء بالـ CSF بين الأنابيب تساعد على التفريق بين الـ SAH والـ traumatic tap. إذا الأنبوب الأول والأخير فيهم عدد كبير من الكريات الحمراء فالـ SAH الأرجح، أما الفرق الكبير بينهم فيعني traumatic tap، وما في رقم محدد مطلوب لتشخيص الـ SAH، وهون الكريات الحمراء متقاربة بالعدد بين الأنابيب.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون النتيجة اللي فيها فرق كبير بين الكريات الحمراء بالأنبوب الأول والأخير، لأنهم بفكروا كل نزف لازم يعطي فرق. لكن الفرق الكبير يعني traumatic tap، والاختيار اللي فيه كريات حمراء عالية بالأنبوب الأول ومنخفضة جداً بالأخير مو SAH.

question: A 65-year-old man with a history of alcohol-related cirrhosis presents to the emergency department with sudden onset left arm weakness and facial droop. Which of the following studies is required prior to administration of tissue plasminogen activator in this patient?
englishExplanation:
The administration of tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with suspected ischemic stroke. Due to the relatively high risk of catastrophic bleeding associated with tPA, patients must be evaluated carefully for indications and contraindications for tPA. A blood glucose level obtained by fingerstick should be obtained prior to the administration of tPA. A fingerstick blood glucose < 50 mg/dL is a relative contraindication to the administration of tPA. This is because both hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia can mimic the symptoms of a stroke. If symptoms persist after correction of hypoglycemia, tPA can be administered in the absence of contraindications. Head imaging must be performed prior to the administration of tPA to rule out hemorrhagic stroke. In the emergency department, this is typically done with a noncontrast CT scan.



CT angiogram of the brain (A) is recommended in patients eligible for endovascular therapies. CTA does not need to be done prior to the administration of tPA.

Liver function tests (C) do not have to be performed or resulted prior to the administration of tPA.

While more sensitive for early ischemic stroke than CT, MRI (D) is less readily available and takes longer to perform than a CT scan, which may delay tPA administration.

One Step Further
Question:
After what period do patients become ineligible for endovascular therapy in the setting of acute ischemic stroke?

Reveal Answer:
> 24 hours after symptom onset.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Ischemic Stroke

Anterior cerebral artery: frontal lobe dysfunction, apraxia, contralateral paralysis (lower > upper)
Middle cerebral artery: contralateral paralysis (upper > lower), aphasia
Posterior cerebral and vertebrobasilar arteries: LOC, nausea or vomiting, CN dysfunction, ataxia, visual agnosia
Dx: CT might reveal loss of gray-white interface, acute hypodensity
Rule out hypoglycemia
CTA to evaluate for large-vessel occlusion
NIHSS to evaluate severity of stroke
Acute Tx: thrombolytics within 4.5 hours, possible thrombectomy within 24 hours
DAWN or Defuse3 can help risk-stratify for mechanical thrombectomy
arabicExplanation:
ليش: إعطاء الـ tissue plasminogen activator حسّن النتائج عند مرضى الـ ischemic stroke المشتبه، وبسبب الخطر العالي نسبياً للنزف الكارثي لازم تقييم دقيق للدواعي وموانع الاستعمال. فحص سكر الدم بالـ fingerstick لازم يُعمل قبل إعطاء الـ tPA، لأن قيمة أقل من 50 mg/dL تعتبر مانعاً نسبياً للإعطاء، والسبب إن نقص السكر أو زيادته ممكن يقلّدوا أعراض السكتة. وإذا استمرت الأعراض بعد تصحيح نقص السكر ممكن نعطي الـ tPA بغياب الموانع الأخرى. كذلك تصوير الرأس ضروري قبل الإعطاء لاستبعاد النزف، وعادة بالـ noncontrast CT.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون MRI أو CT angiogram لأنهم يحسبوا إن تصوير أدق يعني تقييم أفضل. لكن الـ CTA مطلوب للمرشحين للعلاجات داخل الأوعية وما لازم قبل الـ tPA، والـ MRI أقل توفراً ويأخذ وقت أطول فيؤخر الإعطاء، والـ liver function tests ما لازم تكون جاهزة قبل الإعطاء.

question: Which of the following features is most highly associated with a positive biopsy result in a patient with suspected giant cell arteritis?
englishExplanation:
With a mean age of onset of 70 years, giant cell arteritis is a systemic vasculitis that affects medium-sized vessels. Although primarily known for affecting the temporal artery, it can also affect the subclavian, aortic, vertebral, and iliac arteries. Patients present most frequently with a new onset localized headache in association with nonspecific symptoms such as fatigue, low-grade fever, and weight loss. There may be tenderness with palpation of the temporal artery in addition to a decreased temporal artery pulse. Jaw claudication occurs in half of patients and is the symptom most highly associated with a positive biopsy. The most feared complication is visual loss, which can be sudden and painless, partial or complete, and involve one or both eyes. Criteria for diagnosis of giant cell arteritis include age > 50 years, new onset localized headache, temporal artery tenderness or decreased pulsation, erythrocyte sedimentation rate > 50 mm/hr (although often > 80 mm/hr), and abnormal biopsy results. Patients meeting two or fewer criteria require a biopsy for confirmation of the diagnosis. Any patient in whom the diagnosis is suspected should be started on high-dose corticosteroids while arranging for a temporal artery biopsy.



While common symptoms like a fever (A) and headache (B) are associated with giant cell arteritis, they do not increase the likelihood of a positive temporal artery biopsy.

Polymyalgia rheumatica (C) presents with symptoms of morning stiffness and aching in the shoulders, hip girdle, and neck. About half of patients with giant cell arteritis will be diagnosed with polymyalgia rheumatica, but it is not associated with an increased likelihood of a positive biopsy.

One Step Further
Question:
What are two major risk factors for temporal arteritis?

Reveal Answer:
Age (almost never occurs in patients < 50 years old) and ethnicity (increased incidence in people of Scandinavian descent).

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Temporal Arteritis (Giant Cell Arteritis)

Risk factors: age > 50, female sex
Sx: unilateral headache, jaw claudication, monocular visual loss
PE: tender temporal artery
Lab results: ESR > 50 mm/hour, ↑ CRP
Dx: temporal artery biopsy
Treatment: high-dose steroids, do not wait for biopsy if strong suspicion to prevent blindness
Associated with polymyalgia rheumatica
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الـ giant cell arteritis التهاب وعائي جهازي يصيب الأوعية متوسطة الحجم، ومتوسط عمر البدء 70 سنة، ومع إنه معروف بإصابة الشريان الصدغي إلا إنه ممكن يصيب الـ subclavian والـ aortic والـ vertebral والـ iliac. المرضى غالباً يجوا بصداع موضعي جديد مع أعراض غير نوعية كالتعب والحرارة الخفيفة ونقص الوزن، وممكن يكون في إيلام عند جس الشريان الصدغي ونقص نبضه. الـ jaw claudication بيصير بنصف المرضى وهو العرض الأكثر ارتباطاً بنتيجة خزعة موجبة، وأخطر مضاعفة هي فقدان البصر المفاجئ غير المؤلم.
الفخ: الطلاب يختارون fever أو headache لأنهما الأعراض الأكثر شهرة بالـ giant cell arteritis. لكن الـ fever والصداع شائعان ومع ذلك ما بيزيدوا احتمال خزعة الشريان الصدغي الموجبة، والتاريخ المرضي للـ polymyalgia rheumatica مرتبط بالمرض بس مو العرض الأكثر ارتباطاً بنتيجة الخزعة الموجبة.

question: A 26-year-old man presents to the emergency department with lower back pain and lower extremity weakness. The patient has a medical history significant for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and intravenous drug use. He describes the low back pain as 9/10 and sharp with “electric-like” shocks radiating to his lower extremities. He states the pain started last week as a dull ache and it has progressively worsened to the point that he is having weakness in both legs. Vital signs are remarkable for a temperature of 39°C, heart rate of 128 bpm, respiratory rate of 18/min, and BP of 105/75 mm Hg. Physical examination is remarkable for back stiffness and pain. The patient has 3+/5 strength with hip and knee extension and plantar flexion. Bedside post-void residual demonstrates 350 mL of urine. The patient has track marks. What lab test will be most helpful in determining this patient's diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
This patient is demonstrating clinical features concerning for cauda equina syndrome. With his history, vital signs, and physical examination, the most concerning etiology is a spinal epidural abscess. Although spinal epidural abscesses are rare, they are an important central nervous system infection that requires emergent consideration, diagnosis, and treatment. Due to the limited space within the bony confines of the skull or spinal column, abscesses within these spaces can expand rapidly and cause compression of the brain or spinal cord and result in severe symptoms, permanent complications, and even death in some cases.

The spinal epidural space is the area that is between the dura mater and the bony vertebral wall. Spinal epidural abscesses are most commonly found in the thoracolumbar areas where the epidural space contains more fatty tissue that is infection-prone. The cause is usually secondary to bacteria gaining access to the epidural space hematogenously, by direct extension from infected contiguous tissue, or via direct inoculation. Risk factors include epidural catheter placement, paraspinal injections, diabetes mellitus, alcohol use disorder, HIV, trauma, bacteremia, intravenous drug use, and hemodialysis. The classic triad of symptoms include fever, spinal pain, and neurologic deficits (may be consistent with cauda equina syndrome). However, these three only occur simultaneously in a small group of patients. Other clinical features include focal and severe back pain and electric-like nerve root pain that radiates. Once paralysis is present it quickly becomes irreversible, thus early recognition and treatment is crucial.

The white blood cell count may be elevated or normal and thus is not helpful with the diagnosis. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) lab values are typically obtained for evaluation with both being elevated in the majority of cases. However, several studies have found that ESR has better sensitivity as well as specificity compared to CRP. An MRI is the imaging modality of choice, as this will be positive even early in the course of the disease. This will also help determine an alternative diagnosis for the patient’s presentation if a spinal epidural abscess is not the cause.

Treatment relies on early surgical decompression which can be accomplished by a combination of aspiration, drainage, and antibiotic therapies. Antibiotics should be started as soon as the diagnosis is strongly suspected or confirmed. Vancomycin plus cefotaxime or ceftriaxone are appropriate empiric antibiotics. If Pseudomonas is considered a possible organism, cefepime or ceftazidime should be used instead of cefotaxime or ceftriaxone.



Blood cultures (A) are often not helpful in making this diagnosis but should be obtained as they sometimes can help identify a causative organism.

Lactate (C) levels have not demonstrated any usefulness in diagnosing spinal epidural abscesses. Lactate levels are used in patients with sepsis to help determine the severity of the disease.

A white blood cell count (D) has been found to be elevated and normal in almost equal numbers of patients with a spinal epidural abscess. Therefore, it is not commonly used or helpful in the diagnosis of a spinal epidural abscess.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the causative organism in the majority of spinal epidural abscesses?

Reveal Answer:
Staphylococcus aureus.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Spinal Epidural Abscess

Most commonly caused by S. aureus
Risks: diabetes, IV drug use, recent back surgery, immunodeficiency, endocarditis, bacteremia
Sx: back pain, fever, and neurological deficits
Dx: elevated ESR or CRP
MRI
Tx: IV antibiotics, spine surgery consultation for drainage
arabicExplanation: ليش: هالمريض عنده أعراض توجّه لـ cauda equina syndrome، وأخطر سبب محتمل هو spinal epidural abscess بسبب تاريخ الـ intravenous drug use والحرارة العالية وتسمم الدم. الـ abscess بالـ epidural space بيضغط على الحبل الشوكي والنerves بسرعة لأنه المكان ضيق، وعلامته الكلاسيكية ثلاثية: fever وspinal pain وعجز عصبي يظهر كضعف بالأطراف واحتباس بول. الـ ESR هو التحليل الأنسب لأنه مرتفع بالعدوى عادة ويساعد بالتشخيص. الفخ: الطلاب يختارون blood cultures أو white blood cell count لأنهم يفكرون بالعدوى مباشرة. لكن الـ cultures تاخذ وقت لتطلع النتيجة، بينما الـ ESR يعطي دلالة سريعة على وجود التهاب بجسم المريض.

question: A 28-year-old previously healthy woman presents with a 2-day history of fever, stiff neck, photophobia, and nausea. On physical exam, she is alert but appears uncomfortable, with a positive Kernig sign. CSF analysis reveals mildly elevated protein, mildly decreased glucose, and a neutrophilic pleocytosis. Gram stain of the CSF is negative. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
englishExplanation:
The CSF findings of mildly elevated protein, mildly decreased glucose (not as profoundly low as often seen in bacterial meningitis), and a lymphocytic (or in early stages [< 48 hours], neutrophilic) pleocytosis with a negative Gram stain are highly suggestive of viral meningitis. While some bacteria can present with a negative Gram stain initially, this patient's overall CSF profile is most consistent with a viral etiology. This patient's young age and previously healthy status also make common bacterial causes like Streptococcus pneumoniae and Neisseria meningitidis less likely in the absence of specific risk factors.

Viral meningitis is a less severe inflammation of the meninges, often caused by enteroviruses (e.g., coxsackievirus, echovirus), herpes simplex virus (HSV), varicella-zoster virus (VZV), and others. The epidemiology of viral meningitis shows a seasonal variation, with enterovirus infections being more common in the summer and fall. Risk factors are less well-defined compared to bacterial meningitis but can include recent viral illness or exposure.

The signs and symptoms of viral meningitis are often similar to bacterial meningitis but tend to be less severe. Patients may present with fever, headache, stiff neck, photophobia, and sometimes a rash. Physical exam findings may include mild meningeal signs. Diagnosis involves lumbar puncture and CSF analysis. In viral meningitis, the CSF typically shows a normal or slightly elevated protein level, a normal or slightly decreased glucose level, and a pleocytosis that is initially neutrophilic but shifts to lymphocytic within 48 hours. PCR testing of the CSF can help identify specific viral pathogens (e.g., HSV, enterovirus).

Treatment for viral meningitis is primarily supportive, including analgesics for headache, antipyretics for fever, and hydration. Antiviral medications like acyclovir are used for specific viral etiologies such as HSV or VZV meningitis. Complications are usually less common and less severe than in bacterial meningitis, with most patients making a full recovery.



Fungal meningitis like Cryptococcus (A) typically has a more insidious onset and is more common in immunocompromised patients. CSF findings usually include a lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, and low or normal glucose. While this patient's glucose is consistent with fungal meningitis, the acute presentation and the lack of significant immunocompromise make fungal meningitis less likely than a viral etiology in this case.

While Listeria (C) can cause meningitis with variable CSF findings, it is more common in older adults, pregnant patients, and immunocompromised individuals. A negative Gram stain would also be less typical for a significant Listeria infection.

Streptococcus pneumoniae (D) is a common cause of bacterial meningitis and typically presents with a high neutrophil count, significantly elevated protein, and significantly low glucose in the CSF. The negative Gram stain in this patient with only mildly elevated protein and mildly low glucose levels makes S. pneumoniae less likely.

Similar to S. pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis (B) causes bacterial meningitis with characteristic CSF findings of neutrophilic pleocytosis, high protein, and low glucose. It is also often associated with a petechial rash, which is not mentioned in this patient.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the recommended empiric antibiotic regimen and dosage to treat suspected bacterial meningitis?

Reveal Answer:
Ceftriaxone 2 g every 12 hrs or cefotaxime 2 g every 4–6h plus vancomycin loading dose of 20–35 mg/kg.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Bacterial Meningitis - Adult

Sx: headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, phonophobia, fever
PE: meningismus, jolt accentuation, Brudziński sign (flexing neck causes hips and knees to flex), Kernig sign (resistance and pain with knee extension while hip is flexed at 90 degrees)
Mnemonic: Brudziński (bend the brain), Kernig (extend knees)
Most commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae
Treatment is empiric antibiotics by age
18–50 years: ceftriaxone + vancomycin
> 50 years: ceftriaxone + vancomycin + ampicillin (to cover Listeria)
Empiric antibiotics if LP delayed for CT
Consider chemoprophylaxis for close contacts
arabicExplanation: ليش: نتيجة الـ CSF عند المريضة تبين protein مرتفع قليلاً وglucose ناقص قليلاً فقط، مع pleocytosis وGram stain سلبي، وهذا كله يوجه بقوة نحو viral meningitis مو bacterial. الـ viral meningitis أعراضه أخف من البكتيري وعادة يحدث بسبب enteroviruses مثل coxsackievirus وechovirus، وخصوصاً بفصل الصيف والخريف. صغر سن المريضة وسلامتها قبل المرض تخلي الأسباب البكتيرية الشائعة أقل احتمالاً. الفخ: الطلاب يختارون Streptococcus pneumoniae أو Neisseria meningitidis لأنهم يشوفون stiff neck وfever. لكن نزول الـ glucose بشكل بسيط وGram stain السلبي والـ pleocytosis الخفيف كلها تفرّق لصالح السبب الفيروسي.

question: A 22-year-old man presents to the ED with a sustained spasm of his neck to the right. Which of the following drugs is he most likely taking?
englishExplanation:
This man is having a dystonic reaction, which is a common side effect of haloperidol and other typical (first-generation) antipsychotic drugs. Haloperidol is a high-potency antipsychotic that blocks dopamine D2 receptors at the basal ganglia, which can lead to acute dystonia shortly after drug initiation (50% occur within 48 hours, 90% within 5 days) and sustained movement disorders (parkinsonism and tardive dyskinesia) with prolonged use.

Symptoms of acute dystonia include intermittent, involuntary, and uncoordinated hyperkinetic movements, most often affecting the tongue, face, neck, trunk, or extremities. Treatment is with IM or IV benztropine or diphenhydramine, and recovery is rapid after medication administration.



Benztropine (A) has both anticholinergic and antihistamine activity and is commonly used for the treatment of movement disorders.

It is possible for citalopram (B) to cause acute dystonia, but this is rare, and the risk is much higher with first-generation antipsychotics.

Although cocaine (C) does not typically cause dystonia, it can increase the risk for dystonic reactions and is associated with choreoathetoid movements that are referred to as crack dancing.

Ziprasidone (E) is an atypical antipsychotic drug that is much less likely to cause dystonia and other extrapyramidal symptoms.

One Step Further
Question:
What second-generation antipsychotics cause the most prominent anticholinergic side effects (e.g., dry mouth, constipation)?

Reveal Answer:
Olanzapine, quetiapine, and clozapine.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Dystonia

History of taking antipsychotics, antidopaminergic drugs
Characteristic findings
Abnormal posturing of head (torticollis, retrocollis)
Jaw muscle spasms (trismus)
Tongue protrusion
Deviated eyes in one direction (oculogyric crisis)
Abnormal positioning of limbs of the trunk (opisthotonos)
Impaired speaking, swallowing, or breathing
Treatment is IV or IM diphenhydramine, benztropine
Risk factors
History of acute dystonic reaction
High-potency first-generation antipsychotic
Young age
Male sex
Recent cocaine use
arabicExplanation: ليش: هالشاب عنده dystonic reaction، وهي علامة جانبية شائعة لـ haloperidol والأدوية الـ typical antipsychotics لأنها تحجب مستقبلات dopamine D2 بالـ basal ganglia. الـ acute dystonia عادة تبدأ خلال 48 ساعة من بدء الدواء، وأعراضها حركات لا إرادية تصيب اللسان والوجه والرقبة والجذع. الرقبة الملتفة للجهة الوحدة من أشهر صورها. الفخ: الطلاب يختارون cocaine لأنه يفكرون بالحركات اللا إرادية عند متعاطي المخدرات. لكن الـ cocaine يرتبط بحركات choreoathetoid تسمى crack dancing مو الـ dystonia، والـ haloperidol هو السبب الأشيع والأقوى.

question: A 71-year-old man presents to the ED after a witnessed collapse while walking on ice. He was intubated before arrival for a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 5. He has no obvious facial or head trauma. His head CT is shown above. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this finding?
englishExplanation:
Intraparenchymal hemorrhage is caused by spontaneous vessel rupture. It makes up approximately two-thirds of all hemorrhagic strokes. Men are more commonly affected than women. Noncontrast computed tomography (CT) of the head will diagnose 99% of intraparenchymal hemorrhages > 1 cm. Acute hemorrhage will appear bright white on a noncontrast CT scan.

Management includes control of hypertension, neurosurgical consultation, administration of antiepileptic medications if seizures occur, airway intervention when indicated, aggressive glycemic control, and reversal of coagulopathy (if needed). The 30-day mortality from intraparenchymal hemorrhage approaches 50%, and patients should be monitored in an intensive care setting.



Macrovascular thrombosis (A) causes acute ischemic strokes. Early signs of acute ischemic strokes on noncontrast head CT include loss of grey-white matter interface, hyperdensity within a thrombosed artery, or an acute hypodensity in the region of the infarct.

Middle meningeal artery laceration (B) creates an epidural hematoma, which appears as a lenticular (lens) shaped hyperintense (i.e., white) fluid collection in the extradural space on noncontrast head CT.

Torn bridging veins (D) are responsible for creating subdural hematomas. These appear as crescent-shaped fluid collections that may cross suture lines but do not cross the midline.

One Step Further
Question:
What medical condition commonly places patients at risk for acute embolic strokes?

Reveal Answer:
Atrial fibrillation.

Rapid Review
