question: You are on a 10-day mountain climbing excursion in Colorado with one of your 55-year-old coworkers. After ascending to an altitude of 9,200 feet, your coworker develops a mild bifrontal headache associated with nausea. He reports feeling hungover but did not drink any alcohol the previous night. He has no other symptoms. On examination, there are no focal neurologic deficits. He wants to continue the climb. Which of the following is the best next step in the management of this condition?

options.text: Arrange for an airlift to a lower altitude
Continue to ascend but at a slower rate

englishExplanation:
This patient has mild acute mountain sickness (AMS). This syndrome is characterized by headache, nausea, dizziness or lightheadedness, and generalized weakness or fatigue. Development of AMS is associated with rapid ascent to altitude, altitude where sleeping occurs, and respiratory factors such as low ventilatory response and diminished vital capacity. Age has little influence on the incidence of AMS, but individuals with cardiac or pulmonary comorbidities are at increased risk.

AMS usually begins in the setting of rapid ascent of an unacclimatized person to > 2,440 m (8,000 ft). Usually, the person feels lightheaded and slightly breathless with increasing altitude. Symptoms typically develop within 6 hours but may be delayed for 1–2 days. Typical symptoms of mild AMS closely resemble an alcohol hangover. Headaches are usually bifrontal and worsen with bending over or performing a Valsalva maneuver. GI symptoms include anorexia, nausea, and vomiting. The presence of altered mental status and ataxia, especially with ascent to > 9,000 feet, should prompt consideration of high-altitude cerebral edema (HACE).

Mild AMS is self-limited and generally improves after 12–36 hours of acclimatization if ascent is suspended. Oxygen may help relieve symptoms. Pharmacologic therapy offers an alternative to descent or oxygen administration in patients with mild to moderate AMS. Acetazolamide is the initial agent that helps to accelerate acclimatization and prevent development of altitude-related illness. This drug prompts development of a mild metabolic acidosis, leading to an increase in respiratory drive and ventilatory acclimatization. Descent to a lower altitude is the definitive therapy in AMS. However, in people with mild symptoms, AMS is usually self-limiting and acetazolamide can be taken to accelerate acclimatization.



Dexamethasone (B) is also effective in AMS, but because of potential side effects, its use is reserved for moderate to severe cases. Dexamethasone does not aid in acclimatization and can result in rebound symptoms when discontinued.

Aeromedical rescue (C) is indicated for severe cases of AMS and all cases of HACE or high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). This patient’s symptoms are relatively mild, so air transport is not needed.

With the onset of symptoms, it is critical to suspend, not continue ascent (D), until further acclimatization.

One Step Further
Question:
What drug allergy is a relative contraindication to acetazolamide therapy?

Reveal Answer:
Sulfa drugs, many of which contain a sulfhydryl moiety.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Mountain Sickness

Risk: climbing a mountain, unacclimatized to high altitude
Sx: hangover-like headache, nausea, vomiting, generalized weakness, fatigue
Tx: halt ascent, NSAIDs, antiemetics, acetazolamide, dexamethasone
Sulfa allergy: low cross-reactivity but avoid acetazolamide in anaphylactic or SJS allergies

الفخ: الطالب قد يختار مواصلة الصعود ببطء أو ديكساميثازون أو النزول فقط، لكن التعليق مع acetazolamide هو الخطوة الأنسب لحالة خفيفة مستقرة بلا خلل عصبي. التمييز أن أي علامة على التغير الذهني أو ataxia فوق 9000 قدم تستدعي النزول فوراً.

question: A 48-year-old man who was recently evicted from his apartment presents to the emergency department with a core temperature of 30°C. Which of the following is likely seen on his electrocardiogram?
englishExplanation:
Hypothermia is defined as a core temperature < 35°C and causes characteristic changes on the electrocardiogram. Hypothermia causes slowed impulse conduction through the potassium channels resulting in prolongation of the PR, QRS, and QT intervals. Also seen is the J wave, or Osborn wave, which is a positive deflection of the J point (negative deflection in aVR and V1). It is seen most prominently in the precordial leads. The height of the deflection roughly correlates with the degree of hypothermia. Typically seen when the body temperature is < 32°C, J waves can also be seen in hypercalcemia and subarachnoid hemorrhage.



A delta wave (A) is a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex that can be seen in patients with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

Hypothermia will cause prolongation of the QT interval, not a shortened QT interval (C).

A U wave (D) or small deflection immediately following the T wave, can be seen with electrolyte abnormalities such as hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, and hypomagnesemia, as well as with bradycardia.

One Step Further
Question:
At what temperature does shivering typically stop?

Reveal Answer:
32°C (89.6°F).

Rapid Review

Core body temp < 35°C (95°F)
Metabolic excitation followed by slowing phase
Initial increase in BP, HR, CO followed by decrease
ECG: Osborn (J wave)
< 30°C (86°F): patient appears dead, cardiac dysrhythmias
Oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve shifts (oxygen delivery)
Kidney concentrating ability, cold diuresis
Treat only life-threatening dysrhythmias (Vfib, asystole)
Treatment
Mild: passive rewarming
Moderate: passive and active external rewarming
Severe without significant cardiovascular instability: active external and internal rewarming
Severe with significant cardiovascular instability: invasive core rewarming

question: What is the most common cause of minor hemoptysis in the emergency department?
englishExplanation:
Acute bronchitis is the most common cause of minor hemoptysis in the emergency department. Hemoptysis describes the presence of blood in sputum expectorated from the respiratory tract.

Most episodes of hemoptysis are minor, with small amounts of blood. Life-threatening hemorrhage occurs in < 5% of patients with hemoptysis. Bronchitis results from inflammation in the bronchial tree and can lead to hemoptysis. Additionally, forceful coughing further irritates the inflamed mucosal surfaces and can result in bleeding. Hemoptysis in bronchitis is typically self-limited.



Bronchogenic carcinoma (B) is associated with life-threatening hemoptysis due to the involvement of pulmonary vasculature.

Pneumonia (C) can cause minor hemoptysis but to a less common degree than acute bronchitis.

Hemoptysis is an uncommon presenting symptom of pulmonary embolism (D) and is typically small volume when it occurs.

Tuberculosis (E) can cause life-threatening hemoptysis due to ulceration of nearby vessels.

One Step Further
Question:
What are the most common sites of hemorrhage in massive hemoptysis?

Reveal Answer:
Massive hemoptysis typically involves the bronchial or pulmonary arteries.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Bronchitis

Most common cause of minor hemoptysis
Most commonly caused by viruses
Sx: productive cough for > 5 days
PE: wheezing and rhonchi
CXR: thickening of the bronchial walls in the lower lobes
Tx: symptomatic management
Routine Abx therapy not indicated

question: Which of the following patients will benefit most from receiving tissue plasminogen activator for acute pulmonary embolism detected in the emergency department?

options.text: 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension with vital signs showing HR 100 bpm, BP 80/40 mm Hg, RR 24/min, and SpO2 92%
55-year-old man with a history of hypertension with vital signs showing HR 145 bpm, BP 136/86 mm Hg, RR 24/min, and SpO2 92%
55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and systemic lupus erythematosus with vital signs showing HR 100 bpm, BP 116/86 mm Hg, RR 24/min, and SpO2 87%
55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension with vital signs showing HR 110 bpm, BP 122/80 mm Hg, RR 24/min, and SpO2 92% with evidence of right ventricular dysfunction on echocardiogram

correctAnswer: 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension with vital signs showing HR 100 bpm, BP 80/40 mm Hg, RR 24/min, and SpO2 92%
englishExplanation:
Thrombolytic therapy, such as tissue plasminogen activator, helps to form plasmin which results in accelerated lysis of thrombi. Thrombolytic agents have been used in a variety of disorders including myocardial infarction, stroke, and acute pulmonary embolism. Thrombolytic therapy for acute pulmonary embolism can lead to hemodynamic improvement but at a risk of major bleeding. The effect of thrombolytic therapy on mortality in acute pulmonary embolism remains questionable in many circumstances. Typically, only patients with confirmed pulmonary embolism are candidates for therapy, as the adverse effects of thrombolytics can be devastating. Persistent hypotension or shock due to acute pulmonary embolism is the only widely accepted indication for systemic thrombolysis. Other possible indications for thrombolytics in acute pulmonary embolism include increasing tachycardia, worsening right heart dysfunction, and significant hypoxemia. However, unless the patient is hemodynamically compromised, thrombolytics are generally not recommended at this time. Clinicians must consider on a case-by-case basis whether to use thrombolytic therapy as there is some suggestion of improved quality of life in hemodynamically stable patients with other evidence of stress from pulmonary embolism.



The 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension with vital signs showing HR 145 bpm, BP 136/86 mm Hg, RR 24/min, and SpO2 92% (B) has significant tachycardia but is otherwise hemodynamically stable. Thrombolytics would not be indicated in this situation.

The 55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and systemic lupus erythematosus with vital signs showing HR 100 bpm, BP 116/86 mm Hg, RR 24/min, and SpO2 87% (C) is hypoxic but is otherwise hemodynamically stable. Thrombolytics would also not be indicated in this situation.

Finally, the 55-year-old woman with a history of hypertension with vital signs showing HR 110 bpm, BP 122/80 mm Hg, RR 24/min, and SpO2 92% with evidence of right ventricular dysfunction on echocardiogram (D) is a much more controversial scenario for thrombolytic therapy. Clinicians rationalize that patients with significant right ventricular hypokinesis will have a worse prognosis than patients without right ventricular strain. However, randomized controlled trials have not shown a convincing mortality benefit in these patients, especially if there is not associated hemodynamic instability.

One Step Further
Question:
What is the dosage of tissue plasminogen activator that should be given for acute pulmonary embolism?

Reveal Answer:
100 mg IV infused over 2 hours.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review

PE: tachypnea, tachycardia, possible signs of DVT (calf pain or swelling)
ECG: sinus tachycardia, nonspecific ST segment and T wave changes, RV strain, S1Q3T3 (classic finding)
CXR: nonspecific abnormalities, Hampton hump (pleural-based wedge infarct), Westermark sign (vascular cutoff sign)
U/S: right ventricle hypokinesis, flattened interventricular septum, diastolic septal bowing
Dx: Wells criteria ± PERC or YEARS criteria for low pretest probability
CT pulmonary angiography preferred, V/Q scan alternative
Tx
Use Hestia criteria or PESI to determine risk of complications and help with disposition planning (outpatient vs inpatient)
Anticoagulation: heparin, LMWH, warfarin, novel oral anticoagulants (NOACs)
Thrombolytics, embolectomy in hemodynamically unstable patients
Comment: in low clinical suspicion, negative D-dimer excludes PE (D-dimer threshold varies based on practice patterns)

ليش: العلاج المذيب للجلطة مثل tissue plasminogen activator يشكّل plasmin الذي يسرّع إذابة الخثرات، لكنه يحمل خطر نزف كبير وأثره على وفيات الانسداد الرئوي يبقى غير واضح في كثير من الحالات. المؤشر الوحيد المقبول على نطاق واسع هو هبوط الضغط المستمر أو الصدمة بسبب الانسداد الرئوي، وتشمل المؤشرات المحتملة الأخرى تزايد تسارع القلب أو تدهور خلل البطين الأيمن أو نقص الأكسجة الشديد. ومع ذلك لا يُوصى بالعلاج المذيب إذا كان المريض مستقراً من ناحية الدورة الدموية.
الفخ: الطالب قد يختار المريض المستقر أو المريضة التي لا يوجد بها صدمة، لكن العلاج المذيب مخصص للمرضى غير المستقرين. التمييز أن تسارع القلب ونقص الأكسجة وحدهما لا يكفيان للعلاج المذيب في مريض مستقر.

question: A 36-year-old man is transferred from an outlying facility following a drowning incident. He was intubated at the scene for severe respiratory distress. He is notably hypoxic on arrival, with saturations of 88% on the ventilator settings used for transport. Repeat chest X-ray to confirm endotracheal tube position is shown above. Which of the following is most likely to be found in this patient?

options.text: PaO 2 of 92 mm Hg on 30% FiO 2
Pulmonary artery wedge pressure > 18 mm Hg

englishExplanation:
Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a diffuse bilateral inflammatory lung injury that causes accumulation of excess fluid in the interstitium and alveoli, leading to decreased lung compliance, impaired gas exchange, and rapidly worsening respiratory status. ARDS can be precipitated by many conditions, including sepsis, aspiration, pneumonia, and severe trauma. Symptoms usually appear 6–72 hours after the inciting event and progress rapidly. In this patient’s case, aspiration from drowning, whether from fresh or salt water, washes out surfactant from alveoli and results in noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and ARDS. The diagnosis of ARDS requires demonstration of diffuse bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on imaging, exclusion of a cardiac etiology (through normal echocardiography, B-type natriuretic peptide, or right heart catheterization), and a PaO2:FiO2 of < 300. While the mortality of ARDS is still high, certain supportive measures have been shown to decrease mortality. These include low tidal volume ventilation with a target volume of 4–6 mL/kg ideal body weight, high positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), and prone positioning. Low tidal volume ventilation and high PEEP prevent alveolar overdistention and collapse, one of the principal means of lung injury associated with positive pressure ventilation. Prone positioning improves gas exchange.



A PaO2 of 92 mm Hg on 30% FiO2 (B) is consistent with a PaO2:FiO2 of 307. A PaO2:FiO2 of < 200 is consistent with moderate ARDS, the most likely cause of the patient’s presentation. Sepsis is the leading cause of ARDS. However, this patient’s history is not consistent with infection as a cause of his ARDS, and initial blood cultures (C) are unlikely to be positive. A pulmonary artery wedge pressure > 18 mm Hg (D) is suggestive of a cardiac cause of pulmonary edema. For a diagnosis of ARDS, the characteristic pulmonary infiltrates cannot be fully attributable to a cardiac cause.

One Step Further
Question:
What are the three stages of acute respiratory distress syndrome?

Reveal Answer:
Exudative, fibroproliferative, and fibrotic.

Rapid Review
Rapid Review
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)

Diffuse alveolar damage → ↑ alveolar capillary permeability → acute respiratory distress syndrome
Causes: sepsis > gastric aspiration, shock
Hypoxemia refractory to O2
PA wedge pressure < 18 mm Hg
PO2: FiO2 ≤ 300 mm Hg
↑ A-a gradient
CXR: bilateral infiltrates
Tx: PEEP, low TVs (6 mL/kg)
Adjuncts: prone positioning, pulmonary vasodilators, neuromuscular blockade

question:
A 35-year-old male presents to the Emergency Department with fern-like, branching red marks on his skin after
being struck by lightning during a thunderstorm. Which of the following best describes these skin findings?
englishExplanation:
Lichtenberg figures
Explanation
Lichtenberg figures, also known as "lightning flowers" or "lightning trees," are distinctive, fern-like patterns that appear on the skin of some lightning strike victims. These transient, painless markings are caused by the passage of electric current through the skin and superficial blood vessels. They typically fade within hours to days.

question: A 35-year-old man is brought to the Emergency Department after being electrocuted while working on a high-voltage power line. He is conscious but complaining of severe muscle pain and weakness. Which of the following complications is most likely to occur in this patient?
englishExplanation:
Acute kidney injury
Explanation
Electrical injuries, particularly those involving high-voltage currents, can cause severe muscle damage (rhabdomyolysis). This leads to the release of myoglobin and other cellular contents into the bloodstream, which can overwhelm the
kidneys and cause acute kidney injury.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الإصابات الكهربائية التي تشمل تياراً عالي الجهد تسبب تلفاً عضلياً شديداً مع انحلال العضلات (rhabdomyolysis). ينتج عن ذلك إطلاق الميوغلوبين ومحتويات الخلايا الأخرى في الدم، فيصير الحمل على الكلى كبيراً ويسبب إصابة كلوية حادة. هذه هي المضاعفة الأكثر شيوعاً بعد الصعق الكهربائي عالي الجهد، خصوصاً مع ألم العضلات الشديد والضعف الذي يشكو منه هذا المريض الواعي.
الفخ: الطالب قد يختار استرواح الصدر أو وذمة الدماغ لأن الصعق الكهربائي يبدو خطيراً على العمود الفقري، لكن الأثر الكلوي عبر الميوغلوبين هو الأوثق ارتباطاً. التمييز أن انحلال العضلات هو الآلية التي تقود إلى الإصابة الكلوية الحادة.

question:
A 28-year-old male presents to the Emergency Department after collapsing during a marathon on a hot summer
day. He is confused, has a temperature of 40.5°C (105°F), and his skin is hot and dry. Which of the following is the
most likely diagnosis?
englishExplanation:
Heat stroke
Explanation
The key features that distinguish heat stroke from heat exhaustion are:
Central nervous system dysfunction (confusion in this case)
Core body temperature above 40°C (104°F)
Hot and dry skin (as opposed to profuse sweating in heat exhaustion)
arabicExplanation:
ليش: ضربة الحرارة (heat stroke) تتمايز عن الإعياء الحراري (heat exhaustion) بثلاث علامات أساسية: خلل في الجهاز العصبي المركزي مثل التشوش الذي يظهر عند هذا المريض، ودرجة حرارة أساسية تتجاوز 40 درجة مئوية، وبشرة حارة جافة. أما الإعياء الحراري فيتميز بعرق غزير ودون خلل عصبي مركزي، والاختلاف في التعرق وحده يميز الحالتين بوضوح. وقد ترافق هذه الحالة أيضاً الالتهاب العام وتلف بطانة الأوعية، وهي من شدة الحرارة التي تميز الحالات الخطيرة.
الفخ: الطالب قد يختار الإعياء الحراري أو الجفاف أو نقص الصوديوم لأن marathon في الصيف يقترحها، لكن خلل الوعي مع درجة حرارة فوق 40 وبشرة جافة يميز ضربة الحرارة. التمييز أن التعرق الغزير موجود في الإعياء الحراري وليس في ضربة الحرارة.

question:
A 35-year-old factory worker presents to the Emergency Department after accidental exposure to a non-caustic
chemical agent during a workplace incident. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial decontamination method?
englishExplanation:
Dry decontamination using absorbent materials
Explanation
Dry decontamination should be the initial method after exposure to a non-caustic chemical agent. This approach involves using absorbent materials such as paper towels or cloth to remove contaminants from the skin and clothing
without introducing water.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في التعرض لعامل كيميائي غير كاوٍ تكون الخطوة الأولى إزالة التلوث بشكل جاف باستخدام مواد ماصة مثل المناشف الورقية أو القماش، والهدف إزالة الملوث من الجلد والملابس دون إدخال الماء الذي قد ينشر التلوث أو يزيد امتصاص المادة بالجلد. تُجمع المواد المستخدمة في كيس محكم وتُتلف بطريقة آمنة. أما الغسل الفوري بالماء أو التحايد الكيميائي أو تأجيل إزالة التلوث حتى بعد التقييم الطبي فخيارات غير مناسبة هنا.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication of heat stroke?
englishExplanation:
Pancreatitis
Explanation
Pancreatitis is not a common complication of heat stroke. The other options are all well-documented complications of
severe heat stroke.
Acute kidney injury can occur due to dehydration, decreased renal perfusion, and direct thermal injury to the kidneys.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation is a serious complication resulting from systemic inflammation and endothelial damage.
Rhabdomyolysis occurs due to the breakdown of muscle tissue, which can lead to acute kidney injury and electrolyte
imbalances.
Liver failure can result from direct thermal injury to hepatocytes and decreased hepatic perfusion.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: التهاب البنكرياس (pancreatitis) ليس من المضاعفات الشائعة لضربة الحرارة، أما المضاعفات الشائعة الموثقة لضربة الحرارة الشديدة فهي إصابة الكلى الحادة والتجلط داخل الأوعية الدموية المنتشر (DIC) وانحلال العضلات (rhabdomyolysis) وفشل الكبد، وتعود أسبابها إلى الجفاف وضعف التروية الكلوية والأرضية الحرارية المباشرة للكلية وإلى الالتهاب العام وتلف بطانة الأوعية في DIC وإلى تلف الخلايا العضلية في الانحلال وإلى الضرر الحراري المباشر لخلايا الكبد مع ضعف التروية الكبدية.
الفخ: الطالب قد يختار إصابة الكلى الحادة أو انحلال العضلات أو فشل الكبد لأنها مضاعفات حقيقية لضربة الحرارة، لكن السؤال يطلب ما ليس شائعاً. التمييز أن Pancreatitis هو الاستثناء المكتوب في السؤال.

question:
A 32-year-old hiker presents to the emergency department with a
severe headache, nausea, and fatigue after ascending to an altitude
of 3,500 meters over the past 24 hours. Which of the following is the
most appropriate initial management?

options.text: Continue ascending to a higher altitude

englishExplanation:
Oral acetazolamide 250 mg twice daily
Explanation
Acetazolamide is the first-line pharmacological treatment for acute
mountain sickness (AMS). It works by increasing renal bicarbonate excretion, leading to metabolic acidosis, which stimulates ventilation and
improves oxygenation. This medication is most effective when started
24-48 hours before ascent but can also be used for treatment. 
https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/yellowbook/2024/environmental-hazards-risks/high-elevation-travel-and-altitude-illness
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الخط الأول الدوائي لمرض الجبال الحاد (AMS) هو acetazolamide عن طريق الفم بجرعة 250 ملغ مرتين يومياً، وهو فعّال أكثر إذا بدأ قبل الصعود بـ 24 إلى 48 ساعة لكنه مفيد أيضاً كعلاج. آلية عمله زيادة طرح البيكربونات الكلوية فيحدث حماضاً أيضياً يحفز التنفس ويحسن الأكسجة، وهذا ما يفسر فعاليته في تخفيف الأعراض. أما الاستمرار في الصعود فهو ضد التشخيص لأنه يزيد من نقص الأكسجة.
الفخ: الطالب قد يختار الاستمرار بالصعود أو السوائل الوريدية أو Nifedipine أو ديكساميثازون، لكن acetazolamide هو العلاج الدوائي الأول لمرض الجبال الحاد. التمييز أن تعليقه للصعود مع الدواء هو الأنسب.

question: In a HAZMAT incident involving, which of the following best describes the "Hot Zone"?

options.text: The area where decontamination procedures are performed
The location where emergency responders don their protective equipment
The immediate area surrounding the incident with the highest level of contamination
The area where medical treatment is provided to affected individuals
The outer perimeter where the public is restricted from entering

correctAnswer: The immediate area surrounding the incident with the highest level of contamination
englishExplanation:
The immediate area surrounding the incident with the highest level of contamination
Explanation
 The Hot Zone, also known as the Exclusion Zone, is the area immediately surrounding a HAZMAT incident where the
contamination or hazard is most severe. It requires the highest level of protective equipment and is restricted to essential personnel only.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المنطقة الحارة (Hot Zone) هي المنطقة المباشرة المحيطة بالحادث التي تحتوي على أعلى مستوى من التلوث، وتتطلب أعلى مستوى من معدات الحماية وتقتصر على الأفراد الضروريين فقط. أما منطقة إزالة التلوث أو منطقة العلاج أو المحيط الخارجي فكلها مناطق بمستويات حماية مختلفة. التمييز واضح من الاسم نفسه لأنه المنطقة الأقرب والأكثر خطراً من حيث التلوث الكيميائي أو الإشعاعي.
الفخ: الطالب قد يختار منطقة إزالة التلوث أو منطقة العلاج أو المحيط الخارجي، لكن Hot Zone هي المنطقة المباشرة المحيطة بالحادث بأعلى تلوث. التمييز أن المحيط الخارجي هو المنطقة التي يُقيد فيها دخول العامة وليس المنطقة الأكثر خطراً.

question:
A 10-year-old boy complains of headaches and nausea. His teachers have noticed he is less attentive during
lessons. He has no past medical history and is not on any regular medications. Which is the most useful
investigation?
englishExplanation:
COHb
Explanation
These symptoms are suspicious of carbon monoxide poisoning- the most useful test would be a COHb level from a
blood gas.
In carbon monoxide poisoning, an initial carboxyhaemoglobin (COHb) concentration >30% is likely to be associated
with severe poisoning.
Headache is present in 90% of cases, and nausea and vomiting in half of cases.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: الأعراض عند هذا الطفل (صداع وغثيان ونقص انتباه دون تاريخ مرضي) تشير بقوة إلى تسمم أول أكسيد الكربون، وأفضل فحص هو قياس COHb في الدم من غاز الدم. في التسمم الحاد يكون تركيز COHb أكثر من 30 بالمئة عادة مع صداع في 90 بالمئة من الحالات وغثيان في نصفها. أما تشبع الأكسجين أو الجلوكوز أو ETCO2 أو الهيموغلوبين فلا يكشف التسمم بأول أكسيد الكربون لأنه لا يؤثر مباشرة على تشبع الأكسجين الظاهري.
الفخ: الطالب قد يختار تشبع الأكسجين أو الجلوكوز أو ETCO2 أو الهيموغلوبين، لكن هذه لا تكشف التسمم بأول أكسيد الكربون. التمييز أن COHb هو الفحص الأكثر فائدة ويُطلب من غاز الدم مباشرة.

question:
A 45-year-old patient presents to the Emergency Department with a
history of anaphylaxis after a bee sting. He has been treated with 1
doses of intramuscular adrenaline, given 25 minutes after the sting,
to which he responded right away. His symptoms have completely
resolved, and his vital signs are normal. He has an EpiPen at home,
and he will be at home with his wife as well. 
What is the recommended observation period for this patient before
considering discharge?
englishExplanation:
2 hours
Explanation
Consider fast-track discharge (after 2 hours observation from resolution of anaphylaxis) if:
Good response (within 5–10 minutes) to a single dose of adrenaline given within 30 minutes of onset of reaction and
Complete resolution of symptoms and
The patient already has unused adrenaline auto-injectors and has been
trained how to use them and
There is adequate supervision following discharge

question:
A 32-year-old construction worker collapses whilst working on a
building site during a heatwave.
His colleagues report that he complained of muscle cramps and
dizziness earlier in the day.
On arrival of the paramedics, he becomes combative and confused.
In the Emergency Department, his consciousness level fluctuates

between GCS 11-14.
Vital signs:
• Temperature 42.6°C
• Heart rate 122 beats per minute
• Blood pressure 92/58 mmHg
• Respiratory rate 28 breaths per minute
• Oxygen saturation 98% on room air
• Blood glucose 5.1 mmol/L
Clinical examination:
• Hot, dry skin
• No neck stiffness
• No focal neurological signs
• No evidence of infection
• No signs of trauma
Past medical history: Nil
Which of the following treatments would lower his temperature the
fastest?

options.text: Placing ice packs on the groin and axillae

englishExplanation:
Ice water immersion
Explanation
This patient has clear signs of heat stroke: hyperthermia (42.6°C), altered mental status, tachycardia, hypotension, and dry skin. Ice water
immersion provides the fastest cooling rate (9-21°C/hour) through conductive and convective heat loss. The severe hyperthermia and end-organ dysfunction require rapid cooling to prevent mortality.
Incorrect Answers:
A) Tepid sponging with fans: Much slower cooling rate (1.2-3°C/hour).
While evaporative cooling can be effective for heat exhaustion, it's inadequate for heat stroke, where rapid cooling is essential.
C) Cold IV fluids: While necessary for treating hypotension and supporting organ perfusion, the cooling rate (approximately 1.2-
1.8°C/hour) is too slow for this critically ill patient. It should be used as
an adjunct to more aggressive cooling methods.
D) Haemodialysis: While it can cool blood directly, the setup time and
slower cooling rate make it impractical for emergency cooling. Would
be considered in cases complicated by severe renal failure or electrolyte
disturbances.
E) Ice packs on groin and axillae: Surface cooling with ice packs is too
slow (1.2-1.8°C/hour) and affects too little body surface area to achieve
rapid temperature reduction needed in heat stroke.

Here are the cooling rates for common cooling methods (6, 27-29, 42-
46). The dotted line represents the minimum recommended cooling
rate for an EHS patient.

question:
A 44-year-old male construction worker arrives to 
your emergency department with a burn injury to his 
leg. He was preparing cement when he accidentally 
spilled it on his leg (Figure 14.3). Which of the following is the BEST INITIAL management of this type of 
injury?

options.text: Brushing off remaining particles from the wound
Neutralization with a dilute acidic solution

correctAnswer: Brushing off remaining particles from the wound
englishExplanation:
12.  The answer is A. (Chapter 218) The patient has been 
exposed to lime (calcium oxide), a common ingredient in 
cement. Lime converts to the calcium hydroxide, an alkali, 
on contact with water producing an exothermic reaction. 
Even small amounts of remaining particles can produce 
this reaction and cause worsening damage to the wound. 
For this reason, particles of remaining irritant should be 
brushed away before aggressive irrigation takes place. 
For the same reason, neutralization of the exposed area 
should be avoided. Compartment pressures are elevated 
in compartment syndrome, which is usually caused by 

188

also with jaundice, lethargy, elevated transaminases, and 
disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), followed 2 
to 4 days later with multiorgan failure. Fungemia is not a 
common cause of death in mushroom ingestion, which 
is amatoxin mediated. End-organ damage resulting in 
acute renal failure is possible from profound dehydration 
in these ingestions and is a hallmark of amanita toxicity, 
but typically it does not occur without liver failure. Direct 
cardiac toxicity is not specific to amanita toxicity.

الفخ: يختار بعضهم copious irrigation أو neutralization ويظنونها الخطوة الأولى، لكن هذا خطأ لأن الجزيئات المتبقية تتفاعل مع الماء وتسبب مزيداً من الضرر.

question:
The toxic agent in poison hemlock is structurally 
MOST similar to which substance?
englishExplanation:
15.  The answer is C. (Chapter 221) Poison hemlock contains alkaloids that are structurally similar to nicotine. 
Mild toxicity can result in tremulousness and anxiety from 
sympathomimetic stimulation. Late toxicity can result in 
paralysis from nicotinic receptor stimulation at the neuromuscular junction. The alkaloids of poison hemlock are 
not structurally related to norepinephrine, histamine, or 
acetylcholine.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: Poison hemlock يحتوي على alkaloids تشبه nicotine structurally، مما يسبب tremulousness و anxiety من sympathomimetic stimulation، ثم paralysis من nicotinic receptor stimulation عند neuromuscular junction، وهي ليست مرتبطة بـ norepinephrine أو histamine أو acetylcholine.
الفخ: يختار البعض acetylcholine أو histamine ويظنون التشابه مع toxidrome cholinergic، لكن التشابه الهيكلي مع nicotine هو المفتاح.

question:
Which toxidrome would be expected in an ingestion 
of deadly nightshade?
englishExplanation:
16.  The answer is A. (Chapter 221) Deadly nightshade 
(Atropa belladonna) contains atropine-like alkaloids 
that produce the antimuscarinic toxidrome in overdose. 
Expected signs/symptoms include tachycardia, hyperthermia, mydriasis, dry flushed skin, urinary retention, 
and altered mental status. Treatment is largely supportive. 
Benzodiazepines may be used for agitation. Physostigmine inhibits acetylcholinesterase and may be used for 
reversal of muscarinic symptoms. Both can be redosed as 
needed.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: Deadly nightshade (Atropa belladonna) تحتوي على atropine-like alkaloids تُنتج antimuscarinic toxidrome: tachycardia، hyperthermia، mydriasis، جفاف الجلد، urinary retention، و altered mental status. العلاج داعم مع benzodiazepines، ويمكن استخدام physostigmine لعكس الأعراض الموسكارينية.
الفخ: يختار البعض cholinergic toxidrome ويخلط بين atropine ومفعول acetylcholine، لكن العلامات هنا غياب إفرازات وتشوش ذهني وجفاف.

question: The most common cause of hypomagnesemia in the ED is likely
englishExplanation:
Between 30% and 80% of alcoholics have magnesium deficiency. Patients with 
hypomagnesemia are frequently asymptomatic or manifest only nonspecific symptoms. The 
most prominent symptoms in the ED are neuromuscular and cardiovascular, and magnesium 
deficiency tends to mimic calcium deficiency. The mechanism of hypomagnesemia in alcoholism 
is thought to be a combination of malnutrition, increased renal excretion, and GI losses from 
vomiting and diarrhea. Diuretic therapy is also a very prevalent cause of hypomagnesemia, 
although the subsequent volume loss increases magnesium reabsorption in the proximal tubule. 

Therefore, magnesium depletion in the setting of diuretic therapy tends to be modest. 
Hypomagnesemia is the most common electrolyte abnormality in ambulatory diabetic patients 
and is also common in DKA. In these patients, magnesium is lost through the urine due to 
glycosuria.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: بين 30% و 80% من مدمني الكحول لديهم magnesium deficiency، والآلية تشمل سوء التغذية، زيادة الإفراغ الكلوي، وخسائر GI من القيء والإسهال. diuretics شائعة أيضاً، لكن حجم السوائل المتصاعد يعزز إعادة امتصاص المغنيسيوم في proximal tubule، لذلك النقص متواضع. كما أنه شائع في DKA بسبب glycosuria.
الفخ: يختار البعض diuretic therapy أو acute tubular necrosis ويظنونها السبب الأبرز، لكن alcoholism هو الأكثر شيوعاً في ED حسب النص.

question:
A 40-year-old male presents with delirium, polyuria, and a serum calcium level of 15 mg/dL. 
Which of the following is true?

options.text: Nifedipine is the agent of choice for initial treatment.
Thiazide diuretics are more helpful than loop diuretics in promoting urine calcium excretion.
Calcitonin can be used as monotherapy in the treatment of hypercalcemia.
Sodium bicarbonate infusion will increase the amount of ionized calcium.
Glucocorticoids may be helpful if the patient has an underlying hematologic malignancy or

correctAnswer: Glucocorticoids may be helpful if the patient has an underlying hematologic malignancy or
englishExplanation:
This patient has hypercalcemic crisis (generally defined as any patient with a serum 
calcium >14 mg/dL), which is typically characterized by altered mental status, polyuria, and 
dehydration. The initial goals are to restore intravascular volume with intravenous saline and to 
rapidly lower the serum calcium level by enhancing urinary excretion and reducing bone 
resorption (primarily through osteoclast inhibitors such as pamidronate or other 
bisphosphonates). Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) such as nifedipine, play no role in the 
treatment of hypercalcemia. Loop diuretics are the most effective drugs in enhancing urinary 
calcium elimination. In contrast, thiazides increase calcium reabsorption in the distal tubule 
resulting in a further increase in serum calcium levels. Calcitonin is the fastest acting, but 
weakest agent in reducing serum calcium and cannot be used for monotherapy. Bicarbonate is 
not useful in hypercalcemia. However, in the setting of a true alkalosis, more free calcium will be 
bound to albumin, thereby decreasing the amount of free ionized calcium. Glucocorticoids are 
useful in patients with hypercalcemia caused by an underlying hematologic malignancy or 
granulomatous disease due to their effects on vitamin D metabolism and cytokine release. 
Glucocorticoids do not exert their effect for 1 to 2 days after initiation of treatment.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض يعاني من hypercalcemic crisis (>14 mg/dL) مع delirium و polyuria و dehydration. الأهداف الأولية هي استعادة حجم الدم بـ intravenous saline وتخفيض الكالسيوم عبر loop diuretics (الأكثر فعالية) ومثبطات العظام مثل bisphosphonates (pamidronate). CCBs مثل nifedipine لا دور لها، و thiazides تزيد إعادة امتصاص الكالسيوم. calcitonin أسرع لكن أضعف ولا يُستخدم وحده. glucocorticoids مفيدة في malignancy أو granulomatous disease فقط.
الفخ: يختار البعض nifedipine أو thiazides ويظنونها مفيدة، لكن الأولى لا دور لها والثانية ترفع الكالسيوم بدلاً من خفضه.

question:
Upon starting your shift, you receive sign-out on a 46-year-old male diabetic patient who is 
being treated with an intravenous insulin drip for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). Two hours later, a 
repeat chemistry panel reveals the following: Na+ 141 mEq/L, Cl- 112 mEq/L, HCO3- 17 mEq/L, 
blood urea nitrogen (BUN) 16 mg/dL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, glucose 278 mg/dL. Which of the 
following is true?

options.text: The patient has a mixed high anion gap (AG) ketoacidosis and nonanion gap hyperchloremic
He should be given subcutaneous insulin and his insulin infusion can be discontinued after 30
His DKA is not yet resolved and he requires an ongoing intravenous insulin infusion.
The patient should be given bicarbonate replacement therapy.
A repeat arterial blood gas (ABG) should be performed to guide further therapy.

correctAnswer: He should be given subcutaneous insulin and his insulin infusion can be discontinued after 30
englishExplanation:
This patient’s AG is 12, which is normal. Assuming that the patient has a normal 
albumin concentration (the major contributor to the AG in healthy patients), the normal AG 
reflects a resolution of the ketoacidosis. If substantial ketoacids were still present, the AG would 
be persistently elevated and the patient would require an ongoing insulin infusion. The 
persistently low bicarbonate signifies that a metabolic acidosis is still present, but it is an HCMA 
(nonanion gap). The development of an HCMA is a common complication of DKA therapy. This is 
partly due to the infusion of a large volume of saline, which contains chloride in concentrations 
far greater than plasma (154 mEq/L). Another major contributor is the loss of ketoanions in the 
urine that would normally serve as precursors for bicarbonate regeneration. The development 
of HCMA is benign and requires no therapy. In the setting of normal renal function, it will 
resolve spontaneously over the next 24 hours due to increased renal acid secretion. 
Subcutaneous insulin should always be overlapped with an insulin infusion when discontinuing 
continuous insulin therapy.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: AG = 12 طبيعي، مما يعني حل ketoacidosis، لكن HCO3- منخفض (17) فيدل على HCMA (nonanion gap) بسبب infusion من saline غني بـ chloride (154 mEq/L) وخسارة ketoanions في البول. هذا benign ويحل تلقائياً خلال 24 ساعة عبر زيادة renal acid secretion. يجب overlap subcutaneous insulin مع infusion عند التوقف.
الفخ: يعتقد البعض أن DKA لم تحل ويختار استمرار insulin infusion، أو يختار bicarbonate، لكن AG طبيعي يعني حل الكيتوز.

question:
Which of the following correctly matches the clinical entity and its effects on phosphate 
metabolism?

options.text: Treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) causes hypophosphatemia.

correctAnswer: Treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) causes hypophosphatemia.
englishExplanation:
The most common causes of hypophosphatemia in the ED are probably respiratory 
alkalosis, treatment of DKA, and alcoholism. The most common mechanism is an intracellular 
shift of phosphate (respiratory alkalosis, treatment of DKA). Renal insufficiency leads to 
phosphate retention, whereas hyperparathyroidism causes increased renal excretion.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: أكثر أسباب hypophosphatemia في ED هي respiratory alkalosis، وعلاج DKA، والإدمان على الكحول. الآلية الأساسية هي intracellular shift من الفوسفات (في respiratory alkalosis وعلاج DKA). الفشل الكلوي يسبب retention، وفرط نشاط الغدة الجار درقية يزيد الإفراغ الكلوي.
الفخ: يظن البعض أن hyperparathyroidism يسبب نقصاً، لكنه يسبب زيادة الإفراغ، وليس نقصاً مباشرة.

question: Which of the following is true in alcoholic ketoacidosis (AKA)?

options.text: In addition to glucose, insulin is useful in management.
The alcohol level is usually >100 mg/dL.
The osmolal gap is usually elevated.
β-hydroxybutyrate is the primary ketone responsible for the acidosis and is produced due to

correctAnswer: β-hydroxybutyrate is the primary ketone responsible for the acidosis and is produced due to
englishExplanation:
AKA is an elevated anion gap metabolic acidosis that usually occurs in chronic 
alcoholics after a recent binge of alcohol results in vomiting, starvation, dehydration, and 
acidosis. Due to complex pathophysiology, the acidosis is dominated by β-hydroxybutyrate, 
which is not detected by standard urinary ketone tests. Furthermore, as the acidosis resolves, 
β-hydroxybutyrate is converted to acetoacetate and acetone resulting in a paradoxical (or false) 
“worsening” of the acidosis evidenced by increased detection of acetoacetate in the urine. 
Traditionally, the osmolal gap is normal, although there are case reports of patients with AKA 
and an elevated osmolal gap. It may be difficult to differentiate patients with AKA from chronic 
alcohol abusers with toxic alcohol ingestion. Toxic alcohol ingestion should always be in the 
differential of AKA and should be the top consideration whenever the osmolal gap is elevated. 
The alcohol level is typically zero as AKA is primarily a starvation ketosis. Glucose levels are not 
usually elevated and insulin is unnecessary. Treatment is with saline and glucose solutions as 
well as electrolyte replacement.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: AKA هو elevated anion gap metabolic acidosis في مدمني الكحول بعد binge مع قيء وتجفاف. السائد هو β-hydroxybutyrate، وهو غير مكتشف في standard urinary ketone tests (nitroprusside). مع حل الحموضة يتحول إلى acetoacetate و acetone فيظهر تفاقم كاذب. osmolal gap عادة طبيعي. Alcohol level عادة صفر لأنه starvation ketosis. العلاج بـ saline و glucose و electrolytes، ولا حاجة لـ insulin.
الفخ: يختار البعض أن insulin مفيد أو أن alcohol level مرتفع، لكن insulin غير ضروري والمستوى عادة صفر.

question:
A 24-year-old diabetic male presents with rapid, deep breathing in the setting of severe 
hyperglycemia. Lungs are clear and SaO2 is 100% on RA. His urine dipstick is only mildly positive 
for ketones. Which of the following is the likely explanation?

options.text: β-hydroxybutyrate, which is poorly detected by dipsticks, is the predominant ketone
His rapid breathing is likely due to pulmonary pathology not a metabolic acidosis
Acetoacetate interferes with the dipstick analysis
He has lactic acidosis from sepsis not detected by dipsticks

correctAnswer: β-hydroxybutyrate, which is poorly detected by dipsticks, is the predominant ketone
englishExplanation:
β-hydroxybutyrate, which isn’t detected by standard nitroprusside urine dipsticks, is 
the predominant ketone in diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), especially in severe cases. That can yield 
false negative or weakly positive results and can cause confusion. Nitroprusside reacts with 
acetoacetate and to a lesser degree, with acetone. In DKA, the ratio of 
β-hydroxybutyrate:acetoacetate can be as high as 10:1.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: β-hydroxybutyrate هو predominant ketone في DKA الشديد وهو غير مكتشف في nitroprusside urine dipsticks التي تتفاعل مع acetoacetate و acetone فقط. نسبة β-hydroxybutyrate:acetoacetate قد تصل إلى 10:1، مما يسبب نتائج سلبية أو ضعيفة.
الفخ: يختار البعض أنه lactic acidosis أو أن dipstick يعكس كل الكيتونات، لكن β-hydroxybutyrate هو المهيمن وغير مكتشف.

question: Hypernatremia …

options.text: Almost never occurs in alert patients with an intact thirst mechanism.
May occur after the administration of a single dose of charcoal.
Is most commonly due to increased body stores of sodium (or sodium gain).
Is best treated with normal saline.
May result in central pontine myelinolysis if not treated within 72 hours.

correctAnswer: Almost never occurs in alert patients with an intact thirst mechanism.
englishExplanation:
Hypernatremia is almost always caused by the loss of free water and rarely by sodium 
gain (which is usually iatrogenic). Regardless of the underlying cause, it almost never occurs in 
alert patients with an intact thirst mechanism. It is a known complication of multiple doses of 
activated charcoal, occurring in 6% of patients receiving such therapy. Treatment with saline 
should only occur in patients who have hemodynamic compromise. Almost all patients, 
however, require treatment with half-normal saline or more dilute solutions with lower tonicity. 
The main complication of therapy is cerebral edema, so the rate of correction should be 0.5 to 
1.0 mEq/L/hour on average (though it may be more rapid for the initial few hours if the patient 

is suffering life-threatening complications of hypernatremia). Central pontine myelinolysis is a 
complication of therapy for hyponatremia.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: Hypernatremia دائماً تقريباً بسبب فقدان free water ونادراً بسبب sodium gain، وتحدث فقط عندما يكون thirst mechanism معطلاً. العلاج بـ half-normal saline أو أكثر تخفيفاً، مع معدل تصحيح 0.5-1.0 mEq/L/hour لتجنب cerebral edema. Central pontine myelinolysis هو مضاعفة علاج hyponatremia، لا hypernatremia.
الفخ: يختار البعض normal saline أو يظن أنه يحدث في المرضى اليقظين، لكن الضرورة وجود فقدان ماء مع عجز العطش.

question: Which of the following findings may be present in hypothyroidism?

options.text: Delayed relaxation phase of deep tendon reflexes

englishExplanation:
Hypothermia is one of the most common manifestations of severe hypothyroidism 
(e.g., myxedema) although body temperature is rarely <95°F. In the setting of myxedema, a 
“normal” temperature should trigger a search for a focus of infection. Nonpitting edema is due 
to hyaluronic acid deposition and is initially found in the periorbital region. Pseudomyotonic or 
“hung up” reflexes are another common finding (delayed relaxation phase of deep tendon 
reflexes). Paresthesias are present in >80% of patients and median nerve neuropathy (carpal 
tunnel syndrome) is the most common manifestation.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: Hypothyroidism الشديد (myxedema) يُظهر hypothermia، و nonpitting edema حول العين بسبب hyaluronic acid، و reflexes متأخرة (delayed relaxation)، و paresthesias، و median nerve neuropathy (carpal tunnel) في أكثر من 80%. درجة الحرارة الطبيعية يجب أن تدفع للبحث عن عدوى.
الفخ: يظن البعض أن edema pitting أو أن hypothermia دائماً <95°F، لكن edema nonpitting والحرارة نادراً أقل من ذلك.

question:
A 65-year-old male with a history of myasthenia gravis (MG) presents with acute generalized 
malaise and hypotension. He reports that he ran out of his medicines a week ago but doesn’t 
recall their names. His vital signs are 98.5°F, 85, 18, 90/62, 99% RA. His EKG is normal. Which of 
the following is the most likely cause of hypotension in this patient?
englishExplanation:
Most patients with myasthenia gravis (MG) take glucocorticoids. This patient’s 
hypotension is likely caused by adrenal insufficiency precipitated by glucocorticoid withdrawal. 
The degree of insufficiency depends partly on the dosage, duration, and frequency. Addison 
disease refers to primary adrenal insufficiency and occurs far less commonly than 
corticosteroid-induced disease. Adrenal hemorrhage is very rare and most cases do not cause 
insufficiency. Viral, fungal, and mycobacterial infections can occasionally cause adrenal 
insufficiency; bacteria are almost never implicated. Myasthenic crises are characterized by 
generalized or bulbar weakness in most patients and with primary respiratory symptoms in a 
few patients. Hypotension is not characteristic.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: المريض مصاب بـ myasthenia gravis ويأخذ glucocorticoids، وانقطاعها يسبب adrenal insufficiency ثانوية. Addison disease (primary) أقل شيوعاً. hemorrhage نادر، والعدوى نادرة، وبكتيريا نادراً implicated. Myasthenic crisis يسبب ضعفاً عام/بلعومياً، وليس hypotension.
الفخ: يختار البعض Addison disease أو myasthenic crisis ويظنها سبب انخفاض الضغط، لكن الانسحاب من corticosteroids هو السبب الأرجح.

question:
A 55-year-old female on long-term steroids for sarcoidosis is brought in by paramedics with 
generalized weakness and altered mental status. You quickly suspect acute adrenal 
insufficiency. Which of the following are primarily responsible for the majority of acute 
morbidity and mortality in acute adrenal insufficiency?
englishExplanation:
Patients with acute adrenal insufficiency should be aggressively treated for 
hypotension and hypoglycemia, which are the most immediately life-threatening complications. 
Hypotension from adrenal insufficiency responds to fluids and glucocorticoid replacement 
therapy far more readily than vasoactive agents. Most patients have moderate–severe 
hypoglycemia and should be given dextrosecontaining fluids. Hypernatremia and hypokalemia 
are never seen in adrenal insufficiency. Incontrast, hyponatremia and hypokalemia are common. 
However the severity of these electrolyte abnormalities is generally not significant enough to 
require aggressive correction. Similarly, hypothermia and hypercalcemia do occur but do not 
cause immediately serious complications. Anorexia is a problem in chronic adrenal insufficiency 
and can result in significant weight loss. Mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation (occurring in 
Addison disease but not in secondary adrenal insufficiency) is not a cause for immediate alarm. 
Emergent dermatologic consultation is not indicated.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: حادة adrenal insufficiency تهدد بالحياة عبر hypotension و hypoglycemia. Hypotension يستجيب لـ fluids و glucocorticoid replacement أفضل من vasoactive agents. Hypernatremia و hypokalemia لا يحدثان (بينما hyponatremia و hypokalemia شائعان). Hypothermia و hypercalcemia يحدثان لكنهما غير عاجلين فوراً.
الفخ: يظن البعض أن hypernatremia و hypokalemia شائعان، أو أن anorexia و hyperpigmentation عاجل، لكن الخطورة المباشرة من انخفاض الضغط والسكر.

question:
An 87-year-old female is brought to the ED by her caretaker with dehydration and excessive 
somnolence. Her initial blood work reveals a sodium level of 119 mEq/L and a glucose level of 
900. Which of the following represents her actual sodium level?
englishExplanation:
Since glucose exerts an osmotic pressure on cell membranes, water is extruded from 
cells into the intravascular space, thereby diluting plasma sodium. The sodium level must 
therefore be corrected for hyperglycemia by using the following formula: 
Corrected Na+ = [Na+] + {2.4 × ([glucose] − 100)/100} 
In their 1999 paper, Hiller et al. found that the classically taught 1.6 correction factor was less 
accurate and determined that the actual correction factor was 2.4.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: تصحيح sodium في hyperglycemia يستخدم factor 2.4، لا 1.6. المعادلة: Corrected Na+ = [Na+] + {2.4 × ([glucose] − 100)/100}. عند glucose 900 و Na 119، التصحيح حوالي 138 mEq/L. هذا يوضح أن الصوديوم الحقيقي أعلى بكثير بسبب osmotic water shift.
الفخ: يستخدم البعض عامل 1.6 ويختار 109 أو 119 أو 125، لكن العامل الصحيح 2.4 ويعطي ~138.

question: The normal anion gap (AG) is primarily due to which of the following?
englishExplanation:
The AG is used to signify the difference between the concentration of sodium ([Na+]), 
and the sum of the concentrations of chloride ([Cl−]) and bicarbonate ([HCO3−]) such that: AG = 
[Na+] − [Cl−] − [HCO3−]. However, because of the law of electroneutrality, all aqueous solutions 
must have an equal number of positive and negative charges such that the entire solution is 
neutral. Therefore, the AG does not reflect a true “positive” or “negative” charge in the plasma. 
Instead, it reflects the presence of an anion which the formula is not measuring. In normal 
patients, albumin accounts for the bulk of these “unmeasured anions.” Each 1 g/dL decrease in 
the concentration of albumin will decrease the expected AG by approximately 2.5 to 3 (the 
normal albumin concentration is roughly 4 g/dL × ∼3 ≈ expected AG of 12). Therefore, patients 
with hypoalbuminemia (e.g., cirrhosis, malnutrition) will have a smaller, normal AG. Sulfate, 
phosphate, and citrate make up the bulk of the remaining unmeasured anions.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: AG = [Na+] − [Cl−] − [HCO3−] يعكس unmeasured anions، ليس شحنة حقيقية. Albumin هو المساهم الأكبر (كل 1 g/dL نقص يقلل AG بـ 2.5-3). Sulfate و phosphate و citrate باقي المكونات. بذلك، hypoalbuminemia (cirrhosis، malnutrition) يسبب AG طبيعي أصغر.
الفخ: يختار البعض phosphate أو acetate ويظنونها المساهم الأكبر، لكن albumin هو المسؤول عن الجزء الأكبر.

question:
Which of the following is true regarding osmotic demyelination syndrome (or ODS, also 
known as central pontine myelinolysis)?

options.text: Partial recovery occurs after induction of hyponatremia through infusion of 5% dextrose in
It is more common after correction of acute rather than chronic hyponatremia.
It is more common in diabetic patients with pseudohyponatremia due to hyperglycemia.
Most common initial symptom is burning paresthesias in the hands and feet.
Patients do not typically present until a few days after treatment of hyponatremia.

correctAnswer: Patients do not typically present until a few days after treatment of hyponatremia.
englishExplanation:
ODS is a complication of hyponatremia treatment that most commonly affects 
alcoholics and patients with chronic malnutrition. It carries a grave prognosis with no known 
treatment. It does not typically occur after the treatment of patients with acute hyponatremia 
(<48 hours). Patients with pseudohyponatremia (e.g., diabetic patients with severe 
hyperglycemia) are not at risk for ODS and have normal sodium body stores. Sensory 
abnormalities are not common in ODS. The classic presentation is altered mental status 
(lethargy to coma) with pseudobulbar palsies and spastic quadriplegia after treatment for 
hyponatremia. Patients most commonly have an initial improvement in their sensorium after 
treatment of hyponatremia with hypertonic saline, but patients developing ODS then rapidly 
decline in the ensuing 48 to 72 hours. Most patients present 1 to 6 days after initial treatment of 
hyponatremia.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: ODS (central pontine myelinolysis) يحدث بعد treatment من hyponatremia المزمن (>48 hours) وليس الحاد. لا يحدث في pseudohyponatremia (hyperglycemia). لا توجد حساسية شائعة، وال presentation يتأخر 48-72 ساعة أو 1-6 أيام بعد إصلاح الصوديوم، مع تدهور سريع بعد تحسن مؤقت.
الفخ: يظن البعض أنه يحدث بعد تصحيح حاد أو أنه شائع في السكريين، لكن الشرط الأساسي هو hyponatremia مزمن.

question:
A 25-year-old female presents with diffuse myalgias and dark urine after running a 
marathon. Which of the following treatments is likely to be most effective?
englishExplanation:
The patient likely has rhabdomyolysis, which is due to significant skeletal muscle 
breakdown from a variety of causes. The most serious complication is acute renal failure from 
myoglobin accumulation in renal tubules. Treatment involves normal saline hydration in very 
large quantities (up to 10 to 20 L). No pharmacologic intervention has been shown to improve 
outcomes in randomized controlled trials. This includes mannitol, bicarbonate, and chelation 
therapy. These agents may be employed on a case-by-case basis. Potassium should never be 
supplemented, as myocyte breakdown in rhabdomyolysis releases large amounts of intracellular 
potassium into the bloodstream. Although hypocalcemia can occur in many cases of 
rhabdomyolysis, supplementing calcium can actually increase intracellular calcium and worsen 
myocyte injury. Furosemide and other loop diuretics cause urinary acidosis and should be 
avoided.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: Rhabdomyolysis يتطلب normal saline بكميات كبيرة (10-20 L). لا دواء أثبت فائدة عشوائية: mannitol، bicarbonate، chelation لا ضرورة. Potassium لا يُكمل لأنه يُطلق من الخلايا. Calcium supplementation قد يزيد الضرر. Furosemide يسبب urinary acidosis ويجب تجنبه.
الفخ: يختار البعض potassium أو calcium أو mannitol ويظنونها مفيدة، لكن كلها ضارة أو غير ضرورية.

question:
A 64-year-old female with small cell lung cancer presents with a chief complaint of fatigue, 
dizziness, and imbalance. Her blood work is significant for a sodium level of 112 mmol/L. You 
suspect she has a syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone (SIADH) due to 
her lung cancer. 
Administering normal saline to this patient will likely:

options.text: Make no difference in her sodium level, and cause water retention and edema.

englishExplanation:
In the setting of SIADH, hypertonic saline (3%) must be given in order to correct 
hyponatremia. When isotonic normal saline is given (0.9%), the body “desalinates” it, delivering 
the salt to the kidneys to make concentrated urine, retaining the free water, and worsening the 
hyponatremia. Therefore, in symptomatic patients with critical hyponatremia (sodium <120 
mmol/L), hypertonic saline must be given. However, fluid restriction is the mainstay of 
treatment for more mild reductions in plasma sodium. Neoplasms are the most common cause 

of SIADH and small cell lung carcinoma is the most common neoplasm associated with the 
disorder.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في SIADH، 0.9% saline يُعطى للكلية لصنع بول مركز، ويحتفظ free water ويزيد hyponatremia. لذلك hypertonic saline (3%) مطلوب في الأعراض الحرجة (Na <120). fluid restriction هو العلاج الأساسي للحالات الخفيفة. small cell lung carcinoma هو أكثر الأورام ارتباطاً.
الفخ: يعتقد البعض أن normal saline يحسن الصوديوم، لكنه في الحقيقة ي worsens عند SIADH بدون hypertonic saline.

question:
A 20-year-old male presents with diffuse lower extremity myalgias and dark urine after 
participating in an adventure race. Which of the following is true?

options.text: Hypercalcemia is the most common electrolyte abnormality.
Detection of serum myoglobin is the most sensitive means of diagnosing rhabdomyolysis.
Acute kidney injury is likely if the creatine kinase (CK) is >2,000 Units/L
Loop diuretics are an effective treatment adjunct.
Creatine kinase (CK) has a much longer half-life than myoglobin.

correctAnswer: Creatine kinase (CK) has a much longer half-life than myoglobin.
englishExplanation:
This patient presents with rhabdomyolysis. Hypocalcemia is the most common 
electrolyte abnormality as calcium floods the intracellular space when myocyte membranes fail. 
Because hyperphosphatemia may also occur, treatment of hypocalcemia is not recommended 
unless symptoms are severe or unless severe hyperkalemia develops. Otherwise, calcium 
phosphate may precipitate and form deposits in tissues. Myoglobin has a plasma half-life of only 
1 to 3 hours, making detection sometimes difficult. Although myoglobinuria is pathognomonic 
for rhabdomyolysis, measurement of creatine kinase (CK) is the most sensitive method to detect 
muscle cell injury. CK has a half-life of 1.5 days. The classic finding of a urine dipstick that is 
positive for blood while microscopic urinalysis reveals no red blood cells is present only 50% of 
the time. In addition to trauma, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors are a well-known cause of 
rhabdomyolysis. IV fluids are the mainstay of treatment, and should be started when the CK 
>5,000 Units/L. Alkalinization may be helpful while loop diuretics offer no benefit.
arabicExplanation:
ليش: في rhabdomyolysis، hypocalcemia هو الأكثر شيوعاً، ولا يُعالج إلا إذا كانت الأعراض شديدة أو hyperkalemia شديد، لتجنب calcium phosphate precipitates. Myoglobin half-life 1-3 ساعات، CK 1.5 أيام. الكشف بـ CK أكثر حساسية. IV fluids عند CK >5000 وحدها مفيدة. Loop diuretics لا فائدة.
الفخ: يختار البعض hypercalcemia أو أن myoglobin أكثر حساسية من CK، لكن العكس هو الصحيح.

question: Primary chronic adrenal insufficiency is usually due to:
englishExplanation:
Increasingly, acute adrenal insufficiency is thought to be a rare condition, and most 
cases of acute adrenal insufficiency probably represent an exacerbation of chronic disease. 
When acute adrenal insufficiency occurs, it is most commonly due to exogenous glucocorticoid 

administration. Chronic adrenal insufficiency is idiopathic (thought to be autoimmune-mediated 
destruction of the adrenal gland) in 66% to 75% of cases.

control Grave’s disease. She was euthyroid at the time of operation. 
No complications arose from the surgery. The next day she was 
complaining of tingling in her fingers and around her mouth and 
spasm of her fingers. An ECG showed a prolonged QT interval. The 
ward doctor had given three boluses of 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate 
intravenously and prescribed oral calcium supplements but the patient 
remained symptomatic.
After the 10% calcium gluconate intravenous boluses blood results were 
as follows.
Investigations:
serum corrected calcium
1.87 mmol/L
(2.20–2.60)
serum phosphate
0.9 mmol/L
(0.8–1.4)

0.61 mmol/L

Repeat the bolus of 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate intravenously
Start a calcium gluconate infusion intravenously

2. E.  Start a calcium gluconate infusion intravenously
The patient is still symptomatic and hypocalcaemic, despite three boluses of calcium gluconate. 
Start an infusion of calcium gluconate. Dilute 10 ampoules of 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate in either 
sodium chloride 0.9% or glucose 5%. This is 22 mmol of calcium. Start at 50 mL/hr and titrate to 
maintain calcium in the low normal range; 0.30–0.40 mmol/kg of elemental calcium should increase 
serum calcium by 0.5–0.75 mmol/L. If the hypocalcaemia is likely to persist, oral vitamin D in the 
form of an activated vitamin D supplement (e.g. 1- alfacalcidol) should be commenced.

due to inadvertent removal or interruption of blood supply. Symptoms and signs appear between 
one and seven days post-op depending on the severity of insult. The other cause of hypocalcaemia 
after thyroidectomy is due to calcium retention by bone. Thyrotoxicosis leads to demineralization 
of the bones, and so this can be restored once the hyperthyroid state is resolved.

A 48-year-old man with lower limb cellulitis attended the ambulatory 
care unit for assessment for outpatient intravenous antibiotic 
treatment. This was the second episode of cellulitis requiring 
antibiotics in the previous six months. There was no history of trauma 
or insect bites to the skin. He had no other past medical history and 
was symptomatically well and specifically had no symptoms of thirst, 
polyuria, polydipsia, or weight loss. 
On examination, he had a body mass index (BMI) of 31 kg/m2, 
temperature 37.7°C, pulse 89 beats per minute, and blood pressure 
146/78 mmHg. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal examination 
was normal. There was cellulitis of the right calf with dry skin on the 
heels and tinea pedis. A random capillary blood glucose was 8.4 mmol/L. 
He had previously had a random plasma glucose of 10.4 mmol/L, but had 
not had any further investigations. Haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) was sent 
on this admission.
The next step in management is:

options.text: Refer to GP to follow-up the result of the HbA1c
Refer to the community diabetes education team
Start metformin 500 mg od increasing up to 1 g bd as tolerated

englishExplanation:
4. A.  Refer to GP to follow up the result of the HbA1c
The patient is asymptomatic and has not had a diagnostic blood glucose reading.
Diagnosis and initial treatment of diabetes: the diagnostic criteria for diabetes changed in January 
2011. This, for the first time, allowed for the use of the HbA1c in the diagnosis of diabetes rather 
than relying on the oral glucose tolerance test. The HbA1c cannot be used for diagnosis in the following patients:
● All children and young people
● Patients of any age suspected of having type 1 diabetes
● Patients with symptoms of diabetes for less than two months
● Patients at high diabetes risk who are acutely ill (e.g. those requiring hospital admission)
● Patients taking medication that may cause rapid glucose rise (e.g. steroids, antipsychotics)
● Patients with acute pancreatic damage, including pancreatic surgery
● In pregnancy
● Presence of genetic, haematological, and illness-related factors that influence HbA1c and its 
measurement
Diagnostic criteria: an HbA1c >48 mmol/mol is the cut-off point for diagnosing diabetes; however, 
if glucose tolerance tests have diagnosed diabetes and the HbA1c is <48 mmol/mol, this does not 
rule out diabetes.
Previous World Health Organization (WHO) criteria were: diabetes symptoms (i.e. polyuria, polydipsia, and unexplained weight loss) plus:
● a random venous plasma glucose concentration >11.1 mmol/L; or
● a fasting plasma glucose concentration >7.0 mmol/L (whole blood >6.1 mmol/L); or
● two-hour plasma glucose concentration >11.1 mmol/L two hours after 75 g anhydrous glucose in an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT).
With no symptoms, diagnosis should not be based on a single glucose determination but requires 
confirmatory plasma venous determination. At least one additional glucose test result on another 
day with a value in the diabetic range is essential, either fasting, from a random sample, or from the 
two-hour post-glucose load. If the fasting or random values are not diagnostic, the two-hour value 
should be used.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidance for the treatment of type 2 
diabetes has structured patient education as the core of treatment. At diagnosis, all patients 
should have the opportunity to take part in an education programme (e.g. DESMOND (Diabetes 
Education and Self Management for Ongoing and Newly Diagnosed)) that focuses on diet and 
lifestyle to encourage a healthy, balanced diet with appropriate activity levels (current recommendation is for 30 minutes of physical activity five times per week). If after three months of diet 
and lifestyle interventions the HbA1c is still >48 mmol/mol then medication, usually metformin, 
is introduced.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE Guideline 28: Type 2 diabetes in adults: management. December 2015.
World Health Organization. Use of Glycated Haemoglobin (HbA1c) in the Diagnosis of Diabetes Mellitis, 2011. http://www.who.int/diabetes/publications/report-hba1c_2011.pdf

14. D.  Primary hyperparathyroidism
The commonest causes of hypercalcaemia are:
1.	Primary and tertiary hyperparathyroidism
2.	Malignancy—myeloma, bony metastases, humoral hypercalcaemia (paraneoplastic)
Less common causes are:
1.	Hyperthyroidism
2.	Addison’s disease
3.	Vitamin D toxicity
4.	Thiazide diuretics
5.	Renal failure
6.	Immobilization
7.	Vitamin A toxicity

150
Symptoms of hypercalcaemia are renal stones, abdominal pain, constipation, depression, arthralgia 
(‘stones, bones, groans, psychic moans’), thirst, polyuria, and polydipsia. Often, the hypercalcaemia 
associated with primary hyperparathyroidism is asymptomatic.
Primary hyperparathyroidism has an incidence of 1 in 500 in the general population. It is most 
common in postmenopausal women. In primary hyperparathyroidism there is an inappropriately high parathyroid hormone (PTH) for the level of calcium. The commonest cause is a single 
parathyroid adenoma (85%); parathyroid hyperplasia occurs in 14% and in <1% the cause is parathyroid carcinoma. Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) syndromes are associated with parathyroid 
hyperplasia rather than a discrete adenoma and occur in younger patients; there may be a family 
history.
Calcium and phosphate homeostasis is controlled by PTH and vitamin D. The main function of PTH 
is to maintain calcium within normal ranges. When calcium levels fall there is a rise in PTH, which 
has direct effects on bone and kidneys and indirect effects on the gastrointestinal tract.
In the kidney, PTH enhances renal calcium absorption and promotes the 1-hydroxylation of 
25-hydroxyvitamin D3. 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 increases absorption of calcium from the gastrointestinal tract. PTH and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 also have effects on bones to increase resorption of calcium from the bones to increase calcium. PTH inhibits renal phosphate reabsorption, 
which leads to low serum phosphate levels and phosphaturia.
Hyperparathyroidism is not a benign condition and can lead to osteoporosis, renal stones, renal 
impairment, and heart disease.

question:
An anaesthetist doing a list in day-case theatres asked for advice. The 
first patient on the list had type 1 diabetes controlled by a continuous 
subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII or insulin pump). The operation was 
not expected to last longer than an hour, so the patient should be eating 
and drinking within 2–3 hours of the operation finishing. The blood 
glucose reading was 7 mmol/L and the surgeon was due in theatre in the 
next ten minutes to start the case.
What do you advise?

options.text: Keep the pump running at the usual basal rate and monitor the blood glucose hourly
Keep the pump running but increase the basal rate to compensate for the stress of the
Keep the pump running but reduce the basal rate to compensate for the patient being
Stop the pump and start a variable-rate insulin infusion (VRII)
Stop the pump for the duration of the procedure and restart once the patient has

englishExplanation:
16. A.  Keep the pump running at the usual basal rate and monitor the blood glucose hourly
If the patient is having an elective procedure and will not miss more than one meal and the preoperative blood glucose level is between 4 and 12 mmol/L, then it is safe to proceed with the 
pump running at the usual basal rate with hourly monitoring of the blood glucose levels. The 

DIABETES AND ENDOCRINOLOGY | ANSWERS
152
152
cannula needs to be placed away from the operation site. Post-operatively, the patient can then 
manage their blood glucose levels as normal.
If the patient is going to miss more than one meal or the blood glucose is more than 12 mmol/L 
then the pump should be removed (and put in a safe place) or turned off and a variable-rate insulin 
infusion (VRII) should be started.
If the patient experiences hypoglycaemia intra-operatively—treat the hypoglycaemia normally and 
retest in 15 minutes. If there are repeated episodes of hypoglycaemia then the basal rate is too 
high; the pump should be stopped and a VRII started.
There are little data on the use of continuous subcutaneous insulin infusions (CSII) in surgery, so 
recommendations are based on expert opinion.
CSII is used to treat patients with type 1 diabetes. It is approved by NICE for those patients that fail 
to reach HbA1c targets despite intensive management with multiple daily injections with analogue 
insulin and carbohydrate counting or due to severe disabling hypoglycaemia. The patient wears an 
insulin pump that contains a reservoir of short-acting analogue insulin (not actrapid), which is attached to the patient via a short length of fine-bore tubing connected to a special cannula placed in 
the subcutaneous tissues. Modern pumps are about the size of a pager. It is not an artificial pancreas.
Insulin is continually infused at a pre-programmed rate over a 24-hour period with variations 
throughout the 24-hour period to account for changes in hormone levels and activity (basal rate). 
Some patients have different basal rates for work and weekends/holidays which reflect the effect 
of a stressful or physical job on insulin requirements (e.g. lower basal rates for physical jobs, higher 
rates for stress, lower rates needed for relaxing weekends or the hormonal changes during the 
menstrual cycle). There is the ability to set a temporary basal rate should the need arise (e.g. exercise, stress). The patient will bolus insulin when eating based on the carbohydrate content of the 
meal but also to correct for hyperglycaemia.
There is no basal insulin taken, so if the pump is disconnected, accidentally stopped, or if there is 
kinking of the tubing etc., hyperglycaemia and ketoacidosis can follow more rapidly than in patients 
on subcutaneous injections of insulin.
The pump should not be stopped or removed unless an alternative means of insulin delivery is 
available.
If a patient on CSII is admitted to hospital and is still able to use their pump then do not swap to 
another means of insulin delivery. If there is DKA or the patient is unconscious or unable to manage the pump then either swap to VRII or subcutaneous insulin until CSII can be restarted. Always 
involve the diabetes team at the earliest opportunity.
Boyle et al. Guidelines for application of continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (insulin pump) therapy in the peri-operative period. Journal of Diabetes Science and Technology 2012; 6: 184–190.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Technology Appraisal Guidance 151. Continuous 
subcutaneous insulin infusion for the treatment of diabetes mellitus. July 2008, revised 2011.

All patients with hypoadrenalism should be told sick-day rules, which include doubling their normal 
oral steroids if they have a fever of more than 37.5°C or have an infection, taking 20 mg hydrocortisone if they experience nausea or serious injury, and taking 100 mg intramuscular hydrocortisone

Which of the following investigations are not routinely recommended 
for the investigation of suspected dementia?
englishExplanation:
5. D.  Syphilis serology
A dementia screen should be performed at presentation. This should include routine haematology, 
biochemistry (electrolytes, glucose, calcium, and renal and liver function), thyroid function tests, 
and B12 and folate levels. An MSU should be sent if delirium is suspected. A chest X-ray or ECG 
would be appropriate if presenting acutely on the admissions unit. Syphilis serology and HIV testing should only be done if clinically suspected. CSF examination is only appropriate if CJD or other 
forms of rapidly progressing dementias are being considered. An EEG may be useful in a suspected 
delirium, CJD, or seizures associated with dementia. Structural imaging using MRI or CT should be 
used to rule out other causes or cerebral pathology and help identify subtypes. A single-photon 
emission computed tomography (SPECT) is useful to identify Alzheimer’s disease from vascular 
dementia and frontotemporal dementia in the setting of a memory clinic.

with dementia and their carers in health and social care. November 2006 (revised April 2014).
